# Autoware Universe — GitHub Issues: Data Dump & Analysis

> **Source:** `autowarefoundation/autoware_universe` GitHub Issues (the GitHub
> *Issues* connection; pull requests are reported separately by GitHub and are not
> the focus of this dump).
> **Snapshot taken:** 2026-09-11.
> **Method:** GitHub GraphQL `repository.issues` (all states, newest first) with up
> to 100 comments per issue, retrieved via the `gh` CLI.
> **Scale:** **1,136 issues**, **4,807 comments**.
>
> This file has two purposes: (1) a **full analysis** of the issue landscape, and
> (2) the **raw download** of every issue, its labels, body and comments
> (Appendices A and B, auto-generated).

## Part 1 — Quantitative summary

### 1.1 Totals

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total issues | **1,136** |
| Open | **209** (18.4%) |
| Closed | **927** (81.6%) |
| Total comments | **4,807** |
| Issues with no comments | **158** |
| Issues labelled `status:stale` | **340** (30.0%) |

The **close rate is high (82%)**, which reflects active triage — but **30% carry the
`status:stale` label** (195 of them still open), i.e. a large backlog of issues that
have gone quiet without being resolved. For a deployer this is a maintenance-signal,
not a correctness signal.

### 1.2 Issues created per year

| Year | Issues |
|---|---|
| 2021 | 29 |
| 2022 | 356 |
| 2023 | 272 |
| 2024 | 285 |
| 2025 | 138 |
| 2026 (to 09-11) | 56 |

Volume peaked in 2022 and has declined since. This is consistent with (a) migration
of discussion to Discord/working groups and the release/QA process maturing, and
(b) issues increasingly being filed against the **core/launch** repos or tracked
internally. It is **not** evidence that the system became problem-free.

## Part 2 — Thematic analysis

The issues cluster tightly around a few recurring **failure axes**. These map
directly to the architecture's weak points (§11, §22, §33, §34).

### Theme 1 — Planning correctness and state regressions (largest)

- **Paths leaving the drivable area** (#1761) and **unstable yaw in
  `obstacle_avoidance_planner`** (#966) are core planner-geometry failures.
- **Prediction errors**: "Map-Based Prediction incorrect predictions" (#494);
  "Predicted trajectory ignores NPC stopped downhill" (#5776) — exactly the
  compounded-error risk across the module boundary (§2.1).
- **`goal_planner` segfault** in `AstarSearch` deallocation (#5154) — a
  freespace/planning crash, not just a behavior error.
- **State-machine regressions**: "[1.8.0 regression] behavior_path_planner
  permanently silent after first completed mission" (#13021) — demonstrates why
  repeated mission-lifecycle regression testing is mandatory (§21.4, §33G).
- **Parking performance** limitations (#12937).

### Theme 2 — Perception robustness

- **Ground segmentation behind low objects** (#669) → obstacle/free-space errors.
- **Concatenated pointcloud intermittently not published** (#1009) → downstream
  localization + detection starvation (the exact "concatenate/time-sync" stage of
  §7.3).
- **Detector/toolchain churn**: RTMDet (#7235), TVM (#908, #2186, #2309),
  TensorRT build failures (#7944), **BEVFusion on CUDA compute 12.0** (#13067),
  **BEVFormer missing grid_sampler TRT plugin** (#13038), BEVFusion model config
  mismatch (#13023). This is the "ML artifacts must be version-pinned" thesis of
  §3.1 in the wild.
- **Multi-LiDAR scaling**: pointcloud container fails past 5 LiDARs (#2940).
- **Fusion bugs**: projecting/matching issues and stale projector logs (#13172),
  `RingOutlierFilterComponent` azimuth threshold (#13146).

### Theme 3 — Localization fragility (safety-relevant)

- **NDT reinitialization while moving** (#1375) — degenerate/recovery behavior.
- **Low-friction sliding degrades localization** (#6919) and **"vehicle makes
  collision when localization is bad"** (#6616) — localization error propagates to
  collisions; matches §11.6.
- **`map_height_fitter` fails to detect map ground** (#3993) — the known
  dynamic/partial-load trap (§22).
- **Pose instability** appears across threads (NDT/GNSS arbitration, covariance).

### Theme 4 — Sensing, drivers, sync, and contamination

- Ouster/other ROS 2 driver integration (#4978, #551).
- Pointcloud concatenation/sync failures (#1009).
- Sensor component and preprocessing issues (`component:sensing` = 58).

### Theme 5 — Build, CI, CUDA, ARM, dependencies

- **CUDA-dependent packages split** (#3135); TensorRT/GPU build failures
  (#7944); **ARM64** labels; CI efficiency (#4497) and dead workflows (#4279).
- **Missing declared dependencies** (#13207), **model file-structure refactors**
  (#13086), **docker image missing Python subpackage/CSVs** (#13173) — the
  release/artifact-lockstep problem (§3.1).

### Theme 6 — System tools, interfaces and lifecycle

- **`system_monitor` crash on a NUL-containing value** (#12870).
- **RViz plugin lifecycle bugs**: detached worker UAF in
  `planning_factor_rviz_plugin` (#13284), `autoware_tensorrt_vad` segfault on TF
  miss (#13269) — plugin lifecycle (§19.3) hazards.
- **V2X/V2I traffic-signal interface** (#2567) — matches the arbiter design
  (§12, §33D).
- CARLA simulator friction (`simulator:carla` = 33, #13354, #13173).

### Theme 7 — Safety-relevant open issues to watch

| Issue | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **#13012** | Steering frozen during emergency stop → lane departure mid-corner (MRM lateral behavior) |
| **#6616** | Collision when localization degrades |
| **#6919** | Localization worsens on low-friction surfaces |
| **#13021** | Planner silent after first mission (1.8.0 regression) |
| **#5154** | `goal_planner` segfault |
| **#3993** | `map_height_fitter` ground-detection failure → bad init/spawn |

These reinforce the deployment guidance: **validate localization, MRM lateral
behavior, planner lifecycle, and map loading explicitly** before road use.

## Part 2b — Deep Dive: 40 Most-Commented Issues

> Each summary is derived **strictly from the issue body and its comment thread**
> (the same raw data as Appendix B), ordered by comment count. These are the
> threads where the project's hardest problems and design debates actually played
> out.

#### #7235 — Implement RTMDet to Perception Pipeline
- **What it is:** Feature request to add the RTMDet instance-segmentation model to Autoware Universe perception alongside YOLOX, targeting the camera-lidar fusion pipeline.
- **Root cause / detail:** YOLOX was strong for bounding boxes but weak at instance segmentation. The author converted PyTorch models to ONNX/TensorRT, added CUDA preprocessing, NMS, batch support and a ROS 2 package, and compared RTMDet vs YOLOX. Discussion debated whether projected masks outperform projected boxes for `roi_cluster_fusion`/`mask_cluster_fusion`.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed as "won't do" by the author citing lack of reviews/motivation; maintainers later apologized and invited the PRs to be reopened. A separate `mask_cluster_fusion` branch and `trt_batched_nms` repo were created; no final merge confirmed.
- **Why it matters:** Perception. Mask-based fusion could improve labeling of overlapping objects, but the episode exposed a slow review/ownership gap that risks stalling community contributions.

#### #966 — Yaw calculation is unstable in obstacle_avoidance_planner when skipping optimization
- **What it is:** Bug where yaw becomes unstable in `obstacle_avoidance_planner` when optimization is skipped (`skip_optimization=true`), disturbing downstream modules.
- **Root cause / detail:** The planner resamples x, y and yaw from the behavior module, but yaw from `behavior_velocity_planner` is not smoothed; per-dimension spline interpolation overshoots. This occurs only with the non-default `skip_optimization=true`. Debate continued over whether behavior velocity or interpolation is at fault.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed with no clear final fix shown; discussion converged on unsmoothed `behavior_velocity_planner` yaw as the cause and lack of a validation mechanism.
- **Why it matters:** Planning. Unstable yaw expands obstacle-stop detection areas, triggering spurious stops outside the trajectory.

#### #3135 — Move CUDA-dependent packages to a separate repository
- **What it is:** Task to relocate CUDA-dependent packages so Autoware Universe can build from packages available in the ROS index without CUDA.
- **Root cause / detail:** Debian/build-farm and CI concerns drove the split. Discussion covered naming conventions (`_trt`, `_tvm`), merging duplicate `_nodes` packages, and pros/cons of a new repo vs a thin `cuda` package.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed with no clear conclusion. TIER IV first proposed renaming only; proposals included a thin `cuda` package and an `autoware.universe_cuda` repo.
- **Why it matters:** Build/release and perception CUDA packages; the split affects how teams build, package and install Autoware without NVIDIA hardware.

#### #4279 — fix: dead github workflows | spell-check-differential
- **What it is:** CI task to revive the dead `spell-check-differential` workflow by reducing cspell errors to zero.
- **Root cause / detail:** So many cspell errors existed that the check was effectively ignored. The approach was to fix typos, extend the dictionary, add inline ignore comments, and track totals via a spell-check-all workflow (progress logged from ~786 down to ~434 errors), with `spell-check-partial` made required.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed; substantial progress, `spell-check-partial` made required, though no single "all errors fixed" confirmation appears.
- **Why it matters:** CI and code quality; typo noise and dead checks undermine maintainability and contributor discipline.

#### #908 — Run Lidar Centerpoint with TVM
- **What it is:** Feature/investigation to run `lidar_centerpoint` through TVM as a backend-agnostic runtime instead of TensorRT.
- **Root cause / detail:** TVM lacked support for dynamic (`-1`) shapes; fixed dimensions compiled correctly. The CUDA backend needed a TVM runtime built with CUDA, so Vulkan was suggested. Models and `definition.yaml` were pushed to ModelZoo.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed; running CenterPoint with TVM was achieved; documentation of the conversion remained. A follow-up for the CUDA backend was planned.
- **Why it matters:** Perception; part of Autoware's effort to avoid NVIDIA/TensorRT vendor lock-in.

#### #4978 — How to integrate the official Ouster ROS 2 driver into Autoware Universe
- **What it is:** Support question about feeding the official Ouster ROS 2 driver pointcloud into Autoware's preprocessing pipeline.
- **Root cause / detail:** Ouster's point layout differs from Autoware's expected `PointXYZIRCAEDT`, so CropBox/concatenate nodes produced no output. Users resolved it with custom format-converter nodes; the author switched to Livox.
- **Status / resolution:** Open and stale. No upstream integration fix; ad-hoc adapter packages are the workaround.
- **Why it matters:** Sensing/perception. Third-party LiDAR integration remains a recurring field problem for multi-vendor deployments.

#### #1009 — Sometimes the sensing module doesn't publish concatenated pointcloud
- **What it is:** Bug where the sensing module intermittently fails to load `concatenate_data` / `crop_box_filter` components ("Failed to find class with the requested plugin name").
- **Root cause / detail:** Initially blamed on launch order, but `LoadComposableNodes` works regardless of order. The real cause was components being loaded concurrently via the `load_node` service while the default QoS queue was too small, dropping load calls.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Workaround: decouple the container launch; root cause fixed upstream by an `rclcpp` PR for the next Humble update.
- **Why it matters:** Sensing/launch. The intermittent failure leaves Autoware without concatenated pointclouds, breaking localization and perception.

#### #494 — Map Based Prediction Incorrect Predictions
- **What it is:** Bug where `map_based_prediction` produced odd trajectories (e.g. reversing for straight-moving objects) and sometimes crashed with `std::length_error`.
- **Root cause / detail:** The linear-vs-normal prediction decision used only the object's x velocity, but tracked objects were expressed in the map frame with both x and y velocity — an ambiguous coordinate-frame issue. The ASWG agreed velocity should be object-centric.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed/stale. The ASWG agreed on an object-centric frame and to fill the y component, but no confirmed code fix is shown.
- **Why it matters:** Prediction. Bad predicted paths can block intersections and cause unsafe behavior.

#### #551 — Implement sensor drivers for ROS 2
- **What it is:** High-priority task to identify and implement/port missing ROS 2 sensor drivers for the bus ODD platforms.
- **Root cause / detail:** Teams compiled sensor/driver inventories for the ITRI Bus and Leo Drive Isuzu Bus (radar, LiDAR, GNSS-INS, cameras). Some drivers were missing or private; others were published.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Many drivers were developed or open-sourced; some vendors still did not provide code.
- **Why it matters:** Sensing. Driver availability directly gates which vehicles and sensors a team can deploy.

#### #1761 — behavior_path_planner generated path outside of drivable area
- **What it is:** Bug where an inclined goal pose makes `behavior_path_planner` generate a path outside the drivable area, ignoring ego width/length.
- **Root cause / detail:** Smooth goal connection does not thoroughly check lane boundaries; the proposal was to make the goal-angle threshold (`th_angle`) configurable and reject goals whose vehicle footprint falls outside lane boundaries.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Implemented via a PR adding the `th_angle` parameter plus goal footprint check.
- **Why it matters:** Planning. Invalid goals produce strange trajectories outside the drivable area — a safety and reliability risk.

#### #1375 — Adding NDT reinitialization and reinitialization while moving
- **What it is:** Feature request to add NDT reinitialization, especially while moving, as a localization recovery mechanism.
- **Root cause / detail:** NDT initializes once while motionless; if a topic stops and restarts while moving, no reinitialization occurs and the vehicle can "fly" or spin. Discussion weighed NDT match-score/iterations against EKF covariance (`localization_error_monitor`).
- **Status / resolution:** Open and stale. No clear conclusion; fast localization-failure detection was the near-term ask; automatic reinit is mid/long-term.
- **Why it matters:** Localization. Without detection and reinitialization, pose loss can cause runaway behavior; fail-safe/MRM integration is required.

#### #2782 — bag_time_manager_rviz_plugin fails to build (-Werror=deprecated-declarations)
- **What it is:** Build bug where the plugin uses deprecated `rmw_qos_profile_t`, failing under `-Werror=deprecated-declarations`.
- **Root cause / detail:** ROS 2 Rolling API changes introduced the deprecation. Maintainers disagreed on whether to support Rolling (maintenance cost) vs merging a minimal future-proof fix.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Consensus shifted to merging the small change.
- **Why it matters:** Tools/build. Cross-distro compilation and the recurring future-proofing vs maintenance-cost tension.

#### #1121 — detection_area does not visualize debug markers when some obstacles are not detected
- **What it is:** Bug/feature that `detection_area` publishes no debug marker when no obstacle is detected, so state is invisible.
- **Root cause / detail:** Markers are only published when an obstacle is inside the area. The proposal was color-coded states (registered/not-detected, detected, over-deadline, unregistered). The existing code hardcoded colors/attributes rather than parameterizing them.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed/stale. A contributor worked on it but hit push/auth/fork issues; no confirmed merged fix.
- **Why it matters:** Planning debug tooling. Poor visualization makes detection-area/stop behavior hard to diagnose.

#### #669 — Ground segmentation fails for points behind low objects
- **What it is:** Bug where ground points behind small objects such as roadside poles are misclassified as part of the object.
- **Root cause / detail:** `scan_ground_filter` produced a "tail" behind low objects; tuning tolerances reduced it, and the ray filter performed better (accuracy 88.42→89.38 on 748 labeled clouds).
- **Status / resolution:** Closed and resolved via a PR; the reporter confirmed the problem no longer occurs with current ground segmentation.
- **Why it matters:** Perception. False object points create phantom obstacles and degrade detection.

#### #6919 — Localization rapidly gets worse while sliding through a low-friction area
- **What it is:** Bug observed in CARLA where localization degrades quickly as the ego slides through a low-friction area, eventually stopping permanently.
- **Root cause / detail:** TF calibration was suspected and fixed, but the issue persisted; the conclusion was that the `ekf_localizer` motion model cannot handle large drift in low-friction conditions.
- **Status / resolution:** Open and stale. No fix; maintainers stated it is difficult for current Autoware to operate in this location.
- **Why it matters:** Localization. Slippery/low-friction scenarios can cause pose loss and a stuck vehicle (matches §33I).

#### #5154 — Recurrent crashes in goal_planner (segfault in AstarSearch deallocation)
- **What it is:** Bug where `goal_planner` intermittently segfaults while deallocating the A* open list.
- **Root cause / detail:** A `0x0` was seen in `open_list_`; the conclusion was a **concurrency bug** — `StartPlannerModule` creates a separate callback queue and the manager creates/destroys/moves modules at runtime while the freespace callback sleeps before `planFreespacePath()`.
- **Status / resolution:** Open/stale. A PR may fix it; a contributor could not reproduce, so no confirmed resolution.
- **Why it matters:** Planning. A crash in the freespace/goal planner halts goal-reaching and can leave the vehicle stuck.

#### #2940 — Pointcloud Container Not Working with More than 5 Lidars
- **What it is:** Bug where, with more than five LiDARs in the pointcloud container, one random LiDAR fails to publish.
- **Root cause / detail:** Not an Autoware bug but a ROS 2/DDS issue: components loaded simultaneously from multiple launch files dropped `load_node` service calls because the default QoS queue was too small.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Fixed upstream by an `rclcpp` PR reaching the next Humble apt upgrade.
- **Why it matters:** Sensing/perception. Multi-LiDAR vehicles can silently lose a sensor, breaking localization and perception.

#### #3993 — map_height_fitter fails to detect map ground
- **What it is:** Bug where `map_height_fitter` fails to locate the PCD map ground, placing the initial position far under the map.
- **Root cause / detail:** With **dynamic/partial map loading**, `pcd_msg` fields are never set, so `pcl::fromROSMsg` fails; `pointcloud_map_loader` may also fail to start. Could not be reproduced by a maintainer.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed/stale. Workaround: **disable dynamic map loading**; root cause not fixed in-thread (likely an `rclcpp` issue).
- **Why it matters:** Localization/map. The vehicle can be placed underground or never initialize — the exact trap in §22/§9.

#### #6616 — Vehicle makes collision when localization is bad
- **What it is:** Bug in CARLA where the ego collides with a guardrail during poor localization despite obstacles being in the pointcloud.
- **Root cause / detail:** Obstacle-stop z-axis filtering ignored the elevated guardrail because estimated z was stuck near 0 during localization failure (low NDT NVTL, odometry-only updates). Workaround: disable z-axis obstacle filtering.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Identified as localization-related; workaround documented, no planning fix.
- **Why it matters:** Planning/localization safety. Bad pose data can defeat obstacle stopping and cause collisions.

#### #2567 — Change traffic signal interface to support V2X/V2I
- **What it is:** Feature to unify traffic-signal input so V2X/V2I is handled the same way as camera recognition.
- **Root cause / detail:** Planning's traffic-light module had `perception` and `external` inputs, but `external` was meant for operator override, not signal color. The proposal merged image recognition and V2X before planning, separating bulbs and signals via lanelet relation/way IDs.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed and resolved. New messages and perception/planning changes were merged.
- **Why it matters:** Perception/planning. This is the architectural basis for V2X traffic-signal support (the `traffic_light_arbiter` in §12/§33D).

#### #4497 — Improve CI efficiency on build-and-test-differential jobs
- **What it is:** CI improvement: a single changed package triggered building 186 packages via `colcon build --packages-above-and-dependencies`.
- **Root cause / detail:** Proposed `--packages-above-depth 1` plus `--packages-up-to` to cut the set. Reviewers raised API/ABI compatibility and stale-artifact concerns.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed in favor of later work after smaller Docker images and ccache changed the premise; full implementation deferred.
- **Why it matters:** CI/developer productivity.

#### #5776 — Predicted trajectory ignores the NPC vehicle stopping on a downhill
- **What it is:** Bug where the predicted trajectory ignores an NPC stopped on a downhill slope, so the ego fails to brake and collides.
- **Root cause / detail:** Slope compensation in the longitudinal controller did not adjust deceleration enough; measured slope disagreed with the map, and target vs actual velocity diverged. Raising `max_pitch_rad`/`min_pitch_rad` to ±0.5 on a newer version fixed stopping.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed and resolved (newer version + parameter change).
- **Why it matters:** Planning/control. Slope handling is safety-critical for stopping behind obstacles on grades.

#### #2186 — Enable OpenCL Backend for TVM
- **What it is:** Feature to enable TVM's OpenCL backend so TVM packages performed acceptably.
- **Root cause / detail:** Vulkan had an accuracy issue; LLVM was too slow for DL, so OpenCL/CUDA was needed. Accuracy differences appeared on CenterPoint `heatmap`/`vel` outputs.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. OpenCL was set up in the CUDA Docker image; `tvm_vendor` released for Humble (NVIDIA requires an ICD file).
- **Why it matters:** Perception. GPU inference without hard CUDA dependence.

#### #2309 — Implement yolo_TVM
- **What it is:** Feature to implement YOLO inference with TVM, porting TensorRT packages to a TVM pipeline.
- **Root cause / detail:** Work covered accuracy verification for LLVM/OpenCL, ModelZoo PR, CUDA kernels, and porting peripheral functions. The contributor hit TVM import/install and an upstream TVM bug.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed and abandoned. Autoware moved to TensorRT-only inference and TVM packages were being removed.
- **Why it matters:** Perception; signals the project's reversal away from TVM toward TensorRT.

#### #7944 — Colcon build failure of TensorRT (python3.8 / tensorrt-10.1.0.27)
- **What it is:** Build failure in `lidar_transfusion` (`IExecutionContext` lacks `setTensorAddress`/`setInputShape`).
- **Root cause / detail:** The Docker image had TensorRT 8.4.2 but `lidar_transfusion` requires 8.6.1, and source was outdated. Maintainer noted source builds require Ubuntu 22.04, not 20.04.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Solved by upgrading to Ubuntu 22.04 and building from source.
- **Why it matters:** Perception build environment. Version skew between TensorRT, image and source is a common deployment pitfall.

#### #4070 — High latency of lidar pointcloud after launching occupancy grid map
- **What it is:** Bug where raw LiDAR pointcloud in RViz had a 5–10 s delay once perception (specifically the occupancy grid map module) launched.
- **Root cause / detail:** `ros2 topic delay` confirmed ~10 s header delay; skipping NaN points helped, but latency returned with `crop_box_filter`. Could not be reproduced by a maintainer.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. User avoided it by switching to Euclidean clustering; no root-cause fix.
- **Why it matters:** Perception/localization. Pointcloud delay prevents localization from functioning.

#### #1228 — Image messages have latency or are dropped
- **What it is:** Bug where camera images dropped to ~3–4 FPS under the full pipeline vs 20 FPS standalone (~70–80 ms latency).
- **Root cause / detail:** Suspected CPU/DDS overhead. Recommendations: composable nodes and Iceoryx zero-copy; reusing the `pointcloud_container` cut network traffic ~30% and CPU usage.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Fixes in launch PRs; Iceoryx adoption needed further discussion.
- **Why it matters:** Perception/system. Camera throughput/latency constrain 2D detection and fusion.

#### #2095 — Avoidance ignores pedestrian if there is a bus behind
- **What it is:** Bug where `behavior_path_planner` does not target a pedestrian for avoidance, yet still generates a path passing near it when an avoidable bus is behind.
- **Root cause / detail:** Non-target object types produce `ObjectIsNotType`, so the algorithm ignores the pedestrian, but the resulting avoidance path can still pass dangerously close. Discussion weighed checking objects on the path and invalidating/reverting maneuvers.
- **Status / resolution:** Open and stale. Needs discussion after the planning architecture is updated; no conclusion.
- **Why it matters:** Planning safety. Non-target obstacle handling directly affects pedestrian safety.

#### #1543 — Vehicle starts moving before the steering angle converged
- **What it is:** Bug where, after re-initializing with a low `steer_rate_lim_dps`, the car moves before steering converges.
- **Root cause / detail:** `mpc_follower` cannot solve with a very small steer-rate limit, so it sends the previous command (e.g. 30°) instead of the target (0°). Keep-steer-converged options did not help in the sim. Proposal: do not constrain steer rate while stopped.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed/stale. A draft PR and promised follow-up, but no confirmed merge.
- **Why it matters:** Control. Primarily a planning-simulator reinitialization issue, but it can affect real-vehicle resume behavior (links to §14/§27 steering convergence).

#### #2597 — The positioning module is unstable for unknown reasons
- **What it is:** Bug where localization for a large bus shook, drifted and failed, plus DDS throughput dropped with multiple subscribers.
- **Root cause / detail:** The `base_link`→lidar TF was wrong, causing large EKF errors on curves; plus CycloneDDS/network config (`rmem`, multicast on `lo`, `ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY`) and build type. Rebuilding with `RelWithDebInfo` raised FPS from 5→30 Hz.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed and resolved via TF calibration, DDS tuning, loopback multicast, and a `RelWithDebInfo` build.
- **Why it matters:** Localization/sensing. TF calibration and DDS/network config are critical for large vehicles/high bandwidth (§7, §20).

#### #2695 — Some launch files are missing parameters
- **What it is:** Bug/feature noting launch files (e.g. `pose_estimator.launch.xml`) use arguments not declared in the file.
- **Root cause / detail:** TIER IV's internal `tier4_*_launch` files rely on **implicit argument forwarding** from parent launches; some argued ROS requires explicit passing, others said internal launches omit args for maintainability.
- **Status / resolution:** Open and stale. No fix; discussion moved to broader launch restructuring with no consensus.
- **Why it matters:** Tooling/launch. Implicit forwarding makes launches hard to read and modules hard to launch standalone (the "parameter scope bleeding" of §22).

#### #10150 — CI: Ccache is too small, causing longer build times
- **What it is:** CI bug that Ccache is capped at 600 MB, yielding <40% hit ratio and slower builds.
- **Root cause / detail:** GitHub public runners lack disk; options debated included remote backends (Redis/Valkey), local cache volumes, larger caches. A full-build cache was measured at only ~0.35 GB, but multiple versions/branches inflate it.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Tracking moved to later issues evaluating Valkey as remote ccache storage; no immediate fix.
- **Why it matters:** CI. Poor cache hit rates lengthen every PR's feedback loop.

#### #5657 — `behavior_planning_container` dies from the start of driving
- **What it is:** Bug in CARLA where `behavior_planning_container` dies with SIGSEGV from the start, preventing trajectory planning.
- **Root cause / detail:** Traced to `behavior_velocity_planner::IntersectionModule::checkCollision`; `polygon.outer().front()` was called on an empty `trimmed_ego_polygon` — undefined behavior.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed and fixed in the latest version via PR #4655.
- **Why it matters:** Planning. An intersection-module crash stops trajectory generation and can halt the vehicle.

#### #6642 — Guardrail deemed an unknown obstacle makes the vehicle stop
- **What it is:** Bug where a guardrail is treated as an unknown obstacle, preventing the vehicle from driving through a corner.
- **Root cause / detail:** Root cause was **localization**: pose init was shifted, NDT worked but the EKF output shifted after initialization while turning. Disabling **yaw-bias estimation** in `ekf_localizer` solved it; compare-map filter also left guardrail points.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Resolved by disabling yaw-bias estimation and checking calibration angles.
- **Why it matters:** Localization/perception. False obstacles caused by pose error can immobilize the vehicle.

#### #9428 — Calculation method of "latency_ms" in multi_object_tracker seems unreasonable
- **What it is:** Analysis/bug that `multi_object_tracker`'s `debug/pipeline_latency_ms` is large and fluctuates, not reflecting true pipeline latency.
- **Root cause / detail:** The debug time is published in `onTimer`, and the metric uses the **oldest/earliest timestamp in the input queue**; delay-compensation extrapolation enlarges it. Naming (`onMessage`, `last_input_stamp_`) was misleading.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Fix PR was tested; resulting pipeline/input latency values looked reasonable.
- **Why it matters:** Tracking diagnostics. The misleading metric could cause teams to misdiagnose tracking latency.

#### #2773 — Analyze and improve compile time with clang
- **What it is:** Feature/task to reduce Autoware's heavy build times using clang `-ftime-trace` and Ninja.
- **Root cause / detail:** Proposed reducing translation-unit size (fewer headers, forward declarations, `extern template`, fewer inline functions). Findings: ~15 s per `create_subscription` and repeated `ament_auto` macro calls duplicating list variables, slowing CMake.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed/stale. Analysis and some PRs produced; upstream `ament_cmake` fixes could not be merged soon.
- **Why it matters:** Developer productivity. Build time affects iteration on planning-heavy packages.

#### #10275 — How to run the YabLoc localization
- **What it is:** Support question about running YabLoc, whose documentation was said to be wrong.
- **Root cause / detail:** Fix was to play the bag with `--clock` and launch with `pose_source:=yabloc control:=false planning:=false`. YabLoc uses GNSS to determine initial position and matches semantic segmentation with a vector map, so PCD coordinates must use a supported projection (e.g. MGRS).
- **Status / resolution:** Closed/resolved. Correct commands identified and shared; docs should be updated.
- **Why it matters:** Localization. YabLoc enables camera/map localization without LiDAR but requires GNSS and correctly projected maps (§11.2).

#### #679 — Implement any missing calibration tools
- **What it is:** Feature/task (sub-ticket) to implement missing sensor calibration tools: camera intrinsics, camera-camera, LiDAR-LiDAR and camera-LiDAR extrinsics.
- **Root cause / detail:** Autocore shared an open-source LiDAR-IMU calibration tool; Leo Drive provided Applinix + Velodyne data; TIER IV shared its tools. Focus shifted to documentation.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Further work moved to `autoware-documentation`; LiDAR-IMU calibration guides merged.
- **Why it matters:** Calibration. Correct extrinsics/intrinsics underpin localization, fusion and sensor integration (§8).

#### #2636 — DevOps Dojo: ROS Node Configuration (Phase 2)
- **What it is:** Process/design task defining how ROS nodes are configured, with a single source of truth in parameter YAML.
- **Root cause / detail:** The team wanted to avoid `declare_parameter` default values so every parameter appears in config, enabling a YAML→Markdown documentation pipeline and hierarchical naming. They evaluated `generate_parameter_library` but leaned away from the dependency.
- **Status / resolution:** Closed. Contribution guide updated to recommend not setting default values.
- **Why it matters:** Configuration consistency and documentation across all nodes.

#### #11720 — Refactoring plan for `autoware_tensorrt_vad`
- **What it is:** Refactoring plan for the newly added `autoware_tensorrt_vad` package, agreed during PR review.
- **Root cause / detail:** ROS 2 types were deeply mixed into application logic, making unit testing difficult (`VadModel` even pulled in `rclcpp` through a logger header). Goals: replace `void` returns, improve error handling, add tests; approach changed to first separate application logic from ROS 2.
- **Status / resolution:** Open and stale. Separation-driven PRs ongoing, no completion.
- **Why it matters:** Perception/end-to-end ML. Better separation/tests improve maintainability and portability.

## Part 3 — What this means for a deployer

1. **Planning, perception and localization are where the bugs live.** Budget QA
   there. (Open bugs: planning 18; and these are the top three components overall.)
2. **30% stale backlog.** A closed or stale label is not proof of correctness for
   *your* configuration; many issues are version/config/sensor specific.
3. **Integration boundaries dominate.** Timing/sync, calibration, launch/parameter
   scope, model-artifact versioning, CUDA/ARM toolchains, DBW/CAN — exactly the
   areas §20, §22 and §28 warn about.
4. **Regressions happen across releases** (#13021). Pin a release, keep a
   replayable regression suite, and test repeated mission lifecycles (§21.4).
5. **Safety-relevant open issues exist** (#13012, #6616, #6919). Define and test
   failure-specific MRMs; do not assume a generic emergency stop is always optimal.
6. **The raw index below is your triage input.** Filter by your components
   (`planning`, `perception`, `localization`, `sensing`, `control`) and by
   `priority:high`, then read the thread before assuming a behavior.

---

> **Purpose:** turn the issue corpus (top ~160 threads read in detail; all 1,136
> indexed) into an actionable map for a developer **and** for the architecture of
> this project. Every failure mode links to the relevant architecture section
> (`autoware-universe-architecture.md`, cited as **§**) and the setup guide
> (`autoware-universe-setup.md`, cited as **§§**). Use it before and during real
> bring-up.

### 5.3 Component checklists (from real failures)

**Planning**
- Verify goal/lanelet map projection and lane connectivity (#3774, #2633, #2364).
- Guard against NaN/empty trajectories and empty-polygon UB; keep the container alive (#2925, #5657, #4505, #1049).
- Test **repeated mission lifecycle**, not one route — 1.8.0 regression (#13021).
- Tune slope so the vehicle can start on grades and stop behind objects (#5391, #5776).
- Check parking with a close NPC and goal shift (#8699, #6844, #2991).

**Perception**
- Confirm point fields/types reach each preprocessor (#3827, #3112).
- Small objects can be filtered out by validators (traffic cones) (#6938).
- Model/TRT version must match source; prebuild engines (#7944, #6461, #1256).
- Ground segmentation must remove ground cleanly without phantom obstacles (#4350, #2213, #669).

**Localization**
- Do not publish identity pose before init; disable dynamic loading for a single PCD (#1421, #3993).
- Validate TF `base_link`↔sensor and GNSS transform direction (#3640, #2597).
- Watch yaw-bias estimation; it fixed some shifts and caused others (#6642).
- Benchmark NDT with a **Release** build (#9599).

**Sensing / middleware**
- Build **Release/RelWithDebInfo**; use composable nodes/zero-copy for cameras/LiDAR (#9599, #1228).
- Verify DDS implementation and networking on multi-machine setups (#4482, #3569).
- Multi-LiDAR scaling needs the upstream `rclcpp` fix (#1009, #2940).

**Control / calibration**
- Calibrate accel/brake maps so stops are accurate (#993).
- Ensure steering converges before moving / while stopped (#1543, §27).
- Command-gate redesign is ongoing (#9235) — pin your version.

### 5.4 Version / regression watchlist

| Issue | Why |
|---|---|
| **#13021** | 1.8.0: `behavior_path_planner` permanently silent after first mission |
| **#13012** | Steering frozen during emergency stop → lane departure mid-corner |
| **#13067 / #13038 / #13023** | BEVFusion/BEVFormer CUDA-arch and model-plugin breakage |
| **#12870** | `system_monitor` crash on a NUL value |
| **#13284 / #13269** | RViz/TensorRT plugin lifecycle UAF/segfault |

### 5.5 Maintenance & process signals

- **30% `status:stale`**, and many high-traffic threads closed **"won't do" /
  no-conclusion** (#7235, #3135, #494, #2633, #1375) — a closed/stale label is not
  proof of correctness for *your* configuration.
- **TVM direction reversed** to TensorRT-only (#2309) — don't build on TVM.
- **Review bottleneck**: a large perception contribution was abandoned for lack of
  reviewers (#7235) — community packages may stall.
- **ROS transitions** (Rolling→Humble→Jazzy) are active and cause API churn
  (#268, #11418, #2782).

### 5.6 E-Trike-specific action list (this project)

1. **Vehicle/TF:** keep `etrike_vehicle_description` geometry truthful; validate
   the single-front-wheel steering frames; verify no duplicate `map→base_link`
   publisher along with NDT (#6677).
2. **Steering:** enforce `max_steer_angle` at all layers and correct sign/units
   (architecture §27; issues #1543, #535).
3. **Single-PCD map:** set `enable_partial_load=false` / disable dynamic loading
   unless the map is tiled ~20 m (#3993, architecture §22).
4. **Localization:** plan for NDT degeneracy with the current IMU stub; add
   monitoring + MRM; watch EKF yaw behavior (#6919, #6642, #1375).
5. **Build:** always `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`; prebuild TensorRT engines
   (#9599, architecture §28).
6. **DDS/containers:** pin `rmw_cyclonedds_cpp`, size receive buffers; expect the
   upstream `rclcpp` component-load fix for multi-sensor (#1009, #2940).
7. **Fail-closed:** ensure a dead planner/localizer triggers stop, not "keep
   following last path" (#1253); keep `topic_state_monitor`/emergency handling on.
8. **Slopes/parking:** tune slope compensation and freespace margins before track
   tests (#5391, #5776, #8699).

### #13354 — refactor(autoware_carla_interface): extract traffic-light coordination glue out of carla_ros.py

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-09-08  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @hakuturu583
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13354

**Body:**

> ### Description
> 
> Follow-up to #13327, which added CARLA traffic-light state publishing to `autoware_carla_interface`. That PR keeps the coordination logic **in-process** inside `carla_ros2_interface` (`carla_ros.py`), which is the right call architecturally: the feature needs live access to the CARLA `world` handle on the synchronous tick (`actor.get_state()` every tick, `world.get_actors()` at resolve time, `map_origin_x/y` shared with the sensor bridge), and `force_green` must run in the world-owning process. Splitting it into a **standalone ROS node** would require a second CARLA client, duplicate connection/config/world-load-ordering plumbing, risk inconsistent snapshots under synchronous mode, and add server load ΓÇö plus an extra `autoware_launch` PR. So a separate node is intentionally *not* the goal here.
> 
> The remaining concern is purely **code organization**: `carla_ros.py` has grown to ~1370 lines, and the traffic-light glue is a self-contained slice of it. The reusable/testable core is already extracted as the ROS-free, unit-tested `modules/traffic_light_matcher.py`; what's left in `carla_ros.py` is thin coordination glue.
> 
> ### Proposed refactor (post-#13327)
> 
> Extract the traffic-light coordination glue out of `carla_ros2_interface` into a helper class, e.g. `modules/traffic_light_publisher.py`, that `carla_ros` owns and drives by passing in the `world` handle / map origin. Candidate methods to move:
> 
> - `_resolve_traffic_light_groups`
> - `_publish_traffic_lights`
> - `_log_traffic_light_match`
> - `_parse_traffic_light_id_override`
> - `_carla_state_to_autoware_color` and the map-frame head-position helper
> 
> This stays **in-process** (no new node, no new `autoware_launch` PR) while shrinking the `carla_ros.py` monolith and giving the traffic-light path its own focused, testable unit.
> 
> ### Notes
> 
> - Do **not** turn this into a separate ROS node ΓÇö see the rationale above.
> - Depends on #13327 being merged first.
>

### #13284 — planning_factor_rviz_plugin: detached worker in start_vehicle_info_request can outlive plugin lifecycle (race / possible UAF)

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-08-27  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @elyforl
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13284

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> `start_vehicle_info_request` launches a detached thread (`std::thread(...).detach()`), which is not lifecycle-bound to the RViz plugin instance.  
> If the plugin is destroyed while the detached worker still runs, the worker may access invalid plugin-owned state, causing race conditions and potential UAF.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> - No worker should outlive plugin-owned state.
> - Shutdown/unload must be deterministic:
>   - stop/cancel in-flight work
>   - wait for completion (or safe cancellation)
> - Repeated triggers must not spawn uncontrolled concurrent workers.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> - In-flight detached worker may continue after plugin teardown begins/completes.
> - Possible access to destroyed members (`this`-owned resources), causing undefined behavior:
>   - sporadic crash
>   - memory safety sanitizer warning
>   - inconsistent internal/UI state
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start RViz with this plugin enabled.
> 2. Trigger `start_vehicle_info_request` repeatedly (manual UI trigger or high-frequency path).
> 3. While requests are in-flight, rapidly:
>    - disable/enable the display, and/or
>    - reload plugin/config, and/or
>    - close RViz.
> 4. Repeat several cycles.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #13269 — autoware_tensorrt_vad: vad_node segfaults on first TF miss (dangling temporary clock in RCLCPP_ERROR_THROTTLE)

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-08-25  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @germanros1987
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13269

**Body:**

> ## Description
> 
> `autoware_tensorrt_vad`'s `CoordinateTransformer::lookup_base2cam()` crashes the whole `vad_node` with SIGSEGV the first time a TF lookup fails, instead of logging the error it was trying to report.
> 
> The catch block passes a *temporary* clock to the throttle macro
> ([`e2e/autoware_tensorrt_vad/lib/coordinate_transformer.cpp:55-57` on `main`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/e2e/autoware_tensorrt_vad/lib/coordinate_transformer.cpp#L55-L57)):
> 
> ```cpp
> } catch (const tf2::TransformException & ex) {
>   RCLCPP_ERROR_THROTTLE(
>     rclcpp::get_logger("autoware_tensorrt_vad"), *rclcpp::Clock::make_shared(), 5000,
>     ...
> ```
> 
> `RCLCPP_ERROR_THROTTLE` binds its `clock` argument to a reference inside the macro expansion and then calls `.now()` on it in a later statement. `*rclcpp::Clock::make_shared()` dereferences a temporary `shared_ptr` whose only reference dies at the end of that first statement ΓÇö C++ lifetime extension does not apply to `*sp` (it is an lvalue referring to the managed object, not a prvalue), so the `Clock` is destroyed before the macro uses it. The subsequent `now()` call is a use-after-free.
> 
> ## Impact
> 
> - Any transient TF miss at startup (e.g. a camera `frame_id` published before the sensor-kit TF tree is complete, or a `frame_id` not present in the URDF) kills the node with exit code -11.
> - Because the crash happens *inside the error path*, the intended "Failed to get TF transformation" message is never printed ΓÇö the node just dies silently, which makes the underlying TF problem unnecessarily hard to diagnose.
> 
> ## Reproduction
> 
> 1. Launch VAD (`use_e2e_planning:=true e2e_planning_type:=vad`) with any camera whose `camera_info.header.frame_id` has no transform from `base_link` (one misnamed frame is enough).
> 2. `vad_node` exits with `process has died ... exit code -11` on the first frame, with no error log.
> 3. Re-running the exact `vad_node` command line from the death message under `gdb -batch -ex run -ex bt` shows the segfault in the clock use inside the throttle macro expansion in `lookup_base2cam`.
> 
> Reproduced on 0.52.0 + the VAD PR (#1685-based setup) with ROS 2 Jazzy; the same code is present on `main` today.
> 
> ## Suggested fix
> 
> Keep a clock alive for the macro, e.g.:
> 
> ```cpp
> } catch (const tf2::TransformException & ex) {
>   static const rclcpp::Clock::SharedPtr error_clock = rclcpp::Clock::make_shared();
>   RCLCPP_ERROR_THROTTLE(
>     rclcpp::get_logger("autoware_tensorrt_vad"), *error_clock, 5000,
>     "Failed to get TF transformation: %s -> %s. Reason: %s", source_frame.c_str(),
>     target_frame.c_str(), ex.what());
>   return std::nullopt;
> }
> ```
> 
> (or plumb the node's clock into `CoordinateTransformer`, which also makes the throttle honor sim time). We have been running the `static` variant in a CARLA-simulator integration and it both stops the crash and surfaces the intended TF error message. Happy to open a PR if the `static` approach is acceptable.
>

### #13207 — Declare the missing dependencies that packages use

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-08-14  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13207

**Body:**

> ## Description
> 
> 195 packages in this repository use a package or a system library that they never declare. The checker found 1061 missing entries: 959 `<depend>` and 102 `<test_depend>`.
> 
> These packages build today only because another declared dependency re-exports the owner, or because some other package installs the system library. That is luck, not correctness. When an unrelated repository stops re-exporting, the package no longer compiles, and the CI of this repository never sees the change.
> 
> - Parent issue: autowarefoundation/autoware#7263
> - The same cleanup in `autoware_core` is complete: autowarefoundation/autoware_core#1355
> 
> ## How each entry was found
> 
> The checker uses three kinds of evidence.
> 
> - An `#include` of a header, resolved against the package that really ships that header.
> - A qualified name such as `rcl_interfaces::msg::ParameterDescriptor` in code, where the header arrives through another dependency. An include scan cannot see this kind.
> - A system library such as Boost, Eigen or PCL, resolved through the compiler search paths, `dpkg`, and the rosdep cache, and named by the rosdep key this workspace already prefers.
> 
> Comments do not count. The checker blanks comments and string literals before it scans, because a Doxygen example is not a use.
> 
> The tag comes from where the dependency is used.
> 
> - `<depend>` when the use sits in an installed header or in code compiled into the library. 959 entries.
> - `<test_depend>` when only `test/` reaches the dependency. 102 entries.
> 
> The checker refuses an entry that would create a dependency cycle. The measurement ran on 2026-08-15, on `main` at 4260f35f2, in a jazzy workspace.
> 
> ## Validation
> 
> These counts are raw checker output. The core rounds reviewed every core entry per package, and the reviews corrected the checker five times. The simulator, e2e and map entries are reviewed, and that review added one entry the checker missed: `tf2` in `tier4_dummy_object_rviz_plugin`. The other components are not reviewed yet.
> 
> Each component gets the same per-package review before its pull request, so the counts here can change.
> 
> ## The entries by component
> 
> The most frequent missing dependencies are `libboost-dev` (67), `lanelet2_core` (57), `std_msgs` (57), `geometry_msgs` (55), and `eigen` (54).
> 
> | Component | Packages | Entries |
> |---|---|---|
> | `planning` | 57 | 501 |
> | `perception` | 48 | 260 |
> | `control` | 19 | 77 |
> | `localization` | 12 | 47 |
> | `visualization` | 12 | 38 |
> | `sensing` | 11 | 37 |
> | `common` | 10 | 33 |
> | `evaluator` | 6 | 25 |
> | `system` | 13 | 21 |
> | `vehicle` | 4 | 10 |
> | `simulator` | 1 | 5 |
> | `e2e` | 1 | 4 |
> | `map` | 1 | 3 |
> | **Total** | **195** | **1061** |
> 
> ## Pull requests
> 
> One pull request per component, opened one at a time, after its review, smallest first. The three smallest components share one pull request. `planning` is large, and it can split into several pull requests.
> 
> - [x] simulator, e2e and map, in one pull request: #13209
> - [x] vehicle: #13208
> - [x] system https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/13217
> - [x] evaluator https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/13218
> - [ ] common
> - [ ] sensing
> - [ ] visualization
> - [ ] localization
> - [ ] control
> - [ ] perception
> - [ ] planning
> 
> ## Definition of done
> 
> - Every reviewed entry is present in the `package.xml` of its package, with the tag given.
> - A build of the changed packages and their reverse-dependency closure stays clean.
> 
> Adding a `<depend>` cannot break a build, so this work carries no risk to the packages themselves.
> 
> ---
> 
> Written with Claude Code. The entries come from the checker that produced the core list, and a per-package review runs before each pull request.
> 

---

### #13173 — autoware_carla_interface in the pre-built humble Docker image is missing the `modules` Python subpackage and calibration map CSVs

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-08-13  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @Chelvy
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13173

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In the pre-built Docker image `ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:latest-humble-autoware-universe-cuda-amd64` (pulled 2026-08-12), the installed `autoware_carla_interface` package is broken in two independent ways:
> 
> 1. **The entire `autoware_carla_interface.modules` Python subpackage is missing** from `/opt/autoware/lib/python3.10/site-packages/autoware_carla_interface/`. Only the top-level modules (`carla_autoware.py`, `carla_ros.py`, etc.) are installed; the `modules/` directory (`carla_data_provider.py`, `carla_utils.py`, `carla_wrapper.py`, `sensor_manager.py`, ΓÇª) is absent. Launching the interface fails immediately with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'autoware_carla_interface.modules'`.
> 
> 2. **The calibration map CSVs are missing** from `/opt/autoware/share/autoware_carla_interface/`. The shipped `config/raw_vehicle_cmd_converter.param.yaml` references
> 
>    ```yaml
>    csv_path_accel_map: $(find-pkg-share autoware_carla_interface)/accel_map.csv
>    csv_path_brake_map: $(find-pkg-share autoware_carla_interface)/brake_map.csv
>    csv_path_steer_map: $(find-pkg-share autoware_carla_interface)/steer_map.csv
>    ```
> 
>    but none of the three CSVs (from `calibration_maps/` in the source tree) are present in the image, so the `raw_vehicle_cmd_converter` node dies at startup with `Accel map is invalid`.
> 
> Notably, the rest of the package **is** installed: the launch file, the config YAMLs, and the top-level Python files are all there, and the package is registered in the ament index. So the omissions look like a packaging/pipeline artifact rather than a missing package.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> `ros2 launch autoware_carla_interface autoware_carla_interface.launch.xml` starts inside the container using only the files shipped in the image:
> 
> - `python3 -c "import autoware_carla_interface.modules.carla_wrapper"` succeeds.
> - `accel_map.csv`, `brake_map.csv`, `steer_map.csv` exist in `$(ros2 pkg prefix --share autoware_carla_interface)/`, so `raw_vehicle_cmd_converter` can load them.
> 
> This matches what the source tree's `CMakeLists.txt` installs at both `main` and `humble` (`ament_python_install_package(${PROJECT_NAME} PACKAGE_DIR src/${PROJECT_NAME})` and `install(DIRECTORY calibration_maps/ DESTINATION share/${PROJECT_NAME}/)`), so a from-source build does not have this problem ΓÇö only the pre-built image does.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> 1. Launch fails immediately:
> 
>    ```
>    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'autoware_carla_interface.modules'
>    ```
> 
>    and indeed:
> 
>    ```
>    $ ls /opt/autoware/lib/python3.10/site-packages/autoware_carla_interface/
>    __init__.py  carla_autoware.py  carla_ros.py  multi_camera_combiner_node.py  ...
>    # no modules/ directory
>    ```
> 
> 2. After working around (1) by bind-mounting `modules/` from a source checkout, the pipeline gets further but `raw_vehicle_cmd_converter` exits with:
> 
>    ```
>    Accel map is invalid.
>    ```
> 
>    and indeed:
> 
>    ```
>    $ ls /opt/autoware/share/autoware_carla_interface/
>    config  launch  package.xml ...
>    # no accel_map.csv / brake_map.csv / steer_map.csv
>    ```
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Observed via Apptainer/Singularity on an HPC cluster, but the missing files are in the image itself, so Docker shows the same thing.
> 
> 1. `docker pull ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:latest-humble-autoware-universe-cuda-amd64` (or `apptainer pull` the same reference).
> 2. Inspect the installed package ΓÇö both checks fail:
> 
>    ```bash
>    docker run --rm ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:latest-humble-autoware-universe-cuda-amd64 \
>      ls /opt/autoware/lib/python3.10/site-packages/autoware_carla_interface/modules
>    docker run --rm ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:latest-humble-autoware-universe-cuda-amd64 \
>      ls /opt/autoware/share/autoware_carla_interface/accel_map.csv
>    ```
> 
> 3. Or reproduce at launch time (CARLA server not required to hit the first error ΓÇö the import fails before anything connects):
> 
>    ```bash
>    apptainer exec <image>.sif bash -c \
>      "source /opt/autoware/setup.bash && ros2 launch autoware_carla_interface autoware_carla_interface.launch.xml"
>    # -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'autoware_carla_interface.modules'
>    ```
> 
> 4. Bind-mount `simulator/autoware_carla_interface/src/autoware_carla_interface/modules` from an `autoware_universe` checkout into the site-packages path and relaunch (with a CARLA 0.9.15 server up) ΓåÆ `raw_vehicle_cmd_converter` dies with `Accel map is invalid`.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (container); host: Rocky Linux HPC node via Apptainer
> - ROS 2: Humble
> - Autoware: `ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:latest-humble-autoware-universe-cuda-amd64`, pulled 2026-08-12
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The package source is fine: at both `main` and `humble`, `simulator/autoware_carla_interface/CMakeLists.txt` installs the Python package recursively and the calibration maps, and `src/autoware_carla_interface/modules/__init__.py` exists. So the loss appears to happen in the image build/packaging pipeline that produces `/opt/autoware`, not in the package itself.
> 
> One observation that may help: the package migrated from `build_type: ament_python` to `ament_cmake` in #11706 (Feb 2026). The old `ament_python` `setup.py` used `find_packages()` + build-time `glob("calibration_maps/*.csv")` for its data files. If the image pipeline still builds (or caches) the package via the old setup.py path ΓÇö or was built from a snapshot mid-migration ΓÇö that would produce exactly this partial install (top-level modules and launch/config present, `modules/` subpackage and CSVs absent).
> 
> If this actually belongs in the `autowarefoundation/autoware` repo (where the Docker images are built), feel free to transfer it.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> Workaround that makes the shipped image usable without modifying it ΓÇö bind-mount the missing files from a source checkout of `autoware_universe` (`simulator/autoware_carla_interface/`):
> 
> - `src/autoware_carla_interface/modules` ΓåÆ `/opt/autoware/lib/python3.10/site-packages/autoware_carla_interface/modules`
> - `calibration_maps/accel_map.csv`, `brake_map.csv`, `steer_map.csv` ΓåÆ `/opt/autoware/share/autoware_carla_interface/`
> 
> With those two mounts (plus a `carla==0.9.15` client on `PYTHONPATH`), the interface launches and exchanges sensor/vehicle topics with a CARLA 0.9.15 server normally.
>

### #13172 — image_projection_based_fusion: "Still initializing camera projector" log persists. Dangling reference.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-08-13  |  **Closed:** 2026-08-26  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:perception
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13172

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> #### Symptom
> 
> The `Still initializing camera projector for ROI N... please wait...` warning keeps being printed **repeatedly and indefinitely**, even after `Camera projector initialization for ROI N finished.` has been logged. In some environments a single stray line appears after `finished`; in others the false warning never stops. Example:
> 
> ```
> [WARN] ... Still initializing camera projector for ROI 1... please wait...
> [INFO] ... Camera projector initialization for ROI 1 finished.
> [WARN] ... Still initializing camera projector for ROI 1... please wait...   <-- keeps repeating forever
> [WARN] ... Still initializing camera projector for ROI 1... please wait...
> ...
> ```
> 
> #### Why this is real harm (not cosmetic)
> 
> Please read the "Possible Causes" part first to understand the real harm hidden behind the false warning messages.
> 
> - The loop condition reads **freed stack memory**; the value is arbitrary. Observed outcomes range from one extra line to a thread that never exits.
> - A never-exiting thread is **leaked** (one per ROI) and keeps spinning while dereferencing freed memory.
> - The lambda also captures `this` by pointer. If the node is destroyed while such a thread is still running, `this->get_logger()` / `rclcpp::ok()` become **use-after-free**, which can crash.
>   - In my experience, a few processes of Autoware crashes on termination. This can be one of the causes.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The warning messages `[WARN] ... Still initializing camera projector for ROI N... please wait...` should stop after the message `[INFO] ... Camera projector initialization for ROI N finished.`
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Sometimes, the false messages keep being logged forever. Sometimes not.
> The environment may affect the probability of reproduction.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Start up Autoware and check the log.
> 
> #### Reproduced on
> 
> `roi_pointcloud_fusion`; the code path is shared by all fusion nodes (`pointpainting_fusion`, `roi_cluster_fusion`, `roi_detected_object_fusion`, `segment_pointcloud_fusion`).
> 
> #### Possible platform dependency
> I personally observed this problem on NVIDIA Drive Thor (arm64 CPU, ROS2 Jazzy, Ubuntu 24.04).
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 24.04
> - ROS2: Jazzy
> - Autoware: Any recent versions after [PR chore(image_projection_based_fusion): add initializing status log- #11112](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11112)
> - Hardware: NVIDIA Drive Thor (arm64 CPU with Thor SoC)
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> #### Cause
> 
> **Package:** `autoware_image_projection_based_fusion`
> **File:** `src/fusion_node.cpp` ΓÇö `FusionNode::camera_info_callback` (approx. L265ΓÇô291)
> 
> In `camera_info_callback`, the progress flag is a **stack-local** `std::atomic<bool> initializing` captured **by reference** into a **detached** thread:
> 
> ```cpp
> std::atomic<bool> initializing{true};
> std::thread([this, &initializing, rois_id]() {
>   rclcpp::Rate rate(1.0);
>   while (rclcpp::ok() && initializing.load()) {
>     RCLCPP_WARN(this->get_logger(), "Still initializing camera projector for ROI %zu... please wait...", rois_id);
>     rate.sleep();
>   }
> }).detach();
> ...
> initializing = false;   // set right before the callback returns
> ```
> 
> The logger thread sleeps up to 1 s between checks. When `initialize()` finishes, the callback sets `initializing = false` and returns ΓÇö at which point the stack-local `initializing` **goes out of scope and is destroyed while the detached thread is still alive**. From then on the thread evaluates `initializing.load()` on a destroyed object: a dangling reference, i.e. **undefined behavior**. Depending on how that stack memory is subsequently reused, the read may keep returning a stale/non-zero value, so the loop never terminates and the warning is printed forever.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> #### Possible fixes
> 
> 1. **Share the flag's ownership** ΓÇö make it `std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>>` and capture it **by value**.
>    - *Pros:* minimal change; the flag now outlives the thread, so the loop terminates correctly; no new members.
>    - *Cons:* still a detached thread capturing `this`; the node-lifetime use-after-free window (see above) remains, and shutdown stays non-deterministic.
> 
> 2. **Make the thread joinable and join it**, signaling completion via a `std::condition_variable` for immediate wakeup.
>    - *Pros:* deterministic lifetime ΓÇö no dangling flag, no dangling `this`, no leaked threads, no stray logs; stops immediately instead of after up to 1 s.
>    - *Cons:* slightly more code (mutex + condition_variable + `join()`); the thread handle must be owned somewhere.
> 
> 3. **Drop the dedicated thread entirely** ΓÇö log once before/after initialization, and (if progress output during a long cache build is desired) emit it from a ROS wall timer instead.
>    - *Pros:* removes the whole class of thread-lifetime/undefined-behavior problems; simplest and safest; no concurrency to reason about.
>    - *Cons:* loses the 1 Hz "still alive" heartbeat unless a timer is added; changes current logging behavior slightly.
>  
> 4. **1+2: Share the flag's ownership and join the thread after setting "initializing" to "false"**
>     - *Pros:* small change, not minimal. no `std::condition_variable`. `this` is guaranteed to be valid until the thread is joined.
>     - *Cons:* The main thread have to wait for finish of the thread (max. 1 second).

**Comments:**

###### @badai-nguyen (2026-08-14)

> @nishikawa-masaki thank you for your investigation and raising the issue, 
> IMO, since the initializing process normally take only max few ten seconds for each camera, it is acceptable to drop the 1Hz logging message and focus on a simple and safe solution. 
> That said, I prefer solution 3 for this issue.  
> cc @technolojin 

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2026-08-14)

> @badai-nguyen
> cc: @technolojin 
> 
> Thank you for your investigation. As I'm not familiar with perception, let me ask you a question.
> 
> > since the initializing process normally take only max few ten seconds for each camera,
> 
> Doesn't it mean that the later initialization will be delayed for (10-30 * number_of_cameras) seconds?
> If it will, I'm afraid that the total delay is too much.
> If it won't, I think the solution 3 is OK.
> 
> I listed the "possible solutions" because I was not able to judge which one is the best.

### #13146 — RingOutlierFilterComponent `azimuth_diff` threshold is wrong

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-08-04  |  **Closed:** 2026-08-07  |  **Author:** @mojomex
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13146

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> ```cpp
>         azimuth_diff < 1.0 * (180.0 / M_PI)) {  // one degree
>         continue;                               // Determined to be included in the same walk
> ```
> should be
> 
> ```cpp
>         azimuth_diff < 1.0 * (M_PI / 180.0)) {  // one degree
>         continue;                               // Determined to be included in the same walk
> ```
> 
> In the CUDA version, this is already correct:
> 
> ```cpp
>       azimuth_diff < 1.f * M_PI / 180.f) {
>       // Determined to be included in the same walk
> ```
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Azimuth diff threshold is `1 deg`
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> It's actually `3283 deg`
>

### #13093 — Move node autoware system design files to each node packages.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-07-30  |  **Closed:** 2026-08-17  |  **Author:** @technolojin
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13093

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The autoware system designer and the design files are introduced https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/6760.
> 
> 
> distribute node design files to each node packages.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> 
> distribute node design files from a common package https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/tree/main/common/autoware_universe_designs to each node packages
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> PRs will be created per each components.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Distribute node design files to each node packages.
> remove [autoware_universe_designs](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/tree/main/common/autoware_universe_designs) package

**Comments:**

###### @technolojin (2026-07-30)

> 12 draft PRs are open, one per component. Each is a **pure file move** ΓÇö every file is an `R100` rename, so all PRs show `+0 ΓêÆ0`. Destination is the existing in-package convention `<package>/design/<Name>.node.yaml`; no `CMakeLists.txt`, `package.xml`, or CI change is required.
> 
> ### PRs
> 
> | PR | Component | Packages | Files |
> |:---|:---|---:|---:|
> | #13105 | sensing | 12 | 39 |
> | #13104 | perception | 22 | 30 |
> | #13103 | system | 16 | 25 |
> | #13102 | planning | 19 | 24 |
> | #13101 | localization | 13 | 21 |
> | #13100 | control | 17 | 18 |
> | #13099 | evaluator | 7 | 10 |
> | #13098 | vehicle | 4 | 4 |
> | #13097 | common | 3 | 3 |
> | #13096 | simulator | 2 | 2 |
> | #13095 | e2e | 1 | 1 |
> | #13094 | map | 1 | 2 |
> 
> Together these move **179 files across 117 packages**. The PRs touch disjoint file sets and cannot conflict with each other, so they can be reviewed and merged in any order. Each PR body lists the destination package and code owners for every file.
> 
> - [x] #13094
> - [x] #13095
> - [ ] #13096
> - [x] #13097
> - [ ] #13098
> - [ ] #13099
> - [ ] #13100
> - [ ] #13101
> - [ ] #13102
> - [ ] #13103
> - [ ] #13104
> - [ ] #13105
> 
> ### Why the move matters beyond tidiness
> 
> `autoware_system_designer` resolves a design file's owning package from the nearest ancestor `package.xml`, overridden only by a `launch.package` key (`collect_system_design_manifests.py`). The centralized files declare a top-level `package:` block instead, so **all of them are currently attributed to `autoware_universe_designs`** in `share/autoware_system_designer/resource/_package_map.yaml`. Moving each file into its implementing package fixes that attribution, and routes review of node interface changes to each node's own code owners.
> 
> ### Remaining before `autoware_universe_designs` can be removed
> 
> 10 files cannot be moved within this repository:
> 
> | File | Reason | Destination |
> |:---|:---|:---|
> | `design/common/ServiceLogChecker.node.yaml` | package retired in #13002 | delete |
> | `design/planning/behavior/BehaviorVelocityPlanner.node.yaml` | package now in core | `autoware_core` |
> | `design/planning/behavior/PathGenerator.node.yaml` | package now in core | `autoware_core` |
> | `design/planning/common/VelocitySmoother.node.yaml` | package now in core | `autoware_core` |
> | `design/planning/motion/MotionVelocityPlanner.node.yaml` | package now in core | `autoware_core` |
> | `design/localization/autoware_pose_initializer/PoseInitializer.node.yaml` | package now in core | `autoware_core` |
> | `design/sensing/autoware_gnss_poser/GnssPoser.node.yaml` | package now in core | `autoware_core` |
> | `design/sensing/autoware_vehicle_velocity_converter/VehicleVelocityConverter.node.yaml` | package now in core | `autoware_core` |
> | `design/simulator/autoware_simple_planning_simulator/SimplePlanningSimulator.node.yaml` | separate repository | `autoware_simple_planning_simulator` |
> | `design/planning/parking/Parking.module.yaml` | module, has no implementing package | `autoware_launch` ΓÇö `autoware_sample_designs/design/module/planning/` (next to `ScenarioPlanning.module.yaml`, which references `entity: Parking.module`) |
> 
> - [ ] `autoware_core` PR (7 files)
> - [ ] `autoware_simple_planning_simulator` PR (1 file)
> - [ ] `autoware_launch` PR (`Parking.module.yaml`)
> - [ ] delete retired `ServiceLogChecker.node.yaml`
> - [ ] remove the `autoware_universe_designs` package (only external reference is `.github/CODEOWNERS`, which is regenerated automatically)
>

- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13086

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> - for centerpoint, split variant to sub-folders
> - for ml models general, remove model name from file names. containing folder is self-explained.
> - all the artifact files to be described in `ml_package.param.yaml`

> ### Purpose
>

### #13067 — BEVFusion does not work on Cuda compute capability 12.0 series Nvidia cards

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-07-24  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @predrag12
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13067

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> BEVFusion node does not work on either Nvidia Blackwell or Ampere micro architecture cards. On Blackwell, bevfusion_camera_lidar.onnx cannot be compiled, and on Ampere, node initializes but doesn't run detection. Both are on official autoware:universe-devel-cuda container and 570.172.08 driver, same for release and debug build.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> On Blackwell, expected behavior is to be able to compile the bevfusion_camera_lidar.onnx, and once compiled initialize the node.
> On Ampere, expected behavior is that there is a sample rodbag and be able to run Lidar and camera detection.
> 
> ### Actual behavior

> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. docker pull ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-devel-cuda
> 2. docker run -it --shm-size=8gb --gpus all ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-devel-cuda bash
> 3. nvidia-smi
> 4. ansible-playbook autoware.dev_env.download_artifacts -e "data_dir=$HOME/autoware_data"
> 5. source /opt/autoware/setup.bash
> 6. vi /opt/autoware/share/autoware_bevfusion/launch/bevfusion.launch.xml, line 5 remove /ml_models, line 6 change bevfusion_lidar to bevfusion_camera_lidar
> 7. ros2 launch autoware_bevfusion bevfusion.launch.xml
> 8. in separate window, docker ps -a, docker exec -ti <NAME> bash
> 9. ros2 bag play /t4_sample_0/rosbag2/sample_bag --loop
> 10. (before step 7, in /autoware, could build debug from source)
>

> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5
> - ROS2: humble
> - Autoware: April 13 or built debug from main
> - Cuda driver: 570.172.08
> - RAM: GPU 48-96GB, CPU 32GB
>

> On Blackwell, possibly make files not configured for Cuda 12.8 and cuda capability 12.0
> On Ampere, c/c++ files do not account for regular xyzi point clouds and github does not provide sample public xyzirc dataset or shared rosbag for testing. Is there a compatible dataset or rosbag, or which parts of the code can be changed to work with regular xyzi point cloud?
