### #13025 — Fix output topic name in yabloc_pose_initializer README

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-07-20  |  **Closed:** 2026-07-22  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:documentation, component:localization
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13025

**Body:**

> ## Summary
> 
> The README of `localization/yabloc/yabloc_pose_initializer` documents the publication `output/candidates` ([README line 58](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/localization/yabloc/yabloc_pose_initializer/README.md?plain=1#L58)), but the node publishes the `MarkerArray` on `~/debug/init_candidates` ([`src/camera/marker_module.cpp` line 27](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/localization/yabloc/yabloc_pose_initializer/src/camera/marker_module.cpp#L27)), which the launch file remaps to `init_candidates` ([`launch/yabloc_pose_initializer.launch.xml` line 11](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/localization/yabloc/yabloc_pose_initializer/launch/yabloc_pose_initializer.launch.xml#L11)), resolving at runtime to `/localization/pose_estimator/yabloc/initializer/init_candidates`. Anyone following the README and subscribing to `output/candidates` gets no data.
> 
> Found while cross-checking package documentation during the ML artifact hosting migration.
> 
> ## Details
> 
> - The mismatch has existed since the package was introduced in #3946 (2023-06-22): the initial commit already used `~/debug/init_candidates` in code while the initial README listed `output/candidates`, and no rename ever happened (verified via `git log --follow`).
> - All other README rows were cross-checked against the source and are correct (`input/camera_info`, `input/image_raw`, `input/vector_map`, and the `yabloc_align_srv` service).
> 
> ## Suggested fix
> 
> Change the Output table row to `debug/init_candidates`, keeping the package convention of listing topic names without the `~/` prefix as declared in code before launch remapping.
> 

**Comments:**

###### @KYabuuchi (2026-07-22)

> @xmfcx  Thank you for catching this mismatch. I'll fix it soon.

---

### #13024 — Sync lidar_frnet OT128 ML package config with the released frnet/v2 artifact

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-07-20  |  **Closed:** 2026-07-27  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:perception
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13024

**Body:**

> ## Summary
> 
> [`perception/autoware_lidar_frnet/config/ml_package_frnet_ot128.param.yaml` line 67](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/perception/autoware_lidar_frnet/config/ml_package_frnet_ot128.param.yaml#L67) sets `num_points` to `[5000, 60000, 160000]`, but the released `frnet/v2` artifact (pinned by autowarefoundation/autoware ansible, sha256 `96de220d...`; [byte-identical Hugging Face mirror, line 67](https://huggingface.co/AutowareFoundation/lidar_frnet/blob/v2.0/ml_package_frnet_ot128.param.yaml#L67)) sets `[5000, 80000, 160000]`. The QT128 copies are identical on both sides.
> 
> Found while checksum-validating the ML artifacts against the in-repo configs during the artifact hosting migration.
> 
> ## Details
> 
> - The package copy never contained 80000: #12000 introduced the ot128/qt128 split with opt 60000 (a late branch commit raised max to 160000 but kept opt 60000), while the v2 artifact carrying opt 80000 was pinned by autowarefoundation/autoware#6928; both merged 2026-03-24 within a minute of each other, so the final tuning landed in the artifact only.
> - No runtime impact with the default launch: [`launch/lidar_frnet.launch.xml` line 15](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/perception/autoware_lidar_frnet/launch/lidar_frnet.launch.xml#L15) loads `ml_package_param_path` from the artifact directory, and `num_points` opt only sets the TensorRT optimization-profile kOPT dimension ([`lib/lidar_frnet.cpp` lines 49-64](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/perception/autoware_lidar_frnet/lib/lidar_frnet.cpp#L49-L64)); min/max, frame gating, and buffer sizing are unaffected. The divergence only bites users who override `ml_package_param_path` to the package copy (engine tuned for the wrong typical point count plus a forced engine rebuild) or who read the repo copy as documentation of the shipped model.
> 
> ## Suggested fix
> 
> One-line change: set `num_points` to `[5000, 80000, 160000]` in `config/ml_package_frnet_ot128.param.yaml` to match the shipped v2 artifact. Optionally note in the package docs that `config/ml_package_*.param.yaml` are reference copies and the artifact yaml is the runtime source of truth.
> 
> cc @amadeuszsz
> 

---

### #13023 — Make the bevfusion config files match the released model

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-07-20  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:perception
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13023

**Body:**

> ## Summary
> 
> The in-package config files of `autoware_bevfusion` now describe a 7-class model. The two new classes, `TRAFFIC_CONE` and `BARRIER`, map to `Label::HAZARD`. The `detection_class_remapper` matrix grew from 8x8 to 10x10.
> 
> The released BEVFusion artifacts are still the 5-class `t4base_120m/v2` files that the `autoware` repository pins. No public 7-class model exists. The v3 URL `https://awf.ml.dev.web.auto/perception/models/bevfusion/t4base_120m/v3/` returns 403. The live v2 `ml_package` files still list 5 entries in `class_names`.
> 
> - Config update that introduced the 7-class values: #12732
> - Current artifact pin (5-class `t4base_120m/v2`): autowarefoundation/autoware#6615
> 
> I found this mismatch while I compared the checksums of the ML artifacts with the in-package config files during the artifact hosting migration.
> 
> ## Details
> 
> - [`config/ml_package_bevfusion_lidar.param.yaml` line 3](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/perception/autoware_bevfusion/config/ml_package_bevfusion_lidar.param.yaml#L3) and [`config/ml_package_bevfusion_camera_lidar.param.yaml` line 3](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/perception/autoware_bevfusion/config/ml_package_bevfusion_camera_lidar.param.yaml#L3) list 7 classes. The released v2 artifacts list 5 classes. The Hugging Face mirror holds byte-identical copies of the pinned files: [lidar line 3](https://huggingface.co/AutowareFoundation/bevfusion/blob/v2.0/ml_package_bevfusion_lidar.param.yaml#L3), [camera_lidar line 3](https://huggingface.co/AutowareFoundation/bevfusion/blob/v2.0/ml_package_bevfusion_camera_lidar.param.yaml#L3). Their sha256 values `866265b9...` and `50707efc...` match the ansible pins. The class list is the only difference between the in-package config files and the released v2 artifacts.
> - The in-package [`config/detection_class_remapper.param.yaml`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/perception/autoware_bevfusion/config/detection_class_remapper.param.yaml) is 10x10. The [released v2 artifact](https://huggingface.co/AutowareFoundation/bevfusion/blob/v2.0/detection_class_remapper.param.yaml) is 8x8.
> - Runtime behavior with the default launch is correct. [`launch/bevfusion.launch.xml` line 12](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/perception/autoware_bevfusion/launch/bevfusion.launch.xml#L12) loads `ml_package_param_path` from `$(var model_path)`, the downloaded artifact directory, not from the package share directory. The node never reads the extra 7-class entries in the package-share `bevfusion_lidar.param.yaml`. [`postprocess_kernel.cu` line 70](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/perception/autoware_bevfusion/lib/postprocess/postprocess_kernel.cu#L70) indexes `yaw_norm_thresholds` by model label, and a model label is always less than `num_classes`. [`bevfusion_node.cpp` lines 137-139](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/perception/autoware_bevfusion/src/bevfusion_node.cpp#L137-L139) declare `min_confidence_scores` only for the names in `class_names_`. The in-package config files are reference files, and they currently describe a model that is not public.
> - Related: the package [README lines 75-80](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/43019199249092ae7ea8cda8ac476330156ba863/perception/autoware_bevfusion/README.md?plain=1#L75-L80) still links the `t4base_120m/v1` artifacts, one version behind the pinned v2.
> 
> ## Suggested fix
> 
> There are two possible fixes:
> 
> - Publish the 7-class model, for example as `t4base_120m/v3`, together with a companion autowarefoundation/autoware PR that updates the artifact pins.
> - Revert the in-package `ml_package` files and the remapper file to the released v2 content until that model ships. A comment in each file that names the target model version is an alternative to a revert.
> 
> Independently, update the README links from v1 to the pinned version.
> 
> - Related: #12732
> - Parent issue for HAZARD label support: autowarefoundation/autoware#7137
> 
> cc @a-maumau
> 
> AI usage: drafted with Claude Code from a checksum comparison of the artifacts against the in-package config files, then edited by hand.
> 

**Comments:**

###### @xmfcx (2026-08-14)

> @a-maumau -san, could you take a look at this issue?

###### @xmfcx (2026-09-01)

> I think https://huggingface.co/AutowareFoundation/bevfusion/discussions/1 was opened for this task although it is empty for now.

###### @a-maumau (2026-09-03)

> @xmfcx sorry for taking long time ≡ƒÖÅ. I will update the models and paramters after models are ready to publish.
>

### #13021 — [1.8.0 regression] behavior_path_planner permanently silent after first completed mission ΓÇö works correctly in 1.7.1

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-07-17  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @507twm
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13021

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> After completing one mission and re-initializing localization, the
> behavior path planner never plans again for the lifetime of the process:
> a new route is accepted (route state `SET`, system state `PLANNING`), all
> inputs flow normally, but the planner publishes no path and writes no
> error or warning to any log. Every subsequent mission requires a full
> stack restart.
> 
> This is a **regression**: under identical conditions (same host, same
> simulator, same map, same routes, same test harness), Autoware **1.7.1
> completes consecutive missions in one process without issue**; 1.8.0
> fails deterministically after the first.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The route is planned and the vehicle can engage, as in step 2 ΓÇö and as
> 1.7.1 does (we ran five consecutive missions across two process sessions,
> all arrived).
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The route is accepted (`/api/routing/state` = SET, system state PLANNING)
> but the behavior path planner publishes nothing; no ERROR/WARN appears in
> any node log. Engagement then times out. Reproduced **10 out of 10**
> attempts. A related trigger: ~25 route set/clear cycles without any
> driving produce the same permanent silence.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Findings come from an independent, pinned audit environment (all 31
> source repos hash-recorded; two 80-run campaigns ΓÇö one per release ΓÇö
> completed 80/80 with this workaround in place: full stack restart per
> mission). We can attach per-run manifests, rosbags of a failing second
> mission, and route-state/topic-level traces on request.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> | Component | Version |
> |---|---|
> | Autoware | tag 1.8.0, commit `5b27e88e84683deb4afaf0aa917f80082a608871` (fails) / tag 1.7.1 (works) |
> | ROS 2 | Humble |
> | Middleware | CycloneDDS 1.3.4, localhost, stock config |
> | Simulator | AWSIM Labs v1.6.1 official Ubuntu binary, Nishishinjuku map |
> | Launch | `autoware_launch e2e_simulator.launch.xml`, awsim_labs vehicle/sensor models |
> | Host | Ubuntu 22.04.5 bare metal, Ryzen 3700X, RTX 3070, driver 580.159.03 |
> 
> 
> ### Possible causes

### #13012 — Steering is frozen during emergency stop: can cause lane departure when triggered mid-corner

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-07-16  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @ismetatabay
- **Labels:** component:control
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/13012

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> During an emergency stop, vehicle_cmd_gate freezes the lateral (steering) command at the value that was active at the moment the emergency was triggered, while only the longitudinal command is driven to a stop. If the emergency is triggered while the vehicle is entering or negotiating a curve ΓÇö before the steering angle has fully developed ΓÇö the frozen angle no longer matches the path curvature. Because the vehicle keeps moving for the whole stopping distance, the lateral deviation grows and, in the worst case, the vehicle can drift out of its lane before it comes to rest.
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> When an emergency stop is triggered, the vehicle should keep following the planned path laterally while it decelerates, so that it comes to a stop within its lane. The steering command should continue to track the trajectory (as the trajectory follower keeps producing valid commands during the emergency) rather than being frozen at the angle that happened to be active at the moment of activation. This is especially important when the emergency is triggered mid-corner, where a frozen steering angle causes the vehicle to drift out of the lane during the stopping distance.
> 
> ---
> Is freezing the steering during an emergency stop an intentional design decision, and if so, what is the rationale?
> 
> A few possibilities I can think of:
> - Hold-the-wheel is safe and predictable when the emergency is triggered on a straight, and simpler than trusting a controller that may itself be part of the failure.
> - During certain fail-safe conditions (e.g. the trajectory follower or its inputs are unreliable) the last-known steering is the only value that can be trusted.
> 
> If one of these is the reason, that argues for keeping the freeze as the default and making the "keep tracking" behavior opt-in ΓÇö which is what I propose below.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Both emergency paths in vehicle_cmd_gate freeze the lateral command:
> 
> 1. System emergency (MRM), in publishControlCommands()
> ```bash
> if (use_emergency_handling_ && is_system_emergency_) {
>   filtered_control = emergency_commands_.control;   // full replacement, incl. lateral
> }
> ```
> The emergency_commands_.control come from the MRM emergency stop operator, whose calcTargetAcceleration() modifies only the longitudinal fields and copies the lateral command unchanged from the last command received before the MRM started. As a result the steering angle is effectively frozen for the duration of the maneuver.
> 
> 2. External emergency stop, in createEmergencyStopControlCmd()
> ```bash
> cmd.lateral.steering_tire_angle          = prev_control_cmd_.lateral.steering_tire_angle;
> cmd.lateral.steering_tire_rotation_rate  = prev_control_cmd_.lateral.steering_tire_rotation_rate;
> cmd.longitudinal.velocity     = 0.0;
> cmd.longitudinal.acceleration = emergency_acceleration_;
> ```
> Here prev_control_cmd_ is the last published command before the emergency, and it is not updated while the emergency-stop command is being published, so the steering stays fixed.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. launch vehicle
> 2. Send an emergency command or trigger MRM on curvature
> 3. Observe and record control_cmd output from vehicle_cmd_gate
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #12972 — Consolidate duplicated pointcloud preprocessing in last-resort safety consumers onto a shared perception-independent obstacle grid

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-07-09  |  **Closed:** 2026-08-12  |  **Author:** @youtalk
- **Labels:** component:perception, component:sensing, component:localization, component:planning
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12972

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> About eight planning/control nodes subscribe to the no-ground obstacle-segmentation point cloud (`/perception/obstacle_segmentation/pointcloud`, `sensor_msgs/PointCloud2`) and each re-implements its own preprocessing before answering essentially the same question ΓÇö "is there obstacle evidence within a region around ego or the trajectory, and how close?". At [`085b97a5`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/commit/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85) (a recent `main` snapshot used as the reference below):
> 
> | consumer | raw-cloud preprocessing | key parameters | source |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | `autoware_autonomous_emergency_braking` | path-footprint `CropHull` ΓåÆ voxel ΓåÆ Euclidean clustering ΓåÆ cluster-height gate ΓåÆ convex hull | voxel 0.1/0.1/0.5 m, tolerance 0.15 m, min size 10, height ΓëÑ 0.1 m, z Γêê [0.0, vehicle_height] | [crop](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/control/autoware_autonomous_emergency_braking/src/node.cpp#L954-L985), [cluster](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/control/autoware_autonomous_emergency_braking/src/node.cpp#L879-L920) |
> | `autoware_planning_validator_rear_collision_checker` | x-passthrough ΓåÆ voxel ΓåÆ Euclidean ΓåÆ cluster-height gate | x Γêê [ΓêÆ100, +30] m, voxel 0.1/0.1/0.5 m, tolerance 0.15 m, min size **5**, height ΓëÑ 0.1 m, z Γêê [**0.3**, vehicle_height ΓêÆ 1.0] | [cluster](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/planning/planning_validator/autoware_planning_validator_rear_collision_checker/src/rear_collision_checker.cpp#L329-L343) |
> | `autoware_planning_validator_intersection_collision_checker` | x-passthrough ΓåÆ voxel ΓåÆ Euclidean ΓåÆ relative-height gate | x Γêê ┬▒50 m, voxel **0.2/0.2/0.2** m (min 3 pts/voxel), tolerance **0.5** m, min size 10, height > **0.5** m, z Γêê [**0.5**, vehicle_height + 0.5] | [cluster](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/planning/planning_validator/autoware_planning_validator_intersection_collision_checker/src/intersection_collision_checker.cpp#L537-L556) |
> | `autoware_trajectory_modifier` (ObstacleStop) | trajectory-bbox `CropBox` ΓåÆ voxel ΓåÆ Euclidean ΓåÆ height gate | bbox + 1.0 m (hardcoded), voxel 0.2/0.2/0.2 m (min 3), tolerance 0.5 m, min size 10, height ΓëÑ 0.5 m, z Γêê [**0.2**, vehicle_height + 0.5] | [crop](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/planning/autoware_trajectory_modifier/src/trajectory_modifier_plugins/obstacle_stop.cpp#L490-L498), [cluster](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/planning/autoware_trajectory_modifier/src/trajectory_modifier_utils/obstacle_stop_utils.cpp#L380-L410) |
> | `autoware_collision_detector` | none ΓÇö per-point `boost::geometry::distance` against the ego footprint over the whole cloud | collision_distance 0.1 m | [loop](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/control/autoware_collision_detector/src/node.cpp#L452-L481) |
> | `autoware_surround_obstacle_checker` | none ΓÇö per-point distance to the margin-expanded footprint | per-side surround margins | [loop](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/planning/autoware_surround_obstacle_checker/src/node.cpp#L262-L335) |
> | `autoware_obstacle_collision_checker` | per-point radius filter along the resampled trajectory + point-in-footprint | search_radius 5.0 m, resample 0.3 m | [filter](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/control/autoware_obstacle_collision_checker/src/obstacle_collision_checker.cpp#L49-L64) |
> 
> Beyond the maintenance and summed-compute cost of ~7 copies, there are two structural problems:
> 
> 1. **Parameter drift with no principled resolution.** The four clustering consumers disagree on every axis: voxel leaf (0.1/0.1/0.5 vs 0.2/0.2/0.2), cluster tolerance (0.15 vs 0.5 m), minimum cluster size (5 vs 10), cluster-height gate (0.1 vs 0.5 m), z lower bound (0.0 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5 m), and the ROI definitions differ in kind, not just value (path convex hull vs x-only passthrough vs trajectory bounding box). No single parameter set reproduces the current behaviors.
> 2. **These are last-resort consumers, so the obvious fix is unavailable.** They exist to catch what the perception modeling stack misses, so migrating them to `PredictedObjects` or a perception-produced occupancy grid would couple the backup path to the very stack it backs up. Maintainers raised exactly this objection on the Spheric Collision Detector proposal ([discussion #6456](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/6456)), which consolidates collision checkers but depends on object detection.
> 
> The cost of the status quo is visible in the shipped defaults: several of these pointcloud branches ship disabled ([`use_pointcloud: false`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/control/autoware_collision_detector/config/collision_detector.param.yaml#L3) in collision_detector, [`enable_check: false`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/planning/autoware_surround_obstacle_checker/config/surround_obstacle_checker.param.yaml#L7) for the surround pointcloud belt, [`enable_stop_for_pointcloud: false`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/085b97a56aa25e21f9ec8f6accc05f8860c42c85/planning/autoware_trajectory_modifier/config/trajectory_modifier.param.yaml#L23) in trajectory_modifier). A fail-safe that requires tuning seven bespoke pipelines against false positives tends to stay turned off in practice.
> 
> This issue is the sensing-domain follow-up of the interface-design series in [discussion #7180](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/7180) (component interface versioning): everything else in that design's first wave registers existing boundaries with their existing types; this is the one place a new boundary and component are proposed.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> 1. **Deduplicate**: one shared, stateless preprocessing replaces ~7 per-consumer pipelines ΓÇö one place to maintain, one pass over the cloud instead of seven.
> 2. **Preserve last-resort independence**: the shared producer must consume only the no-ground cloud and the static sensorΓåÆ`base_link` extrinsic ΓÇö no objects, tracking, occupancy, map, trajectory, or localization pose ΓÇö so wrong perception output or a perception-process crash cannot compromise the emergency-stop path.
> 3. **Preserve per-consumer semantics**: no central clustering parameters forced on consumers (the drift matrix above shows why that cannot work).
> 4. **Bound the wire**: a fixed-size, content-independent product suitable for multi-ECU / multi-container deployments where the raw cloud should stay inside its producing fault domain.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> **A ΓÇö one shared clustering producer (cluster / convex-hull array).** The natural first idea: run crop+voxel+cluster once and publish clusters or hulls. It fails on the evidence above: (a) three consumers (collision_detector, surround_obstacle_checker, obstacle_collision_checker) run per-point distance loops and need the raw evidence a hull-vertex array discards; (b) there is no single voxel/tolerance/min-size/z-band parameter set that reproduces the four clustering consumers, so the producer degenerates into per-consumer configurations ΓÇö the duplication moves, it doesn't disappear; (c) the producer inherits the KdTree/Euclidean-clustering cost on the full cloud. In fairness: a cluster array is the smallest possible wire format (KB-class), well below any grid.
> 
> **B ΓÇö one shared 2.5D obstacle grid (proposed).** A stateless `O(N)` single-pass rasterizer (`autoware_obstacle_grid_extractor`) co-located with the no-ground-cloud producer emits a fixed-size multi-layer grid (`grid_map_msgs/GridMap`, layers `max_height` / `min_height` / `point_count` / `low_max_height`, cell 0.2 m, `base_link` frame, stamped with the input-cloud stamp; all-NaN grid = "alive, nothing detected" heartbeat; consumers watchdog the stamp age so staleness reads as "unavailable", never "clear"). Every consumer queries the same grid through a small helper (`autoware_obstacle_grid_utils`) but keeps **its own** gate per cell (`point_count` threshold, height band, own ROI polygon) ΓÇö the grid imposes no clustering parameters, which is exactly what the drift matrix demands. Distance to the nearest occupied cell is edge-aware by construction (cells are areas, not hull vertices) and conservative up to the cell diagonal. The wire is bounded and density-independent: 960,448 B/frame at 60├ù40 m @ 0.2 m with 4 layers, no matter how cluttered the scene, and one grid replaces all ~7 raw-cloud subscriptions. Reuses the existing ETH [grid_map](https://github.com/anybotics/grid_map) dependency; no new Autoware message type.
> 
> ```mermaid
> flowchart LR
>     subgraph BEFORE["Before ΓÇö ~7 duplicated preprocessors"]
>         RAW["no-ground point cloud (content-dependent size @ 10 Hz)"]
>         RAW --> B1["AEB: crop+voxel+cluster+hull"]
>         RAW --> B2["rear / intersection checkers: crop+voxel+cluster"]
>         RAW --> B3["ObstacleStop: crop+voxel+cluster"]
>         RAW --> B4["collision / surround / obstacle checkers: per-point loops"]
>     end
>     subgraph AFTER["After ΓÇö one rasterizer, one shared grid"]
>         RAW2["no-ground point cloud"] -->|"O(N) single pass"| EX["autoware_obstacle_grid_extractor"]
>         EX --> GRID["grid_map_msgs/GridMap (fixed size)"]
>         GRID --> HELP["autoware_obstacle_grid_utils + per-consumer gates"]
>     end
> ```
> 
> **C ΓÇö status quo, per-package cleanups only.** Keeps seven pipelines and the drift; every future safety consumer adds an eighth.
> 
> **Scope notes (what this proposal is _not_):**
> 
> - It does **not** change the normal planning/control path: every `PredictedObjects` branch is untouched; this is only about the pointcloud branches of the last-resort consumers.
> - It proposes a **representation and boundary, not an upstream filter**: the extractor rasterizes whatever obstacle-segmentation cloud it is fed. It composes unchanged with today's rule-based ground removal and equally with class-filtered / semantic-segmentation-based clouds if a deployment adopts them upstream.
> - **No velocity/flow layer is needed.** None of the seven consumers uses per-point velocity or perception-tracked velocity on its pointcloud branch (verified at `085b97a5`): the two that need closing speed (rear / intersection checkers) derive it consumer-side by differentiating their own distance series (low-pass + max-accel clamp, and regression over a distance history, respectively), which works on grid queries exactly as it did on cluster distances.
> - Exclusions: the `motion_velocity_planner` pointcloud path consumes the shared clustering in `autoware_core` (`PlannerData`) and is out of scope to keep this change universe-only; `autoware_costmap_generator` fuses the cloud with map/objects/scenario and stays on the raw cloud.
> 
> ### Implementation status
> 
> To de-risk the discussion, the full proposal is implemented and evaluated on a development fork, staged for upstream submission (Jazzy-first; built and unit-tested green in `autoware:universe-devel-jazzy`):
> 
> | stage | PRs |
> | --- | --- |
> | helper + producer | [youtalk/autoware_universe#2](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/2) (`autoware_obstacle_grid_utils`), [#3](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/3) (`autoware_obstacle_grid_extractor`) |
> | first consumer | [#4](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/4) (AEB pointcloud branch) |
> | remaining consumers | [#6](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/6) collision_detector, [#7](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/7) obstacle_collision_checker, [#8](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/8) surround_obstacle_checker, [#9](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/9) planning_validator intersection, [#10](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/10) planning_validator rear, [#11](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/11) trajectory_modifier ObstacleStop |
> | related decoupling | [#12](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/12) spheric_collision_detector dead pointcloud path removal, [#13](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_universe/pull/13) AEB raw-IMU decoupling (yaw rate from `kinematic_state`) |
> | launch integration | [youtalk/autoware_launch#1](https://github.com/youtalk/autoware_launch/pull/1) (extractor beside ground segmentation; consumers repointed) |
> 
> Evaluation on real vehicle data (8├ù LiDAR), replaying against faithful reimplementations of the pre-migration pipelines on byte-identical inputs:
> 
> - **Never anti-conservative on the radial query**: 890/890 frames, the grid's nearest-obstacle distance is never farther than the nearest raw point; error bounded by the cell diagonal (Γëñ 0.26 m @ 0.2 m).
> - **End-to-end parity**: no-ground cloud regenerated from raw LiDAR packets through the actual nebula ΓåÆ `autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor` ΓåÆ `autoware_ground_segmentation` chain (301 frames, ~480 k pts/frame): 301/301 detection parity with the legacy AEB pipeline, zero missed and zero ghost detections; `extract()` p99 6.4 ms vs legacy preprocessing mean 100.5 ms on the same clouds (~20├ù).
> - **Six-consumer wave**: ~3,900 frames across nine bags (dense urban, controlled stop tests, a genuine rear run-out): zero decision-relevant anti-conservative frames; the rear checker flags the run-out intruder ~8 m earlier than the legacy cluster-hopping distance series.
> - **Wire**: measured serialized `GridMap` is density-independent (byte-identical empty vs full) at 960,448 B/frame (60├ù40 m); a dense-urban no-ground cloud averages ~2 MiB/frame and scales with the scene.
> - Two engineering findings are reported, not tuned away, in the consumer PRs: the shared gate's `min_height = 0` acts as a z-gate on sub-ground returns (documented semantics), and the ObstacleStop point-tracker interacts with the dense cell-center lattice (12/2,086 frames, feature default-off; remediation options listed in the PR).
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac9819b0-ba8a-4fd5-afcb-fe4ea62c99bf
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Maintainers agree on the representation (approach B or an amended alternative) and the staged migration order below.
> - [ ] `autoware_obstacle_grid_utils` and `autoware_obstacle_grid_extractor` merged.
> - [ ] AEB pointcloud-branch migration merged.
> - [ ] Remaining six consumer migrations merged, one PR each, with behavior-equivalence evidence per PR.
> - [ ] `spheric_collision_detector` dead-path removal and AEB raw-IMU decoupling merged.
> - [ ] `autoware_launch` integration merged (extractor launched beside ground segmentation, consumers repointed).
> - [ ] Consumer READMEs document the per-cell gate semantics (including the `min_height`-as-z-gate note).
> 
> Deployment-side items (per-consumer watchdog timeout values, diagnostics/MRM escalation policy, producer redundancy level) are functional-safety sign-off concerns for integrators and intentionally do not gate this track.
> 

**Comments:**

###### @youtalk (2026-07-09)

> @technolojin @YoshiRi @interimadd @takayuki5168 Please review this.

###### @youtalk (2026-07-09)

> @mitsudome-r @xmfcx Please review this.

###### @youtalk (2026-07-29)

> The producer side of this work is now up as two draft PRs:
> 
> - #13091 ΓÇö `autoware_obstacle_grid_utils`, the shared header-only helper consumers use to query the grid.
> - #13092 ΓÇö `autoware_obstacle_grid_extractor`, the sensing-side producer node. Stacked on #13091, so its diff also contains #13091's commits until that one merges.
> 
> Both are additive (new packages only, nothing existing modified). The consumer-side migrations are held back for now, pending feedback on the producer side.

### #12937 — Enhance Current Parking Performance

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-07-03  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @bastugdildar
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12937

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> During testing of AutowareΓÇÖs current parking behavior, especially in reverse parking scenarios, the freespace parking planner sometimes generates trajectories with unnecessary forward/backward direction changes. Although the vehicle is eventually able to reach the target parking pose, the generated maneuver can be inefficient and not smooth enough for practical parking behavior.
> In my tests, I observed that the planner may choose a trajectory that includes redundant gear changes or additional maneuvering instead of producing a more direct and smoother reverse parking path. This behavior affects the overall parking performance, increases maneuver complexity, and may reduce the naturalness of the parking motion.
> This issue aims to discuss how the current parking performance can be improved, especially by reducing redundant direction switches and improving trajectory smoothness in freespace parking scenarios.
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose of this issue is to document the observed behavior of the current parking planner in reverse parking scenarios where the generated trajectory may include unnecessary forward and backward direction changes.
> 
> This issue is intended to highlight the impact of these redundant maneuvers on parking smoothness, efficiency, and overall vehicle behavior during parking.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> One possible direction could be to investigate whether the current freespace parking planner parameters affect the number of direction changes and the smoothness of the generated trajectory.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> The issue can be considered resolved when the parking planner no longer generates unnecessary forward/backward direction changes in reverse parking scenarios where a smoother and more direct maneuver is feasible.
> 
> The vehicle should still be able to reach the target parking pose safely while producing a more efficient and natural parking trajectory.

### #12870 — autoware_system_monitor: ProcessMonitor publishes a NUL-containing "S" value, aborting system_monitor_container

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-06-24  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @hsule
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12870

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> `ProcessMonitor` can publish a `"S"` (process-state) `KeyValue` whose value is a single NUL byte (`"\0"`). Fast-CDR rejects NUL-containing strings, so serialization throws an uncaught `BadParamException` and SIGABRTs the whole `system_monitor_container` (`exit code -6`) at startup, taking down every monitor in it, not just ProcessMonitor.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Unfilled ranking slots should publish an empty/placeholder `"S"` value, and `system_monitor_container` should keep running.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> ```
> [component_container_mt-3] terminate called after throwing an instance of 'eprosima::fastcdr::exception::BadParamException'
> [component_container_mt-3]   what():  The string contains null characters
> [ERROR] [component_container_mt-3]: process has died [pid 218, exit code -6, cmd '.../component_container_mt --ros-args -r __node:=system_monitor_container ...'].
> ```
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Start the official container:
> 
> ```bash
> docker run -it ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-devel-cuda-jazzy-1.8.0 bash
> ```
> 
> This setup uses `rmw_zenoh_cpp`; install and start the router first:
> 
> ```bash
> sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y ros-jazzy-rmw-zenoh-cpp
> source /opt/autoware/setup.bash          # re-source AFTER install so libzenohc.so is on the path
> export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
> ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd &
> ```
> 
> ### Option A: full launch
> 
> ```bash
> # NTPMonitor shells out to chronyc; without it the container aborts earlier on an
> # unrelated boost::process execve error, masking this crash.
> sudo apt-get install -y chrony
> ros2 launch autoware_system_monitor system_monitor.launch.xml
> ```
> 
> ### Option B: ProcessMonitor only
> 
> Load `ProcessMonitor` alone with more ranking slots than processes, forcing unfilled default-`state` slots, so it crashes every time:
> 
> ```bash
> ros2 run rclcpp_components component_container_mt --ros-args -r __node:=sysmon_container &
> ros2 component load /sysmon_container autoware_system_monitor ProcessMonitor -p num_of_procs:=40
> ```
> 
> Either way, within ~1ΓÇô3 s the container aborts with the `BadParamException` shown.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 24.04
> - ROS 2: Jazzy
> - Autoware: 1.8.0 (`autoware_universe` 0.51.0)
> - RMW: `rmw_zenoh_cpp` (`ros-jazzy-rmw-zenoh-cpp` 0.2.9)
> - Base image: `ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-devel-cuda-jazzy-1.8.0`
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> A ranking slot not filled by a real process keeps a default `state == '\0'`, which is converted to a length-1 embedded-NUL string and published as the `"S"` value. The chain (`autoware_universe` tag `0.51.0`):
> 
> - [`process_information.hpp#L32`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/0.51.0/system/autoware_system_monitor/include/system_monitor/process_monitor/process_information.hpp#L32) ΓÇö `StatInfo::state` is a `char`, default `'\0'`
> - [`process_monitor.cpp#L407-L415`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/0.51.0/system/autoware_system_monitor/src/process_monitor/process_monitor.cpp#L407-L415) ΓÇö `invalidateRankingEntry()` resets `cpu_usage`/`resident_page` but leaves `state` untouched
> - [`process_monitor.cpp#L610`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/0.51.0/system/autoware_system_monitor/src/process_monitor/process_monitor.cpp#L610) ΓÇö `fillTaskInfo()`: `info.processStatus = raw_p->stat_info.state;`
> - [`diag_task.hpp#L76`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/0.51.0/system/autoware_system_monitor/include/system_monitor/process_monitor/diag_task.hpp#L76) ΓÇö `stat.add("S", info_.processStatus);`
> 
> Confirmed with gdb: at the throw, `key = "S"`, `value = "\x00"` (length 1).
> 
> Proposed fix in `fillTaskInfo()`:
> 
> ```cpp
> info.processStatus =
>   (raw_p->stat_info.state == '\0')
>     ? std::string()                          // empty string serializes fine
>     : std::string(1, raw_p->stat_info.state);
> ```
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> - Why Fast-CDR throws: [`Cdr::serialize(const std::string&)`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-CDR/blob/v2.2.7/include/fastcdr/Cdr.h#L689-L701) throws when `size() > strlen(c_str)`, i.e. an embedded NUL. `processStatus = '\0'` is exactly that (`size()==1`, `strlen()==0`), so Fast-CDR is correctly rejecting an invalid IDL string; the fix belongs on the producer side.
> - RMW-dependent: Fast-CDR-based typesupport (`rmw_zenoh_cpp`) aborts; `rmw_cyclonedds_cpp` tolerates the NUL and keeps running. The malformed value is published either way; only the consequence differs.
> 

**Comments:**

###### @GavinnnK (2026-08-07)

> I confirmed the reported code path on current main: a default-initialized ranking entry leaves `state == '\0'`, and assigning that character directly to `std::string` produces a one-byte embedded NUL.
> 
> I have a focused local fix that maps only `'\0'` to an empty string at the publishing boundary while preserving real Linux process states. The regression test uses the existing dummy `/proc` data containing six processes with `num_of_procs=7`, then verifies that both unfilled CPU and memory ranking entries publish an empty `S` value.
> 
> If this approach looks right, I will submit the focused two-file PR.
> 
> AI usage: Codex assisted with repository inspection and initial patch preparation. I reviewed the proposed change and regression test before posting this comment.
>

### #12691 — [Feature] Implement Interfaces and Components for Redundant System Switching (Proposal 1)

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-06-02  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @TetsuKawa
- **Labels:** status:stale
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12691

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Based on the discussion in [discussions #6932](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/6932), Autoware aims to officially support a redundant configuration to ensure safe failover operations. This issue focuses on implementing the standard interfaces and necessary components based on Proposal 1 (Distributed Decision-Making), where each Autoware ECU autonomously determines its behavior, and an external Switching Function arbitrates them based on priority.
> 
> Note: This issue covers the development of intermediate coordination nodes, bridge configurations, and API management tools required to realize this distributed redundancy framework.
> 
> ---
> 
> # Redundant ECU Configuration Design
> 
> ## Purpose
> 
> This page defines the high-level design for operating Autoware in a redundant ECU configuration.
> It focuses on cases where switching from Main ECU to Sub ECU is required due to software faults, hardware failures, or related conditions.
> 
> The design has two primary goals:
> 
> - Improve system safety by increasing tolerance against system and hardware failures
> - Increase architectural flexibility for higher ASIL targets (including decomposition-oriented design options)
> 
> ## Background and Motivation
> 
> In Autoware Architecture v1, redundancy was treated as future work.
> In practical deployment, however, a single-ECU failure can directly stop autonomous driving functions,
> so the architecture must improve operational continuity (availability) under ECU faults.
> 
> Redundant architecture is particularly effective for:
> 
> - Reducing single points of failure (SPOF) in primary compute platforms
> - Improving operational continuity under fault conditions
> - Expanding design options for safety and certification (ASIL) strategies
> 
> ## Scope
> 
> ### In scope
> 
> - Redundant architecture design based on a dual-ECU Main/Sub configuration
> - Design of abstraction layers related to switching
> - Coordination design between switching behavior and Autoware components
> - Impact assessment and design updates for existing AD API behavior
> 
> ### Out of scope
> 
> - Implementation/provision of the switching function itself
> - Vehicle-specific physical hardware design
> - Formal ISO 26262 work products
> - Byzantine fault handling
> 
> ## About the External Switching Function
> 
> In this design, the external mechanism that performs physical switching between Main and Sub ECUs is called the **External Switching Function**.
> It is outside Autoware, and Autoware does not implement it (out of scope).
> 
> Autoware is designed with this external switching function as a prerequisite.
> Requirements expected from the switching function are defined in Requirements for the Switching Function.
> 
> ## Requirements
> 
> ### Requirements for the Switching Function (Prerequisites)
> 
> The following requirements must be satisfied by the external switching function to enable redundant operation in Autoware.
> These are external requirements; Autoware functional requirements are defined assuming they are met.
> 
> | ID     | Requirement                                                                                     | Notes                                                                                 |
> | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
> | EXT-01 | Switching behavior shall be deterministic                                                       | The same input shall always produce the same switching result                         |
> | EXT-02 | Switching shall complete within a bounded time                                                  | A timeout upper bound must be defined                                                 |
> | EXT-03 | A single ECU or network fault shall not cause failure of the switching function itself          | Single faults must be contained and not propagated into the switching function        |
> | EXT-04 | Current switching state (Active/Standby assignment) shall be shared with both Main and Sub ECUs | ECU-side logic must be able to identify current role                                  |
> | EXT-05 | Switching requests from ECU side shall be accepted                                              | ECU-originated switching triggers must be supported                                   |
> | EXT-06 | Exactly one ECU shall be Active at any time                                                     | Avoiding simultaneous output (split-brain) is the switching functionΓÇÖs responsibility |
> 
> ### Functional Requirements for Autoware
> 
> Assuming EXT requirements are satisfied, Autoware shall fulfill the following:
> 
> | ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                                | Notes                                                                           |
> | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
> | FR-01 | Autoware shall provide ECU identity and heartbeat information to the switching function                                                    | Required for ECU identification by the switching function                       |
> | FR-02 | Main and Sub internal systems shall report local health information to the switching function and support switching-necessity judgment     | Includes process status, communication status, and freshness of critical topics |
> | FR-03 | Main and Sub ECUs shall detect and recognize abnormalities of the switching function (for example communication loss or functional outage) | Reduces risk of the switching function becoming an undetected SPOF              |
> | FR-04 | The architecture shall allow Sub ECU to become Active when Main ECU hardware fails                                                         | Covers hardware faults in addition to software faults                           |
> | FR-05 | ECU switching results (Active side changes) shall be reflected in Autoware vehicle behavior selection (modes, MRM, etc.)                   | Ensures post-switch behavior continuity                                         |
> | FR-06 | Sub ECU shall continue to provide a minimum AD API capability even after ECU switching                                                     | Minimizes impact on external applications                                       |
> 
> ### Non-Functional Requirements
> 
> | ID     | Requirement                                                                    | Notes                                      |
> | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
> | NFR-01 | Switching-related events and decision data shall be recorded as auditable logs | Required for safety analysis and debugging |
> 
> ---
> # Connection Design Between the Switching Function and Autoware
> 
> ## Purpose
> 
> This page defines the high-level design for connecting an external ECU switching function (External Switching Function) to Autoware.
> The scope covers responsibility boundaries between vehicle behavior selection nodes running on both Main and Sub ECUs and the node that bridges to the switching function.
> 
> ## Overall Architecture
> 
> This section first distinguishes between elements that already exist in the single-ECU configuration and elements added for redundancy.
> 
> ### Existing Elements in the Single-ECU Configuration (Prerequisites)
> 
> The following elements are pre-existing MRM switching components. They are not newly introduced for ECU redundancy.
> 
> - Nodes
>   - `command_mode_decider`
>   - `command_mode_switcher`
>   - `aggregator`
> - Topics
>   - `command_mode_request`
>   - `command_mode_status`
>   - `command_mode_availability`
> 
> Roles of existing elements:
> 
> - `command_mode_decider`: Generates behavior-switch requests (`command_mode_request`)
> - `command_mode_switcher`: Determines which behavior is enabled based on requests and current state
> - `aggregator`: Aggregates per-command-mode executability and publishes `command_mode_availability`
> - `command_mode_request`: Represents behavior-switch requests
> - `command_mode_status`: Represents the current state of each command mode
> - `command_mode_availability`: Represents availability of each command mode
> 
> ### Elements Added for Redundancy
> 
> - Added node: `redundancy_switcher_interface`
> - Added topic: `active_control_unit`
> 
> `redundancy_switcher_interface` connects to the external ECU switching function and shares switching results with existing MRM nodes via `active_control_unit`.
> This enables behavior selection with ECU switching while minimizing changes to the existing MRM design.
> 
> ### Nodes Launched on Each ECU
> 
> Both Main ECU and Sub ECU launch the following:
> 
> - Existing MRM nodes: `command_mode_decider` / `command_mode_switcher` / `aggregator`
> - Added node: `redundancy_switcher_interface`
> 
> In addition, `command_mode_status` and `command_mode_availability` are shared between ECUs to maintain decision consistency across both systems.
> 
> ## High-Level Connection Diagram
> 
> <img width="1080" height="969" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87d9e53b-b95e-421f-b426-4cabb564d723" />
> 
> ## Details of Added Elements
> 
> ### `redundancy_switcher_interface` (Added Node)
> 
> `redundancy_switcher_interface` is a bridge node placed between existing MRM nodes and the external ECU switching function.
> 
> #### Connection to Existing Nodes
> 
> - Receives `command_mode_request` from `command_mode_decider` and converts it to an ECU-switching request when needed
> - Passes `active_control_unit` received from the external switching function to `command_mode_switcher`
> 
> #### Connection to the External ECU Switching Function
> 
> - Forwards Autoware-side requests (for example, MRM requests and switch reset requests) to the external interface
> - Receives switching results from the external switching function and normalizes them into a representation usable by Autoware
> 
> #### Design Intent
> 
> The switching decision/execution logic is not embedded into existing MRM nodes.
> Instead, it is centralized in `redundancy_switcher_interface`, making responsibility boundaries explicit.
> 
> #### Plugin Architecture (Interchangeable Switching Function Integration)
> 
> The connection between `redundancy_switcher_interface` and the external switching function is implemented through replaceable plugins.
> Each plugin implements:
> 
> - Interface connectivity to a target switching function
> - Conversion from switching-function-specific protocols to AutowareΓÇÖs common abstraction
> 
> This approach keeps core Autoware node responsibilities stable while isolating switching-function-specific differences inside plugins.
> 
> ### `active_control_unit` (Added Topic)
> 
> `active_control_unit` is the key topic introduced to propagate ECU switching results inside Autoware.
> 
> - Meaning: Indicates which control unit (Main/Sub) is currently Active
> - Publisher: `redundancy_switcher_interface`
> - Consumer: `command_mode_switcher`, for `network gate` Open/Closed control
> 
> `command_mode_switcher` control examples:
> 
> - Main ECU is Active: Main-side `network gate = Open`, Sub-side `Closed`
> - Sub ECU is Active: Sub-side `network gate = Open`, Main-side `Closed`
> 
> This allows existing MRM behavior-selection logic to remain intact while incorporating ECU switching outcomes.
> 
> If `active_control_unit` is undefined, inconsistent, or empty, the system treats it as a transient or abnormal switching state,
> and transitions to safe-side behavior (restricted executable modes and upstream notification).
> 
> ## Information Flow
> 
> 1. `command_mode_status` and `command_mode_availability` are continuously shared between ECUs to maintain consistency.
> 2. `command_mode_decider` generates a switching request.
> 3. `redundancy_switcher_interface` forwards the request to the external ECU switching function.
> 4. The external switching function returns active control unit information, which `redundancy_switcher_interface` normalizes into `active_control_unit`.
> 5. `redundancy_switcher_interface` provides `active_control_unit` to `command_mode_switcher`.
> 6. `command_mode_switcher` updates the `network gate` (Open/Closed) and controls executable behavior accordingly.
> 
> 
> ---
> # AD API Design for Redundant ECUs
> 
> ## Purpose
> 
> This page defines the high-level AD API design for a redundant ECU configuration.
> It addresses three main design concerns during Main/Sub switching:
> 
> - Applying the same service request consistently to both Main and Sub systems
> - Handling MRM recovery requests while hiding internal differences between redundant and non-redundant configurations
> - Preventing API output collisions between Main and Sub
> 
> ## Design Principles
> 
> Internal architectural differences (redundant vs. non-redundant) should not be exposed to external API users.
> From the API perspective, recovery from MRM state back to autonomous operation should be handled through a consistent request interface.
> 
> To achieve this, the design introduces:
> 
> - Standardized service fan-out (`generic_service_divider`)
> - Unified MRM reset orchestration (`mrm_reset_manager`)
> - Active-ECU-based API output filtering (`redundancy_adapi_switcher`)
> 
> ## Existing vs Added Elements
> 
> ### Existing Elements (from the Single-ECU Configuration)
> 
> - `command_mode_decider`
>   - Receives services such as `change_operation_mode` and `change_autoware_control`
>   - For node-level responsibilities, see [switching-connection-design.md](switching-connection-design.md)
> - `aggregator` diagnostic latch behavior
>   - Once diagnostics become `diag ERROR`, the state is latched
>   - Even if diagnostics later return to `diag OK`, the latch is not cleared automatically
>   - Latch release requires an explicit service call after human safety confirmation
> 
> ### Added Elements (for Redundant Configuration)
> 
> - `generic_service_divider`
> - `mrm_reset_manager`
> - `redundancy_adapi_switcher`
> 
> ## Service API Architecture Diagram
> 
> <img width="2124" height="1302" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da0deafb-207e-40cf-9127-bb084023fd8c" />
> 
> ## Service Fan-Out Design (`generic_service_divider`)
> 
> In Main/Sub switching, a key requirement is to apply the same request coherently to both ECUs.
> 
> For example, the following service calls to `command_mode_decider` must be applied to both Main and Sub:
> 
> - `change_operation_mode`
> - `change_autoware_control`
> 
> `generic_service_divider` republishes one incoming service request to multiple clients.
> This allows one request to be fanned out into ECU-specific calls (Main-targeted and Sub-targeted).
> 
> This is not limited to `command_mode_decider`.
> Any service that must be applied simultaneously to both ECUs can be added via plugins.
> For example, in a configuration where `ekf_localizer` is deployed on Sub ECU, a `trigger_node` service for initial pose setup can be added as a fan-out target.
> 
> ## Unified MRM Reset Design (`mrm_reset_manager`)
> 
> ### Background
> 
> MRM recovery involves both redundant-system resets and existing-system resets:
> 
> - ECU switching-function reset
>   - When resuming autonomous driving by returning Main ECU to Active after a MainΓåÆSub switch
>   - When initializing the internal state of the ECU switching function itself
> - `aggregator` diagnostic latch release
>   - To avoid unintended automatic resume and require explicit operator judgment after safety confirmation
> Expand commentComment on lines R75 to R80Resolved
> ### API Unification
> 
> These internal reset paths are hidden behind a single external request: `/system/mrm/reset`.
> `mrm_reset_manager` receives this request and translates it into:
> 
> - ECU switching reset request
> - Diagnostic latch release request
> 
> Note: `/system/mrm/reset` is currently a design proposal and is not yet supported as an AD API endpoint.
> 
> ### Initialization-Phase Control
> 
> `mrm_reset_manager` also controls initialization-phase enable/disable behavior.
> Initialization is considered complete when:
> 
> - Localization is set
> - Route is set
> - Autoware Control is `on`
> 
> During initialization:
> 
> - `aggregator` latch behavior is turned `off` to avoid latching transient startup `diag ERROR`
> - `redundancy_switcher_interface` is notified via `set_initializing` to suppress unnecessary ECU switching
> 
> After initialization completes, `set_initializing` is updated to enable normal behavior.
> 
> In summary, `mrm_reset_manager` serves two roles:
> 
> - API entry point for MRM-related external reset requests
> - Orchestrator for enabling/disabling reset target functions according to initialization phase
> 
> ## Minimum Sub-ECU API Set and Output Switching
> 
> When switching from Main to Sub, Sub ECU provides a minimum API subset required for failure-related HMI reporting:
> 
> - `/api/system/diagnostics/status`
> - `/api/system/diagnostics/struct`
> - `/api/fail_safe/mrm_state`
> - `/api/system/heartbeat`
> 
> Sub ECU runs `default_adapi` for this limited scope.
> (As a design option, emitting the full API set from both Main and Sub is also possible.)
> 
> To avoid simultaneous output collisions, `redundancy_adapi_switcher` applies output filtering:
> 
> - If Main ECU is Active: stop API source-topic output from Sub ECU
> - If Sub ECU is Active: stop API source-topic output from Main ECU
> 
> ## Information Flow (Summary)
> 
> 1. An external service request is received and fanned out by `generic_service_divider` to Main and Sub.
> 2. When ECU switching is relevant, `redundancy_switcher_interface` handles switching-function integration.
> 3. An MRM recovery request (`/system/mrm/reset`) is received by `mrm_reset_manager` and translated into switching reset + diagnostic latch release requests.
> 4. During startup initialization, `mrm_reset_manager` controls latch behavior and switching-function enable state.
> 5. API outputs are gated by `redundancy_adapi_switcher` so only the Active ECU side is exposed.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> This task will be considered complete when all the following Pull Requests implementing the respective components are reviewed and merged:
> 
> - [ ] https://github.com/tier4/tier4_autoware_msgs/pull/226
> - [ ] https://github.com/tier4/tier4_autoware_msgs/pull/227
> - [ ] https://github.com/tier4/tier4_autoware_msgs/pull/228
> - [ ] https://github.com/tier4/tier4_autoware_msgs/pull/229
> - [ ] https://github.com/tier4/tier4_autoware_msgs/pull/230
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12692
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12693
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_core/pull/1157
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12694
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12695
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12696

>  - FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/home/user/autoware/install/autoware_carla_interface/share/autoware_carla_interface/autoware_carla_interface.launch.xml'
> 
> ```
> The file is not present after a standard source build of Autoware 1.8.0.
> 
> 2. I tried a manual workaround. After manually copying the [missing launch file](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/0.51.0/simulator/autoware_carla_interface/launch/autoware_carla_interface.launch.xml) from the repository source into the corresponding folder (`~/autoware/install/autoware_carla_interface/share/autoware_carla_interface/autoware_carla_interface.launch.xml`), the system launches successfully.

(VoxelGridDynamicMapLoader() at /home/user/autoware/src/universe/autoware_universe/perception/autoware_compare_map_segmentation/lib/voxel_grid_map_loader.cpp:379)

### #12535 — build-and-test-differential-above fails do to missing dependency to autoware_system_designer

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-05-01  |  **Closed:** 2026-06-23  |  **Author:** @mitsudome-r
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12535

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> build-and-test-differential-above fails do to missing dependency to autoware_system_designer.
> Examples:
>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/actions/runs/25223454355/job/73961133809?pr=12534
>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/actions/runs/24873773551/job/72825820765?pr=12496
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Workflow passes without failure
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Workflow is failing
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Create a package that modifies packages that trigger the build of autoware_system_designs package in autoware_launch (e.g., autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor).
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> ## Why it fails
> packages_above.repos clones launcher/autoware_launch into the workspace, which contains autoware_sample_designs. Therefore, whenever there is a package that is depended by autoware_sample_designs is modified (like autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor), the workflow fails with the error.
> 
> ## How to fix
> I can think of the following options to fix the error:
> 1. Add autoware_system_designer to build_depends_above.repos or build_depends_stable. Ensures the workspace builds it from source matching a pinned tag.
>  2. source `/opt/autoware/` since autoware_system_designer should be already built within ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-dependencies-* images used for the ci. 
> 
> I prefer to go with option 2 so that we don't have to rebuild the package which are already built. One drawback is that when ever we want to update the package version, we would have to wait for the docker build pipeline in `autowarefoundation/autoware` to finish, but I don't think we would expect frequent change for the repo. 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2026-05-01)

> After [discussion in the draft PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12536#issuecomment-4361155871), I decided to fix the error with approach 1 for now. 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12538

> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12735

> I added a trap in `BehaviorPathPlannerNode::run()` when I get `path->left_bound.size() == 2` and rebuilt `autoware_behavior_path_planner` and `autoware_behavior_path_planner_common` in debug mode. Catching the trap in gdb, I can call `planner_manager_->run(planner_data_)` manually again and investigate what is going on.
> 
> The issue root cause is in:
> 
> - [`BehaviorPathPlannerNode::run`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/4d6292d549e5c34b4e865ac3a7c0d8bfb7a52b2e/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_planner/src/behavior_path_planner_node.cpp#L431)
>   - `PlannerManager::run`
>     - `PlannerManager::generateCombinedDrivableArea`
>       - [`utils::generateDrivableArea`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/4d6292d549e5c34b4e865ac3a7c0d8bfb7a52b2e/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_planner_common/src/utils/drivable_area_expansion/static_drivable_area.cpp#L815)
>         - [`utils::calcBound`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/4d6292d549e5c34b4e865ac3a7c0d8bfb7a52b2e/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_planner_common/src/utils/drivable_area_expansion/static_drivable_area.cpp#L1632)
>           - [`utils::postProcess`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/4d6292d549e5c34b4e865ac3a7c0d8bfb7a52b2e/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_planner_common/src/utils/drivable_area_expansion/static_drivable_area.cpp#L1492)
>             
> 
> The problem is that `goal_idx` is not calculated properly [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/4d6292d549e5c34b4e865ac3a7c0d8bfb7a52b2e/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_planner_common/src/utils/drivable_area_expansion/static_drivable_area.cpp#L1600). > 
> 

###### @satoshi-ota (2026-05-13)

> @VRichardJP Thank you for the bug report and detailed investigation. ≡ƒæì 
> 
> This issue may indeed be related to some parts of the system being designed with 2D assumptions. In addition, it may also be related to the fact that loops are intentionally avoided/cut in some parts of the planning pipeline from the viewpoint of nearest-point search on the trajectory.
> 
> In the past, we experienced issues where looped trajectories caused unexpected behavior around intersections, such as failing to correctly determine the nearest trajectory point to the ego vehicle near crossing points. Because of this, some modules currently assume non-looping paths/trajectories.
> 
> Also, if the emergency stop is actually triggered by Localization MRM, it might be possible to keep the vehicle running in simulation by excluding localization failure from MRM targets, for example by commenting out the following parameter(s).
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/9ae050966a9565a3ed7c8bc3f94effe749ce5688/autoware_launch/config/system/diagnostics/autoware-main.yaml#L36
> 
> In any case, this particular use case (multi-level overlapping routes such as spiral parking structures) is currently outside the supported scope of the existing Planning stack ≡ƒÖÅ 

###### @VRichardJP (2026-05-13)

> @satoshi-ota I don't think assuming the route is flat with no loop is necessarily the problem here. This spiral map example rather highlights that an upstream module (`route_handler`?) fails to cut a looped route.
> 
> As you can see in the reported data, the intermediate route `behavior_path_planner` modules are processing contains a perfect loop: first point and last point x/y are equal. So maybe the problem could be fixed by adding a cut margin (e.g. cut at least 5m before the loop)? Assuming no route would loop within such a short distance, I think this could be a reasonable fix.

###### @satoshi-ota (2026-05-20)

> I see. I also traced the code again, and it looks like there may be an issue in the logic that determines the start/end of the drivable bound.
> 
> I think your proposed approach could fix the issue. Another possible approach might be to first calculate the point on the bound closest to the ego position (`closest_idx`) when determining the bound start/end, and then search for the point closest to `path.points.back()` only within the range of indices after `closest_idx` for the end point. This could also help prevent the start/end indices from overlapping.
