### #12517 — Segfault in crosswalk module due to non-strict std::sort comparator

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-04-28  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @Ching-Hsiang-18
- **Labels:** status:stale
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12517

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> `sortCrosswalksByDistance` in `autoware_behavior_velocity_crosswalk_module` uses a comparator lambda whose `(!l1_ep || !l2_ep) -> return true` branch violates the strict-weak-ordering precondition required by `std::sort`. For NΓëÑ17, some valid input arrangements with no-endpoint entries trigger libstdc++'s introsort path, where `__unguarded_partition` can read past the end of the vector and the `behavior_planning_container` process terminates with `SIGSEGV`. In closed-loop operation, this kills the entire planning pipeline mid-drive and the vehicle stalls on the road with no automatic recovery.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> `sortCrosswalksByDistance` should provide a strict weak ordering for every pair of crosswalk lanelets passed to `std::sort`, including lanelets whose polygons conflict with the ego road lanelet but do not intersect the ego path.
> 
> In the closed-loop planning scenario, `behavior_planning_container` should not crash when the ego vehicle approaches the active crosswalk. The planner should continue publishing trajectories, handle the crossing pedestrian normally, and complete the route instead of dropping out of autonomous operation because of a process-level `SIGSEGV`.
> 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> We reproduced the failure in `planning_simulator` using the synthetic Lanelet2 map shown below. The map contains one long ego road lanelet, one active ego-path-crossing crosswalk (`c_active`), and 16 additional pedestrian crosswalk polygons that conflict with the same road lanelet but do not intersect the ego path.
> 
> <img width="1624" height="880" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b07904a9-e47f-4662-a79a-43cbeff850f4" />
> 
> On the buggy build, `behavior_planning_container` exits with `SIGSEGV` (exit code -11) the moment ego's planning horizon first reaches the active crosswalk, on the very first invocation of the sort. The process never recovers, no further trajectories are published, and ego coasts to a halt roughly 50 m short of the crosswalk while `/api/operation_mode` drops out of `AUTONOMOUS`. With only the comparator patched (no other changes), the same scenario completes the route normally.
> 
> The end-to-end behavior is shown below: before the patch, the planner process dies and the vehicle stalls before the crosswalk; after the comparator fix, the same scenario yields to the crossing pedestrian and completes the route.
> 
> <img width="2396" height="646" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/506fee56-d21a-4e18-ad67-cb5b3c39d1d5" />
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Build/run Autoware Universe with the current implementation of `autoware_behavior_velocity_crosswalk_module::sortCrosswalksByDistance`.
> 2. Create a situation where `clampAttentionRangeByNeighborCrosswalks` receives at least 17 pedestrian crosswalk lanelets from `conflictingInGraph(road_lanelet, PEDESTRIAN_GRAPH_ID)`.
> 3. Ensure that the active crosswalk intersects the ego path, but at least one of the returned conflicting crosswalks does not have a path-intersection endpoint on the ego path.
> 4. Let the planning horizon reach the active crosswalk so that `sortCrosswalksByDistance` is invoked.
> 5. On libstdc++ 11, the invalid comparator can trigger an out-of-bounds read in `std::sort`'s introsort path, causing `behavior_planning_container` to exit with `SIGSEGV`.
> 
> A minimal standalone C++ reproducer is included below. It reproduces the same
> strict-weak-ordering violation without requiring a full Autoware launch.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - **Autoware Universe**: bug reproduced on `14ae8fd36cf50158ed6153b29154d9ba0b320543`;  buggy code unchanged in current main `d40e111069d247db426fd3d1266b996515862f98` ([lines 144-146](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/d40e111069d247db426fd3d1266b996515862f98/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/autoware_behavior_velocity_crosswalk_module/src/scene_crosswalk.cpp#L144-L146)).
> - **Autoware Core**: 1.7.2 (per `repositories/autoware.repos`).
> - **ROS 2**: Humble (`ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-devel`, image `sha256:eaa0c1919ade009fdd7f32a7509ad9d508197eb6ab16e0ba3517f3a3baf80f59`).
> - **Compiler**: g++ 11.4.0 (Ubuntu 22.04 / `11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3`), libstdc++-11.
> - **Architecture**: x86_64.
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> ## Affected code
> 
> [`planning/behavior_velocity_planner/autoware_behavior_velocity_crosswalk_module/src/scene_crosswalk.cpp#L135-L167`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/d40e111069d247db426fd3d1266b996515862f98/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/autoware_behavior_velocity_crosswalk_module/src/scene_crosswalk.cpp#L135-L167)
> (`sortCrosswalksByDistance`, comparator at lines 139-156, offending branch at [lines 144-146](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/d40e111069d247db426fd3d1266b996515862f98/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/autoware_behavior_velocity_crosswalk_module/src/scene_crosswalk.cpp#L144-L146)):
> 
> ```cpp
> const auto compare = [&](const lanelet::ConstLanelet & l1, const lanelet::ConstLanelet & l2) {
>     const auto l1_end_points_on_crosswalk =
>       getPathEndPointsOnCrosswalk(ego_path, l1.polygon2d().basicPolygon(), ego_pos);
>     const auto l2_end_points_on_crosswalk =
>       getPathEndPointsOnCrosswalk(ego_path, l2.polygon2d().basicPolygon(), ego_pos);
> 
>     if (!l1_end_points_on_crosswalk || !l2_end_points_on_crosswalk) {
>         return true;                                                // <-- buggy branch
>     }
>     // ... arc-length comparison
> };
> ```
> 
> For any pair where either operand lacks a path-intersection endpoint, the comparator returns `true` regardless of operand order, so `compare(a, b) == compare(b, a) == true`. This breaks antisymmetry; for two no-endpoint operands it additionally breaks irreflexivity (`compare(x, x) == true`).
> 
> ## Trigger conditions
> 
> The vector passed into `std::sort` is built by `clampAttentionRangeByNeighborCrosswalks` from `conflictingInGraph(road_lanelet, PEDESTRIAN_GRAPH_ID)`. SIGSEGV reproduces deterministically when **all** of these hold:
> 
> 1. The active `CrosswalkModule`'s ego path actually crosses its own polygon (otherwise the module early-exits in `modifyPathVelocity` before reaching the sort).
> 2. `conflictingInGraph` returns ΓëÑ17 crosswalks for the ego lanelet ΓÇö libstdc++'s `std::sort` switches from insertion sort to introsort at N=17. In our tests, NΓëñ16 stays on the insertion-sort path and does not trigger the observed OOB, while NΓëÑ17 reaches the introsort path where the UB manifests.
> 3. At least one returned crosswalk has no endpoint on the ego path (its polygon overlaps the ego lanelet polygon but the path polyline does not enter it).
> 
> These are realistic in production: any road lanelet long enough to overlap a dense set of pedestrian polygons satisfies (2) and (3). The Nishishinjuku sample map ships road lanelets up to 331 m (p99 = 225 m); whether 17+ conflicting pedestrian polygons land on a single lanelet depends on the mapping vendor's segmentation choices for long urban arterials.
> 
> A 2000-trial Monte-Carlo scan over (has-ep, no-ep) splits at fixed N=17 shows the trigger is sharply deterministic at extreme splits and probabilistic in between (numbers are crash rate over 2000 random shuffle seeds per split, libstdc++ from g++ 11.4):
> 
> | has-ep | no-ep | crash rate |
> | ---: | ---: | ---: |
> | 0  | 17 | 100.00% |
> | 1  | 16 | 100.00% |
> | 7  | 10 |  88.05% |
> | 13 |  4 |  47.85% |
> | 16 |  1 |  14.30% |
> | 17 |  0 |   0.00% |
> 
> The "1 has-ep + 16 no-ep" case is interesting because it is the smallest configuration that combines deterministic crashing (every shuffle seed crashes) with the natural runtime semantic of "ego is approaching exactly one active crosswalk and 16 others happen to be polygon-conflicting".
> 
> ## Standalone reproducer
> 
> The following program reproduces the SIGSEGV deterministically. 
> 
> ```cpp
> // Minimal standalone reproducer for the SWO violation in
> // sortCrosswalksByDistance.
> //
> // The buggy comparator returns true whenever EITHER operand lacks a
> // path-intersection endpoint. For all-no-endpoint arrays, this makes
> // compare(x, y) = true for every pair, violating irreflexivity, which
> // libstdc++'s __unguarded_partition treats as UB and reads past array
> // bounds.
> //
> // Build (AddressSanitizer):
> //   g++ -std=c++17 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
> //       -o test_swo_oob_asan test_swo_oob.cpp
> // Build (plain):
> //   g++ -std=c++17 -O1 -g -o test_swo_oob test_swo_oob.cpp
> //
> // Usage:
> //   ./test_swo_oob_asan <n> <buggy|patched>
> //
> // Expected:
> //   buggy + n>=17 -> ASan heap-buffer-overflow or SIGSEGV
> //   patched + any n -> clean exit
> //   buggy  + n<=16 -> clean exit (insertion-sort path, no OOB)
> 
> #include <algorithm>
> #include <cstdio>
> #include <cstdlib>
> #include <optional>
> #include <string>
> #include <vector>
> 
> struct Crosswalk {
>   int id;
>   std::optional<double> endpoint_dist;  // nullopt == no-ep on ego path
> };
> 
> static bool buggy_compare(const Crosswalk& a, const Crosswalk& b) {
>   if (!a.endpoint_dist.has_value() || !b.endpoint_dist.has_value()) {
>     return true;
>   }
>   return *a.endpoint_dist < *b.endpoint_dist;
> }
> 
> static bool patched_compare(const Crosswalk& a, const Crosswalk& b) {
>   if (!a.endpoint_dist.has_value() && !b.endpoint_dist.has_value()) {
>     return a.id < b.id;
>   }
>   if (!a.endpoint_dist.has_value()) return false;
>   if (!b.endpoint_dist.has_value()) return true;
>   return *a.endpoint_dist < *b.endpoint_dist;
> }
> 
> static std::vector<Crosswalk> make_all_noep(int n) {
>   std::vector<Crosswalk> v(n);
>   for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
>     v[i].id = 3000000 + i;
>     v[i].endpoint_dist = std::nullopt;
>   }
>   return v;
> }
> 
> int main(int argc, char** argv) {
>   int n = (argc > 1) ? std::atoi(argv[1]) : 20;
>   std::string which = (argc > 2) ? argv[2] : "buggy";
> 
>   auto xs = make_all_noep(n);
>   std::fprintf(stderr, "[test] n=%d comparator=%s\n", n, which.c_str());
> 
>   if (which == "buggy") {
>     std::sort(xs.begin(), xs.end(), buggy_compare);
>   } else if (which == "patched") {
>     std::sort(xs.begin(), xs.end(), patched_compare);
>   } else {
>     std::fprintf(stderr, "[test] unknown comparator: %s\n", which.c_str());
>     return 2;
>   }
> 
>   std::fprintf(stderr, "[test] sort returned; first.id=%d last.id=%d\n",
>                xs.front().id, xs.back().id);
>   return 0;
> }
> ```
> 
> Build with AddressSanitizer for a clear `heap-buffer-overflow` diagnostic, or plain for a raw `SIGSEGV` (exit 139):
> 
> ```bash
> g++ -std=c++17 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
>     -o test_swo_oob_asan test_swo_oob.cpp
> ./test_swo_oob_asan 17 buggy        # crashes
> ./test_swo_oob_asan 17 patched      # clean exit
> ./test_swo_oob_asan 16 buggy        # clean exit (insertion-sort path)
> ```
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> ## Proposed fix
> 
> Restore strict weak ordering by replacing the `||` branch with explicit no-endpoint handling:
> 
> ```cpp
> if (!l1_end_points_on_crosswalk && !l2_end_points_on_crosswalk) {
>     return l1.id() < l2.id();    // both no-ep: order by lanelet id
> }
> if (!l1_end_points_on_crosswalk) {
>     return false;                 // single no-ep sorts after has-ep
> }
> if (!l2_end_points_on_crosswalk) {
>     return true;
> }
> const auto dist_l1 = calcSignedArcLength(...);
> const auto dist_l2 = calcSignedArcLength(...);
> return dist_l1 < dist_l2;
> ```
> 
> This restores irreflexivity (`compare(x, x) = false` for all `x`), antisymmetry (at most one of `compare(a, b)` / `compare(b, a)` returns true), and transitivity, so introsort's unguarded partition stays in bounds for any input. Validated against the standalone test (clean exit
> across 2000 shuffle seeds for every (has-ep, no-ep) split) and in the closed-loop simulator (planner survives, ego yields to a crossing pedestrian, completes the route).
> 
> ## Optional follow-up: API-level concern
> 
> `sortCrosswalksByDistance`'s only caller uses the result solely to find `c_active`'s immediate `prev` / `next` neighbor. Sorting an entire `O(n)` set including no-endpoint entries (whose ordering is geometrically ill-defined) is more work than necessary; replacing the sort with a linear `prev` / `next` scan over has-endpoint entries only would eliminate the SWO question entirely and avoid invoking the comparator on ill-defined pairs in the first place. Happy to open a separate discussion if that direction is of interest, but the minimal comparator fix above is sufficient on its own and is what we recommend merging first.

**Comments:**

> 
> The proposed fix direction also makes sense to me.
> If possible, could you please create a Pull Request based on the proposed approach?
> 
> I believe this is an important issue since it can lead to planner crashes and autonomous disengagement, so I would really appreciate your support on this.
> 
> Thank you again for the thorough analysis.

### #12497 — Support trajectory switching and update the decision logic for operation mode and MRM

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-04-21  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @isamu-takagi
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12497

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> While we've added support for a command switching mechanism for MRM in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/9235, we now need a trajectory switching function to support the AI ΓÇïΓÇïplanner. This is to allow switching from traditional rule-based planners or to use a trajectory generator for MRM as a backup.
> 
> It also supports interfaces for ECU redundancy: https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/6932
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - Using AI planner and rule-based planner together
> - Support for MRM that outputs trajectory
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Autoware's behavior is represented by a combination of several gates/selectors. Here, we will refer to each behavior as a "driving mode" for identification purposes, but the specific details will be determined during the vehicle integration process. The following diagram considers five modes: AutoMode1, AutoMode2, MRM1, MRM2, and RemoteMode.
> 
> <img width="961" height="481" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/400527cc-e638-4398-b472-9496dc9a5867" />
> 
> 
> A trajectory gate takes three candidate inputs: T1, T2, and T3. Similarly, a command gate also takes three candidate inputs: C1, C2, and C3. The vehicle interface is a bit unique, but it also has control modes such as MANUAL, AUTO, and STEER_ONLY. The driving modes are represented by combinations of these, as shown in the table below.
> 
> | Driving Mode | Trajectory Gate | Command Gate | Vehicle Interface |
> | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- |
> | AutoMode1 | T1 | C1 | AUTO |
> | AutoMode2 | T2 | C1 | AUTO |
> | MRM1 | T3 | C1 | AUTO |
> | MRM2 | any | C2 | AUTO |
> | RemoteMode | any | C3 | AUTO |
> 
> The diagnostic graph is configured to show the availability of each driving mode. From this, the currently available driving mode is determined and the gate is switched.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] https://github.com/tier4/tier4_autoware_msgs/pull/223
> - [ ] https://github.com/tier4/tier4_autoware_msgs/pull/233
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12640
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12650
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12759
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12838
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12718
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12760
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/1897
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_tools/pull/451
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/13252
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/13251
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/13250
> - [ ] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/13249
> - [ ] Remove external_cmd_selector

### #12460 — `autoware_behavior_path_planner` node crash when a new planning goal published

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-04-09  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @smk-robotics
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12460

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> A random crash of the `autoware_behavior_path_planner` node sometimes appears when a new planning goal is published. During the everyday operations we're facing this issue roughly once a day. It happens randomly, but annoys operators very much because the only way to fix it is to restart the stack completely. 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The `autoware_behavior_path_planner` is not crashing after a new planning goal is published.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> A random crash of the `autoware_behavior_path_planner` node sometimes appears when a new planning goal is published. 
> 
> ---
> Logs of the crash:
> ```
> [component_container_mt-62] terminate called after throwing an instance of 'rclcpp::exceptions::RCLError'
> [component_container_mt-62] what(): failed to add guard condition to wait set: guard condition implementation is invalid, at ./src/rcl/guard_condition.c:172, at ./src/rcl/wait.c:460
> [component_container_mt-62] *** Aborted at 1775119751 (unix time) try "date -d @1775119751" if you are using GNU date ***
> [component_container_mt-62] PC: @ 0x0 (unknown)
> [component_container_mt-62] *** SIGABRT (@0x3e800000383) received by PID 899 (TID 0x7ed64f7fe640) from PID 899; stack trace: ***
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed65f7644d6 google::(anonymous namespace)::FailureSignalHandler()
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed6622df520 (unknown)
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed6623339fc pthread_kill
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed6622df476 raise
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed6622c57f3 abort
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed66258ab9e (unknown)
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed66259620c (unknown)
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed662596277 std::terminate()
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed6625961fe std::rethrow_exception()
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed66282e519 rclcpp::exceptions::throw_from_rcl_error()
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed66283231c rclcpp::detail::add_guard_condition_to_rcl_wait_set()
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed662844e27 (unknown)
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed662831b05 rclcpp::Executor::wait_for_work()
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed662834883 rclcpp::Executor::get_next_executable()
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed66283b7e2 rclcpp::executors::MultiThreadedExecutor::run()
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed6625c4253 (unknown)
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed662331ac3 (unknown)
> [component_container_mt-62] @ 0x7ed6623c38c0 (unknown)
> [ERROR] [component_container_mt-62]: process has died [pid 899, exit code -6, cmd '/opt/ros/humble/lib/rclcpp_components/component_container_mt --ros-args -r __node:=behavior_planning_container -r __ns:=/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning -p use_sim_time:=False -p wheel_radius:=0.305 -p wheel_width:=0.185 -p wheel_base:=2.755 -p wheel_tread:=1.469 -p front_overhang:=0.721 -p rear_overhang:=0.666 -p left_overhang:=0.128 -p right_overhang:=0.128 -p vehicle_height:=2.44 -p max_steer_angle:=0.7 -p use_sim_time:=False'].
> ```
> 
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Launch the planning_simulator.
> 2. Set the vehicle initial pose.
> 3. Launch script to publish the planning goal. 
> 4. Wait till the behavior_path_planner dies. It always happens.
> 
> Limiting the docker container cpu resources will help.
> 
> ---
> The planning_goal_abuse_runner test tool.
> 
> ```
> #!/usr/bin/env python3
> """
> Standalone runner for the planning goal abuse scenario.
> 
> Procedure:
>   1. Wait for behavior_path_planner and mission_planner to come online.
>   2. Publish the vehicle initial pose once.
>   3. Continuously publish planning goals at random intervals.
>   4. Monitor required nodes; exit(1) if any node disappears (crash detected).
> """
> import random
> import sys
> import threading
> import time
> import rclpy
> from geometry_msgs.msg import PoseStamped, PoseWithCovarianceStamped
> 
> STARTUP_TIMEOUT    = 120.0  # seconds to wait for required nodes after launch
> CHECK_INTERVAL     = 0.2    # seconds between liveness checks
> GOAL_MIN_INTERVAL  = 0.25   # minimum random delay between goal publications (s)
> GOAL_MAX_INTERVAL  = 1.5    # maximum random delay between goal publications (s)
> INITIAL_POSE_TOPIC = "/initialpose"
> GOAL_TOPIC         = "/planning/mission_planning/goal"
> MAP_FRAME          = "map"
> INITIAL_POSE = dict(
>     x  =  219.064,
>     y  =  579.993,
>     z  =   20.311,
>     ox =    0.0,
>     oy =    0.0,
>     oz =    0.838,
>     ow =    0.545,
> )
> GOAL_POSE = dict(
>     x  =  133.534,
>     y  =  778.934,
>     z  =    0.0,
>     ox =    0.0,
>     oy =    0.0,
>     oz =    0.831,
>     ow =    0.556,
> )
> REQUIRED_NODES = [
>     "behavior_path_planner",
>     "mission_planner",
> ]
> 
> 
> def _wait_for_nodes(node, node_names, timeout):
>     """Block until every name in *node_names* appears in the ROS 2 graph."""
>     deadline = time.time() + timeout
>     while time.time() < deadline:
>         alive = node.get_node_names()
>         missing = [n for n in node_names if n not in alive]
>         if not missing:
>             node.get_logger().info(f"All required nodes online: {node_names}")
>             return
>         node.get_logger().info(
>             f"Waiting for nodes: {missing}",
>             throttle_duration_sec=5.0,
>         )
>         time.sleep(1.0)
>     alive = node.get_node_names()
>     missing = [n for n in node_names if n not in alive]
>     raise TimeoutError(
>         f"Required nodes not available after {timeout} s. Missing: {missing}"
>     )
> 
> 
> def _publish_initial_pose(node, pub):
>     msg = PoseWithCovarianceStamped()
>     msg.header.stamp            = node.get_clock().now().to_msg()
>     msg.header.frame_id         = MAP_FRAME
>     msg.pose.pose.position.x    = INITIAL_POSE["x"]
>     msg.pose.pose.position.y    = INITIAL_POSE["y"]
>     msg.pose.pose.position.z    = INITIAL_POSE["z"]
>     msg.pose.pose.orientation.x = INITIAL_POSE["ox"]
>     msg.pose.pose.orientation.y = INITIAL_POSE["oy"]
>     msg.pose.pose.orientation.z = INITIAL_POSE["oz"]
>     msg.pose.pose.orientation.w = INITIAL_POSE["ow"]
>     msg.pose.covariance         = [0.0] * 36
>     msg.pose.covariance[0]      = 0.25     # x variance
>     msg.pose.covariance[7]      = 0.25     # y variance
>     msg.pose.covariance[35]     = 0.06854  # yaw variance
>     pub.publish(msg)
>     node.get_logger().info("Published initial pose.")
> 
> 
> def _goal_abuse_loop(node, pub, stop_event):
>     """Publish planning goals at random intervals until *stop_event* is set."""
>     while not stop_event.is_set():
>         msg = PoseStamped()
>         msg.header.stamp            = node.get_clock().now().to_msg()
>         msg.header.frame_id         = MAP_FRAME
>         msg.pose.position.x         = GOAL_POSE["x"]
>         msg.pose.position.y         = GOAL_POSE["y"]
>         msg.pose.position.z         = GOAL_POSE["z"]
>         msg.pose.orientation.x      = GOAL_POSE["ox"]
>         msg.pose.orientation.y      = GOAL_POSE["oy"]
>         msg.pose.orientation.z      = GOAL_POSE["oz"]
>         msg.pose.orientation.w      = GOAL_POSE["ow"]
>         interval = random.uniform(GOAL_MIN_INTERVAL, GOAL_MAX_INTERVAL)
>         node.get_logger().info(
>             f"Publishing planning goal (next in {interval:.2f} s)..."
>         )
>         pub.publish(msg)
>         stop_event.wait(timeout=interval)
> 
> 
> def main():
>     rclpy.init()
>     node = rclpy.create_node("planning_goal_abuse_runner")
> 
>     initial_pose_pub = node.create_publisher(
>         PoseWithCovarianceStamped, INITIAL_POSE_TOPIC, 1
>     )
>     goal_pub = node.create_publisher(PoseStamped, GOAL_TOPIC, 10)
> 
>     spin_thread = threading.Thread(
>         target=rclpy.spin, args=(node,), daemon=True
>     )
>     spin_thread.start()
> 
>     exit_code = 0
>     stop_event = threading.Event()
>     abuse_thread = None
> 
>     try:
>         # Step 1 ΓÇö wait for the planning stack.
>         _wait_for_nodes(node, REQUIRED_NODES, timeout=STARTUP_TIMEOUT)
> 
>         # Step 2 ΓÇö publish initial pose once and let the system settle.
>         _publish_initial_pose(node, initial_pose_pub)
>         time.sleep(1.0)
> 
>         # Step 3 ΓÇö start goal abuse in a background thread.
>         abuse_thread = threading.Thread(
>             target=_goal_abuse_loop,
>             args=(node, goal_pub, stop_event),
>             daemon=True,
>         )
>         abuse_thread.start()
> 
>         # Step 4 ΓÇö monitor required nodes; exit if any disappear.
>         node.get_logger().info(
>             f"Monitoring {REQUIRED_NODES} for crashes..."
>         )
>         monitor_start = time.time()
>         while True:
>             alive = node.get_node_names()
>             missing = [n for n in REQUIRED_NODES if n not in alive]
>             if missing:
>                 uptime = time.time() - monitor_start
>                 node.get_logger().error(
>                     f"Node(s) disappeared (crash detected): {missing} "
>                     f"after {uptime:.1f} s of monitoring"
>                 )
>                 exit_code = 1
>                 break
>             time.sleep(CHECK_INTERVAL)
> 
>     except KeyboardInterrupt:
>         node.get_logger().info("Interrupted by user.")
>     except Exception as e:
>         node.get_logger().error(f"Fatal error: {e}")
>         exit_code = 1
>     finally:
>         stop_event.set()
>         if abuse_thread is not None:
>             abuse_thread.join(timeout=GOAL_MAX_INTERVAL + 1.0)
>         node.destroy_node()
>         rclpy.shutdown()
> 
>     sys.exit(exit_code)
> 
> 
> if __name__ == "__main__":
>     main()
> ```
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS2 Humble
> - Autoware version: 0.48, 0.49, 0.50
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The crash is caused by the deleted `lane_parking_timer_cb_group_` and `freespace_parking_timer_cb_group_` callback groups. When a planning goal is published, the `GoalPlannerModule` instance is deleter with its callback groups. But weak pointers to these callback groups are stored in the Node Executor and might be suddenly accessed by this weak pointer. The callback groups suppose to stay alive and be available whole time while the node and executor is running. 
> 
> The crash happens in the situation when the node executor tries to lock a timer callback group using a weak smart pointer, fails and throw exception. Because of this exception the whole executor and behavior path planner dies.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> Any callback groups in ROS2 should never be deleted while the node is running. 
> But there is a quick hack that can help with a crash. The `freespace_parking_timer_cb_group_` and `lane_parking_timer_cb_group_` can be static class properties. This fixed the issue for me.
> 
> ---
> Changes in the goal_planner_module.hpp:
> ```
> static rclcpp::CallbackGroup::SharedPtr lane_parking_timer_cb_group_;
> static rclcpp::CallbackGroup::SharedPtr freespace_parking_timer_cb_group_;
> ```
> 
> ---
> Changes in the goal_planner_module.cpp:
> ```
> rclcpp::CallbackGroup::SharedPtr GoalPlannerModule::lane_parking_timer_cb_group_           = nullptr;
> rclcpp::CallbackGroup::SharedPtr GoalPlannerModule::freespace_parking_timer_cb_group_ = nullptr;
> 
> // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
> 
> if (!lane_parking_timer_cb_group_) {
>     lane_parking_timer_cb_group_ = node.create_callback_group(rclcpp::CallbackGroupType::MutuallyExclusive);
>   }
> 
> // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
> 
> if (!freespace_parking_timer_cb_group_) {
>       freespace_parking_timer_cb_group_ = node.create_callback_group(rclcpp::CallbackGroupType::MutuallyExclusive);
> }
> ```

### #12454 — Fix cppcheck CI: weekly has been failing for over a year

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-04-09  |  **Closed:** 2026-04-09  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12454

**Body:**

> ### Problem
> 
> `cppcheck-weekly` has been failing every single run for over 14 months (59+ consecutive failures since at least Feb 2025).
> 
> See the [workflow run history](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/actions/workflows/cppcheck-weekly.yaml) -- every run is red. [Latest failing run (2026-04-06)](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/actions/runs/24013883752).
> 
> Latest error breakdown (2026-04-06):
> 
> | Count | Error ID | Severity |
> |-------|----------|----------|
> | 369 | useStlAlgorithm | style |
> | 79 | useInitializationList | performance |
> | 39 | unusedFunction | style |
> | 2,047 | missingInclude | information |
> | 10,699 | missingIncludeSystem | information |
> | 5 | unmatchedSuppression | information |
> 
> ### Proposed improvements
> 
> #### Both workflows
> 
> 1. **Switch to `ubuntu-latest` with `ros:jazzy` container** and replace `snap install cppcheck` with `apt install cppcheck`. The original comment states that cppcheck from apt doesn't support `--check-level`, but this is only true for Ubuntu 22.04. Ubuntu 24.04 (jazzy) ships a version that supports it natively:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/4fbfaac075bcc46711195130bdf5b312ed57034d/.github/workflows/cppcheck-differential.yaml#L32
> 
>    | Platform | cppcheck version | `--check-level` support |
>    |----------|-----------------|------------------------|
>    | Ubuntu 22.04 (apt) | 2.7 | No |
>    | Ubuntu 24.04 (apt) | 2.13.0 | Yes |
>    | Snap | 2.13.99 | Yes |
> 
>    This eliminates the fragile snap dependency (snap store intermittently returns 503 errors). Using the ROS container also provides colcon out of the box.
> 
> 2. **Update `actions/checkout` to `@v6`.**
> 
> #### `cppcheck-weekly`
> 
> 3. **Fix or suppress the cppcheck findings** so the weekly job goes green.
> 4. **Add failure notifications** so scheduled workflow failures don't go unnoticed for over a year.
> 
> #### `cppcheck-differential`
> 
> 5. **Remove colcon installation from scratch.** The `ros:jazzy` container already includes colcon.

### #12452 — Switch check-build-depends to universe-devel-jazzy container and rename build_depends_humble.repos

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-04-09  |  **Closed:** 2026-04-09  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12452

**Body:**

> ## Problem
> 
> The `check-build-depends` workflow currently runs on `ros:humble` container, which does not have `acados` installed. This causes `autoware_path_optimizer` to fail with:
> 
> ```
> CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:20 (find_package):
>   Could not find a package configuration file provided by "acados"
> ```
> 
> Our `build-and-test` workflows use the `ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-devel` images that include `acados` and other dependencies. The `check-build-depends` workflow should use the same image.
> 
> ### Affected PRs
> 
> All of these PRs are blocked by this CI failure:
> 
> - #12365 - feat(build_depends_humble.repos): minor update autowarefoundation/autoware_utils to 1.7.1
> - #12388 - feat(build_depends_humble.repos): major update autowarefoundation/autoware_lanelet2_extension to 1.0.0
> - #12343 - feat(build_depends_humble.repos): patch update autowarefoundation/autoware_core to 1.7.2
> 
> ## Proposed changes
> 
> 1. **Switch container to `universe-devel` image** - Use `ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-devel-jazzy` instead of `ros:humble`, matching what `build-and-test` uses.
> 2. **Run against jazzy only** - Drop the humble matrix entry since jazzy is the primary target.
> 3. **Rename `build_depends_humble.repos` to `build_depends_stable.repos`** - The file contains pinned/stable versions and is not humble-specific. The name should reflect its purpose rather than a specific ROS distro.
> 4. **Update all references** - Update the workflow, combine-repos-action usage, and any documentation that references the old filename.

> ## Affected packages by check

> ### `bugprone-unchecked-optional-access` (284 errors)

### #12429 — ci(codecov): differential PR builds should upload under the same flag as total builds

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-04-08  |  **Closed:** 2026-04-08  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12429

**Body:**

> ## Problem
> 
> The current Codecov setup uses separate flags for total and differential builds:
> 
> - **Full builds** (`build-and-test.yaml`) upload under `total-jazzy-cuda`
> - **Differential PR builds** (`build-and-test-differential.yaml`) upload under `differential-jazzy-cuda`
> 
> In [`codecov.yaml`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/codecov.yaml#L17-L31), `carryforward` is configured per-flag:
> 
> ```yaml
> flag_management:
>   default_rules:
>     carryforward: false
>   individual_flags:
>     - name: differential-jazzy-cuda
>       carryforward: true
> ```
> 
> The intent is for differential PR builds to carry forward coverage so that the PR shows a complete coverage picture. However, **carryforward in Codecov is strictly per-flag** ([docs](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/carryforward-flags#how-carryforward-flags-work-a-motivating-example)). This means `differential-jazzy-cuda` only carries forward from previous `differential-jazzy-cuda` uploads, never from `total-jazzy-cuda`.
> 
> Since differential builds only test changed packages, the carried-forward baseline is incomplete and patchy -- it's whatever packages happened to be tested in previous PRs, not a full picture of the codebase.
> 
> ## How Codecov merges flags
> 
> All flag uploads are merged into a single unified total for the commit/PR. From the [flags documentation](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/flags):
> 
> > "The reports will be merged and contribute to the project's total coverage and the total coverage of the files covered under the flag."
> 
> Flags create categorized *views* of coverage, but the overall project coverage is the union of all uploaded (and carried-forward) flag data. This means if we upload differential coverage under the **same flag** as total, Codecov will merge fresh partial data with carried-forward full-build data.
> 
> ## Proposed fix
> 
> Upload differential PR builds under the same flag as total builds (`total-jazzy-cuda`) and enable carryforward on that flag.
> 
> ### 1. `codecov.yaml`
> 
> ```yaml
> flag_management:
>   default_rules:
>     carryforward: false
>     statuses:
>       - name_prefix: project-
>         type: project
>         target: 0%
>         threshold: 100%
>       - name_prefix: patch-
>         type: patch
>         target: 0%
>         threshold: 100%
>   individual_flags:
>     - name: total-jazzy-cuda
>       carryforward: true
> ```
> 
> ### 2. `.github/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml`
> 
> ```diff
> -          flags: differential-${{ inputs.rosdistro }}-cuda
> +          flags: total-${{ inputs.rosdistro }}-cuda
> ```
> 
> ### How this works
> 
> 1. Full build on `main` uploads complete coverage under `total-jazzy-cuda` -- establishes the baseline
> 2. PR differential build uploads partial coverage under the **same** `total-jazzy-cuda` flag
> 3. Codecov merges fresh partial data with carried-forward full-build data from the base branch
> 4. PR comment shows accurate total coverage impact
> 
> This is the [recommended pattern](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/carryforward-flags#before-getting-started) for monorepos and partial/delta testing setups.
> 
> ## References
> 
> - [Codecov: Carryforward Flags](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/carryforward-flags)
> - [Codecov: Flags](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/flags)
> - Current config: [`codecov.yaml`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/codecov.yaml)
> - Differential upload: [`build-and-test-differential.yaml#L143`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml#L143)
> - Total upload: [`build-and-test.yaml#L34`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-and-test.yaml#L34)
> 
> ## Related PRs
> 
> - #12413 - ci(workflow): merge upload-coverage job into build-and-test
> - #12417 - ci(codecov): disable search and bump to v6
> - #12418 - ci(codecov): limit differential upload to jazzy-cuda and disable global carryforward
> - #12422 - ci(codecov): add upload-coverage param to limit coverage uploads
> - #12427 - ci(codecov): disable gcov plugin to speed up uploads

### #12399 — fix(autoware_tensorrt_yolox): missing cstdint include and ament_index_cpp test dependency

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-03-31  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-31  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12399

**Body:**

> ## Description
> 
> `autoware_tensorrt_yolox` fails to compile on Ubuntu 24.04 / ROS 2 Jazzy with two errors:
> 
> ### 1. Missing `#include <cstdint>` in `label.hpp`
> 
> [`label.hpp`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/fe12efd70793bd1d5b4e06a20016dd2c9e1803d2/perception/autoware_tensorrt_yolox/include/autoware/tensorrt_yolox/label.hpp) uses `uint32_t` but does not include `<cstdint>`. This causes compilation to fail:
> 
> ```
> include/autoware/tensorrt_yolox/label.hpp:38:33: error: 'uint32_t' has not been declared
> ```
> 
> ### 2. Missing `ament_index_cpp` test dependency
> 
> [`test/test_label.cpp`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/fe12efd70793bd1d5b4e06a20016dd2c9e1803d2/perception/autoware_tensorrt_yolox/test/test_label.cpp) includes `<ament_index_cpp/get_package_share_directory.hpp>` but `ament_index_cpp` is not listed as a `<test_depend>` in [`package.xml`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/fe12efd70793bd1d5b4e06a20016dd2c9e1803d2/perception/autoware_tensorrt_yolox/package.xml). This causes the test to fail:
> 
> ```
> test/test_label.cpp:15:10: fatal error: ament_index_cpp/get_package_share_directory.hpp: No such file or directory
> ```
> 
> ## Fix
> 
> 1. Add `#include <cstdint>` to `label.hpp`
> 2. Add `<test_depend>ament_index_cpp</test_depend>` to `package.xml`

---

### #12398 — Incorrect mpc_lateral_controller behavior

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-03-31  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @smk-robotics
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:control
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12398

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In the latest releases (0.50.0, 0.49.0, and 0.48.0), we found that the actual predicted trajectory produced by the autoware_mpc_lateral_controller is incorrect and does not follow the reference trajectory in corners. Because of this, all of the safety checks for a predicted trajectory are triggered, including the lane departure check, as well as the control and planning validator checks.
> 
> An additional problem is that the visualization in RViz for the predicted trajectory is incorrect. It visualizes a debug predicted trajectory in the Frenet coordinate system, which is not actually used anywhere in the stack.
> 
> <img width="825" height="996" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ae06e0c-7616-43b6-b1e6-a96d9786cac5" />
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea2a81b7-73e2-47ae-9a16-1d3109c88e79
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The /control/trajectory_follower/lateral/predicted_trajectory is optimized to follow the reference trajectory at all times, not just for the first couple of meters before straightening out.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The predicted trajectory from the /control/trajectory_follower/lateral/predicted_trajectory topic, which is used everywhere in the stack, is not following the reference trajectory in corners. This is triggering the lane departure and control validator safety checks.
> 
> Only the predicted trajectory in Frenet coordinates, which is used solely for debug visualization purposes, is actually following the reference trajectory perfectly for some reason. You can see the worst-case scenario on the image below. For some reason, the predicted trajectory just gives up on following the reference trajectory after a few meters. This is incorrect behavior for the model predictive lateral controller.
> 
> <img width="843" height="1159" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/326484fd-36a0-4e9d-94ab-97921a204ad5" />
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Pull the latest universe-cuda image (ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-cuda).
> 2. Download the standard Autoware sample map. 
> 3. Launch the docker container with the stack 
> `docker run -it --rm --gpus all \                                                                                                                                                                                                                -e DISPLAY=$DISPLAY \
> -e QT_X11_NO_MITSHM=1 \
> -e NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all \
> -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all \
> -e XAUTHORITY=/tmp/.docker.xauth \
> -e XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR \
> -v /tmp/.X11-unix:/tmp/.X11-unix \
> -v /tmp/.docker.xauth:/tmp/.docker.xauth:ro \
> -v /home/map:/autoware/map \
> ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-cuda \`
> 4. Fix issue with the missing trajectoris and paths visualization by installing the  ros-humble-rviz-2d-overlay-plugins package (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/issues/6971).
> 5. Launch the planning simulator 
> `ros2 launch autoware_launch planning_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=/autoware/map`
> 6. Fix the visualization in RViz. Go to "Displays" panel in RViz and open: Control -> Predicted Trajectory.
> Switch the topic from: "/control/trajectory_follower/controller_node_exe/debug/predicted_trajectory_in_frenet_coordinate" to: "/control/trajectory_follower/lateral/predicted_trajectory". It's even better to visualize both of them at the same time and the reference trajectory.
> 7. Check the deviation in 90 degree turns. The predicted trajectory is going outside of the lane.
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS: ROS2 Humble:
> - Autoware: 0.50.0, 0.49.0, 0.48.0 
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> - Removed current steering angle component from the mpc state matrix.
> - Other changes in the mpc processing pipeline.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> When the prediction horizon becomes bigger, the problem is getting way worse. The predicted trajectory goes outside of the current lane in 100% cases in turns which is triggering the lane departure checker safety check and basically any other check for a predicted trajectory.
> 
> <img width="843" height="1203" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05883d72-c018-4f31-beaa-6b4113cfa5a9" />

> 
> Sorry for the delayed response.
> Regarding the reported issue it is most likely related to how the world coordinate trajectory is generated, specifically the function [calculatePredictedTrajectoryInWorldCoordinate](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/control/autoware_mpc_lateral_controller/src/vehicle_model/vehicle_model_bicycle_kinematics.cpp#L72)

### #12340 — `goal_pose_visualizer` crashes: class not found in libgoal_pose_visualizer_component.so in container universe-devel-cuda-1.7.1-jazzy-amd64

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-03-17  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-31  |  **Author:** @hsule
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12340

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The `goal_pose_visualizer` node dies on startup because it cannot find the component class in libgoal_pose_visualizer_component.so.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> `goal_pose_visualizer` should start successfully.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> ```
> [goal_pose_visualizer-41] [ERROR] [1773742174.834126501] [goal_pose_visualizer]: Class rclcpp_components::NodeFactoryTemplate<autoware::mission_planner_universe::GoalPoseVisualizer> not found in library libgoal_pose_visualizer_component.so
> [ERROR] [goal_pose_visualizer-41]: process has died [pid 666, exit code 1, cmd '/opt/autoware/lib/autoware_mission_planner_universe/goal_pose_visualizer --ros-args -r __node:=goal_pose_visualizer -r __ns:=/planning/mission_planning -p use_sim_time:=True -p wheel_radius:=0.383 -p wheel_width:=0.235 -p wheel_base:=2.79 -p wheel_tread:=1.64 -p front_overhang:=1.0 -p rear_overhang:=1.1 -p left_overhang:=0.128 -p right_overhang:=0.128 -p vehicle_height:=2.5 -p max_steer_angle:=0.7 -p use_sim_time:=True -p use_sim_time:=True -p use_sim_time:=True -p wheel_radius:=0.383 -p wheel_width:=0.235 -p wheel_base:=2.79 -p wheel_tread:=1.64 -p front_overhang:=1.0 -p rear_overhang:=1.1 -p left_overhang:=0.128 -p right_overhang:=0.128 -p vehicle_height:=2.5 -p max_steer_angle:=0.7 -p use_sim_time:=True -p wheel_radius:=0.383 -p wheel_width:=0.235 -p wheel_base:=2.79 -p wheel_tread:=1.64 -p front_overhang:=1.0 -p rear_overhang:=1.1 -p left_overhang:=0.128 -p right_overhang:=0.128 -p vehicle_height:=2.5 -p max_steer_angle:=0.7 -p use_sim_time:=True -p wheel_radius:=0.383 -p wheel_width:=0.235 -p wheel_base:=2.79 -p wheel_tread:=1.64 -p front_overhang:=1.0 -p rear_overhang:=1.1 -p left_overhang:=0.128 -p right_overhang:=0.128 -p vehicle_height:=2.5 -p max_steer_angle:=0.7 -p use_sim_time:=True -p wheel_radius:=0.383 -p wheel_width:=0.235 -p wheel_base:=2.79 -p wheel_tread:=1.64 -p front_overhang:=1.0 -p rear_overhang:=1.1 -p left_overhang:=0.128 -p right_overhang:=0.128 -p vehicle_height:=2.5 -p max_steer_angle:=0.7 -r input/route:=/planning/mission_planning/route -r output/goal_pose:=/planning/mission_planning/echo_back_goal_pose'].
> ```
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Launch Autoware using container ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-devel-cuda-1.7.1-jazzy-amd64
> 2. `goal_pose_visualizer` dies on startup
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 24.04
> - ROS 2: Jazzy
> - Autoware: 1.7.1 (Jazzy)
> - Container: ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-devel-cuda-1.7.1-jazzy-amd64
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The component class is not properly registered in `autoware_mission_planner_universe`, but the same component works in `autoware_mission_planner` (core).
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> Workaround: replacing the launch include from `autoware_mission_planner_universe` to `autoware_mission_planner` resolves the issue:
> ```
> sudo sed -i 's|autoware_mission_planner_universe)/launch/goal_pose_visualizer|autoware_mission_planner)/launch/goal_pose_visualizer|' /opt/autoware/share/tier4_planning_launch/launch/mission_planning/mission_planning.launch.xml
> ```                                                  
> This suggests the component class is properly registered in `autoware_mission_planner` (core) but not in `autoware_mission_planner_universe`.

### #12317 — feat(autoware_tensorrt_genad): Add TensorRT-accelerated GenAD end-to-end driving package

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-03-16  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @YSH-research
- **Labels:** type:improvement, status:stale
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12317

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> ## Summary
> Add a new package autoware_tensorrt_genad that integrates GenAD 
> (Generalized Autonomous Driving) as a TensorRT-accelerated 
> end-to-end planning module for Autoware.
> 
> ## Vision
> The ultimate goal is to build an E2E + Rule-Based hybrid platform 
> in Autoware that is capable of obstacle avoidance, and to demonstrate 
> it in both CARLA simulation and real-vehicle driving. 
> This package is the first step toward that goal.
> 
> ## Background
> - GenAD is a vision-based end-to-end autonomous driving model that performs perception and planning jointly.
> - Training and validation have been completed on B2D dataset (GenAD_no_hlc variant).
> - TensorRT quantization (FP16) is nearly complete.
> - This follows the same pattern as the existing autoware_tensorrt_vad package.
> 
> ## Related
> - Reference package: autoware_tensorrt_vad
> - Model: [GenAD paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11502)
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Enable real-time end-to-end autonomous driving inference in Autoware by deploying GenAD with TensorRT acceleration. This provides an alternative E2E planning model alongside autoware_tensorrt_vad, with improved trajectory prediction performance validated on the B2D dataset.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. Follow the existing autoware_tensorrt_vad package structure as a reference implementation
> 2. Export GenAD (GenAD_no_hlc variant) to ONNX, then build TensorRT engine (FP16)
> 3. Wrap the inference pipeline in a ROS2 node with Autoware-compatible trajectory output interface
> 4. Reuse the DL4AGX pipeline for ONNX-to-TensorRT conversion
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] autoware_tensorrt_genad package builds successfully in Autoware workspace
> - [ ] TensorRT engine runs inference with FP16 precision
> - [ ] ROS2 node publishes trajectory messages compatible with Autoware planning stack
> - [ ] Launch files and README documentation are provided
> - [ ] Basic performance benchmark (latency, FPS) is documented

### #12270 — convex_hull() in common/alt_geometry can cause infinite recursion and stack overflow

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-03-10  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** type:bug, type:arm64, status:stale, component:common
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12270

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> On ARM64 environment, the function convex_hull() can cause infinite recursive calls of make_hull() lambda (may be due to floating point precision different from that of x86/AMD).
> It triggers stack overflow and makes CI unit tests fail.
> 
> I issued a dummy draft [PR #12267](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12267) to show the situation and the possible cause of the problem.
> (The dummy draft PR will be closed when this issue is solved and closed.)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> convex_hull() never causes infinite recursion with any possible data (including the data used in the CI unit test).
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> convex_hull() can cause infinite recursion on ARM64 environment with the data used in the CI unit test.
> It triggers stack overflow and the following results:
> * CI unit tests fail on ARM64
> * Autoware on ARM64 may run into severe problems (including segmentation fault or freeze) depending on data.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> See the result of unit tests in [PR #12267](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12267) .
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS2: Humble
> - Autoware: 2f64d6c6f0a4702a4e79f5e340a890a9d175cce7 (autoware_universe)
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> There are 2 problems with the code.
> 
> 1. The function is_above() does not treat "nealy zero" as 0. The precision of float calculation is different on ARM64.
> 2. The lambda make_hull() puts "farthest" point itself into "subset1" or "subset2".
> 
> I believe these 2 problems should be fixed.
> * is_above() should be fixed to work on any CPU architecture.
> * make_hull() should be fixed to avoid infinite recursion even if any mathematical error occurs. 
> 
> However, I don't think I'm qualified to fix these problems because I'm not familiar with the geometrical logic used here.
> I'll attach my conversation with Github CoPilot on this issue.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2026-03-10)

> The following is the markdown log of the conversation between Github CoPilot and me (User).
> I haven't scrutinized the answer and I can't guarantee that it is correct, but I hope that it can be help.
> 
> ## User
> **I added a printf() to convex_hull() to see if infinite recursion is happening in make_hull().**
> **The following is the output. It is happening.**
> **Do you see the reason why it happens?**
> -----
> ```
> 1:  - .../test_autoware_universe_utils --gtest_output=xml:...
> 1: [==========] Running 120 tests from 16 test suites.
> 1: [----------] Global test environment set-up.
> 1: [----------] 18 tests from alt_geometry
> 1: [ RUN      ] alt_geometry.area
> 1: [       OK ] alt_geometry.area (0 ms)
> 1: [ RUN      ] alt_geometry.convexHull
> 1: make_hull: p1=(2.000000, 1.300000), p2=(5.400000, 1.200000), points.size=7
> 1: make_hull: p1=(2.000000, 1.300000), p2=(4.100000, 3.000000), points.size=1
> 1: make_hull: p1=(2.000000, 1.300000), p2=(2.400000, 1.700000), points.size=1
> 1: make_hull: p1=(2.000000, 1.300000), p2=(2.400000, 1.700000), points.size=1
> ...
> 1: make_hull: p1=(2.000000, 1.300000), p2=(2.400000, 1.700000), points.size=1
> ```
> 
> ## GitHub Copilot
> Yes, the reason is clear from the logs. You have **infinite recursion** because the algorithm keeps selecting the same point as "farthest" and then re-adding it to the `subset` for the next recursive call.
> 
> ### The Mechanism of Failure
> 
> 1.  **Context**: `make_hull` is called with `p1=(2.0, 1.3)`, `p2=(2.4, 1.7)`, and a single point in `points`.
> 2.  **Selection**: `find_farthest` picks that single point. Let's call it `P_farthest`.
> 3.  **Partitioning**: The code iterates through `points` to split them into `subset1` (left of line `p1->farthest`) and `subset2` (left of line `farthest->p2`).
> 4.  **The Bug**: The `is_above` check is likely returning true for `P_farthest` itself relative to `p1->P_farthest` (or `P_farthest->p2` relative to itself) due to floating-point anomalies or an inclusive check.
> 5.  **Result**: `P_farthest` is added back into `subset1` (or `subset2`).
> 6.  **Loop**: `make_hull` is called again with `p1`, `P_farthest`, and `subset1` (which still contains `P_farthest`), leading to the exact same state forever.
> 
> ### Fix
> You must ensure that the point selected as `farthest` is **never** included in the recursive subsets.
> 
> ```cpp
> // ...existing code...
>       const auto & farthest = *find_farthest(points, p1, p2);
> 
>       alt::Points2d subset1, subset2;
>       for (const auto & point : points) {
>         // Explicitly skip the farthest point to prevent infinite recursion
>         if (equals(point, farthest)) {
>           continue;
>         }
> // ...
> ```
> 
> ## User
> **It seems that the infinite recursive occurs only on AMD64, not on x86/AMD.**
> **Can you explain the reason?**
> 
> ## GitHub Copilot
> The reason for the discrepancy between architectures (likely **x86 32-bit** vs **x86-64/AMD64**) is almost certainly due to differences in floating-point precision standards.
> 
> ### 1. The Root Cause: Extended Precision (x87) vs. SSE/AVX
> *   **x86 (32-bit)**: Historically, 32-bit x86 Linux applications often use the **x87 FPU** for floating-point math. The x87 FPU operates internally with **80-bit extended precision** (long double).
> *   **AMD64 (64-bit)**: The x86-64 ABI mandates the use of **SSE/SSE2** registers for floating-point operations. SSE arithmetic is strictly **64-bit IEEE 754** compliant.
> 
> ### 2. How This Affects Geometry
> The infinite recursion happens because of a check like `is_above(point, p1, farthest)`.
> 
> Mathematically, a point $P$ cannot be "strictly above" the line segment $(P1, P)$. However, with floating-point math:
> *   **On AMD64 (SSE)**: The value is computed with strict 64-bit precision. If there is a tiny epsilon error (e.g., $1.0 \times 10^{-17}$), the geometric check might return `true`.
> *   **On x86 (x87)**: The internal 80-bit precision might hold the intermediate result differently, resulting in exactly $0.0$ or a negative epsilon, causing the check to return `false`.
> 
> ### 3. The Fix
> Regardless of architecture, relying on exact floating-point comparisons is unsafe. The logic **must** explicitly exclude the `farthest` point from the next recursion step to guarantee termination.
> 
> ## User
> **Isn't it better to fix the bug by changing is_above() to take floating point precision into account?**
> 
> ## GitHub Copilot
> Yes, absolutely. Modifying `is_above` to handle floating-point precision (using an epsilon) is the **numerically correct** fix.
> 
> The infinite recursion happens because `is_above` likely returns `true` for a point that is effectively *on* the line (distance $\approx 0$) due to tiny floating-point errors.
> 
> ### The Fix
> 
> You should enforce a small `epsilon` threshold. A point is only "above" if it is significantly far from the line.
> 
> ```cpp
> // ...existing code...
>       // Define a robust is_above check with epsilon
>       auto is_strictly_above = [](const alt::Point2d & p, const alt::Point2d & a, const alt::Point2d & b) {
>         const double cross_product = (b.x() - a.x()) * (p.y() - a.y()) - (b.y() - a.y()) * (p.x() - a.x());
>         constexpr double epsilon = 1e-9; // Standard epsilon suitable for this scale
>         return cross_product > epsilon;
>       };
> // ...existing code...
> ```
> 
> ## User
> **Wouldn't it be better if we use the two fixes together?**
> 
> ## GitHub Copilot
> Yes, absolutely. Using both approaches together provides **Defense in Depth**.
> 
> 1.  **Geometric Robustness ($\epsilon$ check)**: This handles the general case of points that are *extremely close* to the edge but not identical to the endpoints. It prevents numerical noise from creating false "outside" points.
> 2.  **Algorithmic Safety (Explicit Skip)**: This guarantees that the algorithm *cannot* enter an infinite recursive loop on the same point, regardless of floating-point weirdness.
> 
> Here is the combined, robust implementation:
> 
> ```cpp
> // filepath: common/autoware_universe_utils/src/geometry/alt_geometry.cpp
> // ...existing code...
>     auto make_hull = [&vertices](
>                        auto self, const alt::Point2d & p1, const alt::Point2d & p2,
>                        const alt::Points2d & points) {
>       if (points.empty()) {
>         return;
>       }
>       // ...existing code...
> 
>       const auto & farthest = *find_farthest(points, p1, p2);
> 
>       // Robust check with epsilon
>       auto is_strictly_above = [](const alt::Point2d & p, const alt::Point2d & a, const alt::Point2d & b) {
>         const double cross_product = (b.x() - a.x()) * (p.y() - a.y()) - (b.y() - a.y()) * (p.x() - a.x());
>         constexpr double epsilon = 1e-9;
>         return cross_product > epsilon;
>       };
> 
>       alt::Points2d subset1, subset2;
>       for (const auto & point : points) {
>         // 1. Explicitly skip the farthest point (Safety Guarantee)
>         if (equals(point, farthest)) {
>           continue;
>         }
> 
>         // 2. Use epsilon for geometric check (Numerical Stability)
>         if (is_strictly_above(point, p1, farthest)) {
>           subset1.push_back(point);
>         } else if (is_strictly_above(point, farthest, p2)) {
>           subset2.push_back(point);
>         }
>       }
> 
>       self(self, p1, farthest, subset1);
>       vertices.push_back(farthest);
>       self(self, farthest, p2, subset2);
>     };
> 
>     alt::Points2d above_points, below_points;
> // ...existing code...
> ```

### #12259 — [collision_detector] Object filtering logic based on UUID may miss moving obstacles during keep_ignoring_time

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-03-09  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @Zuwei-Zhao
- **Labels:** type:improvement, status:stale
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12259

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> ## [collision_detector] Object filtering logic based on UUID may miss moving obstacles during `keep_ignoring_time`
> 
> ### Summary
> 
> The current object filtering logic in `collision_detector` continues to ignore an object based on its UUID, without considering whether the object has moved. This can lead to a situation where a previously static object that begins to move ΓÇö or a newly appearing dangerous obstacle that is mistakenly assigned an already-ignored UUID ΓÇö goes completely undetected for up to `keep_ignoring_time` (default: 10 seconds).
> 
> ### Affected Module
> 
> `control/autoware_collision_detector`
> 
> ### Problem Description
> 
> The current condition for keeping an object in the ignored state is:
> 
> ```
> (uuid is in ignore list)
> AND (classification unchanged)
> AND (within nearby_filter_radius)
> ```
> 
> This logic has two potential failure modes:
> 
> **Case 1 ΓÇö Object transitions from static to moving:**
> If an object is initially recognized as static and added to the ignore list, but then begins to move toward the ego vehicle within the `keep_ignoring_time` window, the system will continue to ignore it because its UUID matches. The collision detector will not re-evaluate its threat level until the ignore period expires.
> 
> **Case 2 ΓÇö UUID misassignment by the perception module:**
> The perception module may occasionally reassign a previously used UUID to a newly detected object (e.g., after a tracking loss). If the old UUID belongs to an object currently in the ignore list, the new ΓÇö potentially dangerous ΓÇö obstacle inherits the ignored status and will not be checked for collision for up to 10 seconds.
> 
> Both cases represent a safety risk, as real obstacles may go undetected during the ignore window.
> 
> ### Suggested Fix
> 
> The ignore condition should be extended to include a displacement check, binding the ignored status to both the object's identity **and its spatial stability**:
> 
> ```
> (uuid is in ignore list)
> AND (classification unchanged)
> AND (within nearby_filter_radius)
> AND (object displacement < 0.5 m, i.e., approximately static)   ΓåÉ NEW
> AND (elapsed_time < keep_ignoring_time)
> ```
> 
> If an object's displacement exceeds the threshold (e.g., 0.5 m) since it was first added to the ignore list, it should be **immediately removed from the ignore list** and re-evaluated for collision detection.
> 
> The displacement threshold (suggested: `0.5 m`) could be exposed as a configurable parameter, for example `ignore_state_max_displacement`, to allow tuning based on deployment environment.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> An ignored object that moves significantly should lose its ignored status immediately, regardless of whether `keep_ignoring_time` has elapsed.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> An ignored object retains its ignored status for the full `keep_ignoring_time` duration (default 10 s), even if it has moved into a dangerous position.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> This logic has two potential failure modes:
> 
> **Case 1 ΓÇö Object transitions from static to moving:**
> If an object is initially recognized as static and added to the ignore list, but then begins to move toward the ego vehicle within the `keep_ignoring_time` window, the system will continue to ignore it because its UUID matches. The collision detector will not re-evaluate its threat level until the ignore period expires.
> 
> **Case 2 ΓÇö UUID misassignment by the perception module:**
> The perception module may occasionally reassign a previously used UUID to a newly detected object (e.g., after a tracking loss). If the old UUID belongs to an object currently in the ignore list, the new ΓÇö potentially dangerous ΓÇö obstacle inherits the ignored status and will not be checked for collision for up to 10 seconds.
> 
> Both cases represent a safety risk, as real obstacles may go undetected during the ignore window.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> ### Related Parameters
> 
> | Parameter | Default | Description |
> |---|---|---|
> | `keep_ignoring_time` | 10.0 s | Duration to keep ignoring a filtered object |
> | `nearby_filter_radius` | 5.0 m | Radius within which objects may be filtered |
> | `nearby_object_type_filters` | `{unknown: true}` | Object types subject to filtering |
> 
> ### Suggested New Parameter
> 
> | Parameter | Suggested Default | Description |
> |---|---|---|
> | `ignore_state_max_displacement` | 0.5 m | Maximum displacement allowed before an ignored object is re-evaluated |

### #12215 — `autoware_component_monitor` reports `process_memory_bytes` 1024x smaller when `top` RES has no unit suffix

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2026-02-27  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @mikeedi
- **Labels:** status:stale, type:build
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12215

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> `autoware_component_monitor` reads the `RES` column from `top` (`top -b -n 1 -E k -p <pid>`) and converts it to bytes.
> 
> On Ubuntu/procps `top`, when `RES` is displayed **without a unit suffix**, the value is **KiB**, not bytes ([source](https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/xenial/man1/top.1.html)).
> 
> Current implementation [treats](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/system/autoware_component_monitor/src/component_monitor_node.cpp#L149) a suffix-less number as **bytes**, so `process_memory_bytes` becomes ~`1024x` smaller than the real RSS.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> process_memory_bytes should always represent the process memory in bytes, regardless of how top formats RES.
> 
> If RES is printed without a suffix, it should be interpreted as KiB (i.e. RES * 1024), or top should be invoked/configured so the task area always has an explicit unit suffix (so parsing is unambiguous).
> 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> autoware_component_monitor reads the RES column from:
>   `top -b -n 1 -E k -p <pid>`
> 
> When top prints RES without a unit suffix (e.g. "14020"), that value is in KiB, but the current implementation treats a suffix-less value as bytes.
> 
> Example (Ubuntu 22.04 / procps 3.3.17):
> 
> ```bash
> $ top -b -n 1 -E k -p 3136933 
> ...
>     PID USER      PR  NI    VIRT    RES    SHR S  %CPU  %MEM     TIME+ COMMAND
> 3136933 mikhail   20   0  547020  14020  11160 S   0.0   0.0   0:00.75 autoware_compon
> 
> ```
> RES=14020 means 14020 KiB = 14020 * 1024 = 14356480 bytes, but the suffix-less parsing path interprets it as 14020 bytes (1024x under-report).
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. `ros2 run autoware_component_monitor autoware_component_monitor_node --ros-args -p publish_rate:=5.0`
> 2. `ros2 topic echo /component_monitor/component_system_usage --once`
> 3. take `PID` and paste to command `top -b -n 1 -E k -p PID`
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Any of these fixes would solve it:
> 
> 1. Treat suffix-less values as **KiB**:
>    - Change `parse_memory_res()` digit-only branch to `kib_to_bytes(...)`.
> 
> 2. Force `top` to print `RES` with a suffix (e.g. `-e m`) and keep parsing by suffix.
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #12176 — Removing the direct glog integration from some nodes (perception nodes)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-02-25  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-16  |  **Author:** @TetsuKawa
- **Labels:** type:improvement
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/12176

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> To enable backtraces on nodes applying Agnocast and CIE, glog was integrated into the main function of Agnocast.
> 
> Our understanding is that the forked [tier4/glog](https://github.com/tier4/glog) is used instead of the standard apt package to prevent double initialization of glog. The forked version allows us to call `google::IsGoogleLoggingInitialized()`, which is not available in the standard apt version.
> 
> **Problem**
> Currently, we are encountering the following dependency issues with the Agnocast integration:
> 
> - Autoware uses the forked version of glog. If we specify this in Agnocast, an error occurs on the ROS 2 Buildfarm because the glog rosdep key does not exist.
> - Conversely, if we specify the correct rosdep key (libgoogle-glog-dev) in Agnocast, a version mismatch error occurs in packages that depend on both Autoware's forked glog and Agnocast.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To resolve the dependency conflict, we will remove the direct glog integration from autoware_universe nodes.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Removed tier4/glog from autoware_universe.
> 
> Impact:
> 
> - AWF Autoware: As a trade-off, backtraces will no longer be obtainable when this node is launched as part of AWF's Autoware.
> 
> **Notes**
> However, in Ubuntu24, `google::IsGoogleLoggingInitialized()` is available in the standard apt version([v0.6.0](https://github.com/google/glog/tree/v0.6.0)). Each nodes is able to use apt version glog again.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Removed glog from following:
> 
> - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12163
> - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12164
> - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12165
> - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12166
> - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12167
> - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12225
> - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/12226

> > Cuda Runtime (out of memory) 1770828917.4040604 [

### #11961 — Lane Change Fails Initially but Succeeds After Reversing

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-01-22  |  **Closed:** 2026-01-30  |  **Author:** @yuntianyi-chen
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11961

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The Autoware ego vehicle fails to initiate a valid lane change despite having sufficient clear space and a valid route. The planning module keeps the vehicle in the current lane without triggering the maneuver. However, if the vehicle is manually reversed (moved backward) a short distance, the planner successfully generates a lane change trajectory, and the vehicle executes the maneuver. This indicates a potential issue with how the lane change start conditions or safety checks are evaluated when the vehicle is at a specific position or velocity state.
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9761c463-7b9d-4a40-b51f-94bfa49764b2
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> When the ego vehicle is positioned in a lane with a clear target lane and a goal that requires a lane change, the system should immediately plan and execute the lane change maneuver. It should not require the vehicle to be repositioned (reversed) to trigger the planning logic.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The vehicle remains in its current lane and does not attempt to change lanes, even though the visualization shows the target lane is unobstructed. The path planning visualization indicates the vehicle intends to continue straight. After the vehicle is manually moved backward, the planner re-evaluates and immediately generates a valid lane change path.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Launch Autoware (e.g., using the planning simulator).
> 
> 2. Initialize the ego vehicle on a multi-lane road segment.
> 
> 3. Set a 2D Nav Goal that requires a lane change to reach.
> 
> 4. Observe that the vehicle does not initiate the lane change despite clear space.
> 
> 5. Manually reverse the vehicle or reset the initial pose slightly behind the original starting point.
> 
> 6. Observe that the lane change is now successfully planned and executed.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #11943 — Remove `pip3 install` from `CMakeLists.txt`

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2026-01-21  |  **Closed:** 2026-02-06  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:build
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11943

**Body:**

> ≡ƒÜ¿ **This is *really* not okay** ≡ƒÜ¿
> 
> After looking into this packageΓÇÖs `CMakeLists.txt`, I noticed the following lines:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/0446229b26093de8535aeb1bda9a0810ce9bcfa8/control/autoware_smart_mpc_trajectory_follower/CMakeLists.txt#L14-L15
> 
> This means **building this package will unconditionally run `pip install` on the userΓÇÖs system**.
> 
> Let that sink in for a moment.
> 
> * This **mutates the userΓÇÖs global Python environment**
> * It **force-reinstalls** a specific version of `numba`
> * It bypasses virtualenvs, rosdep, system package managers, and user intent
> * It makes the build **non-reproducible, non-hermetic, and fragile**
> * It can silently break *unrelated* Python projects on the same machine
> 
> CMake is a *build system*, not a package manager, and certainly not a place to execute side-effectful system-wide installs. This violates pretty much every expectation users have when running `colcon build`.
> 
> **I Strongly recommend**:
> 
> * Removing all `pip3 install` calls from this CMake
> * Declaring Python dependencies explicitly (e.g. via `package.xml`, `requirements.txt`, or documented setup steps)
> 
> This absolutely needs to be fixed before it causes real damage to someoneΓÇÖs environment.
> 
> ---
> 
> At least I have Ubuntu 24.04 so it cannot install these because it doesn't have `--break-system-packages`.
> But it probably broke many Ubuntu 22.04 developers' pip setups...
> 
> _Originally posted by @xmfcx in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11942#issuecomment-3775800784_
>
