> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11857
> 

**Comments:**

###### @yukkysaito (2026-01-12)

> @xmfcx Thank you for your suggestion.
> 
> I think the countermeasures can be organized into three layers: operations, design, and implementation.
> 
> From an operations and system design perspective, product deployments should assume that nodes are not allowed to freely join the network.
> Enabling DDS Security and enforcing network isolation are essential to ensure the system is properly segmented from external access.
> 
> At the implementation level, it is important not only to cast multiplication checks to uint64_t, but also to perform overflow-safe validation.
> ΓÇ╗ Concrete examples of overflow-safe validation are provided in a separate [comment.](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11853/files#r2682461425)
> 
> In addition, rather than directly handling raw addresses or index-based access, it is preferable to actively use wrappers or iterators.
> By ensuring the above safety guarantees within those abstractions, we can continuously reduce the likelihood of similar issues in the future.

###### @xmfcx (2026-01-12)

> > In addition, rather than directly handling raw addresses or index-based access, it is preferable to actively use wrappers or iterators.
> 
> I'm on my way to revive this issue:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1199
> 
> Right now collecting related issues, potential requried changes, smooth transition preparations etc. and creating a timeline and where we are right now.
> 
> **Related:**
> - [≡ƒÆ¼ How to add PointXYZI type support for autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor #5823](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/5823)
> - [≡ƒÆ¼ Incompatibility with pointfield layouts in autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor package #5031](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/5031)
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/6996
> - [≡ƒÆ¼ Perception & Sensing WG Meeting 31/05/2023 #3533](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3533)
> - https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/design/autoware-architecture-v1/components/sensing/data-types/point-cloud/
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-documentation/pull/180
> - (older) [≡ƒÆ¼ Point Types #2480](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2480)

###### @xmfcx (2026-01-12)

> @yukkysaito As for safe multiplication approach,
> 
> - https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Integer-Overflow-Builtins.html
> - https://clang.llvm.org/docs/LanguageExtensions.html#checked-arithmetic-builtins
> 
> We can make generics out of these.
> 
> Link to demo: https://godbolt.org/z/3Eeh8h8P6
> 
> <details>
>   <summary>≡ƒû▒∩╕ÅClick here to expand≡ƒö¢</summary>
> 
> ```cpp
> #include <iostream>
> #include <type_traits>
> #include <limits>
> 
> // Generic checked multiplication
> template <typename T>
> inline bool checked_mul(T a, T b, T& out)
> {
>     static_assert(std::is_integral_v<T>, "T must be an integral type");
>     return !__builtin_mul_overflow(a, b, &out);
> }
> 
> int main()
> {
>     {
>         int a = 12;
>         int b = 34;
>         int result;
> 
>         if (checked_mul(a, b, result)) {
>             std::cout << "12 * 34 = " << result << '\n';
>         } else {
>             std::cout << "overflow!\n";
>         }
>     }
> 
>     {
>         // This will overflow a 32-bit int
>         int a = std::numeric_limits<int>::max();
>         int b = 2;
>         int result;
> 
>         if (checked_mul(a, b, result)) {
>             std::cout << "result = " << result << '\n';
>         } else {
>             std::cout << "overflow detected (int)\n";
>         }
>     }
> 
>     {
>         // Same values, but widen the result type
>         int a = std::numeric_limits<int>::max();
>         int b = 2;
>         long long result;
> 
>         if (!__builtin_mul_overflow(a, b, &result)) {
>             std::cout << "widened result = " << result << '\n';
>         }
>     }
> 
>     return 0;
> }
> ```
> </details>
> 
> 

###### @Ryujiyasu (2026-03-08)

> ### Remaining vulnerability: ring (channel) value OOB in `ring_outlier_filter_node.cpp`
> 
> @xmfcx @yukkysaito @r0s4ngeles ΓÇö Great work on the PointCloud2 validation improvements in #11853.
> 
> While #11853 validates the **structural consistency** of PointCloud2 messages (width/height/data size/layout), the **ring (channel) field value** within the point data is still not bounds-checked in `ring_outlier_filter_node.cpp`.
> 
> #### Vulnerable Code (1st location)
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/sensing/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_node.cpp#L111-L122
> 
> ```cpp
> // ring2indices is initialized with max_rings_num (default=128) entries
> std::vector<std::vector<size_t>> ring2indices;
> ring2indices.reserve(max_rings_num_);
> for (uint16_t i = 0; i < max_rings_num_; i++) {
>     ring2indices.push_back(std::vector<size_t>());
> }
> 
> for (size_t data_idx = 0; data_idx < input->data.size(); data_idx += input->point_step) {
>     const uint16_t ring =
>       *reinterpret_cast<const uint16_t *>(&input->data[data_idx + input_channel_offset]);
>     ring2indices[ring].push_back(data_idx);  // ΓåÉ No bounds check on ring
> }
> ```
> 
> `ring` is a uint16_t read directly from the point cloud data (range: 0ΓÇô65535), but `ring2indices` has only `max_rings_num_` entries (default: 128). A message with `channel >= 128` passes the `is_valid()` check from #11853 (since the message is structurally valid), and causes an **out-of-bounds heap write**.
> 
> #### Vulnerable Code (2nd location): `calculate_visibility_score`
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/sensing/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_node.cpp#L435-L438
> 
> ```cpp
> const uint bin_index =
>     static_cast<uint>((point.azimuth - min_azimuth) / horizontal_resolution);
> frequency_in_ring[bin_index]++;  // ΓåÉ No bounds check
> ```
> 
> If `bin_index >= horizontal_bins`, this also results in an out-of-bounds access.
> 
> #### PoC
> 
> A structurally valid PointCloud2 message (width=1, height=1, point_step=32, data.size()=32) with `channel=65535` at offset 14 is sufficient to trigger the bug:
> 
> ```bash
> # On the same network with ROS2 DDS (SROS2 disabled)
> ros2 topic pub --once \
>   /sensing/lidar/top/pointcloud_before_sync \
>   sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2 "{
>     header: {stamp: {sec: 0, nanosec: 0}, frame_id: 'lidar'},
>     height: 1, width: 1,
>     fields: [
>       {name: 'x',           offset: 0,  datatype: 7, count: 1},
>       {name: 'y',           offset: 4,  datatype: 7, count: 1},
>       {name: 'z',           offset: 8,  datatype: 7, count: 1},
>       {name: 'intensity',   offset: 12, datatype: 2, count: 1},
>       {name: 'return_type', offset: 13, datatype: 2, count: 1},
>       {name: 'channel',     offset: 14, datatype: 4, count: 1},
>       {name: 'azimuth',     offset: 16, datatype: 7, count: 1},
>       {name: 'elevation',   offset: 20, datatype: 7, count: 1},
>       {name: 'distance',    offset: 24, datatype: 7, count: 1},
>       {name: 'time_stamp',  offset: 28, datatype: 6, count: 1}
>     ],
>     is_bigendian: false, point_step: 32, row_step: 32,
>     data: [0,0,128,63, 0,0,0,64, 0,0,64,64, 100,1, 255,255, 0,0,0,63, 0,0,0,0, 0,0,32,65, 0,0,0,0],
>     is_dense: true
>   }"
> ```
> 
> AddressSanitizer output:
> 
> ```
> ==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow
>   READ of size 8 at 0x51f000001348
>   0x51f000001348 is located 1736 bytes after 3072-byte region
> ```
> 
> #### Suggested Fix
> 
> ```cpp
> // ring_outlier_filter_node.cpp, lines 119-122
> for (size_t data_idx = 0; data_idx < input->data.size(); data_idx += input->point_step) {
> +   if (data_idx + input_channel_offset + sizeof(uint16_t) > input->data.size()) {
> +     break;
> +   }
>     const uint16_t ring =
>       *reinterpret_cast<const uint16_t *>(&input->data[data_idx + input_channel_offset]);
> +   if (ring >= max_rings_num_) {
> +     continue;
> +   }
>     ring2indices[ring].push_back(data_idx);
> }
> ```
> 
> ```cpp
> // ring_outlier_filter_node.cpp, lines 435-438
> const uint bin_index =
>     static_cast<uint>((point.azimuth - min_azimuth) / horizontal_resolution);
> + if (bin_index >= horizontal_bins) {
> +   continue;
> + }
> frequency_in_ring[bin_index]++;
> ```
> 
> Happy to submit a PR for these fixes if that would be helpful.

### #11799 — Task: Enable HLC-conditioned VAD inference in Autoware using Bench2DriveZoo ego_fut_cmd

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-12-20  |  **Closed:** 2025-12-25  |  **Author:** @YSH-research
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11799

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In the current autoware_tensorrt_vad integration, the exported VAD ONNX models do not expose an explicit High-Level Command (HLC) input (e.g. lane follow, turn left, turn right).
> 
> During analysis, I observed that:
> 
> Autoware VAD inference appears to behave as lane-followΓÇôdominant, with turning behaviors (e.g. right turn) not being realized
> 
> The ONNX inputs are limited to:
> mlv_feats
> img_metas.shift
> img_metas.lidar2img
> img_metas.can_bus (dim = 18)
> prev_bev
> 
> <img width="497" height="294" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2eb9985d-8eac-4569-9813-5477c46edd7d" />
> 
> There is no visible input corresponding to ego_fut_cmd, which is present in the original VAD / Bench2Drive training pipelines
> 
> After inspecting the ONNX graphs via Netron and reviewing the Autoware VAD interface code, I suspect that the absence of HLC at inference time is the root cause of the observed limitation (only straight / lane-follow behavior).
> 
> This task proposes to train and export a new ONNX model using Bench2DriveZoo, explicitly incorporating ego_fut_cmd (HLC), while keeping the existing autoware_tensorrt_vad input interface as intact as possible.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose of this task is to restore command-conditioned planning behavior (e.g. turn right) in Autoware VAD inference by reintroducing HLC in a controlled and compatible way.
> 
> Specifically:
> 
> Enable VAD to react differently depending on high-level navigation commands
> 
> Address the current limitation where Autoware works for straight driving but fails for turns
> 
> Verify whether the current Autoware VAD behavior is a consequence of missing HLC rather than a planner-side issue
> 
> Maintain maximum compatibility with the existing autoware_tensorrt_vad input format to minimize integration cost
> 
> This is not intended as a redesign of VAD, but as a minimal, compatibility-aware extension based on the original Bench2DriveZoo training design.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Use Bench2DriveZoo
> [https://github.com/Thinklab-SJTU/Bench2DriveZoo](https://github.com/Thinklab-SJTU/Bench2DriveZoo?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
> 
> to train a VAD model that explicitly conditions on ego_fut_cmd
> 
> Export a new ONNX model where HLC is either:
> 
> Added as an explicit additional input, or
> 
> Embedded in a way that minimally extends the current Autoware input schema
> 
> Keep all existing Autoware inputs (mlv_feats, can_bus, prev_bev, etc.) unchanged where possible
> 
> Map Autoware navigation commands to ego_fut_cmd at runtime
> 
> Validate that:
> 
> Lane-follow behavior remains unchanged
> 
> Turn-right / turn-left behaviors become realizable
> 
> If my assumption that missing HLC is the primary cause is incorrect, clarification on the intended VAD command-handling design would be highly appreciated.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> A VAD ONNX model trained with Bench2DriveZoo successfully conditions on ego_fut_cmd
> 
> The model can be integrated into Autoware with minimal changes to autoware_tensorrt_vad
> 
> Autoware VAD inference can produce different behaviors for:
> 
> lane follow
> 
> turn left
> 
> turn right
> 
> It is clearly documented whether:
> 
> HLC is required for correct VAD operation, or
> 
> The current Autoware behavior is intended by design

**Comments:**

###### @Max-Bin (2025-12-23)

> 
> @YSH-research 
> 
> Thank you for discussing.  I'd like to clarify how `ego_fut_cmd` works in the VAD architecture.
> 
> ### `ego_fut_cmd` is NOT a Network Input
> 
> The VAD model **always outputs all trajectory modes** (3 for nuScenes, 6 for CARLA) regardless of command. The `ego_fut_cmd` is used for:
> 
> 1. **Training only** - to weight losses in [`loss_planning()`](https://github.com/hustvl/VAD/blob/main/projects/mmdet3d_plugin/VAD/VAD_head.py#L1113-L1180)
> 2. **Post-inference selection** - to pick which trajectory to use
> 
> You can verify this by checking:
> - [`forward()` signature](https://github.com/hustvl/VAD/blob/main/projects/mmdet3d_plugin/VAD/VAD_head.py#L489-L496) - no `ego_fut_cmd` parameter
> - [`ego_feats` computation](https://github.com/hustvl/VAD/blob/main/projects/mmdet3d_plugin/VAD/VAD_head.py#L784-L794) - only uses `ego_agent_query`, `ego_map_query`, and optionally `ego_lcf_feat`
> 
> Bench2DriveZoo follows the same pattern - after model outputs all 6 trajectory modes ([L393](https://github.com/Thinklab-SJTU/Bench2DriveZoo/blob/uniad/vad/team_code/vad_b2d_agent.py#L393)), it [selects the trajectory using `command` index](https://github.com/Thinklab-SJTU/Bench2DriveZoo/blob/uniad/vad/team_code/vad_b2d_agent.py#L395): `out_truck = all_out_truck[command]`.
> 
> 
> ### Current Status
> 
> The ONNX model already outputs all trajectory modes (`ego_fut_preds: [1, 3, 6, 2]`). The issue is that **auto command selection is not yet implemented** in the current Autoware interface.
> 
> ### Planned for next Stage
> 
> We plan to add navigation command integration in the next phase.
> 
> If you would like to joining improving VAD model in autoware, I will much appreciate.

### #11740 — refactor: Address Design-less Expansion - consolidate pass-through nodes (MEDIUM SEVERITY)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-12-08  |  **Closed:** 2026-04-02  |  **Author:** @youtalk
- **Labels:** type:bug, type:performance
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11740

**Body:**

> ## Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ## Description
> 
> Several packages exist as independent ROS 2 nodes but contain only trivial pass-through logic that could be simple function calls. This increases system complexity without proportional benefit.
> 
> ## Purpose
> 
> Creating independent processes for trivial operations leads to:
> - Unnecessary IPC overhead
> - Increased system complexity
> - More packages to maintain
> - Harder to understand data flow
> 
> **Pass-through nodes identified:**
> 
> | Node | Functionality |
> |------|---------------|
> | `ObjectRangeSplitter` | Splits objects by distance only |
> | `ObjectVelocitySplitter` | Splits objects by velocity only |
> | `DetectedObjectFeatureRemover` | Removes features only |
> 
> These operations could be:
> - Optional parameters in consuming nodes
> - Simple library functions
> - Part of a larger composable node
> 
> ## Possible approaches
> 
> 1. **Convert to library functions**
>    - Create utility functions in a common package
>    - Call from nodes that need the functionality
>    - Removes IPC overhead entirely
> 
> 2. **Add as optional preprocessing in consumers**
>    - Add range/velocity filtering as parameters
>    - Consuming nodes handle filtering internally
>    - Reduces node count
> 
> 3. **Consolidate into single filter node**
>    - Create one configurable filter node
>    - Support multiple filter types via parameters
>    - Reduce number of packages to maintain
> 
> 4. **Keep as ComposableNodes**
>    - If flexibility is needed, convert to components
>    - Use intra-process communication
>    - Minimal overhead with composition
> 
> ## Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Analyze usage patterns of pass-through nodes
> - [ ] Decide on consolidation strategy with maintainers
> - [ ] Implement chosen approach
> - [ ] Update launch files to use new approach
> - [ ] Document migration path for users
> - [ ] Build and test pass successfully

**Comments:**

### #11739 — refactor: Address Mutable State Overuse in vehicle_cmd_gate (MEDIUM SEVERITY)

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2025-12-08  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @youtalk
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, type:performance
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11739

**Body:**

> ## Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ## Description
> 
> The `autoware_vehicle_cmd_gate` package has excessive mutable state with 20+ member variables, making the code difficult to reason about and potentially prone to race conditions.
> 
> ## Purpose
> 
> Excessive mutable state leads to:
> - Difficulty understanding code behavior
> - Potential race conditions between callbacks
> - Hard-to-reproduce bugs
> - Challenging testing and maintenance
> 
> **Main issue:**
> - `control/autoware_vehicle_cmd_gate/src/vehicle_cmd_gate.hpp` - 20+ mutable member variables
> 
> **Specific problems:**
> - Related state scattered across multiple variables
> - Data shared between callbacks without mutex protection
> - Implicit state history (`prev_*` variables)
> 
> ## Possible approaches
> 
> 1. **Group related state into structs**
>    - Create logical groupings (e.g., `VehicleState`, `CommandState`)
>    - Improves code readability
>    - Makes state relationships explicit
> 
> 2. **Add mutex protection for shared state**
>    - Identify variables accessed from multiple callbacks
>    - Add appropriate synchronization primitives
>    - Prevent data races
> 
> 3. **Reduce state through functional patterns**
>    - Pass state explicitly where possible
>    - Reduce reliance on implicit history
>    - Use const references where appropriate
> 
> 4. **Consider state machine pattern**
>    - For complex state transitions
>    - Makes valid states explicit
>    - Easier to test and verify
> 
> ## Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Audit all mutable state in vehicle_cmd_gate
> - [ ] Group related state into logical structs
> - [ ] Add mutex protection where needed
> - [ ] Reduce unnecessary state where possible
> - [ ] Add tests for concurrent callback scenarios
> - [ ] Build and test pass successfully

### #11738 — refactor: Address Node/Callback Explosion anti-pattern (HIGH SEVERITY)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-12-08  |  **Closed:** 2026-04-02  |  **Author:** @youtalk
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, type:performance
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11738

**Body:**

> ## Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ## Description
> 
> The perception pipeline currently runs 14-20+ individual processes for what could be consolidated into fewer processes using ComposableNodeContainers. This causes excessive inter-process communication overhead and resource consumption.
> 
> ## Purpose
> 
> Running many separate processes instead of composable nodes leads to:
> - Increased memory usage (each process has its own address space)
> - IPC overhead for message passing between nodes
> - More complex deployment and debugging
> - Increased latency in the perception pipeline
> 
> **Affected areas:**
> 
> | Component | Issue |
> |-----------|-------|
> | `sensing/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor/launch/` | Individual nodes for each filter |
> | `perception/autoware_object_range_splitter/` | 15 lines of logic as independent process |
> | `perception/autoware_object_velocity_splitter/` | Pass-through filter as independent process |
> 
> **Good example (reference):**
> - `perception/autoware_ground_segmentation/launch/ground_segmentation.launch.py` - Uses ComposableNodeContainer
> 
> ## Possible approaches
> 
> 1. **Consolidate into ComposableNodeContainers**
>    - Group related nodes into single container processes
>    - Use `ComposableNodeContainer` in launch files
>    - Reduces IPC overhead significantly
> 
> 2. **Convert simple nodes to components**
>    - Make standalone nodes available as components
>    - Allow flexible composition in launch files
>    - Maintain backward compatibility
> 
> 3. **Merge pass-through filters into parent nodes**
>    - For trivial operations like range/velocity splitting
>    - Add as optional preprocessing step in consuming nodes
>    - Reduces unnecessary node boundaries
> 
> ## Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Identify all nodes suitable for composition
> - [ ] Convert key perception nodes to ComposableNodes
> - [ ] Create consolidated launch files using ComposableNodeContainer
> - [ ] Verify no regression in functionality
> - [ ] Measure and document performance improvement
> - [ ] Build and test pass successfully

**Comments:**

###### @youtalk (2025-12-09)

> ## Analysis: Current `pointcloud_container` Architecture and Limitations of Related PRs
> 
> I've analyzed the relationship between `autoware_launch`'s `pointcloud_container` and the related PRs (#11750, #11751, #11752). Here are my findings:
> 
> ### Current Architecture
> 
> The current implementation creates **multiple independent containers** despite using the same `container_name` parameter:
> 
> ```
> Runtime Containers:
> Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ /pointcloud_container                                              (from autoware_launch)
> Γöé   ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ nodes: glog_component, concat_component
> Γöé
> Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ /sensing/lidar/top/pointcloud_preprocessor/pointcloud_container    (from nebula_node_container.launch.py)
> Γöé   ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ nodes: glog, nebula_ros, crop_box x2, distortion, ring_outlier
> Γöé
> Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ /sensing/lidar/left/pointcloud_preprocessor/pointcloud_container   (from nebula_node_container.launch.py)
> Γöé   ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ nodes: glog, nebula_ros, crop_box x2, distortion, ring_outlier
> Γöé
> Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ /sensing/lidar/right/pointcloud_preprocessor/pointcloud_container
> ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ /sensing/lidar/rear/pointcloud_preprocessor/pointcloud_container
> ```
> 
> ### Why This Happens
> 
> In `nebula_node_container.launch.py`:
> ```python
> container = ComposableNodeContainer(
>     name=LaunchConfiguration("container_name"),  # "pointcloud_container"
>     namespace="pointcloud_preprocessor",         # relative namespace
>     ...
> )
> ```
> 
> Combined with the inherited namespace from `lidar.launch.xml`:
> ```xml
> <push-ros-namespace namespace="lidar"/>
>   <push-ros-namespace namespace="top"/>
> ```
> 
> The fully qualified container name becomes `/sensing/lidar/top/pointcloud_preprocessor/pointcloud_container`, which is **completely different** from `/pointcloud_container` created by `autoware_launch`.
> 
> ### Impact on PR #11752
> 
> PR #11752 adds `container_name` parameter to filter launch files (`voxel_grid_downsample_filter_node.launch.xml`, etc.), enabling them to load into existing containers.
> 
> **However, this has limited practical effect because:**
> 
> 1. **`nebula_node_container.launch.py` doesn't use these launch files** - it directly creates `ComposableNode` objects:
>    ```python
>    nodes.append(
>        ComposableNode(
>            package="autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor",
>            plugin="autoware::pointcloud_preprocessor::CropBoxFilterComponent",
>            ...
>        )
>    )
>    ```
> 
> 2. **The main pointcloud preprocessing pipeline bypasses the modified launch files entirely**
> 
> 3. **Each LiDAR still creates its own container** - the fundamental architecture isn't changed
> 
> ### Data Flow Consequence
> 
> ```
> [Per-LiDAR Container]              [Main /pointcloud_container]
>   nebula_ros_wrapper                    
>   crop_box_filter x2          
>   distortion_corrector     
>   ring_outlier_filter  ΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇΓöÇ>  concat_component
>        Γåæ                                     Γåô
>   (Intra-process OK)               (Inter-process overhead!)
> ```
> 
> The preprocessing within each LiDAR container uses intra-process communication, but the transfer to `concat_component` requires **inter-process communication**, which is the main bottleneck.
> 
> ### Suggested Improvements
> 
> To truly address the Node/Callback Explosion anti-pattern, consider:
> 
> 1. **Refactor `nebula_node_container.launch.py`** to use `LoadComposableNodes` into the main `/pointcloud_container` instead of creating new containers
> 
> 2. **Or consolidate all LiDAR preprocessing** into a single shared container
> 
> 3. **Update `lidar.launch.xml`** to avoid creating separate containers per LiDAR
> 
> The current PRs provide useful building blocks but don't address the root architectural issue in `autoware_launch`'s sensor kit configuration.

### #11737 — fix: Add empty data guards to perception packages (HIGH SEVERITY)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-12-08  |  **Closed:** 2026-04-02  |  **Author:** @youtalk
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, type:performance
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11737

**Body:**

> ## Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ## Description
> 
> Add empty data guards to perception packages that process point clouds and other sensor data without checking for empty inputs. Missing guards can cause undefined behavior or crashes when empty data is received.
> 
> ## Purpose
> 
> Processing empty point clouds without validation can lead to:
> - Undefined behavior in PCL functions
> - Potential crashes or segmentation faults
> - Wasted computation on empty data
> - Difficult-to-debug issues in production
> 
> **Affected files (14 locations):**
> 
> | File | Line | Issue |
> |------|------|-------|
> | `perception/autoware_euclidean_cluster/src/euclidean_cluster_node.cpp` | 55 | No check before `pcl::fromROSMsg` |
> | `perception/autoware_euclidean_cluster/src/voxel_grid_based_euclidean_cluster_node.cpp` | 66-74 | Warns but doesn't early return |
> | `perception/autoware_lidar_apollo_instance_segmentation/src/node.cpp` | 57 | No validation |
> | `sensing/livox/autoware_livox_tag_filter/src/livox_tag_filter_node.cpp` | 65 | No check |
> | `perception/autoware_elevation_map_loader/src/elevation_map_loader_node.cpp` | 214, 298 | No check |
> | `perception/autoware_compare_map_segmentation/src/compare_elevation_map_filter/node.cpp` | 75 | No check |
> | `perception/autoware_compare_map_segmentation/src/distance_based_compare_map_filter/node.cpp` | 34 | No check |
> | `perception/autoware_compare_map_segmentation/src/voxel_distance_based_compare_map_filter/node.cpp` | 34 | No check |
> | `perception/autoware_ground_segmentation/src/ray_ground_filter/node.cpp` | 341 | No check |
> | `perception/autoware_ground_segmentation/src/ransac_ground_filter/node.cpp` | 234 | No check |
> | `perception/autoware_shape_estimation/src/shape_estimation_node.cpp` | 122 | No check |
> | `perception/autoware_detected_object_validation/src/obstacle_pointcloud/obstacle_pointcloud_validator.cpp` | 79, 182 | No check |
> 
> ## Possible approaches
> 
> 1. **Add early return guards**
>    - Add empty data checks at the beginning of callbacks
>    - Return early with debug log message
>    - Minimal code change, high impact
> 
> **Recommended pattern:**
> ```cpp
> void Callback(const sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2::ConstSharedPtr msg)
> {
>   if (msg->data.empty() || msg->width == 0 || msg->height == 0) {
>     RCLCPP_DEBUG(get_logger(), "Empty point cloud received");
>     return;
>   }
>   // Continue processing
> }
> ```
> 
> **Good examples in codebase:**
> - `perception/autoware_image_projection_based_fusion/src/segmentation_pointcloud_fusion/node.cpp:73`
> - `perception/autoware_traffic_light_classifier/src/traffic_light_classifier_node.cpp:98`
> 
> ## Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Empty data guards added to all 14 affected locations
> - [ ] Consistent pattern used across all packages
> - [ ] Unit tests verify empty data handling
> - [ ] Build and test pass successfully

### #11736 — fix: Address Process Respawn Loop anti-pattern (HIGH SEVERITY)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-12-08  |  **Closed:** 2025-12-08  |  **Author:** @youtalk
- **Labels:** type:bug, type:performance
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11736

**Body:**

> ## Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ## Description
> 
> Address the Process Respawn Loop anti-pattern across multiple system monitor packages. Currently, some nodes use `respawn="true"` without delay and lack retry/backoff logic, causing rapid respawn loops when external connections fail.
> 
> ## Purpose
> 
> Rapid respawn loops consume system resources, cause log flooding, and can lead to system instability. Proper respawn delays and retry logic are essential for robust system behavior.
> 
> **Affected components:**
> 
> | Component | File | Issue |
> |-----------|------|-------|
> | Bluetooth Monitor | `system/autoware_bluetooth_monitor/launch/bluetooth_monitor.launch.xml:3` | `respawn="true"` without delay |
> | Velodyne Monitor | `system/autoware_velodyne_monitor/launch/velodyne_monitor.launch.xml:5` | `respawn="true"` without delay |
> | Bluetooth Monitor | `system/autoware_bluetooth_monitor/src/bluetooth_monitor.cpp:53-86` | No retry/backoff on socket errors |
> | Velodyne Monitor | `system/autoware_velodyne_monitor/src/velodyne_monitor.cpp:213-230` | No retry/backoff on HTTP errors |
> 
> ## Possible approaches
> 
> 1. **Add respawn_delay to launch files**
>    - Add `respawn_delay="5.0"` to all affected launch files
>    - Quick fix with minimal code changes
> 
> 2. **Implement retry/backoff logic in nodes**
>    - Add exponential backoff when connection errors occur
>    - Implement circuit breaker pattern
>    - Prevent rapid failure loops at the application level
> 
> 3. **Migrate to LifecycleNode (long-term)**
>    - Convert to LifecycleNode for proper state management
>    - Allow graceful handling of connection failures
>    - More comprehensive solution
> 
> ## Definition of done
> 
> - [x] `respawn_delay` is added to `bluetooth_monitor.launch.xml`
> - [x] `respawn_delay` is added to `velodyne_monitor.launch.xml`
> - [ ] Retry logic with backoff is implemented in `bluetooth_monitor.cpp`
> - [ ] HTTP retry logic with backoff is implemented in `velodyne_monitor.cpp`
> - [ ] Unit tests are added/updated
> - [ ] Build and test pass successfully

### #11509 — Autoware_system_monitor reports OK as the status summary for Network Usage even when a connection is down

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-10-16  |  **Closed:** 2025-10-16  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:system
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11509

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The "net_monitor" node in the "autoware_system_monitor" component reports OK as the status summary for "Network Usage" in the "/diagnostics" topic even when one of the network connection is down, while the "status" key for the connection has "down" as its value.
> 
> It means that the status summary for "Network Usage" in the "/diagnostics" topic can't be used for detection of broken network connection.
> 
> The "Network Connection" entry was expected to report dynamic status of network connections, but it reports only whether the networks are valid and correctly initialized and it reports OK every time after successful initialization.
> Therefore, it can't be used for detection of network disconnection.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The "net_monitor" node in the "autoware_system_monitor" component should report ERROR as the status summary for "Network Usage" in the "/diagnostics" topic when a connection is down.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The "net_monitor" node in the "autoware_system_monitor" component reports OK as the status summary for "Network Usage" in the "/diagnostics" topic even when one of the network connection is down.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Open 2 terminals.
> 2. On terminal 1, run ΓÇ£ros2 launch autoware_system_monitor system_monitor.launch.xmlΓÇ¥
> 3. On terminal 2, run ΓÇ£ros2 topic echo -f /diagnosticsΓÇ¥
>     a. If necessary, redirect the output to a log file.
> 4. Repeat disconnection and connection of a network cable a few times.
> 5. Examine the status summary (level and message) of the "Network Usage" entry.
>     a. The status summary is always OK (\0).
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS 2: Humble
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> * Misunderstanding of "Network Connection" behavior
>   - Expected to be dynamic, but is static.
> * Incomplete specification of "Network Usage", caused by the misunderstanding. 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> When this bug is fixed, only the crucial network devices for Autoware should be explicitly listed on the "devices:" line in the configuration file "net_monitor.param.yaml".
> Or, unused (not connected) network  devices are reported to be "down" and false ERROR is reported for the "Network Usage" entry.

**Comments:**

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-10-16)

> This issue has been fixed by #11488 . Closed.

---

### #11446 — Planner does not react to dummies' predicted trajectory when on priority road

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2025-10-03  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @LLusvarghi
- **Labels:** type:improvement, status:stale
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11446

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi,
> I am using autoware.universe 2024.01 on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS.
> I am currently running autoware on CARLA's Town01 map. 
> 
> I noticed that the planner does not react (i.e., does not modify the currently planned trajectory) to the dummy vehicles' predicted trajectories when the dummy vehicles are on a road with lower priority.  It reacts to a dummy vehicle only when it physically is on the currently planned trajectory and is therefore perceived as an "obstacle on the path". 
> 
> Does anybody know why this is happening?
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The planner should plan a new trajectory to avoid the imminent collision with a dummy vehicle that has a predicted future trajectory that crosses the currently planned trajectory. This is what normally happens when the ego-vehicle is on a road with lower priority or when all roads have the same priority. See screenshot below. 
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5300721c-b4d3-4442-9a3d-08ce8a41a0f8)
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The planner does not take into account potential collisions that could occur with dummy vehicles that are driving on a lower priority road. It seems like that the planner is giving more importance to the road priorities and it assumes that the dummy vehicles will respect the driving rules and stop since they are on a lower priority road. The planner does not take into accoutn the dummy vehicles' predicted trajectories estimated by the perception module and reacts to the dummy vehicle only when it physically is on the currently planned trajectory. See screenshot below.
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/495209a7-e5ed-4390-9e0d-c416f481deb1)
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Assign different priorities to CARLA's Town01 map roads
> 2. Launch the ego-vehicle on a higher priority road in correspondence of an intersection
> 3. Set the ego-vehicle's goal destination so that it will cross the intersection
> 4. Generate a dummy vehicle on a lower priority road such that it will cross the ego-vehicle's planned trajectory in correspondence of the intersection
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @marvsee (2025-10-08)

> Hi @LLusvarghi 
> 
> Thanks for raising this issue.
> 
> I'm not entirely sure what you mean by assigning different priorities to the roads. Are you referring to defining the right-of-way using a regulatory_element with right_of_way and yield attributes?
> If so, I believe the "Actual Behavior" you described is the correct and intended functionality. If the planner were to yield to every predicted trajectory regardless of the right-of-way, the ego vehicle would almost always yield, even when it has priority.
> 
> In your example, this would mean the following: The ego vehicle is on a priority road and detects a predicted trajectory intersecting its path. It would then stop and yield, even though it has the right-of-way, and would only proceed after the other vehicle comes to a complete standstill (causing its predicted trajectory to disappear).
> This is not how a human would drive, and it would be overly cautious. In my opinion, it's reasonable to assume that other road users will follow the rules, at least to a certain degree. Driving too defensively can also lead to unpredictable and unsafe behavior in traffic.
> 
> If you have a different opinion on that, I am happy to discuss it further with you :)

###### @LLusvarghi (2025-10-09)

> Hi @marvsee,  thank you for your prompt reply!
> 
> We are not actually using the right_of_way and yield attributes to define the road priorities. We are just setting the turn_direction tag and I understand that this is sufficient to let autoware understand road priorities. I am attaching Town01's lanelet file (in txt format) to this message. The IDs of the lanelets involved in the issue mentioned above are 29086 and 28984.
> 
> I understand the point of your reply, and I partially agree with you. I understand that "_if the planner were to yield to every predicted trajectory regardless of the right-of-way, the ego vehicle would almost always yield, even when it has priority_" and I agree that this would not be a very human-like driving behaviour. 
> Yet, I think that there might be corner cases (such as the one reported in my issue) where an imprudent vehicle (or an emergency vehicle, for example) on a non-priority road might not respect road priorities and that the ego-vehicle should be able to detect and react to such abnormal behavior. For example, I think that the ego-vehicle should be able to understand when a vehicle approaching from a non-priority road will not have sufficient time (considering the braking capabilities of a standard vehicle, for example) to decelerate and stop before the intersection. In my opinion, it should not completely disregard its predicted trajectory and react only when the vehicle is exactly on its planned trajectory. 
> 
> In summary, I believe that a more "normal" behavior could lie between the two extremes: reacting to every predicted trajectory and not reacting to any predicted trajectory. When the ego has the priority, predicted trajectories should be taken into account when there is no physically feasible way for the approaching vehicle to decelerate and give priority to the ego. 
> 
> But this is just my opinion. Looking forward to hearing your feedback!
> 
> Town01's lanelet file: 
> [lanelet2_map.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22791644/lanelet2_map.txt)

###### @marvsee (2025-10-09)

> Hi @LLusvarghi 
> 
> Thanks for the clarification. I understand your point now, and I agree. The ideal behavior is to react to a vehicle that is clearly not going to stop, even if we have the right-of-way.
> 
> You made a great point here:
> > For example, I think that the ego-vehicle should be able to understand when a vehicle approaching from a non-priority road will not have sufficient time (considering the braking capabilities of a standard vehicle, for example) to decelerate and stop before the intersection.
> 
> I think to achieve this, the system would require a more advanced prediction module that can distinguish between a vehicle that is decelerating to stop and one that will run through the intersection. Or it would need a collision check that considers physical braking capabilities, not just the positions and standard predictions.
> 
> But as far as I am aware, these specific capabilities are not currently implemented in Autoware. But I agree, that this would make sense for future developments.

###### @LLusvarghi (2025-10-09)

> Hi @marvsee,
> 
> Thank you very much for the support and the insightful discussion. 
> Do you know if, by any chance, this kind of feature is supported (actually, learned) by the new AI planner recently released by autoware? 

###### @idorobotics (2025-10-17)

> > Hi [@marvsee](https://github.com/marvsee),
> > 
> > Thank you very much for the support and the insightful discussion. Do you know if, by any chance, this kind of feature is supported (actually, learned) by the new AI planner recently released by autoware?
> 
> @m-zain-khawaja is this feature supported or expected soon?

###### @stale (2025-12-16)

>

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-09-29  |  **Closed:** 2026-04-05  |  **Author:** @liuXinGangChina
- **Labels:** type:improvement
- **Comments:** 10  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11418

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> - **Parent Issue:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/issues/6695
> 
> We will make some necessary modification to current autoware code to make it work with ros2 jazzy.
> In order to achieve that, we should follow below steps:
> 
>     add ci support for ros jazzy
>     edit current core code to make it pass ci check
>     support humble and jazzy at the same tim
>

> it's optional by default, but it's actually used in later link:

> ```

> 
> spconv is optional

> build autoware_tensorrt_plugins
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
>

> 
> _No response_

> Hi @felixf4xu 
> 
> We can't label is as `REQUIRED` because build will fail. We want to let all the CUDA-specific packages silently fail as we want to make sure Autoware can build on all the platforms.
> 
> > Change to find_package(spconv REQUIRED), so that the cmake will fail earlier and **it's easier to debug.**
> 
> We have logging:
> ```
> if(${cumm_FOUND} AND ${spconv_FOUND})
>   message(STATUS "spconv is available!")
>   set(SPCONV_AVAIL ON)
> else()
>   message(WARNING "spconv is NOT available")
>   set(SPCONV_AVAIL OFF)
> endif()
> ```
> 
> which should appear, at least at the first build.
>

### #11370 — external_velocity_limit_selector: Bug - Velocity Limit Not Updated on Empty Table Clear

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-09-16  |  **Closed:** 2026-04-09  |  **Author:** @marvsee
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11370

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> There is a logical bug in the `ExternalVelocityLimitSelectorNode` implementation:
> 
> - When a velocity limit clear command is received, `onVelocityLimitClearCommand` calls `clearVelocityLimit`, then `getCurrentVelocityLimit` and `publishVelocityLimit`.
> 
> - If `velocity_limit_table_` is empty, `clearVelocityLimit` returns early and does not call `updateVelocityLimit()`.
> 
> - This means `hardest_limit_` is not updated, and subsequent calls to `getCurrentVelocityLimit()` may return invalid or stale data.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> After a clear command (even when the table is empty), the node should always update its internal state and publish a valid/default velocity limit.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> When a clear command is send before any velocity limit command, an undefined value will be published as the external velocity limit. In RVIZ the speed limit is immediately set to 0 km/h.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start the planning simulation with the external_velocity_limit_selector.
> 2. Do not send any external velocity limit
> 3. Send a clear command (VelocityLimitClearCommand). E.g. via Terminal: ``ros2 topic pub -1 /planning/scenario_planning/clear_velocity_limit tier4_planning_msgs/msg/VelocityLimitClearCommand "{command: true, sender: "examplesender"}"``
> 4. Observe that the published velocity limit may be inconsistent or default-initialized.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The undefined state of the `hardest_limit_` can be avoided, if `updateVelocityLimit()` is always called. My proposal to fix this is:
> 
> ```
> void ExternalVelocityLimitSelectorNode::clearVelocityLimit(const std::string & sender)
> {
>   if (velocity_limit_table_.empty()) {
>     RCLCPP_WARN(get_logger(), "no velocity limit has been set from internal.");
>     updateVelocityLimit(); // <-- this should be added, so the limit is always updated, even if the table is empty
>     return;
>   }
> 
>   velocity_limit_table_.erase(sender);
>   updateVelocityLimit();
> }
> ```
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> This bug was found together with the EDGAR team (especially @korbinianmoller and @tmasc31) while working on an integration of electronic speed limit signs for the [EDGAR Demo rides at IAA 2025](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/6304).

**Comments:**

### #11334 — cpu_monitor should issue warning/error about CPU temperature for NVIDIA Tegra platforms

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-09-08  |  **Closed:** 2025-11-07  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:system
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11334

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, the "cpu_monitor" node reports temperature of CPU cores (on Intel/AMD) or CPU thermal zones (on ARM, Tegra, Raspberry Pi), but it doesn't issue warning or error even when the temperature is high.
> This is because the "cpu_monitor" node had raised "false alarms" on Intel/AMD platforms in the past and "temperature warning/error" was disabled to avoid the problem.
> More reliable "thermal throttling" diagnostics is used on Intel/AMD platforms.
> 
> In the case of NVIDIA Tegra family (ex. Jetson AGX Orin), there is no direct method to detect thermal throttling.
> Therefore, "cpu_monitor" should issue warning and error about high CPU temperature.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Enable warning and error about high CPU temperature only on NVIDIA Tegra platforms.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> In CMakeLists.txt, define the macro "ENABLE_TEMPERATURE_DIAGNOSTICS" if the platform belongs to NVIDIA Tegra family.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> * When CPU temperature goes higher than warning/error threshold, warning/error is reported in the "/diagnostics" topic.
> * With appropriate warning/error threshold, there should not be "false alarm".

**Comments:**

###### @stale (2025-11-07)

>

> 
> Closed.

### #11325 — gpu_monitor fails to report GPU Usage on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-09-05  |  **Closed:** 2025-09-17  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:system
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11325

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> On NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the "gpu_monitor" node of the "autoware_system_monitor" component fails to report "GPU Usage" in the "/diagnostics" topic with the error message "load files not found" .
> It used to work on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xarier without any problem.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The "gpu_monitor" node reports "GPU Usage" successfully both on Xavier and Orin, though Xavier doesn't support Ubuntu 22.04 which is required by ROS2 humble.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> On NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the "gpu_monitor" node of the "autoware_system_monitor" component fails to report "GPU Usage" in the "/diagnostics" topic with the error message "load files not found" .
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Build the "autoware_system_monitor" component.
> 2. On terminal 1, execute "ros2 launch autoware_system_monitor system_monitor.launch.xml" .
> 3. On terminal 2, execute "ros2 topic echo -f /diagnostics > /tmp/log" .
> 4. Wait 10 seconds and terminate the "ros2 topic" command on terminal 2 with Ctrl-C.
> 5. Investigate the "/tmp/log" file. The "gpu_monitor" reports "load files not found" for "GPU Usage" in "/diagnostics" topic.
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - Platform: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (Jetpack 6)
> - ROS 2: Hamble
> - Autoware: 0.47.0
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The current implementation was for NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier with Ubuntu 20.04.
> Xavier provides a symbolic link "/sys/devices/gpu.0" to its device file and the "gpu_monitor" node reads the GPU load value from that symbolic link, but Orin doesn't provide any symbolic link with the same name.
> 
> "/sys/device/platform/gpu.0" is provided on both Xavier and Orin.
> The "gpu_monitor" should read that symbolic link.
> Reference: NVIDIA Developer Forum https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/how-to-programmatically-query-igpu-load/237266
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-09-05)

> This issue is addressed by PR https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11326.

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-09-17)

> PR #11326 has been merged to main and the problem has been solved.

> ### Description
> 
> [This code](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/57ef86be70227e0f36a9e7433b12885fc623eb3e/localization/yabloc/yabloc_image_processing/src/lanelet2_overlay/lanelet2_overlay_core.cpp#L160) is causing a serious compiler warning. I've confirmed that the code itself works fine, but disabling this warning is problematic.
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> No serious warnings will be generated.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> ```
> --- stderr: yabloc_image_processing            
> CMake Warning (dev) at CMakeLists.txt:15 (find_package):
>   Policy CMP0074 is not set: find_package uses <PackageName>_ROOT variables.
>   Run "cmake --help-policy CMP0074" for policy details.  Use the cmake_policy
>   command to set the policy and suppress this warning.
>   CMake variable PCL_ROOT is set to:
>     /usr
>   For compatibility, CMake is ignoring the variable.
> This warning is for project developers.  Use -Wno-dev to suppress it.
> In this package, headers install destination is set to `include` by ament_auto_package. It is recommended to install `include/yabloc_image_processing` instead and will be the default behavior of ament_auto_package from ROS 2 Kilted Kaiju. On distributions before Kilted, ament_auto_package behaves the same way when you use USE_SCOPED_HEADER_INSTALL_DIR option.

> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> `colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args "-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-Wno-error=maybe-uninitialized -Wno-error=array-bounds -Wno-error=nonnull" "-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release"`
> 
> ### Versions

> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Below are Copilot's suggested fixes. I think the former is sufficient.
> ---
> Let's analyze the highlighted snippet:
> 
> ```cpp
> Eigen::Vector3f uv1;
> Eigen::Vector3f uv2;
> if (p1_is_visible) uv1 = from_camera1 / from_camera1.z();
> if (p2_is_visible) uv2 = from_camera2 / from_camera2.z();
> ```
> 
> ## 1. Code Smells or Antipatterns
> 
> - **Uninitialized Variable Use:** If `p1_is_visible` or `p2_is_visible` is `false`, then `uv1` or `uv2` will remain uninitialized, which may lead to undefined behavior if they are used later without being explicitly set. This is a common code smell known as "uninitialized variable."
> - **Potential for Implicit Initialization:** In C++, declaring `Eigen::Vector3f uv1;` without initialization does not guarantee zero-initialization. If the variable is later used without being set, bugs can be hard to track.
> - **Readability:** The if-statements are terse and rely on the reader to notice that either variable might not be set, which can hinder maintainability.
> 
> ## 2. Recommendations and Example Improvements
> 
> - **Explicit Initialization:** Initialize `uv1` and `uv2` to a safe default value (e.g., zero vector) to prevent undefined behavior.
> - **Make Assignment More Clear:** Consider using an else clause or initializing within the declaration to clarify intent.
> - **Comment the Logic:** Brief comments can help future maintainers understand why these are conditionally set.
> 
> **Improved Example:**
> 
> ```cpp
> Eigen::Vector3f uv1 = Eigen::Vector3f::Zero();
> Eigen::Vector3f uv2 = Eigen::Vector3f::Zero();
> if (p1_is_visible) {
>     uv1 = from_camera1 / from_camera1.z();
> }
> if (p2_is_visible) {
>     uv2 = from_camera2 / from_camera2.z();
> }
> // Now uv1 and uv2 are always initialized, minimizing risk of undefined values.
> ```
> 
> Or, if the use of `uv1` and `uv2` later depends strictly on the visibility, consider restructuring:
> 
> ```cpp
> std::optional<Eigen::Vector3f> uv1;
> std::optional<Eigen::Vector3f> uv2;
> if (p1_is_visible) {
>     uv1 = from_camera1 / from_camera1.z();
> }
> if (p2_is_visible) {
>     uv2 = from_camera2 / from_camera2.z();
> }
> // Later, check uv1.has_value() before using.
> ```
> 
> ## 3. C++ Best Practices
> 
> - **Avoid Uninitialized Local Variables:** Especially with types like Eigen vectors, always initialize variables unless performance absolutely demands otherwise and correctness is assured.
> - **Prefer Explicitness:** C++ code is often easier to maintain when initialization and assignment are straightforward and obvious.
> 
> ---
> 
> **Summary:**  
> The main issue here is the risk of using uninitialized variables. By initializing `uv1` and `uv2` to zero or using `std::optional`, you make the code safer and more maintainable, following modern C++ best practices.
>

### #11295 — Explore the use of Valkey (Redis-compatible KV store) with ccache remote storage

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-08-29  |  **Closed:** 2026-04-07  |  **Author:** @esteve
- **Labels:** status:stale, type:performance
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11295

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> [Valkey](https://valkey.io/) is a fork of Redis that is developed by the Linux Foundation, with developers from Google, Amazon, and many others.
> 
> ccache has support for storing the cache in a Redis-compatible server via https://github.com/ccache/ccache/wiki/Redis-storage
> 
> The goal of this task is to explore the feasibility of using Valkey as a remote storage for ccache to improve build times.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> GitHub has a storage limit for caching, our self-hosted runners are not affected, but most of the CI builds happen in public runners, hence we keep hitting that limit.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The approach we're exploring here is setting up Valkey on one of our machines and let both the public and the self-hosted runners use it for storing ccache objects.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Results of running Valkey as a remote storage for ccache will be provided at the end of the evaluation.

### #11285 — gpu_monitor reports a false warning every second when GPU is idle

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-08-27  |  **Closed:** 2025-09-17  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11285

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> gpu_monitor of autoware_system_monitor reports a false warning message every second when the GPU is completely idle.
> 
> > [component_container_mt-1] [WARN 1756285485.062733682] [gpu_monitor]: Failed to nvmlDeviceGetProcessUtilization(2nd) NVML: Not Found (addProcessUsage() at /home/masakinishikawa/work/fix_issue_11269/autoware/src/universe/autoware_universe/system/autoware_system_monitor/src/gpu_monitor/nvml_gpu_monitor.cpp:242)
> 
> According to [the specification of nvmlDeviceGetProcessUtilization()](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/group__nvmlDeviceQueries.html#group__nvmlDeviceQueries_1gb0ea5236f5e69e63bf53684a11c233bd:~:text=nvmlReturn_t%20nvmlDeviceGetProcessUtilization%20(%20nvmlDevice_t%C2%A0device%2C%20nvmlProcessUtilizationSample_t*%C2%A0utilization%2C%20unsigned%20int*%C2%A0processSamplesCount%2C%20unsigned%20long%20long%C2%A0lastSeenTimeStamp%20)), the function returns [NVML_ERROR_NOT_FOUND](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/group__nvmlDeviceEnumvs.html#group__nvmlDeviceEnumvs_1gg06fa9b5de08c6cc716fbf565e93dd3d0a1bfb13c6d0f00249b20f556c2d5d23f) if sample entries are not found.
> 
> It means that, when the GPU is completely idle, nvmlDeviceGetProcessUtilization() finds no sample entry and returns NVML_ERROR_NOT_FOUND, because there is **no** process that uses the GPU.
> 
> This is a **false warning** and gpu_monitor should report "GPU Usage 0%" with no error or warning.
> The false warning messages are recorded in log and they will lower the quality of the log data.
> 
> In addition to the main issue, gpu_monitor dynamically allocates/frees heap memory every second.
> ```
>   std::unique_ptr<nvmlProcessUtilizationSample_t[]> utils;
>   utils = std::make_unique<nvmlProcessUtilizationSample_t[]>(util_count);
> ```
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Gpu_monitor should report "GPU Usage 0%" with no error or warning when the GPU is completely idle.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Gpu_monitor reports a false warning message every second when the GPU is completely idle.
> 
> The "/diagnostics" topic published by gpu_monitor does not report any error or warning even when it reports the false messages. This is an expected behavior.
> 
> > - level: "\0"
> >   name: 'gpu_monitor: GPU Usage'
> >   message: OK
> >   hardware_id: dpc2500001
> >   values:
> >   - key: 'GPU 0: status'
> >     value: OK
> >   - key: 'GPU 0: name'
> >     value: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
> >   - key: 'GPU 0: usage'
> >     value: 0.0%
> >   - key: execution time
> >     value: 1.027751 ms
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Build "autoware_system_monitor".
> > $ cd autoware
> > $ MAKEFLAGS="-j8" colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON --parallel-workers 8 --packages-up-to autoware_system_monitor
> 2. Launch "autoware_system_monitor".
> > $ ros2 launch autoware_system_monitor system_monitor.launch.xml
> 3. The false warning messages will be printed on the launcher terminal after other messages.
> > [INFO] [launch]: All log files can be found below /home/masakinishikawa/.ros/log/2025-08-27-18-04-43-635712-dpc2500001-2170492
> > [INFO] [launch]: Default logging verbosity is set to INFO
> > [INFO] [component_container_mt-1]: process started with pid [2170506]
> > (SKIPPED)
> > [component_container_mt-1] [INFO 1756285484.081323387] [system_monitor.system_monitor_container]: Instantiate class: rclcpp_components::NodeFactoryTemplate<VoltageMonitor> (create_component_factory() at ./src/component_manager.cpp:133)
> > [INFO] [launch_ros.actions.load_composable_nodes]: Loaded node '/voltage_monitor' in container '/system_monitor/system_monitor_container'
> > [component_container_mt-1] [WARN 1756285485.062733682] [gpu_monitor]: Failed to nvmlDeviceGetProcessUtilization(2nd) NVML: Not Found (addProcessUsage() at /home/masakinishikawa/work/fix_issue_11269/autoware/src/universe/autoware_universe/system/autoware_system_monitor/src/gpu_monitor/nvml_gpu_monitor.cpp:242)
> > [component_container_mt-1] [WARN 1756285486.061922095] [gpu_monitor]: Failed to nvmlDeviceGetProcessUtilization(2nd) NVML: Not Found (addProcessUsage() at /home/masakinishikawa/work/fix_issue_11269/autoware/src/universe/autoware_universe/system/autoware_system_monitor/src/gpu_monitor/nvml_gpu_monitor.cpp:242)
> > (Similar messages are printed with 1 second intervals.)
> 4. Make the GPU busy with the CUDA sample program "nbody" or others.
> > $ ./nbody -benchmark -numbodies=1048576
> 5. While the "nbody" sample is running, the false warning messages stop.
> 6. The "/diagnostics" topic from gpu_monitor can be logged for observation.
> > $ ros2 topic echo -f /diagnostics > /tmp/log
> 7. Instead of the false warning, real errors are reported in "/diagnostics" topic while the GPU is quite busy.
> 
> > - level: "\x02"
> >   name: 'gpu_monitor: GPU Usage'
> >   message: very high load
> >   hardware_id: dpc2500001
> >   values:
> >   - key: 'GPU 0: status'
> >     value: very high load
> >   - key: 'GPU 0: name'
> >     value: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
> >   - key: 'GPU 0: usage'
> >     value: 100.0%
> >   - key: 'GPU 0: process 0: pid'
> >     value: '2143962'
> >   - key: 'GPU 0: process 0: name'
> >     value: ./nbody
> >   - key: 'GPU 0: process 0: usage'
> >     value: 100.0%
> >   - key: execution time
> >     value: 1.568001 ms
> > 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> This issue can be observed only on x86_64 platform with NVML library.
> - Ubuntu Linux 22.04
> - ROS2 Humble
> - NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit 12.04
> - NVIDIA GPU Driver 550.163.01
> - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
> 
> This issue became visible after update of NVIDIA driver and CUDA Toolkit, but it is not so sure.
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> * Misunderstanding about the specification of nvmlDeviceGetProcessUtilization().
> * Change of NVML library's behavior.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-09-17)

> The PR #11291 has been merged to main and this issue has been solved.

### #11269 — gpu_monitor causes a failure in CI workflow cppcheck_differential

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-08-25  |  **Closed:** 2025-09-02  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** component:system, run:build-and-test-differential
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11269

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When a Pull Request changes some codes in gpu_monitor_base.cpp, the CI workflow "cppcheck_differential" triggered by the change fails as the following lines.
> 
> > Run cat cppcheck-report.txt
> > Error: /home/runner/work/autoware_universe/autoware_universe/system/autoware_system_monitor/src/gpu_monitor/gpu_monitor_base.hpp:70:16: style: Virtual function 'shut_down' is called from destructor '~GPUMonitorBase()' at line 60. Dynamic binding is not used. [virtualCallInConstructor]
> >   virtual void shut_down();
> >                ^
> > /home/runner/work/autoware_universe/autoware_universe/system/autoware_system_monitor/src/gpu_monitor/gpu_monitor_base.cpp:60:3: note: Calling shut_down
> >   shut_down();
> >   ^
> > /home/runner/work/autoware_universe/autoware_universe/system/autoware_system_monitor/src/gpu_monitor/gpu_monitor_base.hpp:70:16: note: shut_down is a virtual function
> >   virtual void shut_down();
> >                ^
> 
> This problem blocks the PR #10888 and needs a quick and independent fix because it may block other PRs.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The CI workflow "cppcheck_differential" should pass with no error.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The CI workflow "cppcheck_differential" fails and PRs related to gpu_monitor_base.cpp can't be merged.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Submit a PR which contains changes in gpu_monitor_base.cpp. Example: #10888 
> 2. The CI workflows start execution.
> 3. The workflow "cppcheck_differentials" fails.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The error is reported because the destructor of the base class GPUMonitorBase calls the virtual function shut_down() defined by its derived class, which does not exist after destruction of the derived class.
> 
> The change was introduced by PR #11022.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> Why didn't the CI workflow "cppcheck_differential" fail for PR #11022?
> ~~Was there any update in the CI workflow itself?~~
> ~~The CI workflow "cppcheck_differential" was introduced recently after PR #11022.~~ <- It was introduced 1 year ago.
> 
> The reason is still unknown, but it isn't worth the effort to find it out.

**Comments:**

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-08-26)

> This issue will be solved by the PR [#11279](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11279).

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-09-02)

> The PR [#11279](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11279) , which fixes this issue, has been merged at commit [8237d93](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/commit/8237d9343f3c20e9645297ce01ada354b57ad041).

### #11241 — Auto button is not available to start auto mode.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-08-20  |  **Closed:** 2025-09-15  |  **Author:** @gnykumar
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11241

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi, I was able to run the carla-autoware at first then not able to re-run the same again. Auto button is not allowing to select after localization done and goal selected.
> 
> I tried setting `ROS_DOMAIN_ID` to avoid multiple system communication. But still same issue.
> 
> Attaching the log.
> 
> <img width="1920" height="1080" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51db6b7d-b351-4222-a509-58c5bf54e3ed" />
> 
> [launch.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21890802/launch.log)
> 
> <img width="1920" height="1080" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3666f212-1601-4070-ba10-3c45352b0788" />
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> auto button as to enable to start auto mode
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> auto button is disabled
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Run carla 0.9.15 server : ./CarlaUE4.sh -prefernvidia -quality-level=Low -RenderOffScreen      (quality and other args changing doesn't solve)
> 2. Run autoware universe with autoware carla interface : ros2 launch autoware_launch e2e_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=/home/ubuntu22/autoware_map/Town01 vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=awsim_sensor_kit simulator_type:=carla carla_map:=Town01
> 3. Initialize localization and select 2d goal.
> Then next to select auto button it is not working.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> OS : ubuntu 22
> ROS : ROS2 foxy
> Autoware : Autoware.universe latest
> 
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> some safety enable to disable to auto button from autoware stack
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @gnykumar (2025-09-15)

> I found it. It is due to localization. which is not showing as converged or matching with score. So I hardcoded in ndt scan matching saying localization done. Then it started working. 

---

### #11219 — Prevent possible "IPC cross-talk" caused by cpu_monitor and hdd_monitor in "multiple ECUs" environment

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-08-15  |  **Closed:** 2025-10-15  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** type:documentation, status:stale, component:system, component:interfaces
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11219

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Use a UNIX domain socket for IPC between "cpu_monitor" and its helper "msr_reader" (for Intel/AMD x86_64 platforms) instead of a TCP/IP socket.
> Use a UNIX domain socket for IPC between "hdd_monitor" and its helper "hdd_reader" instead of a TCP/IP socket.
> 
> These changes are for avoiding possible "IPC cross-talk" among multiple ECUs on the same network.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> "cpu_monitor" (on Intel/AMD x86_64 platforms) communicates with its helper application "msr_reader" via a TCP I/P socket.
> "hdd_monitor" communicates with its helper application "hdd_reader" via a TCP I/P socket.
> 
> At the time when they were implemented, systems are expected to have only 1 ECU, but this is not true anymore.
> 
> With the current implementation (TCP/IP sockets with INADDR_ANY), "IPC cross talk" can occur in environments where multiple ECUs are connected on the same network.
> 
> "IPC cross talk" should be prevented because modern systems have multiple ECUs for task sharing.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Use UNIX domain sockets instead of TCP/IP sockets, because UNIX domain sockets can be used only for local IPC.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - UNIX domain sockets are used instead of TCP I/P sockets.
> - "cpu_monitor" and "hdd_monitor" should work the same as before.
> - Related documents are updated accordingly.
> - Related configuration files are updated accordingly.

**Comments:**

###### @stale (2025-10-14)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-10-15)

> This issue had been fixed by merging of PR #11199.

### #11159 — hdd_monitor fails to retrieve statistics data from eMMC storage devices

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-08-12  |  **Closed:** 2025-09-02  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11159

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The "hdd_monitor" node of  the "autoware_system_monitor" component fails to retrieve statistics information (ex. read/write data rate, S.M.A.R.T. data) from eMMC storages, which are used by NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> All of the HDD statistics data entries are retrieved from the storage devices on the supported platforms.
> 
> Currently, there is no problem with SCSI I/F storages (/dev/sd*) and NVMe SSD (/dev/nvme*) , while NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin has only an eMMC storage device (/dev/mmcblk*), which the "hdd_monitor" node can't handle.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The "/diagnostics" topic published by the "hdd_monitor" node on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin includes the following entries:
> - Reported as ΓÇ£hdd_reader errorΓÇ¥ with the reason "No such file or directoryΓÇ¥
>   - HDD Temperature
>   - HDD PowerOnHours
>   - HDD TotalDataWritten
>   - HDD RecoveredError
> - Reported as ΓÇ£stat file read errorΓÇ¥
>   - HDD ReadDataRate
>   - HDD WriteDataRate
>   - HDD ReadIOPS
>   - HDD WriteIOPS
> - Works fine
>   - HDD Usage
>   - HDD Connection
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Execute "sudo hdd_reader" to run the "hdd_reader" application in the background, which retrieves S.M.A.R.T. data from storage devices.
> 2. On terminal 1, execute "ros2 launch autoware_system_monitor system_monitor.launch.xml" .
> 3. On terminal 2, execute "ros2 topic echo -f /diagnostics > /tmp/log" .
> 4. Wait 10 seconds and terminate the  "ros2 topic" command on terminal 2 with Ctrl-C.
> 5. Investigate the "/tmp/log" file. The "hdd_monitor" reports errors in "/diagnostics" topic.
> 6. Be sure to terminate the "hdd_reader" process running in the background and the "ros2 launch" process.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubunts 22.4
> - ROS: Humble
> - Autoware: autoware_universe 0.47.0
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> "hdd_monitor.cpp" recognizes only "/dev/sd" and "/dev/nvme" as valid bases for storage device files and it ignores "/dev/mmcblk", which is used for eMMC storage devices and SD cards.
> 
> In addition to that, another problem was found during investigation.
> 
> Jetson AGX Orin has the following partitions.
> - /dev/mmcblk0p1 mounted on '/', which should be monitored by hdd_monitor.
> - /dev/mmcblk0p10 mounted on '/blk/efi', which should NOT be monitored by hdd_monitor.
> 
> An unnecessary regular expression in the source code, which used to be meaningful in the early versions, mixed up these 2 partitions and produced a wrong report.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-09-02)

> The PR [#11160](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11160) that fixes this issue has been merged at [2fbcd05](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/commit/2fbcd059a5dec945be3e1025efe8fb0ad17f4f07).

### #11105 — [lane change bug] The possibility of a lane change depends on the specified goal point.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-08-01  |  **Closed:** 2025-08-07  |  **Author:** @Parkeunseok
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11105

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hello,
> 
> I am currently studying Autoware and using it with a Korean autonomous driving test track map, instead of the default maps provided by Autoware.
> 
> I would like to request help regarding the following issue:
> 
> As shown in the first attached image, when the goal point is set to a certain location, the lane change is not performed.
> 
> <img width="4400" height="2457" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/638ef50b-b785-4b61-9358-1aca3d147b7b" />
> 
> <img width="992" height="668" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/909c5ea3-6618-4002-b8e0-1ce78207c150" />
> 
> 
> 
> However, when a nearby goal pose is set instead, the lane change is successfully executed.
> 
> <img width="1707" height="953" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a40d255-154d-4032-81fa-4ec3b121b193" />
> 
>
