### #11053 — Reduce high CPU usage of `autoware_remaining_distance_time_calculator`

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-07-24  |  **Closed:** 2026-01-10  |  **Author:** @satoshi-ota

> ### Description
> 
> The `autoware_remaining_distance_time_calculator` node consumes a significant amount of CPU resources during operation. This high processing load puts pressure on the CPU, potentially affecting the performance of other critical modules, especially in low-performance hardware.
> 
> <img width="1320" height="969" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1002fc59-6f1b-40c9-b8c0-b9fb9f7b5740" />
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The goal is to reduce the CPU usage of this node to a level that does not interfere with the execution of core modules such as Planning and Perception.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Reduce processing frequency: Lower the update rate of the node (e.g., from 10 Hz to 1 Hz), or make it configurable via a launch or ROS parameter.
> - Profile and identify bottlenecks: Use tools like perf, htop, or ROS timers to measure execution time per callback and focus optimization on the most expensive parts.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> TBD

>

### #11012 — The header files for autoware_system_monitor package should be relocated.

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2025-07-18  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** type:improvement, status:stale
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11012

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> [The "Directory Structure" section](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/contributing/coding-guidelines/ros-nodes/directory-structure/#directory-structure) of Autoware Documentation requires that only exported header files should be located in "PACKAGE/include/autoware" directory and that internal header files should be located at "PACKAGE/src" or "PACKAGE/src/include".
> 
> The current implementation (as of 2025/07/20) of the "autoware_system_monitor" package places its internal header files (not expected to be exported) at autoware_system_monitor/include/system_monitor/???_monitor.
> This is against the rule and may cause misunderstanding.
> 
> The header files should be relocated at autoware_system_monitor/src/???_monitor, where the source files reside.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Improve consistency of the source code file structure.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Because some components (???_monitor) have only 1 header, digging src/include directories is not a good idea.
> As the number of header files is relatively small, header files can be placed in the directories where their related source files reside.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Header files are relocated and all of the CI workflows finish successfully.

> **Status update:** Closing the linked PRs as they have gone stale and have unresolved design issues. Keeping this issue open since the use case is valid.
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_core/pull/570
> 
> Summary of where things stand:
> 
> **What works:** The concept of bus stop pull-out/pull-over behavior is well-motivated. @kyoichi-sugahara confirmed start_planner support makes sense.
> 
> **Open design decision:** @soblin objected to adding a `"bus_stop"` tag on road lanelets because road lanelets feed into the shared routing graph (used by all vehicles, not just buses). He proposed a `bus_bay` **subtype** instead, similar to how `road_shoulder` and `bicycle_lane` are handled. This was never resolved.
> 
> **For anyone picking this up**, the key question to resolve first is the map format:
> - **Option A -- `bus_bay` subtype:** A new lanelet subtype handled like `road_shoulder`. Cleaner architecturally, routing graph can include/exclude based on vehicle type. Requires map format update.
> - **Option B -- attribute on road lanelet:** Simpler but pollutes the routing graph and breaks the existing convention.
> 
> The implementation approach also needs rethinking -- the `1e+10` magic penalty should be replaced with candidate pre-filtering, and the `getLaneletAngleOnEgoCenterline` change should be a separate PR.

### #10936 — autoware_system_monitor (cpu/gpu_monitor)  cannot report CPU, GPU temperatures on NVIDIA Jetson GLX Orin

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-07-07  |  **Closed:** 2025-07-11  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** type:bug, priority:low, type:arm64, component:system
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10936

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin is a member of NVIDIA's Tegra family.
> 
> On NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the "/diagnostics" topic from the "autoware_system_monitor" contains the following lines for "CPU Temperature" and "GPU Temperature", failing to get the actual temperature data about CPU and GPU.
> 
> **Additional Info:**
> NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier is also a member of NVIDIA's Tegra family.
> The current implementation had been tested on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier, but Xavier supports only JetPack 5.x with Ubuntu Linux 20.04.
> Xavier doesn't support JetPack 6.x with Ubuntu Linux 22.04, which is necessary for ROS2 Humble (or later) required by current implementation of Autoware.
> Briefly, the current implementation of Autoware can't work on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier any more.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The following lines should be found in the '/diagnostics' topic.
> 
> > status:
> > - level: "\0"
> >   name: 'cpu_monitor: CPU Temperature'
> >   message: OK
> >  (measured temperature data follow)
> 
> > status:
> > - level: "\0"
> >   name: 'gpu_monitor: GPU Temperature'
> >   message: OK
> >  (measured temperature data follow)
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The following lines are found in the '/diagnostics' topic.
> It means that the "autoware_system_monitor (cpu_monitor and gpu_monitor) cannot locate the files for reading temperature data."
> 
> > status:
> > - level: "\x02"
> >   name: 'cpu_monitor: CPU Temperature'
> >   message: temperature files not found
> 
> > status:
> > - level: "\x02"
> >   name: 'gpu_monitor: GPU Temperature'
> >   message: temperature files not found
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. On "terminal1", execute the following line.
> 
> > $ ros2 launch autoware_system_monitor system_monitor.launch.xml
> 
> 2. On "terminal2", execute the following line.
> 
> > $ ros2 topic echo -f /diagnostics > /tmp/log
> 
> 3. Investigate the "/tmp/log" file.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS : Ubuntu Linux 22.04 (JetPack 6.x provided by NVIDIA)
> - ROS2: Humble
> - Autoware: 0.45
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The naming convention for temperature files are different between Xavier and Orin.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-07-07)

> This issue will be solved by PR #10937 .

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-07-11)

> PR #10937 has been merged to autowarefoundation/main.
> This issue is closed as "fixed".

### #10932 — Speed up CI builds by caching dependent repositories

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2025-07-07  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @mitsudome-r
- **Labels:** type:improvement, status:stale, component:tools
- **Comments:** 14  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10932

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, autoware_universe requires build-and-test-differential to pass before merging, but it sometimes takes a long time to wait for the CI to pass, especially when you make modification to packages that depends on many other packages.
> 
> I would like to think of a solution to make the CI/CD to run faster by utilizing build cache of dependent repositories.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Make build-and-test-differential CI faster. 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> One of the possible approaches is to utilize the build cache of packages [build_depends.repos](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/build_depends_humble.repos). Instead of building the full workspace from scratch, we can create a cache for workspace with only packages from dependent repositories, and reuse the cache to do build-check for packages from Autoware Universe.
> 
> The drawback is that build might fail if there are breaking changes in underlying workspace (e.g., in autoware_msgs), but we can make the cache generation workflow to be triggered manually for such case. 
> 
> 1. Create a workflow to create a underlying colcon ws (dependency_ws) for build_depends.repos and push the cache to GitHub cache.This workflow can run daily or can be triggered manually.
> 2. Modify the build-and-test-differential workflow to source the underlying workspace before colcon build and colcon tests.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> 1. build_dependent_workspace workflow is merged
> 2. modify build-and-test-differential workflow to use the dependency_ws 

**Comments:**

###### @esteve (2025-08-04)

> One approach we could take for this issue is to leverage the Debian buildfarm and use the released packages to create an overlay workspace and in the Autoware_universe CI only build the packages that have changed.

###### @xmfcx (2025-08-05)

> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/build_depends_nightly.repos
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/build_depends_humble.repos
> 
> - Build cache: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/actions/caches
> 
> For build depends repos, we can cache build and install folders from these repositories and load

###### @esteve (2025-08-05)

> @mitsudome-r @xmfcx how are these caches generated? Is it a GitHub action?

###### @xmfcx (2025-08-06)

> We have multiple types of caches in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/actions/caches:
> 
> ## ccache (ccache-main-X64-humble-92c96f76b32b769ab7638150e33c47c312f8f430):
> 
> This contains a central ccache cache and all general and partial builds load and use it.
> 
> Generated and used by:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-and-test.yaml
>   - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/f4d8bd98328c1bbdde5984b08494a27e59e6013f/.github/workflows/build-and-test-reusable.yaml#L149 this part specifically pushes the cache.
> 
> Used by:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-and-test-daily.yaml
> 
> 
> ## per pr build caches (build-X64-humble-default-Release-b902b54d918cd4fd7721484573fe8b663fd2f1cb)
> 
> This exists because clang-tidy and colcon-build are triggered by different workflows.
> It is created by every PR that calls colcon-build, unique to PR.
> 
> Generated by:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-github-actions/blob/51fa2052bd6497eb65f42358b49a1eebc02ed6b9/colcon-build/action.yaml#L198
> 
> Used by:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-github-actions/blob/51fa2052bd6497eb65f42358b49a1eebc02ed6b9/clang-tidy/action.yaml#L93
> 
> ## rosdep  cache (rosdep-X64-humble)
> 
> This is generated and reused with the following algorithm:
> 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-github-actions/blob/51fa2052bd6497eb65f42358b49a1eebc02ed6b9/colcon-build/action.yaml#L94-L135
> 
> We've created this cache to avoid the rate limits when `rosdep update` calls `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ros/rosdistro/master/ ...`.  
> - explained here: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-github-actions/pull/346
> 
> ## others
> 
> There is also a pre-commit cache but I didn't investigate that one before.

###### @esteve (2025-08-06)

> @xmfcx thanks. If I'm not mistaken, the goal is to generate caches for the packages https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/build_depends_nightly.repos and 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/build_depends_humble.repos, store them in the GitHub cache and then reuse them for build-and-test-differential, instead of building all the packages in the workspace. Is my description of the problem correct?

###### @xmfcx (2025-08-06)

> Yes, primarily that's the goal. The tricky part is to decide when to rebuild them.
> - a new workflow vs adding it to an existing workflow
> - how to detect changes in target branches/heads of repositories
>   - event based or how often to check if periodical

###### @esteve (2025-08-06)

> @xmfcx I'm going to start by creating a new workflow to avoid interfering with the existing ones, but if later on we see that it's better to integrate it into another one, we can do that too. Thanks for the explanation.

###### @xmfcx (2025-08-15)

> Reposting from the PR to here for reference:
> 
> ---
> 
> This workflow currently builds the entire `autoware_universe` repository and caches it **once per day**.
> That approach has two major drawbacks:
> 
> 1. **Low update frequency** -> daily runs are not frequent enough to keep up with upstream dependency changes.
> 2. **Risk of stale or conflicting artifacts** -> if a package in `autoware_universe` is renamed, restoring a cached build will leave both the old and new packages in place, making it harder for CI to detect build issues accurately.
> 
> ### Why not cache the whole repository?
> 
> Caching the main `autoware_universe` workspace directly bakes in whatever was in that branch at the time of caching.
> This makes it brittle against:
> 
> * Package renames
> * Build system changes
> * Files left over from previous package structures
> 
> ### What we should cache instead
> 
> The dependencies defined by combining:
> 
> * [`build_depends_humble.repos`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/build_depends_humble.repos)
> * [`build_depends_nightly.repos`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/build_depends_nightly.repos)
> 
> Notes:
> 
> * `build_depends_humble.repos` is only used for PR validation against the `humble` branch. Therefore thereΓÇÖs no need to cache that on its own.
> * PRs against `main` are tested against the **merged** dependency file:
>   `build_depends_humble.repos` + `build_depends_nightly.repos`.
> 
> `build_depends_nightly.repos` points to **branches** that change frequently. That means our cache must be invalidated when:
> 
> * The `.repos` files themselves change, or
> * Any of the branches/tags they reference move to a new commit.
> 
> ## How to detect changes in GitHub Actions
> 
> **Key idea:** use `vcs export --exact-with-tags` to freeze all moving references to immutable tags or commit SHAs, and use that frozen manifest as the cache key.
> 
> ### Cache update workflow (scheduled, **every hour**)
> 
> 1. Generate the combined `build_depends.repos`.
> 2. Import it into a temporary workspace.
> 3. Export an exact manifest (`build-depends-exact.repos`) with pinned versions.
> 4. Use `hashFiles('build-depends-exact.repos')` as the cache key.
> 5. If the hash matches the last run, exit early (nothing to rebuild).
> 6. Otherwise, build dependencies and save the `install/` and `build/` directories to the cache.
> 
> ### PR workflow (build & test differential)
> 
> 1. Generate the combined `build_depends.repos`.
> 2. Import and export an exact manifest as above.
> 3. Restore the dependency cache **only if the exact key exists** (no restore-keys fallback).
> 4. If no exact match, build dependencies from scratch (but do not save cache as only the scheduled workflow updates it).
> 
> ---
> 
> **Example keying logic:**
> 
> ```yaml
> - name: Prepare build_depends.repos (combine)
>   uses: ./.github/actions/combine-repos-action
>   with:
>     base_file: build_depends_humble.repos
>     overlay_file: build_depends_nightly.repos
>     output_file: build_depends.repos
> 
> - name: Resolve exact dependencies
>   run: |
>     vcs import dependency_ws < build_depends.repos
>     vcs export dependency_ws --exact-with-tags > build-depends-exact.repos
> 
> - name: Restore deps cache
>   uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
>   with:
>     path: |
>       install
>       build
>     key: deps-ws-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ env.rosdistro }}-${{ env.BUILD_TYPE_CUDA_STATE }}-${{ hashFiles('build-depends-exact.repos') }}
> 
> - name: Save deps cache
>   uses: actions/cache/save@v4
>   with:
>     path: |
>       install
>       build
>     key: deps-ws-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ env.rosdistro }}-${{ env.BUILD_TYPE_CUDA_STATE }}-${{ hashFiles('build-depends-exact.repos') }}
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> This way, the cache represents **only the exact dependency set** for a given build, and it automatically updates when either the `.repos` files change or any moving branch/tag they reference is updated upstream.
> 
> 

###### @xmfcx (2025-08-15)

> On a separate note, I've checked that the cache generated from workflow_dispatch on main can be accessed from the PRs with this dummy repo:
> - [this workflow creates cache](https://github.com/xmfcx/cache-test/blob/1b9c3fa962ab9790bf9dfb8cd46fb71601d32c31/.github/workflows/seed-cache.yml)
> - [this workflow uses the cache](https://github.com/xmfcx/cache-test/blob/1b9c3fa962ab9790bf9dfb8cd46fb71601d32c31/.github/workflows/use-cache.yml)
> - [it is restored here successfully Γ£à](https://github.com/xmfcx/cache-test/actions/runs/16997001743/job/48190007394?pr=1#step:3:19)

###### @xmfcx (2025-08-15)

> In any case, **the cache should be keyed with exact repo hashes** as I mentioned in the PR and above, the stale cache can create all sorts of issues.
> 
> The restore operation should restore the cache with the `build_depends.repos` exported with exact repository hashes file.
> 
> This is in tangent to having the option for `workflow_dispatch` as a trigger.

###### @mitsudome-r (2025-08-18)

> I agree with Fatih on this.
>  
> * We should update the build cache build_depends_nightly.repos
> * We can use hashFiles('build-depends-exact.repos') to detect changes in packages in build depends.

###### @mojomex (2025-08-19)

> As a low-effort, high-impact solution, we could also introduce a [Ccache Remote Storage Backend](https://ccache.dev/manual/4.7.html#_remote_storage_backends).
> 
> The current Ccache is effectively non-existent since it is limited to 0.5 GB (whereas a full Autoware build produces > 15 GB of Ccache). See also: #10150. This cannot be fixed since our runners have limited hard drive space (#7555).
> 
> A remote cache can be shared across all runners, workflows and steps, and will handle changed dependencies, different compilers etc. correctly. It would however require a hosted Redis instance. Cost-wise this should be quite cheap, and might be offset by saving AWS costs when building CUDA code that would also utilize this new backend.

> Hi @cjmodi306 and sorry for late response.

> 
> Please use g++11 instead.
> 
> We would be also happy if you could refine affected kernels in order to achieve compatibility with g++11 and g++12!

### #10830 — autoware_system_monitor/process_monitor outputs huge integer for negative process priority

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-06-17  |  **Closed:** 2025-06-26  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:system
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10830

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> After merging of #10379 , /diagnostics topic published by the "autoware_system_monitor/process_monitor" node sometimes contain huge integer values for "PR" (priority) keys in process data.
> The versions before #10379 employed Linux command "top" for retrieving process data .
> The "top" command uses "rt", which means "real-time", for special system processes with negative priority values smaller than -99.
> 
> As the values for "PR" is not used for further processing, this bug won't cause any serious problem.
> 
> Example:
> > - level: "\0"
> >   name: 'process_monitor: High-load Proc[10]'
> >   message: OK
> >   hardware_id: dpc2500001
> >   values:
> >   - key: COMMAND
> >     value: migration/1
> >   - key: '%CPU'
> >     value: '1.0'
> >   - key: '%MEM'
> >     value: '0.0'
> >   - key: PID
> >     value: '160'
> >   - key: USER
> >     value: root
> >   - key: PR
> >     value: '**18446744073709551516**'
> >   - key: NI
> >     value: '0'
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The "autoware_system_monitor/process_monitor" node should handle negative priority values accordingly and use special value "rt" for processes with negative priority smaller than -99 and positive priority larger than 999.
> These conditions are derived from the source code of the "top" command.
> 
> Example:
> > - level: "\0"
> >   name: 'process_monitor: High-load Proc[10]'
> >   message: OK
> >   hardware_id: dpc2500001
> >   values:
> >   - key: COMMAND
> >     value: migration/1
> >   - key: '%CPU'
> >     value: '1.0'
> >   - key: '%MEM'
> >     value: '0.0'
> >   - key: PID
> >     value: '160'
> >   - key: USER
> >     value: root
> >   - key: PR
> >     value: '**rt**'
> >   - key: NI
> >     value: '0'
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> See "Description".
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Modify the "num_of_procs" parameter in install/autoware_system_monitor/share/autoware_system_monitor/config/process_monitor.param.yaml 
>  so that more processes than the default (5) are reported. 40 is large enough.
> 2. On terminal 1, execute the following command.
> > $  ros2 launch autoware_system_monitor system_monitor.launch.xml
> 3. On terminal 2, execute the following command.
> > $ ros2 topic echo -f /diagnostics > /tmp/log
> 4. Investigate the file "/tmp/log".
> 5. If necessary, repeat 3 and 4 several times.
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> This problem was caused by merging of the PR #10379 .
> On ARM64 Ubuntu 22.4, the problem can be observed more frequently because some processes with negative priority values appear in the ranking of resource consumers.
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> 1. The "priority" member of struct "StatInfo" in autoware_universe/system/autoware_system_monitor/include/system_monitor/process_monitor/process_information.hpp is defined as "uint64_t" while negative values are allowed.
> 2. The implementation didn't care about the special cases about "rt" (real-time).
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-06-18)

> This issue will be fixed by PR #10832 .

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-06-26)

> PR #10832 was merged to main.

> 
> Evaluate the strengths and limitations of the selected simulator for potential off-road vehicle integration and simulation for space and Earth applications
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The pros and cons of the selected simulator will be compared to other simulators, which helps determine the most suitable simulator for off-road vehicle simulation.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. Install the simulator. Outlining the hardware requirements and assessing the level of installation complexity.
> 2. Access the off-road simulation demo from the simulator (if any) or manually integrate an off-road vehicle with suspension and drive it on rough terrain
> 3. Evaluate the accuracy of vehicle dynamics and physics simulation
> 4. Experiment with the vehicle on deformable terrain (if possible)
> 5. Evaluate the level of graphical realism and real-time performance for off-road simulation
> 6. Identify any issues or glitches
>

> Complete an off-road simulation demo using the selected simulator. Identify the key strengths and limitations and summarize them in a documentation

### #10679 — Radar pipeline update

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-05-22  |  **Closed:** 2025-07-08  |  **Author:** @technolojin
- **Labels:** type:improvement, component:perception
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10679

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Since a new radar is supported https://github.com/tier4/nebula/releases/tag/v0.2.6, tracked object from radar ECU
> became reliable.
> Update the radar pipeline to fully utilize tracked object of radar ECU
> 
> [TIER IV INTERNAL](https://tier4.atlassian.net/browse/RT1-5640)
> 
> #### requirement
> - message https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_msgs/pull/120
> - nebula driver https://github.com/tier4/nebula/pull/284
> - adapter https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10459
> - autoware https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pull/6128
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Remove redundant filters and processes of radar pipeline, so that the radar tracked object could be used without drawback.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Radar objects are published in both `detected objects` and `tracked objects`.
> 
> 1. use `detected objects` and implement tracker of autoware
> 2. use `tracked objects` to utilize tracker information from radar
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Integrate radar tracked object pipeline.
> - universe launcher https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10580
> - aip_launcher https://github.com/tier4/aip_launcher/pull/446
> 
> Support tracked object
> - autoware_simple_object_merger
> - lanelet filter (autoware_detected_object_validation)
> 
> Revise algorithm
> - autoware_tracking_object_merger [WIP] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10680
> 
> Remove unused packages to reduce maintenance cost.
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10654
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/1449
> 
> 
> 
> Node updates for tracked object pipeline
> 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10785
> - https://github.com/tier4/aip_launcher/pull/481
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10883
> - range and velocity filter for tracked objects https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10925
> - autoware_universe pipeline (launcher) update https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10916
> - autoware_launch parameter update https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/1531
> 
> 
> Related bug fix
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10930
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10934
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/1541
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10946
> 
> Deprecated packages (used in some modes)
> - autoware_radar_tracks_msgs_converter
> - autoware_object_range_splitter
> - autoware_object_velocity_splitter
> - autoware_radar_object_tracker

### #10641 — Remove the obstacle_stop_planner and obstacle_cruise_planner packages

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-05-15  |  **Closed:** 2025-05-27  |  **Author:** @takayuki5168
- **Labels:** type:improvement
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10641

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Remove the obstacle_stop_planner and obstacle_cruise_planner packages since they are obsolete packages.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Previously, for the following features, the `obstacle_stop_planner` (over two years ago) and the `obstacle_cruise_planner` (until last year) were used.
> - the stop feature against surrounding obstacles
> - the slow down feature against surrounding obstacles
> - the adaptive cruise planning
> 
> However, since the node structure has changed for the Autoware.Core and increasing the readability & maintainability of the features, currently the following packages are used for each feature respectively.
> - motion_velocity_obstacle_stop_module (in Autoware.Core)
> - motion_velocity_obstacle_slow_down_module (in Autoware.Universe)
> - motion_velocity_obstacle_cruise_module (in Autoware.Universe)
> 
> Therefore, for now, the `obstacle_stop_planner` and `obstacle_cruise_planner` packages are obsolete and confusing to exist in Autoware.Universe.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Remove the obstacle_stop_planner and obstacle_cruise_planner packages
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> The obstacle_stop_planner and obstacle_cruise_planner packages are removed from Autoware.Universe

**Comments:**

###### @takayuki5168 (2025-05-15)

> The above proposal is from the TIER IV's planning team.
> Let me confirm maintainers outside TIER IV.
> 
> @brkay54 @beyzanurkaya 
> Please have a comment about this issue.

###### @takayuki5168 (2025-05-23)

> @brkay54 @beyzanurkaya 
> friendly ping.

###### @beyzanurkaya (2025-05-23)

> Hi @takayuki5168 -san
> I agree with the proposal ΓÇö removing the obstacle_stop_planner and obstacle_cruise_planner packages makes sense since the functionality has already been replaced with more maintainable modules.

### #10622 — autoware_multi_object_tracker: Mahalanobis Threshold Causes Duplicate Tracking

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-05-13  |  **Closed:** 2025-05-27  |  **Author:** @kaancolak
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:perception
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10622

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Sometimes, especially when tracking stationary buses or trucks, the autoware_multiple_object_tracker creates duplicate tracks for the same object. These duplicate tracks tend to appear and disappear suddenly.
> 
> In the video below, I logged and displayed Mahalanobis distance values observed when a duplicate issue occurs.
> 
> Currently, the default Mahalanobis threshold value is set to 3.035, which corresponds to the 99th percentile of the chi-squared distribution with 2 degrees of freedom. This setting is intended to filter out moderate outliers.
> 
> ≡ƒöù [Code Reference ΓÇô Line 183](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/perception/autoware_multi_object_tracker/lib/association/association.cpp#L183)
> 
> However, real-world data shows that the Mahalanobis distance for detections of the same object can reach up to ~3.51
> 
> TrackerProcessor::removeOverlappedTracker does not work as expected because duplicated track objects have recent updates.
> 
> ≡ƒöù [Code Reference ΓÇô Line 186](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/main/perception/autoware_multi_object_tracker/src/processor/processor.cpp#L186)
> 
> Check the 8th second for duplicate tracking:
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95f8e311-8de8-4413-83cf-a4f70f1d49ba
> 
> 
> Detection results for the same scene: 
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32e3fb34-92a0-49c8-ab8d-50c7cfe9010e
> 
> 
> *Possible Solutions:*
> 
> *Option 1:*  
> ### ***UPDATE*** : _In some cases, especially when the bounding box undergoes significant changes (e.g., from large to small), the Mahalanobis distance can reach values as high as 5ΓÇô6. Using the 99.99% threshold for a 2-degree-of-freedom Chi-square distribution (Γëê 4.29), or even completely ignoring the Mahalanobis distance, might be a better choice._
> 
> To better accommodate real-world variation, we can increase the Mahalanobis threshold to ~3.461, which corresponds to the 99.7th percentile. This setting is intended to filter out strong outliers.
> 
> *Option 2:*
> Update the removeOverlappedTracker function logic to better handle the removal of highly overlapped objects
> 
> 
> FYI: @YoshiRi @technolojin @miursh @yukkysaito 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Tracked objects continuously without duplication.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The autoware_multi_object_tracker creates duplicate tracks for the same object.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Run Autoware. 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @technolojin (2025-05-14)

> @kaancolak 
> Thank you for your analysis. @ogrex and I also see similar situation.
> 
> @ogrex 
> I would like to request to share your analysis result, and suggest appropriate threshold value.
> 

###### @ogrex (2025-05-22)

> ### Analysis and Tuning for Yaw Stability based on Mahalanobis Threshold together with Q,R
> 
> We investigated the impact of yaw-related parameter tuning on the consistency and robustness of EKF-based state estimation, especially under sharp vehicle turns. The evaluation focused on three primary strategies:
> 
> ---
> 
> #### (1) Tuning Measurement Covariance for Yaw (`R`)
> 
> By increasing the measurement covariance for yaw, we reduce the EKFΓÇÖs sensitivity to rapid yaw changes, which helps prevent overestimating the error during real-world turning maneuvers.
> 
> - **Observation**: With the default covariance of `20`, some Mahalanobis distances exceeded the gating threshold.
> - **Adjustment**: Setting `R.yaw = 40` generally brings most cases within threshold.
> - **Caution**: An excessively large value may result in under-correction, so it's important to strike a balance between robustness and measurement responsiveness.
> 
> ---
> 
> #### (2) Adjusting Process Noise for Yaw Rate (`Q`)
> 
> Increasing process noise allows the EKF to expect higher variability in yaw rate during the prediction phase. This results in a more forgiving prediction covariance, reducing the relative innovation (residual) when compared to actual sensor data.
> 
> - **Trade-off**: While higher process noise improves turn performance, it may degrade accuracy during straight-line driving. Proper tuning is critical to maintain overall estimation quality.
> 
> ---
> 
> #### (3) Revisiting the Gating Threshold
> 
> We experimented with increasing the Mahalanobis gating threshold from the default to around **3.4ΓÇô3.5**.
> 
> - **Outcome**: This adjustment improved acceptance of measurements overall, though a few edge cases still exceeded the gate.
> - **Risk**: Loosening the gate increases the chance of incorporating outliers, so this must be carefully managed.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### Evaluation Focus
> 
> For this round of evaluation, we focused on **(1)**, **(2)**, and **(3)**.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### Experiment Results
> 
> We compared different settings of `R.yaw` (measurement covariance) and `Q.yaw_rate_max` (process noise) by evaluating the **maximum Mahalanobis distance** across several scenarios:
> 
> | R.yaw | Q.yaw_rate_max | Max Mahalanobis Distance (samples)                  |
> |-------|----------------|------------------------------------------------------|
> | 40    | 15             | 2.24, 2.68, 2.28, 3.12, 3.30, 3.35                   |
> | 20    | 15             | 2.28, 3.20, 2.58, 3.28, 3.62, 3.74 *(default)*       |
> | 5     | 15             | 2.80, 5.67, 4.59, 4.14, 6.75, 6.27 *(too strict)*    |
> | 20    | 30             | 1.84, 2.51, 2.21, 3.03, 3.34, 2.96 *(effective)*     |
> | 20    | 20             | 1.94, 2.65, 2.24, 3.18, 3.32, 3.10                   |
> 
> ---
> ### Impact of Gate Threshold Setting
> 
> 
> 
> To analyze the effect of different gate thresholds, we plotted the current measurement points alongside the current `Q` and `R` configuration in a diagram.  
> 
> In this plot, any point that lies **above and to the right of the QR setting line** indicates a case where the Mahalanobis distance **exceeds the threshold**.
> 
> This visualization helped guide the appropriate adjustment of the gating threshold, ensuring that parameter tuning remains effective while avoiding unnecessary rejections.
> Tuning (1)R, (2)Q, (3)Threshold
> 3.035 (Default)
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/173b0335-2d39-4326-b651-4206ff7ff057)
> 3.4
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/121650fa-4c98-43de-806e-c890b43d717a)
> 3.6
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12a1d8df-82c2-4e27-adce-04e42fb52978)
> 3.717
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ea1cc72-fd24-4994-a917-116532e1a05c)
> 
> ---
> 
> ### Tuning Strategy: Gradient-Based Adjustment
> 
> To minimize system perturbation while improving gating performance, we applied a **gradient-based tuning approach**. Specifically:
> 
> - The Mahalanobis distance gate threshold was temporarily increased to **3.42**.
> - Parameters `R` (measurement covariance) and `Q` (process noise) were then fine-tuned **along the gradient direction**, aiming to balance sensitivity and robustness.
> - This method helped suppress abrupt parameter-induced fluctuations while converging on a more stable and effective configuration.
> 
> ≡ƒôî See related commit:  
> [`feat(multi_object_tracker): parameters tuned for mahalanobis distance`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/commit/020d03d)
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Conclusion
> @technolojin 
> From the experiment, we observed that by carefully adjusting `Q` (process noise) and `R` (measurement covariance), the Mahalanobis distance can be tuned to stay around **3.4**, which helps minimize disruptive changes to the Mahalanobis threshold.
> 
> However, since modifying `Q` and `R` can impact overall tracking behavior, a threshold of **3.717** appears to be a temporarily appropriate and balanced choice ΓÇö aligning well with the analysis results while ensuring system stability. This is also supported by the QR tuning visualization, where the **threshold point (3.717)** nearly covers all cases ΓÇö with the corresponding lines lying **below the point**, indicating that most measurements remain within the gate.
> 
>

### #10610 — CUDA related libraries are not being compiled for target architectures

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2025-05-12  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @knzo25
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10610

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> While developing the ptv3 node I realized that cuda code is not being compiled with target architectures.
> This ends up with code compiled for `sm_52`, and a just-in-time compilation and execution in modern gpus (potentially slower).
> 
> In a rudimentary experiment, the preprocessing from centerpoint went down a whole ms, whereas the sub sample filter from @manato did not see any reduction.
> 
> This can be checked using cuobjdump
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> cuobjdump shows that the code has been compiled for the architectures that autoware is actually used in
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> ```text
> cuobjdump libautoware_lidar_centerpoint_cuda_lib.so

> arch = sm_52
> code version = [1,7]
> host = linux
> compile_size = 64bit

> Fatbin ptx code:

> host = linux
> compile_size = 64bit
> compressed
> ptxasOptions =

> 
> Fatbin ptx code:

> host = linux
> compile_size = 64bit
> compressed
> ptxasOptions = 
> 
> Fatbin elf code:
> ================
> arch = sm_52

> host = linux
> compile_size = 64bit
> 
> Fatbin ptx code:
> ================
> arch = sm_52
> code version = [8,7]
> host = linux
> compile_size = 64bit
> compressed
> ptxasOptions = 
> 
> Fatbin elf code:
> ================
> arch = sm_52
> code version = [1,7]
> host = linux
> compile_size = 64bit
> 
> Fatbin ptx code:
> ================
> arch = sm_52
> code version = [8,7]
> host = linux
> compile_size = 64bit
> compressed
> ptxasOptions = 
> ```
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Compile autoware using any version and check with cuobjdump
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @knzo25 (2025-05-12)

> I will create individual PRs for the target packages to avoid reverting the while idea if just one package has issues (should not though)

> The following PRs address this issue:

>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10612
>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10613
>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10614
>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10615
>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10616
> 
> The flags could be defined in the `autoware_package`, but it it the meantime this should be ok (until we know there is no problem for a while).
> I added the architectures that autoware is likely/expected to be run in according to:
> https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-gpus

###### @amadeuszsz (2025-05-14)

> @knzo25 
> This is great discover!
> 
> > I will create individual PRs for the target packages to avoid reverting the while idea if just one package has issues (should not though)

> > [@amadeuszsz](https://github.com/amadeuszsz) The problem with any dynamic approach is that you want to distribute a single image right?

Anyway, as you pointed correctly, deployed image has to be shipped with all architectures so we can't save here a space with a dynamic approach. ### #10596 — lane change module gives inconsistent result in specific situation

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-05-08  |  **Closed:** 2025-07-23  |  **Author:** @Joonki0111
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10596

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When there is a goal in front of a obstacle and lane change is also needed to be happened, the lane change module gives a inconsistent result as shown like the footage below.
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66fe2d42-828f-4981-bf5d-caa1a5ad1422
> 
> It sometimes successfully reaches to the goal but sometimes get's stuck behind the obstacle.
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6383678-4096-49e1-8004-8f75a2c7fa2f
> 
> I have changed some parameters like `prepare_duration`, `lateral_acceleration.max_values: [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]` to prevent this error but nothing worked.
> Is this a known issue? or is it because I'm using a old version of Autoware?
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Reach to the goal by lane change
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Randomly behaves which might lead to failure.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> simple planning simulator
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> Ubuntu 22.04
> Humble
> release/v1.0
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2025-05-09)

> Thank you so much for the report.
> Case 1 is not so clear to me. Do you mean ego couldn't lane change properly?
> 
> In case 2. The target object is too close to the goal. In lane change, we compute the minimum lane change distance, and in your case, the default parameter is not suitable. You can try increasing lateral jerk to -1.0 m/s3, and minimum lane change velocity to 1.5m/s.

###### @Joonki0111 (2025-05-09)

> @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 
> Case 1 & 2 has the same issue, which is giving two different paths rapidly. And this is what I described as 'inconsistent result'.
> This result leads to random arrival. It could arrive as normal(not shown at the video), or it could just get stuck behind obstacle like the second video.
> 
> Thanks for your reply :)

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2025-06-18)

> @Joonki0111 
> Most probably this happens in old version.
> With the latest version, the result shouldn't flicker that much and it has a more stable result.
> 
> Also I noticed that the stop line at the end of the trajectory seems to be short, did you happened to modify minimum lane change velocity?

###### @Joonki0111 (2025-07-17)

> @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 Sorry for the late reply, yes I have made some changes in lane change parameters. Currently, this is not a issue anymore because we made it through with this situation. I also tried the latest version of Autoware and seems good enough. Thanks :)
> 

###### @maxime-clem (2025-07-23)

> From the last reply it seems the issue is solved. If not please reopen the issue.

### #10587 — Static obstacle avoidance makes the vehicle oscillates too much on the planned avoidance path

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2025-05-06  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @vincentcheng62
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10587

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01346910-332f-44d3-9416-fecb5bde50e9
> 
> As shown in the attached video, when the static obstacle avoidance module is enable, 
> the avoidance path can be planned successfully.
> However, when the vehicle engages, it is not quite following the pre-planned avoidance path and starts to oscillates
> The oscillation does not converge and the pointcloud does not align with the map, finally the vehicle turns into the obstacle when it is about ~5m away from the obstacle, and it stops by the obstacle stop planner.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The vehicle should follow the pre-planned avoidance path smoothly and avoid the obstacle and then come back to the ego path finally.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The vehicle starts to oscillate when travelling through the pre-planned avoidance path. The oscillation does not converge and the pointcloud does not align with the map, finally the vehicle turns into the obstacle when it is about ~5m away from the obstacle, and it stops by the obstacle stop planner.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Draw a lanelet2 with double lane of 2m width facing the same direction
> 2. Enable static object avoidance
> 3. Place obstacle ~15m away from the vehicle in the ego path, the obstacle size is large enough so that it is detected and tracked stably using euclidean cluster (i.e. not centerpoint)
> 4. Plan a 2D goal ~40m away from the vehicle in the ego path, the avoidance path will be generated after 3 seconds since it is an "UNKNOWN" type obstacle
> 5. Engage the vehicle and the issue will happen
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> -OS: ubuntu 22.04
> -ROS2: humble
> -autoware version: ~ Feb 2025 
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The default localization method: NDT is not very sensitive to rotational changes. Hence, when the vehicles turns in the avoidance path, the pointcloud starts to deviate from the map, which affect the subsequents planning and motion control module performance.
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @yhisaki (2025-07-09)

> I suppose you are using a small robot. However, the parameters of static_obstacle_avoidance are tuned for the vehicle, so they may not work well for a small robot. I recommend using dynamic_obstacle_avoidance instead. Empirically, I think dynamic_obstacle_avoidance works better than static_obstacle_avoidance.

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
>

### #10554 — The "cpu_monitor" node takes more than 1 second for publishing while it is expected to publish /diagnostics topic with 1 second intervals.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-04-24  |  **Closed:** 2025-06-26  |  **Author:** @nishikawa-masaki
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:system
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10554

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The "cpu_monitor" node of the "autoware_system_monitor" component spends more than 1 second (typically 1.4sec) for publishing "/diagnostics" topic while it is expected to publish the topic with 1 second intervals.
> This causes the following problems:
> * Extra CPU load is consumed by "autoware_system_monitor" itself.
> * The safe margin against error detection is decreased.
>   * If "/diagnostics" topic stops being published for more than 3 seconds, it is recognized as an error.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The "cpu_monitor" node should publish "/diagnostics" topic with 1 second intervals.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The "cpu_monitor" node publishes "/diagnostics" topic with 1.4 second intervals or more.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Run "ros2 launch autoware_system_monitor system_monitor.launch.xml" on a terminal.
> 2. Run "ros2 topic echo -f /diagnostics > /tmp/log" on another terminal.
> 3. Inspect timestamp intervals of topics published by "cpu_monitor". The intervals are expected to be about 1 second, but actual intervals are considerably longer than 1 second.
> 4. Observe that the "execution time" values of 'cpu_monitor: CPU Usage' are more than 1000 ms (1 second), too.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> This is caused by the following reasons:
> * The "cpu_monitor" node uses "mpstat -P ALL 1 1 -o JSON" command to get CPU usage.
>   * The command sleeps 1 second in it to collect data with fair amount of interval for calculating CPU usage.
>     * The interval can't be shorter than 1 second. ("mpstat" takes only integer arguments)
> * The "cpu_monitor" node uses boost::process::child() to execute "mpstat" command.
>   * Spawning of child processes takes time and introduces extra CPU load.
>     * It also interferes with context switching in Linux kernel.
> * The "cpu_monitor" node collects statistics information in the publishing thread context.
>   * Execution of "mpstat" for CPU load takes 1 second.
>   * Other statistics are read from /proc pseudo-filesystem, but it also takes some time.
>   * A similar problem with "process_monitor" has been reported and fixed.
>     * #939
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> This problem should be fixed with 2 steps.
> 
> 1. Move collection of statistics from the publishing context to a newly added timer-callback context.
>   * [fix(cpu_monitor): collect cpu information on timer thread #10545](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10545)
> 2.  Avoid use of "mpstat" command and boost::process::child().
>   * [fix(cpu monitor): read /proc/stat directly instead of executing mpstat #10873](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10873)

**Comments:**

###### @nishikawa-masaki (2025-06-26)

> Both of the following changes have been merged to "main" and this issue has been resolved.
> 
> 1. Move collection of statistics from the publishing context to a newly added timer-callback context.
> 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10545
> 
> 2. Avoid use of "mpstat" command and boost::process::child().
> 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10873

### #10505 — path_optimizer crashes: vector::_M_range_check error when approaching goal or using short-distance goal

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-04-19  |  **Closed:** 2025-04-19  |  **Author:** @iumida
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10505

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When setting a goal via AD API (/api/routing/set_route), the motion_planning container crashes with a std::out_of_range error when either:
> 	ΓÇó	The goal is too close to the current pose, or
> 	ΓÇó	The vehicle is approaching the goal during autonomous driving.
> 
> This crash causes an emergency stop.
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The system should handle short goal distances or end-of-path conditions gracefully without crashing.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The path_optimizer module crashes due to an out-of-range access on a vector when calculating the start point of a bound segment:
> 
> ```
> [component_container_mt-74] terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::out_of_range'
> [component_container_mt-74]   what():  vector::_M_range_check: __n (which is 1) >= this->size() (which is 1)
> [component_container_mt-74]     @     0xffff87b407f0 std::__throw_out_of_range_fmt()
> [component_container_mt-74]     @     0xffff60627350 autoware::path_optimizer::(anonymous namespace)::getStartPoint()
> [component_container_mt-74]     @     0xffff606273c4 autoware::path_optimizer::(anonymous namespace)::isFrontDrivableArea()
> [component_container_mt-74]     @     0xffff60627f6c autoware::path_optimizer::geometry_utils::isOutsideDrivableAreaFromRectangleFootprint()
> [component_container_mt-74]     @     0xffff605aea00 autoware::path_optimizer::PathOptimizer::insertZeroVelocityOutsideDrivableArea()
> [component_container_mt-74]     @     0xffff605aecf4 autoware::path_optimizer::PathOptimizer::generateOptimizedTrajectory()
> [component_container_mt-74]     @     0xffff605af5fc autoware::path_optimizer::PathOptimizer::onPath()
> [component_container_mt-74]     @     0xffff605cc248 ...
> [ERROR] [component_container_mt-74]: process has died [pid 13740, exit code -6]
> ```
> 
> [crash.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19819116/crash.txt)
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Case 1: Crash when approaching the end of a normal-length route
> 	1.	Set a long route via /api/routing/set_route
> 	2.	Engage autonomous mode
> 	3.	When the ego vehicle is about to reach the goal, the motion_planning container crashes
> 
> Case 2: Immediate crash with short goal distance
> 	1.	Set a route where the goal is only a few meters from the current pose
> 	2.	The container crashes immediately
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> ΓÇó	Autoware: autoware.universe v0.43
> ΓÇó	ROS 2: Humble
> ΓÇó	OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> 
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #10481 — LiDAR semantic segmentation for Autoware

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-04-17  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @amadeuszsz
- **Labels:** component:perception
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10481

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Introduce a new module for LiDAR semantic segmentation to the perception component. This module will classify 3D LiDAR point clouds into semantic categories such as road, sidewalk, vehicle, pedestrian, vegetation, etc., using a machine learning model. The module should process raw point cloud data and produce per-point semantic labels.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> * Enhance perception capability with richer understanding of the scene.
> * Improve robustness in complex environments where ground segmentation alone is insufficient.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> * Integrate SOTA algorithms into Autoware.
>   * [FRNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04484)
>   * [Point Transformer V3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.10035)
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Selected and integrated a suitable semantic segmentation ML model into [AWML](https://github.com/tier4/AWML?tab=readme-ov-file#3d-segmentation) with one of available OSS dataset for 3D semantic segmentation.
>   - [x] FRNet 
>   - [x] Point Transformer V3
> - [x] Integrated module as a ROS C++ node with proper message interfaces and topics.
>   - [x] FRNet -> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10503
>   - [x] Point Transformer V3 -> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10600
> - [x] Retrained model with internal dataset.
>   - [x] FRNet -> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pull/6928
>   - [x] Point Transformer V3 -> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pull/6918

**Comments:**

###### @amadeuszsz (2025-04-18)

> PR for FRNet in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10503.

###### @knzo25 (2025-05-12)

> universe's PR for PTv3 in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10600
> 
> In addition, the following tensorrt plugins are needed:
>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10601
>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10602
>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10603
>  - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10604

###### @stale (2025-07-11)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @knzo25 (2025-10-04)

> @amadeuszsz 
> All PRs are merged. We good to close this?

> @knzo25 
> Retrain part is still not fully addressed for both models. We are working on it

### #10427 — Ego frame ID is hard-coeded in "autoware_multi_object_tracker"

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-04-09  |  **Closed:** 2025-04-10  |  **Author:** @urasakikeisuke
- **Labels:** component:perception
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10427

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> We are trying to use autoware_multi_object_tracker in a system that does not have "base_link" as an ego frame. However, as shown below, since the "base_link" is hard-coded as an ego frame, nothing is output from the tracker because it is always rejected in the nearest point calculation part.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/a20e0e6ec40577b5f66d7a994ff60a1d68332a26/perception/autoware_multi_object_tracker/include/autoware/multi_object_tracker/odometry.hpp#L54
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/a20e0e6ec40577b5f66d7a994ff60a1d68332a26/perception/autoware_multi_object_tracker/src/processor/input_manager.cpp#L98-L102
> 
> I think it should be possible to change the ego frame from the configuration file.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The results are output even if the ego frame is not ΓÇ£base_linkΓÇ¥.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Nothing is output if the ego frame is not ΓÇ£base_linkΓÇ¥.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Run autoware_multi_object_tracker on data with non ΓÇ£base_linkΓÇ¥ ego frames in the default configuration.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> v0.43.0
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @amadeuszsz (2025-04-10)

> Hi @urasakikeisuke 
> 
> Thank you for reporting this issue. I addressed your idea in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10428 and https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/1397.
> Let's check if we can merge it.

###### @urasakikeisuke (2025-04-10)

> Hi @amadeuszsz 
>

### #10311 — Steering Command Converter for CARLA Set Up Incorrectly

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-03-19  |  **Closed:** 2025-05-20  |  **Author:** @stevenbrills
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10311

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The config file for the raw_vehicle_command_converter in the current autoware_carla_interface package is set to NOT convert steering commands from Autoware.
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9e02de4-d9c5-471a-abbc-8934c70349dc)
> 
> However, the interface in carla_ros.py uses the steering command as a steering actuation command itself and not a steered tire angle. See the line where out_cmd.steer is being set in the image below. The existing conversion uses the "in_cmd.actuation.steer_cmd" which is the steered wheel angle (since raw vehicle command converter is not converting the tire angle to actuator signals) and multiplies it by the steer ratio and the maximum wheel angle of the vehicle. Then it assigns it to the out_cmd.steer control command which takes in actuator values and not steered tire angles.
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bb2b01a-da48-49d3-99f8-50987cb7221a)
> 
> This apparently works for small tire angles that are used as steering actuation signals directly but breaks down for large angles, particularly during high curvature free-space maneuvers. In any case this is incorrect semantically.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The input steering tire angle should be converted to valid steering actuation signals that lie between -1 and 1 and can be consumed by CARLA.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The vehicle is unable to track high curvature paths when interfacing with CARLA.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Load a CARLA town with a valid parking lot
> 2. Launch the stack with CARLA as the sim option and set a goal in a parking lot that requires sharp maneuvers.
> 3. The is_steering_converged flag should stop the vehicle from continuing mid-way.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS2: Humble
> - Autoware: main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Incorrect conversion of the steering tire angle to actuator signals. However, simply setting the conversion to be true is insufficient as CARLA uses a constant high steering rate to simulate the wheel angle movement and leads to oscillations using the current steering map. The out_cmd.steer_cmd should simply be set as the input actuator command times the max_steer_ratio.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @maxime-clem (2025-03-20)

> @stevenbrills Thank you very much for working on this ! I should be able to test your PR on Monday and I look forward to the improved steering performance.

### #10295 — Invalid trajectory is being published during lane change when use_waypoints is true and the lane has embedded centerline

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-03-18  |  **Closed:** 2025-05-01  |  **Author:** @MertClk
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10295

**Body:**

> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> **Background:**
> In Lanelet2, the centerline guides the vehicleΓÇÖs path, but its current use in Autoware causes issues such as inaccurate object path predictions and incorrect Frenet frame transformations. To address these, overwriteLaneletsCenterlineWithWaypoints converts the centerline into waypoints for ego path planning, solving the issues but making Autoware's centerline usage harder to interpret. In contrast, overwriteLaneletsCenterline keeps the explicit centerline but retains the limitations. 
> 
> [Link to docs](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_lanelet2_extension/blob/main/autoware_lanelet2_extension/docs/lanelet2_format_extension.md#centerline)
> 
> **Issue:**
> When performing a lane change with an explicit centerline and use_waypoints = true, the trajectory becomes unstable.
> 
> [Video](https://youtu.be/XmLjWD9eNy0)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> - Valid trajectory is being published
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> - Invalid trajectory is being published
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Run PSim with [this](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1yqy1OAoxthCz3U8zoZ4yK60HT5SP00DH/view?usp=sharing) map.
> 2. Try lane change 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> - [getCenterLinePath](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.core/blob/main/planning/autoware_route_handler/src/route_handler.cpp#L1477) function can not clip the path when use_waypoints is true and when the lane has centerline.
>

### #10290 — Compare_map_segmentation degradation at high speed or during turns

- **Labels:** status:stale, component:perception
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10290

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> - `Compare_map_segmentation`'s result is unstable when ego-vehicle moves at high speed or turns. 
> - 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd194bc2-db09-4187-996c-cbdb144c6ed1
> 
> - A large static objects' pointcloud remain even after `compare_map_segmentation`
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61c4e910-8b05-4c5a-a9a6-f137bbe67bf2)
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/184ae0de-0226-46bd-a72e-c08092304565
> 
>   - White point: ground_segmentation result
>   - Pink: compare_map_segmentation result
>   - Green: downsampled map 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> - Compare_map_segmentation should remain stable regardless ego-vehicle's speed
> - Large static objects will be also removed successfully at high speed.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> - Compare_map_segmentation is unstable when ego-vehicle moves fast or turn.
> - Even large static objects' pointcloud remain at high speed moving.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> - Using `logging_simulator`
> - Test with high-speed moving vehicle rosbag 
> - Rendering `/perception/object_recognition/detection/pointcloud_map_filtered/pointcloud` topic to check `compare_map_segmentation` result
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> - Current dynamic transform is always select the latest time (`rclcpp::Time(0)`) to lookup the transform: 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_utils/blob/182c967b189f786faf0f01a08dd7cd2da7999f2f/autoware_utils/include/autoware_utils/ros/managed_transform_buffer.hpp#L211-L212
> 
> - However, some filter such as `compare_map_segmentation` which compare lidar pointcloud with the map pointcloud to remove static objects need to lookup the transform at the time when lidar pointcloud recorded. 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> - An Option for lookup time should be added and set the pointcloud header time for transform during `compare_map_segmentation`

### #10287 — Static Obstacle Avoidance fails to avoid parked vehicle after limited avoid_margin

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2025-03-17  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @MertClk
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10287

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Objects without an avoid_margin are not considered is_avoidable. As a result, the static_obstacle_avoidance module transitions to the onExit process, ultimately causing the ego vehicle to move and miss the deadline."
> 
> 
> 
> [Video](https://youtu.be/MhiZ8nllamY)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> - Ego waits until it can avoid the parked vehicle.
> - Starts avoidance when the space is empty.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> - Ego drives toward the parked vehicle and overran the deadline.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> A scenario file has been generated for this issue. Please use following map and scenario file.
> 
> Map: [Drive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IniR5QFkE8Naum_i5Mn6MlXPGfsAnLRO/view?usp=sharing)
> Scenario File: [Drive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ftACnA-sPx526klK2NTX0_X6mUW61Sbc/view?usp=sharing)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> In shif_line_generator, when the drivable area is limited temporarily, the target object is not kept as avoidable.
> [shift_line_generator.cpp@274](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_static_obstacle_avoidance_module/src/shift_line_generator.cpp#L274)
> 
> ```    if (!o.avoid_margin.has_value()) { 
>       if (
>         data.red_signal_lane.has_value() &&
>         data.red_signal_lane.value().id() == o.overhang_lanelet.id()) {
>         o.info = ObjectInfo::LIMIT_DRIVABLE_SPACE_TEMPORARY;
>       } else {
>         o.info = ObjectInfo::INSUFFICIENT_DRIVABLE_SPACE;
>       }
>       if (o.avoid_required && is_forward_object(o) && is_on_path(o)) {
>         break;
>       } else {
>         unavoidable_objects.push_back(o);
>         continue;
>       }
>     }
>  ```
>  For this reason, the object becomes _isAbsolutelyNotAvoidable_  and this will cause static_obstacle_avoidance module to move to **onExit** phase.
> [scene.cpp@564](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_static_obstacle_avoidance_module/src/scene.cpp#L564)
> 
> As a solution, the object should become "is_avoidable" before following [break](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_static_obstacle_avoidance_module/src/shift_line_generator.cpp#L275) statement.
> 
> [Solution](https://youtu.be/EzveylMVKZo)
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @MertClk (2025-03-17)

> @satoshi-ota @yhisaki  This issue impacts the avoidance module's behavior in narrow lanes. When you have a moment, could you kindly share your thoughts on this?

###### @satoshi-ota (2025-04-02)

> @MertClk I met similar issue and found a bug of avoidance module.
> I've fixed it in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10242 and I guess this PR effective for your issue as well. Could you try to apply above PR on your branch?

###### @MertClk (2025-04-02)

> @satoshi-ota 
> Thank you so much for your follow up on this issue. I tried this scenario with the latest Autoware and I confirm that I'm using [#10242](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10242). Here are my findings,
> 
> 1. The default `stop_buffer` value is set to 1 m. With this value, the scenario fails and ego can not keep stopping.
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2eb48784-14a6-4f9d-ad44-c7691f86bf81
> 
> 2. When `stop_buffer` set to 2 m, it is possible to pass the scenario. However, ego still can not keep stopping. 
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d7853ee-261f-40d8-bc2a-0e6eb36c3f87
> 
> 3. If we modify the scenario so that the adjacent lane is busy a bit more after the traffic light turns green, the scenario fails again. 
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98e4beff-963a-4be0-a433-f264a7765971
> 
> [New scenario file](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1L2eMBkVwT5m1YglyqhInsEGhK92l99oc/view?usp=sharing)

###### @stale (2025-06-01)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @Ajay-Kumar-ELM (2025-06-05)

> Hi Autoware team,
> 
> IΓÇÖm working with the behavior_path_planner module from autoware.universe, specifically testing static obstacle avoidance on a two-lane same-direction road with the following layout:
> 
> - Left lane
> - Right lane
> - Road shoulder (on the right)
> 
> All lanes are in the same driving direction.
> 
> When I place a stopped vehicle in the left lane, the ego vehicle successfully avoids it by shifting to the right lane, as expected.
> However, when I place a stopped vehicle in the right lane, the ego vehicle does not attempt to avoid it by shifting to the left lane, even though:
> 
> - The left lane is drivable and part of the same route group
> - There are no other obstacles present in the left lane
> - Lane change attribute is add on all the lanes
> 
>  I'd like to clarify:
> 
> 1. Is left-lane avoidance from the right lane currently supported in the static obstacle avoidance module?
> 2. Are there known constraints or failure conditions (e.g., can_execute_shift, safety margins, avoidance maneuver rejection) that might block this behavior?
> 
> FYI https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/19ffe7f739801064242dc1b73505829b43e1a0bf/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_static_obstacle_avoidance_module/config/static_obstacle_avoidance.param.yaml#L153 is set to "auto"
> 
> Failed Scenario: Right to Left Expected
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6df354e8-9895-4a22-ad05-63c1163a97cc)
> 
> Success Scenario: Left to Right Overtake success
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ef4ca6f-819f-42bb-883e-75a7e3aabf4c)

###### @satoshi-ota (2025-07-09)

> Sorry for the late reply. 
> 
> > Is left-lane avoidance from the right lane currently supported in the static obstacle avoidance module?
> 
> Left-lane avoidance from the right lane is supported.
> 
> However, please note that the avoidance module does not attempt to avoid every stopped object. It is designed to avoid objects that are not expected to move again in the short term.
> 
> For example, parked vehicles are assumed to remain stationary for a while, so the module determines that they should be avoided.
> On the other hand, for vehicles stopped at a red traffic light, the ego vehicle can simply continue following them once the light turns green, so avoidance is not strictly necessary. As a result, the current implementation does not perform avoidance in such cases.
> 
> Based on the image you shared, the system has determined that there is no vehicle that needs to be avoided in this position.
> Unfortunately, the current system does not support avoidance behavior in such situations. ≡ƒÖÅ
