### #10285 — Drivable area limitation -before red traffic light- fails when driving in narrow lane

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-03-17  |  **Closed:** 2025-07-10  |  **Author:** @MertClk
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10285

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The avoidance module considers traffic light information to determine the appropriate behavior for the ego vehicle. If the ego has not yet initiated an avoidance maneuver, the module restricts the maximum shift length and ensures that the vehicle remains **only** within the current lane during a red traffic signal. This prevents the ego from obstructing other vehicles, even if it begins an avoidance maneuver but subsequently stops at a red signal.
> 
> However, when the ego vehicle is driving in a narrow lane, and its footprint exceeds the boundaries of the concatenated lanelets (previous, current, and next), the avoidance module **fails** to enforce drivable area restrictions. This results in unintended behavior.
> 
> A video demonstrating the issue is provided below.
> 
> [Demonstration](https://youtu.be/VcYZDIpdtjc)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> - The ego behaves as documented in the [readme](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_static_obstacle_avoidance_module#planning-at-red-traffic-light) 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> - The ego vehicle starts avoidance maneuver and blocks the adjacent lane 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> This issue can be reproduced with the provided scenario file and Autoware sample map which can be download from [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1499_nsbUbIeturZaDj7jhUownh5fvXHd/view).
> 
> Scenario File: [File](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OWo6gG-ETUselO70s6_PmX0z-K6JB-vx/view?usp=sharing)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> [This](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_static_obstacle_avoidance_module/src/scene.cpp#L221) value returns false, since ego exceeds the the boundary while turning.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #10282 — localization/map component is dependent on the packages outside of localization/map component

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pull/5586 found that the planning/control component is dependent on the following packages outside of the planning/control component.
> 
> - sensing/autoware_pcl_extensions
> - sensing/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor
> - system/autoware_default_adapi_helpers/autoware_automatic_pose_initializer
> 
> Since the dependencies will no longer follow a parent-child relationship, the components become tightly coupled.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Ensure that there are no dependency packages spanning across components. Connections between components should depend only on the `core` packages or the `autoware.universe/common` packages.
> 
> Ref. https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/8805
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Ensure that there are no dependency packages spanning across components. Connections between components should depend only on the `core` packages or the `autoware.universe/common` packages.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> The localization/map packages will no longer directly depend on the following packages.
> 
> - [ ] sensing/autoware_pcl_extensions
> - [ ] sensing/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor
> - [ ] system/autoware_default_adapi_helpers/autoware_automatic_pose_initializer

###### @KYabuuchi (2025-03-18)

> @shpark98  YabLoc determines its initial position using **GNSS** and estimates orientation by matching semantic segmentation results with a vector map.  
> Without GNSS, the initial position cannot be automatically determined.  
> 
> In environments where GNSS is unavailable, such as indoors, global coordinate information in the PCD is not necessary.
> In such cases, GNSS-based position correction and automatic initial position estimation is not available.
> 
> If you plan to use it outdoors, I recommend creating the PCD in a global coordinate system.
> For example, the sample data I am proposing in this thread uses global coordinates (MGRS).

>

> Or is it embedded in the vector map created by the vector map builder?

###### @KYabuuchi (2025-03-18)

> @shpark98 GNSS positions are not compared to anything. Autoware projects the latitude and longitude output by GNSS into local coordinates using the specified projection type.
> 
> Autoware supports several projection methods for converting latitude/longitude to local coordinates, and [this page](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/map/autoware_map_projection_loader#map-projector-info-file-specification) provides detailed information.
> For example, if using MGRS, latitude = 36┬░ and longitude = -115┬░ would be projected to `11SPV 67305, 97905`.
> 
> 
> If you use the MGRS projection type, you need to create the PCD's x, y coordinates in the MGRS XXXXX, YYYYY coordinate system.
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5eccd077-1ba1-409e-84df-39cf856e7fee)

###### @shpark98 (2025-03-18)

> @KYabuuchi I'm glad given image helped. Your answers have been extremely helpful!
> 
> So, if you transform the origin of the PCD map based on the MGRS information, the GNSS data will be aligned with the PCD map, allowing you to use GNSS within Autoware.
> 
> This is just a personal curiosity, but do you know the approximate error if I only connect GNSS to Autoware without using Yabloc?
> And if the vector map only contains roads without additional information like traffic lights, can Yabloc still function properly?

###### @KYabuuchi (2025-03-18)

> @shpark98 
> > t do you know the approximate error if I only connect GNSS to Autoware without using Yabloc?
> 
> I'm not sure.
> 
> >  if the vector map only contains roads without additional information like traffic lights, can Yabloc still function properly?
> 
> Since YabLoc relies on road markings, information other than the road surface is unnecessary.
> YabLoc functions even if the map does not include traffic signals.

### #10225 — Add pointcloud_densifier package

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-03-04  |  **Closed:** 2025-04-02  |  **Author:** @kaancolak
- **Labels:** component:perception, component:sensing, run:build-and-test-differential, perception
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10225

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> This issue addresses the implementation of a PointCloud Densifier component for Autoware, which enhances sparse LiDAR point cloud data by leveraging information from previous frames. Long-range LiDAR data is often sparse(after 80-90 meters), limiting the effectiveness of downstream perception algorithms. This component overcomes this limitation by selectively integrating points from previous frames into the current frame, resulting in a denser representation of the environment.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The main purpose is to detect long range stationary vehicles on the road, such as those stopped at an intersection or traffic light.
> 
> This package increases the density of long-range points for detects stationary vehicles with rule-based LiDAR algorithms. Additionally, we plan to create a pull request (PR) to add  roi_excluded_downsample_filter for preventing the downsampling of long-range points, with OT128 stationary objects detection accuracy improved to around 150-200 meters.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The algorithm works as follows:
> 
> 1- **ROI Filtering:** First filters the input point cloud to only keep points in a specific region of interest (ROI), typically focused on the distant area in front of the vehicle.
> 
> 2- **Occupancy Grid Creation:** Creates a bas┼ƒc 2D occupancy grid from the filtered points to track which areas contain valid points in the current frame.
> 
> 3- **Previous Frame Integration:** Transforms points from previous frames into the current frame's coordinate system using TF transformations.
> 
> 4- **Selective Point Addition:** Adds points from previous frames only if they fall into grid cells that are occupied in the current frame. This ensures that only relevant points are added, avoiding ghost points from dynamic objects.
> 
> 5- **Combined Output:** Returns a combined point cloud that includes both the current frame's points and selected points from previous frames.
> 
> The implementation follows Autoware's filtering architecture by inheriting from the `Filter` base class, providing compatibility with the existing preprocessing pipeline and support for point cloud indices.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Create meta package

> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware in Carla, and I found a situation that Autoware fails to yield to a vehicle at a roundabout.
> Here's a video of the situation: [[rviz](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/12N5dh1fuK56n5gdrlRm7LHK0Fs7WI5w/1CYIKRD4ZqfQ6wSNyZRkW4sbO8ZudUu1-crlg3drlFww)]

> 
> In the video, as shown in the image above, a vehicle, which is 'unknown' to Autoware, is ignored at a roundabout.
> 
> Here's more information of the situation.
> - Starting/Goal pose (from `launch.log` file)
> ```
> initial pose - x: 43.210449, y: 7.834843, z: 0.066023
> initial orientation - qx: 0.000052, qy: -0.000355, qz: 0.999972, qw: 0.007506
> goal pose - x: -18.544405, y: -130.888123, z: 2.000000
> goal orientation - qx: -0.000000, qy: 0.000000, qz: 0.999936, qw: -0.011316

### #10206 — goal_planner can not generate candidate goal poses when there is an opposite neighbor lane

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-03-01  |  **Closed:** 2025-03-13  |  **Author:** @MertClk
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10206

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Goal planner can not generate candidate goal poses and stop before the goal when there is an opposite direction neighbor lane.
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00a1e81e-48d7-4a26-9491-2979b3327e47)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Goal planner should generate goal poses and complete the pull over maneuver.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Ego vehicle stops before the rough goal pose due to empty set of candidate goal poses.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Run PSim by using shoulder_lane test map provided in autoware_test_utils package.
> 2. Initialize ego in lane section with 4.0m width with 2 direction(Provided image below).
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9d5b62b-f2e7-4669-ba9c-f44fd0006335)
> 
> 3. Publish a rough goal pose somewhere on the ego lane.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> When filtering candidate goal poses, goal_planner checks if the ego's footprint stays in the pull over lane. This check rejects all possible candidates. 
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/autoware_behavior_path_goal_planner_module/src/goal_searcher.cpp#L248
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #10176 — Autoware_carla_interface does not work with CARLA

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-02-20  |  **Closed:** 2025-03-21  |  **Author:** @Sephiroth1118
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 11  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10176

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I'm testing the co-simulation between autoware.universe and the CARLA simulator. I use the autoware_carla_interface. The launch file is `e2e_simulator.launch.xml`. Before this one, I ran the `planning_simulator.launch.xml` successfully.
> 
> This is the log file.
> 
> [launch.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18882195/launch.log)
> There are mainly three errors:
> 
> 1. `[component_container_mt-74] [ERROR] [1739958327.899700638] [planning.scenario_planning.parking.costmap_generator]: Could not find a connection between 'map' and 'base_link' because they are not part of the same tree.Tf has two or more unconnected trees.`
> 2. `[service_log_checker_node-9] [ERROR] [1739958327.991541454] [system.service_log_checker]: /localization/initialize: status code 1 'The vehicle is not stopped.' (/localization/util/pose_initializer)`
> 3. `1740032228.9587953 [service_log_checker_node-9] [ERROR] [1740032228.957593316] [system.service_log_checker]: /localization/initialize: status code 4 'align server failed.' (/localization/util/pose_initializer)`
> 
> I searched the errors and found this issue: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3208. I tried the methods mention in it but not work.
> 
> 1. This the output of topic `/sensing/vehicle_velocity_converter/twist_with_covariance`
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8bb98b4-0920-4475-8254-158fa3000a4b)
> 2. I then checked the `stop_check_enabled`, found it in the file `/home/qiujing/autoware/src/universe/autoware.universe/launch/tier4_simulator_launch/launch/simulator.launch.xml`, but it is already False.
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c4911d53-4818-46de-be3d-517fb813a15a)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I expected the "2D Pose Estimate" in Rviz will initialize the localization of the vehicle and then I can set the goal by "2D Pose Goal". 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Nothing happened. The localization of the vehicle can not be initialized.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start the CARLA by `./CarlaUE4.sh`
> 2. Start autoware.universe by `ros2 launch autoware_launch e2e_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=$HOME/autoware_map/Town01 vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=awsim_sensor_kit simulator_type:=carla carla_map:=Town01`
> 3. Set the Pose of the vehicle.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS2: Humble
> - Autoware: autoware.universe from the `main` branch
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> I think the vehicle is detected not stopped so that I can not set the Pose of the vehicle. But I do not know how to solve it. There are some similar problems from others, but not suitable for mine.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

###### @maxime-clem (2025-02-20)

> Yes 6GB is not enough to run both Autoware and Carla at the same time. Even with 8GB I sometimes have issues.
> A possible workaround:
> 1. only run the `autoware_carla_interface` and the Carla simulator.
> 2. record a rosbag of the topics published by the interface.
> 3. close the Carla simulator, run Autoware.
> 4. replay the previously recorded bag (with the `--clock` argument).
> 
> This should allow you to at least test the perception and localization components.

### #10168 — Ear clipping triangulation problem when loading .osm format map

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-02-20  |  **Closed:** 2025-02-28  |  **Author:** @seuganger
- **Labels:** component:map
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10168

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [ ] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I have met a bug when loading lanelet2 format vector map when launching planning simulation. I made the vector map with bag2lanelet and Vector Map Builder Tool, and in the tool the vector map are what they expected to be. 
> Other people have met the same question before: https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/5603
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> In the Vector Map Builder Tool, my vector map was like:
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b67cd39b-50f0-4a59-a5b6-b82c4f110d3d)
> As it can be shown up in this tool, it should be used in simulation. 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> When importing this map to planning simulation, it was like:
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0283bf6-7913-4f7d-b909-801216962093)
> The white point in the middle of this picture is point cloud, and the green area is the lane area. It seem that a lanelet2 node was located far from other nodes. To be more specific, I will show pictures in different scales below. 
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b14c3cff-8bd7-4864-bec2-2b46cac5976d)
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec0ed6e5-a244-4672-b699-434ff21f1bbe)
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91ac4417-39de-4b27-9794-2473289bef2b)
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4856d3d9-12eb-49ba-a57b-fa3cd0ebba1a)
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Use my lanelet2 and PCD files
> https://entuedu-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/n2402056d_e_ntu_edu_sg/EmqltdP8bZZHqo4XXkVgwOUBbUEuJiHzwt59VR5UaZrj5A?e=Qwj0EA
> 2. Download the files, rename them, put them in ~/autoware_map/rosbag-test (or your map path), change the launch file ~/autoware/src/launcher/autoware_launch/autoware_launch/launch/planning_simulator.launch.xml line 15,16 into map names
> 3. run the autoware planning simulation with
> `ros2 launch autoware_launch planning_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=$HOME/autoware_map/rosbag-test vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit`
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> -OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> -ROS: humble
> -Autoware: universe (docker installation)
> -Hardware: Nvidia 3090 GPU
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> There is a warning: Could not find valid vertex for ear clipping triangulation. Triangulation result might be invalid. I suspect that a node was not initialized properly, which causes the ear clipping triangulation fail. It seems a node was put far away from its original place, which has been shown in the pictures above. I have checked all of my nodes in osm format lanelet map, none of them was far away from others such significantly to generate this problem in simulation. So the possible cause is, some node information was written in the code, when testing with sample maps, it did not arouse problems. 
> Besides, I find out that the the distance between wrongly initialized node and point cloud is approximate the distance between sample map config and  my map config. This picture shows the distance between point cloud and wrong node:
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/876f268f-6459-4353-b96f-6c29f8c5e787)
> The [lat, lon] in my config is: [latitude: 35.22312494103  longitude: 138.80245834626]
> In sample config is: [latitude: 35.23808753540768  longitude: 139.9009591876285]
> The distance between 2 map configs is about 60 kilometers, which echos the distance in the picture. 
> 
> So the conclusion is, the config file might be the cause of this problem, whose path is fixed in the code and the default is in sample-map-planning. In the next step, I will try to change the path of config file to find a solution. If it succeeded, I will report in the comments and give a suggestion on how to avoid this problem. However, this should still be reported as a bug because both the tutorial and the launch.xml file did not mention any information about the location of map config files. 
> 
> In later experiments, it is known that this problem is not caused by config file, the most possible cause is there is a lanelet node inside the code, which will arouse problems when using lanelet map that generated in PCDs whose frame is different from the sample PCD. It means that changing config file will not influence the real start point of lanelet map. 
> 
> ### Additional context
> I also suspected that the negative x position cause problems in ear clipping triangulation. Next week I will try to add 1000 on every x,y of points in PCD and .osm files. If this can avoid this problem to occur, it is certain that x value closed to zero will influence the ear clipping triangulation. 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @YamatoAndo (2025-02-25)

> @seuganger Hi,
> In `map_projector_info.yaml`, MGRS coordinate system `54SVE` is specified, but it seems that your map was not created using the MGRS coordinate system.
> Please update `map_projector_info.yaml` as follows.
> 
> ```
> projector_type: Local
> ```
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/map/autoware_map_projection_loader#using-local-coordinate
> 

###### @seuganger (2025-02-27)

> Solved, thank you for your reply!

- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10155

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
>

No messages will be sent to it. Last incompatible policy: RELIABILITY_QOS_POLICY (default_incompatible_qos_callback() at ...)

> 
>       <include file="$(find-pkg-share radar_scan_to_pointcloud2)/launch/radar_scan_to_pointcloud2.launch.xml">

> 
>   </group>
> <launch>

> 2. Launch logging simulator and provided launch file.
> 3. Play your bag file which includes radar data.

### #10150 — CI: Ccache is too small, causing longer-than-necessary build times

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-02-18  |  **Closed:** 2025-11-18  |  **Author:** @mojomex
- **Labels:** type:ci
- **Comments:** 18  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10150

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When looking at [a random CI run](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/actions/runs/13368521713/job/37335100701) I noticed that the Ccache size is limited to a very small `600 MB` whereas GitHub allows for payloads of up to [`10 GB`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/caching-dependencies-to-speed-up-workflows#usage-limits-and-eviction-policy) in their cache action.
> 
> The observed cache hit ratio is quite poor as a result:
> ```
> 525M	/root/.ccache
> Summary:
>   Hits:             2867 /  7670 (37.38 %)
>     Direct:         1671 /  7892 (21.17 %)
>     Preprocessed:   1196 /  6004 (19.92 %)
>   Misses:           4803
>     Direct:         6221
>     Preprocessed:   4808
>   Uncacheable:      5398
> Primary storage:
>   Hits:             5667 / 16696 (33.94 %)
>   Misses:          11029
>   Cache size (GB):  0.55 /  0.60 (91.25 %)
>   Cleanups:           34
> ```
> 
> @xmfcx 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I'd expect the Ccache to be limited to 10 GB, and to have hit rates of close to 100% for PRs such as the one that triggered the above CI run: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/10116
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The cache has only 600 MB and a hit rate of under 40% for a PR with no code or build system changes.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> See the above CI pipeline run
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @xmfcx (2025-02-18)

> It is limited to 600MB because Github Public Runners don't have much space available.
> 
> Please see:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/7555
> 
> Parent Issue:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/7501
> 
> Maybe with current `ubuntu-24.04` images, we might have slightly more space but it's a tight rope.

###### @mojomex (2025-02-18)

> Thanks for the fast respose ≡ƒÜÇ 
> I see...  sad times ≡ƒÿÑ 

###### @mojomex (2025-08-19)

> As posted [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10932#issuecomment-3199109952):
> 
> We could also introduce a [Ccache Remote Storage Backend](https://ccache.dev/manual/4.7.html#_remote_storage_backends).
> 
> A full Autoware build produces ~> 15 GB~ around 5GB (see [@xmfcx's comment](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10150#issuecomment-3199507217)) of Ccache, but as seen in the comments above, this cannot be fixed since our runners have limited hard drive space (#7555).
> 
> A remote cache can be shared across all runners, workflows and steps, and will handle changed dependencies, different compilers etc. correctly. It would however require a hosted Redis instance. Cost-wise this should be quite cheap, and might be offset by saving AWS costs when building CUDA code that would also utilize this new backend.

###### @esteve (2025-08-19)

> The disk space limit was back when we were using public runners, right @xmfcx ? Don't we use hosted runners nowadays? 

###### @xmfcx (2025-08-19)

> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/8c162649aa7e7319b8c8c01c3896500f0b4e5a51/.github/workflows/build-test-tidy-pr.yaml#L43-L76
>

> | build-and-test-differential-cuda           | Self-hosted     |
> | build-and-test-packages-above-differential | Self-hosted     |
> 
> And here is the check for cuda-necessity:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/8c162649aa7e7319b8c8c01c3896500f0b4e5a51/.github/workflows/build-test-tidy-pr.yaml#L29-L36
> 
> And even if cuda is required for a PR, both `build-and-test-differential` and `build-and-test-differential-cuda` are run in parallel to make sure the build is still successful on non-cuda version too.
> 
> So, many (more than half) of the CI runs are made in public runners.
>

###### @mojomex (2025-08-19)

> @xmfcx Hmm, it might have been a debug build or a build of an internal product based on Autoware wehn I did my testing a while back.
> One important additional factor in CI is that a few versions of the code might be cached at once (different PRs, branches like main/humble). Ccache deals with this correctly, but overall cache size will be bigger than with just one version of Autoware.
> 
> Although, I reckon that increasing the CCache size to 5GB would already be a huge improvement for our build times...

###### @xmfcx (2025-08-19)

> Will ~~sacrifice~~ re-allocate one of the 8 self hosted runners to host a Redis cache with 24GB of effective cache with a single Redis instance. The machine is 8c16t and 32GB RAM, since Redis is single-threaded it will be slightly underutilized but it's a good way to start testing.
> 
> This is not a very urgent issue for now, since [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/actions/runs/16671491300/job/47188653507) the modification of `pointcloud_preprocessor` on `build-and-test-differential-cuda` took 6 mins to compile, I think it's reasonable.
> 
> But definitely worth giving it a shot. If it works, it would simplify the CI since we wouldn't need to maintain a ccache cache with github, instead would pass a password to the redis and they all would pull/push from the remote cache.

> https://github.com/marketplace/actions/local-cache-on-self-hosted-runner

###### @xmfcx (2025-08-19)

> @esteve [this was my response to your question](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10150#issuecomment-3199507217).
> 
> To reiterate, more than half of the usages of the cache is performed on public runners which lack space. This is why we had to limit the ccache cache size.
> 
> I will also link the original issue where I introduced ccache to the CI:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7501
> 
> ```mermaid
> graph TD
>     bntc["build-and-test-cuda"]
>     --> ccache([ccache])
>     -->|"actions/cache/save@v4"| ghac[("GitHub Actions Cache")]
>     
>     ghac-->|"actions/cache/restore@v4"| bntd["build-and-test-differential"]
>     ghac-->|"actions/cache/restore@v4"| bntdc["build-and-test-differential-cuda"]
>     ghac-->|"actions/cache/restore@v4"| bntc
>     ghac-->|"actions/cache/restore@v4"| bnt["build-and-test"]
> 
> bnt:::cla_bnt
> bntc:::cla_bnt
> bntd:::cla_bntd
> bntdc:::cla_bntd
> ccache:::cla_cache
> ghac:::cla_cache
> 
> classDef cla_bnt fill:#00E678,stroke:#555,color:#000
> classDef cla_bntd fill:#3F2EE3,stroke:#555,color:#FFF
> classDef cla_cache fill:#00C8FF,stroke:#555,color:#000
> ```
> 
> This still holds true. The system is fairly simple, it's just that for build-and-test-differential (non-cuda) workflows, we utilize public runners which lack space.
> 
> > https://github.com/marketplace/actions/local-cache-on-self-hosted-runner
> 
> This probably wouldn't work because with build-and-test-differential workflow, we don't operate on the runner directly, we utilize [container:](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/731e345663d726210a63077c072ab5bf4af5ca57/.github/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml#L43) argument, so it is isolated from the system.

###### @esteve (2025-08-19)

> # Summary, reflection and comparison with CI
> 
> Also to give perspective, here is the CI:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/actions/runs/19425155918/job/55570817548 (build-and-test run from the same time as my runs)
> 
> **Runner Specs:**
> 
> ```
> Intel(R) Xeon(R) E-2288G CPU @ 3.70GHz (8c 16t)
> Mem: 31 GiB
> Swap: 74 GiB
> ```
> 
> Max ccache size = 600MB
> 
> **ccache stats before build:**
> 
> ```
> Summary:
>   Hits:                0 /  9110 (0.00 %)
>     Direct:            0 /  9329 (0.00 %)
>     Preprocessed:      0 /  9115 (0.00 %)
>   Misses:           9110
>     Direct:         9329
>     Preprocessed:   9115
>   Uncacheable:      6414
> Primary storage:

>   Misses:          18444
>   Cache size (GB):  0.52 /  0.60 (86.70 %)
>   Cleanups:           26
> ```
> 
> - Summary: 329 packages finished [50min 58s]
> 
> **ccache stats after build:**
> 
> ```
> Summary:
>   Hits:              710 /  9110 (7.79 %)
>     Direct:           80 /  9329 (0.86 %)
>     Preprocessed:    630 /  9035 (6.97 %)
>   Misses:           8400
>     Direct:         9249
>     Preprocessed:   8405
>   Uncacheable:      6414
> Primary storage:
>   Hits:             1380 / 19034 (7.25 %)
>   Misses:          17654
>   Cache size (GB):  0.53 /  0.60 (88.41 %)
>   Cleanups:           82
> ```
> 
> It builds noticeably less packages since it doesnt include `tool.repos`
> 
> Yet it has more hits albeit **low (7.25 %)** but **larger than my (0%).**
> 
> Since the autoware_universe CI builds less packages, I wanted to replicate that locally too. (I wish I did this sooner.)
> 
> ```bash
> mkdir universe_ws
> cd universe_ws/
> git clone https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe.git
> mkdir deps
> vcs import deps < autoware_universe/build_depends_humble.repos
> vcs import deps < autoware_universe/build_depends_nightly.repos
> colcon build \
>   --event-handlers console_cohesion+ \
>   --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
>   --mixin coverage-gcc coverage-pytest compile-commands \
>   --packages-above-and-dependencies \
>   $(colcon list --base-paths autoware_universe/ --names-only | xargs)
> 
> ...
> Summary: 344 packages finished [35min 5s]
> 
> mfc@whale:~/projects/universe_ws$ ccache -s
> Summary:
>   Hits:                0 /   9284 (0.00 %)
>     Direct:            0 /   9509 (0.00 %)
>     Preprocessed:      0 /   9289 (0.00 %)
>   Misses:           9284
>     Direct:         9509
>     Preprocessed:   9289
>   Uncacheable:       225
> Primary storage:
>   Hits:                0 /  18798 (0.00 %)
>   Misses:          18798
>   Cache size (GB):  0.75 / 600.00 (0.12 %)
> ```
> 
> The package count **discrepancy of 15** between **CI's 329** and **local run's 344** is probably from the fact that some packages in the CI make use of the ROS buildfarm debian packages.
> 
> Then I reduced the cache size to `600 MB` and rebuilt the autoware_universe.
> 
> ```bash
> Summary: 344 packages finished [34min 33s]
> 
> Summary:
>   Hits:              342 /  9284 (3.68 %)
>     Direct:           23 /  9509 (0.24 %)
>     Preprocessed:    319 /  9266 (3.44 %)
>   Misses:           8942
>     Direct:         9486
>     Preprocessed:   8947
>   Uncacheable:       225
> Primary storage:
>   Hits:              669 / 19102 (3.50 %)
>   Misses:          18433
>   Cache size (GB):  0.54 /  0.60 (90.72 %)
>   Cleanups:          106
> ```
> 
> Even though it is still slow, at least got some hits. I am guessing, with 15 less packages, it would be closer to what we have in the CI.
> 
> ## My Verdict
> 
> We don't need a very large ccache cache.
> Even with 15 more packages, my local tests created cache of `750 MB` of cache.
> So I'd say even `900 MB` would be plenty for the universe repository.
> 
> But my tests show that even going from `750 MB` cache to `600 MB` of cache reduces the hit rate drastically.
> And it increases the build time way too much, almost same as no-cache situation, rendering it useless.
> 
> So I'd say, we reduce the `autoware:universe-devel` image size by `300 MB` and increase the ccache max size to `900 MB`.
> 
> ## Reducing the image size to open up space
> 
> ```bash
> xhost +local:docker
> 
> docker run -it \
>     --env DISPLAY=$DISPLAY \
>     --env QT_X11_NO_MITSHM=1 \
>     --volume /tmp/.X11-unix:/tmp/.X11-unix \
>     ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:universe-devel \
>     bash
> 
> sudo apt update
> sudo apt install -y qdirstat
> qdirstat
> ```
> 
> <img width="1421" height="1198" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40b9c212-6149-47ce-b35a-98bdb243f4ed" />
> 
> Right now, in the `autoware:universe-devel` we have the following things that can be removed:
> ```
> root@c92e985967a2:/autoware# du -sh /opt/autoware
> 1.1G	/opt/autoware
> 
> root@c92e985967a2:/autoware# du -sh /root/.local/pipx/venvs/ansible
> 439M	/root/.local/pipx/venvs/ansible
> ```
> Both these folders could be removed, they have no use for the CI and probably for the developers too. This is a development image after all, not a runtime image.
> And we could increase the cache size and still end up with 1.2GB more empty space.

> After migrating to the `autoware_` prefix, especially the `autoware_` prefix in the readme file, it is now a disaster to search for the documentation of the package I would like to see.

> Here are some suggestions on how to write a document title
> 1. avoid "autoware_detection_by_tracker"
> 2. use "Autoware Detection by Tracker"

> **Continuation from:** 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3135#issuecomment-2634342143
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To simplify filtering out packages that depend on CUDA.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Create a meta package with a basic CMakeLists that checks for CUDA.
> 
> All packages that **directly** depend on CUDA should depend on this meta package.
> 
> **Package name:** `autoware_cuda_dependency_meta`
> 
> The README of this package should explain why the package exists and should contain possible usages.
> 
> **Example:**
> - `colcon build --packages-ignore $(colcon list --packages-above autoware_tensorrt_common autoware_cuda_utils --names-only | tr '\n' ' ')`
> 
> ### Useful graph
> 
> `colcon graph --packages-above autoware_cuda_utils autoware_tensorrt_common --dot | dot -Tsvg -Grankdir=LR -Gnodesep=0.2 -Granksep=0.3 -Gconcentrate=true -o graph.svg`
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09aea4a1-25b2-4fd9-9bcf-c3997400f4bd)
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Create the meta-package
> - [x] Update the package.xml files of the packages that directly depend on CUDA.

### #10051 — Backward trajectory is generated when the ego vehicle invades a drivable area

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2025-01-30  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, simulator:carla
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/10051

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team, 
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla, and I found a situation that a backward trajectory is generated when the ego vehicle invades a drivable area.
> 
> Here's the video of the situation: [[rviz](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11xNTtzZfvKBendreTpLPoC7sLBMsW23/hQ84HhJYZQqpsI2WVkFpMpt_1apYxNwr-pLrgQl3zAww)]
> In the video, the ego vehicle initially stepping a drivable area, and the generated trajectory is for driving backward.
> At 0:29, the NPC vehicle drives to behind the ego and  the ego starts to turn left (I cannot sure the NPC has an impact on this issue), which makes the ego vehicle invades the center line.
> 
> I tried to reproduce the situation with [the planning simulation](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/), and **I think the issue occurs when the ego vehicle invades the drivable area at the initial point**.
> Here's the video for more details: [[planning simulation](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11xNi3JQkWFFKZpA5aIke8BbQRYF0tqV/2c5QCtpALyPkPQreMNpKIl-Wb6-pa-7x-1rsg0iX0Aww)]
> The video shows two cases:
> 1. (The ego does not invade the drivable area) At 0:06, the ego vehicle is initialized and drives to the destination well.
> 2. (The ego invades the drivable area): However, At 0:29, Autoware generates backward trajectory, and the ego vehicle reaches the destination only after following the trajectory.
> 
> Actually, I cannot point out the reason why the ego vehicle drives forward in the first video, even though backward trajectory is generated. (I don't know why the gear does not changed)
> But I thought that the situation in the planning simulation is similar to that of the first video.
> 
> Here are more details of the situation:
> - Starting/Goal pose (from `launch.log` file)
> ```
> initial pose - x: 0.726764, y: 190.627121, z: 0.068133
> initial orientation - qx: -0.000201, qy: 0.000178, qz: -0.715753, qw: 0.698354
> goal pose - x: 209.993347, y: -9.808371, z: 0.275307
> goal orientation - qx: 0.000000, qy: 0.000000, qz: -0.007468, qw: 0.999972
> ```
> - Map: [Town03](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rt1pKEfY-hqC2pMrHfajg1EVfjlIcAX5)
> - ros2bag file: [[ros2bag](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11xNWerWmWIQ2hXT5z8eFnhGgcKHRsZL/prM_15FK_y5RYxHkrAuGbt-XpjlnpMCV-Cr9AX0X2Aww)]
> - launch.log file: [[launch.log](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11xNgdFo2fvNwyv6lqilLQflkIUfT42d/e-pXWN0A2tFt32fa8Y6UAfCukH5TFJnK-H79AHlP2Aww)]
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope the ego vehicle drives following the center of the lane.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> However, the ego vehicle invades the center line.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Pull image from `https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware/334254906?tag=universe-devel-cuda-0.40.0-amd64`, and run Autoware.
> 2. Run ros2bag file above.
> 
> In the planning simulation, I could utilize the initial/goal pose above.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (Docker), Ubuntu 20.04 (host)
> - Autoware: [0.40.0](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/tree/0.40.0)
> - Carla: 0.9.15
> - autoware_carla_interface: [link](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/0.40.0/simulator/autoware_carla_interface)
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #9844 — Erroneous dynamic expansion of drivable area makes the ego vehicle stop.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2025-01-07  |  **Closed:** 2025-07-22  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** component:planning, simulator:carla
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/9844

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla, and I found a situation that the ego vehicle stops due to an erroneous dynamic expansion of drivable area.
> Here's the video of the situation: [[rviz](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11eHR2chyqXx1CsPMgslA59V6zMAVFHg/hHDQPg4Ecus7_DNunw2JNog03mqFQ38o-O7ygUmMk9Qs)]
> 
> From the start of the video, a drivable area at the corner sometimes invades the trajectory(I cannot know why the message `outside_drivable_area` does not appear.), and when the vehicle is turning at the corner, it eventually stops as one of the rear wheel is at outside the drivable area, which was caused by the update of the area.
> 
> Here's more information of the situation.
> - Starting/Goal pose (from `launch.log` file)
> ```
> initial pose - x: 334.279584, y: 168.742911, z: 0.263412
> initial orientation - qx: -0.000302, qy: -0.000023, qz: -0.003080, qw: 0.999995
> goal pose - x: 212.669266, y: 364.220459, z: 2.857196
> goal orientation - qx: 0.000000, qy: 0.000000, qz: -0.003752, qw: 0.999993
> ```
> - Map: [Town04](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ZZYgqQJ8l2VRAZxYVt4shTU_PMzF9C7Y)
> - ros2bag file: [[ros2bag](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11eHR7OlbW0kyBuUuHbYb2fwNeVIraQh/E3CzYQq85CsYW5eouYbK2GAYIdFOs768-U7NgJBUo9Qs)]
> - launch.log file: [[launch.log](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11eIIrHK0FrKMjp8PM9s9dBbhR66SbcS/xscUB9d7UyPLX9newHugPZpEMDUFpFEU-d7OACSgo9Qs)]
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope the ego vehicle not to stop before reaching the destination.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The vehicle stucks before reaching the destination.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Pull image from `https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware/321564631?tag=universe-devel-cuda-0.39.1-amd64`, and run Autoware.
> 2. Run ros2bag file above.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (Docker), Ubuntu 20.04 (host)
> - Autoware: [0.39.1](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/tree/0.39.1)
> - Carla: 0.9.15
> - autoware_carla_interface: [link](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/0.39.0/simulator/autoware_carla_interface)
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @stale (2025-03-09)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @maxime-clem (2025-06-17)

> I have been able to reproduce the issue. There is a bug in the dynamic drivable area expansion since the feature is only supposed to push the drivable area bounds futher and not bring them closer to the path.

###### @maxime-clem (2025-07-14)

> The bug happens when the Path goes outside the original drivable area (i.e., the left/right bounds of the lane).
> The expansion assumes that the input path is always between the original left/right bounds, but it seems to not always be the case.
> The issue may be caused by the input Path being incorrectly resampled, causing its linestring to "cut the corner" and go out of the drivable area. The image bellow shows the input path and drivable area of the expansion, and in Rviz we see the resulting drivable area and the final Path (which has correct points).
> 
> <img width="3344" height="1689" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7251200b-278d-41d5-8582-ab127391fae1" />
> 

###### @maxime-clem (2025-07-22)

> Fixed with https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/10989

### #9816 — Non-blocking obstacle makes the vehicle stop.

> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla, and I found a situation that the ego vehicle cannot move due to an obstacle, which does not block the vehicle actually.
> Here's the rviz video of the situation: [[rviz](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11YNOzNFTSzIxMmuMeiu4ve4mSdMYYHf/YFx9oJYMWd9MLMxFFjhrKZ80kZdA69UL-ersgeO-M8As)]
> 
> The vehicle stops twice, and I think the details are as below:
> - The vehicle stops at [0:02] first. It seems the pointclouds from the tree are filtered well, but after the vehicle is at below of the tree, the points are not filtered and it makes the vehicle stop.
> - After recovering from the first stop ([0:06]), another tree in front makes the vehicle stop. It seems the pointcloud is filtered well at first, but they are not filtered well as the vehicle gets closer to the tree.
> 
> I also checked the similar issue https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/6940 and I thought the issue  could be resolved for the latest release, but it seems the issue remains.
> 
> Here's more information for the reproduction:
> - Starting/Goal pose (from launch.log)
> ```
> initial pose - x: -71.782125, y: 88.019365, z: 0.069840
> initial orientation - qx: -0.000343, qy: 0.000011, qz: -0.001882, qw: 0.999998
> goal pose - x: -195.079193, y: 29.398745, z: 2.600000
> goal orientation - qx: 0.000000, qy: 0.000000, qz: -0.707009, qw: 0.707204
> ```
> - Map: Town05 [[Town05](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1y5dYpL6o3dp_nSo79ar-MMwDpvdcQOY8)]

> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope Autoware to ignore the irrelevant pointcloud.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> However, the irrelevant pointcloud is not filtered and makes the vehicle stop.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Pull image from `https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware/321564631?tag=universe-devel-cuda-0.39.1-amd64` and run Autoware with Carla, using [autoware_carla_interface](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/0.39.0/simulator/autoware_carla_interface).

> I failed to find why the ego vehicle could not recover from stopping, but I think the ego vehicle stops after the following steps:
> (The timestamp is for the video above)
> 1. [0:10] The NPC vehicle in front keep driving backward slowly, and the ego vehicle drives forward correspondingly.
> 2. [0:25] A large portion of the pointcloud of the NPC vehicle is filtered as below, for some reasons.

> 4. [0:30] The pointcloud of the NPC vehicle starts to be recovered and it makes the ego vehicle misunderstand the NPC is driving forward, even though the NPC is driving backward as before. (I could check that the NPC keeps driving backward at the video [here](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11UKF07Jpm1zGh6zb64bXOPjwpOPhJif/b2tnwTzdOCuyddSDbTxLSFleBlA_PBnC-PbYAhR5p7Qs).)

### #9755 — Add new messages to handle 2d ROI tracking information

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2024-12-24  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @YoshiRi
- **Labels:** type:improvement, status:stale
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/9755

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> 2D object tracking is common task and it may consistent in some scene compared to lidar/radar sensing.
> I want to add new message like `TrackedObjectsWithFeature` to handle 2D tracking information.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Current autoware can only handle 2D ROI information with `DetectedObjectsWithFeature` message and it  results in the shortage for handling tracking information such as uuid or existence probability. (See [bytetrack](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/perception/autoware_bytetrack/README.md) package for example. )
> 
> I think we need some alternative messages to handle 2D tracking message.
> 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> For shortly, I think copying `DetectedObjectWithFeature` will be easy to implement and handle. 
> 
> I suggest `TrackedObjectWithFeature` and `TrackedObjectsWithFeature`
> - `TrackedObjectWithFeature` 
> 
> ```
> autoware_perception_msgs/TrackedObject object
> Feature feature
> ```
> 
> - `TrackedObjectsWithFeature`
> 
> ```
> std_msgs/Header header
> TrackedObjectWithFeature[] feature_objects
> ```
> 
> 
> 
> c.f. TrackedObject includes minimum information like object_id and existence_probability.
> 
> ```
> unique_identifier_msgs/UUID object_id
> float32 existence_probability
> ObjectClassification[] classification
> TrackedObjectKinematics kinematics
> Shape shape
> ```
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Close when new message definition is available.

**Comments:**

###### @YoshiRi (2024-12-24)

> cc: @technolojin @yukkysaito 

###### @YoshiRi (2024-12-24)

### #9722 — Leverage cuda acceleration in the sensing perception pipeline

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-12-23  |  **Closed:** 2025-07-06  |  **Author:** @knzo25
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:perception, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/9722

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Background:
> We have long struggled with the latency in our sensing/perception pipeline. Even though we use very rudimentary algorithms, the latency is considerable enough that we can not opt to use more complex ones due to fear of increasing reaction times.
> In the same vein, autoware has proven to be too heavy for new sensors with higher data rates and we have had to resort to down sample approaches to bound the execution times, even though using the new sensors fully holds the potential to increase the overall performance of autoware.
>  
> Previous conversations:
>  - In the sensing / perception WG, the idea of acceleration and some PoCs were discussed. There was no opposition other than compatibility and granularity when possible.
>  - A similar feature request was mentioned in https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/5396
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Accelerate the sensing/perception pipeline via cuda-based acceleration
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
>  - Accelerate the pointcloud preprocessing pipeline
>  - Accelerate nodes that use the pointcloud in the perception pipeline
>  - Implement a transport layer for CUDA so that we can avoid host->device->host copies whenever possible
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> PRs that implement 
>  - acceleration of the sensing perception pipeline
>  - type adaptation and negotiation
> are merged to universe and/or autoware

**Comments:**

### #9719 — Replace Traffic light detection model

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2024-12-23  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @badai-nguyen
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:perception
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/9719

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> - Current Trafic Lights (TLs) fine detection model operates using cropped image obtatined via rough ROIs. It requires following input topics:
>   - `image_raw`
>   - `camera_info`
>   - `rough/rois`
>   - `expect/rois`
> - [traffic_light_recognition pipeline](https://app.diagrams.net/?lightbox=1#Uhttps%3A%2F%2Fautowarefoundation.github.io%2Fautoware-documentation%2Fmain%2Fdesign%2Fautoware-architecture%2Fnode-diagram%2Foverall-node-diagram-autoware-universe.drawio.svg#%7B%22pageId%22%3A%22T6t2FfeAp1iw48vGkmOz%22%7D) 
> ![traffic_light_recognition pipeline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf88939d-7d21-41e7-a6ac-e24573300b61)
> 
> - Limitations of the current approach
>   - The fine detection is executed only after `traffic_light_map_based_prediction` which causes unnecessry delays. 
>   - The fine detector relies only local image of TLs, lossing global feature such as vehicles, road related features which might increases false-positive result when some vehicle's lamps included in rough rois regions. 
>   - This significantly relies on [autoware_traffic_light_occlusion_predictor](https://github.com/badai-nguyen/autoware.universe/blob/f808124ca8f7b3370415577c2e6b49ebc3048279/perception/autoware_traffic_light_occlusion_predictor/README.md) which is high computation cost and cause heavy bandwith of raw pointcloud transfer. 
>   - It might be a challenge to intergrate with other open-source TL detection models such as YOLOX.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The task is open to update TLR pipeline to address the above limitations
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Replace the current fine detector model by TLs detector model like Yolox which takes whole images as input and reuse current `autoware_tensorrt_yolox` package for inference.
> - The interest TLs inside images which neccessrary for Planning module could be selected by a new node (`traffic_light_selector`)
> - Remove pointcloud based `autoware_traffic_light_occlusion_predictor` when DNN TLs detector can ignore occluded TLs. To keep the update as minimum, current classifier will be re-used and the result will be combined by a new simple traffic_signal_merger node.
> The new pipeline as figure below
> ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/497082f4-2830-4aec-b857-e50b768a7afb)
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Training and upload new TLs detector model
> - [x] Update autoware for new model downloads
> - [x] Implement `traffic_light_detector` in the `autoware_tensorrt_yolox` package
> - [x] Add executor for new TLs detector model
> - [x] Add `traffic_light_category_merger`
> - [x]  Add `traffic_light_selector`
> - [x] Update `tier4_perception_launcher` and `autoware_launch` for new pipeline
> - [x] Update autoware_documentation and perception diagram

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla, and found a situation that the vehicle stucks at uphill.
> Here's the rviz videos of the situation: [[rviz1](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11MppuIWhMYs4vTIVcWtT1Tu7rmbXa6g/AIatw9bqHVlhMJ41TZXd-RK2_TGoq2FI-Qr5g7pqd5ws)] [[rviz2](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11MrDaIG5NWRGGdRT4g6D7J8vgKpMXHV/XD7gU2T0ZLktvYv2XseR4P99IZ8gF1UE-qbQgeI2f5ws)]
> 
> - rviz1: This video shows a driving with default setting of [slope compensation](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/control/autoware_pid_longitudinal_controller/#slope-compensation_1), and it shows that the vehicle cannot go uphill.
> - rviz2: I tested the situation with [planning simulator](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/), and this also shows that the vehicle cannot go uphill either. I checked this because I thought this issue could be from bad localization at the uphill, but it seems not (at least for now).
> 
> Also, while running the simulation above, I cannot know why the shape of the drivable area is weird.
> ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef88e592-1ac2-4058-a12e-7e3f80b6a673)
> 
> Here's more information of the situation:
> - Starting/Goal point (from launch.log)
> ```
> initial pose - x: -74.346236, y: 17.611892, z: -0.062959
> initial orientation - qx: -0.004039, qy: 0.003657, qz: 0.707924, qw: 0.706268
> goal pose - x: -1.848311, y: 87.232613, z: 2.275307
> goal orientation - qx: 0.000000, qy: 0.000000, qz: -0.719365, qw: 0.694632
> ```
> - Map: Town03 [[Town03](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rt1pKEfY-hqC2pMrHfajg1EVfjlIcAX5)]
> - ros2bag file: [[ros2bag](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11MpdAmgOMq56Ig3PHN9dCxX9gevdxdh/Hf_X_lznGsAWgfwV2vXhV1xAnUtB6-Hy-obAg4DGj5ws)]
> - launch.log file: [[launch.log](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11MpodbfHdckKFblZgNZsu6Yqwx9FrCy/D3t_suCTMxSxZG6EVqV93U5JRj5Jrdzj-xrDAEzyj5ws)]
> 
> 
> Could anyone please check this?
> 
> Thanks!
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope the vehicle to drive uphill well, and reach to the goal point.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But the vehicle could not reach to the goal, as it stucks before the uphill.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Pull image from `https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware/321564631?tag=universe-devel-cuda-0.39.1-amd64` and run Autoware with Carla, using [autoware_carla_interface](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/0.39.0/simulator/autoware_carla_interface).
> 2. Run ros2bag file above.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (Docker), Ubuntu 20.04 (host)
> - Autoware: [0.39.1](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/tree/0.39.1)
> - Carla: 0.9.15
> - autoware_carla_interface: [link](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/0.39.0/simulator/autoware_carla_interface)
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> I guess this issue is from slope compensation, as the issue also occurs at hill, and is observed from the planning simulation too.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @maxime-clem (2024-12-18)

> It looks like the slope where ego stops is too sharp (~0.12 rad) for the default configuration (0.1).
> Please try increasing the parameter (e.g., to 0.2 since the map seems to contain slopes of up to 0.2 rad).
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/main/autoware_launch/config/control/trajectory_follower/longitudinal/pid.param.yaml#L80-L81

###### @Kim-mins (2024-12-30)

> Thank you for the response @maxime-clem!!
> 
> I tried the planning simulation with your suggested parameter, and I found that the vehicle completes the driving well! Thanks a lot!
> 
> By the way, would you mind sharing the idea for the weird shape of the drivable area in z-axis?
> In my opinion, the drivable area of uphill in the image above seems not being captured well.
> 
> Thank you!

### #9672 — False positive of Emergency Stop

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-12-17  |  **Closed:** 2025-01-07  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** simulator:carla
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/9672

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla, and found a situation that Autoware activates emergency stop, and makes the vehicle immobile, even though there's no reason for stopping.
> Here's the rviz video of the situation: [[rviz](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11MnuwkpGCtk4fXnUsIuC7Gh6Db2yJ0Q/adxKAkkN40RKVS0bjSo_Nijkfi8jlcj1-eL8AqsOT5ws)]
> 
> As the video shows, while turning left, emergency stop is activated, and the vehicle eventually stops.
> 
> Actually, I could not get any error message, so I checked the message from `/diagnostics`, and I could observe the message below many times at the end of the simulation.
> ```
> ...
> header:
>   stamp:
>     sec: 97
>     nanosec: 300001449
>   frame_id: ''
> status:
> - level: "\0"
>   name: 'autonomous_emergency_braking: aeb_emergency_stop'
>   message: '[AEB]: No Collision'
>   hardware_id: autonomous_emergency_braking
>   values: []
> ...
> ```
> which could be related to this issue.
> 
> Here's more information of the situation:
> - Starting/Goal pose (from launch.log)
> ```
> initial pose - x: -74.345708, y: 17.612380, z: -0.063144
> initial orientation - qx: -0.004035, qy: 0.003669, qz: 0.707917, qw: 0.706274
> goal pose - x: -60.503540, y: -187.431732, z: 2.275307
> goal orientation - qx: 0.000000, qy: 0.000000, qz: 0.952253, qw: 0.305310
> ```
> - Map: Town03 [[Town03](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rt1pKEfY-hqC2pMrHfajg1EVfjlIcAX5)]
> - ros2bag file: [[ros2bag](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11Mnv3u3tpN61z4sZnZeCVF9fO9rYc0p/bKWX_NEZKtEfNoqwAgxPlOBoU_OONXfP-jrpgDquX5ws)]
> - launch.log: [[launch.log]](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11Mo3OkCZqmfD2kTq2Yn2XLId6q42jMp/T2O84S2RG3dPptoRtaz9xgO4seJ3ia9t-prpgxrOX5ws)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope the vehicle to drive well to the goal point.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But the vehicle could not drive to the goal point.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Pull image from `https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware/321564631?tag=universe-devel-cuda-0.39.1-amd64` and run Autoware with Carla, using [autoware_carla_interface](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/0.39.0/simulator/autoware_carla_interface).
> 2. Run ros2bag file above.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (Docker), Ubuntu 20.04 (host)
> - Autoware: [0.39.1](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/tree/0.39.1)
> - Carla: 0.9.15
> - autoware_carla_interface: [link](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/0.39.0/simulator/autoware_carla_interface)
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @maxime-clem (2024-12-17)

> Using the [`rqt_diagnostic_graph_monitor`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_tools/tree/main/system/rqt_diagnostic_graph_monitor), I identified that the issue comes from the `/autoware/localization/scan_matching_status` diagnostic.
> If I understand correctly, localization fails to find a good match between the lidar pointcloud and the pointcloud map.
> 
> One workaround is to remove the corresponding diagnostic from the configuration of the `system_diagnostic_monitor` (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/0.39.0/autoware_launch/config/system/system_diagnostic_monitor/localization.yaml#L11).

###### @Kim-mins (2025-01-07)

> Thank you for the investigation @maxime-clem!
> 
> I tried your suggestion and the ego vehicle could drive well to the destination!
> 
> Thank you so much!

### #9666 — Cannot reach to the goal at the corner.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-12-17  |  **Closed:** 2024-12-19  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** simulator:carla
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/9666

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla, and found a situation that the vehicle cannot reach to the goal at the corner.
> Here's the rviz video of the situation: [[rviz](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11MdXFZTggpXLKJdckskEl4vED6Nkx1a/JZmtqSUkKlN3IvzS-CH_P605amnE-nJJ-wLgAvMdx5ws)]
> 
> As the video shows, the goal point is at the corner and the vehicle stops before reaching to the goal.
> 
> I partially checked the control command(from `/control/command/control_cmd`) published in last few seconds, and I could get the figure below: (x: # of published data, y: velocity/acceleration)
> ![velacc](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/856102aa-0a0e-4aa8-a165-d893beff3137)
> And it shows the velocity and the acceleration at the end of the driving is `0` and below `0`, respectively.
> 
> For better debugging, here's more information: 
> - About starting and end points (from launch.log):
> ```
> initial pose - x: 145.509345, y: -133.451777, z: 0.069356
> initial orientation - qx: -0.000332, qy: -0.000049, qz: -0.000555, qw: 1.000000
> goal pose - x: 342.991272, y: -2.307267, z: 2.000000
> goal orientation - qx: 0.000000, qy: 0.000000, qz: 0.147707, qw: 0.989031
> ```
> - Map: Town01 [[Town01](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1bZfKbq6H9dF1DveuW7iIJiJKN0-W5l03)]
> - ros2bag file: [[ros2bag](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11McxHAUk1nW2gZSlg1iOVdify9NxTpd/eFYq7DkZ8fG5zvLxbP506wdVTL3wlom6-tbsgGAFz5ws)] 
> - launch.log file: [[launch.log](https://salbox.synology.me/drive/d/s/11MdEAPpYToNVjW8ITurgocU5hXgVeiK/3IMk3tUggFrmV3QqtmyFIze4O0XPsTAr-3LtADAxz5ws)]
> 
> Could anyone please check this? Let me know if further investigation is needed.
> 
> Thanks!
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope the vehicle to reach to the goal point.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But the vehicle could not reach to the goal point, and stops before the goal.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Pull image from `https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware/321564631?tag=universe-devel-cuda-0.39.1-amd64` and run Autoware with Carla, using [autoware_carla_interface](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/0.39.0/simulator/autoware_carla_interface).
> 2. Run ros2bag file above.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (Docker), Ubuntu 20.04 (host)
> - Autoware: [0.39.1](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/tree/0.39.1)
> - Carla: 0.9.15
> - autoware_carla_interface: [link](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/0.39.0/simulator/autoware_carla_interface)
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @maxime-clem (2024-12-17)

> The emergency stop activates and causes the early stops.
> I am not sure what triggers the emergency stops, and I am not sure why the vehicle does not restart at the end.

###### @Kim-mins (2024-12-17)

> Thank you for the response @maxime-clem!
> 
> Actually, I have no idea for debugging. Could you please provide me some recommendations for better investigation?
> 
> Thanks!

###### @maxime-clem (2024-12-17)

> I found why the vehicle does not restart. It is because when ego last stops (because of the emergency stop), it is around 40cm away from the next trajectory stop points. In the parameters, it is defined that the longitudinal controller node transitions to the `STOPPED` state when within 49cm of the next stop point (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/main/autoware_launch/config/control/trajectory_follower/longitudinal/pid.param.yaml#L14C5-L14C29).

###### @Kim-mins (2024-12-17)

> Thank you for the investigation @maxime-clem!
> 
> I read your comment, and maybe I should shorten the `stopping_state_stop_dist` threshold value from  `0.49` to `0.40`(or less than `0.40`). Could you please check if I'm doing right?

###### @maxime-clem (2024-12-17)

> Reducing the value of this parameter would allow the ego vehicle to restart yes.
> But here the main issue is the emergency stop. I will investigate it and I suspect it is the same issue as https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/9672.

###### @Kim-mins (2024-12-17)

> Thank you for the response @maxime-clem!
> 
> I tested after shortening the distance, and the vehicle could move after the emergency stop. So the error seems gone after your suggested patch! Thanks!
> 
> For the emergency stop issue, I just checked your answer in #9672. Can I follow the workaround you suggested there?
> 
> Thanks a lot!

###### @maxime-clem (2024-12-17)

> > For the emergency stop issue, I just checked your answer in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/9672. Can I follow the workaround you suggested there?
> 
> Yes it looks to be the same issue.

### #9599 — NDT Scan matching takes too long to execute

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-12-09  |  **Closed:** 2024-12-10  |  **Author:** @shin-ka
- **Labels:** component:localization, component:planning
- **Comments:** 10  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/9599

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I am using the standalone NDT scan matcher package to localize in an indoor environment simulation. I am using a 16 channel lidar. The initial pose estimate is the same as the current groundtruth pose coming from the simulation and the robot is stationary. Upon configuring the param file and launch file and loading the offline map (again generated using 16 channel lidar), I am seeing that NDT is taking too long to execute, approximately ~5000 ms. This is the behaviour in the ideal scenario where the scans are already aligned and the predicted ndt_pose is actually same as my initial guess given.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I am expecting the scan alignment to work faster and not take 5 seconds.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> It is taking ~5000 ms to predict the ndt_pose.
> 
> Here the groundtruth pose is the red marker and initial guess is yellow marker. The current lidar scan is also shown.
> ![Screenshot from 2024-12-09 18-26-49](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fa377a5-5e89-41ec-af93-515069e4f001)
> 
> This is the result after NDT matching. Green marker is the estimated pose and purple points correspond to the loaded offline map.
> ![Screenshot from 2024-12-09 18-30-48](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/969f3d90-c1b7-4da1-b047-ab495e567b10)
> 
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. The global frame of reference in my project is 'odom'. The offline map has also been saved in the odom frame.
> 2. The config file that I am using :

### #9549 — Use `TrackedObjectKinematics` instead of `DetectedObjectKinematics` for `TrackedObject & object`

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-12-03  |  **Closed:** 2024-12-04  |  **Author:** @felixfeixu
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/9549

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In autoware, there are 2 kinds of ObjectKinematics definition, one is `TrackedObjectKinematics` and the other is `DetectedObjectKinematics`, they are equal to each other in integer value, but they should have difference namespaces.__
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> 1)
>  
> ```
> void MapBasedPredictionNode::updateObjectData(TrackedObject & object)
> {
>   std::unique_ptr<ScopedTimeTrack> st_ptr;
>   if (time_keeper_) st_ptr = std::make_unique<ScopedTimeTrack>(__func__, *time_keeper_);
> 
> 
>   if (
>     object.kinematics.orientation_availability ==
>     autoware_perception_msgs::msg::DetectedObjectKinematics::AVAILABLE) {
>     return;
>   }
> ```
> `DetectedObjectKinematics` is a wrong type, it should be `TrackedObjectKinematics` because of code type `TrackedObject & object`
> 
> 2)
> 
> for same reason,
> code
> ```
>  switch (object.kinematics.orientation_availability) {
>     case autoware_perception_msgs::msg::DetectedObjectKinematics::SIGN_UNKNOWN: {
> ```
> should also use `TrackedObjectKinematics`
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> `DetectedObjectKinematics` is used for `TrackedObject` type.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> check source code, code review.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> autoware, latest main branch
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @amadeuszsz (2024-12-03)

> @felixf4xu good catch & thank you for your report! Addressed in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/9553

---
