### #8645 — The implementation of ring_outlier_filter seems to have incorrect part

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-08-27  |  **Closed:** 2025-02-18  |  **Author:** @taisa1
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8645

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> There appears to be some issues of the implementation of ring_outlier_filter, so I listed them below.
> The target of this issue is [this code](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp).
> 
> ## 1. The last point in each ring seems to be not processed
> After exiting the for loop (starts from [line 126](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp#L126)), `walk_last_idx` is `indices.size() - 2`. So even if it loops over `[walk_first_idx, walk_last_idx]`, the last element will be ignored. 
> 
> ## 2. The same point can be pushed back to `outlier_pcl` multiple times
> In the for loop (starts from [line 185](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp#L185)), `input_ptr` is always same, because the index is always `walk_first_idx`. I think the index should be `i`.
> 
> ## 3. Incorrect type specification when copying point data
> According to [ring-outlier-filter.md](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/a64566ee7437075c75f30d128940dd4823e9d27a/sensing/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor/docs/ring-outlier-filter.md), input is in PointXYZIRCAEDT format, so `channel` should be `uint16_t`. However, when copying, it is read as `uint8_t`. Also, `intensity` should be `uint8_t`, but it is read as `float` in [line 226](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp#L226).
> 
> ## 4. Same process
> It's a matter of style, but I think the same processing can be unified.
> 
> Below is the psuedo code that shows the solution of problem 1 and 4.
> 
> before: 
> ```
> l=0, r=-1
> for i=0 to N-2 {
>     r=i
>     if is_same_walk(a[i], a[i+1]) then
>         continue
>     copy_points(a[l,r])
>     l=i+1
> }
> if l>r then 
>     continue
> copy_points(a[l,r])
> ```
> 
> after:
> ```
> l=0, r=-1
> for i=0 to N-1{
>     r=i
>     if i < N-1 then
>         if is_same_walk(a[i], a[i+1]) then
>             continue
>     copy_points(a[l,r])
>     l=i+1
> }
> ```
> 
> It will change the output topic and it may be difficult for me to test, so I posted this as a issue.
> Please let me know if the behavior is intended or if I've misunderstood something.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> None
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> None
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> None
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @badai-nguyen (2024-08-29)

> @mojomex As I mentioned internally, I really appreciate if you could follow up this issue as you did a major change in algorithm recently.

###### @mojomex (2024-09-02)

> Hi @taisa1, thank you for the issue.
> As for 1), you are absolutely correct. Actually, there is a performance improvement PR (that has been rolled back until dependent modules can deal with reordered points) that restructures this code (and should be correct):
> * #4185 
> * #6148 (reverted here)
> 
> Good catch for 2) and 3)!
> I will push a PR with a fix some time this week.
> 

###### @stale (2024-11-05)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @idorobotics (2025-02-18)

> > Hi [@taisa1](https://github.com/taisa1), thank you for the issue. As for 1), you are absolutely correct. Actually, there is a performance improvement PR (that has been rolled back until dependent modules can deal with reordered points) that restructures this code (and should be correct):
> > 
> >     * [perf(ring_outlier_filter): a cache friendly impl (continuation of VRichardJP's work) #4185](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4185)
> > 
> >     * [revert(perf_ring_outlier_filter): temporal revert for further investigation #6148](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6148) (reverted here)
> > 
> > 
> > Good catch for 2) and 3)! I will push a PR with a fix some time this week.
>

### #8590 — AEB module incorrectly calculates target obstacle's velocity at first calculation

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-08-22  |  **Closed:** 2024-09-26  |  **Author:** @ismetatabay
- **Labels:** component:control
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8590

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, in the default Autoware setup, point cloud data is used as obstacle information, and the nodes calculate the obstacle's velocity to use in the RSS formula. When obstacle points enter the predicted path, a miscalculation of the target object's velocity results in the RSS distance being calculated too high at the beggining. This situation triggers an emergency when the ego vehicle is overtaken by an NPC due to the excessively high calculated RSS distance.
> 
> - Calculated RSS distance for a constant velocity overtaking NPC
> 
> RSS Distance    |  Calculated Object Velocity for 5.55 m/s NPC  
> :-------------------------:|:-------------------------:
> <img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fce550de-11bf-4646-b68a-c038fc449a86" width="100%"/> |  <img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44b68dab-3cfd-4ede-aa19-53212a92a951" width="100%"/>
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Prevent unwanted emergency braking while driving in the city.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Extend the object tracking area to start calculating velocity before the object enters the predicted ego footprint area.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - Start calculating the speed of obstacles before they become the target obstacle.
> - If an object isnΓÇÖt in the predicted area, donΓÇÖt trigger an emergency.
> - Add a debug marker for the object search area.

### #8589 — After performance improvements of autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor voxel_based_compare_map_filter doesn't work

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-08-22  |  **Closed:** 2024-09-09  |  **Author:** @sebekx
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8589

>

> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In latest perf improvements of `autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor` [in this PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/8174) changed the way how tf are retrieved in `filter` class, which is used i.e. in  `voxel_based_compare_map_filter`. New improvements assumes that only static tf's are used, however in  `voxel_based_compare_map_filter` there is transformation from `base_link` to `map`.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> `voxel_based_compare_map_filter` filter pointcloud based on poincloud map. correctly transform input pointcloud to `map` frame and filter matching points and transform back to `base_link` 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> `voxel_based_compare_map_filter` after start correctly filter pointcloud but after vehicle moves old tf is used which cause filter to not match input pointcloud points with map points
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1 Start autoware
> 2. Enable  /perception/object_recognition/detection/pointcloud_map_filtered/pointcloud topic in rviz
> 3. Observe filtered points after vehicle moves
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> performance improvements of autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor [in this PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/8174) which retrieves tf only once which in case of `base_link` <-> `map` transform is incorrect 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #8539 — [Dense-Urban-ODD] Improve avoidance for parked NPCs

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-08-20  |  **Closed:** 2024-11-26  |  **Author:** @ahmeddesokyebrahim
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8539

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Part of:
> - #7485
> 
> ### Dense Urban ODD Characteristics
> - **Low-Speed Driving:** Typical speeds around 15 km/h.
> - **Complex Traffic Elements:** Includes dense traffic with various dynamic interactions.
> - **Dynamic Agents:** Frequent encounters with moving pedestrians and cyclists.
> - **Bidirectional Movement:** Vehicles operate in lanes supporting bidirectional flow.
> - **Traffic Rule Non-compliance:** Other road users may exhibit behaviors such as:
>   - Driving in the wrong direction.
>   - Cutting in unexpectedly from off-road areas.
>   - Jaywalking pedestrians.
>   - Improper overtaking by drivers.
>   - Inaccurate parking
>   
> In the context of Dense Urban ODD, we need to fine-tune the existing features of the `autoware_behavior_path_static_obstacle_avoidance_module` and potentially develop new features to better avoid parked and low speed NPC in dense urban areas.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> 
> #### Parked NPC in the same direction of ego "UC-NTR-002-0001" "1st iteration"
> The following image describes the scenario where
>  
> ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f36b239f-3b88-47fc-a3e8-f5b9fdc60ca2)
> 
> #### Parked NPCs in the same and opposite direction of ego "UC-NTR-002-0002"
> ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ee879bf-b85b-4b7f-ad56-2aa2b31aaffb)
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The `autoware_behavior_path_static_obstacle_avoidance_module`  should be capable of handling the situations mentioned above.
> - The primary goal will be to tune the parameters of the package to achieve the success of above scenarios.
> - If tuning the parameters is not enough for having successful scenarios, the `autoware_behavior_path_static_obstacle_avoidance_module` implementation should be improved.
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Create a proposal for changing parameters.
> - [ ] If the package is inadequate to handle scenarios, propose improvements.
> - [ ] Ensure all scenarios for Dense Urban ODD pass.

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
>

> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.

> 
> ### Description
> 
> If moving to side lanes by [behavior_path_external_request_lane_change_module](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/release/v1.0/planning/behavior_path_external_request_lane_change_module), the module doesn't work as expected.
> 
> 
> 1. Path planned with both left and right path candidate as expected
> ![1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91877b23-bbf5-4717-a5eb-3fd727d00727)
> 
> 
> 2. Ego triggered to change lane 
> ![2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/579f1609-3e1f-41f0-a8be-893f28f43760)
>

> 3. In middle of changing lane 
> ![3](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdb859d2-fbb0-4ed1-9a2b-d7d6ed52145d)

> ![4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b044595b-92e2-4e5b-9e27-fd2253b37596)

> change lane freely with [behavior_path_external_request_lane_change_module](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/release/v1.0/planning/behavior_path_external_request_lane_change_module)

> Autoware release/v1.0

> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2024-08-19)

> @Joonki0111 
> 
> Thank you so much for the report.
> Is the goal in the middle lane?
> 
> The unlike normal LC, external request LC typically searches for non-preferred lane to use as target. If the goal is in the middle lane, it will become preferred lane, hence external request LC will not to be able to find its  target lane.

###### @Joonki0111 (2024-08-19)

> @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 Thanks for the reply. I found the answer couple of hours ago which is same as your reply. I'm now currently working on modifying the /planning/mission_planning/route topic when external request LC is processed to change lane in any situation. Glad to hear it's not a bug.

### #8511 — Update bag files due to message type and PointCloud layout changes in Autoware Universe

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-08-16  |  **Closed:** 2024-09-18  |  **Author:** @batuhanbeytekin
- **Labels:** type:improvement
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8511

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> While running the reaction analyzer tool within Autoware Universe, I encountered errors due to changes in message types and PointCloud layout. The current bag files and PointCloud layout need to be updated to be compatible with the new message types in Autoware.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The reaction analyzer tool should execute without errors, correctly processing the updated message types and PointCloud layout used in the current version of Autoware Universe.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The tool fails due to incompatible message types and PointCloud layout in the existing bag files, resulting in runtime errors.
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2024-08-16 16-45-35](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e4d1178-632e-428c-a399-e0ee7eb14f1e)
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Download the demonstration test map from the link [here](https://github.com/tier4/AWSIM/releases/download/v1.1.0/nishishinjuku_autoware_map.zip). After downloading, extract the zip file and use its path as [MAP_PATH] in the following commands.
> 
> 2. - Download the rosbag files from the Google Drive link [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-Qcv7gYfR-usKOjUH8I997w8I4NMhXlX/view?usp=sharing).
> 
>     - Extract the zip file and set the path of the .db3 files to parameters path_bag_without_object and path_bag_with_object.
>     - You can start to test with the following command:
> `ros2 launch reaction_analyzer reaction_analyzer.launch.xml running_mode:=perception_planning vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=awsim_labs_sensor_kit map_path:=[MAP_PATH]`
> 
> 3. Observe the errors related to message type and PointCloud layout incompatibility.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> ROS 2: Humble
> Autoware: Latest version
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The bag files and PointCloud layout were recorded using previous versions of Autoware, where the message types and layout were different. Recent changes in message definitions and PointCloud structure within Autoware Universe are causing the incompatibility.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> Updating the bag files and PointCloud layout to align with the current message types and structure in Autoware Universe should resolve the issue.

### #8458 — bug(crosswalk): findEgoPassageDirectionAlongPath does not calculate direction always right

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-08-13  |  **Closed:** 2024-08-23  |  **Author:** @mehmetdogru
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8458

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> [findEgoPassageDirectionAlongPath](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/bbc85252a5ebf6ea9cd901b536f051c5bd57cff2/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/autoware_behavior_velocity_crosswalk_module/src/scene_crosswalk.cpp#L595-L625) function does not calculate direction always right when **no path point intersects with crosswalk lanelet polygon**.
> 
> 1) If condition above is met, `idx1 = idx2` so front and back points are not assigned right resulting wrong direction value.
> 2) [findObjectPassageDirectionAlongVehicleLane](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/bbc85252a5ebf6ea9cd901b536f051c5bd57cff2/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/autoware_behavior_velocity_crosswalk_module/src/scene_crosswalk.cpp#L627-L659) function returns the direction value using object predicted path.
> 3) If condition above is met the values from these two functions have almost 180 degree difference even though bicycle and ego moves to the same direction and ego stops for crosswalk.
> 
> ![Untitled Diagram (1)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1880d1ed-e5ff-4255-9d41-76b68d319ede)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Front and back points should be assigned right in any condition
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Front and back points are not assigned right in every condition
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1) Set a gol on a lanelet where there is a crosswalk on the way
> 2) Visualize [sparse_resample_path](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/bbc85252a5ebf6ea9cd901b536f051c5bd57cff2/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/autoware_behavior_velocity_crosswalk_module/src/scene_crosswalk.cpp#L324) and make sure no path point collides with crosswalk lanelet polygon
> 3) Create a bicycle goes the same direction as ego and observe crosswalk virtual wall
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #8437 — Obstacle stop planner node doesn't start when running in a component container

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-08-12  |  **Closed:** 2024-09-04  |  **Author:** @mbharatheesha
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8437

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When the obstacle stop planner node is started using a component container, only the component container is shown as running but the actual functionality of the obstacle stop planner node is unavailable.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The obstacle stop planner node gets loaded as a composable node plugin into a component container and is listed when `ros2 node list` is run and the expected features of the obstacle stop planner node such as slowing down and stopping behaviors are triggered based on input trajectory and obstacle data (from a lidar pipeline for example).
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Only the component container starts, but the node doesn't get listed when `ros2 node list` is done. Further, the expected output topics of the obstacle stop planner, `~output/trajectory` and `~output/stop_reasons` are not published and the desired functionality of slow down (if enabled) and stopping aren't available.
> 
> What is also difficult to explain is that, a linux process corresponding to starting the node does start and can be found by running a command such as `ps aux | grep <name_of_obstacle_stop_planner_node_in_launch_file>`. Further, the launch file as shown in the example below doesn't report any errors upon launch.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Create a composable node launch file in a ros2 package as follows (Ex: `my_pkg/launch/obstacle_stop_planner_composable.launch.xml`):
> ```
> <launch> 
>   <node_container pkg="rclcpp_components" exec="component_container" name="obstacle_stop_planner_container" namespace="" >
>         <composable_node pkg="autoware_obstacle_stop_planner" plugin="motion_planning::ObstacleStopPlannerNode" name="obstacle_stop_planner" namespace="" >
>             <!-- We need to disable object related velocities for the cruise control here -->
>             <param from="$(find-pkg-share autoware_obstacle_stop_planner)/config/common.param.yaml"/>
>             <param from="$(find-pkg-share autoware_obstacle_stop_planner)/config/adaptive_cruise_control.param.yaml" />
>             <param from="$(find-pkg-share autoware_obstacle_stop_planner)/config/obstacle_stop_planner.param.yaml" />
>             <param from="$(find-pkg-share autoware_vehicle_info_utils)/config/vehicle_info.param.yaml" />
>             <remap from="~/input/trajectory" to="/input/trajectory"/>
>             <remap from="~/output/trajectory" to="/planning/scenario_planning/trajectory"/>
>             <remap from="~/output/max_velocity" to="/planning/scenario_planning/max_velocity_candidates"/>
>             <remap from="~/output/velocity_limit_clear_command" to="/planning/scenario_planning/clear_velocity_limit"/>
>             <remap from="~/input/pointcloud" to="/obstacle/clusters"/>
>             <remap from="~/input/odometry" to="/odom"/>
>             <remap from="~/input/objects" to="/perception/object_recognition/objects"/>
>             <remap from="~/output/stop_reason" to="/planning/scenario_planning/status/stop_reason"/>
>             <remap from="~/output/stop_reasons" to="/planning/scenario_planning/status/stop_reasons"/>
>         </composable_node>
>     </node_container>
> </launch>
> ```
> 2. `ros2 launch <my_pkg> obstacle_stop_planner_composable.launch.xml`
> 3. `ros2 node list` - Only lists `obstacle_stop_planner_container`, but not `obstacle_stop_planner`.
> 4. `ps aux | grep obstacle_stop` will return a hit for a process that gets created upon launch, but it seemingly isn't doing anything as expected.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu Jammy 22.04 LTS
> - ROS2: Iron/Jazzy
> - Autoware: Latest version of `autoware_obstacle_stop_planner` on `main` branch of `autoware.universe`
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The likely cause is that the composable node plugin is not registered correctly in the `CMakeLists.txt` [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/13ac473947a282293196a984a40e911e5c935137/planning/autoware_obstacle_stop_planner/CMakeLists.txt#L28).
> 
> In the source file for the node, [the node component is exported](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/13ac473947a282293196a984a40e911e5c935137/planning/autoware_obstacle_stop_planner/src/node.cpp#L1607) as `autoware::motion_planning::ObstacleStopPlannerNode`, while in `CMakeLists.txt`, it is registered as `motion_planning::ObstacleStopPlannerNode`, _without_ `autoware::` scoping.
> 
> I did a source checkout and changed the registration in `CMakeLists.txt` to include `autoware::` scoping and then tested the composable node from the same launch file as mentioned above. Everything works as expected, i.e.,
> - The node is listed when `ros2 node list` is run
> - The expected output topics are published
> - And the expected markers such as the obstacle stop and obstacle slow down can be visualized in RViz when obstacles are on the desired trajectory of the vehicle.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

---

> We want visualizer to show every traffic light detection results.
> That would be something like:
> 
> ```
> ΓùÅ: 100%
> ΓåÉ : 100%
> Γåæ: 100%
> ```
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> We want to distinguish detection error and visualization error.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> First of all, all of the detection results should be visualized.
> The easiest solution is to concatenate visualization text with vertically or horizontally.
> 
> ```
> ΓùÅ: 100%
> ΓåÉ : 100%
> Γåæ: 100%
> ```
> 
> ```
> ΓùÅ, ΓåÉ, Γåæ
> 100, 100, 100
> ```
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> 
> When we confirmed all of the detection results should be visualized.
> 
> Currently TIER IV has the sample data. [TIER IV INTERNAL DATA LINK](https://star4.slack.com/archives/C076ZGRC15X/p1722936498548229?thread_ts=1722932121.436609&cid=C076ZGRC15X), if there are someone interested in this issue, we will annonimise and share this rosbag.

> Few things to note:
> - Due to the duplicate lanes drawn on top of each other (which I assume are to allow two way movement), It was difficult to run the simulations smoothley using the provided lanelet map, in many cases the mission planner fails to find a route.
> - In current Autoware configurations, costmap_generator has buffer size of 1.0 m around object polygons, and freespace_planner has a safety margin of 0.5 m added to ago vehicle shape for collision detection, so free space path planning requires at least 1.5 m between ego and detected objects. In the layout of the provided map the spacing between the parking slots is not sufficient to satisfy these settings when trying to park next to a vehicle.

### #8311 — [Dense-Urban-ODD] Improve cruise planner handling to a VRU maneuver overlapping with ego vehicle trajectory

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-08-01  |  **Closed:** 2024-09-30  |  **Author:** @ahmeddesokyebrahim
- **Labels:** type:improvement, component:planning
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8311

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Part of:
> - #7485
> ### Dense Urban ODD Characteristics
> - **Low-Speed Driving:** Typical speeds around 15 km/h.
> - **Complex Traffic Elements:** Includes dense traffic with various dynamic interactions.
> - **Dynamic Agents:** Frequent encounters with moving pedestrians and cyclists.
> - **Bidirectional Movement:** Vehicles operate in lanes supporting bidirectional flow.
> - **Traffic Rule Non-compliance:** Other road users may exhibit behaviors such as:
>   - Driving in the wrong direction.
>   - Cutting in unexpectedly from off-road areas.
>   - Jaywalking pedestrians.
>   - Improper overtaking by drivers.
>   - Dangerous and sudden maneuvers by VRUs that is overlapping with ego vehicle trajectory
>   
> In the context of Dense Urban ODD, we need to fine-tune the existing features of the `obstacle_cruise_planner` and potentially develop new features to achieve the characteristics mentioned above.
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> #### Bicycle driving through ego vehicle trajectory "UC-VRU-002-0002"
> The following image describes the scenario where
> - a bicycle is on the ego lane side (right or left)
> - while ego vehicle is approaching, the bicylce start to move in a way overlapping with ego trajectory.
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/36835765/05390394-a436-4acc-b99b-3b76810e6126)
> 
> The purpose of improvement in the following cases is to slow-down for overtaking bicycle until enough space exists to overtake
> 
> ##### Bicycle moving from right side of ego lane
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/36835765/b913905d-eacb-45dc-87d0-1d6effd8d960
>

### #8219 — lidar_centerpoint does not compile with CUDA 12.5

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-07-26  |  **Closed:** 2024-08-03  |  **Author:** @PPeltzerFka
- **Labels:** component:perception
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8219

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Building Universe fails for me when following the [Source installation](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/installation/autoware/source-installation/) guide, with running the `./setup-dev-env.sh` on Ubuntu 22, installing the latest Cuda 12.5 (released in May). When trying to build Autoware Universe, the compilation fails for lidar_centerpoint, pointing to missing declaration for the `__syncthreads()` function and more.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Following the tutorial, compilation is expected to be successful.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The compilation fails for lidar_centerpoint. Unfortunately, I only have a part of the error message right now as I dont have the time capacity to reinstall CUDA 12.5 again. This one was originating from test_preprocess_kernel.cpp :
> 
> ```
> /usr/local/cuda/include/cub/util_ptx.cuh:271:5: error: ΓÇÿ__syncthreadsΓÇÖ was not declared in this scope
>   271 |     __syncthreads();
> ```
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Run ./setup-dev-env.sh
> 2. Validate you're running CUDA 12.5 (`nvcc --version`)
> 3. Build autoware universe, or only up to lidar_centerpoint: `colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release --packages-up-to autoware_lidar_centerpoint`
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22
> - ROS 2: Humble
> - Autoware: Initially tried with 2024.06 tag, but issue appears to be still there in latest Universe main commit
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Google spits out the following threads related to this:
> 
> - [Unable to include thrust/host_vector.h and others with CUDA 12.5](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78784236/unable-to-include-thrust-host-vector-h-and-others-with-cuda-12-5)
> - [When upgrade from CUDA12.4 to 12.5 the compilation became broken](https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/when-upgrade-from-cuda12-4-to-12-5-the-compilation-became-broken/295814)
> 
> 
> There appears to be an API change in the thrust library released in CUDA 12.5, no longer allowing the inclusion of certain (?) headers in the .cpp/.hpp files instead of .cu files (judging from the linked topics).
> 
> lidar_centerpoint includes thrust libraries in a couple of files:
> 
> test_preprocess_kernel.cpp
> ```
> #include <thrust/host_vector.h>
> #include <thrust/reduce.h>
> ```
> 
> circle_nms_kernel.hpp
> ```
> #include <thrust/device_vector.h>
> ```
> 
> postprocess_kernel.hpp
> ```
> #include <thrust/device_vector.h>
> ```
> 
> test_preprocess_kernel.cpp
> ```
> #include <thrust/host_vector.h>
> #include <thrust/reduce.h>
> ```
> 
> Note that the lidar_transfusion package has the same include pattern, so the issue is probably present there as well.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> When removing CUDA 12.5 and installing CUDA 12.4, compilation is successful.

**Comments:**

###### @amadeuszsz (2024-07-29)

> Hi @PPeltzerFka, thank you for your detailed report.
> 
> Currently Autoware is developed with [CUDA 12.3](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/ede026d9dd799b5372fd20cb4d916950e1a49cb9/amd64.env#L4).  I can reproduce your issue and seems CUDA 12.5 came with API breaking changes. For the time being, could you use CUDA 12.3 / 12.4?  Also here is another [link](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cccl/issues/1373) which cover this issue.
> 
> EDIT:
> Workaround will be setting appropriate device system before affected header e.g.
> ```cpp
> #define THRUST_DEVICE_SYSTEM THRUST_DEVICE_SYSTEM_CPP
> ```
> I didn't test it yet but I guess it will bring performance drawbacks. I think we can just use headers in our CUDA library target directly. Could you please test [this](https://github.com/amadeuszsz/autoware.universe/tree/fix/centerpoint-thrust-device-system) branch if it solves your issue?

###### @amadeuszsz (2024-07-31)

> Hi @PPeltzerFka 
> We made a fix PRs. I will appreciate if you could let us know later you can build and run Autoware successfully on your machine ≡ƒÖç≡ƒÅ╗ΓÇìΓÖé∩╕Å

### #8128 — Reduce dependence on Boost.Geometry

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2024-07-22  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @mitukou1109
- **Labels:** type:improvement, status:stale
- **Comments:** 15  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8128

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, Autoware relies on Boost.Geometry for most geometric calculations. However, Boost's generic implementation is considered to extend the build time.
> The goal of this task is to reduce the build time by minimizing (or eliminating) dependency on Boost.Geometry.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> This task aims to shorten the build time by reducing dependency on Boost.Geometry. This involves adding utility functions that compile independently of Boost and omitting unnecessary features for Autoware to improve function execution efficiency.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The following functions are planned to be replaced:
> - [ ] `area()` @mitukou1109 
> - [ ] `convex_hull()` @mitukou1109 
> - [ ] `covered_by()` @mitukou1109 
> - [ ] `disjoint()` @mitukou1109 
> - [ ] `distance()` @mitukou1109 
> - [ ] `intersects()` @mitukou1109 
> - [ ] `within()` @mitukou1109 
> - [ ] `difference()` @mraditya01 
> - [ ] `union_()` @mraditya01 
> - [ ] `envelope()` @mitukou1109 
> - [ ] `simplify()` @mitukou1109 
> - [ ] `buffer()` @mitukou1109
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] All replaceable Boost.Geometry functions are migrated to self-implementations.
> - [ ] Build and processing time are reduced compared to Boost.Geometry.

**Comments:**

###### @mitukou1109 (2024-07-22)

> Here are the current benchmark results with 500 randomly generated polygons with 9 vertices:
> 
> |function|Boost|self-impl.|task|
> |----|----|----|----|
> |`area()`|0.18ms|0.65ms|calculate the area of 500 polygons|
> |`convex_hull()`|1.93ms|4.59ms|calculate the convex hull of vertices of 500 polygons|
> |`covered_by()`|278.20ms|946.09ms|check if each vertex of 500 polygons is covered by (= inside or on border of) another 500 polygons|
> |`disjoint()`|195.58ms|180.81ms|check if 500 polygons are disjoint (runs totally 250,000 times)|
> |`intersects()`|195.41ms|145.11ms|check if 500 polygons intersect (runs totally 250,000 times)|
> |`within()`|842.81ms|120.63ms|check if each of 500 polygons is within 500 polygons|
> 
> I will need to work on speeding up (especially for `convex_hull()` and `covered_by()`) before starting migration.

###### @mitukou1109 (2024-07-29)

> Latest benchmark results with 500 randomly generated polygons with 9 vertices:
> 
> |function|Boost|self-impl.|task|
> |----|----|----|----|
> |`area()`|0.03ms|0.03ms|calculate the area of 500 polygons|
> |`convex_hull()`|0.38ms|0.32ms|calculate the convex hull of vertices of 500 polygons|
> |`covered_by()`|309.93ms|307.29ms|check if each vertex of 500 polygons is covered by (= inside or on border of) another 500 polygons|
> |`disjoint()`|198.91ms|77.51ms|check if 500 polygons are disjoint (runs totally 250,000 times)|
> |`intersects()`|199.10ms|58.56ms|check if 500 polygons intersect (runs totally 250,000 times)|
> |`touches()`|309.29ms|343.14ms|check if each vertex of 500 polygons touches (= on border of) another 500 polygons|
> |`within()`|1058.86ms|55.80ms|check if each of 500 polygons is within 500 polygons|
> 
> Now all functions except `touches()` work equally or faster than Boost's.

###### @mitukou1109 (2024-08-02)

> At this moment, the implementation assumes that polygons are convex.
> But considering that the purpose is to replace Boost.Geometry functions, it would be better for the alternatives to work with concave polygons.
> Is it OK to keep the current implementation or should I use convexity-independent algorithms?

###### @maxime-clem (2024-08-21)

> @mraditya01 is implementing a triangulation algorithm which allows to split any concave polygon into a set of convex polygons (triangles). This will allow using convex-only algorithms with any type of polygons. Of course the effect on performance will need to properly be investigated, and in some case it may be better to implement generic algorithms rather than use triangulation+convex algorithms.

###### @mitukou1109 (2024-09-06)

> Now that @mraditya01 's https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/8609 is merged, I'll begin working on supporting non-convex polygons. But first let me re-implement the triangulation algorithm without using Boost.Geometry.

###### @mitukou1109 (2024-09-06)

> I asked @mraditya01 to clean up the code of triangulation algorithm first. I'm working on adding `alt::Polygon2d` class that accepts non-convex polygons.

###### @mitukou1109 (2024-09-10)

> I added `alt::Polygon2d` class and modified some functions to support non-convex polygons. After @mraditya01 finishes refactoring I will make the existing geometry functions accept `Polygon2d` by triangulation.

###### @mitukou1109 (2024-09-27)

> #8965 enabled the triangulation function to be used with `alt::Polygon2d`. I'm now adding overloads of geometry functions to support concave polygons.

###### @mitukou1109 (2024-10-25)

> I finished working on #8974, but it cannot be merged since it is not  fully tested yet.
> Currently, the concave polygon generator for random test occasionally creates a polygon with self-intersections, which my implementation does not expect.
> It will be fixed by #8995, and after the PR is merged, I will confirm every function works with random non-convex polygons. I've already added equivalence class and boundary value test cases and they are passing.
> 
> By #7778, #8592 and #8974, the following classes will be added:
> 
> |Class|Geometry types|Notes|
> |---|---|---|
> |`alt::Vector2d`|vector|
> |`alt::Point2d`|point|equivalent to `alt::Vector2d`|
> |`alt::Points2d`|point set|equivalent to `std::vector<alt::Point2d>`|
> |`alt::PointList2d`|ring, line|equivalent to `std::list<alt::Point2d>`|
> |`alt::Polygon2d`|polygon|mutually convertible with `autoware::universe_utils::Polygon2d`|
> |`alt::ConvexPolygon2d`|convex polygon|subclass of `alt::Polygon2d`|
> 
> Note:
> - Polygons have closing points (i.e. the last vertex in the list should match the first, as any polygon given is considered to be closed)
> - Polygons can only be created by calling `alt::Polygon2d::create()`, and convex polygons by `alt::ConvexPolygon2d::create()`.
>   They are `correct()`-ed internally, and their convexity is checked as needed.
> 
> In addition, the following functions will be available without dependence on Boost.Geometry:
> 
> |Function|Supported geometry types|Non-convex support|
> |---|---|:---:|
> |`area()`|ring / polygon|o|
> |`convex_hull()`|point set|-|
> |`correct()`|polygon|o|
> |`covered_by()`|point & ring / point polygon|o|
> |`disjoint()`|polygon & polygon|o|
> |`distance()`|point & segment (2 edge points) / point & polygon|o|
> |`envelope()`|polygon|o|
> |`equals()`|point & point / polygon & polygon|o|
> |`intersects()`|segment & segment / polygon & polygon|o|
> |`simplify()`|line|-|
> |`touches()`|point & segment / point & polygon|o|
> |`within()`|point & ring / point & polygon / polygon & polygon|o|
> 
> Note:
> - **All functions supporting non-convex polygons cannot be used for self-intersecting polygons.** Some may work but possibly cause unintended behavior.

###### @mitukou1109 (2024-10-25)

> Below are not implemented yet:
> - `difference()` (@mraditya01)
> - `intersection()` (@mraditya01 ?)
> - `union_()` (@mraditya01)
> - `buffer()` (@mitukou1109 -> @mraditya01 ?)

###### @stale (2025-02-02)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @mraditya01 (2025-02-03)

> Merged Polygon Clipping implementation [#8728 ](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/8728) with benchmark as below.
> 
> | Vertices | Operation     | Custom (ms) | Boost::geometry (ms) | Matching Polygon | Different Polygon |
> |----------|-------------|-------------|----------------------|------------------|------------------|
> | 5        | Union       | 753.72      | 1471.03              | 249500           | 0                |
> | 5        | Intersection | 385.73      | 1170.93              | 249500           | 0                |
> | 7        | Union       | 1071.70     | 1867.30              | 249500           | 0                |
> | 7        | Intersection | 618.66      | 1456.06              | 249500           | 0                |
> | 9        | Union       | 1443.39     | 2295.15              | 249500           | 0                |
> | 9        | Intersection | 831.60      | 1806.78              | 249500           | 0                |
> 
> - The function will replace `boost::union_`, `boost::intersection`, `boost::difference`.
> - Additionally, verified results to be equally match with Shapely using an epsilon of 1e-6.
> - Work with both convex and concave polygon, but not self-intersecting polygon.

> If you are able to reproduce the issue, could you try to catch it with gdb? You just need to recompile with `-CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` and add `launch-prefix='gnome-terminal -- gdb -ex=r --args'` at the end of `<node_container ...>` in the `behavior_planning.launch.xml`. ### #8114 — Test Autoware.Universe Modules in a University Campus Environment

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2024-07-19  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @ismetatabay
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:perception, component:localization, component:planning
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8114

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> To observe the current capabilities of Autoware, we plan to test it in real-world conditions using the [Yildiz Technical University](https://yildiz.edu.tr/en) Campus environment and the Leo Drive's Autonomous Robo-Taxi vehicle.
> 
> ### Yildiz Technical University (YTU) Campus Environment
> 
> Y─▒ld─▒z Technical University (YTU) is located in Istanbul, Turkey, and encompasses multiple campuses. One of these campuses is the [Davutpa┼ƒa Campus](https://earth.google.com/web/search/%c3%87ifte+Havuzlar,+YT%c3%9c-Davutpa%c5%9fa+Kamp%c3%bcs%c3%bc,+Esenler%2f%c4%b0stanbul/@41.02440194,28.8919709,71.99656676a,786.37532144d,35y,343.96893324h,44.97811094t,0r/data=CqgBGn4SeAolMHgxNGNhYmFlNGY4OTk3MmE3OjB4MzY4N2NmY2QxM2MwZjBmNxm8QQ8QJ4NEQCE-5C1XP-Q8QCo9w4dpZnRlIEhhdnV6bGFyLCBZVMOcLURhdnV0cGHFn2EgS2FtcMO8c8O8LCBFc2VubGVyL8Swc3RhbmJ1bBgCIAEiJgokCddkbt8xhkRAEa6i6Ji7gkRAGUgxJMMY6TxAIW9pdpYr3zxAOgMKATA), where we operate autonomous vehicles.
> 
> <p align="center">
>   <img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0bda813-a6db-4d79-b881-6c803d8f4297" />
> </p>
> 
>  Here is some general information about the YTU Davutpa┼ƒa Campus:
> 
> **1. Slopes and Terrains**
> The YTU Davutpa┼ƒa Campus has a varied topography. Some areas are flat, while others have gentle or steep slopes. These features can pose significant challenges for perception, planning, and control modules.
> **2. Greenery and Trees**
> The YTU Davutpa┼ƒa Campus is typically landscaped with various plants and trees, providing aesthetic appeal, shade, and contributing to the overall environment. These plants and trees can be beneficial for testing perception and planning behaviors.
> **3. Building structures**
> The Davutpa┼ƒa Campus features a diverse range of buildings, varying in size from small-scale structures to larger ones. These buildings are suitable for localization using LiDAR-based methods (NDT).
> 
> ---
> 
> **Map Files:** [PCD and Lanelet2 map Link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1t8wUqqWeFRJHs4N12d0RL9N1Ai8oi3MW?usp=drive_link)
> 
> ---
> 
> ### Leo Drive's Autonomous Test Vehicle
> 
> To perform autonomous driving tests in the YTU Campus Environment, the Leo Drive Robo-Taxi vehicle will be used during these tests.
> <p align="center">
>   <img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be89a75d-bcfe-4388-be7b-d880f81eaabb" />
> </p>
> 
> This vehicle includes six LiDAR sensors and one GNSS/INS device for autonomous driving stacks. The internal IMU of the GNSS/INS device is used as the IMU sensor.
> 
> The LiDAR sensors consist of:
> - **1x** Velodyne VLS-128
> - **4x** Velodyne VLP-16
> - **1x** Robosense Bpearl
> 
> The eight Lucid Vision cameras are used for camera-LiDAR fusion in the perception pipeline, and the SBG Ellipse D is utilized as the GNSS/INS device for the sensing and localization pipeline.
> 
> #### ECU of Test Vehicle
> 
> The ECU specs of our test vehicle are as follows:
> 
> Complement | Product
> --- | --- 
> CPU | AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3975WX 32-core, 64-thread 
> Memory | 256 GB RAM
> GPU | 3x NVIDIA RTX A4000 (TensorRT YOLOX doesn't support multi-GPU usage, we plan to add it.)
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The main purpose of this task is to observe and assess Autoware's capabilities in real-life usage and address issues identified during tests. As mentioned above, the YTU test environment provides challenging conditions for autonomous driving vehicles, such as trees, slopes, and bumpy and rough road conditions.
> 
> <p align="center">
>   <img src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16fe861f-74bb-4ad7-9ed8-2244f4aac4f6" />
> </p>
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Integrate Autoware into the test vehicles
> - Perform autonomous driving and collect data
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Perform autonomous emergency braking (AEB) tests and create a report 
>   - [Test Results of the Autonomous Emergency Braking (AEB) Module in Real Life](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/5020)
> - [ ] Perform intersection module tests in roundabouts and create a report
> - [ ] Perform autonomous driving on roads with trees (using obstacle_cruise_planner as the motion planner)
> - [ ] TBA
> - [ ] ...

### #8073 — Adjust the predicted path of the object to follow the direction of traffic flow in bi-directional lanes

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-07-17  |  **Closed:** 2024-09-09  |  **Author:** @beyzanurkaya
- **Labels:** component:perception, component:planning
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8073

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Part of 
> 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/7689
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The `map_based_prediction` package creates a straight predicted path if the object is moving in the opposite direction, and a predicted path on the centerline if it is moving in the same direction. Although this approach works in single-direction lanes, it causes some problems in bi-directional lanes. While EGO moves on the lane, an accurately predicted path must be created to ensure that an object coming from the opposite direction can continue driving safely.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> It should be determined that the lane on which the object is located is bi-directional, and a predicted path should be created on which side of the lane the object is currently on - according to the traffic flow - and not on the centerline.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] It will be determined that the lane is bi-directional and in which direction the object is moving.
> - [ ] According to the traffic flow, a predicted path will be created so that the object stays on that side of the lane.

### #8069 — Localization issue while driving uphill

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-07-17  |  **Closed:** 2024-07-22  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** component:localization, simulator:carla
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/8069

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla using [bridge implementation](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6859#issuecomment-2196138040), and I found a situation that the localization gets bad while driving uphill, and it eventually makes the ego vehicle stop.
> 
> Here's the rviz video and `launch.log` file: [[video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vz-Dd7rFJtIqiZESJqlk2kCGF2F2220q/view?usp=sharing)] [[launch.log](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_UbGENr7QTZ3DNX5F7yk_5hZ08FSUPi2/view?usp=sharing)]
> 
> At the start of the video, the poincloud matches with the given .pcd file, but it gets worse as the vehicle goes up, and the vehicle eventually stops and could not reach to the goal point.
> Also, the trace(skyblue line) in rviz shows that there are oscillation on the baselink.
> 
> And according to the log file, there are logs that saying`NVTL` gets worse.
> ```
> ...
> 1721137556.6314461 [ndt_scan_matcher_node-42] [WARN] [1721137556.630878637] [localization.pose_estimator.ndt_scan_matcher]: Score is below the threshold. Score: 2.23286, Threshold: 2.3
> ...
> 1721137561.2945189 [ndt_scan_matcher_node-42] [WARN] [1721137561.293876881] [localization.pose_estimator.ndt_scan_matcher]: Score is below the threshold. Score: 1.28923, Threshold: 2.3
> ...
> ```
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope the ego vehicle to drive to the destination well.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But it could not reach to the given goal point.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Here's the ros2bag file for the reproduction: [[ros2bag](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mAuC3-OLcD-dB2ktzT56bACCm5ZNjsw0?usp=sharing)]
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - autoware.universe: [7877192cb5700c1db15109dcd959785fc381951d](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/7877192cb5700c1db15109dcd959785fc381951d)
> - Carla: 0.9.15
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @KYabuuchi (2024-07-17)

> I checked your rosbag in my environment. I found your point cloud map is missing some buildings, which seems to be causing the scan matching to not work correctly.
> 
> <img src=https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6b2d44a-dd76-44e7-8a90-f58adb4660f9 width=500>
> <img src=https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ddee0bd-fee3-4b49-b43f-56bc155af72e width=500>
> 
> 
> Therefore, I believe this issue will be resolved if you fix the point cloud map.

###### @KYabuuchi (2024-07-17)

> On the other hand, I have successfully prevented the scan matcher from failing on hills by adjusting the following parameters, without updating the map.
> 
> *  `autoware_launch/config/localization/ekf_localizer.param.yaml`
> ```diff
> -      z_filter_proc_dev: 1.0
> +      z_filter_proc_dev: 3.0
>        roll_filter_proc_dev: 0.01
> -      pitch_filter_proc_dev: 0.01
> +      pitch_filter_proc_dev: 0.1
> 
> ```
> 
> * `autoware_launch/config/localization/ndt_scan_matcher/pointcloud_preprocessor/crop_box_filter_measurement_range.param.yaml` 
> ```diff
> -    min_x: -60.0
> +    min_x: -30.0
>      max_x: 60.0
> -    min_y: -60.0
> -    max_y: 60.0
> +    min_y: -30.0
> +    max_y: 30.0
> 
> ```
> This change is intended to cut off the point cloud and prevent the virtual building and hill from being observed simultaneously.
> 
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a4994ae-bf3c-4140-b386-375726f416a5
> 
> It is still unstable but I think we can improve it more by adjusting the parameters.
> 

###### @Kim-mins (2024-07-20)

> Thank you for your detailed investigation @KYabuuchi!
> 
> I did not notice that my `.pcd` file misses some pointclouds. Thank you for pointing out.
> 
> I agree to your modification works well, but I got one small question for this issue.
> 
> - Question: I think using the default parameters for ndt scan matcher is encouraged, and seems I should change the parameters if I want to resolve the issue. If I don't change the parameters, should I fill the missed part of the `.pcd` file?
> 
> I really appreciate to your help! Thanks!

###### @KYabuuchi (2024-07-22)

> @Kim-mins 
> I don't think using the default parameters of the NDT scan matcher is necessarily encouraged. It's expected that parameters will be adjusted according to the environment.
> 
> If you don't change the parameters, you'll need to fix the pcd file. Alternatively, avoiding unmapped areas should prevent the issue from occurring.

###### @Kim-mins (2024-07-22)

> Thank you for the clear answers @KYabuuchi!
> 
> Then it seems better for me to change the parameters.. Thanks a lot!
> 
> The issue seems gone now, so can I close this issue?

###### @KYabuuchi (2024-07-22)

> @Kim-mins  Yes. Please close this issue :ok_hand:

> 
> ### Description
> 
> Due to the poor detection performance of the current BEVDet model on the TIER4 dataset, we plan to retrain the BEVDet model on the TIER4 dataset.
> 
> Reference this BEVDet train code baseline: [Link](https://github.com/LCH1238/BEVDet)
> TIER4 Dataset  [Link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UaarK88HZu09sf7Ix-bEVl9zGNGFwTVL/view?usp=sharing)
> 
> Note: Now, the data provided by the above link only has 39 scenes, totaling 2874 keyframes, which does not meet the training requirements. We will first use the TIER4 dataset to complete the training process.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Retrain the BEVDet model on the TIER4 dataset.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. Use the same network configuration as the deployed onnx model to train on the Nuscenes dataset to ensure that the model can converge normally.
> 2. train on the TIER4 dataset.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> to write a script for converting TIER4 dataset to BEVDet train pkl file format

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla using [bridge implementation](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6859#issuecomment-2196138040), and I found a situation that Autoware keeps acceleration less than 0 and the ego vehicle does not drive at all from the starting point.
> 
> Here's the rviz video of the situation: [[video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NpCeUIaOOOr9vTVTIxGWleLMMyGYuDpi/view?usp=sharing)] and corresponding `launch.log` file: [[launch.log](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jQ3YVHXiK3QGfAmySIGKtoykGpshXys2/view?usp=sharing)]
> 
> When I checked the control command by subscribing the topic `/control/command/control_cmd` and plotted `acceleration` and `speed` as below, it showed that the acceleration is below 0 and  the speed does not increase (the values oscillates though..).
> ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd8e57f1-bc92-421c-895e-51f1cbfe6713)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope the ego vehicle to drive well to the goal point.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But the ego vehicle does not start to drive.
>

> - Vehicle is expected to stay within the left or right lane (depending on the follow of traffic)
> - Currently, the vehicle moves to the center of the lane
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> We need to fine-tune the existing parameters of `behaviour_path_planner` or potentially develop new features to allow the detection of bi-directional lanes and flow of traffic. This, in turn, will allow the vehicle to stay within either the left or right lane (depending on the flow of traffic) instead of moving to the center of the lane.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - The `behaviour_path_planner` module defines a path and drivable area the vehicle can move depending on the traffic situation. Investigation within this module may be a good starting place.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] The vehicle to stay within the left or right lane in a bi-directional lane
> - [ ] The vehicle detects the correct flow of traffic and follows the correct lane
> - [ ] The vehicle to slow down if there are obstacles within the same lane, staying within the lane and not overtaking if there are obstacles in the other lane

### #7922 — [Dense-Urban-ODD] Improve cruise planner safe distance when cruising a front npc

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-07-09  |  **Closed:** 2024-09-30  |  **Author:** @ahmeddesokyebrahim
- **Labels:** type:improvement, component:planning
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7922

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Part of:
> - #7485
> 
> #### Dense Urban ODD Characteristics
> - **Low-Speed Driving:** Typical speeds around 15 km/h.
> - **Complex Traffic Elements:** Includes dense traffic with various dynamic interactions.
> - **Dynamic Agents:** Frequent encounters with moving pedestrians and cyclists.
> - **Bidirectional Movement:** Vehicles operate in lanes supporting bidirectional flow.
> - **Traffic Rule Non-compliance:** Other road users may exhibit behaviors such as:
>   - Driving in the wrong direction.
>   - Cutting in unexpectedly from off-road areas.
>   - Jaywalking pedestrians.
>   - Improper / sudden overtaking by other road users.
> 
> In the context of Dense Urban ODD, currently `obstacle_cruise_planner` keeps a very long safe distance between ego and front npc which makes the driving scenario not natural. or potentially develop new features to improve the slowing down of ego vehicle to overtaking road user maintaining both passengers safety and comfortability.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Based on description above, the purpose of this issue is to improve  `obstacle_cruise_planner`  safe distance calculations to have a more near human driving scenarios while cruising a front npc.
> 
> #### Cruising front npc "UC-NTR-005-0001"
> The following image describes the scenario where ... 
> - an npc is driving in in front of ego vehicle
> - the npc slows down from 14 km/h to 10 km/h
> - ego vehicle is expected to have a safe distance of 2-seconds (follow distance / separation distance) with front npc.
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/36835765/39643caa-08f5-4a19-be70-0a12517176f5)
> 
> The purpose of of this improvement is to mitigate any unnecessary distance (very long distance between ego and npc) that makes the driving scenario not natural / human-like.
> 
> ##### Npc slowing down from 14 km/h to 10 km/h
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ce9d596-0150-4b66-b766-3658440e8695
> 
> 
> For reproducing the issue using scenario simulation, you can use the these [scenario](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16348835/UC-NTR-005-0001.zip) and [map](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16348855/LEO-VM-00001.zip) files.
> :exclamation: Note :exclamation: 
> In this previous scenario, the safe distance is updated to be 12.5 m following the 3-seconds inter-vehicle time-distance distance performance requirements [here](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1t8PaJIXKCQ7GElig4dVbbkcjLEphHQ9ARmWCci5IML4/edit#slide=id.gd38c585fc3_0_7)
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The `obstacle_cruise_planner`  already depends on a function named `calcRSSDistance()` to get the `target_dist_to_obstacle`
> This function basically depends on this equation : 
> ```
> d_safe =  v_ego * t_reaction + (v_ego^2) / (2 * a_max) - (v_obstacle^2) / (2 * a_min) + d_margin
> ```
> The `d_margin` is set to 6.0 m which yields to a very long distance in the afortmentioned scenario between ego and front npc.
> 
> A possible approach is to provide speration between stop and cruise parameters and reduce the value for cruise paramter used by RSS equation to be just a small constant to avoid zero distance )
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Add/separate needed parameters.
> - [ ] Reflect needed changes in the code after parameters separation
> - [ ] Ensure the target scenario is passing.

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2024-07-16)

> @brkay54 @ahmeddesokyebrahim  
> Could you provide the reasons behind the safety distance of 2 seconds?Could you post the link to the reference you used to define this?
> 
> It would be also nice if you could also what original function is  considering. Depending on the intention of function, it might be better to update the scenario to use the rss criteria.

###### @villaoningfootball (2024-09-18)

> Will different NPCs set different times∩╝ƒ

> Closing this issue as completed after merging the relevant [PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/1166).

> ### Description
> 
> We are trying to visualize the test coverage of each package in autoware.universe with @yhisaki . 
> Specifically, the current approach is to first run tests locally on packages under the planning directory, and then use codecov to visualize the test results.
> When running tests locally, we've confirmed that tests for some packages fail. To my understanding, in autoware.universe, having all colcon tests succeed is a required condition for merging PRs, so this shouldn't occur even on locally.
> Therefore, I think there might be an issue with how we're running the tests locally. 
> 
> Possible reasons could be:
> - There's a problem with the test execution method
> - There's a valid reason for test results to fail locally

> If anyone has insights on this, please let me know.

> 
> pass all test
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> When executing
> ```
> colcon test --event-handlers console_cohesion+ --base-paths ./src/autoware/universe/
> ```
> 
> to run tests for packages in autoware.universe locally, some tests fail. We've also noticed that results vary between executions and when run on different PCs.
> 
> To mimic the colcon test behavior in GitHub Actions, we tried:
> ```
> colcon lcov-result --zero-counters --verbose
> colcon lcov-result --initial
> colcon test --executor sequential --base-paths ./src/universe/autoware.universe/
> ```
> referencing https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-github-actions/blob/main/colcon-test/action.yaml

> ```
> colcon lcov-result --zero-counters --verbose
> colcon lcov-result --initial
> colcon test --executor sequential --base-paths ./src/universe/autoware.universe/
> ```

> The following image describes the scenario where ... 
> - an npc is driving in adjacent lane to ego. 
> - then it passes the ego vehicle and overtakes the ego lane. 
> - after overtaking, it starts to slow down.
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/36835765/92a91aa3-ffd8-4de6-a8b3-0613e828cb18)
> 
> The purpose of improvement in the following cases is to mitigate any unnecessary declaration (slowing down) value by ego vehicle while keeping the distance with overtaking npc.
> 
> 
> ##### NPC slowing down from 20 to 15 km/h "**PASSED** :heavy_check_mark: "
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/917cda44-981e-42f1-9347-f7e694c41fd6
> 
> 
> ##### NPC slowing down from 20 to 12.5 km/h "**FAILED** :x:"
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/53c59784-d77e-4438-b367-d6689d1e2109
> 
> 
> ##### NPC slowing down from 20 to 10 km/h "**FAILED** :x:"
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fc53112-fbc0-48a5-aab8-57528b8b6f7e
> 
> 
> For reproducing the issue using scenario simulation, you can use the these [scenario](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16450289/UC-NTR-001-0008.zip) and [map](https://evaluation.ci.tier4.jp/evaluation/maps/980?project_id=awf) files.
> 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The `obstacle_cruise_planner` should be capable of handling the situations mentioned above. 
> - The primary goal will be to tune the parameters of the package to achieve the success of above scenarios.
> - If tuning the parameters is not enough for having successful scenarios, the  `obstacle_cruise_planner` implementation should be improved.
>

### #7864 — [Dense-Urban-ODD] Enhance Cruise Planner's Responsiveness to Other Road Users

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-07-05  |  **Closed:** 2024-10-08  |  **Author:** @brkay54
- **Labels:** type:improvement, component:planning
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7864

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Part of:
> - #7485
> 
> ### Dense Urban ODD Characteristics
> - **Low-Speed Driving:** Typical speeds around 15 km/h.
> - **Complex Traffic Elements:** Includes dense traffic with various dynamic interactions.
> - **Dynamic Agents:** Frequent encounters with moving pedestrians and cyclists.
> - **Bidirectional Movement:** Vehicles operate in lanes supporting bidirectional flow.
> - **Traffic Rule Non-compliance:** Other road users may exhibit behaviors such as:
>   - Driving in the wrong direction.
>   - Cutting in unexpectedly from off-road areas.
>   - Jaywalking pedestrians.
>   - Improper overtaking by drivers.
>   
> In the context of Dense Urban ODD, we need to fine-tune the existing features of the `obstacle_cruise_planner` and potentially develop new features in speed planning to achieve the characteristics mentioned above.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> ### Improvement in Cruising for Cut-In and Cut-Out Obstacles
> 
> - The `obstacle_cruise_planner` package currently uses predicted objects in a limited way for speed planning. We need to consider objects further away from the trajectory by expanding the coverage area.
> - The planner should respond more effectively to obstacles. If the predicted paths of other vehicles intersect with our planned path, Autoware should react much earlier to avoid potential collisions.
> 
> **Late Reaction to Potential Collisions**
> 
> [Video Link](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/c7124008-c9b3-437c-820c-432d6081c9b4)
> 
> **Late Reaction for Pedestrian**
> 
> [Video Link](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/fdb76b28-dd86-41bf-ae33-06dbb5ab1d63)
> 
> - For objects that briefly enter and exit our path without posing a significant collision risk, the planner should avoid unnecessary reactions. This selective response will prevent abrupt and unnecessary slowdowns, ensuring smoother and more efficient driving.
> 
> **Unnecessary Stop for Transient Object**
> 
> [Video Link](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/12d31bf5-c30b-4d59-95ad-073bc978dd1f)
> 
> ### Stop for a Vehicle Coming Fast from Behind
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/78fc9b3a-fae7-4ef0-a384-abbfbc60ba5e)
> 
> - This is a common scenario in our real vehicle testing. While the Ego is starting to drive, a vehicle approaches quickly from behind and overtakes the Ego. In this situation, `obstacle_cruise_planner` reacts uncomfortably. We want to make the `obstacle_cruise_planner` more reactive to vehicles approaching from behind.
> 
> ### Possible Approaches
> 
> The `obstacle_cruise_planner` is capable of handling the situations mentioned above. My primary goal will be to fine-tune the parameters of the package. If any function is inadequate in handling these situations, I will improve it.
> 
> ### Definition of Done
> 
> - [x] Create a proposal for changing parameters.
> - [x] If the package is inadequate to handle scenarios, propose improvements.
> - [x] Ensure all scenarios for Dense Urban ODD pass.
> - [x] Create additional scenarios if necessary.

---

### #7834 — The stop judgment method for freespace_planner is inconsistent with that for mission_planner

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-07-04  |  **Closed:** 2025-09-30  |  **Author:** @Try110
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7834

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The stop judgment method for freespace_planner is inconsistent with that for mission_planner;
> The stop judgment of mission_planner takes into account the velocities in three directions of xyz, while the velocities in x-direction are considered in freesspace_planner
> 
> 
> `
> //mission_planner
> bool VehicleStopCheckerBase::isVehicleStopped(const double stop_duration) const
> {
>   if (twist_buffer_.empty()) {
>     return false;
>   }
>   constexpr double squared_stop_velocity = 1e-3 * 1e-3;
>   const auto now = clock_->now();
>   const auto time_buffer_back = now - twist_buffer_.back().header.stamp;
>   if (time_buffer_back.seconds() < stop_duration) {
>     return false;
>   }
>   // Get velocities within stop_duration
>   for (const auto & velocity : twist_buffer_) {
>     double x = velocity.twist.linear.x;
>     double y = velocity.twist.linear.y;
>     double z = velocity.twist.linear.z;
>     double v = (x * x) + (y * y) + (z * z);
>     if (squared_stop_velocity <= v) {
>       return false;
>     }
>     const auto time_diff = now - velocity.header.stamp;
>     if (time_diff.seconds() >= stop_duration) {
>       break;
>     }
>   }
> 
>   return true;
> }`
> 
> 
> `//freespace_planner
> bool isStopped(const std::deque<Odometry::ConstSharedPtr> &odom_buffer,
>                const double th_stopped_velocity_mps) {
>   for (const auto &odom : odom_buffer) {
>     if (std::abs(odom->twist.twist.linear.x) > th_stopped_velocity_mps) {
>       return false;
>     }
>   }
>   return true;
> }
> `
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> When Fressspace_planner determines that the task is over,mission_planner should also determine that the task is over, otherwise there will be no executor
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> However, because this speed determination is inconsistent, and even the mission_planner is stricter than the freespace_planner, it will occasionally lead to the freespace_planner judging that the task has ended, but the mission_planner will not complete the task. Under these circumstances, the mission never ends.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> sometimes 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The stop judgment of mission_planner takes into account the velocities in three directions of xyz, while the velocities in x-direction are considered in freesspace_planner
> 
> 
> `
> //mission_planner
> bool VehicleStopCheckerBase::isVehicleStopped(const double stop_duration) const
> {
>   if (twist_buffer_.empty()) {
>     return false;
>   }
>   constexpr double squared_stop_velocity = 1e-3 * 1e-3;
>   const auto now = clock_->now();
>   const auto time_buffer_back = now - twist_buffer_.back().header.stamp;
>   if (time_buffer_back.seconds() < stop_duration) {
>     return false;
>   }
>   // Get velocities within stop_duration
>   for (const auto & velocity : twist_buffer_) {
>     double x = velocity.twist.linear.x;
>     double y = velocity.twist.linear.y;
>     double z = velocity.twist.linear.z;
>     double v = (x * x) + (y * y) + (z * z);
>     if (squared_stop_velocity <= v) {
>       return false;
>     }
>     const auto time_diff = now - velocity.header.stamp;
>     if (time_diff.seconds() >= stop_duration) {
>       break;
>     }
>   }
> 
>   return true;
> }`
> 
> 
> `//freespace_planner
> bool isStopped(const std::deque<Odometry::ConstSharedPtr> &odom_buffer,
>                const double th_stopped_velocity_mps) {
>   for (const auto &odom : odom_buffer) {
>     if (std::abs(odom->twist.twist.linear.x) > th_stopped_velocity_mps) {
>       return false;
>     }
>   }
>   return true;
> }
> `
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

> @xmfcx Thanks for your cooperate :+1:

###### @xmfcx (2024-07-02)

> @KeisukeShima the build-and-test jobs (not differential) are running on:
> 
> Either on:
> - [EC2 c6a.xlarge](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/instance-types/c6a/) with 4vCPU 8GiB RAM
> - `leo-copper` machine with 4c8t CPU and 32GB RAM
> 
> On this failure instance, it was running on [`leo-copper` machine](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/actions/runs/9743179438/job/26886066688#step:1:2)
> 
> And if we look into the colcon test command, we can see it is being called with sequential flag:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-github-actions/blob/a1960b03b1d3f5c4320ec1d4e7916ffac437f4f1/colcon-test/action.yaml#L89-L93
> 
> > ```
> > colcon test --event-handlers console_cohesion+ \
> >   --mixin coverage-pytest \
> >   --packages-above ${{ inputs.target-packages }} \
> >   --executor sequential \
> >   --return-code-on-test-failure
> > ```
> 
> > However, the root cause of the problem is the lack of resources in the testing environment.
> 
> What would be your suggestion for improvements? Do you think for example:
> - `leo-copper` is not strong enough?
> - If not, what kind of machine would you suggest?
> 
> We already run these sequentially and I think machines are strong enough.
> And by design of github-actions-runner, they can only perform one job at a time.

###### @mojomex (2025-07-22)

> This issue now has an intermediate solution: 
> * #10999
> 
> While the long-term solution is to have GPU runners (an absolute necessity as more and more safety-critical functionality is being moved to GPU!), this PR executes all tests on every machine, regardless of GPU capabilities, but skips the tests if they require a GPU and there is none.
> 
> This has the following benefits over the status quo (commented out unit tests):
> 
> * unit tests are always compiled, ensuring that they stay up to date, even if the packages' source code changes
> * unit tests are executed locally (assuming you have an Nvidia GPU), ensuring that any changes are tested at least locally
> * unit tests in non-GPU CI runners show up as `SKIPPED`, clearly indicating that some functionality could not be tested, but without failing CI
> * once GPU runners become available, unit tests will be executed without any further manual changes
> 
> I will do some PRs to modules that have commented-out unit tests.
