### #7713 — oneAPI integration project plan

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-26  |  **Closed:** 2025-10-25  |  **Author:** @kaspermeck-arm
- **Labels:** DevOps Dojo: oneAPI, openadkit
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7713

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [x] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [x] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The UXL Foundation (UXLF) and the Autoware Foundation (AWF) have signed an MOU which aims to use the oneAPIs in the Autoware software stack through the Open AD Kit WG. Find the MOU and description here:
> * [MOU](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zs5zJQ1_-5_4sJQVlwr_TC5VnYvQwoeEV-roM0cVcio/edit?usp=sharing)
> * [UXLF Automotive Demonstrator (Exhibit A)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12BCmZmtGJ9Y33c9PCvkNnBE1xi0T8cbZhrzrQlfRP4o/edit?usp=sharing)
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose of the is project is make accelerated compute portable. This is done by adopting the oneAPIs which removes the need to rewrite the source code when running on different hardware. If a new target hardware is to run the Autoware software stack, then only recompilation should be necessary to deploy Autoware. Find more information on UXLF and oneAPIs here:
> * [UXL Foundation and oneAPIs](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1YqmkyPE-oyRSjdOS-DVsGLv-F08wb3WVXlRpn17hLS8/edit?usp=sharing)
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> ## Identify a Suitable ROS Package
> 
> A highly parallelizable and compute intense workload (initially not ML) is preferred, e.g., some type of point cloud processing. The following ROS nodes have been suggested as suitable as they are compute intense:
> * pointcloud_preprocessor
> * behavior_path_planner
> * behavior_velocity_planner
> * ndt_scan_matcher
> 
> ### Pointcloud preprocessor
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/30662532/0b8070a4-4d29-4a33-9bd8-2f061424f095)
> 
> These nodes are found in the `pointcloud_preprocessor` package
> * [pointcloud_preprocessor](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src)
> 
> and are launched using the following launch script
> 
> * [common_sensor_launch](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/sample_sensor_kit_launch/blob/main/common_sensor_launch/launch/nebula_node_container.launch.py#L97)
> 
> ### NDT Scan Matcher
> [Eigen](https://eigen.tuxfamily.org/index.php?title=Main_Page) is used within the "ndt_scan_matcher_core.cpp" file.
> 
> * Is the Eigen backend configured to use CUDA/Nvidia cards present in the system?
> 
> The following Eigen data types are used:
> * Eigen::Matrix4f (389)
> * Eigen::Quaterniond (423)
> * Eigen::Matrix3d (426)
> * Eigen::Vector3d (698)
> * Eigen::Matrix2d (55)
> * Eigen::Matrix3d (426)
> * Eigen::Vector2d (783)
> * Eigen::Map<const RowMatrixXd>
> 
> The following Eigen functions are used: 
> * Eigen::SelfAdjointEigenSolver<Eigen::Matrix2d> (58)
>   * Calculates the Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a self-adjoint matrix
>   * [Self-Adjoint Matrix -- from Wolfram MathWorld](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Self-AdjointMatrix.html)
> 
> #### LAPACK Analysis
> 
> In order for this module to be converted to oneAPI we will need to target specific LAPACK functions.
> 
> Function used to get eigen-values:
> * LAPACKE_dgeev
> 
> Where is this in oneMKL LAPACK Solver:
> * heevd
> * hegvd
> * syevd
> * sygvd
> 
> These are the functions that would need to be available in vendor back-end implementation of oneMKL LAPACK.
> * Eigen::Rotation2Dd(th).toRotationMatrix() (62)
>   * Represents a rotation/orientation in a 2 dimensional space
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> * applicable ROS package(s) have been identified
>   * how to replace libraries and functions with oneAPI
> * consensus on how to integrate oneAPIs, e.g., into the build system

**Comments:**

###### @kaspermeck-arm (2024-07-17)

>

> .

### #7689 — Dynamic_obstacle_avoidance does not work stable

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-25  |  **Closed:** 2024-09-22  |  **Author:** @beyzanurkaya
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning

> ### Checklist
>

> 
> ### Description
> 
> A moving object is heading towards the EGO vehicle. The dynamic_obstacle_avoidance module cuts the drivable area based on this object, but in some cases, it becomes confused about which side of the drivable area to cut.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/32412808/0eed3525-96c8-4149-8471-e3822c311d7f
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The dynamic_obstacle_avoidance module should stably perform cutting the object from the drivable area without any confusion.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The `dynamic_obstacle_avoidance` module is unable to decide from which side to cut the object from the drivable area.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. run plan_sim
> map: [LEO-VM-00038.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15967776/LEO-VM-00038.zip)
> 2. add a dynamic object
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> 
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> 

**Comments:**

###### @beyzanurkaya (2024-07-01)

> I think the problem here is that the lane is bidirectional:
> 
> Single Directional Lane:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/32412808/41270d47-74ca-4e73-ab87-b3171b611740
> 
> Bidirectional Lane:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/32412808/1d25281e-40c6-47cb-b92d-26ae87258589
> 
> I haven't debugged it yet, but my guess is that the module cannot determine which direction the object is on the lane. Therefore, it cannot properly decide which side of the drivable area to cut.

###### @beyzanurkaya (2024-07-03)

> `isLeft` function sometimes returns `false` even though the NPC is  clearly to the left of EGO vehicle

###### @beyzanurkaya (2024-07-16)

> When the road is single direction, it means that the NPC is going in the wrong direction in this video. That's why only a straight predicted path is generated for the NPC in `autoware_map_based_prediction`.
> 
> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c83f03f9-a250-4b93-8aa5-966c9c04c7d4
> 
> When the road is bi-directional, there doesn't seem to be any situation where either the EGO or the NPC violates the road rules. Therefore, a predicted path is generated as if both vehicles will move along the centerline. This causes the object's future position to be on the path of the EGO. As a result, the module is trying to remove the wrong part from the drivable area.
> 
> In conclusion, If the road is bi-directional, vehicles should drive from the right or left side according to the traffic flow, not from the road's centerline.
> 
> I will open an issue for this in `autoware_map_based_prediction`.

###### @stale (2024-09-14)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @beyzanurkaya (2024-09-22)

> I planned to solve this problem by shifting the predicted_paths of the objects to the right or left. With @technolojin -san's PR, the instability in `dynamic_obstacle_avoidance` was eliminated. I'm closing the issue.

### #7652 — Evaluate current Localization accuracy of current NDT scan matching against Localization dataset

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-24  |  **Closed:** 2024-10-02  |  **Author:** @mitsudome-r
- **Labels:** component:localization
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7652

**Body:**

> ## Description
> We should compare the localization performance of Autoware before/after Autoware Labs activity.
> Once we create a pointcloud map for the data collected in [this issue](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/issues/4725), we should do evaluation of current Autoware's localization accuracy. 
> ## Purpose
> This issue aims to measure the localization performance of autoware in urban environment.
> ## Possible approaches
> For the accuracy, we can try using post-processed  GNSS/INS data output as ground truth. 
> ## Definition of done
> 1. Displaying localization errors with metrics, using Ground Truth (Post Processed GNSS/INS data) as reference.. 
> 2. Determining where localization errors increase in urban environment and where existing autoware localization is inadequate.

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2024-06-24)

> There is no guarantee that RTK is always accurate so I appreciate for any other way of getting ground truth data.

###### @meliketanrikulu (2024-08-15)

> I tested with data which is this [PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-documentation/pull/597) shared.
> I tested  all map with default autoware. I used GNSS/INS Twist Messages instead vehicle velocity because this data collected with mapping setup and there is no vehicle velocity information on it.
> 
> 1.) Here is the localization broken points in [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/18y8qgt8neHZeekriH2pU8tV5p1wL3uMp/view?usp=sharing) on the google earth.
> You can open this .kml file on google earth.
> 
> 2.) Also you can see broken points on pointcloud map in [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16HxTj1WXSrDksJGPdtszkFh5LmEajGCZ/view?usp=sharing)
> You can open this file with Cloud Compare.
> I will also share test video.

###### @meliketanrikulu (2024-08-20)

> I made some parametric changes and also we collected new data because of time problem in last data. You can check out the some test results with new data.
> 1.) To start, I simply wanted to observe how autoware localization works.  [Test Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bk4Oyk6FOg0)
> 
> I did this test with Default autoware. Since I don't have the vehicle velocity as a Twist source, I did this test using the TwistWithCovarianceStamped message from GNSS/INS. 
> There are 2 tunnels on our route. As expected, localization was disrupted while passing through the tunnels. Apart from this, no visible disruption was observed in localization at first glance.
> 
> 2.) The error of GNSS/INS in the tunnel increases as seen in the video above.However, the frequency of the Twist message does not decrease or the Twist message is not interrupted. For this reason, I wanted to check if using the speed coming from here causes an error in the tunnel. For this reason, I tested the localization in the tunnel by giving only NDT poses as input to EKF. In this test, no Twist message was given to EKF. [Test Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ajgedIwwuaM)

###### @meliketanrikulu (2024-08-28)

> I added Show&Tell Discussion for explaining to tests --> https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/5135

###### @meliketanrikulu (2024-10-02)

> Added document to [Autoware Documentation](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/pr-611/tutorials/components_evaluation/localization_evaluation/urban-environment-evaluation/) . We can close this issue .

### #7634 — Improve dynamic_obstacle_avoidance_module 

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-23  |  **Closed:** 2024-09-05  |  **Author:** @beyzanurkaya
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7634

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> **The main issue:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/7485
> 
> The dynamic_obstacle_avoidance_module currently has several limitations that hinder its performance and reliability. Specifically:
> 
> **1. Inaccurate Drivable Area:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/7684
> **2. Stability Issues:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/7689
> **3. Expansion of drivable area:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/7690
> - Limited avoidance: The module can only shift the vehicle up to 0.5 meters to avoid obstacles. Exceeding this limit causes the node to crash.
> - Inability to change lanes: The module cannot change lanes when necessary when avoiding dynamic objects.
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose of this issue is to enhance the dynamic_obstacle_avoidance_module by addressing the current limitations. The goal is to improve the module's flexibility, reliability, and overall performance in dynamic obstacle avoidance scenarios.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> **1. Correct cutting of the drivable area:** 
> 
> - Enhancing the current algorithm to accurately trim the drivable area around dynamic obstacles.
> 
> **2. Increase Stability:**
> 
> - Perform extensive testing and debugging to identify stability issues.
> - Improve the cutting algorithm of the drivable area according to the debugging result.
> 
> **3. Expand Drivable Area:**
> 
> - Develop algorithms to dynamically adjust the drivable area based on obstacle detection.
> - Refactor the module to handle shifts greater than 0.5 meters without causing crashes.
> - Modify the obstacle avoidance algorithm to allow safe lane changes when avoiding dynamic obstacles.
> - Integrate the ability to expand the drivable area to accommodate larger avoidance maneuvers temporarily.
> - Ensure the expanded drivable area maintains safety and compliance with road regulations.
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] The module allows the EGO vehicle to safely change lanes when avoiding dynamic obstacles.
> - [x] The module can handle shifts greater than 0.5 meters without crashing.
> - [x] The module operates consistently and stably under a variety of dynamic obstacle scenarios.
> - [x] The module can dynamically expand the drivable area as needed to effectively avoid obstacles.
> - [x] Documentation is updated to reflect the changes and new capabilities of the module.
> 
> By addressing these areas, the dynamic_obstacle_avoidance_module will become more robust, flexible, and capable of handling complex dynamic obstacle scenarios effectively.

**Comments:**

###### @stale (2024-08-24)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
>

### #7598 — Support ROS 2 Jazzy Jalisco

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-20  |  **Closed:** 2024-06-20  |  **Author:** @HansRobo
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7598

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The new distro, Jazzy Jalisco is out!
> https://discourse.ros.org/t/ros-2-jazzy-jalisco-released/37862
> 
> Lets's start planning to support it.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose is to support new distro, Jazzy Jalisco.
> It is inevitable that some users will request Jazzy support in the near future.
> In the process of supporting Jazzy, we will also see positive results for Autoware running on Humble, such as removing deprecated features.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Identify and migrate features that are deprecated in humble and removed in Jazzy
> - Implement conditional compilation for jazzy
> - Add packages that have not been released for jazzy in the repos file
> - Promote jazzy support for packages that autoware depends on
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> The initial Jazzy support is sufficient to build and minimally run with PlanningSimulator.
> But making distructive changes for autoware behavior with ROS 2 Humble is not permitted.

**Comments:**

###### @HansRobo (2024-06-20)

> Updating dependencies and removing deprecated code for jazzy is going in #6656
> NOTE: the pull request is going to be divided into small ones due to its largeness.
> 

###### @f0reachARR (2024-06-20)

> ### Identified problems to be fixed
> - [ ] [Missing dependency that caused build errors](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/7600)
> - [ ] Replace / introduce conditional include for deprecated header files
> - [ ] Adopt changes of `optional` in Boost library
> - [ ] Replace deprecated Ogre API in RViz plugins
> 
> ### Identified problems, but not fixable now
> - [ ] QoS arguments of create_client / create_service: In jazzy, setting it to rmw_qos_* is deprecated, but humble does not support new method.
> - [ ] Some required packages are not provided by binary distribution.
>     - [navigation2](https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2) (nav2_costmap_2d, etc...). Related issue: https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4428
>     - [grid_map](https://github.com/ANYbotics/grid_map)
>     - [pacmod3_msgs](https://github.com/astuff/pacmod3_msgs)
>     - Open3D (python3-open3d package). Related issue: https://github.com/isl-org/Open3D/issues/6730
> 
> 

###### @HansRobo (2024-06-20)

> `ANYbotics/grid_map` will support Jazzy on v2.2.0
> https://github.com/ANYbotics/grid_map/milestone/1
>

> @yukkysaito -san,
> According to the documentation https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/community/support/support-guidelines/
> 
> > - GitHub Issues
> >   - Confirmed bugs
> >   - **Confirmed tasks**
> 
> The confirmed tasks should be tracked through issues.
> 
> The main reason for this is, when PRs or Issues mention Discussion posts, the backlinks don't appear in discussions. This makes issue tracking very hard.
> 
> Backlinks like these are important for tracking:
> <img width="481" height="119" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01cf5a8c-872f-4cec-b240-c2454ce9864a" />
> 
> This is why:
> - Discussion -> Issue -> PR Γ£à
> - Issue -> PR Γ£à
> - Discussion -> PR Γ¥î (please don't do this, very hard to track)
> - Just PR ≡ƒƒ¿ (if scope is small, it's ok, as long as PR description is good)

### #7587 — Bugs about euclidean_cluster

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-19  |  **Closed:** 2024-07-02  |  **Author:** @beginningfan
- **Labels:** component:perception
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7587

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> 1. `min_cluster_size` is not passed to [clustering algorithm](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/b284599e61d2824049ae76f907ca698abc9bccbe/perception/euclidean_cluster/lib/voxel_grid_based_euclidean_cluster.cpp#L89)
> 2. When the `max_cluster_size_` is large, clustering takes too much CPU and memory because this [line](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/b284599e61d2824049ae76f907ca698abc9bccbe/perception/euclidean_cluster/lib/voxel_grid_based_euclidean_cluster.cpp#L109). This bug is related to this [pr](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6818)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> 1. The size of the cluster is greater than or equal to the `min_cluster_size`
> 2. Memory allocation should be based on the actual size of the point cloud
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> 1. The input parameter of the cluster algorithm is 1 
> 2. Memory allocation is based on the maximum number of clusters
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. print size of clusters before filter in [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/b284599e61d2824049ae76f907ca698abc9bccbe/perception/euclidean_cluster/lib/voxel_grid_based_euclidean_cluster.cpp#L134)
> 2. use a large number such as 30000 as `max_cluster_size` in [config](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/b284599e61d2824049ae76f907ca698abc9bccbe/perception/euclidean_cluster/config/voxel_grid_based_euclidean_cluster.param.yaml#L7)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> OS: ROS2
> autoware: latest
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #7563 — Misdetects the pedestrian near a car

> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The perception system fails to detect and track the pedestrian when they are close to the car. It only recognizes the pedestrian once they move away from the vehicle.
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/115910640/707427b6-0e39-4aee-a937-f74768303fa7)
> ![walker](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/115910640/7e8394d0-915a-4778-b32f-dcf13a3fc680)
> Here is the video of the rviz2.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/115910640/b538ca29-b0c7-4f02-a50a-64bf7100e8c2
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Detect the pedestrian correctly
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Miss detects the pedestrian near the car.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. cd autoware/src/sensor_kit/external/awsim_sensor_kit_launch/awsim_sensor_kit_launch/launch∩╝îmodify the awsim_sensor_kit, only one top lidar is used.
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/115910640/29eb1629-83a9-4ffe-80b9-040e48a65ddb)
> 2. ros2 launch autoware_launch logging_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=map_path vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=awsim_sensor_kit
> 3. replay this bag [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FFE1XTrY-A8ELE1zi32bvGfe-Hah4u7P/view?usp=sharing](url)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> -OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> -ROS2: Humble
> -Autoware: Autoware.universe main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The point clouds of pedestrians and cars are connected together∩╝î and not recognize correctly 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @badai-nguyen (2024-07-04)

> @sgNicola Thank you for your issue report. 
> I think the current DNN model (Centerpoint) is not good enough for pedestrians nearby the vehicle, especially for the large vehicle like bus because of lack of training dataset. 
> Could you try to enable `detection_by_tracker` for pedestrians by [this](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/000527bde7b1a4e4d643591d031818169802188d/autoware_launch/config/perception/object_recognition/detection/detection_by_tracker/detection_by_tracker.param.yaml#L10) and check this again?
> 
> @YoshiRi Do you have further comment?

> Out of curiosity, I tried with TransFusion, hoping intensity field will play main role here. Despite the fact the pedestrian and car results with different intensities, it still brings the same result as CenterPoint.
> ![transfusion_car_with_pedestrian](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/37396312/13ee0830-27d1-4154-bd94-92af5e21a7da)
> 
> For TransFusion It could be due to different intensity profile in input data. I see Velodyne here, AFAIK dataset consist of Velodyne data as well. Therefore, the source for both ML models is lack of similar samples in dataset as @badai-nguyen mentioned.

### #7501 — Cache ccache with GitHub Actions Cache and reuse in `build-and-test-differential` workflows.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-16  |  **Closed:** 2024-06-17  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:ci
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7501

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Related
> 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/4497
> - Being solved in: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/7503
> 
> ### Description
> 
> ```mermaid
> graph TD
>     bntc["build-and-test-cuda"]
>     --> ccache([ccache])
>     -->|"actions/cache/save@v4"| ghac[("GitHub Actions Cache")]
>     
>     ghac-->|"actions/cache/restore@v4"| bntd["build-and-test-differential"]
>     ghac-->|"actions/cache/restore@v4"| bntdc["build-and-test-differential-cuda"]
>     ghac-->|"actions/cache/restore@v4"| bntc
>     ghac-->|"actions/cache/restore@v4"| bnt["build-and-test"]
> 
> bnt:::cla_bnt
> bntc:::cla_bnt
> bntd:::cla_bntd
> bntdc:::cla_bntd
> ccache:::cla_cache
> ghac:::cla_cache
> 
> classDef cla_bnt fill:#00E678,stroke:#555,color:#000
> classDef cla_bntd fill:#3F2EE3,stroke:#555,color:#FFF
> classDef cla_cache fill:#00C8FF,stroke:#555,color:#000
> ```
> 
> #### Additional info
> 
> - `build-and-test-cuda` runs for every commit to the `main` branch.
>    - It also runs once per day.
> - `build-and-test-differential` runs for every PR against main, multiple times.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - To speed up `build-and-test-differential` workflows.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - Being solved in: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/7503
> 
> - [x] ~~Remove unused cache action:~~
>    - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-github-actions/blob/92b81882b5e5a67da07211aa997f61f7d9f94be7/colcon-build/action.yaml#L87-L93
>    - It seems, it is used by clang-tidy action:
>       - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-github-actions/blob/92b81882b5e5a67da07211aa997f61f7d9f94be7/clang-tidy/action.yaml#L84-L91
> - [x] Modify `build-and-test` `cuda` workflow to cache its `ccache` folder
>    - If it was successful
> - [x] Modify `build-and-test-differential` workflows to restore the cache
> - [x] Validate that workflows are faster now.
> 
> cc: @youtalk @mitsudome-r @oguzkaganozt

### #7485 — [Autoware Labs] Dense Urban ODD - Reviewing and Tracking Failed Scenarios

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2024-06-13  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @brkay54
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7485

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> **Follow-up task of:**
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/issues/4636
> 
> **Failed Scenario Summary:** 
> - [Development Tracking Sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1WTqiyUndtdBNgiNnAApjOXhma-QAU_SBPdD626pMr2Q/edit?gid=0#gid=0
> )
> ### Objective
> This issue tracks the progress and improvements related to the scenario catalog created for autonomous driving tests within a Dense Urban Operational Design Domain (ODD). The primary objectives are:
> - **Defining Problems:** Clearly define the problems for developers using the scenarios below.
> - **Tracking Development:** Monitor the development process.
> 
> ### Dense Urban ODD Characteristics
> - **Low-Speed Driving:** Typical speeds around 15 km/h.
> - **Complex Traffic Elements:** Includes dense traffic with various dynamic interactions.
> - **Dynamic Agents:** Moving pedestrians and cyclists are frequently encountered.
> - **Bidirectional Movement:** Vehicles operate in lanes supporting bidirectional flow.
> - **Traffic Rule Non-compliance:** Other road users may exhibit behaviors such as:
>   - Driving in the wrong direction.
>   - Cutting in unexpectedly from off-road areas.
>   - Pedestrians jaywalking.
>   - Drivers overtaking improperly.
> 
> ### Task for Developers
> - **Investigating failed scenarios:** Identify root causes and potential fixes for failed scenarios.
> - **Improving Software Packages:**  Enhance functionalities based on scenario feedback.
>   - **Fine-Tuning Parameters:** If the package already has the functionality to handle the failed case, fine-tune the package parameters.
>   - **Proposing Improvements:** If the package has the functionality but it is insufficient to handle the failed case, propose improvements to the functionality.
>   - **Adding New Functionalities:**  If the package lacks the functionality to handle the failed case, propose adding new functionality to the target package.
> - **Creating Additional Scenarios:** Develop new scenarios to test various other conditions and ensure robustness.
> 
> ### List of the scenarios
> <details>
> <summary>Click to expand the list of the scenarios</summary>
> 
> #### Useful Links
> 
> - **Scenario Suit:** [Autoware Evaluator](https://evaluation.ci.tier4.jp/evaluation/suites/05e1818a-85a8-4940-afb1-9e1795fe7b7f?project_id=awf)
> - **Scenario Description Document:** [Google Presentation](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1t8PaJIXKCQ7GElig4dVbbkcjLEphHQ9ARmWCci5IML4/edit#slide=id.g2d072098d1a_0_4)
> <details>
> - [Development Tracking Sheet](
> https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1WTqiyUndtdBNgiNnAApjOXhma-QAU_SBPdD626pMr2Q/edit?gid=0#gid=0
> )
> 
> <summary>UC-NTR-001-0001</summary>
> 
> - **Scenario Description:** Ego vehicle is overtaken from outside of the road by a faster moving NPC.
> - **Development Focus:** Ensure ego vehicle remains stationary until the high velocity NPC has completed its overtaking maneuver.
> - **Scenario Links:**

> ### Purpose
> 
> The primary goal of this task is to enhance the capability of autonomous driving software for low-speed driving in dense urban areas with mixed road users. This involves improving the system's awareness of various conditions and its responsiveness to these conditions. By fine-tuning trajectory planning, cruise control for dynamic obstacles, adaptive cruise planning, and avoidance strategies, we aim to ensure smoother, safer, and more efficient driving in complex urban environments.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> | Improvement Target                          | Description                                                                                     | Related Scenarios                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Assignees                      | Development                                                                                                                                              |
> |---------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
> | **Path Planning and Trajectory Adjustment** | - Adjust the trajectory to align more closely with the right or left edge of the lane for bi-directional lanes, depending on the direction of traffic flow. | - UC-VRU-002-0005 <br> - UC-NTR-004-0001                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | - @beyzanurkaya                 | [Issue #7923](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/7923)                                                                                                                                                        |
> | **Cruise Planning for Dynamic Obstacles**   | - Expand the coverage area to consider objects further away from the trajectory. <br> - Autoware should react much earlier if the predicted paths of other vehicles intersect with our planned path to avoid potential collisions. <br> - Avoid unnecessary reactions to objects that briefly enter and exit our path to prevent abrupt and unnecessary slowdowns, ensuring smoother and more efficient driving. | - UC-NTR-001-0001 <br> - UC-NTR-001-0002 <br> - UC-NTR-001-0003 <br> - UC-NTR-001-0004 <br> - UC-NTR-001-0005 <br> - UC-NTR-001-0006 <br> - UC-NTR-002-0004 <br> - UC-NTR-003-0001 <br> - UC-NTR-003-0002 <br> - UC-NTR-003-0003 <br> - UC-VRU-001-0002 <br> - UC-VRU-002-0001 <br> - UC-VRU-002-0004 | - @brkay54                     | [Issue #7864](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/7864)                                                                        |

### #7463 — `radar_object_tracker` launches even if no radar has been launched

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-12  |  **Closed:** 2024-10-17  |  **Author:** @mhmdrz-mirdamadi
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7463

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When launching the perception, [this line](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/ab4badbbd00e1687247d1b25a1e3e857ea098fba/launch/tier4_perception_launch/launch/perception.launch.xml#L119C1-L123C5) makes the [radar object tracker](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/perception/radar_object_tracker) to be launched always even if there is no radar to get the [output](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/perception/radar_object_tracker#output) from it.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> `use_radar_tracking_fusion` should be true if and only if the radar has a role in fusion. To be more precise, the [perception mode](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/ab4badbbd00e1687247d1b25a1e3e857ea098fba/launch/tier4_perception_launch/launch/perception.launch.xml#L48C1-L49C1) should be `camera_lidar_radar_fusion`, `lidar_radar_fusion` or `radar`.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> `use_radar_tracking_fusion` will always be true even if no radar has a role in fusion.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Set the [perception mode](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/ab4badbbd00e1687247d1b25a1e3e857ea098fba/launch/tier4_perception_launch/launch/perception.launch.xml#L48C1-L49C1) to one of the `lidar` or `camera_lidar_fusion`.
> 2. Launch the perception.

> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - This repository can be used as a reference: [https://github.com/tier4/lidar_feature_extraction/tree/develop](https://github.com/tier4/lidar_feature_extraction/tree/develop)
>

###### @ataparlar (2024-09-24)

> We noticed that the optimization process makes 30 iterations every time. This was related to the map size and we tried to use the map dynamically with octrees. Red points show the Surface Feature Map and turquoise points show the Corner Feature Map:
> ![Screenshot from 2024-09-17 17-30-33](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a731440-5af8-4f58-9f6d-dacdaacdd670)
> 
> 
> We observed that in that way, our optimization time is reduced from an average of 1 second to 500 milliseconds. Please note that this is for 30 iteration counts. Normally, the optimization is complete in 10 iterations. So, the runtime will be normal. Still, we are testing.
> ![Screenshot from 2024-09-17 17-33-33](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d96fbdbb-ae8a-47b6-95be-18973de8864d)
> 
> 
> However, in some areas, the optimization fails and position cannot be found. I am investigating that right now. The image of the positions is below:
> ![Screenshot from 2024-09-17 17-34-19](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/871ae388-c35e-4727-8e6c-8ec613a4f56e)
> 

###### @ataparlar (2024-09-24)

> We noticed some problems related to reading the points. Normally, each point in the dataset has a 16-bit unsigned integer time field inside it. The program tries to read it as float. So, the time difference between the points cannot be detected and the point cloud undistortion never worked. We have fixed that.
> Additionally, we noticed something with acceleration directions in the dataset and fixed that in the code. Now, the program works fluently without breaking. Here is the situation:
> 
> - Red points: Surface Map Points
> - Turquoise points: Corner Map Points
> - Yellow Points: Surface Cloud Points
> - Blue Points: Corner Cloud Points
> ![Screenshot from 2024-09-24 09-46-21](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74b91d15-2626-49e2-aac0-70a2cdacbdaf)
> 
> 
> In the video below, you can see the performance in the Eurasia Tunnel (the long tunnel). In the end, LOAM stuck but we solved that with IMU bias parameters. So, we can get in and get out of the Eurasia Tunnel.
> [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lo1u--8MLwQ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lo1u--8MLwQ)
> 
> We recorded a different video after the tunnel. We travel here on a highway and travel the Bosphorus Bridge on this part. After the city environment, we get into the Bomonti Tunnel (small tunnel) and the feature matching fails here:
> [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JO3q8bNIxqs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JO3q8bNIxqs) This video only contains the area after the Eurasia Tunnel. As you can see, the rosbag leaps frames. This is related to my ethernet settings at that moment. So, the error in the Bomonti Tunnel might be related to that because we have successfully traversed this part in a different dataset.
> 
> It doesn't break in the long tunnel, because there are very many features to match. In the small tunnel, there are fewer and sometimes it struggles to find the perfect position. I am working on it and I will keep here posted. It is nearly done.

###### @ataparlar (2024-10-06)

> Hi, 
> 
> I have worked on a modified LIO-SAM repo until now. [Here is the link](https://github.com/ataparlar/LIO-SAM/tree/ros2). This branch works with MGRS point cloud map and the XYZ coordinates of all of the points were very large. So, we are translating the point cloud segments to local and calculating the position here. After that, we translate back the calculated pose to the global. In that scenario, the pose is calculated fine but due to the large coordinate numbers, imuPreintegration can corrupt or precision reduces for position calculation. In the end, the position inside of a tunnel can't be calculated. It is stuck. 
> [You can find the MGRS point clouds here.](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pDKgoe9xOY3M8WbZnZBttWU0XJuDnQDD?usp=drive_link)
> - You need to change **line 11 and 12** in `config/params.yaml` to work with the point clouds.
> - We changed the `allocateMemory()` function in that file to initialize ground truth point clouds and octree objects.
> - We are loading the initialized point cloud in the same function.
> - `extractCloud()` function is changed for loading the new map part.
> - The point P(66459, 43620, 42.75) is the starting point in MGRS point cloud. So, the first point cloud will be loaded around that area. After the lidar position comes, `lidar_link` is translated to that area.
> - For translating the first position, we have changed
> 
> [In this branch](https://github.com/ataparlar/LIO-SAM/tree/local-map), which works with a local point cloud map, we do not have that many large coordinates. So, we don't translate anything to local and calculate everything as where it is. In that scenario, we are able to travel the long tunnel (this one has more features) and we are able to travel every urban or highway area. However, it is stuck in the second tunnel. It is 3-4 kilometers far from the origin and it has much fewer features than the long tunnel. Still, we were able to travel that tunnel with a map starting from the start of the tunnel. We have tested that with previously collected data before.
> [You can find the local point clouds here.](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ZzLM7OM7PTMEllM0fn6l1XlGfHnPdsm6?usp=drive_link)
> You need to change **line 11 and 12** in `config/params.yaml` to work with the point clouds.
> - We changed the `allocateMemory()` function in that file to initialize ground truth point clouds and octree objects.
> - We are loading the initialized point cloud in the same function.
> - `extractCloud()` function is changed for loading the new map part.
> 
> So, as far as I observed, the distance from the origin is the issue right now. Used libraries don't accept `double` type so I couldn't change it. 

###### @xmfcx (2024-10-08)

> - See https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/7454#issuecomment-2399877539 for the final status.
> 
> Closing this since there are no resources to complete this task for now.
> 
> If anyone is interested, feel free to reopen.

### #7449 — LOAM Based Localization Task 1 - Implement point cloud undistortion

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-11  |  **Closed:** 2024-07-09  |  **Author:** @ataparlar
- **Labels:** component:localization
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7449

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The distortions in the point clouds must be cleaned in order to find the LOAM features correctly.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Having undistorted point clouds for LOAM based localization.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - The undistortion in the loam-mapper can be used.

### #7427 — Potential output topic mismatch

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-11  |  **Closed:** 2024-06-19  |  **Author:** @YuqiHuai
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7427

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I am studying the source code of Autoware and noticed the input/output topics are often remapped in launch files. I am expecting each node should register publishers for topics that I can find in the launch file.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Topic name should match in implementation and in launch file remap.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> In [autoware behavior velocity planner node implementation](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/autoware_behavior_velocity_planner/src/node.cpp), we have `~/output/stop_reason`
> ```c++
>   stop_reason_diag_pub_ =
>     this->create_publisher<diagnostic_msgs::msg::DiagnosticStatus>("~/output/stop_reason", 1);
> ```
> but in [launch file](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/autoware_behavior_velocity_planner/launch/behavior_velocity_planner.launch.xml) we have `~/output/stop_reasons` (plural at the end).
> ```xml
> <remap from="~/output/stop_reasons" to="/planning/scenario_planning/status/stop_reasons"/>
> ```
> 
> Is this mismatch intended?
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Reading source code of node implementation and launch file.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> Main branch, but the same issue was also in v1.0.
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> I find both `~/output/stop_reasons` and `~/output_stop_reason` are used by obstacle stop planner.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e3a30cd6934081bff443a2b10532b99a279ab062/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/launch/obstacle_stop_planner.launch.xml#L24-L25
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @maxime-clem (2024-06-14)

> You are right this is a bug.
> However that launch file is not used by default so it should not cause any issue when running Autoware.
> The `obstacle_stop_planner` is launched in the motion planning launch file (if selected with the `motion_stop_planner_type`): https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/launch/tier4_planning_launch/launch/scenario_planning/lane_driving/motion_planning/motion_planning.launch.xml#L188
> 
> Some example launch files are provided in the individual packages, but they are not the ones used when running the default Autoware setup.

###### @maxime-clem (2024-06-19)

> I am closing this since there is no bug at runtime.
> We could discuss removing the unused  launch files as they can cause confusion if they are not constantly updated.

### #7255 — Street light is not perceived as an obstacle.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-04  |  **Closed:** 2024-06-13  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** component:planning, simulator:carla
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7255

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla, and I found a situation that a street light is not properly perceived as an obstacle and the vehicle eventually collides with it.
> Here are a front view and rviz video: [[rviz](https://drive.google.com/file/d/15IiPQJzrXU3OTtIbkjzMJyRpVn5SuJXJ/view?usp=sharing)] [[frontview](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XbufX85yv3Tamy3uE1P7kr8ejoWolAry/view?usp=sharing)]
> 
> At 0:12 of the rviz video, the ego vehicle invades the sidewalk, and it eventually collides with a street light while recovering from the error.
> I know that the bridge I used had an issue on processing control command so that is not the point, but while driving out from the sidewalk, I think that the vehicle should perceive the street light as an obstacle and stop before the collision.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope the vehicle to perceive the obstacle properly, and stop before any collision.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> However, the vehicle collides with the obstacle.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Here's the ros2bag file for the reproduction: [[ros2bag](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1dobX9eNsJLCSZcGdDN-ZSRlWmFWX9JV_?usp=sharing)]
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - autoware.universe: [7877192cb5700c1db15109dcd959785fc381951d](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/7877192cb5700c1db15109dcd959785fc381951d)
> - Carla: 0.9.15
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @sgNicola (2024-06-04)

> Hi~,I also encountered this problem and I think this is due to that the vector map used in Carla doesn't contain the traffic lights.

###### @Kim-mins (2024-06-04)

> Hi @sgNicola
> 
> I also aware that our carla map does not contain traffic light information.
> My point on this issue is not the traffic light, but the obstacle at front(in this case, street light), which is not properly perceived as an obstacle.

###### @sgNicola (2024-06-04)

> I see, thank you for your explanation, the route is strange.

###### @maxime-clem (2024-06-13)

> I confirmed that AEB (https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/control/autoware_autonomous_emergency_braking/) works as expected with your bag.
> This means we can detect the collision, but because of the incorrect control, the collision detection is very late and even if we trigger an emergency stop it is too late to avoid the collision.
> By default even if AEB detects a collision the emergency stops is not activated. See this discussion if you want to enable it: https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/4669.

###### @Kim-mins (2024-06-13)

> Thank you for the response @maxime-clem!!
> 
> I did not notice the emergency stop.. thank you so much for the confirmation.
> 
> By the way, I got two questions on this issue:
> 
> 1. I thought there was no emergency stop since I could not check any log regarding emergency stop in [[launch.log](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HGGiBQF87FwgixOL4RY9hm6b5sTswIvQ/view?usp=sharing)] (sorry for not sharing the log..).
> Isn't the emergency stop always logged to `launch.log` when it was activated?
> 
> 2. Also, I thought this was the issue of perception, since there was no red wall in rviz behind the obstacle. Is it not activated in the case of emergency stop?
> 
> Thank you!

###### @maxime-clem (2024-06-13)

> > By default even if AEB detects a collision the emergency stops is not activated. See this discussion if you want to enable it: https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/4669.
> 
> In the default configuration there is no emergency stop with AEB and no messages in the logs. (see  https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/4669)
> 
> I confirmed on the bag that AEB works as expected locally with the current Autoware. However in your bag the output of AEB never switches to the emergency mode and I could not understand why. If you encounter another similar issue please feel free to create another issue.
> 
> Otherwise I think we can close the present issue since the street light is correctly perceived as an obstacle by AEB with the current Autoware.

###### @Kim-mins (2024-06-13)

> Thank you for the response @maxime-clem!
> 
> I think I got your point. thank you for the details.
> I'll close this issue soon, and I'll let you know if I encounter the similar issue.
> 
> Thanks!

---

### #7235 — Implement RTMDet to Perception Pipeline

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-03  |  **Closed:** 2026-08-05  |  **Author:** @StepTurtle
- **Labels:** component:perception
- **Comments:** 40  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7235

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> We plan to add the  [RTMDet](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection/tree/3.x/configs/rtmdet#rtmdet-an-empirical-study-of-designing-real-time-object-detectors) model in addition to the existing YOLOX model in Autoware Universe. While the YOLOX model is successful in the bounding box task, its instance segmentation layer is weak. We aim to improve instance segmentation results by adding RTMDet model.
> 
> ![208044554-1e8de6b5-48d8-44e4-a7b5-75076c7ebb71](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/76053179/155f45e9-5003-4e26-b5cd-6f67c665f4c7)
> 
> ![208070055-7233a3d8-955f-486a-82da-b714b3c3bbd6](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/76053179/fde70467-2c53-4c83-a9c2-b24c14130e02)
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Our goal is to enhance the lidar image fusion pipeline by adding the RTMDet model to Autoware for image segmentation.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> We can convert pre-trained PyTorch models to ONNX and TensorRT formats, and we can create a ROS 2 package to handle the TensorRT models in Autoware Universe perception to implement them in Autoware.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Use pre-trained PyTorch models to detection
> - [x] Convert pre-trained PyTorch models to ONNX and TensorRT format
> - [x] Deploy TensorRT model with Python
> - [x] Deploy TensorRT model with C++
> - [x] Create a ROS 2 package in Autoware Universe which use ONNX models
> - [ ] Compare RTMDet results with YOLOX segmentation results
> - [ ] Decide how can we use the RTMDet segmentation results with image lidar fusion pipeline

**Comments:**

###### @StepTurtle (2024-06-03)

> Here is the results of pre-trained models shared in [this link](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection/tree/3.x/configs/rtmdet#rtmdet-an-empirical-study-of-designing-real-time-object-detectors) from mmdetection.
> 
> **Results:**
> 
> - I used PyTorch models to get these results (models with `.pth` extension)
> 
> | Model  | Score Threshold  | NMS Threshold  | Detection Time Per Image | Video Link |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | RTMDet-Ins-s | 0.3  | 0.3  | ~20 ms | [Video Link](https://youtu.be/rMZjsiv6V5o) |
> | RTMDet-Ins-x | 0.3  | 0.3  | ~33 ms | [Video Link](https://youtu.be/XTCghOU1lDY) |
> 
> ---
> 
> For now, I tested the pre-trained models shared by mmdetection using mmdetection tools. Also they provide a couple of tools to convert `.pth` models to `.onnx` and `.engine` models. I check both of the converted model results and they are looking same and I think we can say their tools clearly convert the models.
> 
> Right now I am trying to handle how can use TensorRT models in `cpp` with TensorRT libraries.

###### @StepTurtle (2024-06-05)

> I deploy TensorRT engine to Python and I get some consistent results.
> 
>  | Model  | Score Threshold  | NMS Threshold  | Detection Time Per Image | Video Link |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | RTMDet-Ins-s (TensorRT) | 0.3  | NO NMS  | ~20 ms | [Video Link](https://youtu.be/ge8leR9OsOs) |
> | RTMDet-Ins-x (TensorRT) | 0.3  | NO NMS  | ~36 ms | [Video Link](https://youtu.be/rBS3KIzIzLI) |
> 
> > [!WARNING]
> > In some parts of the video, you may see incorrect class names. For example, you might see both truck and car class names assigned to a vehicle. This is because I didn't run NMS when I deployed it in Python. I plan to fix this when I deploy it in C++.
> 
> ---
> 
> So, my next plan is doing same things in C++.
> 
> Also, the detection times looks a little bit more. I did not understand the reason right now but I am working on it.

###### @StepTurtle (2024-06-11)

###### @StepTurtle (2024-10-01)

> **Some options to use RTMDet results on camera-lidar pipeline:**
> 
> **1)** Only run RTMDet and use roi outputs with current pipeline. Since the bounding box results from RTMDet is same with YOLOX, you can directly use RTMDet with current camera-lidar pipeline.
> 
> **2)** Fuse instance segmentation mask with clusters from euclidean clustering and assign clusters to label.
> 
> The outputs of euclidean clustering are only point clouds, and it is `UNKNOWN` which objects they belong to. `roi_cluster_fusion` assigns labels to the clusters using bounding boxes. `mask_cluster_fusion` uses instance segmentation masks instead of bounding boxes.
> 
> It may perform better with objects that are close to each other and overlapping. I haven't tested it yet.
> 
> **code:** https://github.com/StepTurtle/autoware.universe/tree/feat/mask_cluster_fusion
> **video:** https://youtu.be/nq7WJUAzpXE
> 
> **3)** Fuse the point cloud with instance segmentation masks and take the points within the mask as object.
> 
> **code:** https://github.com/StepTurtle/autoware.universe/tree/feat/mask_pointcloud_fusion
> **video:** https://youtu.be/MvUnQ120IWE
> 
> **4)** Fuse the point cloud with the instance segmentation mask. Filter out the points that do not correspond to objects within the mask and create a filtered point cloud.
> 
> Couldn't find a useful place where we can use the filtered point cloud.
> 
> **PR:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/8167
> **video:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N8qrGAxzSJM

###### @VeeranjaneyuluToka (2025-02-05)

> @StepTurtle , can i use the model trained using mmyolo - yolox and converted .onnx file using mmdepoly in autoware-perception tensorrt-yolox node directly as they use different github to train yolox model as per autoware documentation?

###### @stale (2025-04-07)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @xmfcx (2026-08-05)

> > @StepTurtle , can i use the model trained using mmyolo - yolox and converted .onnx file using mmdepoly in autoware-perception tensorrt-yolox node directly as they use different github to train yolox model as per autoware documentation?
> 
> @VeeranjaneyuluToka apologies for the very late reply, this thread went quiet and your question deserved an answer.
> 
> **Short version: not directly.** `autoware_tensorrt_yolox` does not care which repo trained the weights, but it does care about the shape of the exported ONNX graph, and a stock mmdeploy export will not work as-is.
> 
> The node picks its post-processing purely from the number of TensorRT I/O tensors ([`tensorrt_yolox.cpp:131`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/3194c4d2cbd9aa9acbaf116cd5d5e865fc39b646/perception/autoware_tensorrt_yolox/src/tensorrt_yolox.cpp#L131)):
> 
> - **2 tensors**: plain YOLOX head, the node decodes the raw output itself.
> - **5 tensors**: the graph ends in `EfficientNMS_TRT`, so the node reads the decoded boxes directly.
> - **anything else**: falls into `default`, which sets `multitask_++` and treats the extra output as a **semantic segmentation head**.
> 
> A stock mmdeploy end-to-end export gives `dets` plus `labels`, so 3 tensors, and it lands in that last branch. There is no graph validation anywhere, so instead of a clean error you get silently wrong output.
> 
> Two ways to make it work:
> 
> 1. Re-export so the graph ends in `EfficientNMS_TRT` (5 outputs, boxes in the letterboxed network-input pixel space), or
> 2. export the raw head in the Megvii layout so it hits the 2-tensor path.
> 
> Either way, match the node's preprocessing, because none of it is configurable: it letterboxes with `scale = min(net_w / img_w, net_h / img_h)` ([`tensorrt_yolox.cpp:285`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/3194c4d2cbd9aa9acbaf116cd5d5e865fc39b646/perception/autoware_tensorrt_yolox/src/tensorrt_yolox.cpp#L285)), pads with **114** ([`preprocess.cu:109`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/blob/3194c4d2cbd9aa9acbaf116cd5d5e865fc39b646/perception/autoware_tensorrt_yolox/src/preprocess.cu#L109)), feeds **BGR**, and applies no mean/std normalisation (`norm_factor` is hard-coded to `1.0`). There is also no `num_class` parameter: the class count comes from the number of entries in the file you pass as `label_path`. Note the package README still calls that parameter `label_file` in a couple of places, which is stale; the actual ROS parameter is `label_path`.
> 
> **One thing specific to this thread:** the RTMDet work is not going forward and is not supported. `autoware_tensorrt_rtmdet` was never merged (#8165 is closed), this issue is being closed, and we are removing the leftover model download and the `trt_batched_nms` dependency. `autoware_tensorrt_yolox` is the supported 2D camera detector. I will follow up here shortly with the full rationale and a link to the cleanup tracking issue.
> 
> If the export still gives you trouble, please open a fresh issue on `autoware_universe` and we will follow up there rather than on a closed thread.
> 

###### @xmfcx (2026-08-05)

> Picking this thread back up to close it out properly, since it has been quiet for a while.
> 
> **Decision: we are not taking RTMDet forward.** The mechanical removal is tracked in autowarefoundation/autoware#7252.
> 
> Why, in short. #8165 (`autoware_tensorrt_rtmdet`) was reviewed thoroughly, 86 commits and 50 review threads all resolved, and was approved by @amadeuszsz on 2024-12-12. It ended up approved, not rejected on code quality. It stalled because @StepTurtle stepped away in early 2025 and nobody took it over, myself included. I closed it on 2025-12-26 after getting it to build against current Autoware and then hitting a TensorRT 10 ONNX parse failure.
> 
> Three things kept it from being worth restarting:
> 
> - **No consumer.** Nothing in `autoware_universe` or `autoware_core` produces or consumes 2D instance masks. `SegmentationMask.msg` has been merged for 20 months with zero producers and zero consumers, and the one consumer candidate, #9482, never got a second review from us.
> - **No benchmark.** The definition of done says "Compare RTMDet results with YOLOX segmentation results", and that has been unticked for 26 months. Latency was posted several times; the accuracy comparison was never produced, by the author or by any of us reviewing it. So we still have no evidence it improves anything measurable.
> - **Unmaintained upstream.** mmdetection's last commit on `main` is 2024-02-05 and mmdeploy's is 2024-09-30, so we would be shipping a 2024 ONNX we have demonstrably failed to re-export, plus a forked NVIDIA NMS CUDA plugin no other Autoware package needs.
> 
> For the record, the TensorRT 10 blocker itself looked fixable. The `/Add_2` Int32 vs Int64 parse error is a bounded defect in `autowarefoundation/trt_batched_nms`, which hardcodes `kINT32` in `getOutputDataType()` and `supportsFormatCombination()` and ships only the `int *` path in `src/nms/gatherNMSOutputs.cu`; `VBTI-development/onedl-mmdeploy` guards all three with `#if NV_TENSORRT_MAJOR < 10` under Apache-2.0. Nobody has carried that through end to end on Autoware's own TensorRT, so it is a documented path rather than a demonstrated one. It is not the reason we are stopping.
> 
> What is being removed: the `tensorrt_rtmdet` model download (462 MB fetched per install, about 957 MB on disk) and the `universe/external/trt_batched_nms` entry in `repositories/autoware.repos`. What is being kept: `SegmentationMask.msg`, marked deprecated rather than removed so any out-of-tree consumer keeps building, and #9018 (`enqueueV3` support in `autoware_tensorrt_common`), which came out of this effort, was merged, and is used today by `autoware_camera_streampetr`, `autoware_tensorrt_vad` and `autoware_diffusion_planner`.
> 
> The capability itself is still worth having, and I would rather that be on the record than buried. `roi_cluster_fusion` still associates by winner-take-all box IoU, and it picked up two more refinements in 2026 (#11828 per-class IoU thresholds, #12019 a pedestrian size gate stated as reducing false positives), so association quality in that path is clearly still being worked on. If anyone wants to revisit it, the preconditions are an owner with a maintainer standing behind them, a benchmark against the current `roi_cluster_fusion` baseline rather than 2024's, and a consumer that lands in the same cycle as the producer. I would also look at a model that exports plain ONNX with no custom TensorRT plugin, since that plugin is exactly what killed this attempt.
> 
> Thank you @StepTurtle for the work and for documenting it so thoroughly as you went. The write-ups in this thread are why a useful post-mortem was possible at all.
> 
> Closing this issue now that the decision is recorded. The mechanical removal is tracked to completion in autowarefoundation/autoware#7252, so there is no reason to keep this one open on top of it. #9482 will be closed separately, with porting notes preserved, since that node is model-agnostic and is worth reviving if an instance-mask producer ever shows up.

### #7211 — C++ bug in lambda capturing of structured bindings

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-06-01  |  **Closed:** 2024-07-22  |  **Author:** @veqcc
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7211

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> There is a bug in C++<=17 around lambda capturing for structured bindings: https://www.reddit.com/r/LLVM/comments/s0ykcj/why_does_clang_fail_with_error_reference_to_local/
> 
> This bug if fixed in C++20: https://releases.llvm.org/16.0.0/tools/clang/docs/ReleaseNotes.html#c-language-changes
> 
> Since Autoware runs with C++<=17, we have to avoid it.
> Fortunately, clang-tidy makes the related warning!!
> For example,
> ```
> reference to local binding 'search_start_pose' declared in enclosing function 'behavior_path_planner::GoalSearcher::countObjectsToAvoid'
> ```
> 
> - search_start_pose : https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/6fe9fc648eaa3c1c36dc75fb8800212bd075bbfe/planning/behavior_path_goal_planner_module/src/goal_searcher.cpp#L212
> - search_end_pose : https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/6fe9fc648eaa3c1c36dc75fb8800212bd075bbfe/planning/behavior_path_goal_planner_module/src/goal_searcher.cpp#L212
> - object_exit_time: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/6fe9fc648eaa3c1c36dc75fb8800212bd075bbfe/planning/behavior_velocity_intersection_module/src/scene_intersection_collision.cpp#L269
> - object_enter_time: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/6fe9fc648eaa3c1c36dc75fb8800212bd075bbfe/planning/behavior_velocity_intersection_module/src/scene_intersection_collision.cpp#L269
> - max_lat_acc: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/6fe9fc648eaa3c1c36dc75fb8800212bd075bbfe/planning/behavior_path_lane_change_module/src/utils/utils.cpp#L95
> - feasible_slow_down_vel: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/6fe9fc648eaa3c1c36dc75fb8800212bd075bbfe/planning/obstacle_cruise_planner/src/planner_interface.cpp#L557
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Do not use lambda capturing for structured bindings.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> nothing
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> nothing
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @soblin (2024-06-01)

> I referred to this article.(japanese)
> 
> https://onihusube.hatenablog.com/entry/2019/10/04/122001
> 
> IMO this is a trivial syntax sugar warning. Initial C++17 N4659 allowed the structured binding specifiers of a tuple to be referred from a lambda. But this was deprecated later because it was only allowed for a tuple-like object(our usage), not array/struct.
> 
> We are using g++ so there is no issue/bug. I want to keep using it because the code looks more tidy.

###### @veqcc (2024-06-01)

> @soblin 
> Thank for your quick investigation!
> 
> We should avoid clang-tidy CIRITICAL level warnings, even if it is actualy not a bug, in terms of maintainability.
> ( so that we can get useful infomation from clang-tidy results)
> As you say, we can easily avoid the warning with a small tidy additional code.

### #7166 — Misclassification of static obstacle into cyclist makes the vehicle stop.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-05-30  |  **Closed:** 2024-11-08  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:perception, simulator:carla
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7166

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla, and I found a situation that the misclassification of static obstacle into cyclist makes the vehicle stop.
> Here's the rviz video:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/50267797/e1b2a8d0-4e4a-4376-bd54-e35edced2c7b
> 
> 
> According to the video, the vehicle does not move because of the static obstacle, which is not cyclist at all.
> I checked that obstacle in Carla, referring to the [[frontview video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/17pwY98e9KuLvOx2b-J6l_GNOiRzAKIff/view?usp=sharing)], it was something other than the cyclist.
> ![something](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/50267797/7d6f5937-d777-4750-a70a-62615050ac2d)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope the vehicle to drive as usual, classifying the static obstacle clearly.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> However, the static obstacle is misclassified as a cyclist, which eventually make the vehicle stop.
>

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2024-05-29  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @beginningfan
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:perception

> ### Checklist
>

> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, the tracking module in Autoware is 2D, which only considers the information of the xy plane and cannot adapt to situations such as uphill and downhill. This task aims to design a 3D tracking module to solve the problem of poor 2D performance.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Design a 3D tracker to improve tracking performance
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Autoware also has a [bytetracker](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/perception/bytetrack). I will try the effect of this tracker. If it works well, I will transform this tracker into 3D. 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Testing the existing bytetracker
> - [ ] Add a new 3D tracking package
> - [ ] Input and output result adaptation to Autoware topics

### #7135 — [intersection] After manual driving, the car will no longer stop due to other vehicles 

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2024-05-27  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @kany-hsu
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/7135

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> We observed vehicles will be ignored after we switch to manual driving in a "closed pattern path".
> 
> Here is a demonstration with the planning simulator:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/170914373/f8c4f21a-5466-46a0-8982-a572abb20a97
> 
> At the beginning, we assigned a start point and destination, and ran it autonomously. The car would stop as we expected. After that, we switched to manual driving, drove the car back to the starting point, and assigned the destination again, but this time the car couldn't stop.
> 
> (We use "2D Pose Estimate" for simulating manual driving behavior in 0:45-0:55.)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Intersection module detects other vehicles, and stops the car.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> After switched to manual driving, drove the car back to the starting point, the car will no longer stop due to other vehicles.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Use the lanelet map below to run planning simulator.
> [lanelet2_map.txt](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/15451944/lanelet2_map.txt)
> `ros2 launch autoware_launch planning_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=<lanelet_map_dir> vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit`
> 2. Do the simulation like the video.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> Ubuntu 22.04
> The demonstration is run with the latest main.
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> When we assigned the position of the car manually like 0:45-0:55 in `intersection.mp4`. It seems the old trajectory still exists, and it will be "extended" based on the new assigned positions of the car. When the old trajectory over some positions in the intersection, it somehow thinks the car is passing or passed the intersection again. Then the variable below will be `true` which make the intersection module ignore other incoming vehicles.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/cbaf62a36685b35110afc46097f9d5bba59f27fa/planning/behavior_velocity_intersection_module/src/scene_intersection.cpp#L1419
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @soblin (2024-05-27)

> Actually this phonemena is out of the scope of intersection module or behavior_velocity_planner. Please reset the goal and path again.
> 
> For intersection module's perspective, it seems that map has a very long "intersection lane". So **you have intentionally/unintentionally set a goal inside the intersection**  and you have not set a route that passes through the intersection. 
> 
> Also you should shorten the intersection lanelet.

###### @kany-hsu (2024-05-28)

> > Actually this phonemena is out of the scope of intersection module or behavior_velocity_planner. Please reset the goal and path again.
> > 
> > For intersection module's perspective, it seems that map has a very long "intersection lane". So **you have intentionally/unintentionally set a goal inside the intersection** and you have not set a route that passes through the intersection.
> > 
> > Also you should shorten the intersection lanelet.
> 
> Thanks for your comment @soblin !
> 
> It works by resetting the goal again after the car arrived the old goal.
> 
> And now I think the current problem is that after the car arrives the goal, **the old route is not reset and still exists**. If we switch to manual driving at this time, the old route will be affected or "extended", leading to this phenomena unless a new route is manually set by resetting the goal.
> 
> For handling unexpected situations and debugging, we often need to switch to manual driving.
> 
> Is it possible to automatically reset the old route after the car arrive the goal?
> 
> 

###### @maxime-clem (2024-06-19)

> > For handling unexpected situations and debugging, we often need to switch to manual driving.
> 
> You are correct and this should be supported. There was a bug with that feature but it is now fixed (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/7505).
> 
> > Is it possible to automatically reset the old route after the car arrive the goal?
> 
> Do you mean we should cancel the previous route once arriving at the goal ?

###### @soblin (2024-08-15)

> Can we close the issue ?

###### @kany-hsu (2024-08-19)

> Sorry for the late reply, I missed the message.
> > Do you mean we should cancel the previous route once arriving at the goal ?
> 
> Yes, if we do what's shown in `intersection.mp4` from 0:45-0:55, the previous route will affect the judgment of the intersection module, causing `is_permanent_go` to become "true", which leads to the failure of the intersection module .
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/28170c3a87752b687344dda563672ae0a8ea598b/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/autoware_behavior_velocity_intersection_module/src/scene_intersection.cpp#L1409C5-L1409C29
> 
>

> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.

> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware with Carla and I found a situation that lazy detection of a static pedestrian makes collision.
> Here are the rviz and the front view videos: [[rviz](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1mL3NWwqJj4NMGH60kpBzBtsKDYfO7oJ1/view?usp=sharing)] [[frontview](https://drive.google.com/file/d/19O5WPguVPwl11oMcTFV41_uArZvK6wL5/view?usp=sharing)]
> 
> The rviz video shows that, Autoware detects the pedestrian only after the vehicle gets close, and eventually makes collision.
> 
> I also reported the similar issue #6709, but it seems the bug remains in that,
> 1. I'm running the latest version now(running the commit [7877192cb5700c1db15109dcd959785fc381951d](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/7877192cb5700c1db15109dcd959785fc381951d))
> 2. I also tried to apply `position_filter`, but the detection performance seems not changed.: [[rviz](https://drive.google.com/file/d/126LfNmUYifHYO9Mui_B5bQ9TxE7JcU0P/view?usp=sharing)].
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I hope the pedestrian to be detected well and to make no collision.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But the pedestrian seems detected too slowly, and they eventually collide.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Here are the ros2bag files:
> - with `lanelet_filter`: [[ros2bag](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1uz7KhiMVLuViQRwRbvOB3wFs6WvVF1VS?usp=sharing)]
> - with `position_filter`: [[ros2bag](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1jrCeSdxs5GF5iCTK1Pe65M0XjCHuyX1W?usp=sharing)]
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - `autoware.universe`: [7877192cb5700c1db15109dcd959785fc381951d](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/7877192cb5700c1db15109dcd959785fc381951d)
> - Carla: 0.9.15
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @YoshiRi (2024-05-31)

> @Kim-mins 
> Thanks for your report. Sorry, I missed your issue due to lack of perception label.
> 
> I briefly checked your rosbag and found pointcloud number is too small.
> Current clustering algorithm output clusters with more than 10 point and the result seems only have 2~4 points until vehicle approaches. The figure below shows the actual pointcloud number is 2 when distance is 30m.
> 
> <img src="https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/20086766/132fcdb4-2734-40f1-a4d6-a25cb79c10b3" width="300">

> - Fix `min_cluster_size: 10` parameter in `voxel_grid_euclidean_cluster.param.yaml` or `euclidean_cluster.param.yaml` to smaller number, such as  `min_cluster_size: 4`. Remember this may increase false positive.
