> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Dear developers,
> 
> When we use CodeQL (GitHub's own static code analysis tool) to analyze the project, it has reported an error from code that may cause breakdown. And we found that this potential error tend to exist in the project for a relatively long time. In this issue we will provide the error form a single file `autoware.universe/planning/static_centerline_optimizer/scripts/app.py`, including its name and location. Hopefully it will get your attention, and we are looking forward to a further communication.
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Initializing SECRET_KEY of Flask application with a **randomly generated value**.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> 
> Initializing SECRET_KEY of Flask application with **Constant value** files can lead to Authentication bypass.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> - **Prepare everything by following the guidance of official docs before running 'colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release'**
> - **Then use CodeQL create database command to establish database and set '--command = 'colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release''**, it looks like: `codeql database create new-database --language=<language> --command='colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release'`
> - **Please note that the process needs a clean build and may take a long time to finish. Using clean command and parallelization techniques based on your hardware environment may help you make it faster**
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Linux Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS 2: Latest
> - Autoware: Latest, but it appears in much earlier version since the file has not been changed for at least 2 years
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> At the end of the code file, line 177:
> `if __name__ == "__main__":
>     app.debug = True
>     app.secret_key = "tmp_secret_key"
>     app.run(host="localhost", port=4010)`
> --------------------------------------------------------------------------^-----------------
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> **Because of the limit of GitHub, we cannot attach the original file directly. You can contact us by email to obtain it: 2654209843@qq.com**

### #6575 — Concatenate module starts to publish point cloud from the past if the system slowed momentarily

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-03-08  |  **Closed:** 2024-04-03  |  **Author:** @brkay54
- **Labels:** component:perception, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6575

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> During the use of the Autoware's e2e_simulator to run sensing and perception pipelines, it was observed that the concatenate module behaves unexpectedly under certain conditions. 
> 
> - _The system was configured with _`separate_concatenate_node_and_time_sync_node`_. And, the _`PointCloud2`_ messages were publised with same header time at the same time to pipeline._
> 
> **Pipeline latency [ms] statistics of the each lidar when the Autoware starts:**
> 
> ![w-dc-first-5min](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/e7b9a778-0aa4-4919-b3f2-8ee6ddeb6fb9)
> 
> Initially, the concatenate module's output displayed a low delay (~24 ms, visible in the above). However, upon a momentary slow-down of the computer system, the concatenate module's reported pipeline latency increased significantly, jumping from an average delay of 24 ms to 116 ms. This behavior suggests that the module's timing becomes misaligned with its inputs after such a system hiccup.
> 
> **System hiccup:**
> ![crash-add-one-step-delay-cropped](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/042006b6-c9d2-4cdb-9332-e80e2b54b67e)
> 
> 
> 
> As seen above, after the system hiccup, concatenate modules start follow the `pointcloud_preprocessor` pipelines one step behind. And, this causes additional delay for perception pipeline.
> 
> **Pipeline latency [ms] statistics of the each lidar after system hiccup:**
> 
> ![after-crash](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/1f4a9653-3d5b-4710-b569-d06d82eae2ed)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> ![before-delay drawio](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/3afedc95-cac8-484c-a004-e229b13ab0a9)
> 
> The concatenate module is expected to maintain consistent timing relative to its inputs, regardless of system performance fluctuations. Even if the system encounters momentary slow-downs, the concatenate module should recover and realign its timing with the incoming messages from the `pointcloud_preprocess` pipeline without introducing additional constant delay.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> ![after-delay drawio](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/2e1108fc-22f3-44de-b1f7-07466e0294a2)
> 
> 
> In the event of a momentary system slow-down, the concatenate module's timing becomes misaligned with the timing of its inputs. This misalignment causes the module to execute its timer and publish messages with a significant delay. Subsequently, the concatenate module continues to publish point cloud messages from the past, resulting in a consistent and increased pipeline latency (as shown in the third image and summarized in the statistics from the first image). This behavior indicates that the timing within the concatenate module does not adequately handle or recover from transient system performance issues.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> - Run the perception & sensing pipeline in Autoware. You can use `e2e_simulator.launch.xml`.
> - Plot the "/debug/pipeline_latency_ms" topics in a topic visualizer such as PlotJuggler.
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> **When I run the `e2e_simulator.launch.xml` with `concatenate_and_time_sync_nodelet.cpp`, I also observed similar behavior visible below:**
> 
> ![concat-time-cropped](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/64e52a4c-f158-4323-8e8a-9954a43de9a2)
> 
> 
>

### #6555 — obstacle cruise planner is setting zero velocity points behind the suddenly spawned obstacle in the trajectory 

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-03-06  |  **Closed:** 2024-03-06  |  **Author:** @brkay54
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6555

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In the `obstacle_cruise_planner` module of Autoware, an issue was observed where, upon the sudden appearance of a predicted obstacle on the planned route, the planner incorrectly sets a zero velocity for the trajectory segment behind the obstacle. This behavior deviates from expected handling, where adjustments are made to the trajectory in front of the obstacle. 
> 
> **Video:**
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/99de723f-0d1c-40b9-bde8-30d1cbb90ed3
> 
> **Snapshot when the stop wall was set:**
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/e9c00c05-24d1-4033-8ac6-6451539cc03c)
> 
> As you can see in the video, `obstacle_cruise_planner` sets zero velocity points far away from the ego in trajectory.
> 
> The scenario was tested as part of the planning_control pipeline in the `reaction_analyzer` (please [see](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5954) for more information.), highlighting the discrepancy in reaction time and trajectory planning when compared to `obstacle_stop_planner`. You can see the test results which are comparing motion_stop_planner_types in **Additional context** below.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> When a sudden obstacle is spawned on the route, the `obstacle_cruise_planner` should dynamically adjust the vehicle's trajectory by reducing speed or stopping in front of the obstacle, ensuring safety and adherence to the planned path without creating impractical or unsafe zero-velocity segments behind the obstacle.
> 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Upon the introduction of a PredictedObject in front of the vehicle, the `obstacle_cruise_planner` incorrectly sets a trajectory with zero velocity behind the sudden obstacle. This results in an unrealistic response to obstacles and may compromise the effectiveness of the planning_control pipeline. The warning message indicates a failure to interpolate the obstacle pose, suggesting a problem in trajectory adjustment logic.
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Set motion_stop_planner_type `obstacle_cruise_planner` in default_preset.yaml
> 2. Create a route for the ego vehicle by using `planning_simulator.launch.xml`
> 3. Simulate the ego vehicle driving at approximately 40 kph.
> 4. Spawn a PredictedObject 15 meters in front of the moving vehicle.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> Tests were made in some conditions:
> - **Pipeline:** ``` [obstacle_cruise_planner or obstacle_stop_planner] -> scenario_selector -> motion_velocity_smoother -> planning_validator -> trajectory_follower -> vehicle_cmd_gate```
> - Spawn obstacle if the distance between obstacle and vehicle is below 15 meters.
> - Wait until all the topics are reacted to the object.
> 
> Reaction times for a sudden object:
> 
> - _The results below indicate in milliseconds._
>

> @brkay54

>

### #6554 — Behavior Planner Time Consumption Due to side_shift Module

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-03-06  |  **Closed:** 2024-05-10  |  **Author:** @StepTurtle
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6554

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When running Autoware with a large-scale map and providing a long route, there is a noticeable increase in time consumption for the side_shift module. This results in a gradual decrease in planner speed to 1 or 2 Hz as the vehicle progresses.
> 
> We have no idea whether the problem will also occur on small maps because we have not figured out how to use small maps to test this situation.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The side_shift module should operate efficiently with large-scale maps and long routes, ensuring that the planner maintains a consistent speed without significant degradation over time.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Currently, the side_shift module exhibits increased time consumption with large-scale maps and long routes, leading to a gradual decrease in planner speed as the vehicle progresses.
> 
> [planning_low_hz_side_shift_module.webm](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/76053179/025ddc5e-3a16-4209-bb1d-d66dce32bd87)
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1.Load a large-scale map into Autoware.
> 2.Plan a long route for the vehicle.
> 3.Run Autoware and observe the performance of the side_shift module over time.
> 
> > [!TIP]
> > - It could take couple of hours
> > - You can open the 'debug' display on Rviz to see planner manager status
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: 22.04
> - ROS 2: Humble
> - Autoware: main branch
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #6547 — Add a new tool to measure end-to-end delay of the Autoware for sudden obstacles

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-03-05  |  **Closed:** 2024-05-17  |  **Author:** @brkay54
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:tools, component:system, component:evaluator
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6547

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In Autoware, accurately detecting the first response to sudden obstacles in various topics is challenging. There's a need for a tool that can create a test environment, listen to critical topics, and measure the system's reaction across different pipelines including Sensing, Perception, Planning, and Control.
> 
> **This is a follow-up from:**
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/5540
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose of this tool is to enhance the reliability and responsiveness of Autoware by providing a means to measure and analyze the delay in reacting to sudden obstacles. This will help in optimizing the system's performance across all stages of its pipeline, ensuring safer autonomous driving capabilities.
> 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. Develop a simulation environment within Autoware that can dynamically spawn obstacles.
> 2. Implement a listener module that subscribes to key topics (the topics such messages have been publishing: PredictedObjects, DetectedObjects, TrackedObjects, PointCloud2, Trajectory, AckermannControlCommand) to monitor and log reactions.
> 3. Design a measurement tool that calculates the time delay from obstacle-spawned time to the generation of a control command.
> 4. Incorporate a reporting mechanism to visualize and analyze the reaction times across different modules.
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] A simulation environment capable of spawning sudden obstacles is implemented.
> - [x] A module for subscribing and listening to the necessary topics is developed.
> - [x] The tool can accurately measure reaction times across Sensing, Perception, Planning, and Control pipelines.
> - [x] #7051
> - [x] Merge the PRs that solve the issue: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/6255
>     - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pull/4212
>     - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_internal_msgs/pull/1
>     - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6440
>     - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6490
> - [x] Merge the PRs to close this issue.
>     - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/886
>     - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6382
>     - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5954
> 

**Comments:**

###### @doganulus (2024-03-06)

> > create a test environment, listen to critical topics, and measure the system's reaction
> 
> It would be nice to write down these topics of interest, valid test conditions, and acceptable/unacceptable values from such measurements. For example,
> 
> - If the value in `/namespace/topic_name` is greater than `0`, then `/namespace/another_topic_name` will be greater than `5` within `10` milliseconds. 
> - Given `/namespace/topic_name` equals to `ENUM_VALUE` and  `/namespace/another_topic_name` is greater than `20`, then `/namespace/topic3` is always `true`.
> 
> What could be other things/constructs you find useful in writing such sentences for such analysis? 

###### @brkay54 (2024-03-06)

> Hi @doganulus thank you for the comment. Currently, we are working on merging this package. However, in the coming days, I am planning to add a detailed report on this issue or show and tell (TBD). 
> 
> Actually, in this report, I am planning to show 2 different kinds of tests for each node: 
> 
> - **1 - Default Time Consumption:** In this test, I am going to show the processing times of each message in each pipeline by using `published_time_publisher`.
> 
> - _For more information please see:_ #6255
> 
> This will show us how much time each node takes when it is executed. I am going to list the average calculation times of each node in the Sensing, Perception, and Planning pipelines.
> 
> - **2 - Reaction Response Time:** In this test, I will measure the reaction times when an obstacle is spawned suddenly in the Perception, Planning, and Control pipelines. 
> `Reaction Time = (published time of the first reacted message) - (spawn time of the object)`
> 
> **Here are the topics of interest for Reaction Response Time tests:**
> 
> - For Planning & Control pipeline:
> ```
>         obstacle_cruise_planner (or obstacle_stop_planner):

>         motion_velocity_smoother:

>         planning_validator:
>           topic_name: /planning/scenario_planning/trajectory
>           message_type: autoware_auto_planning_msgs/msg/Trajectory
>         trajectory_follower:
>           topic_name: /control/trajectory_follower/control_cmd
>           message_type: autoware_auto_control_msgs/msg/AckermannControlCommand
>         vehicle_cmd_gate:
>           topic_name: /control/command/control_cmd
>           message_type: autoware_auto_control_msgs/msg/AckermannControlCommand
> ```
> 
> - For Perception pipeline:

>         map_based_prediction:

> 
> These are the topics I am going to measure the reaction times. Please feel free to share any suggestions or comments with me!

### #6546 — Invalid path is generated when the point behind the vehicle is set as a goal

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-03-05  |  **Closed:** 2024-05-17  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:help-wanted, component:planning
- **Comments:** 13  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6546

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware version 20240115 with prebuilt docker on Carla, and I found that the invalid path is generated when the point behind the vehicle is set as a goal.
> 
> Here's the [[image]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ED0h6Jm6GpjTJBOwpXUBN0PlYLzFGXTB/view?usp=sharing) for the situation.
> I set the goal point as the point behind the vehicle after spawning the ego vehicle, but the vehicle cannot move even though the routing was successful(I could press the button "AUTO" in RViz)
> 
> I also checked the [[launch.log]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zQFXdQhkWdSrRVnavG-oFghdIQmjw97h/view?usp=sharing) file, and I could see the log below,
> ```
> 1709580193.0063493 [component_container-73] [motion_utils] calcLongitudinalOffsetToSegment: Longitudinal offset calculation is not supported for the same points. Return NaN since no_throw option is enabled. The maintainer must check the code.
> 1709580193.0078657 [component_container-73] [ERROR] [1709580193.007519306] [control.control_validator]: predicted_trajectory size is less than 2. Cannot validate.
> ```
> which states there's an error on calculating a longitudinal offset.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I want the vehicle to drive forward successfully to the goal point.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But the vehicle does not move at all.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Run Autoware of version [20240115, prebuilt docker](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe/167294357?tag=humble-20240115-prebuilt-cuda) with the maps here: [[lanelet2 map]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vm9SvalJe7Bc9sh_8jK-0cPulVAov5uD/view?usp=drive_link), [[pointcloud map]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MvJlfjkw3LWFUs5hdE_KQ2_CQTusU8UN/view?usp=drive_link)
> 2. Spawn ego vehicle, and set the goal point as a point behind the vehicle which is on the same lane.
> 
> Or here's a [ros2bag file](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RtaPGsjES0PuiNdmg2Tu30rgSXYPEU-C?usp=sharing) I recorded.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - Autoware: [20240115, prebuilt docker](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe/167294357?tag=humble-20240115-prebuilt-cuda)
> - Carla: 0.9.13
> - OS (host): Ubuntu 20.04
> - OS (docker): Ubuntu 22.04
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> According to the error message, I think the function related to the issue is this:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/7ef61a96008eafc466c315f01a889540335787f1/common/motion_utils/include/motion_utils/trajectory/trajectory.hpp#L401
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> I thought [this](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/5440) and [this](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/5976) could be the same issue, but current issue occurs after fixing the first one, and for the latter one, I think it is not related to the backward path.

**Comments:**

> 
> So.. may I close this issue for now?

###### @maxime-clem (2024-03-13)

>  I now understand the issue you are raising is for forward driving. In your example, we would expect Autoware to find a route to the goal by making the ego vehicle drive forward and "loop" back to the current lanelet.
> This is not currently supported but I think it is a reasonable feature request, so we can keep the issue open.

### #6539 — Consolidate MRM related nodes into a single node

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-03-04  |  **Closed:** 2024-05-28  |  **Author:** @veqcc
- **Labels:** type:improvement, component:system
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6539

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, Minimum Risk Maneuver (MRM) is implemented across multiple nodes like the following:
> (Pullover is a new feature still in Pull Request: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5634)
> ![Screenshot from 2024-03-04 14-51-23](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/26951562/33025510-95ab-4379-9a15-1f27c3df3fee)
> 
> You can refer to https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/1856 to see when these MRM functions are introduced in autoware.universe.
> 
> From a point of safety and performance, I suggest consolidating these five nodes into a single node.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> By consolidating these nodes, we aim to achive:
> - improving reliability: a low probability of MRM failures since redundant ROS 2 node/topic/service will be removed.
> - improving latency: a high performance of MRM behaviors on some emergency since:
>   - we do not have to wait the MRM operation response from each node, or wait a timeout of some behaviors
>   - we do not have to wait the topic/service to be scheduled by the ROS 2 executor
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Implement each operators (including pull_over_manager) as a class in MRM Handler nodes:
> ![Screenshot from 2024-03-04 15-13-12](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/26951562/cc48c82f-29d9-4d2f-bc02-5dfb2695f4e0)
> 
> If you want to add a new operator to MRM, just implementing a new class in MRM Handler is fine.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
>  - [ ] consolidate these nodes into a single node
> 

**Comments:**

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
>

> Hello @veqcc . Thanks for your effort. Is there any update related this issue.

> Hi, @meliketanrikulu, thank you for your reminder.
> 
> Actualy, there will be a interface change in `vehicle_cmd_gate` from @isamu-takagi in the near future.
> I will make some actions after that

###### @veqcc (2024-05-28)

> I will close it.

### #6534 — Autoware Evaluator Bug Report: Inappropriate Ego Car Behavior in Lane Changing and Collision Scenarios

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-03-02  |  **Closed:** 2024-06-05  |  **Author:** @hcn1519
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6534

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> While looking at various scenarios in Autoware Evaluator, I came across a couple of scenarios that Evaluator did not detect as errors but where the driving style seemed inappropriate in real driving situations.
> 
> ### 1. Unsafe Lane Changing
> 
> - [UC-A-04-00007_003_case01_cmn:1](https://evaluation.ci.tier4.jp/evaluation/reports/5d7d61b3-abf7-5970-b30d-35c606ddf1e7/tests/994883fb-ee00-5afe-ae34-f56f12a4d104/97ebaefb-10ed-516c-ac38-05d10edc3056/1e0dc139-f3cf-56c8-bc76-29af2009bd76?project_id=awf)
> 
> The original purpose of the scenario is to detect whether the ego car avoids obstacles well. And it achieves its goal. However, if you look closely at the ego car's behavior, you can see that it is driving along the lines of the lane too long. In this case, a more appropriate behavior for the ego car would be to completely change lanes when it detects an obstacle on the trajectory and then return to the original lane after moving away from the obstacle.
> 
> <img width="1136" alt="image" src="https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/13018877/a2819d5d-4554-41a5-b815-0c355957a4d5">
> 
> ### 2. Collision
> 
> - [UC-A-02-00003_PSim_1_case8_cmn:1](https://evaluation.ci.tier4.jp/evaluation/reports/5d7d61b3-abf7-5970-b30d-35c606ddf1e7/tests/7db0f3b8-a1c3-59dc-a7d1-7bddd1ee596b/a11152cc-f437-5de0-929d-d575384249f1/1ba36ebf-3f27-5385-bc48-fbcfb83fff60?project_id=awf)
> 
> This scenario is for detecting a collision, and `CollisionCondition` does not think ego car collides with another obstacle. However, this scenario should be perceived as a collision because the distance between the ego car and the obstacle is too close. When another car overtakes in front of the ego car while driving, if the distance between the ego car and the overtaking car gets too close, the ego car must slow down faster.
> 
> <img width="516" alt="Screenshot 2024-03-01 at 11 50 31ΓÇ»PM" src="https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/13018877/c3970ff7-2372-4e7e-9f08-5603ab57a9f2">
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> 1. Unsafe Lane Changing: Appropriate behavior for the ego car would be to completely change lanes when it detects an obstacle on the trajectory and then return to the original lane after moving away from the obstacle.
> 2. Collision: When another car overtakes in front of the ego car while driving, if the distance between the ego car and the overtaking car gets too close, the ego car must slow down faster.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> 1. Unsafe Lane Changing: ego car is driving along the lines of the lane too long.
> 2. Collision: Distance between the ego car and the obstacle is too close.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> You can replay the scenario if you have permission to access of the Autoware Evaluator.
> 
> 1. Unsafe Lane Changing: [UC-A-04-00007_003_case01_cmn:1](https://evaluation.ci.tier4.jp/evaluation/reports/5d7d61b3-abf7-5970-b30d-35c606ddf1e7/tests/994883fb-ee00-5afe-ae34-f56f12a4d104/97ebaefb-10ed-516c-ac38-05d10edc3056/1e0dc139-f3cf-56c8-bc76-29af2009bd76?project_id=awf)
> 2. Collision: [UC-A-02-00003_PSim_1_case8_cmn:1](https://evaluation.ci.tier4.jp/evaluation/reports/5d7d61b3-abf7-5970-b30d-35c606ddf1e7/tests/7db0f3b8-a1c3-59dc-a7d1-7bddd1ee596b/a11152cc-f437-5de0-929d-d575384249f1/1ba36ebf-3f27-5385-bc48-fbcfb83fff60?project_id=awf)
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @satoshi-ota (2024-03-28)

> Hi @hcn1519 Sorry for late response.
> 
> > The original purpose of the scenario is to detect whether the ego car avoids obstacles well. And it achieves its goal. However, if you look closely at the ego car's behavior, you can see that it is driving along the lines of the lane too long. In this case, a more appropriate behavior for the ego car would be to completely change lanes when it detects an obstacle on the trajectory and then return to the original lane after moving away from the obstacle.
> 
> For now, the lateral margin for UNKNOWN objects is set to 0.5m in [this](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/954145a38aeba3b7076f9006eedd34b1c76951f3/autoware_launch/config/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning/behavior_path_planner/avoidance/avoidance.param.yaml#L78-L81) yaml. So, if you want to make the ego behavior safer, please increase soft margin or hard margin. The module creates avoidance path so that the ego keeps the lateral distance `soft_margin + hard_margin`.
> 
> ```yaml
>         unknown:
> ...
>           lateral_margin:
>             soft_margin: 0.7                           # [m]
>             hard_margin: -0.2                          # [m]
>             hard_margin_for_parked_vehicle: -0.2       # [m]
> ...
> ```

###### @satoshi-ota (2024-03-28)

> > This scenario is for detecting a collision, and CollisionCondition does not think ego car collides with another obstacle. However, this scenario should be perceived as a collision because the distance between the ego car and the obstacle is too close. When another car overtakes in front of the ego car while driving, if the distance between the ego car and the overtaking car gets too close, the ego car must slow down faster.
> 
> May I ask which module did you use in motion, `obstacle_stop_planner` or `obstacle_cruise_planner`? The former one doesn't have cut-in detection feature, so I think it couldn't deal with such a scenario. On the other hand, the latter one can detect such kind of vehicle and decrease the speed faster (it works based on object recognition result). If possible, please change the module and see the behavior.

###### @yuntianyi-chen (2024-04-01)

> > Hi @hcn1519 Sorry for late response.
> > 
> > > The original purpose of the scenario is to detect whether the ego car avoids obstacles well. And it achieves its goal. However, if you look closely at the ego car's behavior, you can see that it is driving along the lines of the lane too long. In this case, a more appropriate behavior for the ego car would be to completely change lanes when it detects an obstacle on the trajectory and then return to the original lane after moving away from the obstacle.
> > 
> > For now, the lateral margin for UNKNOWN objects is set to 0.5m in [this](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/954145a38aeba3b7076f9006eedd34b1c76951f3/autoware_launch/config/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning/behavior_path_planner/avoidance/avoidance.param.yaml#L78-L81) yaml. So, if you want to make the ego behavior safer, please increase soft margin or hard margin. The module creates avoidance path so that the ego keeps the lateral distance `soft_margin + hard_margin`.
> > 
> > ```yaml
> >         unknown:
> > ...
> >           lateral_margin:
> >             soft_margin: 0.7                           # [m]
> >             hard_margin: -0.2                          # [m]
> >             hard_margin_for_parked_vehicle: -0.2       # [m]
> > ...
> > ```
> 
> The current scenario and condition are against traffic rules and safety concerns. Is this a kind of vulnerability or bug that could be improved (by changing the configurations) to enhance the safety and traffic-rule abidance in the future? @satoshi-ota 

###### @yuntianyi-chen (2024-04-03)

> > > This scenario is for detecting a collision, and CollisionCondition does not think ego car collides with another obstacle. However, this scenario should be perceived as a collision because the distance between the ego car and the obstacle is too close. When another car overtakes in front of the ego car while driving, if the distance between the ego car and the overtaking car gets too close, the ego car must slow down faster.
> > 
> > May I ask which module did you use in motion, `obstacle_stop_planner` or `obstacle_cruise_planner`? The former one doesn't have cut-in detection feature, so I think it couldn't deal with such a scenario. On the other hand, the latter one can detect such kind of vehicle and decrease the speed faster (it works based on object recognition result). If possible, please change the module and see the behavior.
> 
> `obstacle_stop_planner ` was used in this test. Since it doesn't have the cut-in detection feature and was used as the default `motion_stop_planner_type` in the Planning module, it would cause dangerous issues such as collision during an obstacle cut-in scenario. Could we regard this as a potential bug or weakness that could be improved? @satoshi-ota 

###### @satoshi-ota (2024-04-09)

> > Could we regard this as a potential bug or weakness that could be improved?
> 
> Yes. It is a weakness we should improve. And, actually we made it possible to detect cut-in and decelete properly based on perception result in `obstacle_cruise_planner`.

###### @satoshi-ota (2024-04-09)

> > The current scenario and condition are against traffic rules and safety concerns. Is this a kind of vulnerability or bug that could be improved (by changing the configurations) to enhance the safety and traffic-rule abidance in the future?
> 
> Yes. You can improve vehicle behavior by changing params. Please try to increase lateral margin params.

###### @yuntianyi-chen (2024-04-10)

> Thanks for your confirmation! @satoshi-ota

### #6515 — system_error_monitor is reporting diag_array msg timeout during rosbag replay simulation initialization

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2024-02-29  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @ahmeddesokyebrahim
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:system
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6515

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Part of:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/5539
> 
> Currently, we are working on a task for fixing and improving Autoware logging system as Autoware creates a noisy debugging environment, making it challenging to identify and address genuine issues.
> 
> For more details about the issue, plan how to tackle it, and linked PR, please have a look [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/5539).
> 
> For this bug, when starting [rosbag replay simulation](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/rosbag-replay-simulation/) and before replaying the rosbag, `system_error_monitor` is reporting `diag_array` msg timeout as follow : 
> 
> - ` [system_error_monitor-22] [ERROR 1708457713.178562834] [system.system_error_monitor]: diag_array msg is timeout... (isDataHeartbeatTimeout() at ~/autoware/src/universe/autoware.universe/system/system_error_monitor/src/system_error_monitor_core.cpp:420)`
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> `system_error_monitor` is reporting `diag_array` msg timeout when data is actually sent then timeout occurs or after countdown during initialization
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> `system_error_monitor` is directly reporting `diag_array` msg timeout during initialization
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start [rosbag replay simulation](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/rosbag-replay-simulation/#how-to-run-a-rosbag-replay-simulation)
> 2. Before replaying the sample rosbag, you can see the aforementioned error message.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> In the context of a similar [issue](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/6383), @xmfcx proposed the following :
> In real vehicle, this error message could be expected to be seen even when the topic is never received.
> 
> I have 2 proposals to address these:
> ##### 1. System Error Monitor Init Phase
> 
> Allow system_error_monitor node to have an initial countdown (user can set the seconds) and It won't report anything for this period. After it ends, it will publish as usual.
> 
> This period can be set to something like 10s for planning simulator maybe.
> ##### 2. Autoware RViz Side Panel Visualization
> 
> We could have this somehow shown as red in the future side panel for this topic.
> And once this error is gone, it would turn green for this message.
> 
> (This panel issue still hasn't been created so we can skip this solution for now.)
> 
> [Here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5971#discussion_r1486137110) is the full comment and context I am copying the proposal from for reference

**Comments:**

>

### #6494 — Remove the non-cuda build-and-test-differential job

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-02-26  |  **Closed:** 2024-02-28  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:ci
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6494

**Body:**

> ## Parent issue
> 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/4497
> 
> ## Current situation
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e7c354d5ad6b8d9f8d2f5e4e0862b0f32ca5ec4c/.github/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml#L23-L28
> 
> Everytime this job is triggered, it launches 2 jobs in parallel:
> - `build-and-test-differential (humble)`
> - `build-and-test-differential (humble, -cuda)`
> 
> Example:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/actions/runs/8042068924
> 
> ## Problem
> 
> Currently we are running all these on self hosted instances and they take too long.
> 
> ## Solution
> 
> I think we can get away with testing them with only the `-cuda` flag.
> 
> The test without CUDA is only useful for making sure **non-cuda packages don't depend on CUDA library.**
> 
> Let's remove the non-cuda tests from build-and-test-differential jobs. They will be tested in `build-and-test` jobs for each commit anyways.
> 
> What do you think @mitsudome-r @yukkysaito @miursh ?

**Comments:**

###### @xmfcx (2024-02-26)

> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/actions/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml?query=is%3Aqueued
> 
> The queue is too long once again and I am sad ≡ƒÿó .
> 
> This change would reduce the burden by half.
> 
> ![brave_XvLzIPglSd](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/10751153/c9e66e1b-afb9-482a-a5a0-f64c34b84daa)
>

### #6487 — Autoware sometimes drives over the velocity limit.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-02-26  |  **Closed:** 2024-03-26  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6487

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm running Autoware with Carla, and I found that **Autoware sometimes drives over the velocity limit**.
> Here are the video, `ros2bag` file and `launch.log` file for more details: [[rviz]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XlNFVRtcpxF_T2LXbnochsBYYpheeyDv/view?usp=sharing) [[ros2bag]](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xCU2oRWmpiVPYUQlHgLQjT7z06gNpaVl?usp=sharing) [[launch.log]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uD7feWHnc7yPO-XroQrhtcHdmdgblUX_/view?usp=sharing)
> 
> In the video, the `max_velocity` is set to `30 km/h`, but after the cornering, Autoware accelerates ignoring the velocity limit more than 10km/h.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I want Autoware to drive under the velocity limit.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But Autoware sometimes drives over the velocity limit.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Pull prebuilt Autoware docker image: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe/166911012?tag=humble-20240115-prebuilt-cuda-amd64
> 2. Run ros2bag file I provided above.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - Carla: 0.9.13
> - Autoware: [20240115 (prebuilt docker)](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe/166911012?tag=humble-20240115-prebuilt-cuda-amd64)
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @maxime-clem (2024-02-28)

> I will try to reproduce the issue when I get CARLA running. In the meantime I have the following questions:
> - Did you change the velocity limit somewhere or are you using the default parameters ?
> - What map are you using ?
> - Are you encountering this issue on a downward slope by any chance ?

###### @Kim-mins (2024-02-28)

> Thank you for the response @maxime-clem!!
> 
> I used the map `Town01` of Carla, and here's the maps for Autoware: [[lanelet2]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vm9SvalJe7Bc9sh_8jK-0cPulVAov5uD/view?usp=sharing), [[pointcloudmap]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MvJlfjkw3LWFUs5hdE_KQ2_CQTusU8UN/view?usp=sharing).
> 
> Actually, the map **does not contain any information for changing speed limit**, so I changed the velocity limit manually(if not changed, it is fixed to 72km/h), following [the information from Carla](https://carla.readthedocs.io/en/0.9.14/python_api/#getters_17), by publishing a message to `/planning/scenario_planning/max_velocity` (I'm considering the conversion between `km/h` and `m/s` too).
> 
> Also, `Town01` does not have any slope, and the roads are totally flat.
> 
> Thanks!

###### @maxime-clem (2024-03-26)

> @mraditya01 was not able to reproduce the issue when using the new CARLA interface he is working on.

###### @Kim-mins (2024-03-26)

> Maybe I should report it when I meet this issue later again.
> 
> By the way, does the bridge supports the latest version too?
> And will the bridge be merged into the main branch soon? How's your plan?
> 
> Thanks!

###### @maxime-clem (2024-03-26)

> Yes we are planning to merge it into universe as soon as possible, but we are having some issues with the latest Autoware version. Once we can support the latest Autoware we will open the PR for review (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6621).

###### @Kim-mins (2024-03-26)

> Thank you for the quick response @maxime-clem!
> 
> That's a really good news! I'm currently running a past version(20240115), so I always worried about bothering you since the found issues could be outdated.
> I hope the PR to be merged as soon as possible. I really look forward to it.
> 
> Thank you for spending time to this issue @maxime-clem @mraditya01! I'll reopen this issue when I find the same bug.
> 
> Thanks!

###### @gaoyelu1996 (2024-05-09)

> > Autoware requires Ubuntu 22.04 to function.
> > 
> > If you use Ubuntu 20.04, maybe the `galactic` branch might work for you but I don't know.

> Hello, thank you very much for your suggestion, but I installed it through Docker. I modified the nvidia driver from 535 to 545 and the error was resolved.

###### @matthew-rococo (2024-09-23)

> > > > Hello, may I ask if the problem has been resolved? I am currently facing the same problem as you.
> > > 
> > > 
> > > which nvidia driver are you using?
> > 
> > Hello, my computer configuration is as follows: Ubuntu20.04, 4060Ti, nvidia driver 535 I can't find the NVIDIA driver 545 version on my computer. Do you have any good methods to update the NVIDIA driver from 535 to 545?
> 
> 1. Update your system:
> ```
> sudo apt update
> sudo apt upgrade
> 
> ```
> 2.  Add the NVIDIA PPA
> ```
> sudo add-apt-repository ppa:graphics-drivers/ppa
> sudo apt update
> ```
> 3. Install the NVIDIA driver
> ```
> sudo apt install nvidia-driver-545
> 
> ```
> 
> 4. Reboot you system to apply the changes
> ```
> sudo reboot
> ```

### #6443 — Planned trajectory is not aligned with the vehicle's heading when the car is initialized at the intersection.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-02-18  |  **Closed:** 2024-05-13  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 11  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6443

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I found that, when the ego vehicle is initialized at the intersection, the generated trajectory is sometimes vertical to the ego vehicle.
> 
> Here's the [[rviz video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EcFTcsuj909TbDl5y5Tx3rnvkgm3kU27/view?usp=sharing)] and [[launch.log](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1wXLN8RjoIwsLoQXrsaMAgjJ8Q8NUXYgq/view?usp=sharing)] file.
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/50267797/31885269-c83c-4a3e-893f-ae05e0970ccd)
> 
> When I checked it several times, this does not occur every time, but sometimes.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I want the generated trajectory to be aligned with the ego vehicle's heading.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But the generated trajectory is not aligned.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> I ran the [[**planning simulation**](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/)] with the prebuilt docker, version [[20240201](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe/173888915?tag=humble-20240201-prebuilt-cuda-amd64)]
> Pointcloud map: [[link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VygpEdoqm22Zmx9CM9go4UgnEXBcU89J/view?usp=drive_link)]
> Lanelet2 map: [[link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sJPtpktjJorXPam7yZgCP2sfiMxW4kKQ/view?usp=drive_link)]
> 
> And I set the initial pose at the intersection, and set the goal point somewhere.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> I ran the planning simulation with the prebuilt docker, version [[20240201](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe/173888915?tag=humble-20240201-prebuilt-cuda-amd64)]
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> It seems the heading is not considered well for some positions of the intersection.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> I also searched for the similar issues, and I guess https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/6271 could be the similar one, that issue is regarding the `backward trajectory` though.

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2024-02-20)

> I think you face the same problem I face in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/6271#issuecomment-1920884945:
> 
> > Beside the backward trajectory which is really weird, I think there is a problem with the way `RouteHandler::planPathLaneletsBetweenCheckpoints` is implemented:
> > 
> > 1. find all lanelets containing ego pose. If the vehicle is on no lanelet, it looks for the closest lanelet instead (which feels a bit dangerous).
> > 2. find closest lanelet to goal pose.
> > 3. for each starting lanelet candidate, check if ego orientation is acceptable and try to generate a route the goal lanelet. Finally keep the route with the shortest length
> 
> In your case, the initial pose is located on 2 lanelets (the vehicle shape is ignored), so the route handler has to decide which one in correct. 
> 
> For 3, the hard coded yaw threshold is [90 degrees](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/c67bbe75dc7e2bad43aa8a75fe43d94c8f1c6f78/planning/route_handler/src/route_handler.cpp#L2138) (!!), so even a perpendicular lanelet like in your case may be included as candidate. Then, since the goal you have set is located on the right part of the map, the path passing by the perpendicular lanelet is likely shorter than the one passing by the correct lanelet. So eventually the route handler thinks the perpendicular lanelets is the correct one.
> 
> As I mentionned in the other issue, I think the starting lanelets (and goal lanelets?) should be classified into more categories. For example (from higher priority to lower):
> - vehicle fits in lanelet, angle diff is low (e.g. <30 deg)
> - vehicle does not fit in lanelet, but vehicle pose is in the lanelet, angle diff is low
> - vehicle pose is outside lanelet but close (e.g. ~2m), angle diff is high (<45)
> - vehicle pose is far or angle is high
> 
> I am not sure it is a good idea to generate generate a path in the last case.

###### @Kim-mins (2024-02-20)

> Thank you for clarifying the issue @VRichardJP!
> 
> I read your detailed description, and I agree that this issue is same with yours, because of the point 3.
> > 3. for each starting lanelet candidate, check if ego orientation is acceptable and try to generate a route the goal lanelet. Finally keep the route with the shortest length
> 
> And I think this issue can be resolved if the idea you suggested could be applied. So I'll close this issue soon.
> 
> Thank you!

###### @VRichardJP (2024-02-20)

> I would rather leave this issue open. The problem is worth fixing and your issue highlights it better than https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/6271 (which focuses on a different problem.)
> 
> As a temporary fix, you could reduce this value https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/c67bbe75dc7e2bad43aa8a75fe43d94c8f1c6f78/planning/route_handler/src/route_handler.cpp#L2138.
> 

###### @Kim-mins (2024-02-20)

> Thank you for reopening, and your patch suggestion!
> 
> Your patch seems to reduces yaw threshold and I think it would work! I'll try it.
> 
> And I'll check your issue too in my spare time, so that I can sync this issue with yours.
> 
> Thanks!

### #6421 — (mpc_lateral_controller) is_converged gets false after manual driving

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-02-15  |  **Closed:** 2024-03-06  |  **Author:** @TomoyukiaW
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6421

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I'm working with Autoware v1.0. After we drive the vehicle manually, sometimes is_converged in mpc_lateral_controller.cpp gets false, trajectory_follower is staying in stopping state. I feel it's often happened after we drive backward with moving steering (meandering backward). I dumped cmd.steering_tire_angle and  m_current_steering.steering_tire_angle with the following debug print.
> ```bash
> mpc_lateral_controller.cpp: L308
> bool MpcLateralController::isSteerConverged(const AckermannLateralCommand & cmd) const
> {
>   // wait for a while to propagate the trajectory shape to the output command when the trajectory
>   // shape is changed.
>   if (!m_has_received_first_trajectory || isTrajectoryShapeChanged()) {
>     RCLCPP_DEBUG(logger_, "trajectory shaped is changed");
>     return false;
>   }
> 
>   const bool is_converged =
>     std::abs(cmd.steering_tire_angle - m_current_steering.steering_tire_angle) <
>     static_cast<float>(m_converged_steer_rad);
> 
>   {
>     RCLCPP_INFO_THROTTLE(logger_, *clock_, 1000, "cmd_tire_angle=%lf cur_tire_andle=%lf diff=%lf",
>       cmd.steering_tire_angle, m_current_steering.steering_tire_angle,
>       std::abs(cmd.steering_tire_angle - m_current_steering.steering_tire_angle));
>   }
> 
>   return is_converged;
> }
> ```
> ![Screenshot from 2024-02-15 10-16-17](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/91722851/8e7be8d3-a927-44cb-976a-32ce9e8a2700)
> In this log, diff is 0.239239 grater than 0.1.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> After the manual driving and when we start auto operation, is_converged should be true.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Sometimes  is_converged gets false.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. After the auto operation in some path, set autoware control disabled in AutowareStatePanel.
> 2. Drive backward with moving steering.
> 3. Set autoware control enabled, operation mode auto in AutowareStatePanel.
>    ->autoware control gets enabled,  operation mode gets Auto. But the vehicle doesn't move. The console output the log, "target speed > 0, but keep stop condition is met. Keep STOPPED."
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS2
> - Autoware v1.0
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Should we reset m_ctrl_cmd_prev as well as MPC state like the following? In my debugging, sometimes only is_mpc_solved couldn't be detected the above situation, so I added OperationModeState::LOCAL and OperationModeState::REMOTE states conditions to reset in this condition. (Semantically, using autoware control = disabled is better, but it is not passed to mpc_lateral_controller.cpp.)
> ```bash
> mpc_lateral_controller.cpp: L254
>   // reset previous MPC result
>   // Note: When a large deviation from the trajectory occurs, the optimization stops and
>   // the vehicle will return to the path by re-planning the trajectory or external operation.
>   // After the recovery, the previous value of the optimization may deviate greatly from
>   // the actual steer angle, and it may make the optimization result unstable.
>   if (!is_mpc_solved || 
>       input_data.current_operation_mode.mode == autoware_adapi_v1_msgs::msg::OperationModeState::LOCAL ||
>       input_data.current_operation_mode.mode == autoware_adapi_v1_msgs::msg::OperationModeState::REMOTE) {
>     m_mpc.resetPrevResult(m_current_steering);
>     m_ctrl_cmd_prev = getInitialControlCommand();
>   } else {
>     setSteeringToHistory(ctrl_cmd);
>   }
> ```
> 
> ### Additional context
>

### #6419 — Add packages for providing stable interfaces

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2024-02-15  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @isamu-takagi
- **Labels:** type:improvement, status:stale
- **Comments:** 9  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6419

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Add interface class. See https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3922 for background.
> 
> ![universe-6419-interface-adaptor](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/43976882/47f7d542-afae-4764-bb81-7d40ffd94755)
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Autoware uses ROS messages for the following two purposes, so we will make it possible to separate them.
> - interface
> - data transfer implementation
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Add type alias and interface class. Developers can use interface classes instead of ROS messages with the following changes. 
> 
> ```diff
> - rclcpp::Subscription<std_msgs::msg::Header>::SharedPtr sub_;
> - rclcpp::Publisher<std_msgs::msg::Header>::SharedPtr pub_;
> + rclcpp::Subscription<interface_pkg::time_stamp::RosType>::SharedPtr sub_;
> + rclcpp::Publisher<interface_pkg::time_stamp::RosType>::SharedPtr pub_;
> 
> - void callback(const std_msgs::msg::Header & msg)
> - {
> -   rclcpp::Time stamp = msg.header.stamp;
> - }
> + void callback(const interface_pkg::time_stamp::RosType & msg)
> + {
> +   interface_pkg::time_stamp::Interface interface(msg);
> +   rclcpp::Time stamp = interface.get_stamp();
> + }
> 
> - void on_timer()
> - {
> -   std_msgs::msg::Header msg;
> -   msg.header.stamp = now();
> -   pub_->publish(msg);
> - }
> + void on_timer()
> + {
> +   interface_pkg::time_stamp::Interface interface;
> +   interface.set_stamp(now());
> +   pub_->publish(interface.to_msg());
> + }
> ```
> 
> 
> The interface class has a pointer or reference to ROS message.
> 
> ```cpp
> using RosType = std_msgs::msg::Header;
> 
> Class Interface
> {
> public:
>    Interface(RosType & msg) : msg_(msg) {}
>    void set_stamp(rclcpp::Time stamp) { msg_.header.stamp = stamp; }
>    rclcpp::Time get_stamp() { return msg_.header.stamp; }
> 
> private:
>   RosType & msg_;
> };
> ```
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Add rclcpp wrapper library.
> - [ ] Add rclpy wrapper library.
> - [ ] Merge and remove `component_interface_utils` package.
> - [ ] Merge and remove `tier4_api_utils` package.

**Comments:**

###### @doganulus (2024-02-15)

> Hi @isamu-takagi, I am interested in this proposal as a third-party verification tool developer, which needs a well-defined interface specification for Autoware and simulators.  
> 
> Would this proposal include a machine-readable declarative specification format for interfaces? Is there any pointer for any work done in that direction? 
> 
> Do you prefer this issue for further discussion or the original discussion thread?

###### @isamu-takagi (2024-02-16)

> @doganulus Are you talking about a file listing topics and services such as following? If so, that is not the goal of this task. But I want that too, so let's create a new discussion.
> 
> ```yaml
> { type: subscription, name: /diagnostics }
> { type: publisher, name: /diagnostics_agg }
> ```

###### @doganulus (2024-02-16)

> Yes @isamu-takagi, such a file is what I meant. I thought it may be used for a config for third-party tools that interact with Autoware. I have a few technical concerns, like how to address dynamic topic names and the overhead in this case. But maybe your proposal will allow us to see better the landscape. 
> 
> Finally, in the current form, you do require a third-party client tool to use `rclcpp` to communicate with Autoware and get the benefits in this proposal? Can a DDS client based on corresponding IDLs be equally good or not?

###### @isamu-takagi (2024-02-16)

> > Finally, in the current form, you do require a third-party client tool to use rclcpp to communicate with Autoware and get the benefits in this proposal?
> 
> @doganulus I've added a diagram about the implementation to this task description. As shown in the diagram, to use versioned message you need to use the wrapper class that will be added in this task.
> 
> > Can a DDS client based on corresponding IDLs be equally good or not?
> 
> I don't think it can provide the same functionality. The problem is that ROS topics and services only have one layer of data structures. This means that when the data structure is changed due to implementation reasons, the interface is also affected. So at least two data structures are required: an implementation and an interface.
> 
> It may be possible if you can customize serialization and deserialization of DDS client, but it would be difficult.
> 

###### @doganulus (2024-02-17)

> I cannot say for sure without measuring but the overhead of all these conversions seems to be the weakest point of the proposal. Maybe your example implementation can give any hint on how serious it could be. Have you considered publishing twice for old and new interfaces? (this has the overhead of bandwidth but is limited to the transition period.)
> 
> Ok I see this: https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3922#discussioncomment-7325535
> 
> Double publishing is really prohibitive?

###### @isamu-takagi (2024-02-20)

> I think there are some mixed issues about messages, so I will create a thread in the original discussion to organize it.

###### @isamu-takagi (2024-03-23)

> @doganulus  I considered it again here https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3922#discussioncomment-8886781. In conclusion, it seems better to provide an accessor class. This method is simpler and does not require copying the message.
> 
> I will create a new discussion about interface definition files later.
> 

###### @doganulus (2024-03-23)

> @isamu-takagi Thank you very much for letting me know!
> 
> For interface definitions files, I have something in my mind similar to Zenoh's use of configuration files as here:
> https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh-plugin-dds/blob/2cd1424c1b15d1bf730b01c0c9110a3031dd5119/DEFAULT_CONFIG.json5#L44C1-L67C38
> 
> I like to configure our apps to listen to some specific subset of Autoware topics (possibly determined dynamically) so having stable interfaces is quite important.

### #6401 — feat(pointcloud_preprocessor): add crop box filter feature to handle multiple cropboxes and specific frame inputs

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-02-14  |  **Closed:** 2024-05-31  |  **Author:** @YoshiRi
- **Labels:** type:improvement, status:stale
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6401

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Add new crop box feature to 
> 
> - handle multiple cropboxes
> - enable to  choose cropbox frame
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> 
> 
> Currently in some settings, we use crop box filter muiltiple times to filter vehicle body and mirror reflections. Fro example:
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/20086766/0b09ec74-9d31-448f-b4e8-4bca7b9f3e0d)
> 
> This will increase computation burden due to
> 
> - publishing unnecessary pointcloud
> - multiple times inspection for each point
> 
> So I think its better to assign cropbox parameter at once and do not duplicate crop box filter subsequently.
> 
> The other suggestion is; 
> Since current crop box filter is processed in input_frame and crop box is often given in base_link or map frame, we can not filter other frame pointclouds.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - add new node to handle multiple cropboxes
> - add cropbox frame parameters to control in which coordinate the input pointclouds should be filtered.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Merge each feature PR

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2024-02-15)

> How does this perform against cascaded crop box filters?
> 
> If I understand correctly, this feature would do the same than cascaded filters, but without the intra process communication (which is supposedly fast). Is intra process delay that big?

###### @YoshiRi (2024-02-19)

> @VRichardJP 
> 
> > Is intra process delay that big?
> 
> Hmm, It seems not so much(~10ms). 
> In some projects, we confront of CPU resources problems so that it cause unintended system behavior.
> 
> So I wanted to 
> - reduce unnecessary communication
> - reduce process delay by doing same filtering and coordinate transformation
>

### #6392 — gnss_poser: Incorrect transform direction between NavSatFix frame and  gnss_base_link

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-02-13  |  **Closed:** 2024-02-13  |  **Author:** @FranzAlbers
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6392

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hello @YamatoAndo, @kminoda, @meliketanrikulu,
> first of all, thanks for working on this awesome project!
> 
> I would like to reopen issue #3640 because I think the associated PR #5033 introduced the problem it claimed to solve. The direction of the transform between the NavSatFix Frame and `gnss_base_link` was correct before and incorrect after the PR.
> 
> We noticed this bug when our RTK-DGNSS-equipped vehicle recently started having a height and a longitudinal offset between the gnss_base_link published by the gnss_poser and our point cloud and lanelet2 maps, while both the RTK-DGNSS and our maps provide ground-truth quality with at most a few centimeters offset. Before PR #5033, the RTK-DGNSS pose perfectly fitted the map and approximately matched the NDT/EKF pose.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Our NavSatFix is given in the `adma/imu_link` frame, NOT in the `adma/gnss_link.` 
> 
> The image below shows the expected behavior (PR #5033 reverted): `gnss_base_link`  is transformed from `adma/imu_link` in the correct direction and coincides with the `base_link` / `ndt_base_link` frame.
> 
> ![Bild3](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/20774470/a5272edf-4f3d-4d59-993c-53f5b65e4b2c)
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The image below shows the current behavior with `gnss_base_link` being transformed from the `adma/imu_link` in the wrong direction exactly by the transformation from `base_link` to the `adma/imu_link`. Note, that `map`->`base_link`  is estimated by the NDT/EKF localization here to show the issue more clearly (unlike in the left image in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3640#issuecomment-1927752884 where `map`->`base_link` is estimated by the `gnss_poser`, resulting in a floating vehicle).
> 
> ![Bild4](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/20774470/4976dad7-322d-4a35-b6fe-a7a75fb9972a)
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> I've tried to reproduce this with the autoware sample rosbag and the logging simulator, but the gnss_poser pose from the NavSatFix was located around 45 meters above the base_link, so I think this is not precise enough for seeing differences of less than 1m in the pose. 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS2 Humble
> - Autoware container: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe/173838572?tag=humble-20240201-cuda-amd64
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The `source_frame` and `target_frame` in lookupTransform() are often confused, because the transformation of data between the frames and the transformation of the frames themselves are inverse. If the same `source_frame` and `target_frame` are used with lookupTransform and tf2_echo, we obtain inverse transformations (https://github.com/ros/geometry/issues/108#issuecomment-150319158).
> 
> In this case, we intend to use the transform between the frames, so we should use the inverse of what lookupTransform gives us, since lookupTransform returns the transformation for the data, not the frame itself (as tf2_echo does). This was the case before PR #5033, so I propose to revert it (though I agree that the corrected comment in that PR was correct).
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @idorobotics (2024-02-13)

> The issue  https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3640 is re-opened as requested. Feel free to link your PR after discussing your solution in the comments. To avoid duplicates, I'll close this issue.

### #6383 — system_error_monitor is reporting vehicle_state_report msg timeout during planning simulation initialization

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2024-02-12  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @ahmeddesokyebrahim
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:system
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6383

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Part of:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/5539
> 
> Currently, we are working on a task for fixing and improving Autoware logging system as Autoware creates a noisy debugging environment, making it challenging to identify and address genuine issues.
> 
> For more details about the issue, plan how to tackle it, and linked PR, please have a look [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/5539).
> 
> For this bug, when starting planning simulator and before setting vehicle start and goal pose, `system_error_monitor` is reporting `vehicle_state_report` msg timeout as follow : 
> 
> - ` [system.system_error_monitor]: vehicle_state_report msg is timeout... (isDataHeartbeatTimeout() at ~/autoware/src/universe/autoware.universe/system/system_error_monitor/src/system_error_monitor_core.cpp:436)`
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> `system_error_monitor` is reporting `vehicle_state_report` msg timeout when data is actually sent then timeout occurs or after countdown during initialization
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> `system_error_monitor` is directly reporting `vehicle_state_report` msg timeout during initialization
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Open planning simulator
> 2. Before setting vehicle start pose and goal pose you can see the aforementioned error message.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> @xmfcx proposed the following :
> In real vehicle, this error message could be expected to be seen even when the topic is never received.
> 
> I have 2 proposals to address these:
> ##### 1. System Error Monitor Init Phase
> 
> Allow system_error_monitor node to have an initial countdown (user can set the seconds) and It won't report anything for this period. After it ends, it will publish as usual.
> 
> This period can be set to something like 10s for planning simulator maybe.
> ##### 2. Autoware RViz Side Panel Visualization
> 
> We could have this somehow shown as red in the future side panel for this topic.
> And once this error is gone, it would turn green for this message.
> 
> (This panel issue still hasn't been created so we can skip this solution for now.)
> 
> [Here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5971#discussion_r1486137110) is the full comment and context I am copying the proposal from for reference

### #6373 — tracking_object_merger continues to publish old detected object when the number of detected objects are zero

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-02-09  |  **Closed:** 2024-02-13  |  **Author:** @brkay54
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:perception
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/6373

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> While testing the perception pipeline, I faced a weird behavior. If the detected_objects is empty, the perception pipeline continues to publish old detected objects all the time.
> 
> In my test, I am publishing the lidars pointclouds to the pipeline. There are 2 different pointcloud messages: empty area pointcloud (pointcloud A) and pointcloud with an object in front of the ego (pointcloud B).
> 
> In the test, I started to publish pointcloud A to the perception pipeline and I can see there are no detected, predicted, or tracking objects. After a while, I started to publish pointcloud B and we saw the detected and predicted objects in the topics.
> 
> After that, I started to publish pointcloud A again, concat pointcloud was changed, and I can't see any objects in DetectedObjects topics, however, PredictedObjects is still publishing the old object.
> 
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/c8b01da4-0a30-4ffe-85da-8ea629433f5b
> 
> As you can see in the video above, when we published pointcloud A after pointcloud B, the Predicted Object was not removed.
> 
> After some investigation, I realized `tracking_object_merger` is publishing the old detected objects although there are no detected objects in the pipeline.
> 
> In [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/perception/tracking_object_merger/src/decorative_tracker_merger.cpp#L253-L255), if there are no detected_objects, it returns false without any operation and it continues to publish the old object. Therefore, `map_based_prediction` continues to publish an object.
> 
> After I removed the protection of the empty objects, it worked as we wanted as shown below:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/66d27a6d-7cfa-4e8c-952f-4d90c36c2a43
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> It should publish empty objects after detected objects are removed.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> It continues to publish the old detected object as a tracking object although it was removed.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> -
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @YoshiRi (2024-02-11)

> Thanks for your report. This issue is related with tracklet management problem.
> 
> ### About quick fix
> 
> > After I removed the protection of the empty objects, it worked as we wanted as shown below:
> 
> I agree the short-term solution mentioned above. By removing the following section, we can update the survival probability even if the main topic is empty. This change requires minimal code modifications and should suffice as a solution for the current issue.
> 
> ```cpp
> if (main_topic_objects->objects.empty())
> {
>   return false;
> }
> ```
> 
> ### Additional solution
> Ideally, a sanity check of the tracklets should be performed before issuing an object, ensuring a more comprehensive management of tracklet survival without omissions.
> 
> Fortunately, there is a parameter named `max_dt`, which can be utilized to manage the survival of tracklets before publishing. I will add code for this purpose as a precaution.
> 
> I will try to add some sanitizer around following part:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/1121f3b2a5a298ac474835522b97e84d9301dd9a/perception/tracking_object_merger/src/utils/tracker_state.cpp#L274
> 
> 
> ### About future solution
> 
> There's a fundamental issue with entrusting the update() function with tracklet survival management, which should be re-evaluated in the long term. Currently, the survival management of tracklets directly manipulates the existence_probability, which may not be ideal as the number of topics to merge increases, requiring changes to this value each time.
> 
> A less disruptive proposal involves not directly manipulating the existence_probability. Instead, for survival management, the last_updated_time could be referenced to determine survival or demise based on a decayed value.
> 
> I've shared my thoughts, but I'm open to any opinions you might have.

###### @YoshiRi (2024-02-13)

> @brkay54 Hi, could you test this [PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6386) when you have time?

###### @YoshiRi (2024-02-13)

> Thanks for your quick response! :+1:

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2024-02-07  |  **Closed:** 2025-09-24  |  **Author:** @ktro2828

> 
> ### Description
> 
> Integrate ML-based motion prediction to the Autoware perception stack to improve the reliability and accuracy of the predicted paths.
> 
> Current rule-based prediction can only estimate paths aligned to the center line of the road for vehicles or straight paths for other traffic participants (e.g. pedestrian, cyclists).
> 
> ML-based module allow us to predict their future behaviors by considering observed state and their interactions.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To improve accuracy, adaptability and be able to handle uncertanity of future behaviors of traffic participants.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Now we are trying to integrate MTR(Motion TRnsformer), which achieved the 1st place for the motion prediction task in 2022 Waymo Open Dataset Challege.
> - Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.13508
> - Original repo: https://github.com/sshaoshuai/MTR
>

> - Implementation to Autoware
