### #5964 — [motion_velocity_smoother] steer rate calculation looks wrong

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-12-26  |  **Closed:** 2024-02-20  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:help-wanted, component:planning
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5964

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Here:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/2edd55e4f54ec8d0ce92909082049c7f19ee40a9/planning/motion_velocity_smoother/src/smoother/smoother_base.cpp#L218-L235
> 
> we go through trajectory points with a sliding window of 2 points. There are few issues with this loop:
> 
> - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5989 loop does not start at 0 but 1. I don't think it is necessary
> - [ ] (minor?) `front_wheel_angle_rad` values are calculated twice, once with `i+1` and on the next loop with `i`. The loop does 2 things at the same time: calculating `front_wheel_angle_rad` values and `steer_rate`. Duplicated computation could be avoiding by spliting the loop into 2.
> - [x] https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5965 "front" values are for index `i+1` and "back" values are for index `i`, however for the `atan` lines the calculation looks reversed:
> 
> ```c++
>     steer_front = std::atan(base_param_.wheel_base * curvature_v.at(i));
>     steer_back = std::atan(base_param_.wheel_base * curvature_v.at(i + 1));
> ```
> 
> I guess it should be:
> 
> ```c++
>     steer_front = std::atan(base_param_.wheel_base * curvature_v.at(i + 1));
>     steer_back = std::atan(base_param_.wheel_base * curvature_v.at(i));
> ```
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @rej55 (2023-12-26)

> @VRichardJP 
> 
> Thank you for your information.
> I agree it should be fixed.
> I will approve the PR.
> 
> However, the behavior of code is not changed because
> ```
>     const auto steering_diff = std::fabs(steer_front - steer_back);
> ```
> is not changed whether or not change the `atan` calculation.

###### @VRichardJP (2023-12-26)

> Yes, however the PR shifts `front_wheel_angle_rad` by 1 point backward, so this may have a little impact on Autoware turning behavior (if the value is used to compute steering).

###### @VRichardJP (2023-12-28)

> Edit: I still get the issue with the fix, so it may not be the root cause.
> 
> Regarding the loop starting at 1 instead of 0, I think this is the cause of one of the issues I am facing with the freespace planner. When the vehicle is stopped half way in a turning manoeuver, Autoware sometimes refuse to restart the vehicle. The PID longitudinal controller reports this error: [`target speed > 0, but keep stop condition is met. Keep STOPPED.`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/3b0c2542cb0d3aada933e4b5cd2ec5c5313d64f6/control/pid_longitudinal_controller/src/pid_longitudinal_controller.cpp#L629). The stop condition is met because `lateral_sync_data_.is_steer_converged` is `false` and I guess this is because the current steering is far from the target steering of the trajectory (which is 0.0 because not updated by the `motion_velocity_smoother`).
> 
> For example, here is one trajectory calculated by `motion_velocity_smoother` while the vehicle is stopped with the steering wheel turned:
> ```
> header:
>   stamp:
>     sec: 1703740309
>     nanosec: 80912131
>   frame_id: map
> points:
> - time_from_start:
>     sec: 0
>     nanosec: 0
>   pose:
>     position:
>       x: 3738.7482156691976
>       y: 73759.76434660016
>       z: 0.0
>     orientation:
>       x: 0.0
>       y: 0.0
>       z: -0.36787980716724306
>       w: 0.9298733502357146
>   longitudinal_velocity_mps: 0.25
>   lateral_velocity_mps: 0.0
>   acceleration_mps2: 0.10000000149011612
>   heading_rate_rps: 0.060412731021642685
>   front_wheel_angle_rad: 0.0
>   rear_wheel_angle_rad: 0.0
> - time_from_start:
>     sec: 0
>     nanosec: 325953602
>   pose:
>     position:
>       x: 3738.821148558692
>       y: 73759.6959302744
>       z: 0.0
>     orientation:
>       x: 0.0
>       y: 0.0
>       z: -0.35793588138765237
>       w: 0.9337461672292126
>   longitudinal_velocity_mps: 0.28722813725471497
>   lateral_velocity_mps: 0.0
>   acceleration_mps2: 0.37421149015426636
>   heading_rate_rps: 0.11836133897304535
>   front_wheel_angle_rad: 0.500284731388092
>   rear_wheel_angle_rad: 0.0
> ---
> [...]
> ```
> 
> As you can see, the first point `front_wheel_angle_rad` is 0.0, while other points have a valid value.
> 
> This problem may be limited to the planning simulator, as the simulator seems not able to turn the steering in place.
> 
> Anyway, I think it is better not to miss the first point `front_wheel_angle_rad` value.

### #5959 — Feature: Remove Autoware limitations about map boundaries

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-12-25  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @ataparlar
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:map
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5959

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Provide a Dynamic Lanelet2 map loader. (Problem detail below)
> 
> 
> # Autoware Projections
> Autoware has a limitation for map boundaries. Map Projection Loader modules can work for MGRS, Local Cartesian UTM and Transverse Mercator projections. MGRS Projection works inside of the 100km x 100km MGRS grids. Local Cartesian UTM works inside of a UTM zone. Transverse Mercator does not have a limitation.
> Problems are detected via a lanelet2 map generated via Python script that uses CommonRoad API between Istanbul and Ankara in Turkey. The road lenght is approximately 600km. 
> ![Screenshot from 2023-12-25 15-23-31](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44242212/235855f3-0288-41a5-a43f-bade2aea147d)
> 
> ## Problems with Available Projections
> ###  MGRS
> The 100km x 100km MGRS grid visualization can be found below. The road overlays more than 1 MGRS grid and the nodes and line segments reaches out the other MGRS grids than the main one keep being inside in the main MGRS grid. So, the 600km road is stuck inside of the main MGRS grid. It seems like the line segments are bouncing from the edges of the main grid. The image related to that problem can be found below.
> ![Screenshot from 2023-12-25 15-20-39](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44242212/19308986-f6a7-4700-a758-2a2245cea57a)
> ![Screenshot from 2023-12-07 13-14-14](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44242212/dbe9eb69-7759-405f-93c5-5df16bba060b)
> 
> 
> ### LocalCartesianUTM
> Same situation is valid for Local Cartesian UTM projection. Only difference is the map boundaries. Map boundaries here is not 100km x 100km MG
> ![Screenshot from 2023-12-25 15-35-35](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44242212/568699f1-c2fc-4f16-a58f-634d93465f6b)
> RS grids, they are the UTM zone grids. So, this projection involves much area than MGRS projection but still it is insufficient for long routes. UTM projection visualization on the same road and the same error can be seen below.
> ![Screenshot from 2023-12-07 13-13-53](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44242212/ed85a63f-28cc-4893-a1b8-6f92461a01e9)
> 
> 
> ### TransverseMercator
> Transverse Mercator projection hasn't any boundary limitations. Additionally, we are able to load all the roads into the Autoware and visualize it in RViz2 with Planning Simulator or Logging Simulator. However, when we get away from the origin of the lanelet2 map, the line segments, TF markers, 2D Pose Estimate or 2D Goal Pose arrows start to corrupt because of the large numbers. This very looks like a floating point error. RViz2 screenshot can be seen in below GIF. Another issue with Transverse Mercator is corruptions in the map while getting away from the origin. In far places, the map loses its correctness due to the projection surface.
> ![2023-12-25 15-59-32](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44242212/0b2215f4-bc28-42a8-949e-cbe14db9990c)
> 
> Additionally, due to the large numbers of coordinates and 123 MB lanelet2(.osm) file makes the system very heavy. While this GIF is recording, nearly 20 GBs of RAM is used from the computer by Autoware Planning Simulator.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Autoware needs to be compatible with long range drivable lanelet2 maps. While doing that, RAM usage must be kept low.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> ## Dynamic Lanelet2 Map Loading
> Autoware can load point cloud maps dynamicly. This provides better physical component usage for PCs and accelerates the whole Autoware due to the light system. Same situation is valid for Lanelet2 Maps. Error determination tests are implemented with 600 km road overlays different projection zones. Observed that, only Transverse Mercator project is available to use all the map at once but it has floating point problem and loses correctness while getting away from the origin. 
> 
> MGRS and LocalCartesianUTM works in a boundary and they preserves their sufficient accuracy in the boundary. So, for keep getting sufficient accuracy from the map and for keeping the map outsourcing lower, Lanalet2 Maps can loaded dynamicly as the car moves. As a matter of fact, 10 or 5 km MGRS grids can be used for dynamicly loading and this will provide more compatible position data generation with the real world.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - Autoware loads and uses Lanelet2 maps overlays large areas. 
> - Maps does not uses too much source from the computer.
> - Observing no corruption while getting away from the origin.

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-12-27)

> Looks very complicated. Just a random idea:
> - split the lanelet map into N lanelet maps (~MGRS size), each with its own local projection (referred by frame "mapXX").
> - "local" lanelets maps should overlap to have smooth transition from one to the next (similar to dynamic PCD loading).
> - A global server tracks vehicle pose and broadcast the current "mapXX" frame to use. Since all frames are fixed and known on startup, it is not a problem if some nodes use different map frame during transition phases (as long as they carefully check and transform each data).
> - Obviously, it means all node currently using hardcoded "map" frame must be updated.
> - A new global planner must be implemented as the global path from start to goal cannot be known anymore. For this, we could preprocess each "local" lanelet map into a graph saying which lanelet id at the edge of the "local" map can reach which other lanelet id at the edge. The actual local path would only be computed once the vehicle reach the local map.

###### @ataparlar (2023-12-27)

> # Dynamic Lanelet2 Map Loading
> This concept is found necessary for using Autoware in large areas. The main idea is changing the loaded map area while the body is moving. To do that, MGRS grids can be used. Because MGRS grids enables to use the squares of 100km, 10km and 1km areas. We think that 1km MGRS grids will be ok to use. In that way, planning modules can work easily and all the pipeline would use lower amount time towards to larger areas. Here is a demonstration of the idea with a GIF below.
> ![dynamic-lanelet2-map-loader-legend](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44242212/e2e33f55-068c-4812-b531-f8388b4f161a)
> 
> # Editing Planning Pipeline According to Map Loading
> With dynamicly loaded Lanelet2 maps, a problem is occuring. In large areas, we are not able to give a goal point with this planning implementation. Because the lanelet of the goal point could not be known with dynamicly loaded small Lanelet2 maps. 
> 
> This situation can be solved with the suggestion made by @VRichardJP, which is using a graph structure to calculate the route with a full Lanelet2 map. This can work I think but this means one or several new package with various new nodes needed to be written and tested. This will cost too much time and too much energy to implement in my opinion. Additionally, I cannot guess the computational cost and how would be the performance in this stage. Still this can be the solution. Thank you for your sharings @VRichardJP. 
> 
> Another solution can be using a different global planner with implementing it in the Autoware planning pipeline. This solution makes similar approximations with @xmfcx 's thoughts in [another discussion about planning performence in large areas](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/4075#discussioncomment-7946961) from @StepTurtle. We planned to use a global planner for large areas before giving a goal point. In this way, we can know which roads will be used in the route. Additionally, we got a planned route as a linestring and we can use it with planning pipeline. 
> 
> The main idea here is taking the global planned route and giving goal points in each 1.5 or 2 kilometers to planning pipeline (Goal point can change according to the grid size will be used in Dynamic Lanelet2 Map Loading). Planning works fine in small environments has overall 1 kilometer radius. In that point of view, if we use goal points in a limited length and dynamicly changes the goal points along the globally planned route, it should work. Here is a demonstration of the general plan below.
> ![road_divide](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44242212/185208ce-e5cd-4a98-81d6-25e512a688bc)
> 
> Due to the complexity of the issue, we would like to discuss this before implement anything. Any comment or ideas would be great. @xmfcx @mitsudome-r 
> 
> 

###### @ataparlar (2024-01-08)

> @xmfcx @mitsudome-r 
> We can use this issue for only Dynamic Lanelet2 Map Loading and open another issue for route planning if needed. Also those already exist for route planning for large areas:
> - #5940 
> - [Investigation on using Large Scale Lanelet2 Map in Autoware | Planning Simulator #4075](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/4075)
> 

###### @ataparlar (2024-01-15)

> Using an external planner is not planned right now. The main aim is using mission_planner for large areas too. mission_planner can plan a route even in very long routes as can be seen in [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0-z-yjgJaNA). 
> 
> The main goal right now, using mission_planner with Dynamic Lanelet2 Loading. We are aiming it to use in MGRS projection for reaching the lowest projection corruption. However, MGRS projection has a limitation in a 100km x 100km MGRS grid. Besides that being a limitation, it can be an opportunity to use it on our good. 
> 
> In large areas (over 100km routes), we are aiming to use mission_planner to plan the route. Once it plans the route, we can hold the lanelet ids inside of the route. The only issue here is to keeping coordinates low for not getting floating point errors. We thought that MGRS limitations can help with this. Here is a demonstration of what is planned.
> ![mgrs_border](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44242212/d7c61b4b-3420-42c7-a1be-3e910c733825)
> 
> As can be seen in the demonstration, in large areas, we change MGRS grids. In that situation, we will see that the lanelet2 maps of different MGRS grids will overlay due to the MGRS boundaries. To avoid that situation, we are planning that to use MGRS strings to find which MGRS grid the moving vehicle is in. Additonally, with Dynamic Lanelet2 Loading, it is aimed that to load lanelet2 maps according to MGRS string of moving vehicle.
> 
> Additionally, for keeping the coordinates low, we can apply the same method to point cloud maps as NDT input. With an MGRS string specification for each lanelet2 map and each point cloud will be able to solve the localization and mapping problem. 
> 
> We will test this with a point cloud taken from AWSIM and a lanelet2 map generated via CommonRoad API at the crossing of 2 MGRS grids.
> 
> @xmfcx @mitsudome-r 

###### @mitsudome-r (2024-01-22)

> MGRS grid cannot handle goals that is outside 100km x 100km, but can't we use other projection type for longer distance? (e.g., using [TransverseMercator](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/map/map_projection_loader/README.md#using-transversemercator) projection)
> 
> There could be distortion in the long distance anyways, but the topology of lane connection doesn't depend on the projection error so mission_planner should be able to do the route calculation just fine.

###### @stale (2024-03-22)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @ataparlar (2024-04-03)

> This issue is related to the MGRS boundaries. We can use LocalCartesian UTM or Transverse Mercator projections in Autoware. In real-life conditions, there won't be a drive that is too long. So, MGRS boundaries are not a problem right now.

> 
> I report this issue since this error seems so weird("Please report it" in the error statement).
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Run planning simulation tutorial as normal.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Cannot run the tutorial because of the error.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. I ran the command below: 
> ```
> rocker --nvidia --x11 --user --volume $HOME/autoware_map -- ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware-universe:humble-latest-prebuilt
> ```
> 2. Download the map (same with tutorial)
> ```
> gdown -O ~/autoware_map/ 'https://docs.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1499_nsbUbIeturZaDj7jhUownh5fvXHd'
> unzip -d ~/autoware_map ~/autoware_map/sample-map-planning.zip
> ```
> 3. Run simulation
> ```
> source /autoware/install/setup.bash
> ros2 launch autoware_launch planning_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=$HOME/autoware_map/sample-map-planning vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit
> ```
> 
> I also tried to run the simulation with `autoware_data`, which contains machine learning models for the inference, but the situation is the same.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS(host): Ubuntu 20.04
> - Autoware version: [latest(20231215)](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe)
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Sorry, I cannot know..
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @Kim-mins (2023-12-28)

> It seems my configuration was wrong.
> I downloaded `autoware_map` and `autoware_data` again, and I could successfully run the simulation.
> Sorry for bothering.

### #5936 — Controller outputs way too high velocity/acceleration

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-12-22  |  **Closed:** 2024-05-08  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:control
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5936

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I am debugging a freespace planner algorithm with the planning simulator and encountered this crazy situation:
> 
> [Screencast from 12-22-2023 01_42_39 PM.webm](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/577277db-48ad-4221-b1dc-a59554b7b4e7)
> 
> Like astar and other algorithms, the output path of the algorithm is transformed into a trajectory by `freespace_planner` using a fixed speed (default 5km/h):
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/3a0fd31b95852dedc9a1b26c5496cf31a4e26347/planning/freespace_planner/src/freespace_planner/freespace_planner_node.cpp#L166-L178
> 
> The simulation goes usually well, but for some reason this time, the controller started to panic around the goal point and kept outputing very large velocity/acceleration targets. 
> 
> I am not sure what triggered that behavior. I just remember the vehicle was stuck nearby the goal pose for a while before (but that's my algorithm.)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Velocity/Acceleration should be capped
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> velocity/acceleration diverge
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> No idea
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2024-01-12)

> I can reproduce the behavior rather consistently in my environment even with A* by placing an obstacle in front of the vehicle next to a turn point, like so:
> 
> [Screencast from 01-12-2024 10_13_43 AM.webm](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/a026c829-1cad-4463-bccf-9058fdbd2711)
> 
> However I don't get the same effect with current main branch.
> 
> 
> 
> 
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2024-01-12)

> When I visualize trajectory follower and vehicle cmd gate target acceleration or speed I don't see any crazy acceleration:
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/45738a50-6772-45e5-95a1-41e84e781fec)
> 
> Deceleration values are pretty big, but it is supposed to make the vehicle stop, not go crazily fast. 
> 
> I suspect this behavior only exists in the planning simulator, as a normal car would not be able to accelerate that much or instantly switch gears DRIVE <-> REVERSE

###### @VRichardJP (2024-01-12)

> I think the issue is partly due to the replan logic here:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/b51759fa17f40a230749217e0113eea2b5d67657/planning/freespace_planner/src/freespace_planner/freespace_planner_node.cpp#L444-L457
> 
> When `isPlanRequired()` is `true` due to an obstacle on the path or if the vehicle is far from the current trajectory, a new trajectory is generated while the vehicle is still moving (supposedly trying to stop). I am not sure it is a good idea. In particular, by the time the new trajectory is computed, the vehicle may not even be on it. For example in the case the obstacle is in front of the current trajectory, the new trajectory will likely start with a backward manoeuver (away from the obstacle) while the vehicle kept moving forward.
> 
> I have added a simple check on the current motion state, so that a new trajectory is only generated if the vehicle is stopped. The crazy acceleration behavior disappeared after.

### #5931 — The Autonomous Emergency Brake (AEB) does not perform as expected when only using the predicted trajectory.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-12-21  |  **Closed:** 2023-12-22  |  **Author:** @ismetatabay
- **Labels:** component:control
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5931

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In the current design of the `autonomous_emergency_braking` (AEB) node, it can utilize either the predicted trajectory, the IMU path, or both to calculate collisions between the ego vehicle and obstacles. By default, both trajectories are checked, but the predicted trajectory not detect any collisions.
> 
> ## Using IMU for Ego Trajectory:
> There is no issue with using the IMU path, the AEB node can send an emergency diagnostic message when a collision is detected.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/56237550/a264c189-33ec-46f1-8045-c6fcd1cf4b3c
> 
> ## Using Predicted Trajectory:
> When the predicted trajectory, the AEB module fails to detect collisions, leading to a 'motion_utils' logic error. Consequently, Autoware MRM operates based on the control output.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/56237550/28bcbabb-da97-466c-9dd6-dbfdfd8f3b18
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> When utilizing the predicted trajectory, the AEB should detect collisions.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> When utilizing the predicted trajectory, the AEB cannot detect collision and causes the motion util function logic error.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Run Planning Sim
> 2. Enable AEB
> 3. Set `expand_width` -> 5.0 and `collision_keeping_sec` -> 0.2 for using AEB on the planning sim for collision detection. (I incremented expand_width for collision detection on opposite lanelet, otherwise obstacle_stop_planner can stop the vehicle.)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS 2: Humble
> - Autoware: Latest
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #5859 — Tracking getting lost detected bicycle and motorcycle

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-12-13  |  **Closed:** 2023-12-14  |  **Author:** @kaancolak
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:perception
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5859

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In some cases, the L-shape fitting algorithm doesn't provide reliable orientation information for bicycles and motorcycles. This situation causes to lost of detected objects inside multiple object trackers. 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Detected objects track reliably.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Bicycle and motorcycle objects getting lost
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Run autoware.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> 
> Inside into multiple object tracker algorithm, when assigning detected objects and tracked objects, we are losing detected objects. L-shape fitting algorithms provide unreliable orientation for bicycles/motorcycles and due to that detected object doesn't exceed mahallanobis distance gate.
> 
> 
> The below image shows that the tracking object and detected objects almost the same position but due to wrong orientation information we are losing it;
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2023-11-28 19-28-57](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/12658936/50d27831-24da-4539-a65c-e3712ace57aa)
> 
> 
> In the demonstration videos, object detection works over the Apollo instance segmentation algorithm, and bounding boxes provided by the shape_estimation module.
> 
> Bounding boxes are not perfect but look good.  
> Detection results: 
> [![Detection results: ](https://img.youtube.com/vi/hJMYYKc-kK0/1.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hJMYYKc-kK0)
> 
> Tracking results: 
> [![Tracking results: ](https://img.youtube.com/vi/s2gWxL6a07Q/1.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s2gWxL6a07Q)
> 
>  I added bicycle correctors for bicycles/motorcycles like vehicle and bus correctors. 
> 
> [![Tracking after bicycle corrector: ](https://img.youtube.com/vi/ep1ESflPrHY/1.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ep1ESflPrHY)
> 
> 
> FYI: @miursh @YoshiRi @yukkysaito  @xmfcx @shmpwk 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #5808 — ekf_localizer publishes unbiased pose as biased pose

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-12-07  |  **Closed:** 2024-01-09  |  **Author:** @yvzksgl
- **Labels:** component:localization
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5808

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> ekf_localizer confused about `biased_pose` and `pose`.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/566c57f671c4aa01cd0a52b214ffbbda16ef47f9/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_module.cpp#L90-L92 `biased_yaw` and `yaw` variables should be exchanged.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> `biased_yaw` is unbiased and `yaw` is biased I will try to explain in a detailed way.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/566c57f671c4aa01cd0a52b214ffbbda16ef47f9/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_localizer.cpp#L228-L231 biased_pose and pose are assigned with calling `getCurrentPose()`, 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/566c57f671c4aa01cd0a52b214ffbbda16ef47f9/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_module.cpp#L97-L103 Everyting looks fine up here, however when loking at https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/566c57f671c4aa01cd0a52b214ffbbda16ef47f9/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_module.cpp#L90-L92  `biased_yaw` variable contains unbiased yaw and `yaw` contains biased yaw.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> I read the https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/1403, since, it's been a while from the issue I cannot compare it with the current architecture.

**Comments:**

###### @KYabuuchi (2023-12-11)

> Hi! Thanks for reporting it. It may be wrong as you mentioned. 
> However, the code regarding bias is a bit complicated, so I will carefully read the code to make sure.

###### @KYabuuchi (2023-12-11)

> @yvzksgl  I checked the code again and found that the current implementation is correct.
> 
> Firstly, the internally stored yaw in the EKF includes a yaw bias. (The name `IDX::YAW` is confusing.)
> Specifically, `kalman_filter_.getXelement(IDX::YAW)` contains the yaw bias of the LiDAR calibration.
> To make this the YAW of the base_link, it is necessary to add the YAW_BIAS. 
> Please refer to the state transition equation:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/89d4462f45e3af4773f6b930d680cd7ff07f92ea/localization/ekf_localizer/src/state_transition.cpp#L43-L50
> 
> Additionally, in the measurement pose update below, you can observe that the NDT's YAW angle is used directly. 
> (Note that it is normalized to ensure a difference with ekf_yaw less thatn 2╧Ç, but no bias correction is applied.) 
> This is consistent with EKF storing biased yaw internally, since the raw NDT output contains a calibration yaw bias.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/89d4462f45e3af4773f6b930d680cd7ff07f92ea/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_module.cpp#L227-L235
> 
> 

###### @KYabuuchi (2023-12-20)

> @idorobotics @yvzksgl  Hi. What is the current status of this issue? 
> Is someone in the working group working on improving the code?
> 
> If my explanation above is fine, I'll create a PR to improve the code so that users don't misunderstand it.

###### @yvzksgl (2023-12-20)

> Hello @KYabuuchi, sorry for my late response. Last week I had to go on a business travel and this week I was trying to understand where the yaw_bias is updated. It looks all good to me now. If you don't mind I just want to ask a question about, do you know what does mean 
> > multiple inputs with yaw estiamation 
> 
> in here https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/566c57f671c4aa01cd0a52b214ffbbda16ef47f9/localization/ekf_localizer/README.md?plain=1#L235

###### @KYabuuchi (2023-12-21)

> @yvzksgl  No problem. I am glad my explanation makes sense to you.
> 
> Regarding multiple inputs with yaw estimation, please refer to the figure below.
> If multiple pose_estimators are used, the input poses to the EKF will contain multiple yaw biases. However, the current EKF assumes the existence of only one yaw_bias. Therefore, it cannot correctly handle these multiple yaw biases.
> 
> If we are using a single NDT, that is not a problem.
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/24854875/41c91b96-f65d-4d48-ad70-92eded40a2e0)
> 

###### @yvzksgl (2023-12-21)

> I see, thank you for your great explanation and patience!

###### @KYabuuchi (2024-01-09)

> The PR which improves documentation is merged https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5834

###### @VRichardJP (2023-12-15)

> Regarding the incorrect pitch/z localization, I think ekf is responsible for that. Both Z and orientation are smoothened over multiple NDT poses by the `updateSimple1DFilters` function in EKF. The behavior can be tuned by changing the parameters `pose_additional_delay` (default 0.0) and `pose_smoothing_steps` (default 5) in `ekf_localizer.param.yaml`.
> 
> Assuming you are using the default parameters and your simulated LIDAR sensor runs at 10Hz, it means it will take at least 0.5 seconds for z and pitch values to converge on a sudden slope variation. Actually it may even be worse, because it means that the initial pose sent to NDT is not that good during the transition pahse, so the localization result may not be that accurate.
> 
> I think you should be able to get better localization by setting `pose_smoothen_steps` to 1 or 2.

###### @maxime-clem (2023-12-22)

> Thank you for reporting the issue and for the initial investigation.
> I looked at the bag and the slope information (as calculated by the longitudinal controller) does not match the map seen in the video.
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/78338830/2a1a4b29-3d92-470c-9c3e-9535c6e4aa28)
> At the end of the bag when ego collides with the obstacle, the measured slope (black) is positive but in the video the slope was negative (downward slope).
> 
> We can also see that there is a lot of error between the target velocity (orange) and the actual velocity (blue).
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/78338830/455ca7bb-eeda-437a-ba75-1ca57ac5427d)
> 
> So my guess is that the issue is caused by a wrong slope information. Can you share your map so test it locally ?
> On your side you can try to set `use_trajectory_for_pitch_calculation` to `true` and see if it makes a difference.
> 
> I will try to setup Carla to reproduce the issue but I may not be able to do so before a while.

###### @Kim-mins (2023-12-22)

> Hi @maxime-clem! Thank you for the answer!
> 
> Here's the `.pcd` and `.osm` files I used(`Town03` of Carla): [[lanelet2_map.osm](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1U867V_L0DAPzDPPhANzRlhNTgU_gPWtv/view?usp=sharing)] [[pointcloud_map.pcd](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kBsPE0TGwWfSi_9L2JABuzUWw4ijDBRm/view?usp=sharing)]
> 
> I have one question for the trial on my side. Do you mean to enable the parameter `use_trajectory_for_pitch_calculation` [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/36804c87f61a0a13a4e6221c4effc1fa183b71aa/autoware_launch/config/control/trajectory_follower/longitudinal/pid.param.yaml#L73)?
> For the setting with Carla, I'm using the bridge [here(humble branch)](https://github.com/evshary/autoware_carla_launch/tree/humble). I hope it would help you.

###### @maxime-clem (2023-12-25)

> Thank you for sharing your map. I was able to reproduce the issue using the `simple_planning_simulator` (after activating the road slope simulation with this PR https://github.com/autowarefoundation/sample_vehicle_launch/pull/55).
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/78338830/2244bf1b-f839-4ab3-95da-f80996df92a3
> 
> There was no difference when enabling parameter `use_trajectory_for_pitch_calculation`.
> For reference, here is the behavior with no slope compensation in the longitudinal controller.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/78338830/3e0120dc-3247-4e32-ada4-7b0e5fdbb862
> 
> So in conclusion, it looks like a problem with the slope compensation not adjusting the deceleration enough to allow stopping in a downward slope.
> 
> I am not sure if someone will be able to work on this issue before a while. I will at least make sure it is discussed at the next [working group meeting](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/categories/working-group-meetings?discussions_q=is%3Aopen+category%3A%22Working+group+meetings%22++label%3Ameeting%3Aplanning-control-wg+) on January 18 ([google calendar link](https://www.google.com/calendar/event?eid=Z3YxcnY3cjBuYWxxM28xZXVnNzE5dWVsajdfMjAyNDAxMDRUMDgwMDAwWiBhdXRvd2FyZS5vcmdfNmxvbDBobzVmdDAyMTdoOGM2MHBpMWZtMzBAZw)).

###### @Kim-mins (2023-12-26)

> Thank you for the detailed investigation @maxime-clem!
> Then I'll wait for it. Thanks.

###### @mehmetdogru (2024-01-18)

> @brkay54 to test if any PR related slop compensation solves the issue or not

###### @brkay54 (2024-01-31)

> Hi @Kim-mins, I can reproduce the issue like Maxime did. I checked the slope values of the road and I saw that it was higher than 0.1 rad (which is max and min slope for pitch in default parameters). When I changed it to a higher value (0.5 and -0.5). The vehicle can stop at the goal point. Could you try to change [these parameters](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/b7880fea1a03e86874a348ea6511024b08e3168c/autoware_launch/config/control/trajectory_follower/longitudinal/pid.param.yaml#L75-L76) to a higher value if you are using these parameters with default value?

###### @Kim-mins (2024-02-05)

> Hi @brkay54! Thank you for the answer!
> 
> Unfortunately, the ego vehicle still go through the goal point for me..
> I changed the parameter `max_pitch_rad` from `0.1` to `0.5`, and `min_pitch_rad` from `-0.1` to `-0.5`, as you suggested, but I could not observe any difference.
> I'm currently running the Autoware with the prebuilt version (docker, 20230715). Could you please tell me the version you are running?

###### @maxime-clem (2024-02-07)

> I tested the solution of @brkay54 and it completely solves the issue. The version of Autoware you are using (`20230715`) is missing some fixes to the slope compensation feature and this is probably why changing the parameters does not work in your case.
> 
> Can you try switching to a more recent version of Autoware ? Otherwise you can try cherry picking some of the fix PRs (I think all PRs to the `pid_longitudinal_controller` since July: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aclosed+slope+sort%3Aupdated-desc).

###### @Kim-mins (2024-02-07)

> Thank you for the suggestion @maxime-clem!
> 
> I just realized that I can run the planning simulation of the latest version, and I could check the ego vehicle stops right at the goal point with the parameter @brkay54 provided.
> So I think the issue is gone now! I really appreciate to the hard work!! Thank you all!

###### @JunWu-ARM (2024-07-02)

> @oguzkaganozt , @youtalk, could you please review my investigation ?
> ### Summary:
> 
> Whether the test will report an error depends on who runs the test:
> 
> 
> - non-root will report success because the user can not open the /root/autoware_data/lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm/models/baidu_cnn/./deploy_lib.so (no permission), then the test application will skip the test because it will think the .so does not exist, then no error reported.
> 
> - root user will report the error because it can see the .so, then will try to load it, but failed because the deploy_lib.so is a x86_64 version.
> 
> In our development environment, we login as host user by run ./docker/run.sh so the user in docker is non-root, so it reports success (detailed log show test skipped).
> 
> In the autoware github pipeline, it runs docker image as root so it reports the error
> e.g. [build-and-test-daily-arm64 ┬╖ autowarefoundation/autoware.universe@c2f9579 (github.com)](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/actions/runs/9752737364/job/26916784884)
> At "Initialize Containers", the following cmd create and run the docker image
> 
> 
> `/usr/bin/docker create -name 8ffb922c9e784952807e50a2957540e9_ghcrioautowarefoundationautowarelatestprebuilt_96069e --label 591d3a --workdir /_w/autoware.universe/autoware.universe --network github_network_098334ac17b34c44924c79f4b34be4a4┬á -e┬á"HOME=/github/home"┬á-e GITHUB_ACTIONS=true┬á-e CI=true┬á-v┬á"/var/run/docker.sock":"/var/run/docker.sock"┬á-v┬á"/home/ubuntu/actions-runner/_work":"/w"┬á-v┬á"/home/ubuntu/actions-runner/externals":"/e":ro -v┬á"/home/ubuntu/actions-runner/_work/_temp":"/w/_temp"┬á-v┬á"/home/ubuntu/actions-runner/_work/_actions":"/w/_actions"┬á-v┬á"/home/ubuntu/actions-runner/_work/_tool":"/_w/_tool"┬á-v┬á"/home/ubuntu/actions-runner/_work/_temp/_github_home":"/github/home"┬á-v┬á"/home/ubuntu/actions-runner/_work/_temp/_github_workflow":"/github/workflow"┬á-entrypoint┬á"tail"┬ághcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware:latest-prebuilt┬á"-f"┬á"/dev/null"┬ád666295bb0a9aa46129819b0559ff5ab6260ea7a0a128bc1b1962ccbd2b79b80┬á/usr/bin/docker start d666295bb0a9aa46129819b0559ff5ab6260ea7a0a128bc1b1962ccbd2b79b80`
> 
> Please note that the user inside the Docker container depends on how the Docker image was built. If no user is set during the build of the Docker image, the default user inside the container will be root (uid 0) (or we can set userid and groupid when run the docker)
> 

###### @ambroise-arm (2024-07-24)

> Closing the issue as the package is being removed by https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/7996

### #5732 — Libraries and modules mixes between boost::optional and std::optional

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-30  |  **Closed:** 2024-02-05  |  **Author:** @zulfaqar-azmi-t4
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5732

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> 
> Before the release of ROS Galactic, `boost::optional` was commonly used for representing optional values. However, with the shift to Galactic and later to Humble, there has been support for C++17, leading developers who prefer the standard library to start using `std::optional`. This has created some inconsistencies in the `Autoware.Universe` code base, as different parts use either `boost::optional` or `std::optional`. Such a mix has led to both libraries being utilized simultaneously.
> 
> As the codebase continues to expand, this issue contributes significantly to the accumulating technical debt. While some libraries, like lanelet, still use Boost, this shouldn't justify a haphazard combination of different standards. Therefore, I suggest we aim for greater standardization by predominantly adopting `std::optional` in place of `boost::optional`.
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> standardize the library from `boost::optional` to `std::optional`
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> some codebase uses `boost::optional`, which some code uses `std::optional`.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Go to behavior path planner or behavior velocity planner
> 2. see that sometime boost optional are used and sometime std::optional are used.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS: Humble
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Autoware.Universe code is not properly standardized.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #5715 — `behavior_path_planner` does not receive initial operation mode when run with gdb

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-29  |  **Closed:** 2023-12-04  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP

> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> We can see the problem in the video there: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/5649#issuecomment-1822192857
> 
> 1. Autoware is started
> 2. Initial pose is set
> 3. Goal pose is set
> 4. I click on "local" to change the operation mode, and then the path is generated.
> 
> When I don't run the path planner container in gdb, the path is generated as soon as the goal point is set (at 3). But here, when I start the program in gdb it keeps saying "waiting for operation_mode" instead. 
> 
> I don't think gdb has anything to do with this, but I guess it may have an impact on autoware module startup timings.
> 
> That said, the operation mode topic is supposed to be transient, so it should not matter whether the planner is started early or late. The node should receive the current state anyway. Unless it is not set?
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> No need to set the autoware state manually to generate a path.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Need to change the state once.

### #5705 — several packages export the same library

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-28  |  **Closed:** 2023-11-29  |  **Author:** @esteve
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5705

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> `multi_object_tracker`, `object_merger`, `radar_object_tracker` and `tracking_object_merger` all ship the same library (with the same source code), called `libmu_successive_shortest_path`. This is not a problem with building and installing from source if using isolated builds, however when building Debian packages for these packages, they conflict with each other because the paths collide.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Packages can be installed in a non-isolated workspace and none of the installed objects collide.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> See https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-deb-packages/issues/51
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> See https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-deb-packages/issues/51
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> `multi_object_tracker`, `object_merger`, `radar_object_tracker` and `tracking_object_merger` have the following lines in their `CMakeLists.txt` files:
> 
> ```cmake
> ament_auto_add_library(mu_successive_shortest_path SHARED
>   src/data_association/mu_successive_shortest_path/mu_successive_shortest_path_wrapper.cpp
> )
> ```
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #5668 — NPC vehicle's predicted path is unfeasible wrt HD-Map

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-24  |  **Closed:** 2023-11-25  |  **Author:** @mehmetdogru
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5668

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> **map_based_prediction** node predicts that NPC vehicles can make a lane change even though it is restricted in the HD-Map with:
>  
> `<tag k="lane_change" v="no"/>`
> 
> ![issue](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/48479081/423426e3-d631-4e8e-a038-5cc777475844)
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> NPC vehicles predicted paths should not include unfeasible paths wrt HD-Map for some use cases.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Add a parameter that restricts unfeasible (non-routable) predictions and define the necessary condition.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Add a parameter that restricts unfeasible (non-routable) predictions and define the necessary condition

**Comments:**

###### @YoshiRi (2023-11-25)

> @mehmetdogru 
> Hi. Thanks for your suggestion.
> 
> I have several opinion about this issue.
> 
> - In our regular automated driving, it is a regular occurrence for other vehicles to straddle the no lane change line.
> - For example, it is often the case that a vehicle temporarily crosses the line to avoid a car parked in the shoulder lane.
> 
> Therefore, we would like to keep this lane change prediction if possible, because it is possible that other vehicles may cross the line even if it is a boundary that they are not legally allowed to cross.

###### @YoshiRi (2023-11-25)

> Oh, now I just found your PR met all of our requirements :+1:

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-24)

> With the launch prefix, the behavior planning container should start in a new terminal, like here:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/5649#issuecomment-1822192857
> 
> Be careful that due to default gdb pagination, sometimes the program does not start until you press Enter (you can avoid this by creating a `~/.gdbinit` file with `set pagination off` inside).
> 
> Regarding your second issue, either the vehicle is not stopped, or Autoware has not received any velocity feedback from the vehicle (the wording is not clear I know). The simulator should sends this data to `/vehicle/velocity_status`

> 
> This would give a better idea of where your program has crashed (usually the exact line).
> In your case, the crash is most likely caused by a nullptr dereference, so you may be able to identify it immediately (you can navigate through the backtrace with `up` and `down` commands.)
> 
> If there are several candidates or if the trace is obfuscated due to optimizations, you could try to recompile the target module without optimization. For example:
> 
> ```sh
> colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug --packages-select behavior_velocity_planner  # and other crashing modules...
> ```
> 
> If you can catch the same crash in gdb with debug build, it should be pretty easy to find the cause:
> - from the segfault, use `up` until you reach some autoware code (source file should be something like `/home/username/autoware/src/...`). In my example above, I would start to inspect the program from:
> ```gdb
> #10 0x00007ffff42d2ee9 in route_handler::RouteHandler::getLaneletsFromId (this=<optimized out>, id=<optimized out>) at /home/computer/autoware/src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/route_handler/src/route_handler.cpp:512
> ```
> - use `p` to print local variables and see if anything looks suspicious. For example:
> ```gdb
> > p some_ptr
> 0x0
> > p some_vector[0]
> NaN
> ```

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-27)

> You just found the problem:
> 
> ```C++
>         Polygon2d polygon{};
>         for (const auto & p : trimmed_ego_polygon) {
>           polygon.outer().emplace_back(p.x(), p.y());
>         }
> 
>         polygon.outer().emplace_back(polygon.outer().front());
> ```
> 
> We have a `trimmed_ego_polygon` which we use to build another `polygon`. After that we try to close that polygon by adding a copy of the first point at the end (so that `polygon.first() == polygon.last()`)... and this is where the program crash.
> 
> If by any change, the `trimmed_ego_polygon` happens to be empty, then our polygon is empty. So accessing its first element with `polygon.outer().front()` is undefined behavior.
> 
> @soblin @takayuki5168 @tkimura4 @shmpwk 
> Could you check this?
>

### #5645 — Predicted obstacle box is too far from the actual points, which impacts obstacle stop planner

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-21  |  **Closed:** 2024-04-09  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** component:perception
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5645

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I have observed that predicted objects are always "further in time" than their tracked/detected counterpart. Typically, the faster the object is and the farther it will appear from th raw point cloud or raw detection. For example:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/a354804d-3aef-467a-b57b-eff26e3adf14
> 
> I could not find any kind of delay compensation, but I guess this is what the prediction algorithm is doing. 
> 
> One annoying side effect is that obstacle stop planner is sometimes not able to associate points on the path with the tracked objects they come from (because they are too far from each other), and so autoware stops.
> 
> One way I have found to "fix" this issue is to increase the `object_polygon_length_margin` in the adaptive cruise control parameters (which is the case in the video). However it is not a great solution, because it increases the likeliness autoware would associate points to the wrong object.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> obstacle stop planner can reliabily associate points to objects of any speed
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> when the object is fast, the predicted obstacle is too far from the pointcloud obstacle stop planner is using for comparison.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> use lidar based detection.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-30)

> For whoever gets this issue in the future: obstacle cruise planner does not have such issue at all because it does not use pointcloud data. It is also way more reliable than obstacle stop planner module but that's another topic. 

###### @stale (2024-01-30)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @technolojin (2024-04-05)

> Hi!
> 
> I am recently working on perception latency reduction.
> 
> What actually happening is, the tracking objects are in "current time" and the point clouds are "past time".  
> From the sensor time to detection may takes several hundreds micro seconds.
> (in case of 36 kph = 10 m/s of target related speed, 400 ms latency causes 4 m difference) 
> 
> 
> > I could not find any kind of delay compensation
> 
> the delay compensation is done in object tracking - object publish time.
> Config: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/804600599c546e5947d34666e842d6e29840909a/perception/multi_object_tracker/config/multi_object_tracker_node.param.yaml#L15
> Prediction: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/804600599c546e5947d34666e842d6e29840909a/perception/multi_object_tracker/src/tracker/model/normal_vehicle_tracker.cpp#L377
> 
> You can disable this option, but you will get old objects.
> 
> 
> It is impossible to reduce the latency to zero, but can be mitigated.
> This is a case to be improved.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6710
> The improvement will continue.
> 

###### @technolojin (2024-04-17)

> @VRichardJP
> 
> I linked this issue to my latest work for feedback.
> I didn't know that the issue is closed by the PR is merged.
> 
> As I mentioned, the positions of point cloud, detected object, and tracked object cannot be the same unless there is no latency. 
> If it is not acceptable from your side, please reopen the Issue.

> 
> Here, there is an early return if any dynamic target is enabled and the `object_ptr_` is null:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/8e209a146357ec5d613f03b54b9711f0d980bcc6/planning/surround_obstacle_checker/src/node.cpp#L295-L310
> 
> However, if no dynamic target is enabled, then we may proceed even if the `object_ptr` is null. This pointer is dereferenced right after in `getNearestObstacle()` -> `getNearestObstacleByDynamicObject()`:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/8e209a146357ec5d613f03b54b9711f0d980bcc6/planning/surround_obstacle_checker/src/node.cpp#L463
> 
> Resulting in a segmentation fault.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> No crash
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Crash
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Disable all dynamic targets in surround obstacle checker configuration, then use the planning simulator to plan anything.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @kyoichi-sugahara (2023-11-26)

> @VRichardJP cc: @danielsanchezaran 
> Can I close this issue with this PR's merge?
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5671

###### @danielsanchezaran (2023-11-28)

> @VRichardJP can I close this issue? I believe it has been solved with: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5671

### #5633 — The autonomous emergency braking package doesn't account for point cloud timeout

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-20  |  **Closed:** 2023-11-21  |  **Author:** @ismetatabay
- **Labels:** component:control
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5633

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I intend to utilize the autonomous_emergency_braking package to address emergency scenarios, such as when Autoware modules (ndt, ground segmentation, bpp, etc.) fail, to bring the vehicle to a halt before colliding with anything. However, I've identified certain circumstances that could pose challenges for this package's functionality.
> 
> 1. If any control module fails, AEB will also fail since this node is included in the control container.
> 2. The system lacks a mechanism for handling point cloud message timeout. For instance, if the perception module fails while using a ground-segmented point cloud as the input point cloud, AEB will not take any action.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The AEB node sends emergency stop signals to the /diagnostics if the input point cloud is timed out.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Add options to check for input point cloud timeouts.
> 
> - check_input_cloud_time_out: false
> - input_cloud_time_out: 1000 #ms
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Implement options to check input point cloud timeouts.

**Comments:**

###### @ismetatabay (2023-11-20)

> @tkimura4 @TakaHoribe If okay for you, I want to add options to check input point cloud timeouts for AEB node. What do you think?

###### @ismetatabay (2023-11-21)

> Since these problems can be handled with system_error_monitor and diagnostic aggregator, I am closing this issue. :+1:.
> 
> cc: @tkimura4 @TakaHoribe 

---

> 
> ### Description
> 
> Sorry for the lack of information (yet)
> 
> I have caught this crash of the behavior path planner container with gdb:
> 
> ```
> (lost upper trace)
> #4 lanelet::routing::RoutingGraph::previous()
> #5 route_handler::RouteHandler::getPreviousLaneletsWithinRoute()
> #6 route_handler::RouteHandler::getLeftLanelet()
> #7 route_handler::RouteHandler::getLeftMostLineString()
> #8 route_handler::RouteHandler::getLeftMostLineString()
> #9 route_handler::RouteHandler::getLeftMostLineString()
> #10 route_handler::RouteHandler::getLeftMostLineString()
> ...
> #40 route_handler::RouteHandler::getLeftMostLineString()
> ...and so on
> ```
> 
> My map is just a big circular loop, with sometimes multiple lanes and some cross walks (nothing fancy).
> 
> It might be the same crash as in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/5631
> 
> I will update when I have more information.

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-29)

> I got the same crash today after setting a new goal point. The route handler died after 52000 recursions
> 
> I was too clumsy to find the root cause with gdb this time, but from the backtrace and the code, I can think of 2 cases:
> 
> - either `getLeftLanelet(lanelet, enable_same_root)` may return the input `lanelet`, and we have an easy recursion
> - or the same with a cycle (e.g. lanelet B is left of lanelet A, which is left of lanelet B).
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/b65bfe03b241001c5476003d722b43b1c995ac4f/planning/route_handler/src/route_handler.cpp#L1329-L1341
> 
> I am surprised how seldom this bug is (3rd time I see it over 2 weeks). So I guess it might be related to the start/goal point. The lanelet map is just a big one way loop, with sometimes multiple lanes, sometimes a road shoulder on the left, and a few crosswalk. I don't see how such recursion could happen.
> 
> In any case, I don't think it is sane to keep unbounded recursion like this one in the code. Most roads are only a few lanelets wide, so it would not be very costy to keep a list of all explored lanelets and stop if a loop is detected.

### #5631 — Broken path generation when ego vehicle approaches a crosswalk from outside the planned lane

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-11-20  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:help-wanted, status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5631

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In the example here, the vehicle is driven manually on a one way two lanes road, with the goal point is way farther away on the right:
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/b8d53be5-2eaa-414e-a3a9-7cf07ea1b79f)
> 
> Although autoware would like to stay on the left lane, we drive the vehicle on the right lane. This is usually not a problem and Autoware generates a path as if we were driving on the left lane.
> 
> However, as we approach a crosswalk, path generation just fails to plan anything beyond the crosswalk lanelet (blue lines highlights the drivable area).
> 
> Even after passing the lanelet, the planning is still stuck:
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/df3d2950-01a5-4811-8773-f5d43d5d3003)
> 
> It crashes soon after
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Planner should be able to generate valid path at all time
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Here the path planner cannot plan anything beyond the crosswalk lanelet and dies
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Most likely reproducable with the planning simulator and by driving the ego vehicle manually
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-22)

> I have yet to reproduce in the planning simulator, but I have recorded a rosbag of the issue. It could be a combination of crosswalk + unfinished lane change:
> 
> [Screencast from 2023-11-22 17-33-52.webm](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/7a43e0df-d997-46d2-8342-97b70c359661)
> 
> As you can see in the video, Autoware planned a lane change, which actually never happened as our driver kept driving straight.

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-22)

> In the planning simulator:
> 
> [Screencast from 2023-11-22 17-47-24.webm](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/b6e8d2e2-f1bd-4c88-9fd4-3c72cfda8ae1)
> 

###### @rej55 (2023-12-08)

> Sorry for late reaction ≡ƒÖç 
> 
> In `behavior_path_planner`, the scene modules continues to run if the success condition is not satisfied.
> The reason is it may be preferable not to be reset when checking behavior of Autoware with manual driving.
> So, it is difficult to uniquely define the planning behavior during manual driving.
> 
> To meet your request, I suggest to make a tool to reset the planner.
> Currently, if `behavior_path_planner` subscribes a route topic, it resets the planning status.
> By using route resending tool, the system operator can force a planner reset.

### #5614 — EKF gives bad results in speed bump and after a sudden brake or turning scenario

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-16  |  **Closed:** 2024-01-17  |  **Author:** @meliketanrikulu
- **Labels:** component:localization
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5614

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> We encountered the problem of localization shaking when going through speed bump. I checked the inputs for EKF. There doesn't appear to be any delays or errors regarding velocity data. NDT orientation y and orientation y values from GNSS overlap with each other and the values come as they should, but the EKF output responds late because of the sudden change. This causes the localization to shake.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The map and point cloud must always be on top of each other. I expect not to see any shaking
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> I see that the localization shifts on the z axis when going through speed bump. I observe the distortion in localization by checking whether the concatenated point cloud match with the map.
> 
> Here is the test videos:
> 
> [Test Video1](https://youtu.be/LN-2k3F6M-4?t=15)
> [Test Video2](https://youtu.be/RzmZ8L0RN70?t=30)
> 
> At these moments, when I look at the orientation data coming from GNSS, the orientation output of NDT, and the orientation data output of EKF, I see that NDT and GNSS give close and accurate data. However, when I look at the orientation values in the EKF output, I see that they react late. (The value I take into consideration here is the pitch value because the distortion occurs on the pitch.)
> 
> ![shift2](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/41450930/fe79e171-8c88-4ad8-ae67-bdcb58682394)
> 
> 
> 
> -- /localization/pose_estimator/pose/orientation/pitch_deg  --> NDT Output (Green )
> -- /localization/pose_twist_fusion_filter/pose/orientation/pitch_deg --> EKF Output (Yellow)
> -- /sensing/gnss/pose/orientation/pitch_deg  --> GNSS Output (Purple)
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1.) Bag files and videos are here:
> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Nvj1HkRecVttlfBPTliMTGJc7OGRjyYj?usp=sharing
> 
> 2.) Sensor kit:
> https://github.com/leo-drive/golf_sensor_kit_launch
> 
> 3.) Individual Params:
> https://github.com/leo-drive/autoware_individual_params
> 
> 4.)PC Map:
> https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ltgV-rD0a6O7Nv3uxrzs47OFcrcX4DrA/view?usp=drive_link
> 
> 5.) EKF parameters are here
> 
> https://github.com/leo-drive/autoware_launch/blob/golf/autoware_launch/config/localization/ekf_localizer.param.yaml
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> I know that EKF filters sudden changes because it processes data from the past, but working this way will cause many problems and needs to be solved.
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @kminoda (2023-11-22)

> One thing you could do is to tune the parameters for Simple1DFilter in ekf_localizer. Currently it's not prepared as a default parameters, so you need to edit the code to add a parameters here: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/bae5ea79c0879d02aab728e355205a0fb17e6fdc/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_localizer.cpp#L98-L100

###### @meliketanrikulu (2023-11-28)

> @kminoda Thank you for your response. I appreciate your help. The shift problem in EKF was solved when I played with these parameters (pitch_filter_proc_dev parameter affected the result).
> That's why I created two PRs so that I could change them in the parameter file.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/710
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5707
> 
> While localizing with NDT, the shift between EKF decreased from 400 ms to 200 ms. Since the frequency of NDT is low, I think it may be normal that this is not 0. Because when I fed GNSS data to EKF at 100 Hz with new parameters, this shift disappeared. There is no delay or shift anymore. However, this problem was not solved when I localized both with GNSS and NDT. That's why I'm taking a look at other problems in my system right now.

###### @KYabuuchi (2024-01-17)

> Since all relevant PRs have been merged, I close this issue.  Thanks for all of your support.

### #5594 — Add a new pointcloud filter based on image semantic segmentation

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-15  |  **Closed:** 2024-09-08  |  **Author:** @badai-nguyen
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:perception
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5594

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> As I described https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3974, we (TIER IV) and other teams are also facing difficult to deal with unknown from plants, raindrops/smoke/splash pointcloud or pointcloud of ground segmentation fail. 
>  
> Current pointcloud filters including dual_return_filter, outlier_filter, ground_segmentation only based on points kinematics information. Compare_map_filter compare pointcloud with map to remove un-movable objects but it frequently fail with growing plants, tree.. etc. 
> 
> It should be helpful if image semantic information could be used and fused with pointcloud to remove unnecessary pointclouds for autonomous driving such as pointcloud of plants in background, or  drivable area.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To deploy some kind of image semantic or instance segmentation model and matching with pointcloud to filter pointcloud.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. Train and deploy an image segmentation model:
> 
> - By Using a separate model with current detection Yolox model
> - Or adding an additional task/header for into current detection yolox model 
> 
> 2. Publish some 2d mask image of segmentation information or kind of less important image region information for filtering 
> 
> 3. Create new node to fuse image pixel level with pointcloud and remove pointcloud in less important image region.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Train and Deploy an image segmentation model into autoware
> - [x] Publish some topics of image segmentation result 
> - [x] Matching pointcloud and image segmentation result for filtering

**Comments:**

###### @stale (2024-01-15)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @xmfcx (2024-04-03)

> - Retraining the 2D image segmentation model right now.
> - Semantic seg fusion is already merged.
> - Will update the pipeline to have this included.
> - Test on the real vehicle.
> - Eval on old data (e.g. noisy)

###### @xmfcx (2024-05-24)

> 
> ### Description
> 
> In autoware.universe all marker RGBA values are hardcoded in each debug files. I'm planning to define a color palette based on [Kelly's 22 colours of maximum contrast](https://medium.com/@rjurney/kellys-22-colours-of-maximum-contrast-58edb70c90d1). The color palette is designed to easily distinguishable for people with defective color vision.
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - ΓÇ£#fdfdfdΓÇ¥ white
> - ΓÇ£#1d1d1dΓÇ¥ black
> - ΓÇ£#ebce2bΓÇ¥ yellow
> - ΓÇ£#702c8cΓÇ¥ purple
> - ΓÇ£#db6917ΓÇ¥ orange
> - ΓÇ£#96cde6ΓÇ¥ light blue
> - ΓÇ£#ba1c30ΓÇ¥ red
> - ΓÇ£#c0bd7fΓÇ¥ buff
> - ΓÇ£#7f7e80ΓÇ¥ grey
> - ΓÇ£#5fa641ΓÇ¥ green
> - ΓÇ£#d485b2ΓÇ¥ purplish pink
> - ΓÇ£#4277b6ΓÇ¥ blue
> - ΓÇ£#df8461ΓÇ¥ yellowish pink
> - ΓÇ£#463397ΓÇ¥ violet
> - ΓÇ£#e1a11aΓÇ¥ orange yellow
> - ΓÇ£#91218cΓÇ¥ purplish red
> - ΓÇ£#e8e948ΓÇ¥ greenish yellow
> - ΓÇ£#7e1510ΓÇ¥ reddish brown
> - ΓÇ£#92ae31ΓÇ¥ yellow green
> - ΓÇ£#6f340dΓÇ¥ yellowish brown
> - ΓÇ£#d32b1eΓÇ¥ reddish orange
> - ΓÇ£#2b3514ΓÇ¥ olive green
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> ```cpp
> namespace tier4_autoware_utils::color {
> 
> std_msgs::msg::ColorRGBA White(float a) {
>   static constexpr uint64_t code = 0xfdfdfd;
>   static constexpr float r = static_cast<int>(code >> 16) / 255.0;
>   static constexpr float g = static_cast<int>((code << 48) >> 56)) / 255.0;
>   static constexpr float b = static_cast<int>((code << 56) >> 56)) / 255.0;
>   std_msgs::msg::ColorRGBA color;
>   color.r = r;
>   color.b = b;
>   color.g = g;
>   color.a = a;
>   return color;
> }
> ```
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Replace all the markers

### #5540 — Investigate end-to-end delay in sudden obstacle braking response

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-09  |  **Closed:** 2024-03-05  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** component:perception, component:sensing, component:planning, type:performance
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5540

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> 
> During several tests, a notable delay has been observed in the autonomous system's response to sudden obstacles, particularly when braking is required.
> 
> For instance, at [3:32 in a test discussion](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3813#discussioncomment-6924175), the planning/perception components reacted later than expected.
> This issue is not isolated, as searching for "reacts late" in the discussion page reveals multiple instances. 
> 
> The proposed approach to investigate this involves a systematic test in both the planning simulator and AWSIM, focusing on the time taken from the obstacle's appearance to the initiation of the braking maneuver by the ego vehicle.
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose of this investigation is to ensure that the response time of the Autoware system to sudden obstacles meets the necessary safety requirements.
> By identifying the sources of delay within the system, from perception to actuation, we aim to optimize the response time and enhance the safety and reliability of the autonomous driving system.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. **Planning Simulator Test**:
>    - Simulate the ego vehicle traveling at 50km/h on a straight path.
>    - Introduce a sudden obstacle at a predetermined emergency braking distance. (Like 40m)
>    - Measure the latency from the obstacle's appearance to the initiation of the braking sequence with millisecond precision.
>    - Analyze where the delays occur most significantly within the system.
> 
> 2. **AWSIM Test**:
>    - Develop a detailed test procedure that spans from point cloud level detection to the end of the control stack.
>    - Measure and document the delays at each stage of the detection and response process.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] The systematic testing and measurement of delays have been completed in both the planning simulator and AWSIM.
> - [ ] A report detailing the delay times at each stage of the detection and reaction process has been compiled.
> - [ ] Recommendations for improvements, based on the findings, have been documented.
> - [ ] All tests and analyses have been peer-reviewed to ensure accuracy and reproducibility.
> - [ ] Any identified bottlenecks have been addressed with proposed solutions, and a follow-up plan for implementation and testing of these solutions is in place.

**Comments:**

###### @brkay54 (2023-12-25)

> We started work on this issue. To see the reaction time, we are currently working on a package. Currently, our target design is:
> 
> ![PsimObserver](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/6f4f5fc3-bb48-4685-b312-7d3a50a531b3)
> 
> For the first tests, we investigated only the reactions of the control topics.
> 
> Package: https://github.com/brkay54/autoware.universe/tree/feat/reaction-measure-tool/tools/reaction_analyzer
> 
> For an easy start, please read the usage part of the readme of the package and also, you can use the [LEO-VM-00001]( https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zHdSazcH9uQvw1Afj_6TL9N8d7_Z88Yu/view?usp=sharing). You do not need to edit the entity position in the parameter file, it is already set for LEO-VM-00001 map as default.
> 
> **First test results:**
> 15 tests have been made for each case: (obsacle_stop_planner with use_predicted_objects), 
> (obsacle_stop_planner without use_predicted_objects), (obstacle_cruise_planner).
> 
> **Case - 1 - obsacle_stop_planner with use_predicted_objects:**
>
