###### @brkay54 (2024-01-23)

> **Reaction Tests For Perception Pipeline**
> 
> The purpose of the tests is to measure the reaction time of each node in the Perception Pipeline. To achieve this, we developed a test environment by utilizing the AWSIM. We recorded rosbags in AWSIM to be able to launch the perception pipeline easily on the local devices. The disadvantage of this method is time resolution is about ~10ms because we can get a maximum 100 hz clock frequency. We used the sample_vehicle with awsim_sensor_kit (which has only 1 lidar) and tests were made in the **awsim-stable** branch but I am going to change the test environment to be able to run in main branches. 
> 
> Firstly, we wanted to measure the processing time of the `pointcloud_preprocessor` to see how much time takes on the sensing side. To measure the delay times in the `pointcloud_preprocessor` pipeline, we added `accumulated_time` debug information which reports the delay inside of each node. (PR is [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6056))
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2024-01-23 17-19-22](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/c124a816-233d-42cb-bccf-9523de4b271f)
> 
> Because the time resolution is about ~10 ms and the ring_outlier_filter and crop_box_filter processes finished mostly below 10 ms, the results above are not accurate. However, the concatenating process time is higher than 10 ms and we can see that the total pointcloud preprocess finished around ~115 ms on average.  The most time-consuming process is concatenating.
> 
> To measure the times in the perception pipeline, we created a test environment by using AWSIM. Firstly, we recorded two different rosbag files: one of them was in an empty area without any obstacle around the ego vehicle, and the other bag file was recorded in an area where there was a car in front of the ego vehicle. In both environments, the ego vehicle is in the same position and stationary, so all the topics except pointcloud topic are the same.
> 
> In reaction_analyzer node, we took sample messages from pointcloud topic in the rosbags and we recorded both pointcloud messages (pointcloud message without any object and pointcloud message with the car in front of the vehicle) at node initialization. It publishes the pointcloud without any obstacle at the beginning, when we want to spawn the obstacle, it starts to publish the pointcloud with car in front of the ego. After reaction_analyzer publishing the pointcloud with a car, it starts to search the first messages of the perception pipeline topics. 
> 
> To be able to run all test environment, steps are explained below:
> 
> - We should run the rosbag file which will publishes some necessary messages like vehicle_status, gnss_pose etc. to run the Autoware.
> - We run reaction_analyzer to publish pointcloud messages (firstly publishes empty one, then it publishes the pointcloud with car when we want to spawn the car)
> - We run autoware by the command: `ros2 launch autoware_launch e2e_simulator.launch.xml vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=awsim_sensor_kit map_path:=[PATH]`
> 
> **Test video:**
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/7400bd64-345d-4fed-a0c8-3ab0939c6b8b
> 
> After the obstacle is spawned (I mean reaction_analyzer starts to publish pointcloud with a car), reaction_analyzer starts to search for the obstacle in predefined topics. When it finds the reacted message, it calculates the time between the spawn command time and the header time of the reacted message. Nodes in the perception pipeline, header times do not have the timing of the process done. Firstly, I had to change the header times of some nodes by changing them to include the current time of the process done.  
> 
> With this test environment, we made 10 tests with some predefined checkpoints in the perception pipeline:
> 
> ```
> occupancy_grid_map_outlier: /perception/obstacle_segmentation/pointcloud
> voxel_based_compare_map_filter: /perception/object_recognition/detection/pointcloud_map_filtered/pointcloud
> lidar_centerpoint: /perception/object_recognition/detection/centerpoint/objects
> obstacle_pointcloud_based_validator: /perception/object_recognition/detection/centerpoint/validation/objects
> detected_object_feature_remover: /perception/object_recognition/detection/clustering/objects
> detection_by_tracker: /perception/object_recognition/detection/detection_by_tracker/objects
> object_lanelet_filter: /perception/object_recognition/detection/objects
> map_based_prediction: /perception/object_recognition/objects
> ```
> 
> **The results:**
> ![Screenshot from 2024-01-23 18-56-31](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/20898e68-eefe-44ea-b462-f5858f3b2662)
> 
> **Statistics:**
> ![Screenshot from 2024-01-23 18-57-09](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/cb41f211-6405-46db-8e64-ff87921de9d6)
> 
> As we can see, the `DetectedObjects` outputs react in around ~200 ms, however, the PredictedObjects output takes much more time (around ~600 ms).
> 
> **Future Work:**
> - After solving some compatibility issues, I am planning to make these tests in the main branch
> - The current sensor setup has only 1 lidar, I am planning to use another vehicle setup in the AWSIM which will have more than 1 lidar.

###### @brkay54 (2024-02-05)

> **Weekly Update**
> 
> * Last week, to be able to run the perception pipeline reaction test, we ran the reaction_analyzer by playing rosbag in another terminal. This causes ~10ms time resolution while measuring the reaction times. This week, I made some changes to the reaction analyzer to be able to record the necessary messages of the rosbag and replay them inside the node. In this way, we can measure the reaction times in the system time.
> 
> * 3 Lidar test environment created by using AWSIM, and I can run perception pipeline tests by using them successfully.
> 
> **Sample Test Video:** 
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/a27e5413-684d-4b29-8df8-2c20b7ca5ae4
> 
> 
> * Firstly, I investigated the pointcloud_preprocess pipeline to analyze how much delay we got to get concatenated pointcloud output. For this test, I used 3 Lidar setup and I analyzed the `pipeline_latency_ms` which we added [before](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/6056):
> 
> When I published 3 lidar pointcloud outputs, the pipeline_latency_ms started with a lower latency value:
>  
> ![Screenshot from 2024-02-05 06-11-03](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/24f9abbb-b1be-4318-b38f-e45f3f0572c0)
> 
> After 12 minutes:
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2024-02-05 06-23-43](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/35ae9f05-f27d-4257-b16d-762bc75d8fb6)
> 
> As you can see, the latency value of the concatenated nodelet of the right lidar is accumulating.
> 
> After 10 minutes: 
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2024-02-05 06-32-52](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/c50d3851-b9b5-4332-b718-e6339107fb6e)
> 
> After this higher value, the concatenated pointcloud delay decreases immediately as you can see graph below:
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2024-02-05 06-33-46](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/ef6d6d5f-6512-4aba-8b44-f9527d7f2988)
> 
> It seems to me a weird behavior. After, some time, I thought that it would be caused by phase differences between lidar output publishers. Then, I added another feature to the reaction analyzer to make it able to publish pointcloud outputs synchronically.
> 
> After running the reaction analyzer with synchronically published pointcloud, I couldn't see this accumulated pipeline_latency on the concatenating process:
>  
> ![Screenshot from 2024-02-05 06-57-55](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/45468306/b4061c51-5c60-4a8b-8de3-686dac8ea7c1)
> 
> The concatenated pointcloud delay of the top lidar is higher than others. It is caused by the higher delay of the distortion corrector. Distortion_corrector in the top lidar process takes more time than others because the pointcloud size of the crop_box_filtered_mirror of the top lidar is higher than others. The difference in width between the top lidar and right-left lidars is ~13,000 and it causes ~10ms delay. However, because of this ~10ms delay, the concatenate process is always running with the past pointcloud output of the top lidar. (I didn't try yet but I saw that we can set offset values for the specific pointclouds w.r.t documentation of the concatenate nodelet. I am going to try it.)
>

### #5539 — Reduce excessive error and warning logs on Autoware launch

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-09  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:system
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5539

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When Autoware is executed, it generates a significant number of warning and error logs, despite the system running as expected. The logs are not only excessive but also misrepresent the stability of the running application, as they appear even in the absence of actual functional issues. This creates a noisy debugging environment, making it challenging to identify and address genuine issues.
> 
> The issue was replicated using the latest `main` branch with the planning simulator demo as per the Autoware documentation: [Planning Simulation Tutorial](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/).
> 
> A video demonstrating the issue is available here:
> - [Autoware Error and Warning Logs Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JDXDh1oNaMg)
> 
> The logs from the run that showcase the problem can be found here:
> - [Autoware Logs Gist](https://gist.github.com/xmfcx/aebd2fe8a9a7c08a388aafae69dd110a)
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The primary goal is to clean up the logs by either resolving the underlying causes of the warnings and errors or by adjusting the threat levels if the logs are not indicative of real issues.
> This will aid in de-cluttering the console output, making it easier to debug actual problems, and generally improve the developer experience.
> 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. **Log Analysis**: Go through the logs to determine if the warnings/errors are justified. If they represent real issues, then they should be addressed with bug fixes.
> 2. **Adjust Log Levels**: If the logs are overly cautious and do not represent actual errors or critical warnings, then the log levels should be adjusted accordingly.
> 3. **Code Refactoring**: Inspect the sections of the code-base that are generating these logs and refactor if necessary to prevent false positives.
> 4. **Configuration Tweaks**: Check if the verbosity of the logs can be configured, allowing users to set the desired level of log detail.
> 5. **Documentation Update**: If certain logs are expected and do not indicate problems, this should be clearly documented to avoid confusion. (last resort, not preferred)
> 6. **Incremental Fixing**: Tackle the errors and warnings in batches, creating multiple issues or pull requests to address them systematically.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] The error and warning logs that are not indicative of actual issues are eliminated or their threat levels are adjusted.
> - [ ] The logging output should be clear and should accurately reflect the operational status of Autoware.
> - [ ] Documentation should be updated, if necessary, to reflect any changes made to log management.
> - [ ] Additional issues should be created for any unresolved logs that require further investigation or long-term changes.
> - [ ] The Autoware community agrees that the logging is now informative and not excessively verbose, allowing for effective debugging.

**Comments:**

### #5530 — mission_planner fails when enable_correct_goal_pose param is true

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-11-09  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @beyzanurkaya
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5530

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> There are 2 reasons for this problem:
> 
> 1. The route_handler does not check for overlap lanelets for goal_lanelet, it only checks the closest lanelet to the goal_pose.
> 2. When `enable_correct_goal_pose` is true, the goal_pose is calculated with the closest lanelet to it, disregarding the overlap lanelets. Since this lanelet is not found in the `all_route_lanelets` obtained from the route_handler, the error message` Goal is not valid! Please check position and angle of goal_pose` is sent. No route is being generated.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/32412808/27591fcc-230e-451f-bfa4-1b3a60014d0e
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> All overlap lanelets should be checked to generate a proper route, the shortest among the possible routes should be selected, and the route should be generated.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> There is a proper route available based on the given start and goal positions, but it is not being generated.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. set enable_correct_goal_pose to true
> 2. download [map.zip](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/13305659/map.zip)
> 3. run Psim
> 4. give a goal pose on red dot with a single click  
> ![give-goal-pose](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/32412808/19d1aadb-a195-4211-90a2-b5445397740d)
> 
> 
> ### Versions
>

>

> 
> _No response_
>

> 
> _No response_

### #5495 — vehicle moving in a zig-zag manner even if the path is straight

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-06  |  **Closed:** 2023-12-01  |  **Author:** @KRajeswarRao
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5495

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi
> We've just switched from autoware.ai to autoware.universe. While running the vehicle in autonomous mode, we have observed that the vehicle is moving in a zig-zag manner although the path is completely straight.
> 
> when we set the estimate pose(starting point) of the ego vehicle slant or somewhat tilted, and the goal pose (end point) far away in a straight orientation. generally vehicle should try to align quick and better with centerline. 
> 
> Here in our case, the vehicle is trying to align exactly in the path but it is moving as shown in the images below attached. it is continuously trying to do that and in the process it is crashing out of the path/drivable area.
> But when we keep the vehicle perfectly aligned with the center line and the steering angle is also zero degree then the vehicle is moving in a straight line
> 
> Please suggest what parameters or code needs to be changed.
> ![Screenshot from 2023-10-27 16-33-08](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/83784876/4ade0919-5841-4b37-b861-4ae3a11a7e09)
> ![Screenshot from 2023-10-27 16-09-30](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/83784876/9793164e-86a1-4ffc-8ae4-59ddcf222d3e)
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> vehicle has to align with centerline and move straight even when the initial pose is slightly tilted.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The vehicle is moving in a zig-zag manner when we try to give the initial pose as slightly tilted or the initial steering angle has some degree
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Launch Autoware
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> ROS2
> Autoware universe
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @kosuke55 (2023-11-22)

> @KRajeswarRao 
> If you are using MPC for steer control, it may be helpful to tune the parameters with reference to the following page.
> https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/control/mpc_lateral_controller/

###### @kyoichi-sugahara (2023-12-01)

> @KRajeswarRao 
> If you have further questions related this issue, please feel free to open new issue with pasting this link.
> I will close this issue, for now.

### #5453 — cmake error of TRTEXEC_DEFAULT_BIN string value

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-01  |  **Closed:** 2024-07-08  |  **Author:** @felixfeixu
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:perception
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5453

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In cmake file of autoware.universe/common/trtexec_vendor/CMakeLists.txt, this line has a bug:
> ```
> set(TRTEXEC_DEFAULT_BIN /usr/src/tensorrt/bin/trtexec)
> if(NOT EXISTS TRTEXEC_DEFAULT_BIN)
> ```
> it should be:
> ```
> if(NOT EXISTS ${TRTEXEC_DEFAULT_BIN})
> ```
> please notice the `${}`
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> cmake can detect trtexec bin file 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> cmake failes to detect trtexec even if the file exists
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> run cmake of colcon for this package
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> Ubuntu 22
> humble
> autoware main branch
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @xmfcx (2023-11-01)

> Thank you for bringing this to our attention.
> 
> You're right; it's a typo in the `CMakeLists.txt` file which can cause the described issue.
> 
> Would you be interested in contributing a small PR to fix this?
> If not, we'll address it promptly. We appreciate your help in improving Autoware.

###### @isouf (2023-11-22)

> I am facing the same issue when trying to build the workspace (inside Docker) of the latest autoware `main` branch. I also confirm that the solution proposed by @felixf4xu resolves problem :+1: . Would be good to check and merge the PR https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5464 created by @felixf4xu.

### #5450 — Positioning issue causes oversteering

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-11-01  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @mikechan0731
- **Labels:** priority:low, status:stale, component:localization
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5450

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Bus Positioning Issue Leading to Excessive Turning
> 
> As seen in the video, the bus exhibits excessive turning when making a corner. Initially, the positioning is accurate (the map point cloud aligns with the positioning point cloud). However, after the turn, there's a discrepancy between the map point cloud and the positioning point cloud.
> 
> https://youtu.be/XVD0Epaj_JI
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> In a normal scenario:
> 
> When the bus makes a turn, it should execute the maneuver smoothly without any excessive turning. The positioning should remain consistent throughout the process, with the map point cloud always aligning perfectly with the positioning point cloud, ensuring accurate and stable navigation.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> As seen in the video, the bus exhibits excessive turning when making a corner. Initially, the positioning is accurate (the map point cloud aligns with the positioning point cloud). However, after the turn, there's a discrepancy between the map point cloud and the positioning point cloud.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start the LiDAR and driver
> 2. Use the command given to start the autoware.universe locating part of the program:
> 'ros2 launch autoware_launch autoware.launch.xml map_path:=/home/mfc/maps/itri-map vehicle_model:=cbus_vehicle sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit'
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> 1. Autoware.universe Galactic version of the positioning module 
> 2. Sensor we uses an Lidar (Ouster OS1-64).
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> It is currently hypothesized that the relationship between frame_id: lidar and frame_id: base_link might be incorrect, causing a disconnection during turns. 
> 
> We will adjust the coordinate system relationship in subsequent steps.
> 
> 'ros2 run tf2_ros static_transform_publisher 0.0 0.0 2.0 0.0 0.0 0.0 base_link lidar'
> ->
> 'ros2 run tf2_ros static_transform_publisher 4.3 0.0 2.0 0.0 0.0 0.0 base_link lidar'
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> We will begin by tracing the program's condition based on the aforementioned hypothesis. This issue might not be updated quickly. We will continue to update as per operational needs. For now, you can set aside this problem. Thank you.

**Comments:**

### #5449 — Obstacle stop planner causes slow creep and crash

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-10-31  |  **Closed:** 2024-02-15  |  **Author:** @MrRubyRed
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5449

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Creating a simple scene in scenario_v2 of ego trailing a fake agent via ACC where the fake agent eventually stops, it causes ego to stop pass the stop point and to slowly creep forward onto the stopped agent.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> After the other agent stops, ego should stop and not creep forward.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Ego stops past the obstacle stop line and it subsequently starts to creep forward.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Create an agent that goes forward at constant speed and then stops.
> 2. Have ego in the same lane trailing the vehicle with ACC.
> 3. Make agent stop.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS2
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Condition `if (node_param_.enable_slow_down && latest_slow_down_section_)` inside `ObstacleStopPlannerNode::insertVelocity` is the culprit. The logic makes it so the condition is always satisfied.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @xmfcx (2023-11-01)

> Thank you for bringing this issue to our attention. Your detailed description of the problem provides a solid starting point for us to investigate.
> 
> In order to proceed efficiently and replicate the issue on our end, could you please share the exact scenario configuration you created?
> 
> This will allow us to simulate the same conditions and pinpoint the problem.
> 
> Our planning algorithm developers will take a closer look at this logic in `ObstacleStopPlannerNode::insertVelocity` and its implications on the ACC behavior.

###### @MrRubyRed (2023-11-05)

> @xmfcx I finally tracked the problem down. The issue happens in the `searchPredictedObjects` function, particularly this line:  https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/src/node.cpp#L904C1-L910C10 
> 
> The issue is twofold:
> 1. The intersection polygon previously computed is not really a polygon. A quick debug_ptr_->pushPolygon shows that the intersection is actually a segment of the edge of the collision predicted object. I'm fairly sure the boost intersection geometry operations within the the `searchPredictedObjects` is not quite correct.
> 
> 2. The `collision_point` computed as a result of the `bg::intersection` call is a point on the edge of the `one_step_move_vehicle_polygon` which will (with a bit of noise) cause the previously provided code snippet with the condition `bg::within(collision_point, one_step_move_vehicle_polygon)` to fail, which in turn causes the `planner_data.found_collision_points` to be false.
> 

###### @mehmetdogru (2023-11-09)

> @MrRubyRed 
> 
> Thanks for creating the issue.
> 
> Could you create a PR that solves the problem or could you share a scenario where the issue can be reproduced.

Can you try this PR for your case? And also, if you can create a scenario for this problem, I would be grateful.

### #5443 — Inconsistent driving area between normal driving and avoidance

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-10-30  |  **Closed:** 2024-01-17  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5443

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Example situation: a bus is driving on a curvy narrow road. Because the vehicle is big and the road is narrow, Autoware estimate the vehicle would not be able to drive the curve without leaving the driving area. However if any object is detected close to the driving lane, avoidance module kicks in and extend the driving area, letting the vehicle drive where it would normally stop.
> 
> [avoidance-2023-10-30_17.11.56.webm](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/a075b087-45b1-418c-94ea-47ffa4a6b71c)
> 
> I don't mind Autoware stopping because the road is too narrow, but if the drivable area can increase when there is an obstacle, why should it be different if there nothing around?
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> If autoware can't drive when the road is too narrow, the existence or not of an obstacle around the path should not change that decision.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Drivable area increases.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Planning simulator with big vehicle on a narrow road
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2023-11-02)

> @VRichardJP 
> The area can be expanded dynamically when `dynamic expansion` [is enabled](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/2255356e0164430ed5bc7dd325e3b61e983567a3/autoware_launch/config/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning/behavior_path_planner/drivable_area_expansion.param.yaml#L10C1-L11C1). 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-02)

> @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 Thank you for pointing out.
> My point here is the lack of consistency of the default features. Normal lane driving is "simpler"/"safer" than avoidance, so it makes more sense for autoware to be able to do "more complex" things during normal lane driving than during avoidance manoeuvers (and not the opposite). 
> 
> Or maybe the dynamic expansion feature is new/experimental and will be enabled by default in the future? 

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2023-11-06)

> > Or maybe the dynamic expansion feature is new/experimental and will be enabled by default in the future?
> 
> @VRichardJP 
> Yes, it was found that there are degradation during scenario testing when dynamic expansion is activated. Given that this feature primarily benefits longer vehicles, the decision was made to deactivate it as a default setting. 
> 
> The feature is will be enabled by default once it reaches more mature level.

### #5440 — Planning Fails when driving to a lanelet that is "behind" the current lanelet (Doing a loop). Cannot plan new paths afterwards.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-10-30  |  **Closed:** 2023-10-31  |  **Author:** @danielsanchezaran
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5440

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I am trying to make my vehicle go around a loop conformed by 4 lanelets in Psim. When I set a goal pose that happens to be on the lanelet that is behind the ego vehicle's current lanelet, planning fails and it is no longer possible to select another start and goal. The only way to fix the issue is to restart Autoware. I have confirmed that both halves of the road are drivable and doing "half loops" is possible without problems. 
> 
> In the attached video, I make the vehicle do a loop by setting multiple goals (to prove all the areas are drive able). But, when I try to set a goal that is on the "previous" lanelet (See steps to reproduce for example), planning fails and it is not possible to continue moving the vehicle with no warnings. I can provide a ros2 bag if necessary. 
> 
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/25967964/6230c90b-b9a4-4244-87c0-7dd149350cad
> 
> The only log messages I get are these (Using RelWithDebInfo compilation): 
> 
> [planning_failling.txt](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/13201291/planning_failling.txt)
> I also get the message that some node died but there is no stack trace but I did notice these messages:
> 
> [scenario_selector-26] [WARN] [1698645501.368634568] [route_handler]: [Route Handler] getRouteUuid: Route has not been set yet
> [ERROR] [component_container_mt-29]: process has died [pid 77740, exit code -9, cmd '/opt/ros/humble/lib/rclcpp_components/component_container_mt --ros-args -r __node:=behavior_planning_container -r __ns:=/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning -p use_sim_time:=False -p wheel_radius:=0.1878 -p wheel_width:=0.037 -p wheel_base:=0.4 -p wheel_tread:=0.405 -p front_overhang:=0.23 -p rear_overhang:=0.21 -p left_overhang:=0.06 -p right_overhang:=0.06 -p vehicle_height:=0.52 -p max_steer_angle:=0.7'].
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The car should be able to do the full path and path planning should not fail. It should be possible to set new goals or vehicle position without problems.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Planning fails, "Auto" cannot be selected; there is no path, and it is not possible to generate a new path even by changing start and goal pose of the vehicle. It feels like something is stuck on a loop. 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Open PSim with a loop-like set of lanelets.
> 2. Set a start pose in a given lanelet
> 3. Try to set a goal pose on a "previous" lanelet
> 
> In the given example, I am trying to make the car go from a start pose in lanelet "3" to a goal in lanelet "2"  which is "behind" the current lanelet . 
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/25967964/b5b582dd-5e3f-46b0-be1b-f9c74bac93c5)
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> Ubuntu 22
> ROS2 Humble
> Autoware: Latest
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> It looks like a problem with the route handler that makes the behavior_path_planner die.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> It looks similar (but worse) than the issue presented in [#1715](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/1715). But I believe it is not the same issue. In this case, the problem happens when trying to set a goal to the "previous" lanelet in a loop. Also, there is no mention of planning failing to work afterwards, which I am reporting here. 
> 
> Here is the lanelet map I used for the examples (it happens with other maps too though): 
> [lanelet2_map.zip](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/13201426/lanelet2_map.zip)
>

> I found this issue can be fixed by forcing the car to go through the `PARK` gear when switching from reverse to drive.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/3ac90b08c7a57dca222b5c65734b3ffddbad4d60/common/tier4_control_rviz_plugin/src/tools/manual_controller.cpp#L136-L143

> Unrelated, but there might be a bug with the calculation of the time step `dt`.

> Here it is constant but it should be calculation from the difference in the timestamps of the received `VelocityReport`.

### #5391 — Autoware won't start on a downward slope

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-10-24  |  **Closed:** 2023-11-28  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:control
- **Comments:** 13  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5391

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> This is a problem I have observed on site so I wasn't sure what was the cause, but I could easily reproduce it with the planning simulator.
> 
> In this example, the vehicle has to cross a short hilly road:
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/28a1b00c-28bf-44ae-be35-b494174010f4)
> 
> When the vehicle starts from 0km/h on the upward slope, there is no problem. But if it has to start from the downward slope, then it will simply not move. There is no problem if the vehicle has some velocity. 
> 
> I understand the longitudinal controller adjusts target acceleration based on the slope, but here the vehicle will simply not start at all. I remember that when this happened on our vehicle, the control command sent by Autoware to the vehicle was stuck at `target velocity = 0.25, target acceleration = -0.4`.
> 
> Considering the longitudinal controller is PID based, I would expect the vehicle to reach desired velocity/acceleration even if the slope compensation overshoots. Setting `enable_slope_compensation: false` in the `pid.param.yaml` config file fixes the issue (so it is related to slope compensation logic)
> 
> The video below shows the issue, reproduced with the planning simulator:
> 
> [downward_slope-2023-10-24_14.28.44.webm](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/9d365879-29f2-4420-bfbf-e0308a9c1cf5)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Vehicle should be able to start from downward slope.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Stuck
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Planning simulator + hilly lanelet
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @brkay54 (2023-10-25)

> There is no gravity in planning_simulator, this should be the cause of this behavior in the planning simulator. Because while the vehicle in the slope, there is no force in the x direction. IMO, It is a problem of the simulation.

###### @VRichardJP (2023-10-28)

> @brkay54 I think it is a problem if the slope compensation may stop the vehicle forever. With the PID alone, the vehicle struggles to reach the desired acceleration, but at least it never get stuck.
> 
> A few weeks ago I also had the same issue on a different vehicle. There was a stop line on a road going slightly down. Autoware would often stop at the stop line and never restart. I never understood why autoware was sending negative acceleration values while it was supposed to accelerate. But now I think it was caused by the slope compensation.
> 
> 

###### @brkay54 (2023-11-08)

> @VRichardJP Thank you for the comment and sorry for the late reply.
> 
> > @brkay54 I think it is a problem if the slope compensation may stop the vehicle forever. With the PID alone, the vehicle struggles to reach the desired acceleration, but at least it never get stuck.
> 
> Yes, I think it is a problem too. However, the problem you mentioned above (stucks in psim) is a different issue. This issue is the result of not implementing gravity in psim. Just I want to clarify it.
> 
> > A few weeks ago I also had the same issue on a different vehicle. There was a stop line on a road going slightly down. Autoware would often stop at the stop line and never restart. I never understood why autoware was sending negative acceleration values while it was supposed to accelerate. But now I think it was caused by the slope compensation.
> 
> For the issue that arises in real vehicle tests, I also agree with you. We saw the same problem on our tests too. It is normal to send negative acceleration values in a downward slope but sometimes it can not move the vehicle.
> 
> To avoid this problem, what we did was increase the engage acceleration value. ([here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/5ba1301ca2be42405d18915f1441c22a35b3ad8e/autoware_launch/config/planning/scenario_planning/common/motion_velocity_smoother/motion_velocity_smoother.param.yaml#L29)). 
> 
> However, it was not a good solution. I think to avoid getting the vehicle stuck, we should add another functionality. This functionality should handle this getting stuck problem. IMO, we should add another state to pid_controller called `starting` (currently we have 4 state: stopped - stopping - driving - emengency). In the starting state, if everything is okay and the vehicle is not moving, it should force the vehicle to move smoothly.
> 
> 
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-09)

> I didn't check the current algorithm in details, but I think the PID controller should be able to compensate for overshot slope compensation, no? 
> 
> For example, if target acceleration is +0.25m/s2, PID output +0.2 throttle and slope compensation adds a -0.4. Then initially the brakes are pushed. However if the vehicle does not move with that, then the difference between PID target and actual acceleration will quickly accumulate into the PID integral value. Eventually, the PID output will increase enough to compensate for the overshot slope compensation. But here it does not happen (so I guess the implementation is not exactly that).
> 
> Note that in this case, the PID controller should also be able to start the vehicle in the planning simulator. Actually, the simulator is a good example of slope compensation overshooting since there is no gravity.

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2023-11-10)

> > However, the problem you mentioned above (stucks in psim) is a different issue. This issue is the result of not implementing gravity in psim
> 
> With regards to the PSIM, it currently supports pitch angle consideration from [PR4941](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4941). But recently we found some bug, which should be solved with the following [PR#5501](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5501). 
> 
> >  However if the vehicle does not move with that, then the difference between PID target and actual acceleration will quickly accumulate into the PID integral value. Eventually, the PID output will increase enough to compensate for the overshot slope compensation. But here it does not happen (so I guess the implementation is not exactly that).
> 
> The topic was discussed in the Planning Control WG yesterday ([meeting notes](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3973#:~:text=autowarefoundation/discussions/3872-,Discussion%20Topics,-Autoware%20won%27t%20start)). TIER IV have decided to fix this issue, and we will open a discussion thread soon to present our solution.
> 
> on the side note, @VRichardJP, internally we dont really have a suitable map to test, therefore, is it possible to share your vector map with us, so that we can test our proposal later?

###### @danielsanchezaran (2023-11-10)

> Thank you for reporting this issue @VRichardJP I have oppened an issue to discuss possible solutions [here](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3980)

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-10)

> @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 
> Unfortunately, I don't think I can share that map. But if you like I could create a hilly lanelet2 map on which the issue can be reproduced.

###### @mehmetdogru (2023-11-10)

> @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 
> 
> You can use these maps LeoDrive created for test catalogs, some of them has precise slopes so might be useful:
> 
> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/17a_99Gn6EdIrq8xrybN47hnKBPadECGj?usp=sharing

###### @danielsanchezaran (2023-11-27)

> @VRichardJP this [merged PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5549) introduces a way to enable error integration, even if the ego vehicle is starting from a complete stop. The feature is disabled by default. But it can be enabled by setting the   **enable_integration_at_low_speed** parameter to true; you can also tune how long you want the PID to wait (while the vehicle does not move or moves at a very low speed) before integrating the error by changing the **time_threshold_before_pid_integration**. The parameters can be found here: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/main/autoware_launch/config/control/trajectory_follower/longitudinal/pid.param.yaml You can read more about it here: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/control/pid_longitudinal_controller/README.md#pid-control 
> 
> I believe this feature should be enough to compensate for errors in the slope compensation that were causing your vehicle to not start moving. Please let me know if this solves the issue and the ticket can be closed.
> 
> PD: you might be interested in this PR https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5616 that deals with a slope compensation error during simulation (Psim)

###### @Rrooach (2023-11-02)

> > Could you detail these steps please? We could add this as a test to the CI too.
> 
> Hi, sorry for the late response, I'm little preoccupied by some other work.
> 
> Basically, fuzzing is an automatic testing approach, it uses randomly generated input (most cases are a random buffer) to the program under test,  with the help of Address Sanitizer (ASAN), we detect program's memory error.
> 
> I'd be happy to provide some of the detailed steps: 
> Here we use our customized fuzzer to extract some of the interfaces within autoware, and compile them during alone with the entire autoware project.  
> For the ASAN, we can instrument it by adding external ```CXX_FLAG``` augment with ```-fsanitize=address``` 
> The following is the source code: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kITL_eZA7gpJj5tZky0D-rYS8TgeGmQR/view?usp=sharing
> and the following are the related file path:
> ```bash
> ./fuzz.autoware.universe/perception/bytetrack/lib/fuzz_lapjv.cpp 
> ./fuzz.autoware.universe/perception/bytetrack/lib/fuzz_strack.cpp 
> ./fuzz.autoware.common/autoware_utils/math/fuzz_range.cpp 
> ./fuzz.autoware.universe/control/mpc_lateral_controller/fuzz_lowpass_filter.cpp 
> ./fuzz.autoware.universe/vehicle/raw_vehicle_cmd_converter/fuzz_csv_loader.cpp 
> ./fuzz.autoware.universe/localization/ekf_localizer/fuzz_aged_object_queue.cpp  
> ./fuzz.autoware.universe/common/motion_utils/fuzz_distance.cpp
> ``` 
> The fuzzing process involves using our developed fuzzing tool, but here Im sorry that we can not completely open source that due to some commercial reasons.
> 
> The problem is that the code called some of the tool's API, like
> ```C
> WFUZZ_TEST_ENTRYPOINT(linspace);
> ```
> You can bypass that by directly call them in a main function, and passing external input to the target function.
> 
> > Also checked aged_object_queue bug over @VRichardJP 's investigation,
> 
> For this, since we extract some of the API for testing, here we may introduce some false positive during the test, and in that case Im so sorry for the inconvenience.
> 
> MUCH THANK AGAIN for your kindness and detailed response! 
> For any following question I'd like to provide more information you might need.
> 
> best regard.

### #5297 — RTC Manager reports future objects at -100000.0 distance

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-10-13  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:help-wanted, status:stale, component:planning, component:common
- **Comments:** 14  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5297

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
>

> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In this example, the ego vehicle needs to go through 3 traffic lights to reach the goal point, traffic lights handling is set to manual mode to better understand the situation. Before the first traffic light, the RTC manager panel reports multiple events at a distance of -100000.0:
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/0e360161-bfcc-4d02-bc83-c4a91090dde1)
> 
> When the first traffic light is reached, I press the "Execute Velocity Change" button so that the vehicle can resume its course. Note that when I do this, the traffic light at -100000.0 meters is also enabled:
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/83242b78-2f51-4abf-9b50-540bcd2de861)
> 
> The vehicle drives forward a bit, and reaches the second traffic light, which is already enabled, so the vehicle ignores it. You can see the ID is the same than the previously reported traffic light at -100000.0 distance:
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/535d49fa-c261-4f61-86b5-e619d284ed53)
> 
> Finally the vehicle reaches the third traffic light and wait in front of the stop line as expected:
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/d8747260-8256-418c-b883-b079518c6256)
> 
> 
> ****
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I have 2 problems with this:
> - obviously, the events are not at -100000.0
> - but also, clicking on "Execute Velocity Change" enables too many things at once. The 2 traffic lights are separated by like 200 meters, not to be able to enable only the first one without the second makes the RTCManagerPanel a bit akward to use. It would be nice to have a button for each event reported in the table.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Some future events are reported at -100000.0 distance
> 
> It looks like this value is set [here](https://github.com/tier4/tier4_ad_api_adaptor/blob/a58468edcdaf8698153c85e93fe23807edcb8187/autoware_iv_external_api_adaptor/src/rtc_controller.cpp#L136) when the distance is not finite.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> ?
> 
> ### Versions
>

### #5293 — Obstacle Detection and Avoidance happening even if obstacle(trees) is not in path or drivable area.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-10-12  |  **Closed:** 2024-01-18  |  **Author:** @YashuMessi18
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:perception, component:planning
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5293

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hello.
> We've just switched from autoware.ai to autoware.universe. While running the vehicle in autonomous mode, the vehicle is reacting to obstacles which are not in path or outside drivable area especially trees. Like the point cloud clusters are falling inside the path, and it is treating it as an obstacle. We are using only LIDAR and IMU. We do not have any other sensors.
> 
> Either after detection "It is stopping Or It is trying to avoid that " where generally, it won't be needed. We need the vehicle to not treat it as an obstacle and move as it is until the goal pose.
> 
> Please suggest what to do now or what parameters we need to change such that it doesn't consider it as an obstacle.
> PFA rviz and real time pictures.
> 
> If you see IMG.jpeg, it is real time picture taken by phone, where a small plant is on left side outside drivable area, not in the path as well but vehicle is considering it as an obstacle.
> If you see Screenshot.png, the snippet is taken from rviz, where path is turned yellow and while testing it is stopping over there.
> 
> Similarly, if you see Screenshot(2).png, there are trees across both sides and some of the point clusters formed by that is getting treated as an obstacle and vehicle is getting stopped.
> ![IMG](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/assets/131652348/3df66392-5c2b-48a8-ba5c-8ad137e884a1)
> ![Screenshot](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/assets/131652348/ed871eb4-344e-4d75-9b53-345128d50fc4)
> ![Screenshot(2)](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/assets/131652348/7a46e03e-df0c-49ee-b525-c16b8cd67b07)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
>  We need the vehicle to not treat it as an obstacle and move as it is until the goal pose. 
> 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The vehicle is stopping and chattering a lot or else deviating from the path(avoidance).
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Launch autoware 
> Running with our interface
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> ROS 2
> Autoware.Universe
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Maybe the points cluster created by the lidar is effecting it. Need ideas where we can implement such that the leaves/ branches of the tree way too much above from the vehicle or trees on border of the drivable area isn't being considered an obstacle.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-10-19)

> I think your obstacle detection problem can easily be fixed by cheating on the height of your vehicle. For example, the [sample vehicle launch](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/sample_vehicle_launch/blob/main/sample_vehicle_description/config/vehicle_info.param.yaml) defines a vehicle that is 2.5 meter high. If you set the height for example to 2.0 (or lower), then any points above the threshold will be ignored. There is another parameter for maximum height detection somewhere, but I think "cheating" on the vehicle height is the simplest solution.
> 
> As for avoidance you have multiple options:
> - make sure your PCD map includes all trees/bushes: autoware detection module filters out lidar points that are on the map. Unfortunately, this won't do if there is a lot of wind in your area.
> - reduce the size of the lanelet, so that nothing ever appear on top of the road. Of course, because the lanelet shape is modified, the vehicle may look like it is avoiding the bushes/trees, but at least in a controlled way.
> - if you have no real need for obstacle avoidance, you could also simply disable it in the `autoware_launch` parameters. 

###### @xmfcx (2023-11-01)

> Autoware's obstacle stop planner uses this parameter to filter out high obstacles:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/2255356e0164430ed5bc7dd325e3b61e983567a3/autoware_launch/config/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/motion_planning/obstacle_stop_planner/obstacle_stop_planner.param.yaml#L7
> 
> For this to work correctly, your elevation in the localization and the lanelet2 map should be reliable.
> 
> Also you can adjust the `z_axis_filtering_buffer` under that parameter to add additional height to filter out. (Be careful not to overdo this)
> 
> On a funny side, I've generated a small funny image about this, since autonomous vehicles in general usually struggle with plants hanging from sides :smile: 
> 
> <img src="https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/10751153/ce92ef0a-8e35-49b5-b784-679622d5e29a" width="200">
> 
> > Photo illustration of a whimsical battleground where animated plants are on one side, facing off against futuristic autonomous vehicles branded with 'Autoware' logos on the other. In the sky above, there's a banner that reads 'Plants vs Autoware'. The scene should capture the essence of a playful conflict between nature and technology.
> 
> Please tell us if these suggestions helped your case, so we can close this issue.

###### @mehmetdogru (2023-11-09)

> @YashuMessi18 
> 
> As they are already mentioned;
> 
> - About the obstacles above z axis filter in obstacle_stop_planner is the simplest solution.
> 
> - About the plants hanging on the sides you can modify [this section ](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/0cd5d891a36ac34a32a417205905c109f2bafe7b/autoware_launch/config/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning/behavior_path_planner/avoidance/avoidance.param.yaml#L73-L83)not to avoid unknown objects at all or with much smaller lateral margins
> 
> Does these solve your problem. Is it ok if I close the issue?

###### @stale (2024-01-08)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @mehmetdogru (2024-01-18)

> I am closing the issue since it is stale

### #5252 — The frequency of crop box filter node is lower than normal

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-10-08  |  **Closed:** 2023-10-19  |  **Author:** @beginningfan
- **Labels:** component:sensing
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5252

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I am using a lidar which is robosense-m1. There are many NaN points in its pointcloud.
> The input frequency of `crop box node` is 10hz, but the output is about 6hz.
> It is related to #3112
> ![1](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/103237402/bcd90aac-172a-41c3-b6d1-268416eed8a8)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The output frequency is as same as the input frequency
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The output frequency is much lower than the input frequency.
> After after commenting the `RCLCPP_WARN` in [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/83821d4818cf83ea3bcb14511fc64482859ed7f1/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/crop_box_filter/crop_box_filter_nodelet.cpp#L141C7-L141C18), the output frequency is normal
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Launch Autoware
> Run recorded bag file
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> Ubuntu 22.04
> Humble
> Autoware Universe : main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> There are too many NaN points. Frequent printing leads to excessive system usage
> ![Screenshot from 2023-10-08 14-52-22](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/103237402/fc0dedb8-f163-4f3e-a392-37c74dadf902)
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> We should use `RCLCPP_WARN_ONCE` or `RCLCPP_INFO_THROTTLE` instead of `RCLCPP_WARN`

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-10-08)

> Yes! to add a print in the main loop was not a bright idea.
> 
> Throttling could do, but I would rather count the number of rejected points and move the warning outside the loop. If you are not in a rush, I can do propose a PR next week.
> 
> On another topic, I don't think it is normal to have so many NaNs in your data :)

###### @beginningfan (2023-10-08)

> @VRichardJP There is a pcd file of lidar rs-m1. It has 4743 NaN points in 78750 points. Overall, point clouds can also be used normally. As a comparison, there are also 2117 zero values in the files of Oster64.
> [pcd.zip](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/12840102/pcd.zip)
> 
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-10-12)

> @beginningfan 
> I have created a PR that should fix your issue. Could you confirm?

###### @beginningfan (2023-10-12)

> @VRichardJP  Thanks for your PR. It works well.
> I think [there](https://github.com/VRichardJP/autoware.universe/blob/2bc2257566bae2a3d69cfc6215caa566298fcdbf/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/crop_box_filter/crop_box_filter_nodelet.cpp#L170) should be 100 instead of 1000. The frequency of the pointcloud is 10Hz, so printing once per second seems a bit slow

###### @VRichardJP (2023-10-12)

> I added the throttle to avoid spamming the output/log at 10Hz.
> 
> The point of the message is to warn the user there may be a problem with its data. I think 1 Hz is enough so the warning won't be unnoticed. Still, I don't want to bother the user too much if they decide to ignore the warning.
> 
> Or maybe I'm overthinking? Printing for each input cloud is fine to me too (I don't have NaNs in my sensor data anyway). What do you think?
> 
> 

###### @beginningfan (2023-10-13)

> @VRichardJP You are right. 1Hz is good enouth

This will ensure that we can track and manage it more effectively.

**Body:**

> ### Description
>

>

> 
> From now on the vehicle is freezed and nothing can be done to avoid this situation.
> It is not a problem of vehicle or sensor because it happens also with the sample-vehicle and sample-sensor and with your map.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I expected a different behavior, exactly as in the previous version of the planning: where the vehicle move and reach the goal in the simulation without problem or constraints. It is able also to go out of lane in the parking phase and going out from the park slot. 
> Also trying to reset the initial position nothing changes, the system crashed.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Now the system crashed after the vehicle has reached one/two goals and nothing can be do to avoid it even if I try to reset the initial position.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. launch the docker container: `rocker --nvidia --x11 --network host --devices /dev/vid* --user --volume $HOME/autoware --volume $HOME/autoware_map --volume /dev/shm/:/dev/shm -- ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware-universe:latest-cuda &&
> export RCUTILS_COLORIZED_OUTPUT=1 &&
> export RCUTILS_CONSOLE_OUTPUT_FORMAT="[{severity} {time}] [{name}]: {message} ({function_name}() at {file_name}:{line_number})"`
> 2. `vcs import src < autoware.repos &&
> sudo apt update &&
> rosdep update &&
> rosdep install -y --from-paths src --ignore-src --rosdistro $ROS_DISTRO`
> 3. launch the planning simulation
> 4. set the initial position and goal poses more than once after have reached the previous goal.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS
> - ROS 2: HUMBLE
> - Autoware: docker developer download - your branch is up to date with 'origin/main'
> -  Docker container launched as: `rocker --nvidia --x11 --network host --devices /dev/vid* --user --volume $HOME/autoware --volume $HOME/autoware_map --volume /dev/shm/:/dev/shm -- ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware-universe:latest-cuda &&
> export RCUTILS_COLORIZED_OUTPUT=1 &&
> export RCUTILS_CONSOLE_OUTPUT_FORMAT="[{severity} {time}] [{name}]: {message} ({function_name}() at {file_name}:{line_number})"`
> 
> This happens also in the 'origin/humble' branch
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Not finished to develop the planning stack?
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #5182 — Eliminate `RTC Auto Mode Manager` and control auto/manual mode from config file in the module package

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-09-29  |  **Closed:** 2023-10-07  |  **Author:** @kyoichi-sugahara
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5182

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ---
> ### About RTC
> Whether the planning module operates entirely automatically depends on whether it is in `auto mode` or `manual mode`. The explanation of RTC can be found [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/1caa1b3eeff0190255edb6331753b9f7f752e151/planning/rtc_interface/README.md). 
> For instance, if you operate the intersection module in manual mode, it will not enter the intersection until approved by the RTC side even if the module judge it safe. However, in auto mode, it will proceed without approval as long as the module side determines it to be safe.
> 
> ---
> ### Background
> Currently, the control of `auto mode` and `manual mode` at the time of module startup is realized through the service by the `RTC Auto Mode Manager`. We think that this method has the following two problems:
> - The `RTC Auto Mode Manager` must be aware of the module names.
> - After the `RTC Auto Mode Manager` starts up, it changes each module to auto mode one by one through the service.
> 
> 
> ---
> ### Purpose
> 
> Eliminate the `RTC Auto Mode Manager` and enable switching between auto mode and manual mode through the config file on the module side.
> 
> ---
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Enable switching between `auto mode` and `manual mode` from the module side.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4054
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/435
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3894
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/387
> - [x] Eliminate the `RTC Auto Mode Manager`.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5235
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/625

**Comments:**

###### @kyoichi-sugahara (2023-10-07)

> Eliminated `RTC Auto Mode Manager` with 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/5235
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/625

> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Please use attached lanelet map
> [virtual_G_dev_road_shoulder.zip](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/12744530/virtual_G_dev_road_shoulder.zip)
> 
> 
> 1. Place obstacles to recreate a scene where a complicated trajectory should be generated.
> 2. Repeat the following tests:
>   a. Set ego vehicle initial pose. 
>   b. Set various pattern of goal pose.
> 3. At some point, I encountered the problem described in this issue.
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> - `mutex` in the goal_planner, which runs in multi-threading, may not be operating correctly.
> - During the execution of freespace_planning_algorithms, there is a release of memory in the planner manager module.
> - There might be a standalone bug in Astar.
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> This issue results in an occasional crash of the node, affecting the reliability of the path planning process, and thereby requires prompt attention and resolution.

### #5010 — Pointcloud concatenation fails while input data is empty

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-09-16  |  **Closed:** 2023-09-21  |  **Author:** @amadeuszsz
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5010

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Recently, I struggled with the random dying of an entire pointcloud container after integrating a second sensor. I guess the bug fix #3814 generated a new one which provides possible `nullptr` currently [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/9da75550cb9cc512287a35546256fa8e254daa8e/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/concatenate_data/concatenate_and_time_sync_nodelet.cpp#L463). I've used Ouster lidars and as I noticed, there is a high probability that during initialization the sensor / driver may produce empty pointcloud data. Quick fix solves the issue.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Skipping empty data.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Pointcloud container with all components dies.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Provide dummy topic with empty data or just cover / tape the lidar sensor.
> 2. Run concatenate_data_node from pointcloud_preprocessor package.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @kyoichi-sugahara (2023-09-18)

> @amadeuszsz 
> Sorry if it's not helpful but I hope this information is useful.
> In the planning (and control) module, node dying happens often when empty trajectory/path/pose is received.
> So we created test for some node (not for all node) to check node doesn't get died when empty input is given.
> I introduced [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3723).
> With this kind of test, if you implement some fearture/function teat will fail and you can't merge the PR.
> So it may be useful to avoid the described issue.

### #4998 — Unable to init pose with RViz button after latest pull

- **Labels:** component:localization
- **Comments:** 9  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4998

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I'm unable to give an initial pose in Rviz when running with use_sim_time=true and logging_simulation for system_run_mode. 
> 
> Log file here:
> [
> [launch.log](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/12607855/launch.log)
> ](url)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Init pose using Rviz
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Unable to initialize localization even after giving init pose
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Use sim time = true
> System run mode = logging_simulation
> Give init pose using Rviz initialpose button
> Use a rosbag to test
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-09-14)

> @yaukaizhi Hi!
> When checking the log, I noticed that it contains the message `[localization.pose_estimator.ndt_scan_matcher]: No InputSource.`
> This occurs when the ndt_scan_matcher is unable to subscribe to LiDAR point clouds.
> So please check if LiDAR point clouds are being subscribed correctly.

###### @yaukaizhi (2023-09-14)

> May I know where the Lidar topic is for localization? It has been moved around a few times haha

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-09-14)

> The ndt_scan_matcher subscribes to `/localization/util/downsample/pointcloud`.
> You can know which topic it is subscribing to by using the following command.
> ```
> $ ros2 node info /localization/pose_estimator/ndt_scan_matcher 
> /localization/pose_estimator/ndt_scan_matcher
>   Subscribers:
>     /clock: rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock
>     /localization/kinematic_state: nav_msgs/msg/Odometry
>     /localization/pose_twist_fusion_filter/biased_pose_with_covariance: geometry_msgs/msg/PoseWithCovarianceStamped
>     /localization/util/downsample/pointcloud: sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2
>     /parameter_events: rcl_interfaces/msg/ParameterEvent
>     /sensing/gnss/pose_with_covariance: geometry_msgs/msg/PoseWithCovarianceStamped
> ```
> 
> 
> Alternatively, please refer to [node-diagram](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/design/autoware-architecture/node-diagram/).

###### @VRichardJP (2023-09-14)

> I have faced a similar problem recently after the switch to nebula. I would first check the `/sensing/lidar/*` topics for missing data (e.g. `ros2 topic hz` or `ros2 topic info -v`). 
> 
> 

###### @yaukaizhi (2023-09-15)

> ros2 topic hz /lidar_topic shows 10Hz when playing my rosbag only. But once Autoware launches, ros2 topic hz /lidar_topic says the topic isn't being published. What could cause this?

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-09-15)

> @yaukaizhi Could you share your rosbag? I will try it.

###### @yaukaizhi (2023-09-15)

> Here you go, I realised it's only when perception in autoware_launch is set to true
> https://1drv.ms/u/s!Apo0xLUwYEZdmVClyQuu04hhSK72?e=5P9zYw

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-09-15)

> @yaukaizhi 
> > I realised it's only when perception in autoware_launch is set to true
> 
> Is this isuse resolved?

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-09-15)

> It's not ideal, but I was able to execute the initial position estimation using the following method.
> 
> terminal1
> `ros2 launch autoware_launch logging_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=$HOME/map/sample_map vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit`
> 
> termainal2
> `ros2 run tf2_ros static_transform_publisher 0 0 0 0 0 0 base_link velodyne`
> 
> termainal3
> `ros2 bag play mranti_full.db3 --clock 200 --remap /points_raw:=/sensing/lidar/top/outlier_filtered/pointcloud`
> 
> And give an initial pose from Rviz's 2DPoseEstimate

###### @VRichardJP (2023-09-14)

> The problem might comes from the data layout:
> ```
> fields:
> - name: x
>   offset: 0
>   datatype: 7
>   count: 1
> - name: y
>   offset: 4
>   datatype: 7
>   count: 1
> - name: z
>   offset: 8
>   datatype: 7
>   count: 1
> - name: intensity
>   offset: 16
>   datatype: 7
>   count: 1
> - name: t
>   offset: 20
>   datatype: 6
>   count: 1
> - name: reflectivity
>   offset: 24
>   datatype: 4
>   count: 1
> - name: ring
>   offset: 26
>   datatype: 4
>   count: 1
> - name: ambient
>   offset: 28
>   datatype: 4
>   count: 1
> - name: range
>   offset: 32
>   datatype: 6
>   count: 1
> ```
> 
> Point cloud data layout is defined here: https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/design/autoware-architecture/sensing/data-types/point-cloud/#point-cloud-fields
> 
> Which is now implemented here: https://github.com/tier4/nebula/blob/main/nebula_common/include/nebula_common/point_types.hpp
> 
> ```c++
> struct PointXYZIRCAEDT
> {
>   float x;
>   float y;
>   float z;
>   std::uint8_t intensity;
>   std::uint8_t return_type;
>   std::uint16_t channel;
>   float azimuth;
>   float elevation;
>   float distance;
>   std::uint32_t time_stamp;
> };
> ```
> 
> As you can see, the layout is not exactly the same. There are some fields you don't have, and some you 
>  have that don't exist.
> 
> Unfortunately, [the new nebula module seems not to support Ouster Lidar (yet)](https://github.com/tier4/nebula/tree/main#supported-sensors), so you need to modify the driver you have (or add a conversion node) so you get the same fields than above.
> 
> Not all fields are equaly important. The most important are 'x', 'y', 'z' and 'time_stamp'. In your case you have a time field, but it is named 't'. You should also check what is the format used by this field and make sure it is what Autoware expect. AFAIK, 'channel', 'azimuth' and 'distance' are only used by the ring outlier filter (which is not that important so you could remove it), and the other fields are not used.
> 
>

###### @isouf (2024-02-29)

> @TZECHIN6 
> Here is the _"quick"_  method that I made to convert the pointcloud format. Any improvement recommendations are welcomed. 
> 
> ```cpp
> // Receive the pointcloud from ouster lidar and change the format of the message so that it matches
> // the format the is used in autoware pointcloud_preprocessor filters
> void PointcloudFormatAdaptorNode::onPointcloud(
>   const sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2::ConstSharedPtr pcd)
> {
>   // Initiate output messages
>   auto pointcloud_msg = std::make_shared<sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2>();
> 
>   // Initiate pcl pointcloud message for the input point cloud
>   pcl::PointCloud<pointcloud_format_adaptor::PointXYZITRRAR>::Ptr input_pointcloud(
>     new pcl::PointCloud<pointcloud_format_adaptor::PointXYZITRRAR>);
> 
>   // Convert ros to pcl
>   pcl::fromROSMsg(*pcd, *input_pointcloud);
> 
>   // Initiate pcl pointcloud message for the input point cloud
>   pcl::PointCloud<nebula::drivers::PointXYZIRADT>::Ptr output_pointcloud(
>     new pcl::PointCloud<nebula::drivers::PointXYZIRADT>);
>   output_pointcloud->reserve(input_pointcloud->points.size());
> 
>   // Convert pcl ouster to pcl autoware
>   nebula::drivers::PointXYZIRADT point{};
>   for (const auto & p : input_pointcloud->points) {
>     point.x = p.x;
>     point.y = p.y;
>     point.z = p.z;
>     point.intensity = p.intensity;
>     point.return_type = 0;
>     point.ring = p.ring;
>     point.azimuth = std::atan2(p.y, p.x);
>     point.distance = p.range;
>     point.time_stamp = p.t;
>     output_pointcloud->points.emplace_back(point);
>   }
>   output_pointcloud->header = input_pointcloud->header;
>   output_pointcloud->height = 1;
>   output_pointcloud->width = output_pointcloud->points.size();
> 
>   // Convert pcl to ros
>   pcl::toROSMsg(*output_pointcloud, *pointcloud_msg);
> 
>   // Publish updated pointcloud message
>   pub_pcd_->publish(*pointcloud_msg);
> }
> ```
> 
> The `PointXYZITRRAR` point type is defined on a separate header file as follows:
> 
> ```cpp
> struct PointXYZITRRAR
> {
>   float x;
>   float y;
>   float z;
>   float intensity;
>   std::uint32_t t;
>   std::uint16_t reflectivity;
>   std::uint16_t ring;
>   std::uint16_t ambient;
>   uint32_t range;
>   EIGEN_MAKE_ALIGNED_OPERATOR_NEW
> };
> ```

> Distortion corrector should compensate point cloud while driving over speed bump.

> ### Actual behavior

> Distortion corrector cannot fix point cloud on speed bump.

> > ![Screenshot_2023-09-13-08-24-48-246_org mozilla firefox-edit](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/267490037-44f1bda1-9f24-4ab3-a13f-66a99222de2d.jpg)
> 
> Hello, yes, I am talking about that.

###### @VRichardJP (2023-09-14)

> Indeed, current implementation has not been designed to handle speed bumps.
> Distortion corrector only takes into account linear speed (`twist_it->twist.linear.x`) and yaw rate (`imu_it->vector.z`). To handle speed bumps, it would be necessary to check pitch rate as well (`imu_it->vector.y`).
> 
> I am not sure the math is much harder. However, while absolute linear and yaw acceleration stay usually low (i.e. speed and yaw rate are almost constant at scan level), pitch acceleration goes pretty high when the car hits a speed bump. So for the compensation to work properly, it would be necessary to have well synchronized sensors and high frequency IMU. If there is any delay in the measurement, you would end up with the wrong points being corrected, and the "corrected" result would be worse than the non-corrected one.

> I think moving keep_stopped_steering_convergence parameter from pid_controller to vehicle_cmd_gate is a good option to fix it.
