### #4821 — Accelerate the build process of autoware.universe (mostly behavior_planning packages)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-08-30  |  **Closed:** 2023-09-21  |  **Author:** @soblin
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4821

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Previously I found out that some packages are maybe consuming about 1/3 of its build time just for `preprocessing` due to huge header files.
> 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2773#issuecomment-1546600652
> 
> You can check how to measure the compile time of a single header file on the above thread. This table is the example:
> 
> | file | time |
> | ---- | ------- |
> |tier4_autoware_utils/tier4_autoware_utils.hpp | 9.5 |
> |motion_utils/motion_utils.hpp| 9.7 |
> | route_handler/route_handler.hpp | 14.0 |
> | lanelet2_extension/utility/query.hpp | 4.0 |
> 
> To solve this issue a applied several refactorings that aims to
> 1. avoid include of `tier4_autoware_utils.hpp` and `motion_utils.hpp`
> 2. remove unnecessary includes in `tier4_autoware_utils.hpp` and `motion_utils.hpp`
> 3. export template functions in `motion_utils.hpp` as `extern template`
> 4. include `lanelet2_core/lanelet2_routing/lanelet2_extension/Forward.hpp` as much as possible
> 
> on this branch(https://github.com/soblin/autoware.universe/tree/build-fast/individual/behavior_velocity_planner_common) and measured how much the build time /maximum momory usage decreases.
> 
> I compiled all the files in `behavior_velocity_planner_speed_bump_module` in parallel and measured the process with `time -v` command.
> 
> Without the refactoring,
> ```
>         Command being timed: "./all.sh"
>         User time (seconds): 83.14
>         System time (seconds): 8.26
>         Percent of CPU this job got: 308%
>         Elapsed (wall clock) time (h:mm:ss or m:ss): 0:29.65
>         Average shared text size (kbytes): 0
>         Average unshared data size (kbytes): 0
>         Average stack size (kbytes): 0
>         Average total size (kbytes): 0
>         Maximum resident set size (kbytes): 2260592
>         Average resident set size (kbytes): 0
>         Major (requiring I/O) page faults: 581
>         Minor (reclaiming a frame) page faults: 2463525
>         Voluntary context switches: 11377
>         Involuntary context switches: 970
>         Swaps: 0
>         File system inputs: 121160
>         File system outputs: 375512
>         Socket messages sent: 0
>         Socket messages received: 0
>         Signals delivered: 0
>         Page size (bytes): 4096
>         Exit status: 0
> ```
> 
> After the refactorings,
> ```
>         Command being timed: "./all.sh"
>         User time (seconds): 46.03
>         System time (seconds): 5.06
>         Percent of CPU this job got: 348%
>         Elapsed (wall clock) time (h:mm:ss or m:ss): 0:14.66
>         Average shared text size (kbytes): 0
>         Average unshared data size (kbytes): 0
>         Average stack size (kbytes): 0
>         Average total size (kbytes): 0
>         Maximum resident set size (kbytes): 1351576
>         Average resident set size (kbytes): 0
>         Major (requiring I/O) page faults: 621
>         Minor (reclaiming a frame) page faults: 1449186
>         Voluntary context switches: 31465
>         Involuntary context switches: 625
>         Swaps: 0
>         File system inputs: 163024
>         File system outputs: 178976
>         Socket messages sent: 0
>         Socket messages received: 0
>         Signals delivered: 0
>         Page size (bytes): 4096
>         Exit status: 0
> ```
> 
> You can see the build time / maximum memory usage is reduced by about 50%.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> x
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> This task is ready once
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_common/pull/203
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4819
> 
> are approved. Then I will ship each PR in several steps:
> 
> - Phase1:
>   - remove tier4_autoware_utils.hpp from common/
>   - remove motion_utils.hpp from common/
>   - remove tier4_autoware_utils.hpp from vehicle/
> - Phase2:
>   - remove tier4_autoware_utils.hpp from evaluator/ and simulator/
>   - remove tier4_autoware_utils.hpp from system/
>   - remove tier4_autoware_utils.hpp from localization/
>   - remove tier4_autoware_utils.hpp from perception/
>   - remove tier4_autoware_utils.hpp and motion_utils from planning/
>   - remove tier4_autoware_utils.hpp from control/
> - Phase3:
>   - only include forward declaration of lanelet packages in sensing
>   - only include forward declaration of lanelet packages in perception
>   - only include forward declaration of lanelet packages in control
>   - only include forward declaration of lanelet packages in planning
> - Phase4:
>   - refactor tier4_autoware_utils
>   - refactor motion_utils
>   - refactor behavior_velocity_planner_common

### #4686 — No handling of MGRS grid borders in gnss_poser

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-08-21  |  **Closed:** 2023-10-11  |  **Author:** @kasper-helm
- **Labels:** component:sensing
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4686

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently the UTM to MGRS [conversion](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/gnss_poser/include/gnss_poser/convert.hpp#L161) in gnss_poser does not properly handle the case where you cross from one grid into another. I have seen cases where e.g. the mgrs.x position crosses the 100000m mark and then wraps around to 0m, creating a large jump. 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Pose output from gnss_poser should be smooth and continuous, without large jumps. 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> gnss_poser outputs large jumps in position (100 km).
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> - Drive in an area where an MGRS grid line is crossed (e.g. I saw this happen when crossing from 10SEF to 10SFF, south of the SF Bay Area.
> - Have a gnss unit running which is feeding lat/long data to gnss_poser, and the latter is set to use MGRS
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> This seems to be handled properly in Eagleye/llh_converter https://github.com/MapIV/llh_converter/blob/main/src/llh_converter.cpp#L433
> but it would be good to have it here as well since we encountered other issues that prevent us from using Eagleye.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-08-22)

> One change I think I have proposed long ago is to move coordinate conversion logic to its own library, put coordinate system related params in a yaml file along with the PCD and lanelet2 maps, and load them as global parameters (like the vehicle description).
> 
> I have been using this internally for a while and I think it makes more sense: first because lanelet2 map and PCD map points are both expressed in a fixed coordinate system, so it makes little sense to infer e.g. MGRS code at runtime; second because it is then easy to add coordinate conversion features to other nodes (e.g. FMS interface node).
> 
> As a side effect, all map coordinates are always expressed in a fixed reference system (whether it is UTM, MGRS or arbitrary), so there is no wrap around issue (e.g you can have x=12345.0 and y=-123.45). 

###### @kminoda (2023-08-22)

> Hi kasper, 
> I am in charge of this topic, and are now merging the patches to address such situation. Although we are having a bit of delay, I suppose we can merge all the patches within September.
> This discussion may also be a help: https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3582

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-09-29)

> @kminoda 
> >  I suppose we can merge all the patches within September.
> 
> Is it done?

###### @kminoda (2023-10-01)

> (@YamatoAndo Thanks for checking)
> 
> This issue has been overcome with multiple projection type support. If you are operating in some areas that overlaps multiple MGRS grids, you may use `LOCAL_CARTESIAN_UTM` or `TRANSVERSE_MARCATOR` as stated in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/map/map_projection_loader/README.md. By setting `map_projector_info.yaml` properly, the whole Autoware system now converts all the coordinates accordingly (except PCD file, you still need to prepare PCD in the desired coordinate beforehand). Note that eagleye is currently not supported, but will be shortly.

###### @kminoda (2023-10-11)

> @kasper-helm I will close this issue since it was resolved as describe above. But feel free to open this again if you still have troubles. Thanks.

### #4680 — roi pointcloud fusion for small objects detection

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-08-21  |  **Closed:** 2023-11-10  |  **Author:** @badai-nguyen
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:perception
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4680

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> - Vehicle sensor configuration with low resolution LiDAR is limited to detect small objects such as traffic cones since too few points are hit the object and Euclidean cluster failure to cluster those objects. 
> - The analysis shows that current roi_cluster_fusion on sample vehicle is only able detected traffic cones in range between 19m~49m in ideal flat road. It's narrower in the real test and clustering is applied after ground segmentation filter and compare map segmentation filter.
> 
> | cone size | IoU > 0 range | 
> | - | - |
> | ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/94814556/0f5eccb5-b8f7-4ca0-819e-d5f7be9ac301) |![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/94814556/083f85f7-69e5-45cf-b0fa-1ded33b4c8b4)|
> 
> 
>  
> - [min_cluster_size: 10](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/2796d0a2115398f5479d95990dc72deabd09942d/autoware_launch/config/perception/object_recognition/detection/clustering/voxel_grid_based_euclidean_cluster.param.yaml#L6) could be change to small to improve small object clustering. However, Euclidean cluster FP unknown objects output also increase rapidly because of noise pointcloud.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The 2D image detection model like YOLOX may be strong to handle such unexpected small objects even in quite long distance. 
> A new approach which more relies on  2D image detector result and use LiDAR cloud as validation as well as depth information could solve this issue.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Reduce min_cluster_size to cluster cones for roi_cluster_fusion and process the output of fusion to reduce noise unknown object 
> - Add roi pointcloud fusion and focus on small objects ROIs fusion result to cluster/detect the small objects
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - Successful detected small objects such as traffic cones with less points cloud if recoginzed by 2d image detector.

**Comments:**

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
>

> @badai-nguyen Is this issue already resolved? Or this includes current development item?

> @miursh I think the neccessary PRs for this issue are allready merged. The accuracy of this approach also is depend on the performace of Yolox-s model which may need more time to collect and annotate the data, and retrain the model. So I will close this issue.

###### @VRichardJP (2023-08-22)

> I have not check in details how the parking planner is implemented, but I notice your example the vehicle is driving very close from the drivable area boundaries, which is the same than driving very close from an obstacle.
> 
> As you can see, the drivable area is updated constantly. Even if it does not change much,the changes might be enough so that a path that was considered safe is not acceptable anymore. In such case, Autoware has no choice but to generate a new path, which might be rejected 1 second later for the very same reason.
> 
> Rather than a quantization, I think this problem is inherent to A*. In particular because the algorithm does not use any soft constraint: a path that goes 1mm close from a wall is as valid as a path that stays far from every obstacle.

### #4563 — Definition of the control output command is little confusing

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-08-08  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @brkay54
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:control
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4563

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> cc. @TakaHoribe @mehmetdogru 
> Hello everyone I want to report a confusion about the low side of the controller. 
> 
> Firstly, I want to clarify two things about the commands we send to the low-level controller:
> 
> - Reference acceleration: the acceleration vehicle should gain while driving on the road. 
> - Thrust: The command we send to the vehicle to accelerate to the reference acceleration.
> 
> In the current implementation, we are calculating the reference acceleration in `pid_longitudinal_controller` by using the FF (acceleration from the planning side), PID output, slope, and delay compensation. However, the compensation side should be made in thrust calculation.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Split the thrust and reference acceleration.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> I want to propose a solution for handling this difference:
> 
> - The mission of the `pid_longitudinal_control` is the calculate the reference acceleration for the vehicle by using the velocity feedback (also because of this, we should make FF control optional)
> 
> - We should make the `raw_vehicle_cmd_converter` more capable, I am planning to add the following features:
> * Start/Stop calibration: like [here](https://github.com/tier4/CalibrationTools/tree/tier4/universe/control/stop_accel_evaluator), this node should handle the start stop situation.
> 
> * Stop hold and hill take off
> 
> * Slope compensation
> 
> * Maybe compensation for the actuators' delays. I am thinking about it, please feel free to share your opinion.
> 
> Also, users should be able to select the output of the autoware, `raw_vehicle_cmd_converter` will be able to give output as an actuator command or Ackermann Control Cmd.
> 
> If you have any comments, please feel free to share them with me!
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Currently working on a vehicle to implement these features.

**Comments:**

###### @takayuki5168 (2023-08-08)

> @brkay54 Hi, can I ask you more about the reason for splitting into the reference acceleration and thrust? I don't understand the motivation.
> 
> I think the delay compensation cannot be removed from the PID-based feedback controller. If the controller does not know the delay and the target velocity inside the controller is without the delay, how do we apply the delay to the controller's output?

###### @brkay54 (2023-08-09)

> > @brkay54 Hi, can I ask you more about the reason for splitting into the reference acceleration and thrust? I don't understand the motivation.
> 
> Hi @takayuki5168, my motivation is to make more configurable control output for Autoware users. Some users may try Autoware on more primitive ECUs, so we should give them a place to help to integrate it into their vehicles. 
> 
> I think `raw_vehicle_cmd_converter` is a good place for this purpose because it sends actuator commands. I propose that we should make it more configurable. For example; brake and gas are not the same mechanism so the user can define some parameters for both like delay. But I don't know how to implement it yet. On the other side, I want to add the features I mentioned above.
>  
>  Also, in Autoware, all modules use acceleration without gravity. For example, in the controller, we are using acceleration from the planning side as FF output but it does not include gravity or the same for state estimation. So, I propose that control modules in Autoware do not take into account the gravitational things, It only sends the reference acceleration for the vehicle. And, `raw_vehicle_cmd_converter` implement these autoware2vehicle things for the user.
> 
> > I think the delay compensation cannot be removed from the PID-based feedback controller. If the controller does not know the delay and the target velocity inside the controller is without the delay, how do we apply the delay to the controller's output?
> 
> Yes, you are right. I am currently thinking about that. Maybe, Autoware should handle only the state estimation delay and delay for the actuators handled by ECU or `raw_vehicle_cmd_converter`. As I said, I am still thinking about it. However, it is better to start by implementing the other features I mentioned above. The delay compensation should be a future improvement.

###### @brkay54 (2023-08-13)

> @takayuki5168 To handle delay compensation in different node, we can create a control command array in the longitudinal controller. Hence, raw_vehicle_cmd_converter can handle the delays for different actuators.
> 
> I will create detailed work about it.
> 
> Related discussions (thx to @maxime-clem ):
> https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2458
> https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2461

###### @TakaHoribe (2023-08-17)

> @brkay54 Thank you for raising the issue.
> 
> The concept of these nodes is clear:
> - longitudinal/lateral controller: calculates a control command to follow the target trajectory
>   - common features that do not depend on the vehicle/DBW interface should be implemented here.
> - raw_vehicle_cmd_converter: converts the control command to the vehicle-specific signals (e.g. throttle, brake, gas, voltage, torque)
> 
> The "vehicle adaptation design" section in this document could be useful for the explanation.
> https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/design/autoware-architecture/control/#vehicle-adaptation-design
> 
> >my motivation is to make more configurable control output for Autoware users. Some users may try Autoware on more primitive ECUs, so we should give them a place to help to integrate it into their vehicles.
> 
> Therefore, the current design for the configuration is:
> - For users who want to use the generalized command (target velocity, acceleration), they can use the output of the control module directly. 
> - For users who want to use the vehicle-specific command (gas, throttle, voltage), they can use the raw_vehicle_cmd_converter to convert the control module output to their specific command.
> 
> Does this solve your confusion?
> 
> ------
> 
> > However, the compensation side should be made in thrust calculation.
> 
> I'm not sure I'm seeing your real issue, but this is true. Some compensation (e.g. delay compensation) should be done in the raw_vehicle_cmd_converter since it can consider the vehicle-specific information.
> For example, now the delay compensation is applied for the `acceleration`, but there may be different time delays in throttle and brake. The information is only known by the `raw_vehicle_cmd_converter`. To achieve this, using the control command array sounds reasonable.
> What do you think?

###### @TakaHoribe (2023-08-17)

> @brkay54 
> >The mission of the pid_longitudinal_control is the calculate the reference acceleration for the vehicle by using the velocity feedback (also because of this, we should make FF control optional)
> 
> I don't get why the FF should be optional. The mission of the longitudinal controller is to make the reference acceleration to follow the target trajectory. It does not care about the algorithm. (Of course the FF can be optional for some users who want to turn off the feature.)
> 
> > - Stop hold and hill take off
> > - Slope compensation
> 
> Would you explain more why you think these features should be in the raw_vehicle_cmd_converter? 
> Because, if these features can be generalized (these features can be designed without vehicle-specific information), it should be implemented not in the raw_vehicle_cmd_converter. Some example cases are helpful for me to understand well.

###### @brkay54 (2023-08-17)

> @TakaHoribe Thank you for the explanation, it is beneficial!
> 
> >     * For users who want to use the generalized command (target velocity, acceleration), they can use the output of the control module directly.
> > 
> >     * For users who want to use the vehicle-specific command (gas, throttle, voltage), they can use the raw_vehicle_cmd_converter to convert the control module output to their specific command.

> As you said, the longitudinal controller sends the necessary acceleration vehicle should get to come close to trajectory acceleration but It is not responsible to reach that acceleration value, it only sends the reference acceleration the vehicle should be to reach that velocity. 
> 
> If the user's vehicle is supporting the acceleration command, the user can use it directly because the vehicle can already calculate its own thrust value to reach that acceleration. However, the vehicle may not support the acceleration commands, so another module is needed to create thrust value, it is raw_vehicle_cmd_converter. 
> 
> What I want to propose is that the PID controller only calculates the reference acceleration values in some time horizon, and if the vehicle is not capable, raw_vehicle_cmd_converter should calculate necessary vehicle-specific outputs by using the reference acceleration values in the time horizon.
> 
> While raw_vehicle_cmd_converter calculates the necessary thrust, it should make the compensations that are needed because of the environment and vehicle, like slope, brake, and gas pedal delays. The PID controller should not be responsible for these calculations because if these calculations are made, the output won't be acceleration it will be thrust value I think it increases the complexity of the design.

> > > The mission of the pid_longitudinal_control is the calculate the reference acceleration for the vehicle by using the velocity feedback (also because of this, we should make FF control optional)
> >

> > Would you explain more why you think these features should be in the raw_vehicle_cmd_converter? Because, if these features can be generalized (these features can be designed without vehicle-specific information), it should be implemented not in the raw_vehicle_cmd_converter. Some example cases are helpful for me to understand well.
> 
> For the slope compensation, of course, it can be implemented in the PID controller but like said above after it is implemented there, the output won't be reference acceleration anymore.
> 
> For stop hold and hill take off, I am open to another method but it needs some operations on the brake and gas pedal, after setting the reference acceleration, the vehicle moves backward while in time we take off the brake and press the gas. So I think we implement these features in raw_vehicle_cmd_converter.

### #4510 — `/perception/traffic_light_recognition/traffic_signals` message type inconsistency

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-08-03  |  **Closed:** 2023-09-06  |  **Author:** @lchojnack
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4510

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Trying to subscribe the `/perception/traffic_light_recognition/traffic_signals` topic, I've got the message
> ```
> Cannot echo topic '/perception/traffic_light_recognition/traffic_signals', as it contains more than one type: [autoware_auto_perception_msgs/msg/TrafficSignalArray, autoware_perception_msgs/msg/TrafficSignalArray]
> ```
> 
> The issue appears because `traffic_light_arbiter` node publishes the message with type `autoware_perception_msgs/msg/TrafficSignalArray` and `behavior_velocity_planner` [subscribes the topic](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/node.cpp#L104) with `autoware_auto_perception_msgs/msg/TrafficSignalArray` type as presented in the picture below
> 
> 
> ![Screenshot_20230803_153847](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/8416175/bfec1d38-e88b-4f1f-897e-9e4bf2ac65cd)
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> It is possible to subscribe the `/perception/traffic_light_recognition/traffic_signals` by using `ros2 topic echo` command
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> <img width="1394" alt="Screenshot_20230803_155257" src="https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/8416175/e57fd901-879c-47c8-a35d-a313c34353fb">
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Run Autoware e.g.
> ```
> ros2 launch autoware_launch e2e_simulator.launch.xml vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=awsim_sensor_kit map_path:=$HOME/autoware_map/nishishinjuku_autoware_map/
> ````
> 2. In another terminal run
> ```
> ros2 topic echo /perception/traffic_light_recognition/traffic_signals
> ```
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS: humble
> - autoware.universe branch `main`  commit `2f282edb474aabb071746e4ed0f6ff2b0f3403db`
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @isamu-takagi (2023-08-04)

> Looks like this PR (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4133) will solve it.

### #4505 — `/planning/scenario_planning/trajectory` stops to generate trajectory while driving.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-08-03  |  **Closed:** 2023-08-08  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 9  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4505

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hello team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware on Carla, and I found that **sometimes the planning module does not generate a path and makes the ego vehicle stop.**
> 
> Here's a video for RViz: [[video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1N40d4FtEIKhL1CpqO4kAOkE83qF8tHVR/view?usp=sharing)]
> 
> From 0:18 of the video, you can see that the trajectory is not updated and the car eventually stops after passing the last point of the trajectory.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I expected the trajectory to be generated well, so that the car could drive well without stuck.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The trajectory is not generated and the ego vehicle stops.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> - Ros2 bag record file: [[rosbag](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ihQTqVg5yolf1RVwYQBIWJbUtDEZZMTe?usp=sharing)]
> - Map file: [[lanelet](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vm9SvalJe7Bc9sh_8jK-0cPulVAov5uD/view?usp=drive_link)] [[pcd](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MvJlfjkw3LWFUs5hdE_KQ2_CQTusU8UN/view?usp=drive_link)]
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> I ran the experiment on the container from the image [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe/70625594?tag=humble-20230215-prebuilt-cuda-amd64).
> Carla version: 0.9.13
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> After some investigation by myself, I found that the messages from the topic `/planning/scenario_planning/trajectory` is no longer generated.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @maxime-clem (2023-08-03)

> It looks like one of the planning node crashes. Are you able to share your log files ? You can find usually find it in `$HOME/.ros/log/[[DATE_AND_USER]]/launch.log`.

###### @Kim-mins (2023-08-03)

> Thank you for the response @maxime-clem!!
> 
> I could find many logs in the directory you mentioned! thank you!
> But sadly, I ran the scenario about 2 weeks ago, so I cannot find the log file corresponds to the video.
> 
> So I just ran Autoware with the same scenario, and it made a similar situation.
> Here's the log file: [[log](https://drive.google.com/file/d/14CHSW41UU2y-2VkkuKk20eZZsPPwXwkb/view?usp=sharing)].

###### @maxime-clem (2023-08-03)

> The `lidar_centerpoint_node` dies first but it may not be related to the issue.
> > 1691037289.4402609 [ERROR] [lidar_centerpoint_node-42]: process has died  ...
> 
> The issue comes from the motion planner crashing.
> > 1691037432.1712468 [component_container_mt-59] terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
> > 1691037432.1713648 [component_container_mt-59]   what():  Points is empty.
> > 1691037432.2907925 [ERROR] [component_container_mt-59]: process has died [pid 1064, exit code -6, cmd '/opt/ros/humble/lib/rclcpp_components/component_container_mt --ros-args -r __node:=motion_planning_container -r __ns:=/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/motion_planning -p use_sim_time:=True -p wheel_radius:=0.383 -p wheel_width:=0.235 -p wheel_base:=2.79 -p wheel_tread:=1.64 -p front_overhang:=1.0 -p rear_overhang:=1.1 -p left_overhang:=0.128 -p right_overhang:=0.128 -p vehicle_height:=2.5 -p max_steer_angle:=0.7'].
> 
> I think this crash has already been fixed with the latest version of universe.
> Are you able to try a more recent version (the one you are using is 6 months old) ?
> 

###### @Kim-mins (2023-08-03)

> Thank you for more investigation!!
> Yes sure. I'll try the latest version and tell you the result soon.
> By the way, is the crash from my bad configurations or originated from the Autoware itself?
> Maybe I should change my settings if the crash is from my side.

###### @maxime-clem (2023-08-03)

> I think the crash is an issue with the Autoware code as the nodes should never crash.
> You should not have to change any setting on your side.
> If the issue still occurs with a more recent version, then there may be a bug that needs to be fixed.

###### @Kim-mins (2023-08-03)

> I see. Thank you for the answer.
> I'll try the latest version soon.

###### @Kim-mins (2023-08-07)

> Hi @maxime-clem!
> 
> I ran the same driving scenario with the (comparatively) recent version (2023/07/15) of Autoware, and **there was no issue**.
> Sorry for bothering you. I should have tested the issue on the latest version first..
> 
> By the way, I've experienced the (probably) same kind of errors on other scenarios. 
> Could you please tell me whether I can say they have the same root cause with the current issue?
> I also checked the errors below do not occur on the 2023/07/15 version of Autoware.
> - Case 1: [[video]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FNdE4RNqLb9XoeQIdY2Sa26-uvfL-oOz/view?usp=sharing)[[launch.log]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1b7wS3hZQhstNrR_OSUl6rTyNdyL7OaJs/view?usp=sharing)
> - Case 2: [[video]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/11W5xFGXsHiMIwffQl-D8i0moLhPQUkF3/view?usp=sharing)[[launch.log]](https://drive.google.com/file/d/159ZR8bGCUZacX6LuNzqfPeKnST2yhjM0/view?usp=sharing)
> 
> I thought they are on the same issue because I saw the same crash message of motion planner as you mentioned above on each launch.log file.

###### @maxime-clem (2023-08-07)

> I am happy to hear that using the latest version solved the issue.
> From the video and the log it does look like the same issue (some motion planning module crashes and the trajectory is no longer updated).
> 

###### @Kim-mins (2023-08-08)

> Thank you for answering!! I really appreciate to your help!
> I'll close this issue since this is not the issue now.

### #4498 — control_performance_analysis crashes with segfault

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-08-01  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @kasper-helm
- **Labels:** status:help-wanted, status:stale, component:control
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4498

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I have seen `control_performance_analysis` crash when the `idx_prev_wp_` pointer is not initialized, and is dereferenced on https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/control/control_performance_analysis/src/control_performance_analysis_core.cpp#L378
> 
> - this happens when the ego is either beyond `acceptable_max_distance_to_waypoint_` from the trajectory, or the heading error is larger than `acceptable_max_yaw_difference_rad_`, which causes [`closest_segment`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/control/control_performance_analysis/src/control_performance_analysis_core.cpp#L92) to be empty, and the `idx_prev_wp_` to remain uninitialized 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The node should safely handle the case where `closest_segment` is empty 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> ```
> [ERROR] [control_performance_analysis_exe-24]: process has died [pid 216, exit code -11, cmd ...
> ```
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> - I am using a pre-defined fixed `Trajectory` message to test the Autoware control component without the planning component
> - This issue occurs when the localization initializes while the vehicle is somewhat far (> a few meters) from the trajectory
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @kyoichi-sugahara (2024-02-17)

> @kasper-helm 
> Thank you so much for your report and sorry for late response :sob: 
> If it's possible, could you give me the information how to reproduce problem?
> (e.g. which version of autoware you are using, how did you launch autoware, which comman did you run to publish trajectory.
> 

###### @kasper-helm (2024-02-20)

> I think I fixed it by adding the following line above https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/control/control_performance_analysis/src/control_performance_analysis_core.cpp#L378
> 
> `  if (!idx_prev_wp_) {
>     return std::nullopt;
>   }`

> 
> ### Description
> 
>  We have so many [`build-and-test-differential` jobs queued up.](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/actions/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml?query=is%3Aqueued)

> 
> </details>
> 
> We currently have 2 runners just dedicated to run them.
> 1. ec2 c6a.xlarge: 4c4t (EPYC V3) 8gb
> 2. leo-copper pc: 4c8t (7820HK) 32gb
> 
> And these machines are just dedicated to run this `build-and-test-differential` and `clang-tidy-differential` actions only.

> But still, they take so much time on build action.
> 
> A good example to analyze is this job:
> [feat(crosswalk): suppress chattering of GO/STOP decision](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/actions/runs/5725728049/job/15514775990)

>   
> </details>
> 
> And these 186 packages include the infamous `behavior_path_planner` and almost all of the `behavior_velocity_x_module`s.
> 
> This is a waste of time and we can avoid all these and only build the single package. I will explain the plan below.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - To reduce the time wasted in CI machines
> - To reduce the queue in CI
> - To help users get feedback from CI faster
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> It's simple.
> 
> #### Approach 1, upload and download the build artifact
> 
> After a commit is made to the main branch,
> - Update the packages to whatever latest, similar to the build
> - Build the entire Autoware at that time (basically [build-and-test job](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/actions/runs/5727526598/job/15520116853))
> - Upload the compressed `autoware` folder as an artifact. (These are stored for 90 days by default, we can also increase the duration.)
> - In this `build-and-test-differential` job, after pulling the build environment, we run [download-workflow-artifact](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/download-workflow-artifact) to download the artifact from that workflow.
> - We decompress the `autoware` folder and checkout to this repository's branch in `autoware.universe`.
> - Now that we have everything already built,
>    - Instead of `colcon build --packages-above-and-dependencies`
>    - We can run `colcon build --packages-select`
>    - For the example given above, we will only build a single package.
> 
> #### Approach 2 (preferred), push the built version as a docker image
> 
> Another approach can be to build a docker image in the `build-and-test` with following layers:
> - base image
> - the changes made to update the system
> - the changes made to build the autoware
> And push it to the registry.
> 
> `build-and-test-differential` job can use this image as the base image.
> 
> This is much simpler and can be achieved faster probably.
> 
> With these approaches,
> [feat(crosswalk): suppress chattering of GO/STOP decision](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/actions/runs/5725728049/job/15514775990) will take like 4m instead of 40m
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> #### Approach 1:
> 
> - [ ] Modify the [build-and-test.yaml](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-and-test.yaml) to upload the artifact after it successfully builds.
> - [ ] Modify the [build-and-test-differential.yaml](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml) to:
>    - [ ] Download the artifact using [download-workflow-artifact](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/download-workflow-artifact)
>    - [ ] Extract and use it as the `autoware` folder instead of pulling
>    - [ ] Also pull the latest branch in the `autoware.universe` repository
>    - [ ] Build only the packages modified, not their dependencies
> 
> #### Approach 2 (preferred):
> 
> - [ ] Modify the [build-and-test.yaml](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-and-test.yaml) to build and push the `prebuilt` image of the `autoware`.
> - [ ] Modify the [build-and-test-differential.yaml](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml) to:
>    - [ ] Pull the `prebuilt` image instead
>    - [ ] Also pull the latest branch in the `autoware.universe` repository
>    - [ ] Build only the packages modified, not their dependencies

### #4490 — Autoware sometimes stuck in the middle of a parking scenario

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-08-01  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @TakaHoribe
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4490

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Even though the Planning module is still in the middle of the sequence, the goal decision is made by the `misiion_planner` with a large yaw angle error, and the state of Autoware is transited to STOP.
> 
> Changing the [goal threshold](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/mission_planner/config/mission_planner.param.yaml) in the `mission_planner` can improve the behavior, but it will cause other issues like the goal decision will never be made due to poor control performance.
> 
> The essential issue is that the goal decision is made without considering the status of the Planning and Control.
> 
> In the following picture, the planning is still making the trajectory to fix the yaw angle, but the goal decision is made and the Autoware will not move.
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/21360593/a03b9b82-d819-45ee-a75e-2a6738f520ce)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The goal decision can appropriately consider the status of the planning process.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Goal decision is made in the middle of the planning process.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. run Psim
> 2. test the freespace planner
> 3. the issue sometimes happen
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> autoware.universe version: 2212b003ad5efb7f0baba221c976d0c8801ad236
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @TakaHoribe (2023-08-01)

> cc. @yukkysaito @isamu-takagi 

###### @isamu-takagi (2023-08-03)

> @TakaHoribe The mission_planner receives the goal pose and does arrival check with [its own parameters](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/mission_planner/config/mission_planner.param.yaml#L4-L6). Since this parameter does not reflect the control parameter, I think the arrival check should be moved to a path planning or control module that knows the control parameter.

###### @stale (2023-10-06)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @ralwing (2025-12-17)

> 
> <img width="681" height="994" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18ad6240-802c-4c0b-b4f0-a1b53927a37e" />

### #4443 — new ground_segmentation filter 

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-07-28  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @yusufy1ld1z
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:perception
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4443

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> There are many ground points in the output of the current ground filter. I have tried the algorithm accepted by RA-L with IROS'22 option named "TRAVEL: Traversable Ground and Above-Ground Object Segmentation using Graph Representation for 3D LiDAR Scans". The proposed algorithm is sensible and works better in accuracy and processing time than the scan_ground_filter. Due to the fact that this project is licensed with GPL-3.0, I am rewriting the code, making it more performant, and also adapting to Autoware stack by adding pointcloud_preprocessor, etc.
> There is an comparison video of two algorithms : 
> https://youtu.be/VkzRjY9xLdk
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To give more precise output by the obstacle_segmentation/ground_filter with lowering the processing_time_ms.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Adding the travel_ground_filter among the other filters as an option
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - Rewriting the code to license it with Apache-2.0
> - Adapt to Autoware stack and add some features like pointcloud_preprocessor
> - Adjust the launch files by including the new method
> 

**Comments:**

### #4425 — object_merger removes obsacles around known object

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-07-27  |  **Closed:** 2023-08-07  |  **Author:** @mebasoglu
- **Labels:** component:perception
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4425

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> With the default parameters, object_merger node removes the unknown obstacles around a known object. Even though `CAR-UNKNOWN` and `UNKNOWN-CAR` parameters in `can_assign_matrix` are activated, object_merger cannot merge them. Here are photos for the current situation. The first one shows the scenario. The obstacle inside the red circle is removed by object_merger.
> 
> 
> ![IMG_20230726_143014](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/13589149/85deaeb6-42cb-45a5-8d04-4ecadd485bff)
> 
> Here is the RViz2 screen. The removed unknown object is in the red circle.
> 
> ![default_params](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/13589149/98029034-8b8f-4c28-b01e-494de18e48b8)
> 
> Here is the output of camera lidar fusion:
> 
> ![camera_lidar_fusion](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/13589149/d8f3eebf-f257-4369-bb40-5b96e2ee62a5)
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The unknown object in front of the ego vehicle should not be removed.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The unknown object in front of the vehicle is removed by the object_merger.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Launch centerpoint detection and camera_lidar_fusion.
> 2. Launch object_merger with the ouput of detections with default parameters.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS 2: Humble
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> object_merger cannot merge unknown objects and known objects properly. To remove unknown objects inside a known object, `remove_overlapped_unknown_objects` part was added. If the merging is good, there won't be need for `remove_overlapped_unknown_objects`.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @miursh (2023-08-01)

> @badai-nguyen is also working this issue. 
> By tuning the g_iou threshold or defining g_iou threshold for each class.

###### @miursh (2023-08-04)

> @mebasoglu 
> #4499 is merged. Could you please check how this will look using the latest universe?

###### @mebasoglu (2023-08-04)

> Hello, I tested it with a bag file and It worked, thank you. I am going to test it also on our vehicle and I will let you know as soon as I try on the vehicle. The `generalized_iou_threshold` as `-0.1` for CAR-UNKNOWN seems to be working correctly.

###### @mebasoglu (2023-08-07)

> Hello, we have tested this and it works. We can close the issue. Here is an image of `object_merger` merges known and unknown objects successfully:
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/13589149/b6e00fd1-603f-41c9-811c-ba619210f78d)

### #4421 — [pointcloud_preprocessor] launchfile broken on Humble

- **Labels:** component:perception
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4421

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Regression on `humble` for the `pointcloud_preprocessor` launchfiles.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> ```
> $ ros2 launch pointcloud_preprocessor preprocessor.launch.xml
> [INFO] [launch]: All log files can be found below /home/me/.ros/log/2023-07-27-08-40-17-516980-Clephas-518576
> [INFO] [launch]: Default logging verbosity is set to INFO
> [INFO] [launch.user]: input_points_raw_list size = 1
> [INFO] [component_container-1]: process started with pid [518589]
> etc
> ```
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> ```
> $ ros2 launch pointcloud_preprocessor preprocessor.launch.xml
> [INFO] [launch]: All log files can be found below /home/me/.ros/log/2023-07-27-08-37-06-981761-Clephas-510420
> [INFO] [launch]: Default logging verbosity is set to INFO
> [ERROR] [launch]: Caught exception in launch (see debug for traceback): Caught exception when trying to load file of format [py]: 'DeclareLaunchArgument' object has no attribute 'lower'
> ```
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. `git checkout 9da75550cb9cc512287a35546256fa8e254daa8e` (or `git checkout main` at the time of writing)
> 2. `colcon build`
> 3. `ros2 launch pointcloud_preprocessor preprocessor.launch.xml` on ROS Humble
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - ROS 2: Humble
> - package: `pointcloud_preprocessor`
> - Compilation from source
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Commit 9da75550cb9cc512287a35546256fa8e254daa8e introduced `.lower()` ([source](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/commit/9da75550cb9cc512287a35546256fa8e254daa8e#diff-8f13a2a193ac37bbe84117457d716d99ef78a73a67f7cc80756f84b10cf4f954R49)) on what doesn't seem to be a string.

### #4386 — Localization sometimes misbehaves while turning

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-07-25  |  **Closed:** 2023-12-21  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** component:localization
- **Comments:** 11  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4386

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team,
> 
> I'm currently running Autoware on Carla, and I found that the localization module sometimes does not work well while turning.
> 
> [video1](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1v2tTvYibgcLVs6ub-7GEbVsbz4e1yP78/view?usp=sharing) here shows that localization works well at first, but it gets twisted while turning, and it is not corrected.
> 
> [video2](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1txz16aJNi9Wwa_N6vWNpEJOfJGUg7TXw/view?usp=sharing) also shows that the localization has some problem while turning, but unlike video1, it stops at the corner(since there's a car in front of it). 
> While stopping, it seems like correcting the localization error, and the ego vehicle eventually invades the drivable area and stucks.
> 
> Maybe this error is related to the issue [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/1426), but I report this issue since it is closed and expected to be fixed already..
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Localization to be stable while turning
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Localization is somewhat unstable while turning
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Here are the ros2 bag files:
>         - [rosbag for video1](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GaE4ZjjOt_zNh9RCfl10Jij9lsOmb48A?usp=sharing) 
>         - [rosbag for video2](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1yyjT-cVBHQofeq93m6g0yD7qARp5XzNQ?usp=sharing)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> I ran the experiment on the container from the image [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe/70625594?tag=humble-20230215-prebuilt-cuda-amd64).
> Carla version: 0.9.13
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> I don't know about the deep details of Autoware, so I guess this issue is from localization module.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @kminoda (2023-07-25)

> Hi, thank you for the report :+1:
> Unfortunately, it is difficult to tell the exact cause without looking into the rosbag and knowing the context of this experiment. 
> 
> But let me provide you some starting point:
> - Checking the output log of `ndt_scan_matcher` or visualizing some debugging scores and values from NDT and plotting them would be helpful for us to understand what's going on.
> - Visualizing `/localization/pose_estimator/points_aligned` on RViz would be helpful to understand if it's truly a localization issue or not (see the below figure)
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44218668/2b4cac3c-4072-49aa-aadd-f73fa039e80c)
> 

###### @Kim-mins (2023-07-25)

> Thank you for the response @kminoda!!
> 
> I tried your **first suggestion** and here are the additional video:
> - [For video1](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1rTUGMVzsYk8BuPpfddPmpQscxVxECnXe/view?usp=sharing)
> - [For video2](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1p4eeBNR0I9KOfsyVn4-COxjPcz_fuVTt/view?usp=sharing)
> 
> Both of them shows two arrows and they are on the same point at the start of the video.
> However, they are not aligned while driving.
> 
> For the **second suggestion**, I added the topic `/localization/pose_estimator/points_aligned` on RViz, but I could not find any difference of the visualization even though I clicked the check box of `Display` panel.. so I skipped it for now..
> 
> I'm a novice on Autoware, so maybe the provided information is not that meaningful to you.
> So here are **the rosbag files for each video**, for better debugging. I hope these to be helpful:
> - [For video1](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GaE4ZjjOt_zNh9RCfl10Jij9lsOmb48A?usp=drive_link)
> - [For video2](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1yyjT-cVBHQofeq93m6g0yD7qARp5XzNQ?usp=drive_link)
> 
> Thank you again, and please let me know if you need any additional data from me!

###### @kminoda (2023-07-25)

> @Kim-mins Thank you for the quick response :+1: 
> 
> For the first suggestion (about the log of `ndt_scan_matcher`), one possible way is to see the terminal output of Autoware Launch to see `ndt_scan_matcher` outputs any warnings. You can simply check it with `rqt_console` or just launching Autoware with `| grep ndt_scan_matcher`.
> 
> For the second suggection (RViz visualization), your video is partially helpful, but I'd like to see a broader view of it. The basic idea behind this debugging is to check if the green squares (which is the direct output of `ndt_scan_matcher`) matches the pointcloud map. If it does matches, then NDT is working fine. If it does NOT match, then there is some issue in `ndt_scan_matcher`.

### #4359 — Reduce binary size on the CI

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-07-21  |  **Closed:** 2023-09-21  |  **Author:** @soblin
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4359

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> By passing `-Os` option to the compiler, the object file is optimized in terms of the output size. Then we can also pass `-Wl,-s` option to the linker to remove symbol table from the executble. I compiled one file, namely `scene_intersection.cpp` in `behavior_velocity_intersection_module` and checked how much the size is reduced.
> 
> - By default build command: 46.6MB
> - with `-Os` option: 32.6MB
> 
> At least for this file the size is reduced by 30%. The sum of object file (`*.o`, `*.so`, excluding the executable) size under `build/` directory was 2.268GB on my machine according to the following command.
> 
> ```
> find ./ -type f -name "*.so" -o -name "*.o" | xargs du -c
> ```
> 
> I guess we can expect to save the disk size by `2.268 * 0.3 = 0.68` GB.
> 
> NOTE: this includes packages not contained in autoware.universe.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - avoid `No space left on disk`
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Apply `g++ -c -Os -Wl,-s` option
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - Change the compile option only on the CI

**Comments:**

###### @BonoloAWF (2023-07-21)

> cc: @xmfcx @mitsudome-r 

###### @xmfcx (2023-07-21)

> ### With flags
> Run following:
> `colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=1 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-Os -Wl,-s" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-Os -Wl,-s"` on a recent branch of autoware.
> 
> ```bash
> autoware_2$ du -sh build install
> 3,8G	build
> 130M	install
> ```
> 
> ### Without flags
> And run following:
> `colcon build --symlink-install  --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=1 `
> 
> ```bash
> autoware$ du -sh build install
> 4,6G	build
> 138M	install
> ```
> 
> ### Comparison
> These flags might be overridden by things in [autoware_package.cmake](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_common/blob/main/autoware_cmake/cmake/autoware_package.cmake) (didn't have time to check thoroughly) but worst case scenario, we can add the flags here.
> 
> But even without making changes in the repository, it managed **17.39%** disk space usage reduction.
> 
> ### Additional info
> Will also try:
> `-flto : This enables Link Time Optimization (LTO). It allows the compiler to optimize at application scope rather than file scope. This flag can lead to better optimization, but increases compile time.` to see if it reduces the disk space used (probably not).
> 
> Also my test might be a bit flawed too, i think these 2 folders of autoware weren't identical (but close). Will retest it on Monday.

### #4350 — Noisy obstacle pointcloud in CARLA prevents right turns

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-07-21  |  **Closed:** 2023-08-08  |  **Author:** @Kim-mins
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4350

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi team, I'm currently running Autoware on Carla, and I found that the ego vehicle cannot turn right even though there are no obstacles.
> 
> You can refer to the video [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1m8gQJC_LIVwr0EEQEj6tPY6VRAgQ7W5_/view?usp=sharing), and you can see that there are no obstacles, but the vehicle failed to turn right.
> 
> The map is [carla Town01](https://carla.readthedocs.io/en/0.9.12/img/Town01.jpg), and I've observed that this situation occurs on every outer-most corners of the map.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The ego vehicle successfully turns right, since there's no interference.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But it can't.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> [Here](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DPIwh4Q2kPVM26WaiG1Nq1lMWSCBmfpA?usp=sharing)'s the ros2 bag file.
> 
> Or if you want to reproduce it yourself, 
> 1. please download the following map files: [[lanelet2](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vm9SvalJe7Bc9sh_8jK-0cPulVAov5uD/view?usp=drive_link)] [[pcd](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MvJlfjkw3LWFUs5hdE_KQ2_CQTusU8UN/view?usp=drive_link)]
> 2. Run Autoware and spawn the vehicle at the point near to the corner and set a goal to pass the corner, just as the video above.
> 
>  
> Please note that, this issue sometimes does not happen, but I think you can reproduce it in high probability.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> I ran the experiment on the container from the image [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pkgs/container/autoware-universe/70625594?tag=humble-20230215-prebuilt-cuda-amd64).
> Carla version: 0.9.13
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> To my knowledge, the cause is from `obstacle_stop_planner` since it manages a stopping plan while driving.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @maxime-clem (2023-07-21)

> The vehicles stops because, based on the obstacle pointcloud, there obstacles are on the path.
> The default pointcloud processing is maybe not suited to the CARLA simulation and additional filtering may be necessary to solve your issue.

###### @Kim-mins (2023-07-21)

> Thank you @maxime-clem! I just noticed the pointcloud information. 
> Maybe the point cloud map I'm using now has some errors. Thank you for answering.

###### @maxime-clem (2023-07-21)

> As far as I know the pointcloud map is only used for localization.
> The obstacle pointcloud is obtained from the lidar sensor after ground removal (https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/perception/ground_segmentation/). In your case, it looks like the ground is not correctly filtered.

###### @Kim-mins (2023-07-21)

> Thank you for the follow up comment @maxime-clem. I think I got your point.
> In my understanding, maybe you mean there's a misbehavior on the ground removal process of perception module when Autoware runs on Carla simulator.
> 
> By the way, when I run Autoware on Carla, this issue interferes my simulation too frequently and it stops me from running Autoware normally. 
> How's your plan? Can this issue be fixed soon, or in low priority?

###### @maxime-clem (2023-07-21)

> I personally do not use Carla so I cannot work on this issue. Since it is not officially supported by Autoware there are not many people who can help. I suggest trying to tune the parameters of the ground filter by yourself.
> Otherwise, you can try tuning the [`obstacle_stop_planner`](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/), for example by setting `enable_z_axis_obstacle_filtering` to `true`.

###### @Kim-mins (2023-07-23)

> Thank you for answering @maxime-clem! I'll try your suggestion soon.
> Then, should I close this issue or not? This issue seems not urgent and only occurs in carla. 
> How do you think? I can follow your issue management policy.

###### @maxime-clem (2023-07-24)

> It is okay to keep the issue open and I updated the title of the issue to make it easier to track.

###### @Kim-mins (2023-08-07)

> Hi @maxime-clem!
> I have a good news that, this issue is gone on the recent version of Autoware(2023/07/15).
> While I was testing a recent version of Autoware for [another issue that you answered](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/4505#issue-1834151069), I could find that the problem is resolved.
> Maybe the issue can be closed. Thank you so much!
>

> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Add an option for skipping filtering on input external control commands.

> ### Definition of done
> 
> Update external_cmd_converter and vehicle_cmd_gate for this purpose

### #4318 — Unable to use Yabloc with AWSim

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-07-18  |  **Closed:** 2023-09-15  |  **Author:** @yaukaizhi
- **Labels:** component:localization
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4318

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The yabloc localization module expects to receive a /sensor_msgs/CompressedImage message type, but AWSim only outputs /sensor_msgs/Image on /sensing/camera/traffic_light/image_raw topic
> 
> Does this mean yabloc localization is not currently supported on AWSim?
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> yabloc in AWSim
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> no yabloc in AWSim
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Run yabloc localization in AWSim
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @KYabuuchi (2023-07-25)

> @yaukaizhi  Hi! Thank you for your interest in YabLoc. 
> As you pointed out, YabLoc currently subscribes to `CompressedImage` , which makes it incompatible with AWSIM.
> 
> However, you can run YabLoc by converting `Image` to `CompressedImage` using the script provided below. 
> If you decide to use this script, please set [use_traffic_light_recognition](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/launch/tier4_perception_launch/launch/perception.launch.xml#L71) to **false**. The traffic_light node's decompress operation can cause issues with the script's functionality.
> 
> ```py
> #!/usr/bin/env python3
> import rclpy
> from rclpy.node import Node
> from sensor_msgs.msg import Image
> from sensor_msgs.msg import CompressedImage
> from cv_bridge import CvBridge
> from rclpy.qos import QoSProfile, QoSReliabilityPolicy 
> 
> class Compressor(Node):
>     def __init__(self):
>         super().__init__('minimal_publisher')
>         qos= QoSProfile(
>             reliability=QoSReliabilityPolicy.RMW_QOS_POLICY_RELIABILITY_BEST_EFFORT,
>             depth=10
>         )
>         self.publisher_ = self.create_publisher(CompressedImage, '/sensing/camera/traffic_light/image_raw/compressed', qos)
>         self.subscription = self.create_subscription(Image, '/sensing/camera/traffic_light/image_raw', self.on_image, qos)
>         self.bridge_ = CvBridge()
> 
>     def on_image(self, msg):
>         self.get_logger().info('subscribed')
>         mat= self.bridge_.imgmsg_to_cv2(msg)
>         compressed_msg = self.bridge_.cv2_to_compressed_imgmsg(mat)
>         compressed_msg.header = msg.header
>         self.publisher_.publish(compressed_msg)
>         self.get_logger().info('published')
> 
> 
> def main(args=None):
>     rclpy.init(args=args)
>     compressor = Compressor()
>     rclpy.spin(compressor)
>     compressor.destroy_node()
>     rclpy.shutdown()
> 
> if __name__ == '__main__':
>     main()
> 
> ```

### #4307 — Routing no_drivable_lane(s) only when module is enabled

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-07-18  |  **Closed:** 2023-08-07  |  **Author:** @ahmeddesokyebrahim
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4307

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently Autoware is able to [stop by `no_drivable_lane(s)`](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3275#discussioncomment-5379038) and [handle routing to avoid them](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3952) if they exist in the route.
> However, this routing is considered even if [`no_drivable_lane`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/445a73dfc9f28bbc5ed0a3d2d00c271dd139cecb/autoware_launch/config/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning/behavior_velocity_planner/behavior_velocity_planner.param.yaml#L26) module is disabled.
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> This task is to make the routing for `no_drivable_labe` considered only if the module is enabled
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Add a new parameter that indicates considering routing for `no_drivable_lane(s)` or not
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> By proper usage of the proposed parameter :
> - When `no_drivable_lane` is enabled, the routing s considered to handle them if any
> - When `no_drivable_lane` is disabled, the normal shortest path is the only solution available.
>

> Currently, spell-check-differential is one of the CI executed by pull requests as a trigger.
> However, since there are too many cspell errors, the error is almost ignored when pull-request is merged.
> 
> So, it is desirable to reduce typos and revive spell-check-differential workflow!
> if we archieve zero cspell errors, we have the option to set the CI to "required".
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To revive the dead spell-check-differential workflow
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> We can...
> - fix the typos
> - add the words to [dictionary](https://github.com/tier4/autoware-spell-check-dict)
> - add ignore comment inline
> 
> We can track the number of entire cspell errors by [spell-check-all workflow](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4272) 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Pass the [spell-check-all workflow](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4272)

### #4276 — Refactoring the sensing packages parameter definitions

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-07-13  |  **Closed:** 2023-07-14  |  **Author:** @ismetatabay
- **Labels:** component:sensing
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4276

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> At the current design of Autoware.Universe architecture, most parameters migrates along launch files. (with arguments)
> 
> For example, if we want to modify gnss topic names for gnss poser, we must change parameter values in sample_sensor_kit_launch -> gnss.launch.xml:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/sample_sensor_kit_launch/blob/5a66ef0e14e21d5ce13eff16ca63cfcf0cfb7798/sample_sensor_kit_launch/launch/gnss.launch.xml#L9-L12
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Autoware users will not need modify the Autoware.Universe or sensor_kit_launch repository, they can change necessary parameters on autoware_launch package.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Convert the launch file arguments to ROS 2 param.yaml and create necessary param files to autoware_launch
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Definition of done (WIP)
> 
> - Prepare the necessary updates on sensing nodes
>   - gnss_poser:
>     -  read topic names as a parameter from .yaml file: 
>        - PR: #4277 
>        - PR: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/sample_sensor_kit_launch/pull/61

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2023-07-14)

> @ismetatabay 
> Thank you for posting the issue.
> 
> I don't mind extracting the parameters hard coded in the launch file as a parameter file, but I would like to discuss a little about where we put them. Since gnss.launch.xml exists in sample_sensor_launch package, I think it is simpler to place it under sample_sensor_launch's config directory.
> 
> > Autoware users will not need modify the Autoware.Universe or sensor_kit_launch repository, they can change necessary parameters on autoware_launch package.
> 
> Since the sensor configuration is user dependent, our assumption is that the users will fork and modify the sensor_kit_launch for their vehicle anyways. (e.g. people might have no gnss or multiple gnss) Therefore, I think it is easier for such users to modify the parameters in the same package/repository as they customize the launch file. 

###### @ismetatabay (2023-07-14)

> @mitsudome-r Thank you for your valuable comment, you are right. I think we shouldn't migrate sensing parameters to autoware_launch. I will create another PR for adding [missing gnss_poser parameter](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/ef3f0cb1a1b061f6fbb4c9fd5368b3e7617f2139/sensing/gnss_poser/launch/gnss_poser.launch.xml#L29-L39)  to [sample_sensor_kit_launch](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/sample_sensor_kit_launch/blob/5a66ef0e14e21d5ce13eff16ca63cfcf0cfb7798/sample_sensor_kit_launch/launch/gnss.launch.xml#L29-L39). :+1:

### #4209 — Estimated z value is wrong when the vehicle is driving on a slope in a tunnel

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-07-10  |  **Closed:** 2023-08-22  |  **Author:** @SaltUhey
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:localization
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4209

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Now, Autoware localizer is based on 3DoF(x,y,yaw) EKF estimation at 50 Hz, NDT scan matching at 10 Hz and GNSS. 
> In case of tunnel, only NDT scan matching is responsible for updating z, roll, and pitch.
> Due to it, I faced to the following "Actual behavior".
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Position estimation does not fail even on slopes.
> Trajectory estimation is smoother.
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> ![fail_localization_in_the_sloop](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/111027815/89114554-9bea-4839-9f7f-534d8a13225b)
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/111027815/23c86bcd-528d-4752-a8c7-f7f745c527fa
> 
> The light blue line in the figure is the trajectory of the vehicle.
> It can be seen that the self-position estimation is unstable as shown in the red elispse in the figure.
> In other attempts, localization was failed.
> As shown in the video, the vehicles are parallel until the ndt scan matching is read.
> It may be that the ndt scan matching cycle is longer than usual because I am using  Autoware on a laptop.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Launch Autoware in an environment with slopes.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> Ubuntu 22.04
> ROS 2 Humble
> autoware.universe 97b67589fd4c22f07af2aec1b5aa3c2ca508e3e9
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> **Proposed method**
> There are two possible solutions to this issue as follows.
> (1) Expanding EKF 3DoF to 6DoF
> (2) Renewing z, roll, pitch in other way
> Considering minimizing architectural changes and computational load, I adopted method (2).
> Also, since the roll angle rarely changes, changes in the roll angle are ignored.
> Specific methods are described below.
> In addition to the conventional method, the z values are modified based on the pitch angle in a short period of time.
> The proposed method includes two functions.
> (a) Updating z-values to account for slope against 3DoF-EKF
> (b) Updating z-values to account for slope by NDT scan matching delay
> 
> Used topic
>  * pitch_rate(twist.twist.twist.angular.y)
>  * velocity_x (twist.twist.linear.x)
>  * ekf_rate
>  * ndt_delay_time(= current time - acquisition time of point cloud)
> 
> This method updates the z position based on a basic slope motion model shown below.
> ![Screenshot from 2023-07-07 16-50-45](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/assets/111027815/bfaccdeb-32d4-4216-af28-5283f3267349)
> dz [m] = v [m/s]Γ£ò t [s] Γ£ò sin╬╕
> z1 = z + dz 
> 
> z1 : renewed z value
> z : original z value
> dz : z correction amount
> v : the liner speed of the vehicle
> t : time
> ╬╕ : pitch angle
> 
> In this case, the z-coordinate of ekf_pose is updated at 50 Hz (t=0.02 [s]) along with the update by EKF.
> Also, the value of the NDT delay in the z direction is updated according to the basic slope motion model when ndt_pose is read. 
> (Delay compensation has already been made for x,y,yaw.)
> This would enable smooth trajectory estimation even on slopes.
> 
> **Assumption**
>  * roll angle  is close to 0
>   If the value of the roll angle is far from zero or if the vehicle is subject to rapid rotation, the amount of z correction may not be well estimated.
>  * Condition that the pitch does not change suddenly due to emergency braking, etc.

**Comments:**

###### @SaltUhey (2023-07-10)

> In the future, I plan to open a pull request for this issue.

###### @SaltUhey (2023-08-22)

> Merge completed.
