> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Gnss_poser give position as median position. ─░ts good option if gnss accuracy is low. But we want to use directly gnss position. So maybe this option can be added as a parameter.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> It may be suitable for those who want to get from gnss poser according to the location coming directly from gnss. In the future, it will be more appropriate to use the real gnss location of gnss_poser to take localization output with gnss and include it in the ekf.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> In this line gnss_posers output position is median position. Can be add if structure that associated with a parameter in the parameter file.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Being able to use gnss poses directly and using median position parameters can be selected from the config file

**Comments:**

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-07-07)

> @meliketanrikulu 
> It is indeed supposed to take the median, but since [the number of elements defaults to 1](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/gnss_poser/src/gnss_poser_core.cpp#L48-L49).
> So it is the same as the raw value, isn't it?

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-07-07)

> Be that as it may, I think it would be nice to have a parameter that explicitly states whether or not the median should be used :+1: 

###### @yvzksgl (2023-07-12)

> I have a couple of questions. 
> 
> - What is the reason of publishing median value? As far as i understand it works same with publishing coming data immediately, if ```buffer_epoch``` setted as 1. If ```buffer_epoch``` increased what is the effect of publishing median value?
> - I have an idea that provides 3 options as
>        1. Publish coming data immediately (─▒t will set buffer_epoch as1.).
>        2. Publish median of the buffer (buffer_epoch setted by user.).
>        3. Publish average value of the poses in the buffer (buffer_epoch setted by user.).
> 
> 
> 

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-07-13)

> @yvzksgl 
> The reason for using the median is to remove outliers. In the past, there were occasional large jumps in GNSS positioning values, so we used the median to prevent that. However, with the recent significant improvement in positioning accuracy and the increasing prevalence of high-speed autonomous driving, we no longer rely on the use of the median.
> 
> Therefore, we have made it the default to publish coming data immediately, without using the median. However, I believe it would be beneficial to provide options for using the median or publishing the median values under a different topic name.

###### @yvzksgl (2023-07-19)

> In my point of view, it would be better let the user choose what to be published in the existing topic instead of publishing separate topics. If it sounds okay i will modify the node as i stated before, keep the topic same and what to publish will be selected with parameters:

> >       2. Publish median of the buffer (buffer_epoch setted by user.).
> >       3. Publish average value of the poses in the buffer (buffer_epoch setted by user.).

### #4153 — Intersection module dies when object detected at some turns

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-07-03  |  **Closed:** 2023-07-20  |  **Author:** @ismetatabay
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4153

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> As in the video, as the vehicle approaches the intersection, the behavior_planning_component also dies because the intersection module dies. 
> 
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/56237550/9866b042-f0c4-4dfa-b67a-ec2ca6e954d6
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Intersection Module and Behavior Planning Container works well without dying.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Intersection Module dies, so Behavor Pllanning Container dies.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> - Use this lanelet2 map
> [lanelet2_map.txt](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/11937249/lanelet2_map.txt)
> - Follow same steps as video in the description
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS: ROS 2 Humble 
> - Autoware: Latest version of Autoware.Universe
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The reason why the Intersection module dies is because the calculated ["start_arc_length"](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/56b9ed8587098e95eec243dc41df0840bfadcb65/planning/behavior_velocity_intersection_module/src/scene_intersection.cpp#L996C22-L996C38) and ["end_arc_length"](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/56b9ed8587098e95eec243dc41df0840bfadcb65/planning/behavior_velocity_intersection_module/src/scene_intersection.cpp#L999) values are bigger than the combined ```lanelet::ConstLanelets``` in the ```ego_lane_with_next_lane```. 
> 
> So ["trimmed_ego_polygon"](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/56b9ed8587098e95eec243dc41df0840bfadcb65/planning/behavior_velocity_intersection_module/src/scene_intersection.cpp#L1002) becomes empty polygon and this line causes dying of intersection modules. 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/56b9ed8587098e95eec243dc41df0840bfadcb65/planning/behavior_velocity_intersection_module/src/scene_intersection.cpp#L1010
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @ismetatabay (2023-07-03)

> @soblin Hi Sobue, have a nice week. There is 2 approach which I think:
> 
> - First, we can check the `trimmed_ego_polygon` is empty or not, so if estimated `start_arc_length` and `end_arc_length` are outside (bigger) than the combined `ego_lane_with_next_lane` lanelets length, maybe we can say there is no collusion, but  this approach can be dangerous for edge cases.
> - Second, we can add new `getEgoLaneWithNextLane` method which takes arc lengths as parameter, and add lanelets to `ego_lane_with_next_lane` until total lengths of added lanelets is bigger than arc lengths. 
> 
> What do you think?

###### @satoshi-ota (2023-07-13)

> Hi @soblin Could you answer the question?

###### @soblin (2023-07-13)

> I'm sorry I was confusing with this PR which is already merged.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4191
> 
> IΓÇÖll take a look at this PR
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4177

###### @beyzanurkaya (2023-07-13)

> @soblin The intersection module was dying for 2 different reasons. I realized the second reason later because a PR that merged later was the reason, and for this reason, I created 2 PR. If you review https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4177, I'll be glad.

>     * sanity check to ensure all of Autoware builds
>   * build-and-test-differential
>     * runs once the PR is opened, builds a large part of Autoware
>     * should reuse the artifacts from build-and-test
>     * only builds the modified packages and the ones which are directly dependent on the modified package
>     * this approach reduces the time to build from ~8h to less than an hour
> * using "Approach 1" from https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/4497 is preferable
> 
> Scenario simulator is not building on Arm:
> * https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/issues/2413
> * @kaspermeck-arm @ambroise-arm @mitsudome-r @oguzkaganozt  to collaborate on how to build `embree` on Arm
>   * it seems to be an incompatible compiler flag but could potentially be more complicated
> 
> Containerization of Autoware
> * Luke has an interesting proposal https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3651#discussioncomment-7212357
> * @kaspermeck-arm to reach out to Leo and Luke on Ansible and immutable OS

>

###### @kminoda (2023-06-23)

> It's from here: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/25f9d6a03adf91ed2312741b9acdf937560245a9/localization/ndt_scan_matcher/src/pose_array_interpolator.cpp#L78-L92
> Which probably is called here: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e70df1239c67d8ae86a7a8bf8d6c83bc20e7ece7/localization/ndt_scan_matcher/src/ndt_scan_matcher_core.cpp#L362C25-L364
> 
> Since ndt_scan_matcher needs an initial guess pose for optimization, it uses the EKF outputs. But since we need to use a proper EKF outputs with a close timestamp with the received LiDAR timestamp, we add the above timestamp validation. Without it, Autoware may use old EKF pose output and NDT ends up in non-optimal poses.

###### @yaukaizhi (2023-06-23)

> So what would cause the timestamps to have such a large difference?

> use_sim_time==false probably is the direct cause

###### @yaukaizhi (2023-06-23)

> but if I set use_sim_time=true, the LIDAR pointcloud becomes sluggish as if it's in slowmo. This doesn't happen if I play the rosbag with --clock argument, but i can't use --clock argument when doing real-world testing.
>  
> What might cause this?

###### @kminoda (2023-06-23)

> Now I got the issue :+1: I think it's better to change the title as the current one is a bit misleading. It seems it's not about specific package's implementation but rather an issue as an whole system.
> 
> Could you elaborate more on how it's sluggish? You mean on RViz? Could you share any videos that captures the issue here? Please also make it clear when exactly that issue happens. Is it when you are using `logging_simulator` with your recorded rosbag? Or using `autoware.launch.xml` with your onboard PC on your real robot or something?

###### @yaukaizhi (2023-06-23)

> This happens when using logging_simulator or autoware.launch.xml, use_sim_time=true. It does not occur when ros2 bag play <bag name> --clock. 
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/112715209/cd5c6c35-c051-458f-b026-a52e649a83aa
> 
> 

###### @kminoda (2023-06-24)

> You should not use autoware.launch.xml with use_sim_time=true as long as you are not providing /clock. So your rosbag should also contain /clock as well
> 

###### @yaukaizhi (2023-06-24)

> The issue has been solved by ensuring the LIDAR driver syncs with system time on my laptop. Thanks!

> The MPC can calculate target steering with a small steering rate limit
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The MPC fails to calculate target steering with a small steering rate limit

> Please see the details in the previously reported issue https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/4015.
> 
> The MPC parameter should have a small steering rate limit. In the previous issue, the values are as follows.

> ```
>     steer_rate_lim_dps_list_by_curvature: [10.0, 20.0, 30.0]
>     curvature_list_for_steer_rate_lim: [0.001, 0.002, 0.01]

### #4015 — When the initial position of the vehicle and the current lane line are at a significant angle, there is a certain probability of abnormal steering of the vehicle.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-06-20  |  **Closed:** 2023-06-20  |  **Author:** @lixianqiang
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/4015

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When I select a initial pose and a goal pose on a map I have drawn myself, if the initial pose is set at a significant angle with the lane lines, the output steering angle signal from the controller will make the vehicle track towards the desired trajectory. However, the output steering command will continue to instruct the vehicle to turn, resulting in deviation from the desired path.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Due to the significant angular error between initial point and the reference lane lines, the controller will generate a large steering output signal, causing the vehicle to steer towards the direction of the lane line. As the error gradually decreases, the steering output decreases as well. Eventually, the vehicle aligns its heading with the lane line.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The steering output does not decrease as the angular error decreases. Instead, it continues to output steering signals, causing the vehicle to deviate from the lane lines.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. modify the map config in autoware/src/launcher/autoware_launch/autoware_launch/config/map/lanelet2_map_loader.param.yaml, set MGRS to local in parameter lanelet2_map_projector_type
> 2. executor the follower command "ros2 launch autoware_launch planning_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=$HOME/autoware_map/factory_guiyang_outside sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle"
> 3. setting the initial pose and goal pose through replay the rosbag.
> 4. click the 'Auto' button in rviz. i found that the car will deviate from the lane after running some time
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - autoware.universe: main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> video:
> [σ╜òσ▒Å 2023σ╣┤06µ£ê19µùÑ 20µù╢51σêå35τºÆ.webm](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/24970103/3c677bb0-9958-418e-8de0-d5a1830809c2)
> map file:
> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/16wSBrGN4aWGJonxda5pPHAn4dNwnpwnj?usp=sharing
> ros bag:
> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DKcynZEF08vmBVIAs6XNyXlAL8tWsaJK?usp=drive_link

**Comments:**

###### @TakaHoribe (2023-06-20)

> @lixianqiang The predicted path of the MPC seems to be broken in this picture. It usually happens when the MPC optimization fails. Did you get the error messages about MPC like "optimization failed" on the terminal?
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/21360593/35934411-40c2-4fb3-9bd2-1bcc9c462db9)
>

###### @maxime-clem (2023-06-19)

> The compilation issue may come from your CUDA installation. Which version do you have installed ?
> Personally I have no issue with CUDA version 12.0, but the default version installed by the `setup-dev-env.sh` script is version 11.6 (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/amd64.env#L6).

### #3993 — `map_height_fitter` fails to detect map ground

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-06-16  |  **Closed:** 2023-11-29  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:localization
- **Comments:** 23  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3993

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In a simulated environment, the `map_height_fitter` fails to locate the PCD map ground and the initial position ends up 150 meters under the map (z=0):
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/0437bfc8-2758-41af-a85f-eac94e1e3bff)
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/6fb3b25a-e509-425a-a6c7-31392ed85aaa)
> 
> 
> In the log, I see:
> ```
> [rviz2-69] [INFO 1686888780.878679225] [rviz2]: Setting estimate pose: Frame:map, Position(52451.3, 65997.6, 0), Orientation(0, 0, -0.833062, 0.55318) = Angle: -1.96924 (operator()() at ./src/main.cpp:62)
> [initial_pose_adaptor-66] [INFO 1686888780.879371161] [default_ad_api.helpers.initial_pose_adaptor]: map fit1: 52451.301 65997.586 0.000 (fit() at /home/sig/autoware/src/universe/autoware.universe/map/map_height_fitter/src/map_height_fitter.cpp:169)
> [initial_pose_adaptor-66] [INFO 1686888780.879819454] [default_ad_api.helpers.initial_pose_adaptor]: Send request to map_loader (get_partial_point_cloud_map() at /home/sig/autoware/src/universe/autoware.universe/map/map_height_fitter/src/map_height_fitter.cpp:103)
> [initial_pose_adaptor-66] [INFO 1686888780.881185460] [default_ad_api.helpers.initial_pose_adaptor]: Loaded partial pcd map from map_loader (grid size: 0) (get_partial_point_cloud_map() at /home/sig/autoware/src/universe/autoware.universe/map/map_height_fitter/src/map_height_fitter.cpp:115)
> [initial_pose_adaptor-66] Failed to find match for field 'x'.
> [initial_pose_adaptor-66] Failed to find match for field 'y'.
> [initial_pose_adaptor-66] Failed to find match for field 'z'.
> [initial_pose_adaptor-66] [INFO 1686888780.881249434] [default_ad_api.helpers.initial_pose_adaptor]: map fit2: 52451.301 65997.586 0.000 (fit() at /home/sig/autoware/src/universe/autoware.universe/map/map_height_fitter/src/map_height_fitter.cpp:189)
> ```
> 
> I don't know if it is related, but PCL complains it cannot find xyz fields. Lokking at the code, it looks like the error comes from here:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/2465bbfa1de791794b2f49088ef301e20ad7e568/map/map_height_fitter/src/map_height_fitter.cpp#L120-L133 
> 
> As you can see, the `pcd_msg` message is created from the concatenation of all partials pointclouds, but its `fields` are never set. Maybe it causes `pcl::fromROSMsg()` to fail and return an empty cloud?
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> ground height correctly detected
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> ground height not detected
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-06-16)

> I think there is a design issue with `pointcloud_map_loader`:
> - `enable_partial_load` is set to `true` by default in `autoware_launch`.
> - if this flag is set, then `map_height_fitter` call the service to replace the current map.
> - yet, if the flag is set but only 1 pcd map is used, the service returns an empty cloud.
> 
> Considering that using only one PCD map should be the default use case, I don't think the current behaviour is correct. It is not necessarily a problem if the partial loading is enabled by default, however it should not have any impact on the case only 1 PCD map is used.

###### @kminoda (2023-06-26)

> Thank you for the report! We encountered a similar issue before, which I believe was resolved with this PR: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3863. Would you check if the PR is incorporated in your Autoware?

### #3969 — Consider NPC vehicles driving on the wrong direction lane on intersection

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-06-13  |  **Closed:** 2023-07-06  |  **Author:** @beyzanurkaya
- **Labels:** type:new-feature
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3969

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> ![245071125-419053f8-1501-4d9b-8f9e-e3432f9932b6](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/32412808/9b2833ba-514b-4194-bd85-cf0a52b0f609)
> 
> In the above image, the blue area is the adjacent lanelet, and the red area is the detection lanelets where objects search for objects in the intersection module. We should check the yellow area for possible driver mistakes.
> 
> The yellow area is the area where the vehicle can go in the wrong direction. If the vehicle is in the yellow area, we should check the vehicle's direction. If the vehicle is in the yellow area and its direction is opposite the attention lane, we should consider it a target object.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Consider vehicles in the wrong lane at the intersection
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. Expand the detection area for the wrong direction vehicles. 
> 
> ```
> IntersectionLanelets getObjectiveLanelets(
>   lanelet::LaneletMapConstPtr lanelet_map_ptr, lanelet::routing::RoutingGraphPtr routing_graph_ptr,
>   const int lane_id, const lanelet::ConstLanelets & lanelets_on_path,
>   const std::set<int> & assoc_ids, const autoware_auto_planning_msgs::msg::PathWithLaneId & path,
>   const std::pair<size_t, size_t> lane_interval, const double detection_area_length,
>   const double occlusion_detection_area_length, const bool tl_arrow_solid_on)
> ```
> 
> This getObjectiveLanelets function determines the lanes associated with the intersection (attention, conflicting, adjacent, occlusion_attention etc.)
> 
> 2. Check the direction of the vehicle with detection_area_angle_threshold in the expanded new detection area. If the angle between the direction of the vehicle and the direction of the lanelet is greater than 90 degrees, we can conclude that the vehicle is in the opposite direction.
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> If there is a vehicle entering the intersection even though it is in the wrong lane, the intersection module also considers these vehicles.

---

### #3952 — Routing to avoid no_drivable_lane(s)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-06-12  |  **Closed:** 2023-07-06  |  **Author:** @ahmeddesokyebrahim
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:planning
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3952

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, autoware supports [`no_drivable_lane`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_velocity_no_drivable_lane_module/docs/no-drivable-lane-design.md) handling, which is in brief a lane that out of operation design domain (ODD). The way autware handles `no_drivable_lane` is that it stops before exiting the ODD area and if the vehicle starts in non-ODD, it prevents the vehicle to move.
> 
> The purpose of this task is to extend the routing ability in autoware to avoid going through any `no_drivable_lane` between start and goal poses.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> If possible, having the autonomous missions avoiding any `no_drivable_lane`.
> 
> 
> ![routing_no_drivable_lanes](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/36835765/270bda30-27d8-4e01-97bf-3ae471a1ab2d)
> 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> While getting the shortest path between start and goal poses, check it includes any `no_drivale_lane`.
> If it includes any :
> - search for alternative routes that can go from start to goal and does not include any `no_drivale_lane`.
> - find the shortest path in all alternative routes
> - maintain the original shortest path if there is no alternative route and then let the  `no_drivale_lane` module handles it.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Implement proposed feature
> - [x] Test using planning simulator 
> - [x] Review 

---

### #3896 — distortion_corrector should update "azimuth" and "distance" field

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-06-05  |  **Closed:** 2024-10-28  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3896

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Because LIDAR sensors do not shoot laser simultaneously in all directions, raw sensor clouds look distorted when the vehicle turns or drive fast. `pointcloud_preprocessor::DistortionCorrectorComponent` use vehicle twist/imu data to rectify that distortion. Basically, it interpolates cloud points xyz values to make it as if all point laser had been shot simultaneously.
> 
> In the implementation `x`, `y` and `z` fields are modified, but not `azimuth` nor `distance`. Downstream nodes thus cannot use these 2 fields reliably.
> 
> ![distortion_corrector](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/18645627/39149961-b721-4a1c-86a9-7a8564d3e6f6)
> 
> For example, ring outlier filter is used after the distortion corrector filter, and current implementation relies both on azimuth and distance fields values. If the azimuth field is wrong, then the filter output may be incorrect. In ring outlier filter case, distortion effect is not "too bad", because only consecutive points on the same ring are considered (distortion effect over 2 consecutive points is negligible), except for the last and first point of the ring, which would be far away from each other due to distortion.
> 
> This leads to another problem: what do "azimuth" and "distance" fields mean? Are these values related to the sensor origin, or the current frame? Currently, these values are never updated, so they represent points in the original sensor frame, even though the cloud frame may be different (typically `base_link`). I don't think it is a problem per se, since these fields most likely only make sense in the sensor frame. For example ring outlier filter uses azimuth to group ring points together, but if the values were expressed in a different frame the logic would not make sense anymore.
> 
> So if the distortion corrector needs to update the "azimuth" and "distance" fields, it needs to be done in the original sensor frame, not the current one. This would definitely lead to some convoluted implementation.
> 
> Instead, it would be maybe simpler to have the input cloud of distortion corrector (and ring outlier filter) use the sensor frame. For example, in the `sample_sensor_kit`, the `velodyne_node_container` transforms the raw input cloud to `base_link` frame in order to filter points on the vehicle body. The sensor frame could be used as output frame for the distortion filter right after.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> `pointcloud_preprocessor::DistortionCorrectorComponent` also rectifies `azimuth` and `distance`
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Does not 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @stale (2023-08-04)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @vividf (2024-07-12)

> The PR for fixing this is blocked because Velodyne's output azimuth is already wrong before the distortion corrector node. 

###### @vividf (2024-09-05)

> This issue can be solved by this PR https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/8380

### #3882 — map_loader and map_tf_generator can not load georeferenced maps

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-06-01  |  **Closed:** 2023-11-29  |  **Author:** @enesadastec
- **Labels:** component:localization, component:map
- **Comments:** 9  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3882

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> "map_loader" and "map_tf_generator" packages can not load maps which have UTM coordinates like 4.000.000. Because these packages are reading ".pcd" files as pcl::PointXYZ which only supports float32 precision coordinates.
> 
> 
> If we try to load UTM maps like that, the loaded map looks like corrupted on RVIZ (because all points are rounded to float32)
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/94836003/d73d0a48-a11f-4fd0-a387-04f8cdb97fc0)
> 
> 
> 
> Here is an example pcd file which is not compatible with pcl::PointXYZ (float32)
> ![237363331-26c851a5-3f03-493e-9fee-05612abe5f2d](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/94836003/1b4daa9a-05a9-4fe2-b056-c4a5460433f4)
> 
> 
> Discussion topic:
> https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3355
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Loading UTM maps which are not compatible with pcl::PointXYZ (float32)
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Set an origin point from the map and then substract this origin point from all points while reading map process (convert georeferenced coordinates to local coordinates)
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - Converting UTM maps to local coordinates and be able to visualize on RVIZ

**Comments:**

One possible approach we are considering is to create original projection from WGS84 to local coordinate. With this update, Autoware will be able to run without any worries on overlapping MGRS or UTM grids. We are currently in the final step of internal design review for this topic, so I think we can share the design within this month (or maybe in two weeks, if everything goes well) in AWF discussions. We plan to merge this feature within several months.
> 
> And importantly, I believe this will subsidiary solve the issue mentioned here, as long as the map size are within appropriate range (say, 0km to 100km for x and y).

### #3845 — Create a messages_adapter package

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-26  |  **Closed:** 2023-06-19  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:system, component:simulation
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3845

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Create a package that will enable Autoware to convert given messages from `autoware_msgs` to `autoware_auto_msgs`. And publish them.
> - The topic names and types can be configured.
> 
> Follow up from:
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3787
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3677#issuecomment-1553295788
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3674
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Helps resolving
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3674
> - Simulators still use the old messages.
>   - https://github.com/tier4/scenario_simulator_v2
>   - https://github.com/tier4/AWSIM
> - This package will act as an adapter between old `autoware_auto_msgs` and the new `autoware_msgs`
> - This will give simulators time to adapt to the new message types.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - The topic names and types are provided by the parameters.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Create the package
> - [ ] It has the functionality to convert from:
>   - [ ] `autoware_auto_control_msgs` to `autoware_control_msgs`
>   - More issues can be created to add more messages.

**Comments:**

###### @xmfcx (2023-05-26)

> Which one should we go with?
> - **Option A:** Spawning a new adapter node for each message.
> - **Option B:** Having a single node that can subscribe and publish multiple messages.
> 
> ### Option A
> #### Pros
> - Adapters can be integrated into composable node containers, reducing the copy/network cost.
> - Each message is handled by a separate node, allowing for better isolation and fault tolerance.
> - Easier to debug and troubleshoot issues since each node is responsible for a single message.
> 
> #### Cons
> - Increased node count, which may impact system resource utilization and scalability.
> - Requires additional management and coordination overhead for managing multiple nodes.
> - Potential increase in network overhead due to the communication between multiple adapter nodes.
> 
> ### Option B
> #### Pros
> - Only a single node needs to be managed, reducing management overhead.
> - Simplified system architecture with fewer nodes to deploy and maintain.
> - Potentially lower network overhead since communication is concentrated in a single node.
> 
> #### Cons
> - It cannot be integrated into composable node containers, leading to increased copy/network cost.
> - Lack of isolation between messages may increase the risk of failure propagation.
> - Debugging and troubleshooting can be more challenging as multiple messages are handled within a single node.
> 
> ### Additional Considerations
> - **Option C:** Implement a hybrid approach where a limited number of adapter nodes are used, each handling a group of related messages. This can strike a balance between system scalability and resource utilization, allowing for better control over the number of nodes while maintaining some level of isolation and fault tolerance.
> - Evaluate the expected message load and processing requirements to determine if the increased node count in Option A will significantly impact system performance and resource consumption.
> 
> I think Option A is a safer option to go with. Can anyone comment on the potential drawbacks of having too many nodes running at a time? Even if they are composable nodes in containers?
> 
> cc. @isamu-takagi @mitsudome-r @wep21 
> 

###### @isamu-takagi (2023-05-29)

> @xmfcx I prefer Option A. Considering the load on the system, the impact of other processes is greater, so I think it's better to give priority to ease of use for now. It's not too hard to merge the separate nodes into one if someone needs it.

###### @isamu-takagi (2023-05-29)

> > Can anyone comment on the potential drawbacks of having too many nodes running at a time? Even if they are composable nodes in containers?
> 
> @xmfcx I've heard that in rare cases, when there is too many nodes, `MaxAutoParticipantIndex` needs to be increased for Cyclone DDS, but I don't know the specifics. At least the I have never had a problem by number of nodes is large.

###### @xmfcx (2023-05-29)

> Thank you @isamu-takagi san, I will implement it with Option A then.

### #3829 — Improve diagnostics aggregation method

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-26  |  **Closed:** 2024-02-14  |  **Author:** @isamu-takagi
- **Labels:** status:stale
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3829

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Recently MRM supports the multiple behavior that are emergency stop and comfortable stop and will plan to support pull over in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3221. Therefore, the system must select an appropriate MRM from the diagnostics.
> 
> Current diagnostics do not have well-structured diagnostic trees, making it difficult to select a appropriate MRM. Autonomous driving systems are complex, so diagnostic dependencies are directed acyclic graph (DAG) rather than tree.
> 
> For users, there is the problem that it is difficult to understand the error that prevents the switch to automatic driving, and thare are false positives. Also, I feel that terms such as SPF/LF/SF are a little different from their original meanings, so I would like to improve these as well. 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - Select appropriate MRM when detecting errors.
> - Filter errors appropriately according to vehicle status and user interests.
> - Supports DAG diagnostics dependencies.
> - Supports diagnostics for redundant system.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The diagram below is the sample of an improved diagnostic structure. Each block in the diagram has the same information as [DiagnosticStatus.msg](https://github.com/ros2/common_interfaces/blob/rolling/diagnostic_msgs/msg/DiagnosticStatus.msg) with extra "links" field for DAG. The mechanism is almost the same as diagnostic_aggregator. So we need to extend it to support DAG, or create a similar implementation.
> 
> ![improve-diagnostics](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/43976882/3313639f-6c71-4891-98a1-7caa54dfcf1d)
> 
> ### Error classification
> 
> Now the system_error_monitor classifies each status as either SPF/LF/SF/NF. However, the severity of the impact depends on the functionality that requires it. For example, consider a situation where the system has LiDAR and radar, and only LiDAR is broken. The object detection can work if either is fine, so that is not an error. But the object prediction, which needs the exact position of an object, requires LiDAR, so that is an error.
> 
> So instead of categorizing each error, consider the impact on the functionality that each error affects. In this case it is sufficient to create a DiagnosticStatus for that functionality and determine its level. In conclusion, remove the classification (SPF/LF/SF/NF), use the error level (ERROR/WARN/OK) instead.
> 
> ### Select MRM
> 
> Create a DiagnosticStatus for the functionality for each MRM and set the diagnostic dependencies appropriately for that MRM to work. Then the system can easily find the currently available MRMs by checking at their error levels. 
> 
> Also, create a status for normal functionality such as autonomous driving and remote driving in the same way. Then simply prioritize these functionality and select the one with the highest priority.
> 
> ### Error report
> 
> Create a root (it's not a tree, but a node that can reach all other nodes) DiagnosticsStatus for error reporting. It dynamically determines the level of error according to the user's interests and vehicle conditions. For example:
> - Ignore most errors during initialization.
> - Ignore errors of autonomous driving while stopped.
> - Notify errors of autonomous driving as warning while preparing for autonomous driving.
> 
> ### Message types
> 
> - The current status of diagnostic units: `/diagnostics_graph` ([DiagnosticArray.msg](https://github.com/ros2/common_interfaces/blob/rolling/diagnostic_msgs/msg/DiagnosticArray.msg))
> - The static information of graph structure: `/diagnostics_graph_struct` (DiagnosticGraph.msg)
> 
> ```
> # DiagnosticGraph.msg
> Time stamp
> DiagnosticNode[] node
> 
> # DiagnosticNode.msg
> uint32[] links 
> ```
> 
> 
> ### Backward compatibility
> 
> You can create messages compatible with `/hazard_status` by assigning error categories as follows:
> 
> |  | Report OK | Report WARN | Report ERROR |
> | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- |
> | Status OK  | NF | - | - |
> | Status WARN | SF | LF | SPF |
> | Status ERROR | SF | LF | SPF |
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] create aggregator for DAG.
> - [x] create new diagnostics config.

**Comments:**

###### @isamu-takagi (2023-06-05)

> It was not possible to support graph structures without changing the plugin interface for diagnostic_aggregator. It seems that AnalyzerGroup cannot share child Analyzer with others.

###### @stale (2023-08-18)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @isamu-takagi (2023-09-01)

> I'll change the Autoware diagnostics as follows.
> - Replace `diagnostic_aggregator` and `system_error_monitor` with `system_diagnostic_graph` node.
> - Repalce `diagnostics_agg` and `hazard_status` with `diagnostics_graph` and `diagnostics_summary` topic.
>     - `diagnostics_summary` is similar to `emergency, emergency_holding` fields in `hazard_status`
>     - `diagnostics_graph` is similar to `nf, sf, lf, spf` fields in `hazard_status` or `diagnostics_agg`
>  - PR
>     - https://github.com/tier4/tier4_autoware_msgs/pull/96
>     - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/4722
> 
> ![universe-3829-diagnostics-nodes](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/43976882/6ab6cfd7-083e-47b0-9a91-c0899f7eaf1b)
> 

###### @stale (2023-10-31)

### #3827 — Robosense LiDAR cannot get filtered processed pointcloud data

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-25  |  **Closed:** 2023-06-12  |  **Author:** @TZECHIN6
- **Labels:** component:sensing
- **Comments:** 15  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3827

>

> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Pointcloud preprocess container node cannot read from the robosense lidar pointcloud data, and no filtered data output.
> 
> The raw pointcloud data can be seen in Rviz and can be echoed.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> We have also tried the velodyne VLP16, it works fine with this pointcloud preprocess node. Expected to received a filter processed pointcloud from robosense lidar RS80.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Currently I am working with a RS80 lidar as well. However, when I trying to integrate the RS80 into autoware eco system, to use a node container with a pointcloud preprocessing features, it cannot work well, the output topic do not output anything.
> 
> Below is the example template from velodyne VLP16 launch.py, I slightly modified it like below, as Robosense already output pointcloud data, no convertion from packet to pointcloud is needed, thus I directly passing the input topic into this cropbox component.
> ```
>     nodes.append(
>         ComposableNode(
>             package="pointcloud_preprocessor",
>             plugin="pointcloud_preprocessor::CropBoxFilterComponent",
>             name="crop_box_filter_self",
>             remappings=[
>                 ("input", "/rslidar_points),
>                 ("output", "self_cropped/pointcloud_ex"),
>             ],
>             parameters=[cropbox_parameters],
>             extra_arguments=[{"use_intra_process_comms": LaunchConfiguration("use_intra_process")}],
>         )
>     )
>   ```
> 
> the `/rslidar_points` do have data flow in, however the `self_cropped/pointcloud_ex` topic do not have any data when echo it.
>

###### @miursh (2023-05-27)

> @TZECHIN6 I'm sorry let me correct a little bit about used pointcloud fields.. 
> If you want to use 
> * [distorion corrector](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/docs/distortion-corrector.md), the pointcloud must have XYZ and **T** field
> * [ring outlier filer](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/docs/ring-outlier-filter.md#assumptions--known-limits), the pointcloud must have XYZ and **RAD** field
> * [dual return filter](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/docs/dual-return-outlier-filter.md) and [blockage diag](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/docs/blockage_diag.md) needs XYZ, **IRADRT** field (I'm not so confident about this)
> * the other ones only use XYZ fileds, I think...
> 
> So, unless you use the above node, just using XYZIRT is fine.
> 
> FYI, you can use another point type by modifying your lidar driver. You can refer [this](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/awf_velodyne/blob/awf/main/awf_velodyne_pointcloud/src/conversions/convert.cc#L213C22-L214) and [this](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/awf_velodyne/blob/awf/main/awf_velodyne_pointcloud/src/conversions/pointcloudXYZIRADT.cc).

### #3787 — Add vehicle control command message to AD API

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-22  |  **Closed:** 2023-05-26  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:new-feature
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3787

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Right now Autoware publishes `/control/command/control_cmd: autoware_control_msgs/msg/Control` in [control/vehicle_cmd_gate/src/vehicle_cmd_gate.cpp](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/a3ce54a7fc13175e968f2951af8750fff321b622/control/vehicle_cmd_gate/src/vehicle_cmd_gate.cpp#L411) to control the vehicle.
> 
> This issue aims to instead, publish a standardized AD API message.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Internal messaging API shouldn't affect how outside platforms (simulators, vehicles) interface with the Autoware.
> 
> While working on this task: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3677#issuecomment-1553295788 I've realized we are using autoware_auto_control_msgs for the:
> - https://github.com/tier4/scenario_simulator_v2
> - https://github.com/tier4/AWSIM
> 
> And with @mitsudome-r 's guidance, agreed that it's a better idea to use the AD API interface to update them.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Explained in **Definition of done** section below.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Raise this in Planning and Control WG
> - [ ] Create a new message for Autoware's final output for the control command.
>   - [ ] Create the message in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_adapi_msgs
> - [ ] Publish it in an appropriate part of https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/system/default_ad_api
>   - [ ] Create the PR in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe

**Comments:**

###### @xmfcx (2023-05-22)

> cc. @TakaHoribe @takayuki5168 @mehmetdogru @brkay54 @isamu-takagi @yukkysaito @mitsudome-r @yamacir-kit 

###### @isamu-takagi (2023-05-23)

> I think this should be defined in the component interface rather than AD API. [See the abstract section in this page for details.](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/design/autoware-interfaces/#abstract) 
> 

###### @xmfcx (2023-05-23)

> @isamu-takagi I see, @mitsudome-r do you have any comments?
> 
> To communicate with simulators, we can consider following options:
> 
> ## Options
> 
> ### Option A - Use autoware_msgs
> 
> #### Pros
> 
> - **Consistency**: Using `autoware_msgs` maintains consistency across the codebase and communication, making it easier for developers to understand and work with the system.
> 
> - **Less Development Time and Resources**: It requires less development time and resources compared to defining a new interface, as it uses already defined messages.
> 
> - **Compatibility**: There's less risk of compatibility issues as `autoware_msgs` are designed to work with Autoware.
> 
> #### Cons
> 
> - **Dependency**: If there are significant changes in the future versions of `autoware_msgs` or if they are deprecated, it might affect the simulator side.
> 
> - **Versioning Complexity**: If different versions of `autoware_msgs` are used in different parts of the project, it can cause confusion and potential errors.
> 
> - **Possible Inefficiency**: If `autoware_msgs` contains data fields or structures that aren't necessary for the particular simulator integration, it could introduce inefficiencies in communication.
> 
> 
> Using autoware_msgs allows us to maintain consistency and avoid unnecessary work, provided we handle the versioning process correctly. This approach will involve the following steps:
> 
> - [x] **Define Autoware Messages:** Review and finalize the definitions for `autoware_msgs`. This will serve as a standard interface for the project.
> - [ ] **Implement in the Code Base:** Once the definitions are ready, start incorporating them into the code base.
> - [ ] **Document Versioning Process:** Create a comprehensive document detailing the versioning process of `autoware_msgs`. This should include details on how to manage changes, update versions, and how the versioning impacts the overall system.
>   - I will work on this as soon as possible.
> 
> ### Option B - Define a new interface
> 
> #### Pros
> 
> - **Customization**: A custom interface allows you to design a communication protocol that perfectly suits your specific requirements. This could include specific data types, frequency, and synchronization procedures that might not be possible with the existing `autoware_msgs`.
> 
> - **Efficiency**: A custom interface can be designed to be more efficient, avoiding unnecessary data or instructions that may be present in the `autoware_msgs`.
> 
> - **Future Proofing**: Creating a new interface that takes into account potential future needs can help prevent the need for significant changes down the line.
> 
> #### Cons
> 
> - **Resource Intensive**: Defining and implementing a new interface can be time-consuming and requires a good deal of resources and expertise.
> 
> - **Compatibility Issues**: If not designed carefully, a new interface could lead to compatibility issues with other parts of the system or with future updates to Autoware or the simulators.
> 
> - **Maintenance**: Any new interface will need maintenance, versioning, and potentially debugging over time, increasing the long-term workload.
> 
> - **Learning Curve**: There could be a learning curve for anyone needing to work with the new interface, which may slow down development initially.
> 
> - **Testing**: A new interface will require extensive testing to ensure reliable operation. This can take time and resources.
> 
> 
> I find this to be a little bit overkill. If we version `autoware_msgs` better, we shouldn't need to do this.
> 
> ### Option C - Use OSI
> 
> [OSI (Open Simulation Interface)](https://github.com/OpenSimulationInterface/open-simulation-interface) is an option but for our resources, timelines and goals, it's too much of an additional complexity.

###### @isamu-takagi (2023-05-23)

> @xmfcx Thank you for the suggestion. I agree with "Option A - Use autoware_msgs" and suggest the following for the disadvantages. There are two features.
> - Separate message package into public and private parts for each component.
> - Separate message definition by rosidl and interface definition.
> 
> > Dependency: If there are significant changes in the future versions of autoware_msgs or if they are deprecated, it might affect the simulator side.
> 
> The component interface is the public part of the messages for each component. The current update frequency is a little high, but ideally stability is required.  You are concerned about the impact on the simulator, but changing the component interface will affect all implementation of that component such as vehicle drivers and sensor drivers. The simulator works as a kind of driver, so we don't need to think about the simulator specially. If the public part becomes clear, the update frequency should decrease. Mandatory changes are handled by type adaptation described later.
> 
> > Possible Inefficiency: If autoware_msgs contains data fields or structures that aren't necessary for the particular simulator integration, it could introduce inefficiencies in communication.
> 
> This should be resolved by separating the public and private parts of the message. Unnecessary data should probably be moved to private messages. Since the simulator performs by replacing some components such as vehicle and sensing, it is necessary to support the same interface as those components.
> 
> ![component-interface-scope](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/43976882/c2b46b92-0ea6-46dd-b3cd-5b577a6f7e7f)
> 
> > Versioning Complexity: If different versions of autoware_msgs are used in different parts of the project, it can cause confusion and potential errors.
> 
> Message definitions by rosidl include a serialization layer. If you convert to JSON like rosbridge, you can communicate if the fields are the same, but if you are communicating with DDS using rclcpp or rclpy, communication cannot be guaranteed if messages of different versions are mixed because its binary format may not be the same.
> 
> One solution is to separate message definition/serialization by rosidl and interface definition using [type adaptation](https://ros.org/reps/rep-2007.html). This way, we can safely use multiple versions of the interface because only the latest message is used for serialization even if the message type changes. 
> 
> ![component-interface-adaption](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/43976882/6a202645-27c1-47f4-ad6c-e9fb91703ad4)
> 

###### @xmfcx (2023-05-26)

> @isamu-takagi thanks for the comprehensive suggestion you've provided.
> 
> To start simple, I've created following issue:
> - 
> 
> > One solution is to separate message definition/serialization by rosidl and interface definition using [type adaptation](https://ros.org/reps/rep-2007.html).
> 
> I should investigate the type adaptation rep thoroughly and then I can also add my thoughts about your proposal.
> 
> Is it OK to write a simple converter-publisher node for now?
> 
> And we can consider your proposal in a new issue, where we can discuss about the versioning `autoware_msgs`.
> - [X] I will create this issue today.
>   - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-documentation/issues/379
> 
> I am closing this issue for now, we can discuss versioning in detail in the new issue, you can also copy your message there.

Please check position and angle of goal_pose" appears, for example, when the goal position is not in the lanelet, or the goal posture is opposite to the lanelet direction. > @ahuazuipiaoliang I checked it in my environment, and it seems the lane boundary and center line are broken on Rviz. But the Lanelet looks ok in the vectormap builder.
>

> - That is why you have to specify "local" for projection type to use the local_x, local_y tags in the lanelet2 map instead.
> - However, there seems to be a bug in "local" projection type in the universe code (and the bug only happens when you have invalid MGRS grid annotated in the map)

### #3769 — delete and create virtual_wall_marker from behavior_velocity_planner's scene module approprately 

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-19  |  **Closed:** 2023-07-31  |  **Author:** @kyoichi-sugahara
- **Labels:** type:new-feature
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3769

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> `virtual_wall_marker` pubslihed from `behavior_velocity_planner` is deleted by setting the lifetime, for example, to 0.2 seconds and each module runs at 10Hz, the wall marker will be displayed unnecessarily for 0.1 seconds after it is no longer needed. 
> Although it may seem like a short time when considering real time, when running a heavy simulator at a slower speed, for example, at 1/10 of the normal speed, the marker will be displayed for 1 second despite being unnecessary, which can confuse developers.
> 
> For these reasons, I believe that an deletion function at every cycle is necessary when modules determine that the marker is no longer needed.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Ensure that the `virtual_wall_marker` published from the scene module of `behavior_velocity_planner` can be properly deleted/created at the right timing.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> A point to be cautious about is that when deleting or creating `virtual_wall_marker`, it is necessary to specify the namespace and id. However, if the same scene module is launched (e.g., when there are multiple intersections, multiple intersection modules can be launched), `virtual_wall_marker` that should be generated in different locations may be mistakenly deleted due to duplication of namespaces and id. Therefore, when the same scene module is launched multiple times, it is necessary to give a different namespace as an argument. As proposed in this [PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3654), by adding the module_id as a prefix to the namespace, we need to ensure that the namespaces do not duplicate.
> 
> Another point to note is that when using the module_id as a prefix to the namespace, it is necessary for the module_id to be unique among the same scene modules.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Make sure that each scene module of the `behavior_velocity_planner` can use `VirtualWallMarkerCreator` to properly delete/create `virtual_wall_markers` at the right timing.
> 
> - [x] intersection
> - [x] crosswalk
> - [x] blind_spot(module_id should be change to unique)
> - [x] no_stopping_area
> - [x] detection_area
> - [x] occulusion_spot(module_id should be change to unique)
> - [x] out_of_lane
> - [x] run_out
> - [x] speed_bump
> - [x] stop_line
> - [x] traffic_light
> - [x] virtual_traffic_light(module_id should be change to unique)

**Comments:**

### #3724 — Use pluginlib for behavior_velocity_planner

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-16  |  **Closed:** 2023-06-22  |  **Author:** @isamu-takagi
- **Labels:** type:new-feature
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3724

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The behavior_velocity_planner package contains many scene modules. I plan to use pluginlib to split the scene module into separate packages. This allows you to put additional scene modules in separate repositories. In addition, since the number of dependent libraries is minimized, the build efficiency is improved.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - Improve scene module extensibility.
> - Improve build efficiency.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> #### Classes
> 
> Move the interface and utilities into the common package. Move each scene module into its own package.
> 
> ![behavior-velocity-pluginlib-class](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/43976882/a6741898-41e5-479c-a6d3-e93b4b922138)
> 
> #### Packages
> 
> The structure of the package is as follows.
> 
> ```
> planning
> Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_planner         (main node package)
> Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_planner_common  (plugin interface, library/utility)
> Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_foo_module
> Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_bar_module
> ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_baz_module
> ```
> 
> If the number of modules increases, the following structure is also a candidate.
> 
> ```
> planning
> Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_planner         (main node package)
> Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_planner_common  (plugin interface, library/utility)
> ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_modules
>     Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_foo_module
>     Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_bar_module
>     ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ behavior_velocity_baz_module
> ```
>

### #3723 — Implementation of node tests to ensure planning node stability under exceptional inputs

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-05-16  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @kyoichi-sugahara
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3723

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> #### background
> 
> In each node of the planning module, when exceptional input, such as unusual routes or significantly deviated ego-position, is given, the node may not be prepared for such input and could crash. As a result, debugging node crashes can be time-consuming. For example, if an empty trajectory is given as input and it was not anticipated during implementation, the node might crash due to the unaddressed exceptional input when changes are merged, during scenario testing or while the system is running on an actual vehicle.
> 
> #### Important Notes
> 
> During test execution, when launching a node, parameters are loaded from the parameter file within each package. Therefore, when adding parameters, it is necessary to add the required parameters to the parameter file in the target node package. This is to prevent the node from being unable to launch if there are missing parameters when retrieving them from the parameter file during node launch.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose of implementing node test is ensure that node operates correctly when receiving exceptional input.
> 
> planning_test_utils package provides a utility for implementing node test.
> By utilizing this utility and implementing node test for exceptional input, we aim to to reduce bugs that are only discovered when actually running the system, by requiring measures for exceptional input before merging PRs.
> 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Implement node test by utilizing planning_test_utils [package](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/planning/planning_test_utils)
> 
> Node tests are implemented with the file name of test_`module_neme`_node_interface.cpp
> 
> ### Implemented node tests
> 
> Node | Test name | exceptional input | output | Exceptional input pattern
> -- | -- | -- | -- | --
> planning_validator | NodeTestWithExceptionTrajectory | trajectory | trajectory | Empty, single point, path with duplicate points
> planning_validator | NodeTestWithOffTrackEgoPose | odometry | odometry | Off-lane ego-position
> motion_velocity_smoother | NodeTestWithExceptionTrajectory | trajectory | trajectory | Empty, single point, path with duplicate points
> obstacle_cruise_planner | NodeTestWithExceptionTrajectory | trajectory | trajectory | Empty, single point, path with duplicate points
> obstacle_cruise_planner | NodeTestWithOffTrackEgoPose | odometry | odometry | Off-lane ego-position
> obstacle_stop_planner | NodeTestWithExceptionTrajectory | trajectory | trajectory | Empty, single point, path with duplicate points
> obstacle_stop_planner | NodeTestWithOffTrackEgoPose | odometry | odometry | Off-lane ego-position
> obstacle_velocity_limiter | NodeTestWithExceptionTrajectory | trajectory | trajectory | Empty, single point, path with duplicate points
> obstacle_velocity_limiter | NodeTestWithOffTrackEgoPose | odometry | odometry | Off-lane ego-position
> obstacle_avoidance_planner | NodeTestWithExceptionTrajectory | trajectory | trajectory | Empty, single point, path with duplicate points
> scenario_selector | NodeTestWithExceptionTrajectoryLaneDrivingMode NodeTestWithExceptionTrajectoryParkingMode | trajectory | scenario | Empty, single point, path with duplicate points for scenarios:LANEDRIVING and PARKING
> scenario_selector | NodeTestWithOffTrackEgoPose | odometry | odometry | Off-lane ego-position
> freespace_planner | NodeTestWithExceptionRoute | route | route | Empty route
> freespace_planner | NodeTestWithOffTrackEgoPose | odometry | odometry | Off-lane ego-position
> behavior_path_planner | NodeTestWithExceptionRoute | route | route | Empty route
> behavior_path_planner | NodeTestWithOffTrackEgoPose | odometry | odometry | Off-lane ego-position
> behavior_velocity_planner | NodeTestWithExceptionPathWithLaneID | path_with_lane_id | path | Empty path
> behavior_velocity_planner | NodeTestWithOffTrackEgoPose | odometry | odometry | Off-lane ego-position
> 
> ### Unimplemented node tests
> 
> In cases where there are variations of modules operating within nodes, such as `behavior_path_planner` and `behavior_velocity_planner`, we need to configure which specific module is active during testing. Alternatively, we may need to conduct tests under conditions where all modules are operating. 
> 
> Implementation of tests that ensure the operation of all modules within the `behavior_velocity_planner`, and tests configured to activate specific nodes within the `behavior_path_planner`, has not been done yet.
> 
> Moreover, tests for special situations, such as those confirming that nodes remain operational when the vehicle is driven in reverse, or when the vehicle's direction undergoes a significant change, are still unimplemented. The introduction of these tests is essential to assure the system's robustness under a variety of conditions.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> The implementation of node tests, following the configuration for the operation of individual scene modules within the `behavior_velocity_planner` and `behavior_path_planner`, and the assurance of no node failure are confirmed. If test failure occurs, countermeasures should be applied.
> 
> The implementation of tests for other special inputs, as mentioned in 'Unimplemented node tests', is not included in this issue.
> 
> ### tasks
> 
> - [ ] feature to verify within the test that the target scene module is running for `behavior_velovity_planner`
> - [ ] feature to verify within the test that the target scene module is running for `behavior_path_planner`
> - [ ] creation of a document to support test implementation
> 
> behavior_path_planner
> - [x] lane_following
> - [ ] lane_chnage
> - [ ] avoidance
> - [ ] side_shift
> - [ ] dynamic_avoidance
> - [ ] goal_planner
> - [ ] start_planner
> 
> behavior_velocity_planner
> - [x] blind_spot
> - [x] intersection
> - [x] crosswalk
> - [x] detection_area
> - [ ] no_stopping_area
> - [ ] out_of_lane
> - [ ] run_out
> - [ ] speed_bump
> - [x] traffic_light
> - [ ] virtual_traffic_light
>

### #3693 — Adding Orthometric height as an option to the gnss poser package

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-12  |  **Closed:** 2023-05-31  |  **Author:** @meliketanrikulu
- **Labels:** component:sensing, component:localization
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3693

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> We work with different sensors. Some sensors give the height value as ellipsoid height, while others give it as orthometric height. Gnss poser currently uses ellipsoid height. We think that orthometric height should also be added as an option. otherwise, there is a height difference between the gnss poser output using the height from gnss and our map, and we have a problem while initializing it. 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To be able to use the gnss poser correctly at different height types while working with different sensors.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> GNSS POSER : 
> input: ellipsoid height 
> output: orthometric height
> 
> GNSS POSER FEATURE REQUEST :
> input: ellipsoid height /  orthometric height (optional)
> output:  orthometric height
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> We expect gnss poser to be usable with both height types

**Comments:**

> Thank you!
> This feature is something we have been wanting too!

###### @farukbaykara (2023-05-25)

> I tested the feature on Robione vehicle in campus. Initialized immediately without problem at different locations.

### #3673 — ground remover package cannot delete ghost points appears front of car when passing speedbump

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-11  |  **Closed:** 2024-07-05  |  **Author:** @Zeysthingz
- **Labels:** component:perception, component:vehicle
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3673

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently we are using ```scan_ground_filter``` algorithm in ground segmentation  node but when passing speed bumps  the algorithm can not work efficiently because vehicle is shaken and can not delete all ground points ghost points occurs  front of vehicle.Because of point occurs on the way ```obstacle stop planner``` stops the car. Here is an example of this problem:
> ![jiraya2222](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/55089534/44d1a09a-f09c-4859-be47-67eb3e186ac1)
> 
> Default parameter values are below:
> ```
>   global_slope_max_angle_deg: 10.0
>   local_slope_max_angle_deg: 13.0 # recommended 30.0 for non elevation_grid_mode
>   split_height_distance: 0.2
>   non_ground_height_threshold: 0.20
>   grid_mode_switch_radius: 20.0
>   gnd_grid_buffer_size: 4
>   detection_range_z_max: 2.5
>   elevation_grid_mode: true
> ```
> 
> Mainly  increasing   ```non_ground_height_threshold```  parameter affects  deleting these points and this parameter is height threshold of non ground objects for elevation grid mode.Currently we tuned parameters and took better result but when increase parameters to much  we are losing points [tuned_video.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LrOCJON2suw)
> 
> Here is tuned parameters below:
> ```
>     global_slope_max_angle_deg 50.0
>     local_slope_max_angle_deg 35.0 
>     split_height_distance 0.25
>     non_ground_height_threshold 0.50
>     grid_mode_switch_radius 30.0
>     gnd_grid_buffer_size 1
>     detection_range_z_max 2.5
>     elevation_grid_mode true
> ```
> Here is a bag file to help understand problem [ground_remover_bag](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Z5qhQCc0ZsYNf1DM9GbC7n6JBQsndPg9)
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To improve algorithm when passing speed bumps 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> improve algorithm 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Tuned current algorithm and tested it on vehicle

### #3666 — `obstacle_stop_planner` inserts stop point even when the ego don't have to stop

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-11  |  **Closed:** 2023-05-19  |  **Author:** @satoshi-ota
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3666

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When the ego and other vehicle drive paralelly, `obstacle_stop_planner` inserts stop point suddenly behind the ego. I guess that this is unexpected behavior.
> 
> I used following [default config](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/main/autoware_launch/config/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/motion_planning/obstacle_stop_planner/obstacle_stop_planner.param.yaml) and the `stop_lateral_margin` is `0.0`, so the NPC vehicle seems to be `NOT` inside detection area for stop judgement in this movie.
> 
> ```yaml
> /**:
>   ros__parameters:
>     chattering_threshold: 0.5                # even if the obstacle disappears, the stop judgment continues for chattering_threshold [s]
>     lowpass_gain: 0.9                        # gain parameter for low pass filter [-]
>     max_velocity: 20.0                       # max velocity [m/s]
>     enable_slow_down: False                  # whether to use slow down planner [-]
>     enable_z_axis_obstacle_filtering: True   # filter obstacles in z axis (height) [-]
>     z_axis_filtering_buffer: 0.0             # additional buffer for z axis filtering [m]
>     voxel_grid_x: 0.05                       # voxel grid x parameter for filtering pointcloud [m]
>     voxel_grid_y: 0.05                       # voxel grid y parameter for filtering pointcloud [m]
>     voxel_grid_z: 100000.0                   # voxel grid z parameter for filtering pointcloud [m]
>     use_predicted_objects: False            # whether to use predicted objects [-]
>     publish_obstacle_polygon: False          # whether to publish obstacle polygon [-]
>     predicted_object_filtering_threshold: 1.5 # threshold for filtering predicted objects (valid only publish_obstacle_polygon true) [m]
> 
>     stop_planner:
>       # params for stop position
>       stop_position:
>         max_longitudinal_margin: 5.0             # stop margin distance from obstacle on the path [m]
>         max_longitudinal_margin_behind_goal: 3.0 # stop margin distance from obstacle behind goal on the path [m]
>         min_longitudinal_margin: 5.0             # stop margin distance when any other stop point is inserted in stop margin [m]
>         hold_stop_margin_distance: 0.0           # the ego keeps stopping if the ego is in this margin [m]
> 
>       # params for detection area
>       detection_area:
>         lateral_margin: 0.0                  # margin [m]
>         vehicle_lateral_margin: 0.0          # margin of vehicle footprint [m]
>         pedestrian_lateral_margin: 0.0       # margin of pedestrian footprint [m]
>         unknown_lateral_margin: 0.0          # margin of unknown footprint [m]
>         step_length: 1.0                     # step length for pointcloud search range [m]
>         enable_stop_behind_goal_for_obstacle: True # enable extend trajectory after goal lane for obstacle detection
> ```
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44889564/ee1c090a-9438-4a96-b5fb-e3720e8c8f0d)
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44889564/86084aec-6289-40fb-bb86-ecbfaa6d3709
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Don't insert stop point in above situation.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Ego stops suddenly.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44889564/75016bb4-95d2-4d78-992e-ecafcb55bacf
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. build behavior path planner with new architecture (set [`COMPILE_WITH_OLD_ARCHITECTURE`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/f627fc30a6730af52348e0605437d7ed6806170e/planning/behavior_path_planner/CMakeLists.txt#L10) FALSE)
> 2. set ego init pos & goal at straight lane
> 3. engage the vehicle
> 4. set NPC on adjacent lane
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - ubuntu22.04
> - universe:main (hash:[c41ba0638f668bb25053f7f4e61ce0602835e582](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/commit/c41ba0638f668bb25053f7f4e61ce0602835e582))
> - launch:main (hash:[be7f530c2ffe43ddb1d156e5b74586c47bc3a173](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/commit/be7f530c2ffe43ddb1d156e5b74586c47bc3a173))
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> When I revert https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3505, this unexpected behavior doesn't happed.
> (But I don't know why.)
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/44889564/6cbab9dc-7c1b-4336-81a7-d2d999de0efa
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

> @satoshi-ota I created PR to solve the problem. The problem is that if the `enable_stop_behind_goal_for_obstacle` param is true, the extendTrajectory function causes NaN positions. So, createOneStepPolygon creates bad polygons and causes false positive collisions.
