### #3640 — Incorrect transform direction used when calculating gnss_base_link in package gnss_poser

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-08  |  **Closed:** 2024-02-20  |  **Author:** @meliketanrikulu
- **Labels:** component:sensing, component:localization
- **Comments:** 11  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3640

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In gnss poser, gnss_base_link is found by using the gnss data and  transform between gnss to base-link. The following transforms are expected to be multiplied, respectively. gnss_pose * gnss_to_base_link. However, in the package, the multiplication is done as gnss_pose * base_link_to_gnss.
> 
> [Here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/4864b1901c67097bf4b692365af7d8766b42ef43/sensing/gnss_poser/src/gnss_poser_core.cpp#L117) the function to make transforms is called. And [this ](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/4864b1901c67097bf4b692365af7d8766b42ef43/sensing/gnss_poser/src/gnss_poser_core.cpp#L331) line contains transform from base_link to gnss using lookup transform. But I think the exact source and target frame should be swapped. Source frame should be gnss target frame base_link
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> When we give the orientation and position of the gnss to the sensor_kit, we expect the gnss_base_link to appear in the correct rotation
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> 
> We were able to obtain the correct result when we gave inverse while giving the rotation of gnss according to sensor_kit_base_link in sensor_kit.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Since roll pitch yaw values for gnss in sample sensor kit are 0 0 0, we do not encounter this error in autoware demos.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-05-09)

> @meliketanrikulu Thank you for the report!
> First of all, the comments and the code are not matching, which makes it difficult to understand.
> Would you please make the necessary corrections?

###### @VRichardJP (2023-05-10)

> I guess they are refering to this snippet:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/f945c019d4fbd00be2cec7a2f914e06efa9e8251/sensing/gnss_poser/src/gnss_poser_core.cpp#L116-L124
> 
> `tf_gnss_antenna2base_link_msg_ptr` names implies "gnss_link -> base_link" transform and is used that way, but `getStaticTransform(gnss_frame_, base_frame_, ...` returns the transform "base_link -> gnss_link"?

###### @meliketanrikulu (2023-05-12)

> > I guess they are refering to this snippet:
> > 
> > https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/f945c019d4fbd00be2cec7a2f914e06efa9e8251/sensing/gnss_poser/src/gnss_poser_core.cpp#L116-L124
> > 
> > `tf_gnss_antenna2base_link_msg_ptr` names implies "gnss_link -> base_link" transform and is used that way, but `getStaticTransform(gnss_frame_, base_frame_, ...` returns the transform "base_link -> gnss_link"?
> 
> Yes . Thank you for explaining @VRichardJP . The function returns base_link -> gnss_link transform.  But I think it should be the other way ( gnss -> base_link ) around

###### @meliketanrikulu (2023-05-22)

> @YamatoAndo could you check this issue

###### @stale (2023-07-21)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-10-27)

> @meliketanrikulu May I close this issue?

###### @meliketanrikulu (2023-10-27)

> Of course. Sorry i forgot to close issue

###### @FranzAlbers (2024-02-05)

> Hello @YamatoAndo, @kminoda, @meliketanrikulu,
> 
> I would like to reopen this issue because I think PR #5033 introduced the problem it claimed to solve. The direction of the transform was correct before #5033 and incorrect after. 
> 
> We noticed this bug when our RTK-DGNSS-equipped vehicle recently started having a height offset of around 80 cm between the `gnss_base_link` from the `gnss_poser`  and our point cloud and lanelet2 maps, while both the precision of the RTK-DGNSS and our maps should be at most a few centimeters. We noted the same height offset and a longitudinal offset of around 60 cm towards the NDT localization pose (`ndt_base_link`). Before #5033, the RTK-DGNSS pose perfectly fitted the map and approximately matched the NDT/EKF pose. 
> 
> This can be seen in the image below. The map->base_link transformation from the `gnss_poser` is used. Our Navsatfix is given in the `adma/imu_link` frame and transformed in the wrong direction with PR #5033, resulting in a floating vehicle. 
> 
> ![Bild1](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/20774470/19fef99b-7763-4417-9114-111bfb06235f)
> 
> The `source_frame` and `target_frame` in `lookupTransform()` are often confused, because the transformation of data between the frames and the transformation of the frames themselves are inverse. (https://github.com/ros/geometry/issues/108#issuecomment-150319158).
> 
> In this case, we intend to use the transform between the frames, so we should use the inverse of what lookupTransform gives us. This was the case before PR # 5033, so I propose to revert it. 

###### @idorobotics (2024-02-13)

> Reopened after a request from @FranzAlbers in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/6392. 

###### @YamatoAndo (2024-02-14)

### #3628 — Improve MPC modeling accuracy

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-05-05  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @TakaHoribe
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:control
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3628

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The current mpc model uses the "error kinematics model in Frenet coordinate". This model obtains the reference path information from only curvature and indirectly regenerates the reference path information by integrating curvature in the MPC process. However, curvature calculation could have non-small errors, and the reference path information given by integration could also have errors.
> 
> In this video, the green path is the trajectory given by the planning module, and the white path is the trajectory re-generated in the MPC model from curvature. There is a large difference when driving in a curve. ([branch for visualization](https://github.com/tier4/autoware.universe/blob/mpc-debug-visualize-modeling-path/control/mpc_lateral_controller/src/mpc.cpp#L106-L166))
> 
> 
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21360593/236382083-79c2a5ce-58d0-4958-8d9e-5499385f420d.mp4
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To improve the MPC tracking accuracy
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> improve model
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> mpc performance is measured and improved

**Comments:**

###### @TakaHoribe (2023-05-06)

> In the video above, the white line is generated by the linearized model, while in the video below, the nonlinear path model is calculated.
> - orange-line: nonlinear path model generated from curvature
> - white-line: predicted ego-path of the MPC
> 
> The accuracy is much better in the nonlinear model.
> 
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21360593/236626809-1f7cff17-f66b-46a0-9f73-c452045d05ec.mp4
> 
>

### #3626 — Incorrect qt5 includes

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-05-04  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, priority:low, status:stale, component:common
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3626

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Similarly to eigen include issue described here https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3615, some qt5 headers are not included properly:
> 
> ```
> src/universe/autoware.universe/common/bag_time_manager_rviz_plugin/src/bag_time_manager_panel.cpp
> 19:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QHBoxLayout>
> 20:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QLabel>
> 21:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QWidget>
> 
> src/universe/autoware.universe/common/bag_time_manager_rviz_plugin/src/bag_time_manager_panel.hpp
> 20:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QComboBox>
> 21:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QLabel>
> 22:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QPushButton>
> 
> src/universe/autoware.universe/common/tier4_traffic_light_rviz_plugin/src/traffic_light_publish_panel.hpp
> 21:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QComboBox>
> 22:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QPushButton>
> 23:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QSpinBox>
> 24:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QTableWidget>
> 
> src/universe/autoware.universe/common/tier4_simulated_clock_rviz_plugin/src/simulated_clock_panel.hpp
> 20:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QComboBox>
> 21:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QDoubleSpinBox>
> 22:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QPushButton>
> 23:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QSpinBox>
> 
> src/universe/autoware.universe/common/tier4_simulated_clock_rviz_plugin/src/simulated_clock_panel.cpp
> 19:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QGridLayout>
> 20:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QHBoxLayout>
> 21:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QLabel>
> 22:#include <qt5/QtWidgets/QWidget>
> 
> ```
> 
> If you generate and check the `compile_commands.json` of `bag_time_manager_rviz_plugin`, you will see this:
> ```
> -isystem /usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/qt5 -isystem /usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/qt5/QtWidgets -isystem /usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/qt5/QtGui -isystem /usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/qt5/QtCore
> ```
> 
> These are the headers that are found by `find_package(Qt5 ${rviz_QT_VERSION} EXACT REQUIRED Core Widgets)`. Actually, the `find_package` and `target_link_libraries` are not necessary, because `rviz_common` seems to already bring everything (but that would be another topic).
> 
> The point it that none of these includes contains for example `<qt5/QtWidgets/QHBoxLayout>`. If the compiler can still find the header and compile, it is because gcc implicitly looks in `/usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/` (which contains `qt5/`). In this case, it does not cause any harm, because the qt5 headers we want are actually there, but in the case the user has the qt5 library installed somewhere else (or 2 versions), the compiler may find qt5 but not the headers (or pick the wrong one, or mix different versions). 
> 
> Questions:
> - which one to prefer between `<QtWidgets/QHBoxLayout>` and `<QHBoxLayout>`? Both seem valid
> - if `rviz_common` already brings qt5... can we just remove the dependency from all rviz plugins? maybe even from `CMakeLists.txt`. I think (not test yet) that adding a library with `ament_auto_add_library()` while `rviz_common` is marked as `<depend>` should automatically include and link qt5. Tt would be very minor, just makes the files simpler.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> qt5 headers properly included
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> currently only works with qt5 installed once by the package manager
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

>

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.

### #3607 — ML based Occupancy 

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-05-02  |  **Closed:** 2024-08-06  |  **Author:** @lexavtanke
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:perception
- **Comments:** 10  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3607

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Integrate occupancy prediction to the autoware perception stack to increase reliability of occupancy grid map. Because now only heuristic method used in this task in autoware as https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/perception/ground_segmentation/. This method is lack of semantic information and also It is tedious to adjust to environment where vehicle operates. 
> 
> With ML based occupancy prediction it is possible to apply for sophisticated logic for obstacle detection and use additional information in planning to increase reliability and comfort. Also 3d occupancy information allow to cope with situations then shape of detected objects can't be incorporated to the simple form as bounding box (unusual vehicle or just simple  open door) 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Enhance Autoware with ML based occupancy prediction method. 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - [OpenOccupancy](https://github.com/JeffWang987/OpenOccupancy)
> - [TPVFormer](https://github.com/wzzheng/TPVFormer)
> - [VoxFormer](https://github.com/NVlabs/VoxFormer)
> - [BEVFormer](https://github.com/fundamentalvision/BEVFormer)
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - Evaluation of different methods  and choose one for implementation
> - Implementation of chosen method
> - Integration implementation with autoware occupancy grid map (without semantic information)
> - Proposal new occupancy grid format for autoware (BEV with semantics, 3d volumetric with semantic)
> 

**Comments:**

###### @BonoloAWF (2023-05-02)

> @lexavtanke could you create a Discussion here https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/categories/design outlining your proposed approach and how this will integrate with the Autoware architecture? 

###### @lexavtanke (2023-05-04)

> @BonoloAWF I've started discussion in design section [link](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3473)

###### @stale (2023-07-16)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @lexavtanke (2023-07-19)

> Model which will be used as a baseline for the integration in to Autoware is BEVDet (it has occupancy head and it is realtime). In the future it is possible to move to a multimodal model (lidar + cams) like BEVfusion.
> Current actual code for the model and its conversion into TensorRT is in the [repo](https://github.com/lexavtanke/BEVDet)
> Current status is to make a code to convert BEVDet occ model to TensorRT. The autors of the original repo provide tensorrt conversion only for base BEVDet model but alll occ versions based on BEVDet4D with mods (stereo, depth).
> 

###### @lexavtanke (2023-07-19)

> Latest progress report can be acceded in [Perception and Sensing WG Meeting notes](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3654)

###### @lexavtanke (2023-07-27)

> Latest progress report can be accessed [here](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1D3Qzl6v5yAUDypcWtiunD613BGq8xbzO/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=112531336602898847104&rtpof=true&sd=true). 
> 
> And current brief status: 
> Code for exporting BEVDet4D to TensorRT is done and in the [repo](https://github.com/lexavtanke/BEVDet).
> 
> Inference speed test results on RTX 3080 Mobile: 
> 
> - approximately 76,5 fps
> - 13 ms per frame 
> - GPU memory consumption 2658 Mb 
> 
> Now I'm working on conversion BEVDet4DStereoOCC to TensorRT.
> 

###### @lexavtanke (2023-08-02)

> Currently I it possible to export BEVDet4dStereoOcc model to ONNX with the use of the [contrib operators](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/blob/main/docs/ContribOperators.md#commicrosoftinverse) because it supports inverse operator. But after it is impossible to convert this model to TensorRT because it doesn't support inverse operator. 
> 
> Inverse operator is used in method gen_grid of the DepthNet part of the view_transformer net. So I start to investigate how I can work with this.
> 
> After some investigation I found that It is possible to export a pytorch model as several separate engines (as it was  done with the center point model in Autoware) but I didn't find any documentation in Autoware about how it was exported after training. There is a mention that center_point was trained with [mmdetection3d](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d). But I didn't find any export  code for ONNX and TensorRT export there. 
> 
> @miursh  Can you please provide the information about export center_point to ONNX and TensorRT or tell who can help with this question?
> 
> After it will be possible to separate the model in 2 parts and write code for gen_grid in the node which will call the engines and process the data. 
> 
> Also possible way which need a bit more investigation is [TPAT](https://github.com/Tencent/TPAT). They tell that it is possible to autogenerate plugins for unsupported operators but I'm not sure that It will works with contrib operators. 
> 
> And the last way is to write own custom plugin for TensorRT.

### #3569 — LiDAR pointcloud disconnects with vehicle body

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-04-28  |  **Closed:** 2023-05-11  |  **Author:** @ahuazuipiaoliang
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:perception, component:localization, type:performance
- **Comments:** 10  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3569

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The LiDAR pointcloud are not connected with the vehicle when the vehicle is moving.
> The vehicle(orange box) should be at the center of rings of pointcloud.
> It seems like the TF publishing is a little bit lagging.
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35034146/235037226-e8ca9945-21ae-46a3-8a09-ed4031ef539a.png)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The vehicle(orange box) should be at the center of rings of pointcloud.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The vehicle(orange box) was not at the center of rings of pointcloud.
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. launch the Autoware
> 2. drive the vehicle manually
> 
> ### Versions
>

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-05-08)

> @ahuazuipiaoliang This behavior is indeed correct. 
> The LiDAR point cloud being displayed is not the most recent one but rather the one acquired in the past.
> It takes some time, approximately 100ms to acquire LiDAR packets and an additional few tens to a few hundred milliseconds for pointcloud_preprocess, before the LiDAR point cloud is displayed in RViz.
> As a result, the LiDAR point cloud is centered around the past vehicle position.

### #3568 — [obstacle avoidance planner]drivable area error, trajectory disconnects with vehicle body

> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> drivable area looks odd when vehicle avoids obstacles. The reference trajectory disconnected with the vehicle body.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> 1. The drivable area should not be a odd polygon in the picture below.
> 2. The reference should be connected with the vehicle body.
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35034146/235035601-0eaaddd0-2bc1-4407-adca-a760c5287a1b.png)
> 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> In the picture above, the 2 lanelets were parallel and in opposite direction, which share a common boundary, because we created them using copy lanelet in Tier IV VMB. There was a U turn at the end of the down lanelet where the vehicle in, the U turn connected with the up lanelet.
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> in simple planning simulator
> 1. set the vehicle in the down lanelet
> ```yaml
> header:
>   stamp:
>     sec: 1682646747
>     nanosec: 563960181
>   frame_id: map
> pose:
>   pose:
>     position:
>       x: -76.65474700927734
>       y: 116.4011459350586
>       z: 0.0
>     orientation:
>       x: 0.0
>       y: 0.0
>       z: 0.01176164365075141
> ```
> 2. set a goal pose in the up lanelet
> ```yaml
> header:
>   stamp:
>     sec: 1682646776
>     nanosec: 650720080
>   frame_id: map
> pose:
>   position:
>     x: -65.8907699584961
>     y: 122.6998062133789
>     z: -1.7958868438885511
>   orientation:
>     x: 0.0
>     y: 0.0
>     z: 0.9998301774823879
>     w: -0.018428678616139057
> ```
> 3. set a static dumpy car that the vehicle could avoid 
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS2: Humble
> - Autoware.universe: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/commit/eeaff1521d9697e65a41a3561460280b1a0749b0
> - Map: [map download](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_aI2wDkTEyoyTD8hp10CkU66yvgZIM5E?usp=sharing)
> 
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> These 2 lanelets share the same linestring as the boundary. the order of points to generate the drivable area could make mistake in this situation.
> 
> ### Additional context
>

> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.

> 
> After the first position comes from Gnss, it is localized in the correct position, but its rotation is wrong. We encounter this error randomly, not on every run. The same issue occurs in both cases where the use_autoware_orientation parameter is true and false.
>

> 
> After the first position comes from gnss, it is expected to initialize with the correct orientation by finding the most correct orientation using the monte carlo method.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> After the first position comes from Gnss, it is localized in the correct position, but its rotation is wrong.
>

>

>

> _No response_

>  To debug, [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/d93b622da3f8ce75dd62cae6c053b6b26746b49f/localization/ndt_scan_matcher/src/pose_initialization_module.cpp#L107) I found that when I print the scores for each particle, all or nearly all of the scores are calculated as 0.0 if they are not initialized. 
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

> So autoware choses the "best" localization, but all of them are bad. 
> 
> How far is the GNSS position from the actual position? x, y, yaw?

### #3475 — inconsistent `ChangeOperationMode` service definition

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-04-20  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, priority:low, status:stale
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3475

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Although it is mostly harmless, the API v1 defines the following `ChangeOperationMode` service:
> ```
> uint16 STOP = 1
> uint16 AUTONOMOUS = 2
> uint16 LOCAL = 3
> uint16 REMOTE = 4
> uint16 mode
> ---
> autoware_common_msgs/ResponseStatus status
> ```
> however, the requested `mode` is never used. Autoware only uses the [service name](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/design/autoware-interfaces/ad-api/list/api/operation_mode/) to determine what to do.
> 
> You can see in the Rviz state panel code how the request is created:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/642256cc2461d70ce5ab5988012ddae7f8623de3/common/tier4_state_rviz_plugin/src/autoware_state_panel.cpp#L559-L562
> 
> This snippet simply calls this function:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/642256cc2461d70ce5ab5988012ddae7f8623de3/common/tier4_state_rviz_plugin/src/autoware_state_panel.hpp#L163-L180
> 
> which creates a default initialized request of type `ChangeOperationMode`. In other words `request.mode == 0`.
> 
> This request is then processed by this function:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/642256cc2461d70ce5ab5988012ddae7f8623de3/system/default_ad_api/src/operation_mode.cpp#L88-L93
> 
> Which totally ignore the value.
> 
> I don't see the point of having a `mode` field in the request if it is not used.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
>

### #3389 — Development plan: dynamic obstacle avoidance

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-04-13  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @takayuki5168
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3389

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, we have an avoidance module in behavior_path_planner only for static obstacles.
> To drive safer without less risk of collision, avoidance of dynamic obstacles is required.
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Avoid dynamic obstacles which are close to the ego or ego's trajectory to reduce the risk of collision.
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20228327/231690445-9586f52b-d1e2-4a96-aef8-4817f8337656.png)
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20228327/231690636-ea71d6d9-89b8-4fab-8d8b-dc798a269933.png)
> 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The current algorithm for static obstacle avoidance will not work for dynamic obstacle avoidance.
> 
> The algorithm of path planning for static obstacle avoidance is as follows.
> - calculate waypoints a certain lateral distance far from the obstacle
> - connect waypoints and the current ego's lane's centerline smoothly
> 
> Connecting points smoothly does not work well in a complicated scene since it is a rule-based algorithm.
> - avoid obstacles on the right and left side by driving like S-shape.
> - avoid an obstacle during a lane change.
> 
> Dynamic obstacle avoidance requires a dynamic change of the waypoints.
> This is the reason the current algorithm cannot be applied to dynamic obstacle avoidance.
> 
> ---
> 
> **1. Approach based on the sideshift module**
> 
> Based on a quick discussion at TIER IV, by using the algorithm of the sideshift module in behavior_path_planner, we can realize dynamic obstacle avoidance.
> 
> The sideshift module plans a path by shifting a lateral distance, realizing lateral jerk/acceleration limitation.
> 
> - determine dynamic obstacles to avoid
>     - The position is close to the ego or ego's trajectory
>     - TTC(time to collision) is low.
>     - It will not go into the ego's lane by lane change.
>     - Speed is high enough.
>     - etc.
> - calculate a lateral distance to shift to keep a space both from the dynamic obstacle and road boundary
> - plan a path based on the  sideshift module
> 
> **2. Approach with the optimization-based path planner (obstacle_avoidance_planner)**
> 
> Dynamic obstacle avoidance can be realized by obstacle_avoidance_planner.
> The following figure is static obstacle avoidance by obstacle_avoidance_planner.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2880
> 
> By removing dynamic obstacles to avoid and their predicted paths from the drivable area, the avoidance will work.
> How stable it will be is not guaranteed though.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Resolve remaining issues.

**Comments:**

###### @takayuki5168 (2023-04-28)

> Current progress.
> The parameters are tuned for the video to show the performance easily to see.
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20228327/235217296-52ce9757-9e98-4c4a-a190-73ed8a619d9b.mp4
> 
> 

###### @yukkysaito (2023-04-28)

> This is a very nice feature! :+1: 

###### @stale (2023-06-29)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @takayuki5168 (2024-01-18)

> # The current status on 2024/01/18
> 
> ## Implementation
> The second approach was implemented and merged to the autoware.universe.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/planning/behavior_path_dynamic_avoidance_module
> 
> > 2. Approach with the optimization-based path planner (obstacle_avoidance_planner)
> 
> ## Documentation
> Not completed yet
> https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/behavior_path_dynamic_avoidance_module/
> 
> ## How to enable the future
> 1. Enable the following option
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/d3811ef583fa07155c4c5565c3ec95ef816e75eb/autoware_launch/config/planning/preset/default_preset.yaml#L11
> 2. Set the following parameter to false
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/d3811ef583fa07155c4c5565c3ec95ef816e75eb/autoware_launch/config/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/motion_planning/obstacle_avoidance_planner/obstacle_avoidance_planner.param.yaml#L6
> 
> Proposal:
> Regarding the upper 2nd parameter, how about setting it to false by default.
> When this parameter is set to true, when the trajectory is outside the drivable area, the stop point is inserted before the drivable area.
> When set to false, just a green virtual wall is shown and no stop point is inserted.
> 
> 
> ## Validation
> We tested the feature on the Japan Taxi vehicle in Tokyo.
> Mostly, the feature is working well.
> 
> The videos of the examples in the real world are shown here.
> <details>
> <summary>Open</summary>
> 
> The object behind got close to the ego.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/20228327/403ce379-0178-49d0-a5fe-8c7787665022
> 
> The ego got close to the front object in the branch road.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/20228327/f6995443-8f45-4678-9816-243f2a9d3e48
> 
> The oncoming object is close to the ego.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/20228327/dd9b2021-e7cb-42bc-9ec8-b59b8eb66de9
> 
> The front object pulled over.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/20228327/1b49e8f5-eb63-4130-9035-1da9cda67d78
> 
> The front object pulled out.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/assets/20228327/3e1c9785-123d-4c9c-b496-256b6e235db1
> 
> </details>
> 
> ## Limitation
> 
> - The maximum deviation of the trajectory from the reference path is limited to 0.5m by default as a prototype implementation.
>     - To make this value bigger, the following feature is required.
>         - turn on the blinker when the ego will go into the next lane.
>         - check the safety behind when the ego will go into the next lane.
>         - expand the drivable area to the next lane.
> - Avoidance against dynamic pedestrians and bicycles is not supported.
> - Better architecture to send the obstacles to avoid to the motion planning
>     - Currently, they are applied to the drivable area. With this architecture, the motion planning does not know where is the road and the obstacles from the drivable area.
> 
> These are the major remained tasks.

### #3386 — DevOps Dojo: ROS Node Launch (Phase 1 - Motivation)

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-04-13  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @kaspermeck-arm
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, DevOps Dojo: ROS Node Launch
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3386

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> DevOps: ROS Node Launch will address the topic of how ROS nodes are launched. Guidelines, documentation and changes to configuration files will be made, based on best-practices from cloud-native and software defined development methodologies.
> 
> Phase 1 - Motivation
> - [DevOps Dojo: ROS Node Launch (Phase 1 - Motivation)](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3386)
> 
> Phase 2 - Definition
> - Add link
> 
> Phase 3 - Execution
> - Add link
> 
> Phase 4 - Integration
> - Add link
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Phase 1 - Motivation:
> - clear purpose
>   - enable developers and users of Autoware to conveniently reconfigure how Autoware nodes are launched
> - outline proposed features
>   - modify parameter value(s)
>     - reduce max speed
>   - launch fewer nodes than the original launch file does
>     - ability to turn off specific nodes to understand when something stops working
>   - replace existing Autoware node with another/proprietary node ("drop-in")
>     - a student at a university who wants to optimize a single node as a research project
>     - a startup that wants to show off a novel and proprietary algorithm
>   - configure nodes to enable zero-copy
>     - increase performance when nodes are in the same containers
>   - name space and remapping
>     - multiple of the same node, e.g., multi-sensor configuration (BEV camera)
>   - enable and disable logging/debugging nodes
>     - reduce overhead of logging/debugging while in field
> - identify beneficiaries, stakeholders and shareholders
>   - Autoware developers
>     - consistent and reliable launch files
>   - users who deploy Autoware
>     - ease of changing the launch pipeline to suit user's need
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Involve the entire Autoware community to understand current deficiencies and what type of features are desired. Launching Autoware nodes is one of the most fundamental, if not the most fundamental, aspect of developing and using Autoware.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Phase 1 is considered complete once satisfactory motivation, desired personas and features has been outlined and what the requirements for these are.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-04-12  |  **Closed:** 2024-07-23  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:planning

> 
> I have tried to remove unecessary lanelets, but the behavior is still the same (with a few added debug info):
> [outside_drivable_area-2023-04-12_13.40.43.webm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/231352215-ab7365f6-d7aa-464e-9817-64f160a5ccf5.webm)

> No brake
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> strong brake

> TODO

###### @VRichardJP (2023-04-14)

> Since the `right_bound.point.size() == 2` is fairly easy to detect, I could run the program with gdb and stop right a the moment the strange right bound is generated.
> 
> I am still investigating, but while stepping inside [`generateDrivableArea`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/d73c3ae41b53b76589d78a7a019cd065d031fd9d/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/utils/utils.cpp#L897), I have found these strange values:
> ```
> (gdb) p front_pose
> $26 = {position = {x = 75624.150317563472, y = 31114.308224363751, z = 3.8433717986237106}, orientation = {x = -0.0067077158534262181, y = -0.0061622348519188574, z = -0.73638514544570388, w = 0.67650125718772247}}
> (gdb) front_left_start_idx
> Undefined command: "front_left_start_idx".  Try "help".
> (gdb) p front_left_start_idx
> $27 = 0
> (gdb) p front_right_start_idx
> $28 = 34
> (gdb) p left_start_point
> $29 = {x = 75626.080972052165, y = 31114.669336292969, z = 3.8403773480652288}
> (gdb) p right_start_point
> $30 = {x = 75648.644, y = 31111.8014, z = 5.5366999999999997}
> (gdb) p left_start_idx
> $31 = 0
> (gdb) p right_start_idx
> $32 = 33
> (gdb) p goal_pose
> $33 = {position = {x = 75628.205621774119, y = 31111.936214821744, z = 4.0486484954393092}, orientation = {x = 0.018106582803569488, y = -0.00084042451797931123, z = 0.99876042799084508, w = 0.046357877705424495}}
> (gdb) p goal_left_start_idx
> $34 = 29
> (gdb) p goal_right_start_idx
> $35 = 34
> (gdb) p left_goal_point
> $36 = {x = 75627.391000000003, y = 31110.122100000001, z = 3.9397000000000002}
> (gdb) p right_goal_point
> $37 = {x = 75627.708100000003, y = 31113.8724, z = 4.1097999999999999}
> (gdb) p left_goal_idx
> $38 = 29
> (gdb) p right_goal_idx
> $39 = 34
> ```
> 
> Put on the map, the points look like this:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/231963666-6eb5c6dd-aee8-4cd8-9ca0-ed82f07a089f.png)
> 
> - FP: `front_pose`
> - Ls: `left_start_point`
> - RS: `right_start_point`
> - G: `goal_pose`
> - LG: `left_goal_point`
> - RG: `right_goal_point`
> - P: `current_pose`
> 
> The `right_start_point` looks oddly placed. I checked the code beyond, and points are added from `right_start_idx` to `right_goal_idx`. Here only the last 2 points are copied.
> 
> The problem boils down to these lines:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/d73c3ae41b53b76589d78a7a019cd065d031fd9d/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/utils/utils.cpp#L900-L903
> 
> For the right bound it returns `34`, which is very far on the path. We can clearly see that points on the previous comment screenshot

###### @VRichardJP (2023-04-14)

> Down the rabbit hole:
> 
> [`generateDrivableArea`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/d73c3ae41b53b76589d78a7a019cd065d031fd9d/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/utils/utils.cpp#L903) calls [`findNearestSegmentIndexFromLateralDistance`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/d73c3ae41b53b76589d78a7a019cd065d031fd9d/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/utils/utils.cpp#L84), which calls [`findNearestSegmentIndex`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/d73c3ae41b53b76589d78a7a019cd065d031fd9d/common/motion_utils/include/motion_utils/trajectory/trajectory.hpp#L358), which calls `findNearestIndex` with the `right_bound` and the `front_pose`.
> 
> So we get here:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/d73c3ae41b53b76589d78a7a019cd065d031fd9d/common/motion_utils/include/motion_utils/trajectory/trajectory.hpp#L360-L367
> 
> And what happens is that the right bound last point is closer from the target pose than the first few points. So `nearest_idx` is set to `35 = points.size() - 1`, and then the function returns `34`, which causes the issue.
> 
> Visually, it is easy to see the problem with the current logic:
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/231973026-68289fbe-dd2e-423b-b731-f64ffa5c78ec.png)

###### @VRichardJP (2023-04-14)

> One solution could be to find the `right_bound` segment that is the closest from the `front_pose` (i.e. measure the distance point<->segment), and take the first point of that segment, Since `front_pose` is constructed on the centerline and the `right_bound` does not overlap on the path, this method would always return the desired result.
> 
> Edit: this is only true when we have a single lane. When we have multiple lanes the closest segment by projection may not be the one we want.
> 
> Maybe a better approach is not to try to compute anything here? The left and right bounds seems to have been calculated already, so why do we need to calculate new ones?
> If we assume the left and right are "almost" correct and just want to refine them, we could maybe do something like this: explore left/right points in order and keep going while the next point is closer than the previous. In other words getting the "closest point at the beginning". For the goal point it would be the same story but in reverse. In pretty sure this logic is still brittle and would break on some weirdly shaped lanelets (2d geometry is hard...)

###### @VRichardJP (2023-04-14)

> Example with the proposed fix (for single lane only):
> [outside_drivable_area_fix-2023-04-14_20.04.09.webm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/232028108-d3bc527c-f1a5-40ce-b998-2aeefd276bc7.webm)

> +  };
> +

>    const auto front_pose = path.points.empty() ? current_pose : path.points.front().point.pose;
>    const size_t front_left_start_idx =
> -    findNearestSegmentIndexFromLateralDistance(left_bound, front_pose.position);
> +    getClosestSegmentIndex(left_bound, front_pose.position);
>    const size_t front_right_start_idx =
> -    findNearestSegmentIndexFromLateralDistance(right_bound, front_pose.position);
> +    getClosestSegmentIndex(right_bound, front_pose.position);
>    const auto left_start_point =
>      calcLongitudinalOffsetStartPoint(left_bound, front_pose, front_left_start_idx, -front_length);
>    const auto right_start_point =
>      calcLongitudinalOffsetStartPoint(right_bound, front_pose, front_right_start_idx, -front_length);

>    const auto right_goal_point =

>    const size_t left_goal_idx = std::max(
> -    goal_left_start_idx, findNearestSegmentIndexFromLateralDistance(left_bound, left_goal_point));
> +    goal_left_start_idx, getClosestSegmentIndex(left_bound, left_goal_point));

> ```C++

>       | ranges::views::transform([](auto &&p) { return Point2d {p.x, p.y}; })
>       | ranges::views::sliding(2)
>       | ranges::views::transform([=](auto &&segment) { 
>         auto projected_point = pointToSegment(p, segment[0], segment[1]);
>         return projected_point.distance;
>       });
>     const auto min_it = ranges::min_element(distance_to_projected_points);

### #5613 — Double detection of objects 

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-04-11  |  **Closed:** 2024-04-29  |  **Author:** @adamkrawczyk
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:perception
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/5613

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When used with `scenario_simulator_v2` there are cases when the object is detected twice (in the published output topic `/perception/object_recognition/objects` there are sometimes double detections. The input topic `/perception/object_recognition/detection/objects` - from the scenario_simulator_v2 does not contain the duplicated detections). 
> 
> See attached rosbag. 
> [rosbag2_2023_04_11-08_32_18.zip](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/files/11197346/rosbag2_2023_04_11-08_32_18.zip)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> One detection of the pedestrian (it is the case in the attached scenario)
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The pedestrian detection is duplicated
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Build autoware from the main branch (in my case it happens at least from the `18d7f6f22a11582aea568566e6bde77d42c1d794` (~360 commits behind) 
> 2. Run the scenario with the following configuration (launcher could be from the scenario simulator v2 - `scenario_test_runner.launch.py`) : 
>   -  architecture_type : awf/universe
>   -  vehicle_model : sample_vehicle              
>   - sensor_model : sample_sensor_kit
> 
> The rest is the default. 
> 
> The scenario (remove `.txt` - github limitation): 
> [demo-unstructured.yaml.txt](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/files/11197377/demo-unstructured.yaml.txt)
> 
> The map used for testing is the [kashiwanoha map](https://github.com/tier4/scenario_simulator_v2/tree/master/map/kashiwanoha_map), we have used a slightly modified. If there will be some issues with the map I think I can provide it but have to consult before sharing. 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 amd64
> - Ros2: humble
> - Autoware: main
> - Scenario_simulator_v2: [master](https://github.com/tier4/scenario_simulator_v2)
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> I haven't analyzed the autoware but it seems that it is not the issue with the scenario_simulator - the detections are not duplicated
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> Graphical representation (there are also two descriptions that make the view so unclear) but you can see the two yellow boxes representing the object (pedestrian) 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29305346/231079066-0b11806e-7498-48d2-a67f-588fa5567683.png)
>

### #3318 — clearly state and check assumptions on input data of `pointcloud_preprocessor` filters

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-04-08  |  **Closed:** 2024-07-31  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3318

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> As a way to improve filters reliability, and after https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3306 is merged, I would like to add proper assumption checks in `pointcloud_preprocessor` filters.
> 
> As explained in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3306 and https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2618, several `pointcloud_preprocessor` filters make implicit assumptions on the input data. In most cases these assumptions are correct but sometimes it is not the case. And when it is not, it is actually really difficult to find it out.
> 
> For example `ring_outlier_filter` intensity output [has been wrong for at least a year](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/commit/699b60ee4c96e408d19de04f2ab2aa845a2a5830) without anyone noticing.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Improve filters reliability.
> Later, the information could be used to optimize the code further (e.g. use `constexpr` field offset when input data layout is compatible with known types.)
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> A simple solution is to add a simple check in each `filter` function that makes implicit assumptions on the input data, like this:
> ```C++
> void RingOutlierFilterComponent::filter(
>   const PointCloud2ConstPtr & input, [[maybe_unused]] const IndicesPtr & indices,
>   PointCloud2 & output)
> {
>   // make sure we can memcpy from input->data to PointXYZI type
>   if (!utils::is_data_layout_compatible_with_PointXYZI(*input)) {
>     RCLCPP_ERROR(get_logger(), "Invalid input data layout. Output may be incorrect");
>   }
> ```
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> 1. list functions which make strong assumption on the data layout (e.g. `reinterpret_cast<PointXYZI*>`)
> 2. for each, add small check and report an error if the assumptions is wrong (the code is most likely buggy)

### #3269 — `ring_outlier_filter` blows up my cache (and yours too)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-04-04  |  **Closed:** 2023-08-24  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, type:new-feature, status:stale, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3269

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Current `ring_outlier_filter` implementation is slow. I have not run a precise benchmark, but this filter runs significantly slower than any other filter.
> During a recent test drive with our demo vehicle, I observed that when `ring_outlier_filter` is disabled, htop CPU usage is reduced by 20% (!)
> 
> I am pretty sure it is a known problem, and @sykwer is working hard on improving the current implementation.
> His changes already improve the performance a lot, but I have the feeling his approach does not tackle the true cause of the bad performance, so I think it is worth opening a separate issue.
> 
> Let's first look at how the current algorithm is implemented. Roughly it looks like this:
> 1. Iterate over the input cloud and group point indices by ring
> 2. For each ring:
> 2.1. iterate over the ring points, and group points belonging to the same "walk"
> 3.1. when a walk is closed, copy indexed points to the output cloud if the walk is long enough.
> 
> There is nothing wrong with the algorithm in itself. It looks fairly efficient.
> It has a big problem though: it is not adapted to the data it is supposed to process.
> 
> Let me explain.
> By design, LIDAR sensors naturally collect data in "azimut-major order". So unless one of the previous preprocessing node changes that order, the input cloud data of `ring_outlier_filter` always looks like this:
> ```
> p[0] = {ring = 0; azimut = 0}
> p[1] = {ring = 1; azimut = 0}
> p[2] = {ring = 2; azimut = 0}
> p[3] = {ring = 3; azimut = 0}
> ```
> 
> For example here, I have printed the first 100 point indices of ring 0 (from one rosbag of mine):
> ```
> 234000 236352 240432 283680 375552 376608 377664 536064 562800 563904 590160 596352 597360 744000 785136 798624 874032 875088 876144 877200 878256 879312 880272 881280 882288 883392 884544 885648 887904 889056 890208 891216 892128 893136 894048 894912 895824 896784 897696 898656 899664 900624 901680 902688 903552 904416 905376 906288 907152 908064 909024 910080 910992 912048 913056 913920 914832 915696 916608 917568 918384 919200 920112 921024 922080 922992 923856 924912 926112 927216 928272 929184 930144 931344 932256 933408 934464 935280 936240 938304 940560 941616 942576 943824 945024 946176 947520 948624 949776 950928 952176 955632 957072 958464 959664 960864 961824 964320 965616 966960
> ```
> 
> As you can see, consecutive ring points are **very** far from each other in memory. In the previous example, the minimum distance between 2 ring points is 816 bytes!
> 
> If we have a N layers LIDAR sensor, 2 consecutive ring points are separated by `N*sizeof(PointXYZIRADRT)` bytes (if the cloud is "complete" and unfiltered). So with a 32-layers LIDAR sensor, 2 consecutive points are seperated by around 1KB! This is exactly what I observe.
> 
> My poor x86 has a L1 data cache of 32KB, and a L2 cache of 256KB, so the node is bound to cache miss all the time (I should have checked the % of cache miss). No wonder my CPU usage increases by 20% when I use `ring_outlier_filter`: it's not the node which is slow, it's my CPU which has no more cache!
> 
> I think there is no choice but to find a way to rewrite the implementation in a cache friendly manner. For example, instead of exploring ring points separately, it could be better to just process all input points in order (i.e. compute the 128 ring walks simultaneously). The same goes for copying the data in the output buffer∩╝îwe should try as much as possible to keep points in order (easier said than done).
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> ≡ƒÜÇ≡ƒÜÇ≡ƒÜÇfast!≡ƒÜÇ≡ƒÜÇ≡ƒÜÇ
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> ≡ƒÉî≡ƒÉî≡ƒÉîslow!≡ƒÉî≡ƒÉî≡ƒÉî
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Run it!
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

> passthrough_filter/passthrough_filter_uint16_nodelet.cpp
> 49:  const PointCloud2ConstPtr & input, const IndicesPtr & indices, PointCloud2 & output)
> 
> pointcloud_accumulator/pointcloud_accumulator_nodelet.cpp
> 37:  const PointCloud2ConstPtr & input, [[maybe_unused]] const IndicesPtr & indices,
> 
> vector_map_filter/vector_map_inside_area_filter.cpp
> 80:  const PointCloud2ConstPtr & input, [[maybe_unused]] const IndicesPtr & indices,
> 
> polygon_remover/polygon_remover.cpp
> 52:  const PointCloud2ConstPtr & input, [[maybe_unused]] const IndicesPtr & indices,
> ```
> 
> Except for that filter, I propose we modify all other filters as such:
> ```c++
> void VoxelGridDownsampleFilterComponent::filter(
>   const PointCloud2ConstPtr & input, const IndicesPtr & indices, PointCloud2 & output)
> {
>   if (indices) {
>     throw std::runtime_error("indices are not supported yet");
>   }
>   // ...
> ```

###### @yukkysaito (2023-04-07)

> >Several filters within pointcloud_preprocessor do not support indices, yet they don't raise any error if indices are provided.
> 
> @VRichardJP 
> Let me check a little more.
> Does it need to generate an error when indices is provided?
> Is there a problem if it is just not used?

###### @VRichardJP (2023-04-07)

> If the user provides indices, they expect it will be used. So I think it is bad to silently ignore indices if they are provided but not used. At least if a warning is provided, users will know their use case is not supported.
> 
> Autoware does not use indices at the moment, but it is better to make it clear they are not supported (autoware users should not have to check the code to see if something is supported or not).

### #3229 — Lane change module development plan

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-31  |  **Closed:** 2024-01-18  |  **Author:** @rej55
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3229

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Lane change module has features to plan lane changing to arrive goal.
> The features implemented in the current lane change module are following:
> 
> - Driving lane planning
>   - To arrive goal, it plans when and where to change lanes
>   - The module also has a feature to change lanes by a request from operators
> - Safety check
> - Blinker control
> - Path generation (now improving)
> - Aborting lane change (now improving)
> 
> To make it more efficient and safer, some issues remain:
> 
> - Improving path planning
>   - Path planning more like a real driver to improve feeling of riding
> - Improving aborting lane change
>   - To abort more safely, improving aborting behavior planning is required
> - Planning with obstacle avoidance
> - Dynamic route planning
>   - For example, detour if lane change is not possible due to traffic jams
>   - Common issue with mission planner
> - Interactions with other cars
>   - For example, get in a car platoon in a traffic jam
>   - Indication of intention by blinker
> - Perform multiple lanes lane change efficiently.
>   - Currently, multiple lanes lane change is performed by separating the behavior into several single lane changes. 
> - Topic hz is currently an issue for lane change module.
>   - It will be nice if we can reduce the time on the collision assessment. 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> For more efficient and safer lane changes, the remained issues should be resolved.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> We are currently working on the following issues:
> 
> - Improving path planning
>   - Planning including acceleration during lane change
>   - Consideration of curvature according to vehicle speed
> - Improving aborting lane change
>   - Scenario enumeration
>   - Reconsider criteria for returning current lane or entering target lane
> - Planning with obstacle avoidance
>   - Cooperating with avoidance module in behavior path planner
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Resolve remained issues.

### #3224 — Intersection module development plan

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-30  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @soblin
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:help-wanted, status:stale
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3224

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> ## overview
> [intersection module](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/intersection-design/) in behavior_velocity_planner judges if the vehicle can safely pass intersections. This module is responsible for
> - collision checking with upcoming vehicles
>   - behave properly according to the presence of traffic lights, the type of active traffic light bulb, given RightOfWay
> - detect occlusion generated by other static/dynamic objects in the intersection and prevent the possible collisions with vehicles running from occluded area
> 
> This module is activated when the path covers a lane with `turn_direction` tag, and extract `attention_area` from the overlapped lanes. How `attention_area` is extracted depends on the `turn_direction` (left/right, straight) and RightOfWay which is assigned to that lane. The [RightOfWay settings](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_common/blob/main/tmp/lanelet2_extension/docs/lanelet2_format_extension.md#right-of-way) may vary from country to country.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - safe and efficient (not too conservative) collision checking with vehicles on the `detection_area`
>   - collision checking by ttc (time to collision), admissible braking distance, etc.
>   - change `detection_area` according to the traffic light status
> - follow RightOfWay rules
> - handle the cases where
>    - the other vehicle is not following RightOfWay rules
>  - the other vehicle is yielding the way to ego vehicle
> - behave safely when `detection_area` is occluded
>  - consider possible collisions with objects which may be running from the occluded area, even though they are not detected immediately
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Currently occlusion handling is in progress and will be merged in a few weeks. `occpancy_grid_map` package should be improved for better occlusion detection.
> Also `map_based_prediction` package should be improved for better/efficient collision checking.
> For realistic scenarios this module should handle the cases where other vehicles does not follow the traffic rule strictly or they yield their way to ego vehicles.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> The logic is widely checked through scenario testing and stress-tested on real vehicles.

**Comments:**

### #3223 — PullOver/Out limitation and development plan

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-30  |  **Closed:** 2024-02-05  |  **Author:** @kosuke55
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:planning
- **Comments:** 16  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3223

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> pull_over/out modules have the following limitations.
> 
> - [pull_over](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/behavior_path_planner_pull_over_design/)
>   - Support parking on only `road_shoulder` 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39142679/229003311-09e8dff9-ef76-4059-bf3d-0416f4215c9e.png)
> 
>   - Cannot park on the `road` or in the same lane.
>   - Cannot consider moving objects for safety judgment
> - [pull_out](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/behavior_path_planner_pull_out_design/
> )
>   - Cannot start in cases requiring complicated maneuvering
>   - Can only start from `road_shoulder`
>   - Cannot start from the `road` or the same lane
>   - Cannot consider moving objects for safety judgment
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> solve these limitations and improve functionalies
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - pull_over
>   - Support parking on both `road` and `road_shoulder` ->(deal this this patter with LC. pull over support only current road) ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39142679/229003411-d7fa2ff3-dc65-4849-b341-00e4b9893546.png) 
>   - Implement a goal planner
>     - Activate every time when near the goal
>       - If goal adjustment is allowed: park at the side edge of the lane(like pull over) ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39142679/229003431-da95c824-e970-43f2-90d9-485ed19f2f6b.png)
>       - If goal adjustment is not allowed: park at the given goal (like the current lane following)
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39142679/229003573-26ee5ff2-678f-46f7-9a0f-20f1ebfdc46a.png)
> 
>   - work with MRM (Minimum Risk Maneuver)
>     - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3221 
>     - also support rerouting when driving
>   - Consider moving objects
> 
> - pull_out
>   - Support starting from both `road` and `road_shoulder`
>   - Implement a start planner
>     - Activate every time at starting driving
>     - Start towards the centerline or shift from the current lane to the desired lane
>   - Consider moving objects
>   - Use a free space planner for starting driving
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Complete these implementations to resolve limitations and improve functionalies

### #3218 — `ring_outlier_filter` ignores ring's "end" point and "start" point are neighbors

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-30  |  **Closed:** 2023-08-23  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:perception
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3218

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Copied from https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3014#discussion_r1128802859
> 
> In the `ring_outlier_filter` implementation, points that belong to a same ring are stored in a buffer (in azimut order). The filter explores the buffer from start to end, and remove isolated points (i.e. points with no close neighbor). However the current implementation ignores the buffer is circular (the "first" and "last" points of the ring are connected). As a consequence, the filter may delete valid points and create "holes" in the output data.
> 
> For example, let's imagine this ring:
> ```
> ring : xxxx..xxxxxxxxxxx..xxxx.xx
> index: abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
> ``` 
> Where chains of `x` represent points from the same "walk" (close to each other), and `.` the noisy points ment to be filtered (no close neighbor). The index alphabet is just for the explanation. So in the situation here, there are 3 chains:
> 1. from 'g' to 'q'
> 2. from 't' to 'w'
> 3. from 'y' to 'd' (wrapped around)
> 
> However in the current implementation, we start at index 0 ('a') and the start/end of the ring are not considered connected. So we end up finding 3 chains, but different:
> 1. from 'a' to 'd'
> 2. from 'g' to 'q'
> 3. from 't' to 'w'
> 
> The algorithm would consider the walk 'y' -> 'z', but as it is too short (less than 4 points) the points would be filtered out.
> 
> With the default parameters `num_points_threshold_ = 4`, up to 6 points could be missing because of that (3 points at the beginning, 3 points at the end). When using bigger `num_points_threshold_` value, the filter would sometimes produce some big blinspot in the data.
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> In a ring, start and end points are connected, so they may belong to the same walk.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> end-start connection ignored. Some valid points may be wrongfully deleted.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #3217 — `ring_outlier_filter` skips last input point

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-30  |  **Closed:** 2023-08-24  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:perception
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3217

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Copied from https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3014#discussion_r1128788929
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/cb103ec9c8149fffcf2a665ca37b69fe465e0a61/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp#L92-L95
> 
> I think we are skipping the last point with this logic.
> For example, let's imagine a perfect circle ring with N points.
> 
> When we first enter the first loop we have :
> ```
> idx = 0
> walk_first_idx = 0
> walk_last_idx = idx = 0
> current_data_idx = indices[0]
> next_data_idx= indices[1]
> ```
> 
> The ring is a perfect circle, so all the points are part of the same walk. So we always continue here:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/cb103ec9c8149fffcf2a665ca37b69fe465e0a61/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp#L111-L116
> 
> On the last loop we have:
> ```
> idx = N-2
> walk_first_idx = 0
> walk_last_idx = idx = N-2
> current_data_idx = indices[N-2]
> next_data_idx= indices[N-1]
> ```
> 
> So after the loop, we have these lines:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/cb103ec9c8149fffcf2a665ca37b69fe465e0a61/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp#L133-L141
> 
> which basically copy points from `walk_first_idx = 0` to `walk_last_idx = N-2`, thus skipping the last point.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> All points are processed
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Last point missing :(
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #3215 — On abusive use of `reinterpret_cast` UB

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-30  |  **Closed:** 2023-06-05  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3215

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> As pointed [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3014#discussion_r1128758988), there are places in Autoware where `reinterpret_cast` is abusively used to "convert" data types.
> 
> [There are endless talks over the internet](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/573294/when-to-use-reinterpret-cast/) about how misleading `reinterpret_cast` is. Basically, dereferencing a reinterpreted pointer `p` with `*reinterpret_cast<T*>(p)` is only valid if `p` originally points to data of type `T` (e.g. `p = new T()`), or a `const`/`signed`/`unsigned` variant, or if `T==char` (or `unsigned char` or `std::byte`). If `p` originally points to any other type, even if "it looks" the same, is straight UB.
> 
> For example, copying `PointXYIZ` from `uint8_t[]` like here is UB:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/cb103ec9c8149fffcf2a665ca37b69fe465e0a61/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp#L123
> 
> To create a valid `PointXYZI` from the buffer, it would be necessary at least to cast each field separately (e.g. like `p.x = *reinterpret_cast<float*>(&data[p_offset + x_field_offset])`).
> 
> Edit: according to this [excellent writeup](https://gist.github.com/shafik/848ae25ee209f698763cffee272a58f8#type-punning-arrays), reinterpret casting from a buffer violates strict aliasing rules (but I guess it is ok in the scope of an immediate copy?), and could run into misaligned memory issues (but all the data we manipulate is always aligned, right?...). The author suggests the only safe way to manipulate data is to `memcpy` (yew!). Hopefully, C++ makes it possible to wrap things and avoid the memcpy boilerplate (for example the `const_unaligned_pointer` described here: http://pzemtsov.github.io/2016/11/06/bug-story-alignment-on-x86.html)
> 
> Similarly, even though `PointXYZIRADRT` and `PointXYZI` "start the same", it is UB to use `reinterpret_cast` to copy between the 2 structs. For example:
> ```C++
> PointXYZIRADRT p1{};
> PointXYZI p2 = *reinterpret_cast<PointXYZI*>(&p1); // UB
> ```
> 
> It may "work" now... until the compiler decides otherwise.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Remove all UB `reinterpret_cast` in Autoware code base.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. grep!
> 2. fix
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> No more yolo `reinterpret_cast` UB.

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-04-01)

> # Taxonomy of `reinterpret_cast` usage in autoware.universe
> 
> ## 1. Passing pointer to an API
> 
> For example:
> 
> ```C++
> sockaddr_in client;
> int new_sock = accept(sock, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr *>(&client), &len);
> ```
> 
> Valid. Exactly what `reinterpret_cast` has been designed for.
> Note that it is recommended to use `static_cast` in the case it is only necessary to cast from/to `void*`.
> 
> ## 2. Reading/Writing an object byte representation
> 
> For example:
> 
> ```C++
> file.write(reinterpret_cast<const char *>(plan_->data()), plan_->size());
> ```
> 
> Valid. It is possible to cast into `char*`, `unsigned char*`, `std::byte*` and their `const` variants.
> Writing the object bytes is legal, but not portable (e.g. because endianess, data type size, etc).
> 
> ## 3. Reading/Writing from/into a buffer as if is was an object
> 
> For example:
> 
> ```C++
> reinterpret_cast<float32_t *>(v.data())[i] = dis(gen)
> ```
> 
> This is UB and dangerous. I know everyone does that and "it works" because most compilers are kind enough, but it's a tic-toc bomb you leave behind.
> First, why is that not valid C++ code? C++ has [many complex rules regarding what makes a valid "object"](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/object) and using `reinterpret_cast<T*>` on a buffer is not one of them. `reinterpret_cast` is basically a way to say to the compiler "trust me, someone else has created a valid object here before".
> 
> In practice however, this UB is known to work perfectly fine under the following conditions:
> 
> 1. `T` is trivially copiable (such as `int`, `float`, `struct { int, char }`)
> 2. the buffer meet the alignment requirement of `T` (e.g. `float` must be aligned on 4 bytes)
> 3. you are not messing around with aliasing (because you violate strict aliasing rule)
> 
> Condition 1 is not a problem in autoware code base, as I have ever only seen `reinterpret_cast` with simple types and structs.
> Condition 3 is normally not a problem in this context. To make the compiler break the program because of strict aliasing, you [really have to want it](https://gist.github.com/shafik/848ae25ee209f698763cffee272a58f8#preliminary-examples).
> Condition 2 is the important one. If the buffer is not aligned properly, the compiler may definitely break the program. Luckily (or unluckily depending how you see it) modern x86 and ARM64 can access badly aligned data (just slightly slower). So the program may still run fine when optimization level is low. However if you start to push the compiler for more advanced optimizations (e.g. `-msse`, `-march=native`), then your program will either compute rubbish and simply fail. A good illustration [here](http://pzemtsov.github.io/2016/11/06/bug-story-alignment-on-x86.html).
> 
> If 1, 2 and 3 are met, the `reinterpret_cast` is officially an undefined behavior but works in practice. However, if you can't be 100% sure the data is properly aligned (for example if the buffer is created by another library), then [it is better to use `std::memcpy`](https://gist.github.com/shafik/848ae25ee209f698763cffee272a58f8#type-punning-arrays). With `-O2` or `-O3` the `memcpy` has no performance impact over the unsafe `reinterpret_cast`.
> 
> ## 4. Reading/Writing data from different types
> 
> This is just a worse version of 3. Even if the types looks the same, there is no reason not to copy the data properly, which can't break the program and will be optimized out by the compiler.
> 
> ## Grep time
> 
> Here is a list of all `reinterpret_cast` use in universe, categorized by pattern (from 1 to 4). For type 3, I make the difference between A and B: A when the cast is "safe" (typically alignment is correct) and B when it smells:
> 
> ```grep
> perception/traffic_light_ssd_fine_detector/src/nodelet.cpp
> 240:        reinterpret_cast<const float *>(pixels.datastart), // Type 3A: cv::Mat data is aligned on 16-bytes
> 241:        reinterpret_cast<const float *>(pixels.dataend));  // Type 3A: cv::Mat data is aligned on 16-bytes
> 
> perception/traffic_light_ssd_fine_detector/lib/src/trt_ssd.cpp
> 164:  file.write(reinterpret_cast<const char *>(plan_->data()), plan_->size()); // Type 2
> 
> perception/lidar_apollo_instance_segmentation/src/detector.cpp
> 72:    outfile.write(reinterpret_cast<char *>(plan->data()), plan->size()); // Type 2
> 
> perception/lidar_apollo_instance_segmentation/lib/include/Utils.hpp
> 122:  *reinterpret_cast<T *>(buffer) = val;        // Type 3B: unaligned write -> should use memcpy instead
> 129:  val = *reinterpret_cast<const T *>(buffer);  // Type 3B: unaligned read -> should use memcpy instead
> 
> perception/traffic_light_ssd_fine_detector/lib/include/cuda_utils.hpp
> 60:  CHECK_CUDA_ERROR(::cudaMalloc(reinterpret_cast<void **>(&p), sizeof(U) * n));  // Type 1
> 70:  CHECK_CUDA_ERROR(::cudaMalloc(reinterpret_cast<void **>(&p), sizeof(T)));      // Type 1
> 
> perception/traffic_light_classifier/utils/trt_common.cpp

> 
> perception/bytetrack/lib/include/lapjv.h
> 52:  if ((x = reinterpret_cast<t *>(malloc(sizeof(t) * (n)))) == 0) { \  // Speciale case. Looks like a C code (t*)malloc(...) rewritten for C++. static_cast<T*>(malloc()) is a valid C++ object construct, but reinterpret_cast is not. I doubt any compiler would break this, but it could simplified to (x = new t[(n)]). No need for any cast
