###### @ambroise-arm (2023-04-19)

> Very interesting, thanks for the report.
> 
> > With -O2 or -O3 the memcpy has no performance impact over the unsafe reinterpret_cast.
> 
> Do you have resources on this point? It is not obvious to me that it is true.

###### @VRichardJP (2023-04-19)

> It is the common consensus I have found on the internet:
> For example:
> https://gist.github.com/shafik/848ae25ee209f698763cffee272a58f8#how-do-we-type-pun-correctly
> > At a sufficient optimization level any decent modern compiler generates identical code to the previously mentioned reinterpret_cast method or union method for type punning. 
> 
> The article give [this example](https://gcc.godbolt.org/#g:!((g:!((g:!((h:codeEditor,i:(j:1,lang:c%2B%2B,source:'%23include+%3Ccstdint%3E%0A%23include+%3Ccstring%3E%0A%23include+%3Ccstdio%3E%0A%23include+%3Ccinttypes%3E%0A%0Astatic_assert(+sizeof(+double+)+%3D%3D+sizeof(+int64_t+),+%22%22+)+%3B%0A%0Avoid+func1(+double+d+)%0A%7B%0A++++std::int64_t+n%3B%0A++++std::memcpy(%26n,+%26d,+sizeof+d)%3B+//+OK%0A++++printf(+%22%25%22+PRId64+%22%5Cn%22,+n+)+%3B%0A%7D%0A%0Avoid+func2(+double+d+)%0A%7B%0A++++union+u1%0A++++%7B%0A++++++std::int64_t+n%3B%0A++++++double+d+%3B%0A++++%7D+%3B%0A++%0A++++u1+u+%3B%0A++++u.d+%3D+d+%3B%0A++++printf(+%22%25%22+PRId64+%22%5Cn%22,+u.n+)+%3B%0A%7D%0A%0Avoid+func3(+double+d+)%0A%7B%0A++++std::int64_t+n+%3B%0A++++n+%3D+*reinterpret_cast%3Cstd::int64_t+*%3E(%26d)+%3B%0A++++%0A++++printf(+%22%25%22+PRId64+%22%5Cn%22,+n+)+%3B%0A%7D%0A%0Aint+main()%0A%7B%0A++double+d+%3D+0.1%3B%0A++%0A++func1(+d+)+%3B%0A%7D'),l:'5',n:'0',o:'C%2B%2B+source+%231',t:'0')),k:50,l:'4',n:'0',o:'',s:0,t:'0'),(g:!((h:compiler,i:(compiler:clang_trunk,filters:(b:'0',binary:'1',commentOnly:'0',demangle:'0',directives:'0',execute:'1',intel:'1',trim:'1'),lang:c%2B%2B,libs:!(),options:'-std%3Dc%2B%2B17+-O2',source:1),l:'5',n:'0',o:'x86-64+clang+(trunk)+(Editor+%231,+Compiler+%231)+C%2B%2B',t:'0')),k:50,l:'4',n:'0',o:'',s:0,t:'0')),l:'2',n:'0',o:'',t:'0')),version:4)
> 
> This other article give a more advanced use case: http://pzemtsov.github.io/2016/11/06/bug-story-alignment-on-x86.html
> 
> > These days, however, it doesnΓÇÖt have to be implemented as a procedure call at all; the compiler can treat it as an intrinsic, and replace with a memory-to-register load. The GCC definitely does. It compiles the following code into the code similar to the original SSE one, except it uses movdqu instead of movdqa. This instruction allows misaligned data; its performance varies. On some processors it is much slower than movdqa even when the data is actually aligned. On others it runs at virtually the same speed.
> 
> Edit: In [this PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3293#issuecomment-1499901870), I have replaced a few reinterpret_cast by memcpy. I have disassembled reported the hottest spot in the function. This is a memcpy that have been translated to x86 movups instructions (move unpacked 512 bits). I would not be surprised if the reinterpret_cast i changed was initially compiled with a movaps (move aligned).
> 
> I don't think we are in need of performance to the point we have to care about such platform specific details. Program correctness is way more important than micro performance improvement.
> 
> 
> 

###### @ambroise-arm (2023-04-19)

> Thanks!
> 
> > I don't think we are in need of performance to the point we have to care about such platform specific details. Program correctness is way more important than micro performance improvement.
> 
> Absolutely, I wasn't trying to argue the rational for the change.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-29  |  **Closed:** 2023-04-03  |  **Author:** @annb3
- **Labels:**

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I am running autoware autouniverse with my personal vehicle and sensor. The planning launcher works perfectly, however, when I try to run the global launcher, independently if I use my vehicle and its sensor configuration or the sample_vehicle with sample_sensor_kit, when I set the pose from rviz2 or by topic the vehicle doesn't go in the initial position and the log seems not to have receive the initial position. I don't know why. May I wrong something? 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> I expected that the initial pose could be set or using GNSS or by topic or rviz2 independently and moves the vehicle in that position of the chosen map with the repository vehicle.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The initial pose isn't set using the rviz2 initializer and also in the log file doesn't seemd it has received the command, totally strange!
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> clone the autoware auto universe repository using docker updating it at the last version pushed using ros2humble.
> compile the package and inside the docker environment run:
> 
> `ros2 launch autoware_launch autoware.launch.xml map_path:=$HOME/autoware_map/sample-map-planning vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit`
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: ubuntu 20.04LTS
> - ROS_version: ROS2 humble
> - docker environment 
> - autowareautouniverse: installed not using pre-compiled package but in the docker env
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> I don't know, seems that without the gnss position it is unable to set the initial pose from rviz2 button
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> NA

**Comments:**

Or change [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/211dfb4bce4d79b48bbc3b22d7cb838e7404da93/autoware_launch/config/localization/pose_initializer.param.yaml#L6) to false to disable the stop check. Comment out [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/07b7837d42309376dc55bf576e9bcba1497c1799/launch/tier4_localization_launch/launch/util/util.launch.xml#L23-L25) if the log is hard to see due to automatic initialization.

> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51783544/228556738-ede50c8d-8134-4df6-88b4-848f774bd7ed.png)

> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51783544/228563540-0c84fa6f-15ba-47a4-beec-f49b63fd39c7.png)
> 

###### @isamu-takagi (2023-03-30)

> > ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51783544/228559600-bad4116d-371b-449d-a8bd-9206fc5c4745.png) this is what happens if i comment [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/07b7837d42309376dc55bf576e9bcba1497c1799/launch/tier4_localization_launch/launch/util/util.launch.xml#L23-L25)
> 
> This error seems to occur when the NDT scan matcher has not received the point cloud. It seems that the twist and point cloud are not output, so I think that the integration with your vehicle is not done well.

###### @annb3 (2023-03-30)

> But it is not my vehicle, it is the vehicle that I have downloaded from the installer command.
> Here the reference:
> ```
> map_path: sample-map-planning 
> vehicle_model: sample_vehicle
> sensor_model: sample_sensor_kit
> ```
> everything directly downloaded from autowareautouniverse repository.
> 
> So how can I do?
> And why don't I have a problem executing `planning_simulator.launch.xml` with the same settings?

###### @isamu-takagi (2023-03-30)

> For simulation, `planning_simulator.launch.xml` launchs `autoware.launch.xml` with changing parameters and adding dummy modules. Launching `autoware.launch.xml` directly will not work without connecting to sensors and vehicles.

###### @annb3 (2023-03-31)

> Ah, ok, so now everything is clear.
> Just the last doubt: is it not possible to use the sensing part with simulation, so we can use it once connected the real vehicle and sensors or can I use it independently?
> 
> Just to understand if it is possible to test additional functionalities in simulation or I have to do it in real-life.
> Thanks @isamu-takagi 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-04-03)

> You could drive manually with your vehcile while running sensing and vehicle modules from `autoware.launch.xml`, and recording the messages from `/sensing/*` and `/vehicle/*` topics (not everything, just the raw sensor output and vehicle feedback). You could then replay the rosbag with `logging_simulator.launch.xml` and see how Autoware would behave.

###### @annb3 (2023-04-03)

> Ok, clear.
> So thanks a lot for the support, extremely efficient.
> @VRichardJP @isamu-takagi

### #3199 — `cropPoints` functions should not delete points within range?

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-03-29  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3199

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> As pointed out here: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3176, I am wondering if the `cropPoints` function should really delete the first point beyond crop distance. 
> 
> Here is an example for `cropForwardPoints`:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/228404411-3272226a-1f51-48f6-bd98-e2c71e4fded5.png)
> 
> In the diagram, there are 3 arrows:
> - in red, the distance the caller asked to be cropped
> - in blue, the actual cropped distance if we delete points beyond crop distance (current behavior)
> - in green, the actual cropped distance if we want to guarantee the forward length of the output path is at least longer than cropped distance.
> 
> In the current implementation, the output path is always shorter than crop distance. But is it what we want? I think the function is used to remove points that are too far from a pose, while making sure we keep some necessary distance forward/backward.
> 
> For example, if the distance is shorter than the points step, the current implementation delets all the points beyond `target_seg_idx`:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/228407485-2ceeca0d-2b26-49c6-bffa-87bb207b2e0a.png)
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Make sure the cropped path is at least longer than crop distance
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> cropped path is shorted than crop distance. 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @takayuki5168 (2023-03-29)

> @VRichardJP
> Thank you for the issue.
> 
> The reason for my implementation that the output path is always shorter than the designated distance, is I wanna make the backward path as short as possible around 5 meters.
> 
> This is because of the following complicated reasons.
> - If the backward path is quite shorter than 5 meters, the precision of curvature smoothing in mpc_lateral_controller will be worse and the steering is jerky on the physical vehicle.
> - If the backward path is long enough,[ the path cut function for overlapping route](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/1d23e178cb09ece32d9d69998ce1f8e860e9dd1f/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/utilities.cpp#L1005) keeps cutting the path even if the ego gets close to the cut path end especially in a case where the route's loop length is very short as shown in the video.
> 
> [Screencast from 2023σ╣┤03µ£ê28µùÑ 23µÖé22σêå05τºÆ.webm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20228327/228436662-2b6c8ff9-f889-43e4-bb0d-4fda1b4e6112.webm)

###### @takayuki5168 (2023-03-29)

> IMO, in order not to make the output path's forward/backward lengths undefined (depending on the original resampling interval), the best solution for cropPoints is doing the resample containing the two end points, the point exactly `backward_length [m]` backward from the designated position and the point exactly `forward_length [m]` forward from the designated position.
> 
> What do you think?

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-29)

> Interpolating the end points is a cleaner solution indeed.
> I am wondering if it would not make MPC solution more stable as well. Currently the path tail "jumps" from one point to the next. If the crop distance is exact, would it improve the planner stability?

###### @takayuki5168 (2023-03-29)

> > I am wondering if it would not make MPC solution more stable as well. 
> 
> What do you mean? I think interpolating the end points makes MPC stable since a certain length of the backward path is assured.
> 
> If the crop distance is exact, the planner will be stable.

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-29)

> I meant:
> - With the current crop, the backward distance is non linear (it "jumps") = MPC solution could "jump" as well (is it the case atm?)
> - With the interporlated crop, the backward distance would be fixed = MPC solution more stable?

###### @takayuki5168 (2023-03-30)

> That's right.

###### @stale (2023-05-29)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
>

### #3174 — `crosswalk_traffic_light_estimator` output is ignored

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-27  |  **Closed:** 2023-04-11  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3174

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Today I tested Autoware on site. There is a traffic light on the course that usually does not cause any problem, but after a recent update (I am almost up-to-date with main branches), the traffic light classification result seems not to be taken into account anymore.
> 
> I have observed the ROI, fine tuner and CNN classifiers are working as expected. The `crosswalk_traffic_light_estimator` nodes outputs the traffic light result. For example something like:
> ```
> // autoware_auto_perception_msgs::msg::TrafficLight
> color: 1 // RED
> shape: 5 // CIRCLE
> status: 0
> confidance: 0.96
> ```
> But autoware seems to ignore this and does not want to stop when the traffic light is red.
> 
> There is a Rviz plugin that can publish dummy traffic light results. The plugin works as expected: if I publish a red traffic light message, Autoware wants to stop at the stop line. This plugin publishes on the same topic than `crosswalk_traffic_light_estimator`, and the only difference I can see is that the message contains the field `status = 14` (for `SOLID_ON`). 
> 
> I have hacked the `cnn_classifier.cpp` to add `status=SOLID_ON` to the result output, so that both the traffic light classification and rviz plugin output are the same. But the TL classifier output is still ignored.
> 
> Actually, it is not totally ignored, because when I have both the TL classifier and rviz plugin publishing the same RED message, Autoware's path on Rviz is blinking red and green (i.e. Autoware wants to stop, then to go, then to stop, etc). If the TL classifier result was totally ignored, Autoware would only want to stop at the traffic light stop line because of the data published by the rviz plugin.
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Autoware stops by TL stop line when the classification result is RED.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Ignores red.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> use CNN classifier on a real vehicle?
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-04-10)

> This could be related (but not only) to this PR: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2574
> 
> There are a few places in the code where traffic lights with "solid" attribute or "SOLID_ON" status are ignored. These attributes are set by default on traffic lights by the Tier4 map editor tool, so I never investigate much. What do they mean? I could not find any information in the Lanelet2 format specification, nor Autoware extended format.
> 
> @Mingyu1991 @miursh 
> - Do you think my traffic light was ignored because it is "solid"?
> - Is this behavior documented anywhere? If not, could this be added?
> 
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-04-11)

> My bad, the crosswalk traffic light has nothing to with my issue.
> 
> The problem I have is that the classified traffic light message time stamp is too old (default timeout is 1.0). 
> 
> I saw that most of the messages are like 1.5s old. That is strange, because when I check the traffic light processing pipeline, I see that images are processed continuously at 5~10Hz. Most nodes in the pipeline run quite fast (maybe 100ms in the worst case). I don't understand how this could add up to 1.5 seconds.
> 
> Could it be some node has bad QoS configuration? For example if queue size is > 1 somewhere but images are produced faster they are processed, some nodes end up processing only the oldest message in the queue.
> 
> Anyway, that would be a side issue. I'll investigate a bit and open a new issue if I can't solve the traffic light pipeline latency.
> 

---

### #3138 — Multiple markers in the same MarkerArray message in VirtualWall in RVIZ

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-22  |  **Closed:** 2023-04-21  |  **Author:** @ahmeddesokyebrahim
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3138

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Using the planning simulator and visualizing virtual walls, there are always error due multiple markers with same id and ns in the same MarkerArray message.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Status under each VirtualWall to be OK (without errors)
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Status under VirtualWall always includes error
> 
> ![Screenshot_20230322_144014](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36835765/226911905-f5422f62-2de7-4316-86bc-9a1bcbfb5bc5.png)
> 
> ![Screenshot_20230322_145007](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36835765/226912088-777a2965-5277-4bcf-80f2-18ae9c61c2ef.png)
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Open planning simulator
> 2. Plan a scenario with adding a `2D Pose Estimate` and `2D Goal Estimate` , taking into consideration to have any on the behavior planning modules activated (one at lease or multiples) in this scenario. For example, to have `intersection` or `stop_line` or `traffic_light` , ... etc
> 3. Check VirtualWall status under `planning -> ScenarioPlanning --> LaneDriving --> BehaviorPlanning --> VirutalWall`
> 
> This [video](https://youtu.be/O_8vkA155_4) shows example reproduction of the bug.
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> #### Symptom Analysis
> - The marker array that is publish to the topic `/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning/behavior_velocity_planner/virtual_wall/{module_name}` should include 2 entries .. 
>   - one for `virtual_wall` that describes its `frame_id`, `pose`, `color`, **`marker_type` which is `ADD` in this case**.. etc
>   - other one for `factor_text` that visualized the `module_name` for this `virtual_wall`.
> 
> - The problem happens because the marker array includes **4 entries** usually (not 2)
>   -  2 mentioned above
>   - another 2 with same id and ns but with zero pose, and **more interestingly with marker action `DELETE` and empty `frame_id`**
> 
> #### Root Cause Analysis
> The flow of code goes as follows : 
> - Inside scene module --> `debug.cpp` --> `createVirtualWallMarkerArray()` method, the `createStopVirtualWallMarker` is called which is defined in `common` --> `motion_utils`
> 
>  - The markers with zero poses and `DELETE` action are appended to the marker array using a method `createDeletedStopVirtualWallMarker` in `marker_helper.cpp` which uses `createDefaultMarker` in `marker_helper.hpp`
>  
>  - The `createDeletedStopVirtualWallMarker` is called by `handleVirtualWallMarker` which wants to delete duplicated poses based on the flag `previous_stop_pose_is_in_stop_pose`.
> 
> - :point_right:  It looks like this usage of this flag here is problematic or the method that sets this flag `resample_utils::validate_points_duplication` is problematic
> 
> - :point_right: Other possible cause, it could be a problem from rviz2 (similar to [this issue in rviz1](https://github.com/ros-visualization/rviz/pull/874)) that markers with `DELETE` action and without `frame_id` are not deleted !!!
> 
> ### Additional context
> Any module other than scene modules under `behavior_velocity_planner` that uses visualization with same approach will have similar issue.

### #3137 — Move downloading artifacts outside CMake

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-22  |  **Closed:** 2023-11-10  |  **Author:** @esteve

> ### Purpose

> ### Possible approaches

### #3135 — Move CUDA-dependent packages to a separate repository

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-22  |  **Closed:** 2025-02-04  |  **Author:** @esteve
- **Labels:** type:new-feature
- **Comments:** 33  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3135

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> As discussed in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/issues/3222#issuecomment-1478085589, in order to be able to build Autoware.Universe with the available packages in the ROS index, we decided to move those packages that depend on CUDA to a separate repository
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Be able to compile a subset of the Autoware.universe without depending on CUDA
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Move the the packages that depend on CUDA to a separate repository
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> There are no packages that depend on CUDA in Autoware.universe

**Comments:**

###### @miursh (2023-03-23)

> Is there any options not to separate CUDA dependent packages?
> Because of reasons below, I would not want to separate just a part of perception packages
> * If some of perception packages are placed in the different repository, it is very confusing for developers. 
>   * For example, when we want to add some change, we might need to make 3-4 PRs to different repository, such as new perception repo, autoware.unvierse, autoware_launch, and perception utils (new repo too?) 
> * Very difficult to understand especially for new users 
> * There might be some dependency between autoware.universe and separated packages. If there is many dependency, github CI might not work well.
> 

###### @xmfcx (2023-03-24)

> ## Name of the new cuda packages repository
> What are your naming choices about this new repository?
> 
> I'd go for `cuda_autoware_pkgs`, what are your suggestions?
> 
> ## Make naming consistent
> Also after moving the packages, we should make the naming conventions uniform too.
> 
> And for that my proposal is:
> - `cuda_trt_package_name`
> - `cuda_package_name` (we don't have any cuda only packages yet, just convention)
> - `cuda_tvm_package_name` (this is also preserved for future, we will have a wide discussion on what to do with tvm packages in general soon)
> 
> ## Handling of TVM packages
> Also we should move `tvm` packages to `tvm_autoware_pkgs` and they will contain `tvm` packages for non-cuda targets.
> 
> This topic will also be discussed by @ambroise-arm @angry-crab @mitsudome-r @esteve @kenji-miyake and me.
> 
> ## to separate or not to separate
> **Edit:** @miursh @yukkysaito I've just saw your comment after refreshing. Yes, I will think about not separating too. I understand the concerns, this is an issue with all separated repositories.

###### @kenji-miyake (2023-04-17)

> I'm sorry for joining late.
> 
> To give you some additional information, splitting repositories helps us reduce CI time. There is no need to test all packages with CUDA.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/541122f6d214db36b1358c6ba02be2f8d8f7b089/.github/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml#L15-L17
> 
> But I understand splitting repositories may increase maintenance costs and troubles.
> 
> I think it's okay not to split repositories right now, we should do the following at least:
> - As @xmfcx says, make package names consistent, which helps us ignore packages in CI.
>   - Related: https://github.com/jspricke/ros-deb-builder-action/issues/19
> - Plan a migration timeline to be CUDA-independent for hardware-agnostic, which I believe is one of the goals of Autoware.
> 
> I'll discuss how to proceed with this also in TIER IV.

###### @esteve (2023-04-18)

> @kenji-miyake another reason for splitting the CUDA-related packages to another repository is because when/if we submit Autoware to the ROS buildfarm that Open Robotics maintains (https://build.ros.org/), all the packages in the repository are submitted and they need to be distributable and not covered by a proprietary license. 
> 
> However, following @mitsudome-r 's rationale of only submitting Autoware.core and not all of Autoware.universe to the ROS buildfarm, we can either leave CUDA packages in universe, or move them in a separate repository, but we can't migrate them to Autoware.core.

###### @kenji-miyake (2023-04-19)

> > However, following @mitsudome-r 's rationale of only submitting Autoware.core and not all of Autoware.universe to the ROS buildfarm, we can either leave CUDA packages in universe, or move them in a separate repository, but we can't migrate them to Autoware.core.
> 
> Yes, I think so, too.

###### @kenji-miyake (2023-04-24)

> As a result of TIER IV's internal discussion, we'd like to propose the following actions:
> - To resolve the build issues in Debian package release, we'll rename existing packages, and don't move packages to another repository yet.
>   - Having a unified naming convention can help us ignore specific packages in CI.
>   - Moving packages to another repository has significant impacts, so we need step-by-step improvements.
> 
> For that, 
> - Define naming conventions.
>   - For CUDA/TensorRT packages, use `_trt`.
>   - For TVM packages, use `_tvm`.
> - Rename existing packages to follow the defined conventions.
>   - In addition, maybe old-style packages should be fixed.
>     - For example, https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/aba954f30124155afe15ba4f216076101a125265/perception/lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm_nodes can be merged into https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/aba954f30124155afe15ba4f216076101a125265/perception/lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm.
> - Write the naming convention rules in the contribution guidelines.
> 
> ---
> 
> @xmfcx @esteve cc @mitsudome-r What do you think about this?
> If it looks good, we'd appreciate it if @esteve -san would work on these tasks as part of the Debian package issue.
> 
> Regarding the long-term milestones, I think as follows:
> - We should continue discussing how we should utilize TVM.
> - Each one should try to gain a deeper understanding around TVM through learning/experiments.

###### @xmfcx (2023-05-15)

> > I can't clearly remember what was the rationale for having _nodes packages, I think it was inherited from Autoware.Auto because Apex.AI wanted the core functionality separate from the node code because it was incompatible with Apex.OS, but I might be making this up, I don't remember.

> From what I remember, it was to separate ROS libraries from the rest of the packages. And it's a good practice in theory because the library can also be reused by other packages too. But in the implementation, this wasn't adhered strictly. So I think it lost its purpose along the way.
> 
> Found the source:
> https://autowarefoundation.gitlab.io/autoware.auto/AutowareAuto/contributor-guidelines.html#autotoc_md24
> > This design pattern helps to promote separation of concerns and code re-use. The core and the ROS node(s) can be implemented in separate packages; e.g. foo and foo_nodes. There are some trivial cases where a simple ROS Node that does not require a "core" are acceptable but these should be the exception, not the rule.

###### @esteve (2025-01-28)

> Pros and cons of splitting autoware.universe into CUDA and non-CUDA repositories:
> 
> * Pros:
>   * Cheaper CI runs. We can test CUDA-dependant packages in a separate instance that will run only for those packages
>   * Easier generation of Debian packages. We can eventually submit all of autoware.universe to the ROS buildfarm and only generate CUDA-dependant packages in our buildfarm
>   * Clear separation of packages
> 
> * Cons:
>   * More complex CI. Requires coordination between CUDA and non-CUDA packages.
>   * Users would have to create PRs on different repositories if the person is making changes to universe library.
> 
> @mitsudome-r could you please complete the cons here? Thanks
> 
> I just realized that given that all CUDA-dependant packages are in perception, maybe we could move all of the perception packages (CUDA and non-CUDA) to the separate repository to mitigate issues with coordination between them.

###### @xmfcx (2025-02-03)

> In addition to my [comment above](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/3135#issuecomment-2605029526),
> 
> ## Option 0: Do nothing
> 
> - Right now, if machine doesn't have CUDA installed, the CUDA dependent packages will build an empty package. (misleading behavior)
> - We don't have a clear way to separate CUDA packages to handle them with CI or release them to the build farm.
> 
> ## Option 1: Move CUDA packages to a separate repository
> 
> - **Repo name:** autoware_universe_cuda
> - New repo means, we need to update the `autoware.repos` and `autoware-nightly.repos` files to not have them. And provide them with something like `autoware-with-cuda.repos` and `autoware-nightly-with-cuda` repos. This would make things way too confusing and hard to maintain.
> - We need to worry about a change in Universe breaking the build for CUDA repository.
>   - This is because the new repo will depend on Universe. The packages from universe that CUDA packages currently depend:
>     - autoware_component_interface_specs_universe
>     - autoware_component_interface_utils
>     - autoware_euclidean_cluster
>     - autoware_image_transport_decompressor
>     - autoware_interpolation
>     - autoware_object_recognition_utils
>     - autoware_pcl_extensions
>     - autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor
>     - autoware_pyplot
>     - autoware_test_utils
>     - autoware_universe_utils
>     - perception_utils
> - For any changes in the packages above, we need to test if CUDA packages still compile. (Additional CI work if moved to new repo)
> - Many changes will be more painful to introduce because we will have to create multiple PRs for Universe and CUDA repo.
> 
> ## Option 2: Make CUDA hard dependency for Autoware
> 
> If we decide to keep CUDA packages in the same repository, and as @knzo25 said, if we will make more and more packages depend on CUDA, maybe we can just declare CUDA as a hard dependency for the repo as a whole too. As in, we will say that Autoware depends on CUDA, this wouldn't be too weird since many AI projects depend on it anyway.
> 
> This would mean, let's just stop trying to make things work in a non-CUDA environment for Autoware as a whole, there is no deployment of an autonomous vehicle (that I'm aware of) that doesn't already have an NVIDIA hardware anyways. And Autoware won't drive autonomously without CUDA too, all these perception packages are very critical for Autonomous driving.
> 
> ## Option 3: Keep things same, introduce meta-dependency-package
> 
> **Goal:**
> - Make it easy to filter out CUDA packages for CI or building purposes.
> 
> We could also just keep things the same, and somehow make a meta-package as such:
> - **Package name:** `autoware_cuda_dependency_meta`
> - The package only has a basic `CMakeLists` that checks for CUDA dependency.
> - All of the Autoware packages that depend on CUDA has to depend on this meta-package.
> - This way, if we want to filter for CUDA packages for CI purposes, we can call `colcon list --packages-above autoware_cuda_dependency_meta --names-only`
> - Right now, we can also call `colcon list --packages-above autoware_tensorrt_common autoware_cuda_utils --names-only` for a similar effect.
> 
> And here is the "above" dependency graph for all CUDA dependent packages in Autoware:
> 
> `colcon graph --packages-above autoware_cuda_utils autoware_tensorrt_common --dot | dot -Tsvg -Grankdir=LR -Gnodesep=0.2 -Granksep=0.3 -Gconcentrate=true -o graph.svg`
> 
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d0db82a-737c-48ec-84e9-44b04141faf2)
> 
> ## My choice
> 
> Personally I would go with either **Option 2 or 3** because moving a repo out would be very painful and keeping things same makes life harder for CI, Build farm, Debian file generation and also causes confusion.
> 
> **Option 2** might come out too harsh, as this would mean we won't have ROS build farm as a general goal for the Universe. But at the same time, it also has some appeal and would make life simpler if we just stop worrying about CUDA/noCUDA thing once and for all and just go full CUDA.
> 
> **Option 3** I think is the safest, easiest to implement and least obtrusive one. Also would solve all of our problems.

###### @esteve (2025-02-03)

> @xmfcx thanks for summarizing the different options.
> 
> For option 1:
> 
> > We need to worry about a change in Universe breaking the build for CUDA repository.
> 
> I wonder how often this happens. And if it does, it might be a sign that packages are too tightly coupled. It shouldn't happen on a regular basis and packages should aim at being stable in their interfaces by now. One way to mitigate some issues like this would be to move the entirety of perception to its own repository, with or without CUDA. The other packages in `common` (like `*_utils`) shouldn't break their interface often, otherwise we're doing something wrong in our development process.
> 
> For option 2:
> 
> > Personally I would go with either Option 2 or 3 because moving a repo out would be very painful and keeping things same makes life harder for CI, Build farm, Debian file generation and also causes confusion.
> 
> Option 2 would actually make it very difficult to release Debian packages. I'd have to try, but it might make it even impossible. It'd be possible if we used the CUDA package from Ubuntu (rosdistro has a key for nvidia-cuda), but since we're using the latest package from nVidia, we can't rely on rosdistro (ithe package also has a different name).
> 
> For option 3:
> 
> > We could also just keep things the same, and somehow make a meta-package as such:
> 
> I actually implemented something like that in https://github.com/esteve/autoware.universe/tree/add-cuda-deps, adding a thin package called "cuda" and make the CUDA-dependant packages depend on t, but I didn't fully explore it. I can give it another try and see if it works.

###### @mitsudome-r (2025-02-03)

> Thanks @xmfcx and @esteve 
> > I actually implemented something like that in https://github.com/esteve/autoware.universe/tree/add-cuda-deps, adding an thin package called "cuda" and make the CUDA-dependant packages depend on t, but I didn't fully explore it. I can give it another try and see if it works.
> 
> If we can do this, then I think it would be the least disruptive modification for the current users. 

###### @yukkysaito (2025-02-04)

> Thanks ≡ƒæì 
> Personally, I choose Option 3.
> 
> Option 0 is already the current approach that has been taken.
> Option 1 is, in my opinion, out of the question.
> 
> Option 2 is a good option. However, I remember that in previous discussions, Autoware has aimed to avoid being vendor-locked to NVIDIA. For example, we decided not to officially depend on TensorRT and instead transition to the open-source TVM.
> 
> While in practice, not using NVIDIA is hardly an option at the moment, the question is whether AWF should consider supporting alternatives to NVIDIA in the future. I believe this is something that should be further discussed within AWF's WG.
> 
> Option 3 seems to be the most manageable and the best choice.

###### @esteve (2025-02-04)

> @yukkysaito 
> 
> > Option 1 is, in my opinion, out of the question.
> 
> Could you elaborate on that? Thanks.

###### @esteve (2025-02-04)

> @xmfcx another approach, which could be done in addition to option 3, is to move the CUDA-dependant packages to a subfolder of its own (e.g. `cuda`) and recreate the folder structure there (e.g. `cuda/perception`, `cuda/sensing`, etc.) This would have the benefit of simplifying how to build and test a non-CUDA environment by just excluding all the package from the `cuda` folder.

###### @xmfcx (2025-02-04)

>

###### @youtalk (2025-02-04)

> AWF, like ARM being a platinum sponsor, must aim for independence from specific hardware vendors. Therefore, major packages should avoid strong dependencies on CUDA.
> Thus, Autoware Core will first aim to be vendor-free. Additionally, vendor-dependent packages should be separated into different repositories from the perspectives of version control and isolation.

###### @esteve (2025-02-05)

> @youtalk

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2023-03-17)

> It seems like the error comes from a point having invalid values. 
> It should still crop the data with available points, but if you want to remove the error message, you should make sure that there are no points with inf values. (cc. @sykwer)
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/104ebf73bb16ccf2da625ad59bce70656d4662a5/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/crop_box_filter/crop_box_filter_nodelet.cpp#L136-L142
> 

###### @ajay1606 (2023-03-17)

> @mitsudome-r Thank you so much for your quick response, i will check lidar driver once, which causing NAN values in point cloud.
> 
> By the way, suppose in the current data is it fine to replace `nan` values with some least values such as `0.00001` ? 
>  
> Does it has any other issues ?
> 
> Certainly, crop_box_filter is working with above modification, will update if any issues raised in the further process. 
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-20)

> @ajay1606 I don't think replacing NaNs by any value is appropriate.
> The crop box purpose is to filter out points outside or inside a box. However, whether a point is inside or outside the box is undecidable if its xyz coordinates have NaNs.
> Keeping NaNs around is bad, because NaNs break so many common assumptions on float numbers. For example, any comparison with NaNs returns `false`:
> ```c++
> #include <iostream>
> #include <cmath>
> 
> int main() {
>     std::cout << (std::nan("") < 0.) << std::endl;
>     std::cout << (std::nan("") == 0.) << std::endl;
>     std::cout << (std::nan("") > 0.) << std::endl;
>     std::cout << (std::nan("") == std::nan("")) << std::endl;
>     return 0;
> }
> ```
> These all print `0` (even `nan == nan`!).
> 
> For example, `point_is_inside` is always `false` if the point data has any NaNs:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/104ebf73bb16ccf2da625ad59bce70656d4662a5/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/crop_box_filter/crop_box_filter_nodelet.cpp#L145-L147
> 
> So if we use a negative box filter (keep only outside points) on a cloud with NaNs, the NaN points would be copied...
> 
> To avoid any issue, I think the best would be to skip (=delete) NaN points and just print a warning when it happens (maybe with the count of skipped NaN points).
> 

###### @ajay1606 (2023-03-20)

> @VRichardJP @mitsudome-r Thank you so much for your inputs, certainly crop box filtering working well, by skipping nan values points. Assuming this as ideal solution for reported bug, issue closed for this moment.  

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-20)

> @ajay1606 Actually I think the code should be fixed to always skip points with NaNs, currently NaN may leak through when `param_.negative` is `true`.
> 
> Something like:
> ```C++
>     if (!std::isfinite(point[0]) || !std::isfinite(point[1]) || !std::isfinite(point[2])) {
>       // RCLCPP_WARN(...);
>       continue;
>     }
> 
>     if (transform_info.need_transform) {
>         point = transform_info.eigen_transform * point;
>     }
> ```

###### @ajay1606 (2023-03-20)

> @VRichardJP I also modified code almost similar to avoid NaN values. Thank you so much

###### @TZECHIN6 (2023-05-25)

> Sorry to asking in here, but there is not much discussion about Robosense LiDAR out there.

> ### Description
> 
> As in this image, when an object is placed in the Rviz, its center of mass is aligned  to the map or the ground.

> I think this is confusing when we debug the pointcloud/laserscan in planning simulator by changing the height of top Lidar.
> 
> I suggest aligning the `base_link` (the center of the bottom plane) to the map instead.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> When we set the height of top Lidar to 2m from the base_link and set the height of a car to 2.2m with its z height 0m for example, then we expect to see occupied/unknown part on the laserscan-based occupancy grid.
> 
> Currently since only half of the car, which is 1.1m height, is only effective and therefore laserscan-based occupancy grid from 2.0m height does not produce any occupied/known part.
> 
> In the below image `scan_origin_frame` of the occupancy grid map is 2.x [m] and the object height is set to 6m. Then the occupancy grid map is generated properly.
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28677420/225844112-0ac9d1e0-7e8a-4170-8314-323819bf2c84.png)
>

> In the above settings the occupancy grid is all free.
>

> 1. Put ego vehicle

### #3090 — `float` is not precise enough for UTM coordinates.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-16  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3090

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Autoware can load maps using UTM coordinate system, yet it stores a lot of xyz data using `float` type.
> The problem is that `float` is not precise enough to manipulate UTM coordinates.
> 
> Here is a simple example:
> Tokyo station is located at `lat=35.6785133, lon=139.763416`
> With this [converter](https://www.earthpoint.us/Convert.aspx), I get:
> - MGRS local coordinates: `x=88096, y=48996`
> - UTM local coordinates: `x=388096, y=3948996`
> 
> According to this [IEEE-754 float converter](https://www.h-schmidt.net/FloatConverter/IEEE754.html):
> - The next representable `float` value after `88096.0` is `88096.0078125`
> - The next representable `float` value after `3948996.0` is `3948996.25`
> 
> In other words, if I use MGRS coordinate system around Tokyo, coordinate `float` precision is 7 millimeter. If I use UTM, `float` is only 25 centimeter precise...
> 
> One could argue that 7 millimeters is not that precise when using MGRS. Certainly, everyone will agree that 25 centimeters is unacceptable. Unless you are lucky enough to be somewhere with low UTM coordinates, it is basically suicide to use Autoware with UTM maps.
> 
> I don't see many solutions:
> - either Autoware should drop UTM support
> - or Autoware should use `double` type everywhere (in such case we would be nm precise even in the worst UTM cases)
> - or Autoware should move the map frame, so that coordinates expressed in map frame have low values (for example, by changing the map origin to the first point of the map).
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Autoware is precise enough.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Not precise enough if UTM are used.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> N/A
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2023-03-21)

> `float` issue is already known issue in TIER IV.
> Since there are many source codes that assumes float at the moment (like PCL), TIER IV decided to use MGRS.
> If people prefer to use other coordinate, they can select UTM projector + origin to assign their preferred origin to keep the converted numbers low enough to keep their required precision.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/map/map_loader/config/lanelet2_map_loader.param.yaml

###### @stale (2023-05-20)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @mitsudome-r (2026-03-24)

> I'm closing the issue that was inactive for a long time. Feel free to reopen if the issue is still relevant

### #3085 — compare_map_segmentation need support and work with supper large pointcloud map

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-16  |  **Closed:** 2023-05-11  |  **Author:** @badai-nguyen
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:perception
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3085

**Body:**

>

> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> 
> Currently, compare_map_segmentation package loads pointcloud map as input and voxelization for map comparison. However, for scaling up purpose, when pointcloud map become supper large, it is difficult to complete map loading and voxelization/or Kdtree creation at once.
> It is necessary to update compare map segmentation's filter to support dynamic map loader and working fine with large pointcloud maps. 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Update compare_map_segmentation filters to work fine with large pointcloud map.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Regarding to map loader service, recently, dynamic map loading functionality for large pointcloud maps has been discussed [here](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2696)  and developed at: 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1938
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2417
> 
> It is possible to utilize dynamic map loading interface for compare map segmentation to update necessary pointcloud map region when vehicle moving. 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> All compare map filter should update map loader and work with large pointcloud maps
> - [x] distance_based_compare_map_filter_nodelet
> - [x] voxel_based_approximate_compare_map_filter_nodelet
> - [x] voxel_based_compare_map_filter_nodelet
> - [x] voxel_distance_based_compare_map_filter_nodelet

### #3049 — Add `timing_violation_monitor` node

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2023-03-10  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @nabetetsu
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:help-wanted, priority:high, status:stale
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3049

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, there is no common mechanism for detecting timing violation. Autoware is a real-time system, which means that the software shall save time constraints and use more fresh data. If time constraints cannot be saved, any function failed, and it may be difficult to continue the service.
> For example, Localization is one of the critical features of Autoware, and it has time constraints.
> 
> I'd like to add a feature to monitor the timing violation of the time constraints and report it through /diagnostics by debugging purpose.
> 
> This issue is created from the following discussion.
> https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3176
> 
> We have not reached a consensus yet in the discussion, but after internal discussion, I would like to add this feature for debugging purposes. Since it is for debugging purposes, changes to this feature shold be as easy as possible to revert.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> For debugging purposes, the response time of a given path is monitored and the result of a timing violation is reported.
> 
> In the future, I will plan to implement a feature that detects the possibility of deadline violations early and notifies the necessary nodes.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1: To introduce a `timing_violation_monitor` node
> 2: To introduce a timing violation detection function at an end node of a path
> 3: To extend topic_state_monitor to support timing violation detection
> 4: `ros2 topic delay`
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - User can check the results by `rqt_runtime_monitor`
> - User can check the results by FSM

**Comments:**

###### @nabetetsu (2023-03-10)

> possible approaches `#1`:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2983
> https://github.com/tier4/tier4_autoware_msgs/pull/75

### #3040 — Handle NaNs when using OSQP

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-09  |  **Closed:** 2023-05-08  |  **Author:** @maxime-clem
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, priority:high
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3040

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> [OSQP](https://github.com/osqp/osqp) is used to solve optimization problems in several Autoware nodes.
> In some cases, OSQP can return a result containing NaN values, which is not currently handled correctly and can lead to crashes.
> 
> See https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2925 for the original reported issue.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> We want Autoware to remain functional even in the case where OSQP returns NaN values.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Special cases need to be implemented when OSQP returns NaN values.
> 
> - Use a previous solution (e.g., previously computed trajectory).
> - Use an emergency solution (e.g., stopping trajectory).
> - Do not publish anything.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Handling of NaNs is implemented in the following packages:
> 
> - [ ] `motion_velocity_smoother`.
> - [ ] `mpc_lateral_controller`.
> - [ ] `obstacle_avoidance_planner`.
> - [ ] `obstacle_cruise_planner`.

**Comments:**

###### @soblin (2023-03-09)

> I think returning std::optional<solution> is an option. Like returning `nullopt` if not [has_solution](https://github.com/osqp/osqp/blob/e9ee6669f44ae989e5a4cc78896ab6d7ff9e0e19/src/auxil.c#L534).

### #3034 — Address an issue that pcl::transformPointCloud dies when receives pointcloud with zero points

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-09  |  **Closed:** 2024-08-05  |  **Author:** @kminoda
- **Labels:** component:sensing
- **Comments:** 9  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/3034

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> pcl::transformPointCloud, which is used in several packages in Autoware, dies when receiving pointcloud with zero points. This causes a error during runtime.
> 
> (Internal link in TIER IV: https://star4.slack.com/archives/C4P0NSMB5/p1677827663887509)
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To avoid Autoware failing when zero length pointcloud is published
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. Implement alternative function to pcl::transformPointCloud (e.g. in tier4_autoware_utils, maybe moving [this function](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/filter.cpp#L290-L351))
> 2. Install the latest PCL (as a matter of fact, the bug has been addressed here: https://github.com/PointCloudLibrary/pcl/pull/5113)
> 3. Get rid of PCL
> 
> I think 1 is the best approach as a temporary solution.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Autoware does not die because of pcl::transformPointCloud even when the pointcloud with zero width is published.

**Comments:**

> Now, some packages in autoware use `pcl_ros::transformPointCloud`.

> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/faf4bd0286971e7ceaf52f1ff1ff8df3954348e4/perception/ground_segmentation/src/ransac_ground_filter_nodelet.cpp#L177

### #2991 — Autoware parks inappropriately on parking lot

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-03  |  **Closed:** 2023-04-20  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 9  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2991

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In this example, I have set the goal point perpendicular to the initial position (in red), so a maneuver is required. Autoware starts its maneuver but kind of stops halfway, as it considers the goal has been reached as soon as the XY matches:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/222606674-ed336b70-482c-4789-b14a-3bbe576622aa.png)
> 
> I guess this is because the goal heading error tolerance is too high. For lane driving, it is not a problem as we can't maneuver, but when the vehicle is on a parking lot, Autoware should park precisely.
> 
> I guess this should be fixed for cargo ODD.
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Autoware parks precisely on parking lot
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> heading error is too big on goal.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Run simulator with a parking lot and ask autoware to park somewhere.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @yukkysaito (2023-03-04)

> Thanks for the report.
> The parking planner has not been changed for some time since it was created as a prototype.
> The free space planner doesn't generate stable trajectory, so when it stops at a certain place, we create the lanelet.
> 
> It may be better to review the design from the beginning if necessary this time with cargo ODD or bus ODD.

###### @NorahXiong (2023-03-16)

> @VRichardJP Which planning algorithm did you choose? A-star or RRT?
> 
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-16)

> @NorahXiong A* in this example

###### @NorahXiong (2023-03-16)

> I did a similar test with the default settings and I got a pretty good result. 
> @VRichardJP Have you repeated the test? Did it stop halfway everytime? 
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/225558210-01b62e74-9b5a-46ed-841e-edca8cd59744.png)
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-16)

> In my case, I added a few obstacles to make the parking maneuver less trivial. You can see the 2 buses left and right of the parking spot in my screenshot. I only tested a couple times with this setup.

###### @NorahXiong (2023-03-16)

> I added similar obstacles but it still works well. Can you post your map and precise start and goal poses?
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/225573911-a43e8bcd-f5a2-4ff8-baff-237eb96580c6.png)
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-22)

> I am using the same map you are showing.
> 
> Starting position:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/226836790-4d058b7a-1f91-4e2d-b197-2ecedef8bbf0.png)
> After struggling with the maneuver, going back and forth many times just a few meters, autoware drove very quickly close to the target goal and got stuck:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/226837088-a98a970f-1d6f-40b0-9181-3f345a47f5a4.png)
> 
> Another example. Start position:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/226837520-e6ac53f3-2371-4674-b6f6-489e024537d8.png)
> After goal is reached:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/226837636-a117f24e-e65c-4580-9a9c-167b43f3b227.png)
> 
> As @yukkysaito said, it seems that Autoware considers the goal has been reached if it is stopped around the goal, even if the maneuver is not finished. This occurs typically when Autoware moves back and forth to adjust its orientation while it is close to the goal position.

###### @NorahXiong (2023-04-14)

> Hi, @VRichardJP 
> I updated my environment and reproduced your issue. I reduced the "vehicle_shape_margin_m" value to 0.2(m) and the parking procedure succeeded.
> I checked the "vehicle_shape_margin_m" parameter changelog and I found no one modifying the default value recently. The problem may come from the perception module. Maybe algorithms and logic changed in the perception module and it results in unstable/incorrect distance measurement.
> Anyway, hope my information could help you!
> 

###### @liuXinGangChina (2023-04-19)

> Hi, @VRichardJP.
> Since norah has reproduce the issue and come up with the solution, can you mark this one as "answered" and close it.
> 
> happy hacking!

### #2974 — `CropBoxFilterComponent` in `voxel_grid_based_euclidean_cluster.launch.py` are missing `input_frame` and `output_frame` parameters

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-01  |  **Closed:** 2023-03-07  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2974

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Makes the container crash after position has been initialized because `tf_input_frame_` is empty:
> ![2023-03-01-18-35-26-487](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/222102243-2da9d3d5-b2b2-4dc6-b339-07d9a604db7d.jpg)
> 
> Example of fix:
> - add `input_frame: base_link` and `output_frame: base_link` to
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/perception/euclidean_cluster/config/voxel_grid_based_euclidean_cluster.param.yaml
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> No crash
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Crash
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Run autoware with lidar based detection
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-02)

> I confused `tf_input_orig_frame_ ` and `tf_input_frame_`.
> 
> According the `filter.cpp` code, since the filter is a `"CropBoxFilter"`, `pointcloud_preprocessor::Filter::faster_input_indices_callback` is used and `tf_input_orig_frame_` is copied from the input cloud here:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/78388cb63b5923a90506c8f8e6e2ca01ce31830c/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/filter.cpp#L433
> 
> Then the [`CropBoxFilterComponent::faster_filter`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/f9075cbcfe88fc0dc81f13e3f9b72e5ff38f73c5/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/crop_box_filter/crop_box_filter_nodelet.cpp#L111) is called and the output header is set to `""` here:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/f9075cbcfe88fc0dc81f13e3f9b72e5ff38f73c5/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/crop_box_filter/crop_box_filter_nodelet.cpp#L152-L153
> 
> Then finally `pointcloud_preprocessor::Filter::convert_output_costly` is called, and we enter the following branch:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/78388cb63b5923a90506c8f8e6e2ca01ce31830c/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/filter.cpp#L377
> 
> Indeed, at this time `tf_output_frame_ == ""` and `output->header.frame_id == ""` and `tf_input_orig_frame_ == "base_link"` (most likely). So the program crashes when it tries to transform "" into "base_link".
> 
> If you think about it, the crop box filter XYZ box is defined relatively to a reference frame, so `tf_input_frame_` cannot be empty.
> 
> So the proper fix is:
> - [x] add missing `input_frame` to the crop box filter: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2979
> - [x] throw an error in `CropBoxFilterComponent` constructor if `tf_input_frame_` is not set: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2980
>

### #2970 — `ring_outlier_filter` output is sometimes empty

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-03-01  |  **Closed:** 2023-03-03  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** component:sensing, component:localization
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2970

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Following the [sample sensor kit](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/sample_sensor_kit_launch/blob/06330e6b07449a3609ced295c0a9ce6a1805ef99/common_sensor_launch/launch/velodyne_node_container.launch.py#L154) I have enabled the ring outlier filter on our car.
> 
> After that the `ndt_scan_matcher` started to crash on startup on receiving empty input cloud:
> ![2023-03-01-17-09-07-209](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/222082549-c1e0a32b-2be4-442d-9601-939285548d06.jpg)
> 
> I found `ring_outlier_filter` is the node responsible for this. On the picture below, I printed on the left the size of `ring_outlier_filter` output cloud (`$ ros2 topic echo /sensing/lidar/top/outlier_filtered/pointcloud --field width`) and on the right the size of its input cloud (`$ ros2 topic echo /sensing/lidar/top/rectified/pointcloud_ex --field width`):
> ![Inked2023-03-01-17-06-10-959_LI](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/222082538-6cc4ef4e-c886-4dd4-8a23-d8045910d923.jpg)
> 
> As you can see, the output is sometimes empty. 
> 
> I could also confirm with Rviz the rectified cloud looks totally normal while the the outlier cloud sometimes "blinks".
> 
> Besides the output being empty, I think it is also annoying `ndt_scan_matcher` crashes because of that.  A small guard could be added to `NDTScanMatcher::callback_sensor_points`.
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> No empty output
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Sometimes empty output
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> use the outlier filter?
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @kminoda (2023-03-01)

> I also observed the similar issue (where the number of points becomes zero occasionally) in the latest awf/autoware with sample rosbag provided in the Autoware tutorial. 
> 
> @sykwer Do you think the above phenomena is related to this PR? https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2908/

###### @YamatoAndo (2023-03-01)

> Thank you for your report!
> 
> I also reproduced the problem of the number of point clouds in `/sensing/lidar/top/outlier_filtered/pointcloud` becomes zero.
> 
> But `ndt_scan_matcher` doesn't crash in my environment (ROS2 galactic).
> According to my sources, it seems that the zero division happens in the PCL installed with ROS2 humble.
> It seems to be fixed in the latest PCL. https://github.com/PointCloudLibrary/pcl/pull/5113

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-01)

> @YamatoAndo I see. I am not sure how I installed PCL on the car PC, but I think I used autoware setup script. So I guess the PCL people normally have installed on their machine will have this bug, no?

###### @kminoda (2023-03-02)

> Reverting the above PR https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2908 solved the problem. Currently @sykwer is trying to investigate and fix the issue for us :pray: 

###### @sykwer (2023-03-03)

> Fixed https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2992

### #2958 — Move out `ekf_localizer` params from the xml launch file to a dedicated yaml config file

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-02-28  |  **Closed:** 2023-04-01  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:new-feature
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2958

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, `ekf_localizer` params are all hardcoded in the [`ekf_localizer.launch.xml`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/localization/ekf_localizer/launch/ekf_localizer.launch.xml) file. This is inconsistent with other packages, for which launch files and runtime parameters are split in different files. 
> 
> For example for `ndt_scan_matcher.param.yaml`:
> - launch file in [`src/autoware.universe/localization/ndt_scan_matcher/launch/ndt_scan_matcher.launch.xml`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/localization/ndt_scan_matcher/launch/ndt_scan_matcher.launch.xml) 
> - pkg default config in  [`src/autoware.universe/localization/ndt_scan_matcher/config/ndt_scan_matcher.param.yaml` ](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/localization/ndt_scan_matcher/config/ndt_scan_matcher.param.yaml)
> - sample `autoware_launch` config in `src/launcher/autoware_launch/autoware_launch/config/localization/ndt_scan_matcher.param.yaml`
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/main/autoware_launch/config/localization/ndt_scan_matcher.param.yaml
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Make `ekf_localizer` consistent with other packages.
> Separating params from the launch file makes it easier to override the configuration.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> To keep the current behavior, we could have:
> 
> - `src/universe/autoware.universe/localization/ekf_localizer/config/ekf_localizer.param.yaml`:
> ```yaml
> /**:
>   ros__parameters:
>     show_debug_info: false
>     enable_yaw_bias_estimation: True
>     predict_frequency: 50.0
>     tf_rate: 50.0
>     extend_state_step: 50
> 
>     # for Pose measurement
>     pose_additional_delay: 0.0
>     pose_measure_uncertainty_time: 0.01
>     pose_smoothing_steps: 5
>     pose_gate_dist: 10000.0
> 
>     # for twist measurement
>     twist_additional_delay: 0.0
>     twist_smoothing_steps: 2
>     twist_gate_dist: 10000.0
> 
>     # for process model
>     proc_stddev_yaw_c: 0.005
>     proc_stddev_vx_c: 10.0
>     proc_stddev_wz_c: 5.0
> ```
> 
> - `src/launcher/autoware_launch/autoware_launch/config/localization/ekf_localizer.param.yaml`:
> ```yaml
> /**:
>   ros__parameters:
>     show_debug_info: false
>     enable_yaw_bias_estimation: True
>     predict_frequency: 50.0
>     tf_rate: 50.0
>     extend_state_step: 50
> 
>     # for Pose measurement
>     pose_additional_delay: 0.0
>     pose_measure_uncertainty_time: 0.01
>     pose_smoothing_steps: 5
>     pose_gate_dist: 10000.0
> 
>     # for twist measurement
>     twist_additional_delay: 0.0
>     twist_smoothing_steps: 2
>     twist_gate_dist: 10000.0
> 
>     # for process model
>     proc_stddev_yaw_c: 0.005
>     proc_stddev_vx_c: 10.0
>     proc_stddev_wz_c: 5.0
> ```
> 
> - `src/universe/autoware.universe/localization/ekf_localizer/launch/ekf_localizer.launch.xml`:
> ```xml
> <launch>
>   <arg name="param_file" default="$(find-pkg-share ekf_localizer)/config/ekf_localizer.param.yaml"/>
> 
>   <arg name="input_initial_pose_name" default="initialpose3d"/>
>   <arg name="input_trigger_node_service_name" default="trigger_node" description="trigger node service"/>
> 
>   <!-- input topic name -->
>   <arg name="input_pose_with_cov_name" default="in_pose_with_covariance"/>
>   <arg name="input_twist_with_cov_name" default="in_twist_with_covariance"/>
> 
>   <!-- output topic name -->
>   <arg name="output_odom_name" default="ekf_odom"/>
>   <arg name="output_pose_name" default="ekf_pose"/>
>   <arg name="output_pose_with_covariance_name" default="ekf_pose_with_covariance"/>
>   <arg name="output_biased_pose_name" default="ekf_biased_pose"/>
>   <arg name="output_biased_pose_with_covariance_name" default="ekf_biased_pose_with_covariance"/>
>   <arg name="output_twist_name" default="ekf_twist"/>
>   <arg name="output_twist_with_covariance_name" default="ekf_twist_with_covariance"/>
> 
>   <node pkg="ekf_localizer" exec="ekf_localizer" name="ekf_localizer" output="screen">
>     <remap from="in_pose_with_covariance" to="$(var input_pose_with_cov_name)"/>
> 
>     <remap from="in_twist_with_covariance" to="$(var input_twist_with_cov_name)"/>
> 
>     <remap from="initialpose" to="$(var input_initial_pose_name)"/>
>     <remap from="trigger_node_srv" to="$(var input_trigger_node_service_name)"/>
> 
>     <param name="pose_frame_id" value="map"/>
> 
>     <remap from="ekf_odom" to="$(var output_odom_name)"/>
>     <remap from="ekf_pose" to="$(var output_pose_name)"/>
>     <remap from="ekf_pose_with_covariance" to="$(var output_pose_with_covariance_name)"/>
>     <remap from="ekf_biased_pose" to="$(var output_biased_pose_name)"/>
>     <remap from="ekf_biased_pose_with_covariance" to="$(var output_biased_pose_with_covariance_name)"/>
>     <remap from="ekf_twist" to="$(var output_twist_name)"/>
>     <remap from="ekf_twist_with_covariance" to="$(var output_twist_with_covariance_name)"/>
> 
>     <param from="$(var param_file)"/>
>   </node>
> </launch>
> ```
> 
> - In `src/launcher/autoware_launch/autoware_launch/launch/components/tier4_localization_component.launch.xml`, add:
> ```xml
>     <arg name="ekf_localizer_param_path" value="$(find-pkg-share autoware_launch)/config/localization/ekf_localizer.param.yaml"/>
> ```
> - In `src/universe/autoware.universe/launch/tier4_localization_launch/launch/localization.launch.xml`, add:
> ```xml
>     <arg name="ekf_localizer_param_path"/>
> ```
> - In `src/universe/autoware.universe/launch/tier4_localization_launch/launch/pose_twist_fusion_filter/pose_twist_fusion_filter.launch.xml`, add:
> ```xml
>   <include file="$(find-pkg-share ekf_localizer)/launch/ekf_localizer.launch.xml">
>     <!-- ... -->
>     <arg name="param_file" value="$(var ekf_localizer_param_path)"/>
>   </include>
> ```
> 
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> `ekf_localizer` runtime parameters are loaded from dedicated config files instead of being hardcoded in its launch file.

**Comments:**

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-09)

> - `autoware_launch`: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/244
> - `autoware.universe`: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/3039

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-08)

> Found the problem... and I feel very stupid about how obvious the cause was.
> 
> So, as I pointed out earlier, components are loaded in the container using a dedicated service and some of the service calls seem to be dropped. What is the number 1 reason a message may be dropped with ROS ? => if the message buffer is full!
> 
> As you can see below, components are managed by the `ComponentManager` node, which creates the `load_node` service with the default QoS profile:
> 
> https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/blob/0f331f90a99da40f7b7a69b4f55b30b7245d294f/rclcpp_components/src/component_manager.cpp#L40
> 
> ```cpp
>   loadNode_srv_ = create_service<LoadNode>(
>     "~/_container/load_node",
>     std::bind(&ComponentManager::on_load_node, this, _1, _2, _3));
>   unloadNode_srv_ = create_service<UnloadNode>(
>     "~/_container/unload_node",
>     std::bind(&ComponentManager::on_unload_node, this, _1, _2, _3));
>   listNodes_srv_ = create_service<ListNodes>(
>     "~/_container/list_nodes",
>     std::bind(&ComponentManager::on_list_nodes, this, _1, _2, _3));
> ```
> 
> The default QoS profile has a depth of 10, so if we try to load 41 components into the container at the same time... yes, a few may be dropped.
> 
> I cloned `rclcpp_components` module into the autoware workspace, added a QoS profile with a queue size of 100, and now it works just perfectly!
> 
> Ping @mitsudome-r 
> Although a fix should be proposed upstream, there is a serious issue with the current code base: there is currently no guarantee autoware containers are properly loaded if they are supposed to contain more than 10 components!
