### #2636 — DevOps Dojo: ROS Node Configuration (Phase 2)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-01-11  |  **Closed:** 2023-04-14  |  **Author:** @kaspermeck-arm
- **Labels:** DevOps Dojo: ROS Node Conf
- **Comments:** 16  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2636

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> DevOps: Ros Node Configuration will address the topic of how ROS nodes are configured. Guidelines, documentation and changes to configuration files will be made, based on best-practices from cloud-native and software defined development methodologies.
> 
> Phase 1 - Motivation
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2631
> 
> Phase 2 - Definition
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2636
> 
> Phase 3 - Execution
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2651
> 
> Phase 4 - Integration
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2652
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Phase 2 - Definition
> - define structure and milestone(s)
> - identify gaps in current software and developersΓÇÖ skills
> - produce actionable items
> - consensus on solution
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> From [12factor config](https://12factor.net/config):
> - ΓÇ£An appΓÇÖs config is everything that is likely to vary between deploys (staging, production, developer environments, etc).ΓÇ¥
> 
> We want to be able to configure any parameter so that the ROS node can be used in different deploys.
> 
> Use following ROS nodes to use for evaluation of changes to be made:
> - [lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm_nodes](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/perception/lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm_nodes)
> - [ndt_scan_matcher](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/localization/ndt_scan_matcher)
> - [lidar_centerpoint](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/perception/lidar_centerpoint)
> - [lidar_centerpoint_tvm](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/perception/lidar_centerpoint_tvm)
> 
> ### Autoware ROS Packages
> See [Autoware.Universe ROS Packages](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1yAnXedY3zv2oD1prDZ_AyYiFMI8T9ZVrRNqm9kEPYcs/edit?usp=sharing) for an extensive list of all ROS packages in Autoware.
> 
> Once the ROS node configuration has been defined, it should be documented here: [Coding guidelines](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/contributing/coding-guidelines/ros-nodes/parameters/)
> 
> ### ROS Parameters
> Parameters are declared using
>   - [declare_parameter(...)](https://docs.ros.org/en/ros2_packages/humble/api/rclcpp/generated/classrclcpp_1_1Node.html#_CPPv4N6rclcpp4Node17declare_parameterERKNSt6stringEN6rclcpp13ParameterTypeERKN14rcl_interfaces3msg19ParameterDescriptorEb)
> 
> Any parameter which has been declared must be listed in the config file to create full visibility for the user. This removes the need to have access to the source code or reading the functions return value.
> 
> If a ROS node has multiple backends, e.g., CPU, GPU, DSP, etc, the selection of backend should be done in the configuration file.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Once consensus on how to structure ROS node configurations has been achieved and actionable items produces.

**Comments:**

###### @kaspermeck-arm (2023-01-11)

> We want to avoid using the default_value in the [declare_parameter(...)](https://docs.ros2.org/dashing/api/rclcpp/classrclcpp_1_1Node.html#a64df64d004b6263c3c04f42179fc8f52) function. This is to ensure that the ROS node configuration file has all the necessary parameters. Is there a way to throw an exception if [declare_parameter(...)](https://docs.ros2.org/dashing/api/rclcpp/classrclcpp_1_1Node.html#a64df64d004b6263c3c04f42179fc8f52) expects a parameter not existing in the ROS node configuration file?

###### @kaspermeck-arm (2023-01-18)

> Two options:
> 1. Define guidelines that any configurable parameter exists in the yaml file
> 2. Throw an exception if a parameter is not in the yaml file
> 
> We don't want to create unnecessary work.

###### @kaspermeck-arm (2023-01-18)

> Coding guidelines should live here: https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/contributing/coding-guidelines/ros-nodes/parameters/

###### @kaspermeck-arm (2023-01-20)

> @mitsudome-r, after discussion with @ambroise-arm, we propose that we go with option number 2. That is:
> - Throw an exception if a parameter is not in the parameter configuration yaml file
> 
> This is because [declare_parameter(...)](https://docs.ros.org/en/ros2_packages/humble/api/rclcpp/generated/classrclcpp_1_1Node.html#_CPPv4N6rclcpp4Node17declare_parameterERKNSt6stringEN6rclcpp13ParameterTypeERKN14rcl_interfaces3msg19ParameterDescriptorEb) states the following:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30662532/213821169-ece98ecd-fc72-4348-84da-a11600d121e0.png)
> 
> That is, if _default_value_ is not set and the parameter configuration file does not provide the parameter or the right format for the parameter, an exception will be thrown. This then solves our issue of matching the expected parameters provided and the actual parameters provided.
> 
> This gives us a single source of truth for parameter configuration. Can we agree on
> - not assigning _default_value_ a value
> - parameter configuration yaml file is comprehensive
>   - I.e., contains all _declare_parameter()_ values
> 
> ?

###### @kaspermeck-arm (2023-01-20)

> If we agree upon having a singe source of truth in the parameter configuration yaml file, we should then decide on a certain format for the yaml file so that it can be parsed and interpreted to an .md file to be used with the documentation.
> 
> For example, in [ndt_scan_matcher](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/localization/ndt_scan_matcher/#core-parameters) there is a table with _Core Parameters_. Let's assume the parameter configuration yaml file [ndt_scan_matcher.param.yaml](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/localization/ndt_scan_matcher/config/ndt_scan_matcher.param.yaml) was parsed and interpreted as an .md file. We would then have a single source for both ROS node configuration and documentation.
> 
> Can we agree upon
> - using parameter configuration yaml file for both
>   - configuring the ROS node
>   - used in ROS node documentation
> 
> ?

###### @kaspermeck-arm (2023-01-20)

> To give an idea of the yaml to .md, see [yaml-to-table](https://github.com/ishswar/yaml-to-table/blob/master/README.md), (I'm not suggesting we use this).

###### @doganulus (2023-01-31)

> I like the idea of having unique and hierarchical names for each and every parameter in the system. For example, I think the dot notation `autoware.module.node.parent.parameter` can be adopted as other similar applications. Further, it is a good idea to specify certain other attributes next to the implementation. 
> 
> - `autoware.module.node.parent.parameter.value` // Current value of the parameter
> - `autoware.module.node.parent.parameter.default_value` // Default value of the parameter
> - `autoware.module.node.parent.parameter.type`  // Type of the parameter -- e.g. bool, number, string, enum, custom
> - `autoware.module.node.parent.parameter.range` // List of allowed values (if the type is enum)
> - `autoware.module.node.parent.parameter.range.min` // Minimum allowed value (if the type is number)
> - `autoware.module.node.parent.parameter.range.max` // Maximum allowed value (if the type is number)
> 
> Not sure if ROS gives that flexibility to define parameters in such a hierarchical way but it would be good to explore possibilities under this Dojo. Definitely, it would improve automated documentation generation using any templating engine and speed up overall development. 
> 

###### @kaspermeck-arm (2023-02-01)

> Autoware.Universe architecture w. nodes: https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/design/autoware-architecture/node-diagram/overall-node-diagram-autoware-universe.drawio.svg

###### @kaspermeck-arm (2023-02-02)

> In the documentation, list all possible parameter values as defined by _Class Parameter Value_. See [Enum ParameterType](https://docs.ros.org/en/ros2_packages/humble/api/rclcpp/generated/enum_namespacerclcpp_1a1b307a4b7368b68f325812cd2aeb8784.html#enum-parametertype).

> Question: is this list of parameter extensive?

###### @kaspermeck-arm (2023-02-07)

- **Labels:** type:new-feature, DevOps Dojo: ROS Node Conf

> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> DevOps: Ros Node Configuration will address the topic of how ROS nodes are configured. Guidelines, documentation and changes to configuration files will be made, based on best-practices from cloud-native and software defined development methodologies.
> 
> Phase 1 - Motivation
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2631
> 
> Phase 2 - Definition
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2636
> 
> Phase 3 - Execution
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2651
> 
> Phase 4 - Integration
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2652
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Phase 1 - Motivation:
> - clear purpose
>   - increase ROS node parameters visibility
>   - remove need to have access to source code to see default parameter values
> - outline proposed work item
>   - remove discrepancies between ROS nodes
>   - create documentation and guidelines
> - identify beneficiaries, stakeholders and shareholders
>   - Autoware developers
>     - consistent and rigid configuration files
>     - visibility into how nodes are configured
>   - Users who deploy Autoware
>     - ease of changing the configuration to suit user's need
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Involve the Autoware community to understand current deficiencies.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Phase 1 is considered complete once satisfactory motivation has been outlined.

### #2605 — Add a validation node for the planning trajectory

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2023-01-02  |  **Closed:** 2023-05-11  |  **Author:** @TakaHoribe
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:planning
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2605

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Sometimes, a faulty path is published due to the poor quality of the planning. This can cause the vehicle to behave abnormally in terms of steering, acceleration, and braking. It is important to continually improve the quality of the planning, but we also need to implement a validation system to ensure the quality of the paths being published.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To avoid publishing abnormal paths.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> A planning validator node is introduced at the final stage of the planning process. The node validates the trajectory and stops publishing if it is invalid.
> 
> 
> The planning node diagram would be like below:
> `planning_modules` -> `planning_validator` -> `control`.
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21360593/210234510-00bc5aa7-69a5-47ec-b058-afd251332b40.png)
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> A validation mechanism of the planning is in the autoware.

**Comments:**

###### @TakaHoribe (2023-01-02)

> Related:
> 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1947
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2604
> - https://github.com/tier4/autoware_launch/pull/675

###### @TakaHoribe (2023-01-02)

> cc. @yukkysaito @xmfcx 

###### @yukkysaito (2023-01-10)

> I think it's a good idea to add one.
> However, I would like to separate what is verified online and what is verified offline (like CI)
> Otherwise, it would be inefficient to run a huge verification online.
> 

###### @TakaHoribe (2023-01-18)

> > to separate what is verified online and what is verified offline (like CI)
>

### #2597 — The positioning module is unstable for unknown reasons (rosbag2 has been provided for testing)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-12-28  |  **Closed:** 2023-04-07  |  **Author:** @mikechan0731
- **Labels:** type:bug, priority:high, component:localization
- **Comments:** 18  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2597

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi I'm Mike from ITRI
> 
> I'm currently using autoware.universe's locator program for locating large buses.
> 
> However, the positioning is always abnormal. After many tests and adjustments, there is still no improvement. 
> 
> The details are as follows:
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> As mentioned in regular meetings, we hope that large buses can output positioning information smoothly and smoothly during positioning, so that the process of automatic driving is comfortable.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> But now our large bus will have positioning problems during travel, for example, the positioning is not smooth but shaking, as shown in the following video link:
> 
> Video1: [https://1drv.ms/v/s!AnJ4ubRnmXsujepAtTg_SjH237xLqg?e=FxwLMU](https://1drv.ms/v/s!AnJ4ubRnmXsujepAtTg_SjH237xLqg?e=FxwLMU)
> 
> Video2: [https://1drv.ms/v/s!AnJ4ubRnmXsujepBy2bgmlmdUxPQUQ?e=6qhyTx](https://1drv.ms/v/s!AnJ4ubRnmXsujepBy2bgmlmdUxPQUQ?e=6qhyTx)
> 
> It will also happen that halfway through the positioning error:
> 
> Video3: [https://1drv.ms/v/s!AnJ4ubRnmXsujepE9Rijr1uZjKBKtg?e=ttVkaK](https://1drv.ms/v/s!AnJ4ubRnmXsujepE9Rijr1uZjKBKtg?e=ttVkaK)
> 
> Video4: [https://1drv.ms/v/s!AnJ4ubRnmXsujepCgb9so2WKTomtaQ?e=c6HDt6](https://1drv.ms/v/s!AnJ4ubRnmXsujepCgb9so2WKTomtaQ?e=c6HDt6)
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> The localization parameters used are provided here as a reference:
> - voxel size: 2.0, 2.0, 2.0
> - downsample pointclouds: 10,000
> - ndt_scan_matcher step_size: 2.1
> 
> The ros2bag link in the corresponding positioning process is provided here. We use the topic /LidarFrontTop as the positioning input point cloud.
> 
> ROSBAG2 Link: [https://1drv.ms/u/s!AnJ4ubRnmXsujeoj9Au-pDLAfEl2mw?e=wujOP1](https://1drv.ms/u/s!AnJ4ubRnmXsujeoj9Au-pDLAfEl2mw?e=wujOP1)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> OS: Ubuntu 20.04
> ROS2 Galactic
> Autoware Universe
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> We speculate that these problems occur because the frequency of the point cloud information provided for positioning is too low. If you use `ros2 topic hz /LidarFrontTop` (point cloud input for positioning), you will find that the frequency is only about 3~5Hz.
> 
> This part extends the second problem: We found that on the host, if two subscribers register the same topic at the same time, it will cause serious transmission slowdown.
> 
> For example, /LidarFrontTop If there is only one subscriber, the transmission speed is 20Hz. But if another subscriber is turned on, the transmission speed will immediately drop to 3~5Hz, even if I just start two `ros2 topic hz /LidarFrontTop` at the same time, this will happen.
> 
> I would like to ask for advice on the above two problems: 
> 
> 1. The positioning is not smooth but shaking,
> 2. The problem of transmission slowdown, 
> 
> Any suggestion is welcomedΓÇªThank you!
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

###### @mitsudome-r (2023-02-07)

> @mikechan0731 
> I'm afraid we don't have any calibration tool that can calculate the value automatically.
> You first have to measure the relative position from your base_link (center of the rear wheels) to lidar position. You can use the design value for the initial position, then use ekf_localizer to adjust yaw angle error as mentioned in Fatih's comment.
> 
> 
> To set base_link->lidar tf, you can run the following command:
> ```
> ros2 run tf2_ros static_transform_publisher --x 0.0 --y 0.0 --z -.0 --roll 0.0 --pitch 0.0 --yaw 0.0 --frame-id base_link --child-frame-id lidar
> ```
>

> 
> # My findings
> 
> ## The DDS settings are potentially not set permanently
> 
> Seeing things not slowing down on my machine, there could be many reasons but my intuition/suspicions is on the lack of DDS optimizations.
> 
> I suggest you look into:
> `sudo gedit /etc/sysctl.d/10-cyclone-max.conf` or `sudo gedit /etc/sysctl.conf` depending on which one you put the settings to.
> And make sure following lines exist in the end of these files:
> ```
> net.core.rmem_max=2147483647
> net.ipv4.ipfrag_time=3
> net.ipv4.ipfrag_high_thresh=134217728
> ```
> 
> Then either restart the pc or run:
> ```bash
> sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=2147483647
> sudo sysctl net.ipv4.ipfrag_time=3
> sudo sysctl net.ipv4.ipfrag_high_thresh=134217728
> ```
> 
> Make sure .bashrc has following:
> ```bash
> export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
> export ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1
> export CYCLONEDDS_URI=/home/yourusername/cyclonedds.xml
> ```
> (adjust to your username)
> 
> And following is my `cyclonedds.xml` for ros2 galactic:
> ```xml
> <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
> <CycloneDDS xmlns="https://cdds.io/config" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="https://cdds.io/config https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eclipse-cyclonedds/cyclonedds/master/etc/cyclonedds.xsd">
>     <Domain Id="any">
>         <General>
>             <AllowMulticast>default</AllowMulticast>
>             <MaxMessageSize>65500B</MaxMessageSize>
>         </General>
>         <Internal>
>             <MinimumSocketReceiveBufferSize>10MB</MinimumSocketReceiveBufferSize>
>             <Watermarks>
>                 <WhcHigh>500kB</WhcHigh>
>             </Watermarks>
>         </Internal>
>     </Domain>
> </CycloneDDS>
> ```
> 
> I hope applying these will help with the performance.
> 
> **Sources:**
> - https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/galactic/installation/additional-settings-for-developers/#dds-settings
> - https://docs.ros.org/en/galactic/How-To-Guides/DDS-tuning.html
> 
> ## Lack of point cloud container (composable node container)
> - The repository doesn't make use of intra-process communication and composable node containers.
>   - This is very important for the sensing and perception stack to not pass large point cloud topics by network to reduce congestion.
>   - I suggest reading through https://docs.ros.org/en/galactic/How-To-Guides/Launching-composable-nodes.html and also seeing how Autoware galactic branch utilizes this functionality.
>   - I foresee mostly launch file modifications to be necessary so far:
>     - Seeing that `autoware_ws3_bk/src/itri_util/ros2_ouster_drivers/ros2_ouster/src/driver_types.cpp` has rclcpp_components registered, it should support the containers.
>        ```
>        RCLCPP_COMPONENTS_REGISTER_NODE(ros2_ouster::Driver)
>        RCLCPP_COMPONENTS_REGISTER_NODE(ros2_ouster::TinsDriver)
>        ```
>     - `lidar_grabber` requires some changes to conform to the composable nodes but it is about ~4 hours of work for an intermediate developer comfortable with composable nodes.
>       - According to my observations, only `autoware_ws3_bk/src/itri_util/lidar_grabber/src/main.cpp` and `autoware_ws3_bk/src/itri_util/lidar_grabber/CMakeLists.txt` needs changes. And a new launch file could be added.
> 
> cc. @mitsudome-r @mikechan0731 @hueirutseng

###### @xmfcx (2023-03-18)

> You see it says: `ros2: selected interface "lo" is not multicast-capable: `
> 
> To resolve it, you need to run `sudo ip link set lo multicast on` every time the you restart the pc. (source: https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/installation/additional-settings-for-developers/#enabling-localhost-only-communication )
> 
> You could also create a service that runs that when ubuntu boots, we will probably add it to the documentation in the future.

###### @xmfcx (2023-03-31)

> Hello,
> This evening I had a chance to access ITRI's lidar pc with help of @mikechan0731 with a remote desktop control software.
> 
> They had reinstalled Ubuntu 20.04 and installed everything from scratch.
> When I got the pc, following were missing:
> - cyclonedds configuration
> - dds configuration (done with `sudo gedit /etc/sysctl.d/10-cyclone-max.conf`, [explained in my post](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2597#issuecomment-1469398009))
> - [ccache configuration](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/how-to-guides/advanced-usage-of-colcon/#using-ccache) (not relevant for this issue but really helps with the compilation times, i find it almost mandatory)
> - [colorized ros2 terminal output and custom format for the logger output](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/installation/additional-settings-for-developers/#colorizing-logger-output) (again not mandatory but i need my colorful output)
> 
> I added them but still surprised that the downsampled point cloud output was 4-5Hz.
> 
> ```bash
> lidar@lidar:~$ screenfetch -n
>  OS: Ubuntu 20.04 focal
>  Kernel: x86_64 Linux 5.15.0-69-generic
>  Resolution: 1920x1080
>  DE: GNOME 3.36.5
>  WM: Mutter
>  Disk: 114G / 912G (14%)
>  CPU: Intel Xeon E-2278G @ 16x 5GHz [48.0┬░C]
>  GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti
>  RAM: 3302MiB / 64158MiB
> ```
> 
> System specs are OK and `gnome-system-monitor` didn't show much cpu activity when running things.
> 
> Then I got suspicious that maybe the downsampling node was not compiled with `Release` or `RelWithDebInfo` tags. When I checked the `~/.bash_history` my suspicions turned out to be correct.
> 
> ```bash
> lidar@lidar:~$ cat ~/.bash_history | grep "colcon build"
> colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
> colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
> colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
> colcon build --symlink-install --continue-on-error
> ```
> 
> So it was started to be built with the release tag but in the end, the tag was dropped.
> 
> Then I've built it with `colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=1 --continue-on-error` and then the issue was fixed.
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2023-03-31 20-17-05](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10751153/229109538-6ac029d5-cc71-4906-93d1-ab78022b9a1c.png)

###### @ajay1606 (2023-03-31)

> @xmfcx Excellent, Indeed it was very useful as i was also following this issues since quite long time and happy to see this got fixed.  

###### @mikechan0731 (2023-04-07)

> Hi, thanks to @xmfcx  for the continued testing, I'm doing a rebuild test today,
> 
> First, I used the original build command `colcon build` to compile the program, resulting in the low FPS phenomenon of the original downsample module:
> 
> https://youtu.be/wWB4-_YJbow
> 
> Later, according to @xmfcx  's suggestion, I re-used the build command
> 
>  `colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=1 --continue-on-error` 
> 
> to compile the program, and the original downsample module.
> 
> The phenomenon of low FPS (5Hz) is immediately increased to 30Hz, and the output of /pose also conforms to the output frequency of point cloud original file output frequency of 15Hz:
> 
> https://youtu.be/wWB4-_YJbow
> 
> I think this problem can be considered solved, thanks to everyone who helped, especially @xmfcx, thank you!

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-12-22  |  **Closed:** 2022-12-22  |  **Author:** @batuhanbeytekin
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2569

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In autoware.universe, faces and license plates are not anonymized for privacy-preserving.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Anonymization of faces and license plates to ensure data privacy
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Read all topics from the bag file and then blur the only image topics. After that write a new bag file that changed new blurred image topics and has the same topics as the previous bag.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Reading bag file with sequential reader
> - [ ] Update image topics in bag file with blurred

### #2567 — Change traffic signal interface to support V2X/V2I

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-12-22  |  **Closed:** 2023-09-09  |  **Author:** @isamu-takagi
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:perception, component:planning
- **Comments:** 21  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2567

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hi, I'm thinking about V2X support in traffic signal interface. Currently, the planning component (traffic_light module in behavior_velocity_planner) has two traffic signal inputs, `perception` and `external`. It looks like we can input V2X information into `external`, but it was actually created for the purpose of overriding vehicle behavior by the operator. So this interface means the operator's decision such as pass and stop rather than the traffic signal color such as green or red, and the pass throuh logic described [here](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/traffic-light-design/#limitations) is not performed.
> 
> ![traffic-signal-discuss-old](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43976882/209082189-7cca5098-5f42-4fcf-95cf-0abeca4b8c56.png)
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> For the planning component, it doesn't matter if the input is image recognition results or V2X. Therefore, I'll unify the input so that V2X can be handled in the same way as image recognition results.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The new architecture is as follows. Merge the image recognition results and V2X before inputting into the planning component. Typically the merge node will use V2X if it is available, otherwise it will use the most confident image recognition result. Also, as described later, light bulbs and traffic signals are treated separately.
> 
> The messages LightBulbsArray (or NewTrafficLightArray) and NewTrafficSignalArray (temporary name) are almost the same as TrafficSignalArray, except for the use of light bulbs ID and regulatory element ID. Or NewTrafficSignalArray could be changed to more semantic information such as `{straight: green, turn_right: red}`.
> 
> ![traffic-signal-discuss-new](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43976882/209082209-57159f1f-f71b-40f9-b4ce-32c50a2d3e75.png)
> 
> ### Map primitive IDs
> 
> There are multiple signals (as equipment) at one intersection, and image recognition targets them. On the other hand, V2X and the planning component only need one traffic signal (as information) in each direction of the intersection. This is defined in lanelet as light_blubs way ID and regulatory_element relation ID. See [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_common/blob/main/tmp/lanelet2_extension/docs/lanelet2_format_extension.md#trafficlights) for details of lanelet format.
> 
> ![traffic-signal-lanelet](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43976882/209090070-04015bbd-5897-468d-b49a-418453a29607.png)
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Add new interface message.
> - [x] Change the perception output interface.
> - [x] Change the planning input interface.
> - [x] Create the V2X output interface.
> - [x] Create the merge node from perception to planning.

**Comments:**

>

>

Note that I changed the definition of traffic signal and traffic light. If there are other good words to distinguish between these, please let me know.
> 
> | Type | Current implementation | Related lanelet ID |
> | ---- | ---- | ---- |
> | TrafficSignal.msg | none | Relation ID (type: regulatory_element) |
> | ~TrafficLight.msg~ | ~TrafficSignal.idl~ | ~Way ID (type: traffic_light)~  |
> | TrafficSignalElement.msg | TrafficLight.idl | ~Node ID if possible~ |
> 
> Updated for https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2567#issuecomment-1611086117

### #2513 — Autoware ignores obstacles located `vehicle_length` away after goal

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-12-16  |  **Closed:** 2023-02-24  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 12  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2513

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When an obstacle is in front of the vehicle, on the path:
> ![Screenshot from 2022-12-16 13-46-38](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/208024646-beb5d37a-cd6a-468a-8203-16ada0f06cea.png)
> 
> When an obstacle is in front of the vehicle, more than `vehicle_length` away from the goal pose
> ![Screenshot from 2022-12-16 13-47-03](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/208024644-2841d3b2-77ff-4988-8a78-47c7f767ee7e.png)
> 
> It seems that `obstacle_stop_planner` is not considering the obstacle in the second situation, because the obstacle is further away than `vehicle_length`. I don't know if it is necessary to keep the same safety distance in both situations. However, we definitely need a bigger margin in the second case
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Keep some safety distance from obstacle, even for the goal.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Autoware stops and touches the vehicle in front
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> planning simulator
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @ismetatabay (2022-12-16)

> @VRichardJP Hi, at ```obstacle_stop_planner``` package, there is a parameter for  extending trajectory to consider after goal obstacle.
> 
> Please check:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/c7d3b7d2132323af3437af01e9d774b13005bace/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/config/obstacle_stop_planner.param.yaml#L18
> 
> At this case below (yellow borders describes vehicle footprint on goal_pose), i updated ```extend_distance``` parameter to 5.0 meter. According to this parameter, ```obstacle_stop_planner``` stops the vehicle before it reach goal_pose.
> 
> ![Selection_031](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/56237550/208095992-d37b155e-1183-4e43-8fe5-f02894f8c455.png)
> 
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2022-12-16)

> I see! Should we then change the default value? Anything is better than 0 at this point.

###### @ismetatabay (2022-12-16)

> It also makes sense to me to set the default value of ```extend_distance```  to ```1.0``` [m] or ```2.0``` [m] to avoid undesirable situations. What do you think? @satoshi-ota 

###### @satoshi-ota (2022-12-20)

> @VRichardJP @ismetatabay I think so too. We set the parameter at 5.0 in other project.

###### @brkay54 (2022-12-20)

> Should it be set as parameter? I think extend_distance should depend vehicle's dimensions and should be calculated in node like: `distance_base_to_front + margin`. 

###### @satoshi-ota (2022-12-20)

> @brkay54 cc @kosuke55  I agree with you. I think we can remove the parameter. On ther other hand, I also think It might be better to add a new parameter (e.g. `stop_for_obstacle_behind_goal`) to indicate whether the vehicle stops for obstacles behind the goal.

###### @ismetatabay (2022-12-21)

> @brkay54 @satoshi-ota @VRichardJP If its okay for you, I will create PR for this issue. I think adding ```stop_for_obstacle_behind_goal``` (default value is true) parameter for the indicate extend trajectory along vehicle length or not extending trajectory after goal for obstacle checking.

###### @VRichardJP (2022-12-21)

> I am not sure I get everything. Is it the current behavior?
> 1. when on the path, ego keeps some distance from obstacles = `base_link` to front + fixed margin
> 2. for the goal case, obstacle search distance is increased by another parameter (currently 0.0). If an obstacle is on the extended path, the behavior is the same than 1.
> 
> With the PR, 1. is unchanged, and 2. is replaced by a bool which, if true, defines the distance automatically (based on the value from 1.)
> 
> Is it correct?

###### @ismetatabay (2022-12-21)

> @VRichardJP Hi, In the current implementation, there is a certain trajectory where the objects will be checked. This is equals to : path trajectory + goal pose + (base to front). With this PR, we extend the obstacle detection area by an extra vehicle length.
> 
> For example, let the object on the trajectory and obstacle stop planner  set a stop point from 20 meters away and its stops the vehicle. If this point far away from goal pose than base to front length of vehicle, object will not be detected and vehicle doesn't stop.
> 
> In other words, we extend the detection area twice with PR (base_link to front + rear_overhang + base_link_to_front):
> >     1. when on the path, ego keeps some distance from obstacles = `base_link` to front + fixed margin
> 
> 
> 

###### @stale (2023-02-19)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @ismetatabay (2023-02-21)

> hi @satoshi-ota @VRichardJP @brkay54, sorry for late (i am busy with field testing). I updated the extending algorithm according to the osbtacle stop planner's ```max_longitudinal_margin``` param ([see](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/#role)). 

###### @kosuke55 (2023-02-27)

> @ismetatabay @satoshi-ota @VRichardJP @brkay54 
> Hi, thanks for your PR, I added a specific margin for behind the goal same to [obstacle_cruise_planner](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/obstacle_cruise_planner/config/obstacle_cruise_planner.param.yaml#L14) in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2953
> This parameter assumes parallel parking behind another car like in [pull_over](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/config/pull_over/pull_over.param.yaml#L19)
>

### #2497 — Dataset License & Usage for Autoware

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-12-13  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @armaganarsln
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:map
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2497

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [x] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> We are continuously trying to understand which open datasets Autoware developers could use since Autoware is not a commercial environment nor an academic environment where dataset licenses are mostly having restrictions.
> 
> Autoware is an open-source project developed by contributors from Universities & companies where the contributors are commonly working in for-profit companies. 
> 
> We will like to ask below dataset owners and starting with Kitti Dataset which datasets we could use in Autoware development, what we should do (like giving references, adding warnings related to the use of the dataset etc.) during our usage and if there is any paid or free method that we could use the dataset without thinking of any breach of the license they have.
> 
> The link to the datasets to be explored as a start: (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/12tFZON4vUlHPdAXoIEua8GM6xsE_Xz8uJnBTYND8Ucc/edit#gid=0)
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Learning how and which open datasets we could use for Autoware development
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Getting in contact with each dataset owner on their website and in the list to introduce Autoware Foundation and getting permissions or rights of use or learning that it's not legal for Autoware developers to use.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Received replies from
> 
> - [x] KITTI
> - [ ] A Stereo Event Camera Dataset for Driving Scenarios (UZH)
> - [ ] Multi-Modal Lidars Dataset for Benchmarking General-Purpose Localization and Mapping Algorithms
> - [ ] KAIST Multi-spectral Day/Night Dataset

**Comments:**

###### @samet-kutuk (2023-01-22)

> Here's the KITTI dataset owner's comment: "The dataset can be used as long as the results of its usage are made public (e.g., via an openly accessible publication) and as long as the dataset does not serve for product development."
> 
> I'm assuming, Autoware wouldn't be categorized as a product. But I'd like to get some comments from @mitsudome-r 
> 
> I will continue with other datasets, but who's maintaining the list of datasets? Are there only four of them? @armaganarsln 

###### @stale (2023-03-23)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @samet-kutuk (2023-04-11)

> I have some updates regarding the dataset use topic.
> 
> - I talked to the KITTI dataset owner, and because the Autoware project can be used to power customer solutions, **it's deemed inappropriate to be used.**
> - I talked to Prof. Scaramuzza about the Stereo Event Camera Dataset for Driving Scenarios. We can **freely use** this dataset (their paper should be cited in the code)
> - I talked to Li Qingqing from the University of Turku about Multi-Modal Lidars Dataset for Benchmarking General-Purpose Localization and Mapping Algorithms, **we can freely use** this dataset
> - Next up, I'll talk to KAIST about their dataset, and keep you posted.

###### @armaganarsln (2023-04-12)

> Thank you Samet, lets discuss the details at TSC. I think we should make Kitti part at least official because we are currently using it for development
>

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @mitsudome-r (2026-03-24)

> I'm closing the issue that was inactive for a long time. Feel free to reopen if the issue is still relevant

- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2495

**Body:**

> ### Checklist

> ### Description
> 
> Found the exact same issue than #2422 here:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/f1a9a9608559a5b89f631df3dc2fadd037e36ab4/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/behavior_path_planner_node.cpp#L657
> 
> The data is accessed outside the `mutex_pd_` lock guard
> 
> While working on my PR, I reset the `route_handler` internal data after a new route has just arrived. The data is only left uninitialized while the new route is being checked/loaded (which happens in the same callback). However I got the following segfault, showing that another thread tried to access the data at the same time:
> ```
> Thread 14 "component_conta" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.

> 1647	  const auto current_point = lanelet_route_ptr->getClosestLaneletPointWithinRoute(ego_pose);
> (gdb) 
> #3  0x00007fffd27a7d78 in behavior_path_planner::BehaviorPathPlannerNode::run (this=0x5555558383d0) at /home/sig/autoware/src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/behavior_path_planner_node.cpp:658
> 658	      util::getDrivableAreaForAllSharedLinestringLanelets(planner_data));

> no concurrent access

> N/A

>

**Comments:**

###### @purewater0901 (2022-12-14)

> @VRichardJP 
> Thanks for your issue. I submitted a new [PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2501). I think this solves all of the problems related to planner data.

###### @VRichardJP (2022-12-14)

> Thank you, I will test it. 
> 
> However, I am not convinced copying the `planner_data_` is a good idea.
> For example, imagine you have any pointer inside the structure:
> 
> ```
> struct PlannerData {
>   DataPtr data_ptr;
>   // some other things... 
> };
> ```
> 
> If you do this:
> ```
> mutex_pd_.lock();
> const auto planner_data = std::make_shared<PlannerData>(*planner_data_);
> mutex_pd_.unlock();
> 
> planner_data.data_ptr->getInternalState();
> ```
> 
> Then, `planner_data->data_ptr` and `planner_data_->data_ptr` points to the same thing. So if someone else does this:
> ```
> // some other thread
> mutex_pd_.lock();
> planner_data_.data_ptr->changeInternalState();
> mutex_pd_.unlock();
> ```
> 
> You may have the `planner_data.data_ptr->getInternalState()` reading something while `planner_data_.data_ptr->changeInternalState()` is writing it.

###### @purewater0901 (2022-12-16)

> @VRichardJP 
> Thank you for your suggestions and comments. I made a new PR, what do you think about this change?
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2510

###### @xmfcx (2023-01-10)

> @VRichardJP does this solve this bug report? https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2510

###### @VRichardJP (2023-01-11)

> I am sorry, I still think there is a concurrency issue.
> 
> The `BehaviorPathPlannerNode::createLatestPlannerData()` function in [`behavior_path_planner_node.cpp`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/72a27d3ccac6f0d1e0e4573a348b29968490ab12/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/behavior_path_planner_node.cpp) returns a simple copy of the `planner_data_`. As a consequence, you have `planner_data_->route_handler == createLatestPlannerData()->route_handler`. In other words, when `createLatestPlannerData()` result is accessed here:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/72a27d3ccac6f0d1e0e4573a348b29968490ab12/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/behavior_path_planner_node.cpp#L686
> 
> Nothing prevents another function from modifying `planner_data_->route_handler`. For example:
>  https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/72a27d3ccac6f0d1e0e4573a348b29968490ab12/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/behavior_path_planner_node.cpp#L916-L920
> 
> There are only 3 ways to solve the issue:
> - Add lock guard very every single read/write of `planner_data_`, or
> - Put every single callback using `planner_data_` in the same `rclcpp::CallbackGroupType::MutuallyExclusive` callback group, or
> - Just make the node single threaded
> 
> I think the second or third option are simpler. Actually, most callbacks are already in the same group. I think only the timer callback to `BehaviorPathPlannerNode::run` is not in the group: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/72a27d3ccac6f0d1e0e4573a348b29968490ab12/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/behavior_path_planner_node.cpp#L175-L176

###### @xmfcx (2023-02-21)

> @VRichardJP is this issue solved by these two PRs above?

###### @VRichardJP (2023-02-22)

> @xmfcx 
> No. 
> 
> In the current state, the code has no concurrent memory access. This was also true before the few changes. But this is just an illusion, as the inherent problem has yet to be solved. My [comment above](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2495#issuecomment-1378149215) still holds: the inner data of `planner_data_` is accessed outside the mutex lock (through `planner_data`).

> --- a/planning/route_handler/include/route_handler/route_handler.hpp
> +++ b/planning/route_handler/include/route_handler/route_handler.hpp
> @@ -292,6 +292,7 @@ public:
>    double getLaneChangeableDistance(
>      const Pose & current_pose, const LaneChangeDirection & direction) const;
>    lanelet::ConstPolygon3d getIntersectionAreaById(const lanelet::Id id) const;
> +  lanelet::ConstLanelets getRouteLanelets() const;
>  
>  private:
>    // MUST
> @@ -336,7 +337,6 @@ private:
>      const lanelet::ConstLanelet & lanelet, lanelet::ConstLanelet * right_lanelet) const;
>    bool getLeftLaneletWithinRoute(
>      const lanelet::ConstLanelet & lanelet, lanelet::ConstLanelet * left_lanelet) const;
> -  lanelet::ConstLanelets getRouteLanelets() const;
>    lanelet::ConstLanelets getLaneletSequenceUpTo(
>      const lanelet::ConstLanelet & lanelet,
>      const double min_length = std::numeric_limits<double>::max()) const;
> ```
> 
> With these changes:
> - `run()` is stuck in an endless loop, printing the size of the route lanelet held by `planner_data` and `planner_data_` every second.
> - A loop timer check if a new map/route has been received, and update `planner_data_` when necessary. Everything happens while `mutex_pd_` is locked, so this code snippet is safe. 
> 
> If everything is safe, the printing loop should always display the same value for `planner_data`, even if `planner_data_` is modified.
> 
> Compile, source, then run autoware in the planning simulator. For example:
> ```
> $ ros2 launch autoware_launch planning_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=../data/autoware_data_universe/sample-map-planning/ vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit
> ```
> 
> Set a start and goal points. In the terminal window, you can see the current route size displayed every second. If you change the goal point so the route has more/less lanelets, you can see the both `planner_data` and `planner_data_` numbers are modified. In other words, the printing loop is accessing `planner_data_` inner data through `planner_data`, despite being outside mutex lock.
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/220552010-0b1251b7-35df-4152-a07f-d9078015bd86.png)
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-03-29)

> Fixed by https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2933

### #2484 — Parking tutorial in documentation fails to reach goal

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-12-09  |  **Closed:** 2022-12-09  |  **Author:** @mitsudome-r
- **Labels:** type:bug, priority:high
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2484

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When I follow the parking planner instruction in [Autoware Documentation](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/#parking-scenario), it does not plan path correctly.
> 
> It should first plan path to the nearest lane, but it tries to reach goal directly without consideration of vehicle kinematic model.
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43976834/206692546-363337df-9a86-4020-b093-7c4a6a7173e9.png)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Fails to reach goal when goal is set in parking area.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Succeeds to reach goal when goal is set in parking area.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Follow parking scenario in [Autoware Documentation](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/#parking-scenario)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS 2 Humble
> - Autoware main branch
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2340
> 
> It seems behavior planner was supposed to refine the goal to closest lane first, but it was removed from this PR. https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2340
> 
> We should probably redesign the system to switch between parking<->lane_driving mode, but I think reverting the commit would be the easiest fix for now.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

And in the lane_change of behavior_path_planner,there are no additional measures to deal with the lane conditions in this case.

> 2.ROS2: Galactic
> 3.Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
>

>

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> This line is outside the `mutex_pd_` lock guard:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/17f1b956a397b1661471ad820cb53219aaeaaa54/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/behavior_path_planner_node.cpp#L645
> 
> This means the `planner_data_` content may be modified when the `getTurnSignal` function is trying to access it.
> 
> For example I have modified the `route_handler::getClosestLaneletWithinRoute` to crash if the route handler is not ready:
> 
> ```
> bool RouteHandler::getClosestLaneletWithinRoute(const Pose & search_pose, lanelet::ConstLanelet * closest_lanelet) const
> {
>   if (!is_handler_ready_) {
>     // TODO(vrichard) clean
>     std::cerr << "Trying to call getClosestLaneletWithinRoute() but handler is not ready" << std::endl; 
>     throw std::runtime_error("debug");
>     return false;
>   }
>   std::optional<lanelet::ConstLanelet> optional_lanelet = lanelet_route_.getClosestLaneletWithinRoute(search_pose);
>   if (!optional_lanelet) {
>     return false;
>   }
>   *closest_lanelet = *optional_lanelet;
>   return true;
> }
> ```
> 
> Then I run the planning simulator and set the goal pose with Rviz, many times. After many tries (it's all about timing), the exception is thrown:
> 
> ```
> [New Thread 0x7fff808ab700 (LWP 114166)]
> Trying to call getClosestLaneletWithinRoute() but handler is not ready
> terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
>   what():  debug
> [Thread 0x7fff808ab700 (LWP 114166) exited]
> 
> Thread 17 "component_conta" received signal SIGABRT, Aborted.
> [Switching to Thread 0x7fffce7fc700 (LWP 108608)]
> __GI_raise (sig=sig@entry=6) at ../sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/raise.c:50

> (gdb) bt
> #0  __GI_raise (sig=sig@entry=6) at ../sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/raise.c:50
> #1  0x00007ffff7947859 in __GI_abort () at abort.c:79
> #2  0x00007ffff7bd0911 in  () at /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6
> #3  0x00007ffff7bdc38c in  () at /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6
> #4  0x00007ffff7bdc3f7 in  () at /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6
> #5  0x00007ffff7bdc6a9 in  () at /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6
> #6  0x00007fffec0f8d68 in route_handler::RouteHandler::getClosestLaneletWithinRoute(geometry_msgs::msg::Pose_<std::allocator<void> > const&, lanelet::ConstLanelet*) const [clone .cold] () at /home/sig/autoware/install/route_handler/lib/libroute_handler.so
> #7  0x00007fffec5acc49 in behavior_path_planner::util::calcLaneletPathAroundPose(std::shared_ptr<route_handler::RouteHandler>, geometry_msgs::msg::Pose_<std::allocator<void> > const&, double, double) () at /home/sig/autoware/install/behavior_path_planner/lib/libbehavior_path_planner_node.so
> #8  0x00007fffec6542ff in behavior_path_planner::TurnSignalDecider::getTurnSignal(std::shared_ptr<behavior_path_planner::PlannerData const> const&, autoware_auto_planning_msgs::msg::PathWithLaneId_<std::allocator<void> > const&, behavior_path_planner::TurnSignalInfo const&) () at /home/sig/autoware/install/behavior_path_planner/lib/libbehavior_path_planner_node.so
> #9  0x00007fffec4fdca2 in behavior_path_planner::BehaviorPathPlannerNode::run() () at /home/sig/autoware/install/behavior_path_planner/lib/libbehavior_path_planner_node.so
> #10 0x00007fffec50ab77 in rclcpp::GenericTimer<std::_Bind<void (behavior_path_planner::BehaviorPathPlannerNode::*(behavior_path_planner::BehaviorPathPlannerNode*))()>, (void*)0>::execute_callback() () at /home/sig/autoware/install/behavior_path_planner/lib/libbehavior_path_planner_node.so
> #11 0x00007ffff7e6ef7d in rclcpp::Executor::execute_any_executable(rclcpp::AnyExecutable&) () at /opt/ros/galactic/lib/librclcpp.so
> #12 0x00007ffff7e754bb in rclcpp::executors::MultiThreadedExecutor::run(unsigned long) () at /opt/ros/galactic/lib/librclcpp.so

> By the time I print `is_handler_ready_` in gdb it is already back to true.

### #2409 — [CI] build-and-test-differential only tests CUDA

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-11-30  |  **Closed:** 2022-12-01  |  **Author:** @ambroise-arm
- **Labels:** type:bug, type:github-actions, type:ci
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2409

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The `build-and-test-differential` workflow only starts a runner with cuda enabled: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/03de605b0998e9a9ee623f9a74a7002f4d2b61a4/.github/workflows/build-and-test-differential.yaml#L17
> This prevents catching issues on systems that don't have cuda enabled.
> For example https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2370 successfully passed CI, but failed once merged: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/actions/runs/3583250712/jobs/6028456850
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> CUDA shouldn't be required to build Autoware
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The CI for PRs doesn't check that.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Build current tip of main (03de605b0998e9a9ee623f9a74a7002f4d2b61a4) on a system without cuda.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @ambroise-arm (2022-11-30)

> cc @kenji-miyake 

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-11-30)

> @ambroise-arm Actually, it was intentionally removed temporarily.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1669
> 
> After we move to Humble and remove Galactic CI workflows by https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2408, I believe we can re-enable no-cuda checks. 

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-11-30)

> Ah, sorry. I might misunderstand your problem. Will fix my comment above.

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-11-30)

> Okay, I think my comment wasn't so wrong.
> 
> > CUDA shouldn't be required to build Autoware
> 
> I believe it's not true. We need CUDA for now because `autoware.universe` depends on CUDA yet.
> But the no-cuda environment should also be tested.
> 
> @ambroise-arm What do you think?

###### @ambroise-arm (2022-11-30)

> I believe your comment gives valuable information as it is.
> Is the re-enablement of the no-cuda checks tracked somewhere? If not we could keep this open until it is done.

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-11-30)

> I'll create a revert PR and relate this issue.

###### @ambroise-arm (2022-11-30)

> > > CUDA shouldn't be required to build Autoware
> 
> > I believe it's not true.
> 
> I understand that cuda is necessary to have the runtime functionality of Autoware. But I strongly believe that it should be possible to built without it.
> For example https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/03de605b0998e9a9ee623f9a74a7002f4d2b61a4/perception/lidar_apollo_instance_segmentation/CMakeLists.txt#L12 has a different behavior whether cuda is present on the system or not, and doesn't fail if it's not.
> 
> > I'll create a revert PR and relate this issue.
> 
> What about the problems from https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1669, won't that just get us back to that?
> 
> EDIT: sorry, I hadn't seen https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2410#issuecomment-1332189526

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-11-30)

> > But I strongly believe that it should be possible to built without it.
> 
> Yes, it's true! We gave up ensuring no-cuda just due to CI jams. Let's re-enable it.

### #2390 — Planning simulator stops for non-existant virtual traffic light

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-11-28  |  **Closed:** 2023-03-14  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:help-wanted, component:perception, component:planning
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2390

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Following the https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/ the vehicle stops at a right turn and stays there forever.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Vehicle to move if there is no traffic light.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Vehicle stops.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> - Follow https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/
> - Give following path:
>   - ![Screenshot from 2022-11-28 15-34-26](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10751153/204279609-155c0cd0-a6a5-4493-aa56-c4a68acbacf2.png)
> - Vehicle will stop here:
>   - ![Screenshot from 2022-11-28 15-22-48](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10751153/204279800-86bee7c6-ece0-4585-acf2-515943df36ab.png)
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS2: humble
> - Autoware Universe
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> There is not even a traffic light nearby, I don't know why it stops.
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2022-11-28 15-41-22](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10751153/204280314-34854c08-0bcb-4cd4-943d-35227a6b92b7.png)

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-11-29)

> Virtual traffic light is meant to be used for V2X communication. The vehicle will wait until it receives approval from the external software (infrastructure) to pass.
> https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/virtual-traffic-light-design/.
> 
> The reason why virtual traffic light being defined in the sample map is because the sample map is originally created by TIER IV to test all features in behavior modules. Maybe we should add tutorial for sending approval in the instruction to avoid confusion.

###### @kosuke55 (2022-12-02)

> thank you for your report. sorry, I did not check the actual behavior but the following command may approve it and the vehicle starts to move.
> ```
> sec=$(($(date +%s) + 30)); ros2 topic pub /awapi/tmp/virtual_traffic_light_states tier4_v2x_msgs/msg/VirtualTrafficLightStateArray "{stamp: {sec: $sec, nanosec: 999999999}, states: [{stamp: {sec: $sec, nanosec: 999999999}, type: 'dummy_infrastructure', id: '$1', approval: true, is_finalized: true}]}" -1
> ```

###### @xmfcx (2023-01-10)

> Thanks, I will add this to the https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/ tutorial steps as a note for newcomers.

###### @soblin (2023-01-25)

> @xmfcx Recently we updated the sample map to contain all kinds of map primitives including virtual_trafic_light, so this is an expected behavior. So the workaround is to
> - (1) disable vtl module by changing the flag defined [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/c1a98f7f8822d7766a65c9fedf4ef805861d320e/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/config/behavior_velocity_planner.param.yaml#L9) in autoware_launch OR
> - (2) follow @kosuke55 -san's  above instruction
> . But this behavior maybe confusing for newcomers, so the tutorial page should be updated. Are you already working on it ? If not, I'll handle that.

###### @mitsudome-r (2023-01-31)

> @soblin It might be difficult for beginners to understand the difference between virtual traffic light(V2I command) and normal traffic light. Unless there is a good documentation for the virtual traffic light use-cases, it might be better to just turn the flag off.

###### @mitsudome-r (2023-01-31)

> @soblin I have talked with Fatih, and it would be nice if you can work on this issue.

###### @soblin (2023-01-31)

> @mitsudome-r Okay! I think we can just disable this flag in awf autoware_launch only.

---

### #2389 — avoidance candidate path can be chattering at return shift

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-11-28  |  **Closed:** 2022-11-29  |  **Author:** @taikitanaka3
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2389

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> as title says
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> during avoidance return, path candidate shouldn't be chattering.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> during avoidance return, path candidate chatter and it's hard to execute path change with rtc
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> launch psim
> 
> set auto mode manager param remove avoidance right and left from auto
> ```
> /**:
>   ros__parameters:
>     module_list:
>       - "blind_spot"
>       - "crosswalk"
>       - "detection_area"
>       - "intersection"
>       - "no_stopping_area"
>       - "traffic_light"
>       - "lane_change_left"
>       - "lane_change_right"
>       - "avoidance_left"
>       - "avoidance_right"
>       - "pull_over"
>       - "pull_out"
> 
>     default_enable_list:
>       - "blind_spot"
>       - "crosswalk"
>       - "detection_area"
>       - "intersection"
>       - "no_stopping_area"
>       - "traffic_light"
>       - "lane_change_left"
>       - "lane_change_right"
>       - "pull_over"
>       - "pull_out"
> ```
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/65527974/204246679-c1c58cb1-9ead-4637-8e02-8eed81a5fd8c.png)
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/65527974/204247026-2fcb2dd8-88b7-419d-b918-ae3caf23ed78.png)
> 
> set avoidance param for small vehicle
> ```
> # see AvoidanceParameters description in avoidance_module_data.hpp for description.
> /**:
>   ros__parameters:
>     avoidance:
>       resample_interval_for_planning: 0.1
>       resample_interval_for_output: 0.3
>       detection_area_right_expand_dist: 1.0
>       detection_area_left_expand_dist: 0.0
> 
>       enable_avoidance_over_same_direction: true
>       enable_avoidance_over_opposite_direction: true
> 
>       threshold_distance_object_is_on_center: 0.0 # [m]
>       threshold_speed_object_is_stopped: 1.0      # [m/s]
>       threshold_time_object_is_moving: 1.0        # [s]
>       object_check_forward_distance: 20.0        # [m]
>       object_check_backward_distance: 2.0         # [m]
>       object_envelope_buffer: 0.3                 # [m]
>       lateral_collision_margin: 0.5               # [m]
>       lateral_collision_safety_buffer: 0.0        # [m]
> 
>       prepare_time: 0.1                           # [s]
>       min_prepare_distance: 0.1                  # [m]
>       min_avoidance_distance: 1.5                # [m]
> 
>       min_nominal_avoidance_speed: 0.28  # [m/s]
>       min_sharp_avoidance_speed: 0.28    # [m/s]
> 
>       road_shoulder_safety_margin: 0.0 # [m]
> 
>       max_right_shift_length: 5.0
>       max_left_shift_length: 0.0
> 
>       nominal_lateral_jerk: 1.0   # [m/s3]
>       max_lateral_jerk: 1.0       # [m/s3]
> 
>       object_last_seen_threshold: 2.0
> 
>       # For prevention of large acceleration while avoidance
>       min_avoidance_speed_for_acc_prevention: 3.0  # [m/s]
>       max_avoidance_acceleration: 0.5  # [m/ss]
> 
>       # for debug
>       publish_debug_marker: false
>       print_debug_info: false
> 
>       # not enabled yet
>       longitudinal_collision_margin_min_distance: 0.0          # [m]
>       longitudinal_collision_margin_time: 0.0
> 
>       # avoidance is performed for the object type with true
>       target_object:
>         car: true
>         truck: true
>         bus: true
>         trailer: true
>         unknown: true
>         bicycle: true
>         motorcycle: true
>         pedestrian: true
> 
>       # ---------- advanced parameters ----------
>       avoidance_execution_lateral_threshold: 0.0
> ```
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> awf/main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> shift point of start longitudinal can sometimes be very low negative value and this will slip creating new shift.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> https://github.com/tier4/autoware.universe/blob/f15188eff98f97b84bc90d6b49720fd5b5043104/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/scene_module/avoidance/avoidance_module.cpp#L2220
> 
> 
> this can solve this problem
> change thresh 0 to epsilon can solve this problem 
> ```
>     if (candidate.start_longitudinal < - 0.01) {
>       continue;
>     }
> ```
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/88d537d1316eaaa97530ad91a76fc257ad4160ac/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/scene_module/avoidance/avoidance_module.cpp#L1763
> or consider it's always positive
> ```
> al.start_longitudinal = std::max(0.0001, arclength_from_ego.at(al.start_idx));
> ```

### #2381 — while ego is lane changing behavior path planner process died when trying another lane change attempt

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-11-28  |  **Closed:** 2022-11-28  |  **Author:** @zulfaqar-azmi-t4
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2381

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When ego vehicle is lane changing, if we abruptly change the ego to another place in the map, and attempted lane change, behavior path planner node will died.
> 
> Since the abrupt change can only be done in PSIM, i think this will not happened in the real environment.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> behavior path planner process not died.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> behavior path planner process died.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. perform lane change at any location in the map.
> 2. while ego vehicle is lane changing, quickly change position of ego in another side of the map and then perform lane change there.
> 
> The following video might help.
> 
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93502286/204183623-f8aa4d53-57e6-40b6-9725-526151e9da21.mp4
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: 20.04
> - ROS 2: Galactic
> - Autoware: `main`
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The cause of the process died is due to  [getCenterlinePath in the getTurnSignal returns empty points.](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/turn_signal_decider.cpp#:~:text=const%20PathWithLaneId%20extended_path%20%3D%20util%3A%3AgetCenterLinePath())
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2022-11-28)

> PR to fix this is merged.

---

### #2375 — rtc_replayer can't replay rosbag rtc command for logsim

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-11-25  |  **Closed:** 2023-03-12  |  **Author:** @taikitanaka3
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2375

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> This uuid is unique for ll2 in behavior velocity but in behavior path planner uuid is completely random so it's impossible to send command using uuid in rosbag. https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/4f6c3d4c5ae134985b2bc2ec0033e86a41530a0b/planning/rtc_replayer/src/rtc_replayer_node.cpp#L113
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> replay behavior path rtc
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> cant replay behavior path rtc
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> ros2 bag play $BAG --remap rosbag api/external/get/rtc_status:=/debug/rtc_status
> ros2 launch rtc_replayer rtc_replyer_node
> 
> ### Versions

### #2374 — Out-of-range access in `obstacle_stop_planner::insertSlowDownSection`

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2022-11-25  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2374

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> While using the slow down planner to increase ACC detection range (see https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2262), we experienced multiple crash due to out-of-range accesses in `obstacle_stop_planner::insertSlowDownSection`. It happened most often after during obstacle avoidance maneuver.
> 
> We added the following snippet to detect the issue, and the node stopped crashing:
> ```diff
> diff --git a/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/src/node.cpp b/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/src/node.cpp
> index 2d26ce7b3..d993c0b32 100644
> --- a/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/src/node.cpp
> +++ b/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/src/node.cpp
> @@ -756,6 +756,33 @@ void ObstacleStopPlannerNode::insertSlowDownSection(
>    const auto & start_idx = slow_down_section.slow_down_start_idx;
>    const auto & end_idx = slow_down_section.slow_down_end_idx;
>  
> +  // for debug
> +  if(start_idx >= output.size())
> +  {
> +    RCLCPP_ERROR(get_logger(), "start_idx >= output.size() (%lu, %lu)",
> +      start_idx, output.size());
> +    return;
> +  }
> +  if(std::min(start_idx + 1, traj_end_idx) >= output.size())
> +  {
> +    RCLCPP_ERROR(get_logger(), "std::min(start_idx + 1, traj_end_idx) >= output.size() (%lu, %lu)",
> +      std::min(start_idx + 1, traj_end_idx), output.size());
> +    return;
> +  }
> +  if(end_idx >= output.size())
> +  {
> +    RCLCPP_ERROR(get_logger(), "end_idx >= output.size() (%lu, %lu)",
> +      end_idx, output.size());
> +    return;
> +  }
> +  if(std::min(end_idx + 1, traj_end_idx) >= output.size())
> +  {
> +    RCLCPP_ERROR(get_logger(), "std::min(end_idx + 1, traj_end_idx) >= output.size() (%lu, %lu)",
> +      std::min(end_idx + 1, traj_end_idx), output.size());
> +    return;
> +  }
> +
> +
>    const auto p_base_start = output.at(start_idx);
>    const auto p_next_start = output.at(std::min(start_idx + 1, traj_end_idx));
>    const auto & p_insert_start = slow_down_section.start_point;
> ```
> 
> However, we now see several of the added error messages appear from time to time in the logs. For example:
> ![Screenshot from 2022-11-17 16-03-20](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/203883393-cdd60233-92c9-4c9b-9e6e-479939db8760.png)
>

> ### Description
>

> All the lanes are changeable up to the traffic merge area, and the road looks long enough for the lane change. Yet, the vehicle seems not to be able to change lane:

> 
> Why is that?
>

> Vehicle can lane change
>

> Autoware fails to generate a lane change and stops halfway

> _No response_

### #2354 — Refactor mission planning to support when is goal behind start on the same lane

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-11-23  |  **Closed:** 2026-04-24  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale
- **Comments:** 9  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2354

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> As pointed in #2291 and #1715, the `mission_planner` and `behavior_path_planner` modules cannot generate neither a route nor a path when the goal pose is behind the start pose on the same lanelet.
> 
> This limitation comes from the way paths are designed in Autoware modules. Basically, all planning modules decribe paths as lists of lanelets (`ConstLanelets` or `std::vector<ConstLanelet>`). This only works as long as Autoware does not need to go through the same lanelet twice (which happens when the goal pose is behind the start pose).
> 
> To support the latter case, path definition should be refined. For example, a path could be:
> - a list of lanelets (`ConstLanelets`)
> - a start point on the first lanelet (if any)
> - a goal point on the last lanelet (if any)
> 
> With this new definition, the first and last lanelet could be the same, yet the starting "segment" and finishing "segment" could be different. In the case the goal point is behind the start point, the first segment would be from the start pose to the end of the lanelet, while the last segment would be from the beginning of the lanelet to the goal pose.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - add support for goal behind start scenario
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 1. In `route_handler`, introduce a new `LaneletPath` class, composed of:
> - `ConstLanelets lanelets`: the list of lanelets composing the path
> - `double start_arc_length`: the arc length of the start point on the first lanelet (if any)
> - `double goal_arc_length`: the arc length of the goal point on the last lanelet (if any)
> 
> 2. Any planning function using `ConstLanelets` as path should use the new type instead. `ConstLanelets` could still be used for non-path purposes (e.g. to list neighbor lanes). As a consequence, the following modules would need to be heavily reworked:
> - `mission_planning`
> - `route_handler`
> - `behavior_path_planner`
> 
> 3. Introduce Helper functions to implement route related logic (e.g. extend a path forward)
> 
> 4. Clean old code 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] new `mission_planner` supports all existing use cases + goal behind start on the same lanelet
> - [ ] new `behavior_path_planenr` supports all existing use case + goal behind start on the same lanelet
> - [ ] all route related logic is handled directly by `route_handler` module
> 
> Obviously, a set of OSM maps is needed to make sure Autoware still behaves the same in the supported cases.

**Comments:**

>

> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Adding a parameter; if this parameter is `true` it will be on the turn signal while the EGO is swerving the obstacle, but if it is false then the turn signal will be off.

> It should ensure that the turn signal is on or off while the obstacle swerving, depending on whether the parameter is true or false.
