### #2052 — Gear should not be changed to DRIVE while autoware is not engaged

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-10-12  |  **Closed:** 2023-01-10  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning, component:vehicle
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2052

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I am using a vehicle with pacmod3.
> 
> When the vehicle is engaged (via /control/control_mode_request) but autoware is not, if the user sets a new goal point, the vehicle gear is automatically changed to DRIVE after the planning is completed.
> 
> Considering autoware is still not engaged at this point, it seems strange for autoware to change the gear.
> 
> Eventually, it could make sense to have the gear changed to PARK while autoware is not engaged (the same way a brake command is sent as long as autoware is not engaged.)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Autoware should not change gear to DRIVE while not engaged.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Gear is changed to DRIVE after planning is finished
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Set goal point without engaging autoware
> 2. check /control/command/gear_cmd topic
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-10-25)

> I think whether this is a bug or not depends on what /autoware/engage means.
> @VRichardJP Just to confirm do you have any issues with changing gear to DRIVE before engaging?

###### @VRichardJP (2022-10-26)

> There is no bug/problem with the current behavior, it is just weird from the user point-of-view. Autoware engage has been split into "autoware engage" and "vehicle engage". So one would expect the vehicle does not follow any autoware command (including gear change) as long as autoware is not engaged. 
> 
> When autoware is not engaged, I think the vehicle behavior should be:
> - push the brake (current behavior)
> - keep the current gear (not current behavior)
> 

###### @xmfcx (2022-12-13)

> We should add this to documentation or link existing documentation here.

###### @brkay54 (2022-12-21)

> @VRichardJP I agree with you, created PR to send current gear if autoware is not engaged. Please check the PR, let me know if it solves your problem.

###### @VRichardJP (2022-12-24)

> I see you subscribe to the current command and send it back when the vehicle is not engaged. 
> 
> Even though it does exactly the same, what if we don't simply send `GearCommand::NONE`? If `NONE` is a valid value, we can understand it as "no command". In other words "do not change gear".
> 
> Then of course, it is up to the vehicle interface to interpret `NONE` value correctly.

###### @brkay54 (2022-12-24)

> After thinking about it, I am not sure about sending current gear if vehicle in Autonomous Mode and autoware is not engaged. I think, if vehicle's gate mode is ::AUTO and autoware is not engaged, vehicle_cmd_gate should send GearCommand::PARK.
> 
> For the situation you mentioned, vehicle_cmd_gate is listening the commands from autoware because current gate is AUTO. If current gate is auto, autoware should send the cmds if it is engaged. But if it is not engaged, we should send proper cmds  until autoware is engaged. In this time (i think) vehicle's gear should be PARK in AUTO gate until autoware engaged, it will be more safely. What do you think?
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2022-12-25)

> From the user point-of-view, I think both options are fine:
> - send brake only (no gear change)
> - or send brake + parking gear
> 
> The brake + park gear feels like the safer option. 
> 
> However, I am curious what happens if both autoware and the vehicle are engaged almost at the same time. For example∩╝îif vehicle engage is processed slightly before the autoware engage, the gear may change to park, then to drive right after, which would look a bit weird. 
> 
> But maybe it is something that can be handled on vehicle driver side. Maybe simultaneous engage is not really a thing either.
> 
> Up to you ≡ƒÿü
> 

###### @brkay54 (2023-01-10)

> Thank you for your suggestions. Sending park gear may be dangerous in some situations such as disengaging autoware while driving, It will change gear to Park while vehicle is moving. So, I implemented the first option. 

---

> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> With the current implementation of [`get_ground_height`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/4e080d2c05da5b1a0356c1ec16ae3c77676914f7/localization/pose_initializer/src/map_height_fitter/map_height_fitter_core.cpp#L46) , when the user sets the initial pose using Rviz, if the initial pose is not within 1 meter of any map point, the `map_height_fitter` node will fail to estimate its height. Most likely, the initial localization will be wrong.
> 
> That situation typically occurs when the vehicle is located in some garage or building, whose inside has not mapped. Like here:
>  
> ![IMG_20221011_163404](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/195047251-551a5319-2b88-4203-8007-e96aba93fbca.jpg)
> 
> ![IMG_20221011_163505](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/195047264-656b73a8-3414-4917-91e0-85c00e81f067.jpg)
> 
> Likely, the issue would also occur if the 3D map has no ground (I don't know if it is a thing)
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Improve the reliability of the height estimator.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Obviously, the hardcoded 1.0 meter radius search makes the implementation not very flexible. 
> 
> I think that simply increasing the radius search would have some undesirable side effects.
> 
> One simple improvement would be to consider all point within r+1.0 radius, where r is the distance to the closest point. This way we make sure we always find a bunch of points, yet we don't look unecessarily far.
> 
> The only downside I see is that it takes slightly more time, since we explore the map twice (once to find the closest point, another time to find min height within radius r+1.0)
> 
> Any other suggestion?
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Pose height estimation give a "decent" estimation even when there is no map point very close.

**Comments:**

###### @YamatoAndo (2022-10-11)

> > One simple improvement would be to consider all point within r+1.0 radius, where r is the distance to the closest point. This way we make sure we always find a bunch of points, yet we don't look unecessarily far.
> 
> I think it is a good idea!

###### @YamatoAndo (2022-10-11)

> > The only downside I see is that it takes slightly more time, since we explore the map twice (once to find the closest point, another time to find min height within radius r+1.0)
> 
> I think it is not problem if we explore the map twice, since dynamic map loading will be implemented soon and the area where the map is loaded will be smaller than before.
> https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2812

###### @isamu-takagi (2022-10-12)

> @YamatoAndo @VRichardJP 
> I think it is unreliable if there is no ground under the vehicle area. Here is an example. If the ground is sloped or stepped, the radius calculated from the closest point is not helpful. Moreover, the inside of the garage given as an example will give erroneous results if there is a ceiling when measured from the outside. Therefore, initialization results cannot be guaranteed at locations where the ground is not measured. Should we have a way to manually specify the height?
> 
> ![map-height-fit](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43976882/195343919-46b4936b-64c4-4f43-a215-300752a09ca8.png)
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2022-10-12)

> I totally understand the proposed change is not perfect, but I still think it is better than the current implementation. 
> 
> In particular, I don't think there is a case where it perform worse than the current implementation. Typically, for both examples you provided, there is no point within a 1 meter radius, so the returned height would be whatever Z value is currently stored in the input pose (most likely wrong?)

###### @isamu-takagi (2022-10-12)

> Ah, I see. Both the old and new logic fail in these cases, but the new one improves some cases.

- **Labels:**

> 
> ### Description
>

> ```

> ```
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Memory consumption(RSS) of the process to which trajectory follower node belongs falls within a certain amount.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Memory consumption(RSS) of the process to which trajectory follower node belongs falls within a certain amount.
> Actual behavior:
> The memory consumption of the process continuously increases up to over 1GBytes as below.  
> ![chart](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32567894/195046671-f30b33ec-cb1f-43bd-b3eb-8d39d981a0a1.png)
> 
>

>

>     ```
>     humble-20220915-amd64:           00e518e86ad3f9a38378f6ab28db48fecce69b75
>     ```  
>     To measure the memory consumption only of the process to which the trajectory follower belongs, you should modify the launch file to contain the trajectory follower node independently in a component container.

> 
>  
> 4. Monitor the memory consumption of the separated component container.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> OS: Ubuntu 22.04 + Docker environment  
> ROS2: Humble included in the docker image   humble-20220915-amd64  
> Autoware: the one in the docker image above.  
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> It seems to be caused by some C++ code of the trajectory follower.  
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> None

###### @VRichardJP (2022-10-13)

> Sorry to jump in.
> By looking at [`csc_matrix` implementation](https://github.com/osqp/osqp/blob/master/src/cs.c#L12), the memory leak seems simple to explain from your valgrind logs:
> - `csc_matrix()` allocate new memory, which should be freed by the user
> - in [`initializeProblem()`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/f234a7d9ae044e0f53a3679060dad08aab5ec90e/common/osqp_interface/src/osqp_interface.cpp#L264), the `csc_matrix()` function is called twice to overwrite `m_data->P` and `m_data->A` pointers, so any data that was previously held by those pointers is now leaking.
> 
> Therefore, adding a `if(m_data->P) free(m_data->P)` before the pointer override should solve the issue. It also means the P and A matrix should be freed when m_data is deleted aswell (but maybe it's only at the end of the program so not a big deal).

###### @maxime-clem (2022-10-13)

> Thanks a lot @VRichardJP for finding the cause of the issue.
> I will prepare a PR with the fix you suggested.

### #2044 — Using a de-grounded point cloud for NDT matching gives a more reasonable match score

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-10-11  |  **Closed:** 2023-01-10  |  **Author:** @cyn-liu
- **Labels:** priority:high, component:localization
- **Comments:** 11  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/2044

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Autoware uses NDT matching for localization. The NDT input point cloud contains ground, which is less helpful for localization, and the ground is very similar in many locations, so the ground point cloud contributes a non-negligible score in NDT matching, resulting in a still high NDT score when localization is lost, so using a de-grounded point cloud in NDT matching for localization may achieve better results.
> 
> Using bag1 for point cloud matching, both the point cloud with ground and the point cloud without ground have high matching scores when the localization is successful.
> The following are the test videos:
> [bag1: Positioning success - NDT input point cloud with ground](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Sg411Y7oc/?vd_source=1a0865e27a7bbd9e74e940639d66bbb7)
> [bag1: Positioning success - NDT input without ground point cloud](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Ve4y1q7Pt/?vd_source=1a0865e27a7bbd9e74e940639d66bbb7)
> The following is a comparison of the NDT matching scores with and without ground point clouds:
> ![σ¢╛τëç](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/104069308/195001701-9260b2a8-bc69-42f8-90bf-fe799976d1d9.png)
> 
> Using bag2 for point cloud matching, both the point cloud with ground and the point cloud without ground have high matching scores when the localization is successful.
> The following are the test videos:
> [bag2: Positioning success - NDT input point cloud with ground](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1gT411N7QM/?vd_source=1a0865e27a7bbd9e74e940639d66bbb7)
> [bag2: Positioning success - NDT input without ground point cloud](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1yG4y1H7wv/?vd_source=1a0865e27a7bbd9e74e940639d66bbb7)
> The following is a comparison of the NDT matching scores with and without ground point clouds:
> ![σ¢╛τëç](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/104069308/195002017-1d064713-05f6-4b13-8e74-db23cb3d8a1f.png)
> **This proves that de-grounded point clouds can achieve good localization results.**
> 
> Using bag2 for point cloud matching, the point cloud with ground scored high when the localization failed and the localization failure was not detected in time.
> The following is the test video:
> [bag2: Positioning failure - NDT input point cloud with ground](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1D8411x7wr/?vd_source=1a0865e27a7bbd9e74e940639d66bbb7)
> Using bag2 for point cloud matching, when the localization fails, the point cloud without ground has a very low score and cannot be matched successfully.
> The following is the test video:
> [bag2: Positioning failure - NDT input without ground point cloud](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1nd4y1i7Lc/?vd_source=1a0865e27a7bbd9e74e940639d66bbb7)
> The following is a comparison of the NDT matching scores with and without ground point clouds:
> ![σ¢╛τëç](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/104069308/195003870-243a66b8-d150-43b3-be4b-d594f681005d.png)
> 
> **This demonstrates that using a de-grounded point cloud for NDT matching yields a more reasonable score, as well as a faster assessment of whether localization is lost.**
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> NDT matching using de-grounded point clouds.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> NDT matching using de-grounded point clouds.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> The ground is removed from the original point cloud, and then pre-processing operations such as downsampling are performed on the ground-removed point cloud.

**Comments:**

###### @YamatoAndo (2022-10-11)

> @cyn-liu Thanks for the suggestion.
> I thought it was problematic that the score is still high when the localization is lost, because it could be matched with the ground point clouds.
> 
> However, if the ground point clouds is removed, the height constraint may be lost.
> So, how about dividing the score into the following two categories?
> πâ╗The score with de-grounded point clouds
> πâ╗The score with only ground point clouds
> 

###### @wjxjmj (2022-10-11)

> > @cyn-liu Thanks for the suggestion. I thought it was problematic that the score is still high when the localization is lost, because it could be matched with the ground point clouds.
> > 
> > However, if the ground point clouds is removed, the height constraint may be lost. So, how about dividing the score into the following two categories? πâ╗The score with de-grounded point clouds πâ╗The score with only ground point clouds
> 
> By height constraint do you mean the altitude of the vehicle (z information in pos)?
> 
> In the simulation, although NDT provides z information and EKF filters it using method [updateSimple1DFilters](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/d714775cc3a930712ea92c5ac86e0789e3929319/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_localizer.cpp#L705) (separately from x and y information), z information seems to be of any practical use. Beside, as shown in [map_height_fitter_core.cpp](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/767e76551e8e23e6e02796cc1b4fdd9f2e6b3546/localization/pose_initializer/src/map_height_fitter/map_height_fitter_core.cpp#L46), z information can be evaluated only using the map's information. Moreover, the potential loss of Z information does not appear to be a problem at this time.
> 
> Can you please explain futher about the height constraint?

###### @YamatoAndo (2022-10-11)

> > By height constraint do you mean the altitude of the vehicle (z information in pos)?
> 
> Yes, correct.
> 
> 
> > In the simulation, although NDT provides z information and EKF filters it using method [updateSimple1DFilters](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/d714775cc3a930712ea92c5ac86e0789e3929319/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_localizer.cpp#L705) (separately from x and y information), z information seems to be of any practical use. Beside, as shown in [map_height_fitter_core.cpp](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/767e76551e8e23e6e02796cc1b4fdd9f2e6b3546/localization/pose_initializer/src/map_height_fitter/map_height_fitter_core.cpp#L46), z information can be evaluated only using the map's information. Moreover, the potential loss of Z information does not appear to be a problem at this time.
> 
> Regardless of whether the z information is used or not for other nodes, the z information must also be properly matched since the NDT scan matching is performed in 3D coordinate.
> 

###### @wjxjmj (2022-10-12)

> > > By height constraint do you mean the altitude of the vehicle (z information in pos)?
> > 
> > Yes, correct.
> > 
> > > In the simulation, although NDT provides z information and EKF filters it using method [updateSimple1DFilters](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/d714775cc3a930712ea92c5ac86e0789e3929319/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_localizer.cpp#L705) (separately from x and y information), z information seems to be of any practical use. Beside, as shown in [map_height_fitter_core.cpp](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/767e76551e8e23e6e02796cc1b4fdd9f2e6b3546/localization/pose_initializer/src/map_height_fitter/map_height_fitter_core.cpp#L46), z information can be evaluated only using the map's information. Moreover, the potential loss of Z information does not appear to be a problem at this time.
> > 
> > Regardless of whether the z information is used or not for other nodes, the z information must also be properly matched since the NDT scan matching is performed in 3D coordinate.
> 
> In most senario, point clouds in the environment are sufficient to provide z information.
> ![Fig.1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17843891/195331447-eb6626b8-623e-462c-9bc5-5e9d77472ab1.png)
> The difference of z information with and without ground points, as shown in the above figure, is not significant. In this figure, z information are collected from these two simulation:
> [bag1: Positioning success - NDT input point cloud with ground](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Sg411Y7oc/?vd_source=1a0865e27a7bbd9e74e940639d66bbb7)
> [bag1: Positioning success - NDT input without ground point cloud](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Ve4y1q7Pt/?vd_source=1a0865e27a7bbd9e74e940639d66bbb7). 
>  It is shown that de-grounded points can also provides acceptable z information.

###### @kminoda (2022-10-13)

> Thanks @wjxjmj, the result you've shared is interesting. Seems the difference is around 10-20 cm?
> 
> Since the current Autoware design is dependent on accurate 6-DoF pose estimation, we should discuss from the perspective of perception & planning modules in deciding whether this relatively-inaccurate z estimation is acceptable or not. Just a quick thought, but it would affect the followings:
> - map-based detection for traffic light recognition (perception)
> - compare map filter for obstacle segmentation (perception)
> 
> IMHO we can consider removing ground information from LiDAR scan if we can guarantee that the estimation difference would not affect the other modules. But unless so, I think it is better to adopt an alternative (more conservative) idea for now, e.g. [the idea from @.YamatoAndo above](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2044#issuecomment-1274173597).

###### @cyn-liu (2022-10-19)

> > Thanks @wjxjmj, the result you've shared is interesting. Seems the difference is around 10-20 cm?
> > 
> YES.
> 
> >I think it is better to adopt an alternative (more conservative) idea for now, e.g. [the idea from @.YamatoAndo above](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2044#issuecomment-1274173597).
> 
> We have discussed the approach proposed by @.YamatoAndo above, but since the NDT matching operation of the localization module is the most time consuming in general, it is likely to be computationally costly to use two types of point clouds for NDT matching.
> 
> Is NDT matching using ground point clouds just to get z? But de-ground point clouds matching can also get a similar z. Generally the z obtained by NDT matching is the ground height of the point cloud map at current location, and we find that the accuracy of the height information provided by the point cloud map is poor.
> 
> In addition, experiments must be done to prove that using both de-grounded and ground point clouds for NDT matching, to ensure that the localization module works well.

###### @kminoda (2022-10-19)

> @cyn-liu 
> His proposal does NOT mean to perform NDT scan matching twice, but to perform NDT scan matching as it is right now and instead add two new metrics (alternative to `transform_probability`) based on de-grounding idea you've proposed.
> 
> So to sum up, there are two ideas came up so far.
> - Idea 1. de-grounding LiDAR scan (from @.wjxjmj)
> - Idea 2. adding new de-grounded metric (from @.cyn-liu)
> 
> For the idea 1, I guess the point is that removing the ground pointclouds from LiDAR scan may work on some environment, but not on the other environment. To further discuss this idea, I would propose
> - to share data (like @wjxjmj posted [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/2044#issuecomment-1276029754)) in various environments, including feature-rich urban area or feature-less rural area (we would also like to work on this, but not sure when we will be available for this)
> - to discuss whether the impact on the localization accuracy is acceptable for perception and planning (especially traffic light recognition and compare map filter, as I posted before)

###### @cyn-liu (2022-10-19)

> What can be determined so far is that the planning module does not use height information and z does not affect the operation of the planning module. 
> The perception module is still open to debate. 

###### @cyn-liu (2022-10-19)

> @kminoda Thanks for your reply∩╝ü
> 
> I think you have some misunderstanding about our issue, our point is that using the de-grounded point cloud for NDT matching gives a more accurate score and enables faster and more accurate detection of localization failure.
> 
> After your proposal, we also found that whether the accuracy of the localization height has an acceptable impact on the perception module is the next issue to be considered.
> 
> After your explanation, we are more confused about YamatoAndo's IDEA, what does dividing the score into the following two categories mean??? How to get the matching score for the de-grounded point cloud and the matching score for the ground-only point cloud if it does not match twice???

###### @kminoda (2022-10-19)

> @cyn-liu Thank you for the response! We agree that we should at least discuss the impact on perception module.
> 
> > How to get the matching score for the de-grounded point cloud and the matching score for the ground-only point cloud if it does not match twice???
> 
> I think this is also open question, but I would say that one possible (and also the most simple) way would be to
> - separate LiDAR scan into ground and non-ground
> - NDT performs scan matching with concatenated scan (= ground + non-ground = raw LiDAR scan)
> - after this, we calculate 
>   - 1. `transform_probability` for ground LiDAR scan and pointcloud map
>   - 2. `transform_probability` for non-ground LiDAR scan and pointcloud map

###### @xmfcx (2022-11-15)

> @cyn-liu will create a PR soon.

### #1994 — lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm not found when Autoware is sourced

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-30  |  **Closed:** 2022-09-30  |  **Author:** @mitsudome-r
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1994

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When you install Autoware with the [official instruction](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/installation/autoware/source-installation/) and source Autoware, it outputs the following error:
> ```
> $ source install/setup.bash 
> not found: "/home/mitsudome-r/autoware.universe/install/lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm/share/lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm/local_setup.bash"
> not found: "/home/mitsudome-r/autoware.universe/install/lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm_nodes/share/lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm_nodes/local_setup.bash"
> ```
> 
> > 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Autoware does not output error when user runs the `source` command
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Autoware outputs error when user runs the `source` command
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Install [Autoware](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/installation/autoware/source-installation)
> 2. run `source ~/autoware/install/setup.bash`
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS Humble
> - Autoware: main branch
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> This is caused by package not creating setup scripts when DOWNLOAD_ARTIFACTS is not set when a user builds Autoware  with `colcon build`.
> 
> This can be fixed by making sure that ament_auto_package() function is run regardless of the flag in the CMakeLists.txt of lidar_apollo_tvm packages.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/6a6532b625ac69c6e6c102ff9fb16cba0a56b0a5/perception/lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm/CMakeLists.txt#L73-L75
>

> 
> _No response_

### #1988 — Investigate `lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm` detection quality

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-29  |  **Closed:** 2022-11-15  |  **Author:** @ambroise-arm
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:perception
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1988

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I have tested the TVM package replacing the TRT package in the [rosbag demo](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/rosbag-replay-simulation/) as part of the PR: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1181#issuecomment-1259269257. And the quality of the detection wasn't as good as the detection from the TRT package, at least visually. Some cars were not detected, the lines and circles which indicate the velocity (or planned trajectory, I'm not sure) were wrong, at least on parked vehicles. And the type of detected vehicles might be wrong, it would need to be checked.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Get the detection quality of the TVM package on par with the TRT package.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> There are multiple possible causes for the difference:
> 
> - The TVM version of the package is derived from an [old version from TierIV](https://github.com/tier4/lidar_instance_segmentation_tvm); I expect the TRT version in this repository is more recent
> - The neural network may have been updated since then; trained differently/better
> - The port may have introduced issues/bugs
> - The parameters may not be correct or not all there
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] confirm and document the issue
> - [x] find the cause(s)
> - [x] update the `lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm*` packages and/or the [neural network](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/modelzoo/tree/master/perception/lidar_obstacle_detection/baidu_cnn/onnx_bcnn) in use, depending on what is necessary

**Comments:**

###### @angry-crab (2022-10-17)

> #1880 has to be merge first. 

###### @angry-crab (2022-10-17)

> ![err](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93699235/196108193-27a1b849-af84-4c85-aba3-16ec0f3a4466.png)
> ![err_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93699235/196109427-97564a84-71d0-4a44-a9ac-85d70dbe9a2c.png)
> 
> Issue confirmed. There are quite a lot of false positive detections. This is the output of `detected_object_feature_remover`. And it seems that all of the objects are removed by other filters.

###### @angry-crab (2022-10-17)

> According to @yukkysaito san, the weights have been update.
> @ambroise-arm I see that the current pipeline only supports `onnx` files. However, `lidar_apollo_segmentation` is using `caffe` model. Are we planning to support other types of model in the future? Or shall we convert it to `onnx` format? 

###### @angry-crab (2022-10-18)

> Converting to `onnx` format seems better since `caffe` operations are not fully supported and will probably be removed in the near future. 
> https://discuss.tvm.apache.org/t/caffe2-frontend-support-is-being-dropped-to-unblock-pytorch-update/12442

###### @ambroise-arm (2022-10-18)

> @angry-crab I don't think the Autoware pipeline for tvm only supports onnx, and other formats could be used. It is really down to what TVM supports. If caffe support is dropped in TVM, then I agree that it can't be used as is and needs to be converted.

###### @angry-crab (2022-10-20)

> To convert `caffe` models into `onnx`, this might be a good choise. 
> https://hub.docker.com/_/microsoft-windowscamerateam-onnxconverter

###### @ambroise-arm (2022-10-26)

> I couldn't convert the current caffemodel files with the microsoft tool, it complains about the "Slice" layer.
> I've also tried to use small tools like https://github.com/asiryan/caffe2onnx, which clains to support "Slice", but there is a "Silence" layer in the network that isn't supported.

###### @angry-crab (2022-10-31)

> > I couldn't convert the current caffemodel files with the microsoft tool, it complains about the "Slice" layer. I've also tried to use small tools like https://github.com/asiryan/caffe2onnx, which clains to support "Slice", but there is a "Silence" layer in the network that isn't supported.
> 
> ![apollo](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93699235/198950731-0f0fa10c-e606-43f8-a67f-b61af70cdb19.png)
> 
> ![apollo_tvm_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93699235/198956386-0a6d2198-a4e7-4896-a7a0-f20c1f56d9e0.png)
> 
> 
> I got it work using the converted model. It looks good. `caffemodel` file contains weights while `prototxt` file describes the structure of network, which does not have `Slice` and `Silence` layers.

### #1959 — `signal_processing` tests rely on uninitialized variable

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-27  |  **Closed:** 2022-10-04  |  **Author:** @ambroise-arm
- **Labels:** type:bug, type:arm64
- **Comments:** 10  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1959

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The low pass filter unit test of the `signal_processing` package fails often on Arm platforms.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The unit test passes consistently.
> There are no uninitialized variables.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> I see a failure rate of the unit test above 50%.
> 
> Example failure output:
> ```
> 1: [ RUN      ] lowpass_filter_twist.filter
> 1: /home/user/autoware/src/universe/autoware.universe/common/signal_processing/test/src/lowpass_filter_test.cpp:44: Failure
> 1: The difference between filtered_twist->linear.y and 0.0 is 7.1114927535527936e+197, which exceeds epsilon, where
> 1: filtered_twist->linear.y evaluates to -7.1114927535527936e+197,
> 1: 0.0 evaluates to 0, and
> 1: epsilon evaluates to 9.9999999999999995e-07.
> 1: [  FAILED  ] lowpass_filter_twist.filter (0 ms)
> 1: [----------] 1 test from lowpass_filter_twist (0 ms total)
> ```
> ---
> 
> Additionally, when building the package with `--cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`, the unit test fails consistently on both x86 and arm with:
> ```
> 1: [ RUN      ] lowpass_filter_1d.filter
> 1: test_signal_processing: /usr/include/boost/optional/optional.hpp:1207: boost::optional<T>::reference_type boost::optional<T>::get() [with T = double; boost::optional<T>::reference_type = double&]: Assertion `this->is_initialized()' failed.
> 1: -- run_test.py: return code -6
> ```
> Which highlights that the package relies on uninitialized `optional` variable.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Run `colcon test --packages-select signal_processing` on an arm64 platform a few times in a row. 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The `LowpassFilterTwist` class has a `x_` member variable of type `boost::optional<geometry_msgs::msg::Twist>`, which is not initialized. And the unit test expects the unitialized value to evaluate 0, which is not always the case.
> Interestingly, it seems to consistently pass on x86.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> Simply default-initializing the variable in question is not enough as the unit test expects it to be uninitialized afterwards.
> Packages that make use of this would need to be checked to see what they rely on and what they expect.
> 
> **Question**: because the issue is shown explicitly when compiling with `Debug`, would it make sense to have that in CI in addition to the currently-tested `Release`?

### #1956 — `obstacle_avoidance_planner::generateOptimizedTrajectory` sometimes produce NaN filled trajectories

> 
> ### Description
> 
> While debugging `obstacle_avoidance_planner`, I observed that the output of `obstacle_avoidance_planner::generateOptimizedTrajectory` contains sometimes NaN values:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/dd190a35f73c9ddd2b9b3a2533add63ae705ab85/planning/obstacle_avoidance_planner/src/node.cpp#L921
> 
> I couldn't find what exactly produce the NaNs, but when it does, the module crashes a bit further because of some data validation deeper down:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/dd190a35f73c9ddd2b9b3a2533add63ae705ab85/planning/obstacle_avoidance_planner/src/node.cpp#L1368
> 
> I first thought I could easily get rid of that issue by simply removing the NaN values, but actually the generated trajectories are filleds with NaNs, and no point is left after the process, leading the planner not to publish any path (or publishing empty ones, but in any case, the vehicle does not seem to generate any new path and stop at the end of the old one.)
> 
> When this happens, I also tried to simply call `resetPrevOptimization` to force the module to re-generate the trajectory from scratch. But it always end up generating NaN-filles trajectories.
> 
> I don't have any rosbag or lanelet to provide. But on my vehicle, this problem would appear very easily with the default configuration (maybe just with `enable_obstacle_avoidance=true`). 
> I am not sure, but it seems to happen most in intersections, when the vehicle has to turn.

### #1942 — Static path planning with optimization

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-22  |  **Closed:** 2022-12-04  |  **Author:** @takayuki5168
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1942

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, the on-line path planning with optimization realizes
> - smooth curvature
> - footprints inside the drivable area
> 
> However, the on-line path planning has following disadvantages.
> - We don't know the path shape beforehand. We can know it only when the vehicle runs.
> - Sometimes the issue happens with the optimization (e.g. optimization fails), and we notice it when the vehicle runs.
> 
> In order to know that there is no issue on the map with the optimized path, static path planning with optimization is required.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> > In order to know that there is no issue on the map with the optimized path
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Create a script
> - Input: map, start/goal lanelet ids
> - Output: optimized path (and debug message if the optimization succeeded or not)
> 
> This script contains
> - map_loader
>     - to load a lanelet map
> - mission_planner
>     - to navigate a route from start lanelet to goal lanelet
> - obstacle_avoidance_planner
>     - to optimize the path
> as a library.
> 
> Therefore, map_loader, mission_planner, obstacle_avoidance_planner also need to be modified to be called from the script.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> get the optimized path from the lanelet map and start/goal lanelet ids with one script.

**Comments:**

###### @stale (2022-12-03)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-12-04)

> The package for static path planning has been already merged.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2013

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
>

> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.

> 
> ### Description
> 
> Several times today, the obstacle_avoidance_planner crashed in my vehicle. With GDB, I identified that `full_traj_points` trajectory below is sometimes empty:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e2c5eda7524ff11bab791f9c6ac19c884a3c314d/planning/obstacle_avoidance_planner/src/node.cpp#L1355

> I modified the code like so, and the node stopped crashing:

Universe. The compilation process needs to tailor some packages according to your own needs, and ultimately ensure that Autoware. Universe core link modules can be started normally.

###### @oguzkaganozt (2023-09-26)

###### @greensky0802 (2023-10-09)

> Hi @oguzkaganozt Sorry for the delay. The first step is to fully install JetPack: 5.1.1 for Orin and get the Ubuntu 20.04 system and CUDA 11.4. There is no problem to manually compile the source code of ROS2 Humble in the Ubuntu 20.04, but when manually compiling the source code of Autoware. Universe, it will be prompted that the library is missing. Note that you cannot use rosdep to install the missing dependent library at this time, but manually search for the source code of the dependent library. When downloading, the ROS2 Humble version is preferred, followed by the ROS2 version. After all the missing dependency libraries are compiled and installed, there are still individual packages in the Autoware. Universe that cannot be compiled, such as those related to TVM and yabloc. These packages do not affect the operation of the core link. At present, we have completed the verification on the real vehicle according to the above method.

###### @ito-san (2022-09-22)

> @kasperornmeck 
> #### If you want to build scenario_simulator_v2, please follow the instructions below.
>   1. Add depencies
>      ```console
>      sudo add-apt-repository ppa:kisak/kisak-mesa -y
>      sudo apt install libegl-mesa0 libglfw3-dev -y
>      ```
>   1. Build oneTBB
>       ```console
>       git clone https://github.com/oneapi-src/oneTBB -b v2021.3.0
>       cd ~/oneTBB
>       mkdir build & cd build & cmake -DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=20 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=debug -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++ -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc -DTBB_CPF='ON' -DTBB_TEST=OFF .. & make & sudo make install
>       ```
>   1. Build embree
>       ```console
>       git clone https://github.com/embree/embree -b v3.13.0
>       cd ~/embree
>       mkdir build && cd build && cmake ../ -DEMBREE_ISPC_SUPPORT=OFF && make && sudo make install
>       ```
> 
>    1. Build your workspace
>       ```console
>       cd ~/autoware
>       vcs import src < simulator.repos
>       rosdep install -y --from-paths src --ignore-src --rosdistro $ROS_DISTRO --skip-keys embree
>       MAKEFLAGS=-j3 colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release --parallel-worker 3
>       ```
> #### But you can also use docker container built for arm64 like this.
> 
> ```console
> docker run --rm -it --net host -v /home/autoware/sample_data:/sample_data ghcr.io/ito-san/scenario_simulator_v2:galactic-arm64 ros2 launch scenario_test_runner scenario_test_runner.launch.py scenario:=/sample_data/t4v2.yaml architecture_type:=awf/universe launch_autoware:=false record:=false
> ```

### #1910 — `accel_brake_map_calibrator` does not want to calibrate some values

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2022-09-20  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:vehicle
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1910

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I have been trying to calibrate accel/brake of my vehicle. 
> 
> After many painful attempts with a joystick controller (too sensitive), I have implemented a keyboard based controller, with which I am able to send fixed accel/brake command values (from -1.0 to 1.0). Event after 2 hours of calibration on a mostly straight circuit, the calibration map is far from being finished:
> 
> ![IMG_20220920_160519](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/191247670-30306f55-0428-48f2-a417-82f041ee34f6.jpg)
> 
> In particular, I observed the calibrator tool "refuses" to map some specific values. In my case, the 0.3, -0.3, -0.5 and -0.6 rows are extremelly difficult to get data on (the cursor is almost always red). But it is also true for all the remaining blue/grey squares. On the other hands, all the pink squares were super easy to get, and would only require a few minutes for each (or even seconds for the 0.2 row).
> 
> How come some cells are nearly impossible to map, while some others are super easy? is there any parameter I should adjust? is it because of the default accel/brake map?
> 
> Unfortunatelly, I tested the calibration result in autonomous mode, and autoware is unable to accurately stop at goal position. I have tried to modify the brake_map.csv values by hand and got some improvement, but this is a less than desirable method. At least, it proved me my issue is a calibration issue.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> calibrator tool can map any actuation/speed value
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> some actuation/speed values are nearly impossible to calibrate
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Have my vehicle? (not a Lexus)
> 
> ### Versions
>

###### @VRichardJP (2022-09-21)

> I went through a lot today :)

> @TakaHoribe
> As you suggested, I went for another calibration with the debug logger and checked why the values were rejected. Most data rejection comes from jerk. I drove 3 loops over my calibration course, one with +-0.4, one with +-0.3 and one with +-0.2 values. After the 3 loops, the calibration map looks like this:
> ![calibration_1_loop_0 2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/191518339-64d6c0da-0f21-4e88-bb15-3c8d371baf85.png)
> 
> I went on and inspected the accel/jerk values received by the calibrator, and it's indeed pretty bad (in many case, it just looks like random values between -3.0 and +3.0). So I checked the /vehicle/status/velocity_status speed report, and it is indeed quite jerky. Actually I am surprised the calibrator even accept any of that data.
> 
> The problem with my vehicle is that the /vehicle/status/velocity_status values are based on the vehicle speed feedback from the CAN network, and that speed feedback seems to have 1km/h step increment. In other words, when I accelerate, the speed report is at 0.0, then jumps to 0.277, then to 0.55 and so on. Needless to say it is impossible to compute accelation with such feedback. For some strange reason, it was when the pedal value was at +0.3/-0.3 that this jerk was the strongest (hence the weird calibration map above)
> 
> I think the speed itself is not an issue for the calibrator. The problem is that the calibrator uses that speed to compute acceleration, then jerk. So I had to find another way to get a smooth acceleration value in autoware.
> 
> Interestingly, autoware produces no good acceleration report. The closest thing I found is /localization/acceleration, but it is based on EKF output, and EKF basically copies the speed value from my inaccurate speed report. Actually EKF does some smoothing because it takes into account several messages. But when I plot the output /localization/acceleration, it just looks like a slightly smoothened step function.
> 
> Since I have a fairly good IMU, I thought it should be possible to use EKF to update the speed. So I modified the imu_corrector to add some fixed stddev covariance to  the IMU longitudinal_acceleration messages, I added this IMU feedback to EKF (I followed the same approach than pose and twist), and added accelation to the EKF model, so I could update speed like so: vx{k+1} = vx{k} + a{k} * dt. After some noise/stdded tuning, I managed to get a very smooth speed estimation from EKF (in /localization/kinematic_state). 
> 
> Finally, I modified the calibrator to use the kinematic state in place of my inaccurate speed report. And the calibration suddenly became quite easy! In ~45minutes, I managed to map almost everything I wanted (I skipped the -0.7/-0.8 rows because this was like emergency brake). The only part I couldn't map was the 0.0 column (<2.5km/h):
> ![IMG_20220921_164430](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/191519595-ab5457d4-263b-447c-b806-aa98f731b7aa.jpg)
> 
> So I guess my calibration is not bad? Here are the files:
> [brake_map.csv](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/9617127/brake_map.csv)
> [accel_map.csv](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/9617128/accel_map.csv)
> 
> and associated plots:
> ![Figure_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/191520422-2445a227-4999-4408-a78d-f682e4d7a1b7.png)
> ![Figure_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/191520432-7a07ccef-5c60-4e4c-8c62-bc1799f76c93.png)
> 
> Unfortunatelly, when I use this calibration to drive the vehicle autonomously, autoware fails to stop at the goal point, but always pass the goal point and eventually stop with an emergency brake. It is somewhat similar to https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/993, except it is a new vehicle and my other one does not have any issue anymore (:

###### @VRichardJP (2022-09-23)

> I solved the that last issue the same way I solved it in #993:
> - reduced normal.min_accel and normal.min_jerk from 1.0 to 0.4~0.5
> - set speed limit to 1m/s 2 meters from stop point
> - shifted all the values of the first column of the brake_map.csv, essentially adding a +0.1 command offset when speed is <5km/h
> 
> Although it seems to work, the last trick is far from ideal. So the problem comes back to:
> - the calibrator should not assume speed is smooth enough to compute accel and jerk. I believe some more sophisticated filter should do that job, such as EKF
> - Even if speed report is accurate, the calibrator struggle to map any value at low speed. As a consequence, it is difficult to have the vehicle stop precisely at any location.

### #1879 — Align TVM packages with ModelZoo changes

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-15  |  **Closed:** 2022-11-11  |  **Author:** @ambroise-arm
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, priority:high
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1879

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The neural network artifacts built for TVM as part of the [ModelZoo](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/modelzoo) CI are changing in layout. The change has been discussed in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/modelzoo/issues/63 and https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/discussions/2508. The Autoware packages need to align with the change.
> 
> ModelZoo artifacts changed from being held in a single archive to one archive per model/backend combination. It allows users to only download needed archives.
> 
> This task depends on https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/628 being completed first.
> 
> The prebuilt asset rework will be needed for the neural networks added in ModelZoo for https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/908 to be available in Autoware.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Reduce bandwidth usage.
> 
> Have a better versioning of the models.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Change from all models being handled by the "neural_networks_provider" package to models being downloaded by packages that need them.
> 
> Leverage the newly added versioning of the prebuilt models.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Rework prebuilt assets management
> - [x] Model descriptors versioning

**Comments:**

###### @angry-crab (2022-09-28)

> Please correct me if I'm wrong. It seems that the currect ci compiles the tvm library and uploads it. The library will be downloaded when building the package. But these packages only contain inference functionality. To make full use of `tvm` utility, I think it is necessary to create pre and postprocessing operations with `tvm` as well. For example, this [page](https://tvm.apache.org/docs/tutorial/tensor_expr_get_started.html) introduces a simple way to create `tvm operations` which can be optimized further using different `schedule` modules. Therefore, in the near future, I'm think of moving the whole pipeline to `tvm` implementation as opposed to current implementation of c++. Do you think it is necessary or not. If the answer is yes, how should we add corresponding operations to the package? Please let me know you thoughts. 

###### @ambroise-arm (2022-09-28)

> You are correct in the description of the inference functionality.
> 
> Note that I have never used those `tvm operations`, so I don't know how difficult, or how appropriate it would be for what we want to achieve. 
> 
> From my point of view, using `tvm operations` in the pre/post processing steps is not necessary. But my motivation for using TVM is mainly based on portability of the hardware, not so much performance. So I am happy with C++ for pre/post processing, but it would most likely be more performant to use code that can be compiled for a dedicated HW backend.
> Maybe a first step could be benchmarking `lidar_centerpoint` with C++ processing to see if it is acceptable or not.
> 
> If we do choose to use `tvm operations`, it may be worth revisiting the way things get compiled. The `tvm operations` would need to be compiled for the same target backend as the inference, so it may then be interesting to move the compilation of the neural network away from the ModelZoo CI and into the build step of the Autoware package.

###### @ambroise-arm (2022-10-26)

> Second step was not done.

- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:system
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1856

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.

> ### Description
> 
> Currently, there is one MRM behavior (e.g., sudden stop) that can be selected on the hazard condition.
> (MRM: Minimum Risk Maneuver)
>

> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Provide a mechanism to select multiple MRM behaviors depending on the hazard state.

> 
> Create intermediate nodes that control MRM behavior, and the emergency handler activates each node according to the hazard state.
> MRM behaviors can be added by creating new intermediate nodes.

> 
> ### Definition of done

> - [ ] Emergency stop can be selected for MRM behavior using the above mechanism as before
> - [ ] Comfortable stop can be selected for MRM behavior using the above mechanism
> 
> Other MRM behaviors will be added in the future.

### #1854 — `behavior_path_planner` do not consistently expand the drivable area

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-13  |  **Closed:** 2022-10-25  |  **Author:** @maxime-clem
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1854

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The `behavior_path_planner` generates the drivable area which can be expanded to the left or right using the following parameters. 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/a4078bdf374fc617f5be531e50e892aefbbc53e0/launch/tier4_planning_launch/config/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning/behavior_path_planner/lane_following/lane_following.param.yaml#L4-L6
> 
> This functionality works most of the time but there are situations when the drivable area is not expanded.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The drivable area is always expanded.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The drivable area is not expanded when an obstacle is near the ego path.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1 - Update parameters to expand the drivable area.
> 2  - Plan a path and observe the drivable area in rviz.
>       - Type: `DrivableArea`
>       - Topic: `/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning/path`
>       - Recommended color scheme: `costmap`.
> 3 - Add an obstacle near the path and observe the drivable area no longer being expanded.
> 
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48479081/188827600-4590d028-34fd-4d2f-9db0-58f80b161c5b.mp4
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/1759#issuecomment-1240550714
> > Static expansion of drivable area is only implemented in lane_following for now.
> By implementing it in other modules, you can use the static expansion in any module.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-09-27)

> @maxime-clem Are you planning to create a PR to fix this issue?

###### @maxime-clem (2022-09-27)

> I will make a PR this week.

### #1850 — endless recursion issue in RouteHandler

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-13  |  **Closed:** 2022-10-05  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1850

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I am using the following lanelet route:
> ![Capture-min](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/189803764-d2bcb0ca-d89b-4fef-a4a5-e2f0bea2b6c5.PNG)
> 
> The vehicle starts from the blue area, makes a clockwise loop and comes back to the blue area in the opposite direction. Half-way in the loop, I see the planning container crashes because RouteHandler gets stuck in an endless recursion [getRightMostLinestring](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e28c1698420c4b13b836f1a04f96591342e24685/planning/route_handler/src/route_handler.cpp#L961) -> [getLeftMostLinestring](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e28c1698420c4b13b836f1a04f96591342e24685/planning/route_handler/src/route_handler.cpp#L988) -> [getRightMostLinestring](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e28c1698420c4b13b836f1a04f96591342e24685/planning/route_handler/src/route_handler.cpp#L961) -> ...
> 
> The particularity of my lanelet2 map is that there are 2 lanelets inside the blue area, sharing the same linestrings but going opposite directions (one for the start and one for the end). So if you think about it, both lanelets are the left and right neighbor of each other... so if the code is not careful, it is easy to get stuck in an endless recursion loop, searching for the most left/right something of one of the 2 lanelets.
> 
> I know one way to fix that is not to share the linestring (or use 'one_way'=false attribute?). But couldn't we make the code more robust?
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> planner does not crash
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> endless recursion
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. have 2 opposite lanelets sharing same linestring
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2022-09-13)

> @VRichardJP
> The way the function is written is intended for the user to properly follow the lanelet2 format, so it that any "bug" related to library can be traceback to the library or if the users doesn't follow the proper convention, then we can also easily trace the issue. 
> 
> However, it is also true that the code should be more robust. So we can think of some way to address this issue.
> 
> Can you share the lanelet and pcd to us so that we can take a look a look and use them for testing?
>  

###### @VRichardJP (2022-09-13)

> Here is the lanelet map I used (changed to .txt to upload on github):
> [lanelet2_map.txt](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/9554161/lanelet2_map.txt)
> 
> 

###### @NorahXiong (2022-09-20)

> I've seen a similar discussion [here](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2600#discussion-4173579).
> Maybe you should set the "one_way" tag as "no".
> You can try this [file](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/9604750/one_way.zip).
> 
> 

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-09-20)

> I believe current planner doesn't support bi-directional lanes. However, as a work around, you can create lanes in opposite direction that does **not** share linestrings.

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2022-09-22)

> @VRichardJP 
> Could you check the recursion issue status.
> This PR (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1901) should be able  to solve them.

###### @xmfcx (2022-10-04)

> @VRichardJP can you check if https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1901 solves this issue?

###### @VRichardJP (2022-10-05)

> I checked with the simulator, it seems to be fixed now.

### #1813 — Change shift to park when vehicle stops

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-08  |  **Closed:** 2022-09-13  |  **Author:** @lilyildiz
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1813

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In autoware.universe, shift does not change when vehicle stopped. After initialized vehicle, vehicle's shift is parking until goal_position set. However, when vehicle arrived to goal, autoware keeps shift in drive.
> 
> [Related discussion](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/discussions/2778)
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Change shift to `GearCommand::PARK` when vehicle stops.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Subscribe to ` /autoware/state` in `shift_decider` node and change the shift to `GearCommand::PARK` when vehicle arrives to the goal position.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Subscribe to `/autoware/state` in `shift_decider.cpp`
> - [ ] Change the shift to `GearCommand::PARK`  in  `shift_decider.cpp` when `AutowareState::ARRIVED_GOAL` is received

---

### #1812 — The paths of behavior module and avoidance module are separated when the "enable_avoidance_over_opposite_direction" is false

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-08  |  **Closed:** 2022-09-09  |  **Author:** @shulanbushangshu
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1812

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The paths of behavior module and avoidance module are separated when the "enable_avoidance_over_opposite_direction" is false.The drivable area can't use the "same_direction" lanes when "enable_avoidance_over_same_direction" is true. The drivable area is restricted to the current Lanes.
> The simulation is shown as below:
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2022-09-08 16-01-05](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102840938/189089461-0f6f42cc-35bb-409d-819d-e7155d7d441b.png)
> 
> 
> 
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> 1.When "enable_avoidance_over_opposite_direction" is false, if the drivable area can't use the "same_direction" lanes by design, the avoidance behavior should not happen. 
> 2.When "enable_avoidance_over_opposite_direction" is false,if the drivable area can use the "same_direction" lanes by design, the drivable area should be changed.
> The paths of behavior module and avoidance module should not be separated .
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> When "enable_avoidance_over_opposite_direction" is false,  the drivable area can't use the "same_direction" lanes.
> The paths of behavior module and avoidance module are separated .
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1.Set "enable_avoidance_over_opposite_direction" to false
> 2.Start autoware planning simulator
> 3. Set initial position and gobal position;
> 4.Set obstacle(like car or bus)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> 1.OS: Ubuntun 20.04
> 2.ROS2: Galactic
> 3.Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2022-09-08)

> Sorry for the mistake, I have made to PR to solve this issue.

###### @shulanbushangshu (2022-09-09)

> @zulfaqar-azmi-t4
> Yes,the bug is fixed and I will close the issue.

### #1797 — Separate point cloud container into a different launch file

### #1784 — Timeout happens at getTransform() in SurroundObstacleCheckerNode, and DynamicObject is not used to find surroud objects

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-05  |  **Closed:** 2023-03-15  |  **Author:** @takeshi-iwanari
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1784

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> - Where the issue happens: [SurroundObstacleCheckerNode::getNearestObstacleByDynamicObject()](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/3cae6eca45b36b75c696780e67aabaee05330629/planning/surround_obstacle_checker/src/node.cpp#L367)
> - Timeout happens when calling `getTransform()` to get a transform ("map" -> "base_link")
> - `getNearestObstacleByDynamicObject()` returns NULL and `nearest_object` becomes NULL. As a result, only `nearest_pointcloud` is used to judge `isStopRequired()` .
> - Once the issue happens, timeout always occurs at every call
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> - Timeout should not happen at `getTransform()`, and both `nearest_object` and `nearest_pointcloud` should be valid
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> - Timeout happens 10 / 10, when playing rosbag with `-r 1.0`
> - Timeout happens 1 / 10, when playing rosbag with `-r 0.2`
> - (It looks this is a timing-dependent problem)
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> - Follow [the Rosbag replay simulation tutorial](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/rosbag-replay-simulation/)
>   - Do not add `-r 0.2` when playing rosbag
>   - Add log, so that we can check if timeout happens
>     - where to modify: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/3cae6eca45b36b75c696780e67aabaee05330629/planning/surround_obstacle_checker/src/node.cpp#L376
> 
>     ```
>       if (!transform_stamped) {
>         RCLCPP_WARN(this->get_logger(), "Timeout getNearestObstacleByDynamicObject");   // Added
>         return {};
>       }
>     ```
> - You'll see "`Timeout getNearestObstacleByDynamicObject`" log on a terminal once every 500msec
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 20.04 (5.15.0-46-generic)
> - ROS2: Galactic
> - Autoware: b1e2f6ef5982ccbe9434bff49397b2783713cb98
> - Autoware.Universe: 3cae6eca45b36b75c696780e67aabaee05330629
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> - In short, timeout setting (= 500msec) is too long. While waiting at `getTransform()` on a timer callback, an executor cannot run a subscription callback and the node cannot receive a new topic.
> - Callbacks in SurroundObstacleChecker
>   - SurroundObstacleChecker has the following callbacks (MultiThreadedExecutor. All callbacks belong to the same callback group)
>     - [onDynamicObjects Calback](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/3cae6eca45b36b75c696780e67aabaee05330629/planning/surround_obstacle_checker/src/node.cpp#L295)
>       - Callback to subscribe `/objects` topic
>     - [100msec Timer Callback](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/3cae6eca45b36b75c696780e67aabaee05330629/planning/surround_obstacle_checker/src/node.cpp#L196)
>       - Call `getNearestObstacle()` and judge if `isStopRequired()`
>       - In `getNearestObstacle()` , `getTransform()` is called using subscribed `/objects` information
>       - Timeout setting = 500msec at `getTransform()`
>     - (Other callbacks are omitted in this explanation)
> 
> - How the issue happens
>   1. It looks, `getTransform()` is called with the future time (around 1 sec later) af the first call. As a result, it waits for 500msec
>       - I confirmed this by comparing `object_ptr_->header.stamp` and "`ros2 run tf2_ros tf2_echo map base_link`"
>   2. While waiting 500msec, new `/objects` topics with latest time are published. However, `onDynamicObjects()` cannot wake-up
>       - I confirmed this by adding log at the top of `onDynamicObjects()` and it's not called
>       - It's probably because the 100msec timer callback is runnig (waiting for 500msec) (*1)
>   3. After 500msec, both the next timer callback and `onDynamicObjects()` callback are ready. However, A timer callback has higher priority than a subscription callback, so the 100msec timer callback will wake-up again and `onDynamicObjects()` callback keeps not running
>       - Reference: https://docs.ros.org/en/galactic/Concepts/About-Executors.html#scheduling-semantics
>   4. `getTransform()` is called with older timestamp contained in older `/objects` msg, but the corresponding transform is not found and it will wait for 500msec again  (*2)
>   5. Go to 2.
> 
> - Possible Solutions
>   - Assign different callback group for onDynamicObjects Calback and 100msec Timer Callback
>     - It may cause another bug in the future, because these functions share variables
>   - Decrease timeout setting from 500msec to 50msec so that `onDynamicObjects()` can wake-up and update `/objects` msg
>     - I confirmed this solved the issue
>     - It can be any as long as less than 100msec
>     - 50msec works to solve this problem, but may not be appropriate for another situatiom
> 
> - Unclear stuffs
>   - *1:  `getTransform()` calls `lookupTransform()` in `buffer.cpp` in ROS2 code. In the code, `sleep_for(10msec)` is called. So, thread switching should happen, but it looks the timer callback occupies the executor
>   - *2: `tf_buffer_` should be able to contain /tf for 10 seconds. So, a transform with older timestamp should be found. It looks `transform_listener` doesn't wake up and cannot update buffer (not yet confirmed)
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @maxime-clem (2022-10-20)

> @piotr-zyskowski-rai do you have any update on this issue ?

###### @piotr-zyskowski-rai (2022-12-05)

> @maxime-clem Sorry for the very late response. @lchojnack  will start to work on this issue after he finishes the current tasks

###### @stale (2023-02-03)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @lchojnack (2023-03-14)

> @takeshi-iwanari 
> I'm really sorry for checking this issue for so long. I cannot reproduce the issue on the latest Autoware.
> Could you please let me know whether the issue appears or doesn't appear anymore?

###### @takeshi-iwanari (2023-03-15)

> @lchojnack 
> Thank you for following up.
> I confirmed the issue doesn't happen with [the latest version (2023/03/15)](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/b93dbc5c3dd5bd497555c5a12a9b2cdd679b5b56).
> 
> Details:
> 
> > i. It looks, 'getTransform()' is called with the future time (around 1 sec later) af the first call. As a result, it waits for 500msec 
> 
> In the past [`object_ptr_->header.stamp`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/b93dbc5c3dd5bd497555c5a12a9b2cdd679b5b56/planning/surround_obstacle_checker/src/node.cpp#L370) was the future time compared to transform map time  and it caused the issue. `object_ptr_->header.stamp` is valid in the latest version and timeout doesn't occur anymore.
>

> ### Purpose
> 
> This is an approach to ensure more system stability and enables developer/operator to get more chance to detect or predict a hazardous event.
> Here is current diagnostic information to be monitored by system_monitor.<br>
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57388357/188095922-24162e2b-297f-4606-86df-f82216979914.png)

> 
> <table>
> <thead>
> <tr>
>   <th>Hardware</th><th>Potential Failure Mode</th><th>Potential Failure Effect</th><th>Potential Causes</th><th>Action Recommended</th><th>New diagnostic Information to be added</th>
> </tr>
> </thead>
> <tbody>
> <tr>
>   <td rowspan=5>Storage</td>

>   <td rowspan=5>Data loss, <br>Read/Write delay</td>
>   <td>Soft error(Transient fault)</td>
>   <td>Observe a CRC error on the storage</td>
>   <td><b>Recovered Error</b></td>
> </tr>
> <tr>
>   <td rowspan=4>High load on communication bandwidth</td>

> <tr>
>   <td>Observe Write data rate</td>
>   <td><b>Write Data Rate</b></td>
> </tr>
> <tr>
>   <td>Observe input/output per second for read</td>

> </tr>
> <tr>
>   <td>Observe input/output per second for write</td>
>   <td><b>Write IOPS</b></td>
> </tr>
> <tr>
>   <td>LAN</td>
>   <td>Error in transferred data</td>

### #1761 — behavior_path_planner generated path outside of drivable area

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-01  |  **Closed:** 2022-12-13  |  **Author:** @beyzanurkaya
- **Labels:** type:bug, priority:high, component:planning
- **Comments:** 26  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1761

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> If you give to EGO a goal pose a bit inclined , the path is still generated without considering of the width and length of EGO. And this generated path is outside the drivable area.
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2022-09-01 10-32-23](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32412808/187857957-b21fd5ea-3edc-4535-b7cb-a8e57e149a42.png)
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2022-09-01 10-34-16](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32412808/187858252-6e998e9d-04b2-4caf-a043-5cdf05e4d950.png)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> If the path to generated is outside the drivable area, the node should not create any path.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> `behavior_path_planner` creates a path even if the path is outside the drivable area.
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2022-09-01 10-34-16](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32412808/187858318-b99c0359-9597-4a64-876d-9476b5ed3904.png)
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Download [1761.zip](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/9469885/1761.zip)
> 2. Change pcd and lanelet2 maps file path in yaml file
> 3. run `ros2 launch scenario_test_runner scenario_test_runner.launch.py sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle \
> scenario:=/scenario/path/1761.yaml \
> architecture_type:=awf/universe launch_rviz:=false launch_autoware:=true`
> 
> 4. Add ` /planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/trajectory` topic in rviz
> 
> 5. When you run the scenario, path occurred outside drivable area.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-09-02)

> @beyzanurkaya Thank you for your report.
> That is because of smooth goal connection in behavior_path_planner.
> https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/#smooth-goal-connection
> 
> behavior_path_planner does not thoroughly consider if the path is inside the lane or not. Sometimes the path from the behavior_path_planner is outside the lanes with a tight right/left turn on a bit narrow road.
> To make the path/trajectory inside the lanes (what we call drivable area) is the role of motion planner (obstacle_avoidance_planner).
> 
> Therefore, IMO, I think no code change is required for the issue. What do you think.

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-09-02)

> If you want, I agree with implementing the function to reject the goal if it's near to the lane boundaries and the angle is weird like in your figure in mission_planner.

###### @beyzanurkaya (2022-09-06)

> I think it makes sense to adding a reject.  because as the vehicle tries to reach this point, a strange trajector occurs at the end of the goal position.

###### @beyzanurkaya (2022-09-06)

> ![Screenshot from 2022-09-06 10-34-20](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32412808/188575837-618dcbed-ccee-4ec8-8176-f5c59ca09bb1.png)

>

> * make this a configurable parameter, or

### #1759 — Turning radius is too short on curves

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-09-01  |  **Closed:** 2022-09-13  |  **Author:** @beyzanurkaya

> ### Checklist
>

> Motion planner output is outside of drivable area.
> 
>
