### #1403 — The topic named `ekf_pose_with_covariance_without_yawbias` contains yaw bias

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-07-22  |  **Closed:** 2022-09-21  |  **Author:** @IshitaTakeshi
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:localization
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1403

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> [ekf_localizer](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/localization/ekf_localizer) publishes a topic `ekf_pose_with_covariance_without_yawbias` but the pose published from this topic contains the yaw bias. 
> 
> The related part in the code is [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_localizer.cpp#L229). `ekf_.getXelement(IDX::YAW)` returns the yaw angle that contains the bias.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Give clear names that do not cause confusion for code readers.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The topic called `ekf_pose_with_covariance_without_yawbias` contains the yaw bias. This causes confusion.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Just read the code. The EKF state contains the yaw angle and its estimated bias as the second and third elements (in the zero-based indices). The topic `ekf_pose_with_covariance_without_yawbias` publishes the yaw angle obtained from the second element without bias correction.
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @IshitaTakeshi (2022-09-21)

> Fixed in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1787

### #1384 — ray_ground_filter can not remove ground points

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-07-20  |  **Closed:** 2022-08-30  |  **Author:** @storrrrrrrrm
- **Labels:** priority:high, component:perception, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 11  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1384

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> test with pointcloud whose frame is not base_link
> 
> when set frame_id to base_link https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/perception/ground_segmentation/src/ray_ground_filter_nodelet.cpp#L62
> 
> it removes ground points correctly
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103425473/179947874-269aeaea-1935-4063-9873-d1c2bce3027f.png)
> 
> when set frame_id to velodyne_top
> it can not remove ground points correctly
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103425473/179951490-983230c6-b365-4120-8a62-8601bac6026b.png)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> remove ground points correctly when start ray_ground_filter with param frame_id set to a value which is not base_link
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> it can not remove ground points correctly if do not transform pointcloud to base_link frame 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> currently there is no a launch file like scan_ground_filter.launch.py in autoware.  i found this issue when writing test program for ground_segmentation.
> 
> if u wanna reproduce this, u can test with a bag whose frame is not base_link, and start ray_ground_filter with frame_id setted same with frame in bag.
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> when compare current_height with general_height_threshold,
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/perception/ground_segmentation/src/ray_ground_filter_nodelet.cpp#L244-L245
> there is an implicit assumption, current_height is height from a fake flat groundπÇé
> 
> however now current_height comes from z. https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/perception/ground_segmentation/src/ray_ground_filter_nodelet.cpp#L223
> 
> so if z is value in base_link frame which is actually on ground, it classify ground points correctlyπÇé if z is value in velodyne_top which is a frame on top  of car, it can not classify correctly.
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> we can add a param like z_offset to tell the height of input pointcloud frame to the flat ground. and refer to z_offset when calculate current_height

### #1375 — Adding NDT reinitalization statement and reinitialization while moving

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2022-07-19  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @ataparlar
- **Labels:** status:stale, component:localization
- **Comments:** 25  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1375

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> NDT is initializes the position once in the beginning while vehicle is motionless. While moving if a topic used by autoware_launch stops streaming and starts streaming again, NDT reinitialization never starts. Eventually, vehicle starts to fly or starts turning around.
> There is no reinitialization statement of NDT in the code. There must be a recovery mechanism for localization.
> 
> [Here](https://youtu.be/MffXnseMeg0) is a video of the issue.
> [https://youtu.be/MffXnseMeg0](https://youtu.be/MffXnseMeg0) 
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Making reinitalization of NDT correctly while moving.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Writing a reinitialization statement to NDT node. 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> This is done when NDT reinitializes itself correctly without flying or turning.

**Comments:**

> I think that this feature will be one of the most important features for Autoware, so we need to discuss the architecture in detail. @mitsudome-r @yukkysaito

###### @cyn-liu (2022-07-20)

> > > what flags are used to monitor localization failure. (my idea is to determine whether the localization fails based on whether score of the NDT match is greater than the threshold value of 2.3 )
> > 
> > We have the [localization_error_monitor](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/localization/localization_error_monitor) node to detect locazation failure using the variance estimated by EKF. How about using this node?
> 
> We believe that it is not accurate to use the pose_with_covariance estimated by the EKF in the localization_error_monitor node to monitor whether the localization fails, because **this variable lacks timeliness.**
> When the NDT score is below 2.3, we consider that the localization has failed at this point, while the ekf covariance is still small (close to 0), and the pose_with_covariance will only change significantly when the car is far from the correct position.
> The following figure is a screenshot of the simulation of the localization module when the point cloud matching fails, and the blue line in the figure is the running track of the car.
> ![σ¢╛τëç](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/104069308/179995859-09cdce1d-b4da-4931-9948-afc6f493c73c.png)
> We recorded two sets of data during the simulation (NDT matching score and pose_with_covariance estimated by EKF ) and plot the curve to observe the trend of the datas (the red horizontal dashed line in the figure is y=2.3). 
> ![σ¢╛τëç](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/104069308/179997476-f11b4073-da8f-4b55-a072-3bb3b9f7971b.png)
> The covariance of x-x and y-y does not change when the matching score starts below 2.3, and these two variables suddenly increase sharply when the car is far from the location. So we believe that using the current EKF estimated variance (pose_with_covariance) is not effective in monitoring the localization failure. The current localization_error_monitor node needs to be modified.

> We did several experiments to plot the graphs using the output results of NDT score and EKF covariance during localization (the red vertical line in the figure below is the time when the NDT score is <2.3 for the first time, and the blue vertical line in the graph is the time when x-x covariance or y-y covariance of EKF is >0.1 for the first time). Assuming that x-x covariance or y-y covariance is greater than 0.1 (the localization error is 0.3m), we consider the localization failure.
> ![σ¢╛τëç](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/104069308/182078317-3ee0705f-08c3-4352-9e2f-41db43b0a348.png)
> ![σ¢╛τëç](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/104069308/182078364-a8ed7aa0-3210-4de0-b328-fefb534eaa74.png)
> As in Figure 1, the two vertical lines are about 3s apart, indicating that the EKF found the localization failure problem 3s later than the NDT.
> As in Figure 2, the two vertical lines are about 4s apart, indicating that the EKF found the localization failure problem 4s later than the NDT.
> The EKF covariance finds localization failure later than NDT score, and several experiments have found that it generally does not exceed 5s. **Although using the EKF output result as the flag for localization failure cannot be very timely in detecting lost localization, if the delay is considered acceptable, the variable can correctly reflect whether the localization has failed.** 
> It should be more timely to use the NDT matching score for determining whether the localization is failure or not.

> > > > Thanks for your reply. Yes our iteration_number is 50. Maybe it's the reason for our results and I will check that. But I think it reacts much, much longer than it should. I also honestly think that NDT score is not a reliable method to detect localization error. What do you think about comparing the position from Gnss with the localization output? Maybe we can get a faster result.
> > > 
> > > 
> > > GNSS usually requires RTK correction to achieve centimeter-level accuracy, but due to occlusion (mountains, shrubs, tall buildings, tunnels, etc.) and poor 4G signal coverage, RTK is always in not-fixed status and the accuracy will drop to meter-level, so it is important to consider a good signal throughout the test road when using GNSS.
> > > My test as below shows, using the integrated GNSS initialization position, **the blue arrows in the figure indicate the position and direction of GNSS**, I found that when NDT matching localization is successful, the position of GNSS may be inaccurate or even deviated from the distance greater than 5 m. Therefore, NDT matching localization is more reliable during vehicle operation at high speed (in scenarios with rich point cloud features). [One of the bag's test results video](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1kU4y1k7xQ/?vd_source=1a0865e27a7bbd9e74e940639d66bbb7)
> > 
> > Hello @cyn-liu . You are not using RTK during this test, are you, or is your RTK connection dropping frequently? Your errors seem a little more than expected. Sometimes incorrect gnss-ins configurations can also cause this error. When we drive using RTK, our error values go up to a maximum of 40-50 cm (we work in an area with a lot of trees). During the general driving, our errors are 2 cm or less. Even when we tested it without using RTK, our error is around 1.5 m maximum. Therefore, we consider it a reliable source.
> 
> We used RTK, the results of this bag test is only an extreme case, in general, the error is not large.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-09-27)

> @cyn-liu Are you still investigating this issue?

###### @cyn-liu (2022-09-27)

> > @cyn-liu Are you still investigating this issue?
> 
> I don't have a better way about which flag to use for faster and more accurate monitoring of whether the positioning is lost or not. 
> The current localization module can already initialize automatically when the vehicle is stopped, but if the vehicle loses its positioning while it is running, the automatic initialization is not possible because the current localization module does not notify other modules to stop the vehicle.
> 
> Now the remaining problem is to achieve automatic initialization of positioning during vehicle operation, and I think the following two things need to be done.
> 
> 1. Select a location loss flag.
> 2. Notify other modules that positioning has been lost and need to make the  vehicle stop.
> 
> For 1, my previous view was to use the NDT matching convergence flag (NDT matching score less than the threshold and NDT iterations greater than the threshold) as the flag for whether the locus is lost or not, because it detects locus loss faster than the pose_covariance of the EKF module, but after discussion, that flag is not the best choice either, so I don't have a better solution yet.
> For 2, in order to make the vehicle stop smoothly, it needs to send the location loss information to the planning module or the control module, and this needs to be discussed and modified with other module developers, so I did not progress.

###### @xmfcx (2022-10-04)

> In the current state of the Autoware,
> 
> The localization nodes report performance,
> 
> Using https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/system/system_error_monitor/config/diagnostic_aggregator/localization.param.yaml#L27 the `system_error_monitor` publishes [HazardStatus](https://github.com/tier4/autoware_auto_msgs/blob/tier4/main/autoware_auto_system_msgs/msg/HazardStatus.idl)
> 
> Then this message is fed to the [emergency_handler](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/system/emergency_handler) to perform the emergency stop.

###### @wjxjmj (2022-10-11)

> > When we test the ndt score, as you said, in general the score falls below 2.3 when ndt deteriorates. However, we noticed that it does not immediately fall below this threshold value every time. [Here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A49Ttdc-c9Y) I shared an example video of this. Even if the NDT fails, you can see here that it does not fall below the NDT score for a long time. Therefore, we have doubts that this score can be used as a reliable source for localization degradation.
> 
> I encountered the same problem in my tests. Theoretically, the NDT score measures how well the point cloud matches the map, and that score should have a significant difference between successful and failed localization. But as the same as the previous disccusion, this was not reflected in the test.
> 
> It was observed that the NDT score remained at a certain level when localization failed, implying that most of the locations  in the map could be partially matched with the point cloud information. This leads me to guess that the problem is due to the ground information.
> 
> Since both map building and vehicle positioning are done on the road, the shape of the vehicle vicinity is similar: they are both  flat. If the ground information is removed during localization, it may be possible to increase the difference in NDT scores between successful and unsuccessful localization.
> 
> I having been working with @cyn-liu to verify the validity of the idea. Considering that the algorithm for removing the ground from the point cloud is already included in autoware, we give a detailed comparative study in this new [issue](2044).
>

> [map.zip](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/9349758/map.zip)
>

###### @raminterpl (2022-08-23)

> Hi @alanmengg  : I confirm above issue. 
> Planning mode is not changing if there is an obstacle in the path of behavior path planner.
> 
> ![MicrosoftTeams-image (10)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/87844531/186131606-1327198f-5585-4799-a92a-65d9ea925789.png)
> 

###### @zulfaqar-azmi-t4 (2022-08-30)

> Hi @alanmengg and @raminterpl 
> Suppose I understand correctly, as lane change is approved while an obstacle is blocking the lane changing path. In that case, you will not be able to continue. 
> 
> Since the behavior path planning uses the behavior tree, only one scene module will be executed at a time. For example, suppose we are currently executing a lane change maneuver. In that case, until the lane-changing process is completed, we will not be able to run other modules. Performing lane change while also avoiding obstacles is currently a limitation that is constantly under discussion internally. And modifying the behavior tree's behavior will take a bit of time for now. 
> 
> Now about the reported scenario, one thing we can do is abort the lane change and only perform the lane changing maneuver as soon as the path is safe. The current universe is able to do so, as shown in the video below.
> 
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93502286/187413754-2ac05792-3d91-45bd-8a34-6b716bab6b13.mp4
> 
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93502286/187414175-4e2db2d4-f3a6-497e-8be6-ece742ee73b7.mp4
> 
> However, there are limitations, for example this scenario over here. In the following scenario, ego vehicle reaches to the point where the remaining distance is equal to `minimum_lane_change_distance` (see [here](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/behavior_path_planner_lane_change/#if-the-lane-is-blocked-and-multiple-lane-changes) for its explanation)
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2022-08-30 19-31-45](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93502286/187414967-3915137d-2d17-4361-bbf7-2771caa68828.png)
> 
> 
> Basically lane change requires a certain amount of distance, and for this case, the path is totally blocked. If such situation happen, then yes, we might not be able to perform lane change, until the vehicle is removed.
> 
> But it is possible to relax the condition, for example, when the object is barely blocking the path.
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2022-08-30 19-37-41](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93502286/187416146-8c1e4828-00b5-4a81-b8a7-b8d0c0cad787.png)
> 
> The latest universe's documentation provide some [explanation of the lane changing process](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/behavior_path_planner_lane_change/). Please let me know you thoughts and I am very happy for any comments and point of improvement.

###### @alanmengg (2022-09-05)

> > 
> thank u for your explanation.
> my first thought was to change to another planning mode but it would cause other problems. but perform the lane changing maneuver in this case is  a better thing to do.

### #1304 — image_projection_based_fusion fails to build on machines without CUDA.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-07-11  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-12  |  **Author:** @mitsudome-r
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1304

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> image_projection_based_fusion fails to build on machines without CUDA.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The package build successfully.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Build fails with the following error:
> ```
> CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR not found or specified
> CUDA NOT FOUND
> TensorRT is NOT Available
> CUDNN is NOT Available
> CMake Error at /opt/ros/galactic/share/ament_cmake_export_dependencies/cmake/ament_export_dependencies.cmake:29 (message):
>   ament_export_dependencies() must be called before ament_package()
> Call Stack (most recent call first):
>   /opt/ros/galactic/share/ament_cmake_auto/cmake/ament_auto_package.cmake:58 (ament_export_dependencies)
>   CMakeLists.txt:177 (ament_auto_package)
> ```
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Run installation steps on machines without GPU. https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/installation/
> 
> (You can still reproduce the error with CUDA installed machines by changing the `if` conditions in the CMakeLists.txt to `FALSE`)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
> - ROS: Humble
> - Autoware: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/tree/humble
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> I have checked the CMakeLists.txt and noticed that if you don't have CUDA:
> * `ament_auto_package()` is called twice (in [L161](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e7f09a8fc1a5a3fd49aa5c27164a0324a6f84e9a/perception/image_projection_based_fusion/CMakeLists.txt#L161) and [L177](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e7f09a8fc1a5a3fd49aa5c27164a0324a6f84e9a/perception/image_projection_based_fusion/CMakeLists.txt#L177))
> * some [nodes](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e7f09a8fc1a5a3fd49aa5c27164a0324a6f84e9a/perception/image_projection_based_fusion/CMakeLists.txt#L167) tries to refer to the [library](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/e7f09a8fc1a5a3fd49aa5c27164a0324a6f84e9a/perception/image_projection_based_fusion/CMakeLists.txt#L125) that is only built when CUDA is available
> * pointpainting_fusion_node, which relies on CUDA, is registered outside `if` condition
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-07-11)

> @mitsudome-r Resolved by #1306? If so, as you might know, it's good to write like `Resolves #1304` in the PR.

### #1272 — Invalid parameter query in scenario_selector node

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-07-07  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-08  |  **Author:** @NorahXiong
- **Labels:** component:planning
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1272

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> According to the design, scenario mode should change to lane_driving mode after parking task is completed and stops in lane but it didn't.
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/177740327-04f26a6d-f803-4e76-8d59-da21ba76841d.png)
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/177738280-626cb344-7d4a-4bbe-babd-e285d513fb13.png)
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> After parking task is completed and the car stops in lane in parking mode, the scenario should changed to lane_driving mode.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> After parking task is completed and the car stops in lane in parking mode, the scenario still keeps in parking mode.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start autoware planning simulator using default
> 2. Set pose estimate in parking spot and goal pose in lane
> 3. Engage the car and echo "/planning/scenario_planning/scenario" topic
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 20.04
> - ROS2: Galactic
> - Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> Parking state information is not correctly transferred to scenario_selector node. Scenario_selector can not [get](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/scenario_selector/src/scenario_selector_node/scenario_selector_node.cpp#L158) the paramter [set](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/freespace_planner/src/freespace_planner/freespace_planner_node.cpp#L383) in freespace_planner. 
> The parameter name remapping does not work. I think even though they are successfully remapped to the same name it still can not work well because they belong to different nodes.
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @NorahXiong (2022-07-07)

> [ThereΓÇÖs no global parameter concept in ROS 2](https://docs.ros.org/en/galactic/How-To-Guides/Launch-files-migration-guide.html#param), so I tried to fix it by substituting parameter by topic.

### #1253 — Autoware keeps following old local path after `behavior_velocity_planner` is dead

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2022-07-06  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:help-wanted, status:stale
- **Comments:** 11  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1253

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> While I experienced the `behavior_velocity_planner` crash (described here: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/1247), I observed autoware did not make the vehicle stop immediately after the crash, but kept driving along the last generated local path, reached the end of the local path and kept driving straight after. Autoware only triggered an emergency stop when the vehicle was ~3m beyond that last point (out of path detected).
> 
> Although the out of path detection range could be reduced to have the emergency triggered earlier, it is very unsafe for autoware to keep following an old local path. For example, even though some new obstacle would be detected on the road, autoware would simply ignore them and follow the last local path it has received.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> An emergency should be triggered if local paths are not generated anymore
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Autoware keep driving on the old path, even after its end has been reached.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. run autoware on a vehicle
> 2. kill `behavior_velocity_planner` while in autonomous mode
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - Ubuntu 20.04
> - galactic
> - main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @xmfcx (2022-07-19)

> A node monitoring node should check the critical nodes and issue emergency stop if one of them crashes.
> 
> You can try to add [topic_state_monitor](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/system/topic_state_monitor) to this launch file: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/launch/tier4_system_launch/launch/system.launch.xml
> 
> And somehow it should issue emergency message and stop the vehicle through the [emergency_handler](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/system/emergency_handler)

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-08-02)

> @mitsudome-r to provide additional documentation regarding emergency handler

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-08-30)

> I've started working on this. I think I will be able to create PR this week.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-09-13)

> I figured out that with the default configuration, topic monitoring function is not turned on. (This probably is because it is not always safe to make a sudden stop at node failure)
> 
> If you add use_emergency handling to control module, you should be able to turn on this function and make vehicle stop when ever major planning nodes dies with unknown error.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/515239b9f1d9c4161629f25c1b8e4c6ec62acfdd/autoware_launch/launch/autoware.launch.xml#L117
> 
> Modify the above launch as the following:
> ```
>   <group if="$(var launch_control)">
>     <include file="$(find-pkg-share tier4_control_launch)/launch/control.launch.py">
>       <arg name="lateral_controller_mode" value="mpc_follower"/>
>       <arg name="vehicle_info_param_file" value="$(find-pkg-share $(var vehicle_model)_description)/config/vehicle_info.param.yaml"/>
>       <arg name="use_emergency_handling" value="true"/>
>     </include>
>   </group>
> ```

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-09-27)

> I will close this issue once I add the above explanation in Autoware Documentation

###### @stale (2023-01-06)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @xmfcx (2023-01-10)

> @mitsudome-r is working on https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-documentation/pull/278

###### @stale (2023-04-22)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @stale (2023-11-03)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @VRichardJP (2023-11-04)

> I have not seen the motion planner dying while autoware is driving for a while, so I am not sure if the problem still exists.
> 
> I think now there would be an emergency stop?

> ### Description
> 
> In [FreespacePlannerNode::onRoute function](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/freespace_planner/src/freespace_planner/freespace_planner_node.cpp#L309), expression in null pointer check seems to be written as an assignment operation by mistake. I think the statement on the right side shows the actual intention. Otherwise the "if" statement will always return the "false" value.
> `if (scenario_ = nullptr) return;`  ->  `if (scenario_ == nullptr) return;` 
> 
> However, if the statement is corrected and try to activate freespace planning in parking scenario immediately after Autoware boots, we can not get a trajectory.
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/177474130-e2012b07-1c18-4667-a936-1ed5d1d115a1.png)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Freespace planner can generate a trajectory in parking scenario as long as Autoware boots normally without any precondition.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Freespace planner can not generate a trajectory in parking scenario in the first planning task.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Correct the null pointer check statement in [FreespacePlannerNode::onRoute function](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/freespace_planner/src/freespace_planner/freespace_planner_node.cpp#L309).
> 2. Start planning simulator.
> 3. Set start pose and goal pose in a parking lot. (no trajectory will be published)
> 4. Move the goal pose to another place in the parking lot. (trajectories can be published)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 20.04
> - ROS2: Galactic
> - Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> In [ScenarioSelectorNode::onTimer function](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/scenario_selector/src/scenario_selector_node/scenario_selector_node.cpp#L252), scenario_selector will not publish scenario info if route is not received.
> In [FreespacePlannerNode::onTimer function](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/freespace_planner/src/freespace_planner/freespace_planner_node.cpp#L409), freespace_planner will not plan unless route is received.
> Mission planner publishes route only once in [goal_pose](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/mission_planner/lib/mission_planner_base.cpp#L87) or [check_point](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/mission_planner/lib/mission_planner_base.cpp#L116) callback functions.
> 
> So freespace_planner can not receive the route mission_planner published for the first time because scenario pointer of freespace_planner is empty as scenario information must be published after scenario selector received route message.
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/177693701-42ab458e-c7b7-4a82-a2cf-7087172890f9.png)
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> Related code is modified in PR https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1155.

### #1249 — LiDAR timestamping policy is required

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-07-06  |  **Closed:** 2023-09-14  |  **Author:** @drwnz
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1249

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, individual LiDAR drivers have differing implementations on how timestamps are applied to pointcloud messages.
> In the commonly used [Velodyne](https://github.com/tier4/velodyne_vls) and [Hesai](https://github.com/tier4/hesai_pandar) drivers, the pointcloud message timestamp comes from the timestamp of the **first point** of the pointcloud. This has some drawbacks:
> 
> - When there are no points in the pointcloud, the message header behavior is undefined
> - When there is a blockage or other cause of no points to be returned at the start of the scan, the pointcloud message timestamp will be later than expected (the time between consecutive pointcloud timestamps will not necessarily be constant)
> - Unpredictable pointcloud message timestamps may cause downstream synchronization tasks to fail or give incorrect correspondences
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Determine a policy for how pointclouds should be timestamped, considering downstream perception tasks and synchronization.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Include parameters in the LiDAR drivers to enable the user to choose how timestamps are added to messages
> - Use the pointcloud's first packet timestamp for the message header timestamp
>   - This may not coincide perfectly with the start of the scan, as packets contain multiple points that may result in the pointcloud start being somewhere in the middle of the packet
> - Use the timestamp from the first point even when no point is present (azimuth and ring data is still in the packet even when there is no return)
> - Also consider options to timestamp at the end of the scan, or middle of the scan to ease synchronization with other sensors
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Definition of a LiDAR pointcloud message timestamping policy for Autoware.
> 
> - [x] Determine the desired behavior for reliable operation in downstream tasks
> - [x] Implement the timestamping methodology in the Hesai, Velodyne, and other supported LiDAR drivers to align with the defined policy
> - [x] Test operation in pointcloud preprocessor and perception tasks (especially where synchronization is required between sensors)

**Comments:**

###### @stale (2022-09-04)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @drwnz (2023-09-14)

> This is now discussed here: https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3578
> 
> And largely handled by this proposal: https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/3442#discussioncomment-5986829
> 
> Therefore, this issue will be closed.

### #1248 — rationalize `boost::optional` dereference in `behavior_velocity_planner`

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-07-06  |  **Closed:** 2022-12-16  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:help-wanted, status:stale
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1248

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> `boost::optional` is used quite often across the code base. In most of the code, it is dereferenced carefully, like so:
> ```c++
> if (optional_value) {
>   const auto val = optional_value.get();
> }
> 
> // or
> if (!optional_value) 
>   return err_value;
> const auto val = optional_value.get();
> ```
> 
> However in the `behavior_velocity_planner`, `boost::optional<double> current_accel` is dereferenced at many places without any prior check. Or sometimes even with a check after the dereference:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/62476712f16cc61c0a6fc08b10f518554f1fbab0/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/scene_module/no_stopping_area/scene_no_stopping_area.cpp#L374-L383
> 
> In the code above, the `if` clause is unreachable since an exception will be thrown at `planner_data_->current_accel.get()` if `planner_data_->current_accel` is not set. `current_accel` is only set after 2 messages have been received from `~/input/vehicle_odometry`
> 
> Here is a list of all unchecked dereference in `behavior_velocity_planner`:
> ```
> src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/include/utilization/trajectory_utils.hpp
> 136:  const double a0 = planner_data->current_accel.get(); // smoothPath()
> 
> src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/scene_module/intersection/util.cpp
> 172:  const double current_acc = planner_data->current_accel.get(); // generateStopLine()
> 
> src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/scene_module/run_out/scene.cpp
> 55:  const auto current_acc = planner_data_->current_accel.get(); // modifyPathVelocity()
> 144:  const float initial_acc = planner_data_->current_accel.get(); // visualizeDetectionArea()
> 
> src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/scene_module/no_stopping_area/scene_no_stopping_area.cpp
> 374:  const auto current_acceleration = planner_data_->current_accel.get(); // isStoppable()
> 
> src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/scene_module/occlusion_spot/scene_occlusion_spot.cpp
> 94:    param_.v.a_ego = planner_data_->current_accel.get(); // modifyPathVelocity()
> ```
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Since `planner_data_->current_accel` may be unset, it would make sense to consistently check its state before dereferencing it (otherwise there is no point using `boost::optional`)
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> add early return in related functions when `planner_data_->current_accel` is not set
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> no more unchecked dereference in:
> 
> - [ ] src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/include/utilization/trajectory_utils.hpp
> - [ ] src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/scene_module/intersection/util.cpp
> - [ ] src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/scene_module/run_out/scene.cpp
> - [ ] src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/scene_module/no_stopping_area/scene_no_stopping_area.cpp
> - [ ] src/universe/autoware.universe/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/scene_module/occlusion_spot/scene_occlusion_spot.cpp

**Comments:**

> @VRichardJP 
> thank you for isssue
> I think these values are not used until current accel is not set commonly
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/32c2e4120cfef2469bf10117de744d871c0460be/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/node.cpp#L219
> , and will be repalced by /localization/accleration
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1213

###### @VRichardJP (2022-07-08)

> Do you have any problem with current implementation?
> I think as long as isDataReady() returns false
> scene modules above you mentioned will not run

###### @VRichardJP (2022-07-13)

> @taikitanaka3 I did not have any runtime issue with these. But since there was a recent case of crash from unchecked boost::optional dereference (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1245) I looked for similar pattern ;)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-07-05  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-12  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug, priority:high

>

> ### Description
>

> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/62476712f16cc61c0a6fc08b10f518554f1fbab0/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/scene_module/intersection/scene_intersection.cpp#L161-L163

> No crash

> crash

### #1242 — Calculate path curvature only once

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2022-07-05  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @maxime-clem
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:planning, component:control
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1242

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Path curvature is an important information when planning and generating control commands.
> Currently, this curvature is calculated in multiple different nodes, sometimes using different methods.
> 
> This task aims at calculating the curvature only once.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Calculating the curvature only once will help avoid errors and will ensure all nodes use the same reference curvature in their calculations.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Add a curvature field to the TrajectoryPoint message (https://github.com/tier4/autoware_auto_msgs/blob/tier4/main/autoware_auto_planning_msgs/msg/TrajectoryPoint.idl).
> - Add a recommended way to calculate curvatures in the documentation.
>    - We may want to add common functions for curvature calculation and interpolation.
> - Add curvature calculation in the `obstacle_avoidance_planner` to populate the curvatures of the output Trajectory message.
> - Update the `motion_velocity_smoother` and the controllers to directly use the curvature of the Trajectory message.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Add a curvature field to the TrajectoryPoint message (https://github.com/tier4/autoware_auto_msgs/blob/tier4/main/autoware_auto_planning_msgs/msg/TrajectoryPoint.idl).
> - [ ] Add a recommended way to calculate curvatures in the documentation.
> - [ ] Add curvature calculation in the `obstacle_avoidance_planner` to populate the curvatures of the output Trajectory message.
> - [ ] Update the `motion_velocity_smoother` and the controllers to directly use the curvature of the Trajectory message.

**Comments:**

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-07-07)

> @maxime-clem @brkay54 @boyali 
> Thank you for raising a nice discussion.
> 
> Currently curvature is calculated in several packages independently. The reason is as follows
> 
> First, the method of curvature calculation differs depending on the application of each module. 
> 
> For example, `motion_velocity_smother` calculates the lateral acceleration from the curvature and do deceleration planning to prevent large lateral acceleration. 
> However, the `motion_velocity_smoother` is not interested in an exact curvature. 
> Say, in a long straight line, if there is very small noise at the path points due to calculation errors or insufficient algorithm performance, the exact curvature will be a very large value in a small interval. The `motion_velocity_smother` is not interested in such exact curvature. The `motion_velocity_smoother` is more interested in how much the path bends at roughly `wheel_base` intervals, so what the module needs is not exact curvature, but something like a curvature that is convenient for "deceleration on curve" planning.
> 
> On the other hand, the `obstacle_avoidance_planner` has a role to smooth the path. Such a module would require accurate curvature calculations since the smoothing is done with even very small curvature noises in mind.
> 
> Second, the curvature is redundant information since it can be recalculated from path shape (not perfectly, but enough accurate in practice).
> 
> This is a background for the current implementation. But this is defined more than 2 years ago, and we can discuss a new approach for the curvature calculation. 
> IMO, it is nice to have curvature information in trajectory if we can solve the first point.
> 
> 
> ---
> 
> At least, there are several methods proposed for curvature calculation, some of them are more accurate then the current implementation. I hope these methods are implemented in utility library (such as [tier4_autoware_utils](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/common/tier4_autoware_utils/include/tier4_autoware_utils/geometry/geometry.hpp/#L530-L542) and available for all nodes.
> Actually, there already is a problem due to an inaccurate curvature calculation in the control module (MPC controller).
> 

###### @boyali (2022-07-08)

> The B-spline library was previously a part of the nonlinear model predictive control package.  I based these libraries mainly on fast matrix computations and some numpy-like matrix concatenation functions. I tried to write helper functions by combining Numpy and Matlab-like semantics. 
> 
> After starting to work on the Autoware control toolbox, I used the same helper functions in the body of control functions. If we put BSplines in autoware_util, there will be duplicate helper functions. Separating them would probably require redesign. 
> 
> Here is a list of what is in these libraries: 
> **BSpline library: (based on the books The Elements of Statistical Learning Chapter 5 Semiparametric Regression David Ruppert )**
> 
> - Smoothing BSplines that can smooth any given path with a chosen smoothing parameter,
> - Interpolating BSpline that does not smooth but interpolates. 
> - Pre-conditioned conjugate gradient-based cubic, or linear spline interpolator (exactly same as the Autoware version but uses Eigen matrix and vectors). 
> - Templated BSpline smoother, which is a template version of BSpline smoother. It uses a pre-determined Eigen matrix instead of dynamic versions to make the computations faster. It computes a coefficient matrix only once and uses the same matrix to smooth and interpolate the paths or curves. 
> 
> ** helper : act_utils**
> - std::vector and scalar multiplication template
> - absolute_difference for non-negative variables 
> - wrapToPi --> Matlab like using an exponential of complex numbers
> - print_container variadic template that prints any std::vector and array
> - Eigen matrix print variadic templates. 
> - Eigen matrix vstack, hstack methods
> - Eigen matrix block_diag --> Matlab method, 
> - Strip leading zeros from a standard vector (for transfer functions)
> - Join std vectors, 
> - Zero padding std vectors,
> - Floating number comparison templates (isEqual, >0, <0)
> - Cross product helper for curvature computations, 
> - Curvature method that uses differential geometric definitions, 
> - Eigen sparse triplet helper that converts a dense matrix to sparse by using triplet construction,
> - Cholesky update for backstitution-based fast least-square solution. 
> 
> **Autoware Control Toolbox**
> - Transfer function classes, that can be multiplied, summed, or taken the power of. 
> - State-space classes that can be constructed from the transfer function with Bilinear discretization and matrix balancing algorithms. 
> - Signal builders that generate triangular, square, and sinusoidal signals for testing purposes. 
> 
> 
> 

###### @stale (2022-09-10)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
>

### #1228 — Image messages have latency or dropped

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-07-04  |  **Closed:** 2022-11-14  |  **Author:** @kaancolak
- **Labels:** type:bug, priority:high, component:perception, component:system
- **Comments:** 18  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1228

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
>  We are using the CycloneDDS configuration provided by @takam5f2 in this [discussion](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/discussions/2636) with tuned DDS advised by the ROS2 page. Without running Autoware.Universe, we are getting 20 fps with 3 cameras without any problem. But if we run the entire Autoware.Universe pipeline, image messages drop to ~3,4 FPS. When we reduce the resolution of the images to around 600x500 and fix the fps to 15, there is no frame loss, but the latency in the topic is around ~70,80 ms. Is there anyone have any advice or solution?
>  
>  CycloneDDS supports shared memory with ROS2 Humble. is there any plan to convert autoware messages to a fixed size for using zero-copy DDS operation with shared memory.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Image message topics must arrive with minimal latency.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Image messages are being dropped or coming with latency
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Run Autoware with a 2D object detection pipeline. 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @armaganarsln (2022-07-04)

> Have you made a test with Multiple high channel Lidars e.g. 1 x 128 channel + 5 x 16 channel lidar without the cameras? Is it possible that you might have the same problem or do you think this is only related to cameras?

###### @xmfcx (2022-07-04)

> Can you try to run image related nodes as [Composable Nodes](https://docs.ros.org/en/galactic/Tutorials/Intermediate/Composition.html) ?
> 
> For visualizing, I think `rviz2` is not good for camera images.
> 
> And I am not sure if `rqt` works as a Composable node. If it doesn't work as one, you might need to write your own image visualizing node for it.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-07-05)

> Possible relevant discussions: 
> * https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2617
> * https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2621
> * https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2555
> 
> Also, as @xmfcx mentioned, if we put all image processing nodes in a single component, we should be able to reduce the image latency.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-07-12)

> We need a rosbag to reproduce this issue.

###### @MertClk (2022-07-18)

> @Zeysthingz can you share bag files to reproduce this issue?

###### @xmfcx (2022-07-26)

> @xmfcx share the bag files.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-08-02)

> @xmfcx Is the bag file ready?

###### @xmfcx (2022-08-16)

> It seems all present messages were recorded instead of just the sensor messages. I will extract the sensor messages using this tool https://github.com/Kettenhoax/ros2bag_tools and upload the bag file.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-09-13)

> @xmfcx is investigating this issue.

###### @xmfcx (2022-09-19)

> The shared bag files are/will be available in autoware documentation through this pr: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-documentation/pull/200

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-09-27)

> Note: the bag file only contains velodyne_packets so needs conversion to pointcloud.
> 
> Sensor configuration: https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/datasets/#leo-drive-isuzu-sensor-data
> Front lidar is VLP16

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-09-27)

> @xmfcx could you share the link to sensor description repository for your vehicle?

###### @xmfcx (2022-10-04)

> https://github.com/vautonomous/isuzu_sensor_description @xmfcx also add this to the documentation.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-10-11)

> From the discussion from LeoDrive's update in ASWG, the latency is likely to be caused by CPU usage. We might not be able to fix this within Bus ODD timeline. 

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-10-11)

> Using Iceoryx zero copy improved the message transportation, but using Iceoryx as AWF projects needs further discussion.

###### @kaancolak (2022-10-19)

>  In the relevant PRs, I passed the same `pointcloud_container` to Velodyne nodes and missed the occupancy grid map package. When working with `sample_sensor_kit` and  `logging_simulator.launch.xml/autoware.lauch.xml`, it decreased network traffic by around -%30 and also CPU utilization decreased.
> 
>  I will test it with a real Velodyne devices, making sure multiple Velodyne drivers work without any problem in the same container with a different namespace. 

###### @xmfcx (2022-11-01)

> Once
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2114
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/sample_sensor_kit_launch/pull/48
> 
> are merged, we can close this issue.

###### @BonoloAWF (2022-11-07)

> > Once
> > 
> >     * [feat(tier4_localization_launch): pass pc container to localization #2114](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/2114)

### #1219 — Humble build error from point_types.h

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-07-03  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-03  |  **Author:** @shmpwk
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1219

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Humble build error which comes from #include <pcl/point_types.h>.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/runs/7160982397?check_suite_focus=true#step:7:4112
> 
> The error log says
> ```
> In file included from /usr/include/pcl-1.12/pcl/point_types.h:354,
>                  from /__w/autoware.universe/autoware.universe/map/map_tf_generator/src/pcd_map_tf_generator_node.cpp:22:
> /usr/include/pcl-1.12/pcl/impl/point_types.hpp:241:12: error: ISO C++ prohibits anonymous structs [-Werror=pedantic]
> ```
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> no build error
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> build error
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. colcon build `map_tf_generator` which cmake is this version https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/4b3ca871df6262721c12b6200f17426e9a93a02a/map/map_tf_generator/CMakeLists.txt
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - ROS2 humble
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> https://github.com/PointCloudLibrary/pcl/issues/2303
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @shmpwk (2022-07-03)

> Resolved by adding following in CMakeLists.txt.
> ```
> include_directories(
>   include
>   SYSTEM
>   ${PCL_INCLUDE_DIRS}
> )
> ```
> Reference: 
> https://github.com/PointCloudLibrary/pcl/issues/2303#issuecomment-1013668713

### #1203 — Launching planning_simulator without pointcloud map (only with vector map)

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-06-30  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-08  |  **Author:** @shmpwk
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:map
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1203

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, launching Autoware needs both pcd map and vector map.
> Here, we'd like to propose launching Autoware without pcd map.
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Autoware new users will easily start their project. 
> No need to prepare pcd map will save time and new users casually try planning simulation for example.
> Also, it will reduce dependency on pcd map from Auoware architecture.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - [x] Create node for calculating static tf from vector map to viewer frame like [map_tf_generator](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/map/map_tf_generator).  -> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/commit/506354ac32699745365f8d4f40463a8e9e016717
> - [x] Change  `map_tf_generator`  from current pcd one to that vector map one. -> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/commit/beed6b6aa1c27351fb90c4767eed48a3de5eec8c
> - [x] Adapt `ad_service_state_monitor` when pcd map is loaded or not. -> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/commit/b2f11c872a65c7d661b418dba92fbde619520af4
> - [x] Adapt [`map_hash_generator`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/map/map_loader/script/map_hash_generator) if no pcd map is loaded.
>   - There is no change for this. 
>     - always publish ll2 hash as before.
>     - publish pcd hash if pcd map is provided, and vice versa.
> - [x] Other modules which depend pcd map have to cope with it.
>   - nothing
>

> 
> In the future, other simulator like scenario simulator can do.

### #1199 — Migrate to point_cloud_msg_wrapper

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2022-06-30  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @esteve
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale, component:perception, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 9  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1199

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The current codebase uses the `PointCloud2Iterator` class for handling point clouds. However, this translates into code that's brittle and unreadable. [Point Cloud Message Wrapper](https://gitlab.com/ApexAI/point_cloud_msg_wrapper) provides a more robust and natural API for handling point clouds.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Make the point cloud handling code more robust and readable
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Use `point_coud_msg_wrapper` to handle point clouds
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> The point cloud iterator classes from `sensor_msgs` are no longer used, in favor of point_cloud_msg_wrapper

### #1174 — tf error in simple_planning_simulator

- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1174

> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When setting initial vehicle pose in simple_planning_simulator, I got following error.
> ```
> [simple_planning_simulator_exe-39] [ERROR 1656307088.172536014] [tf2_buffer]: Do not call canTransform or lookupTransform with a timeout unless you are using another thread for populating data. Without a dedicated thread it will always timeout. If you have a separate thread servicing tf messages, call setUsingDedicatedThread(true) on your Buffer instance.
> ```
> Even when I got this error, the initial vehicle pose succeeded to set. 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> no tf error 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> tf error
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. `ros2 launch autoware_launch planning_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=$HOME/Downloads/sample-map-planning vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit` following [tutorial](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/).
> 2. Set initial pose
> 3. You can see the error on the console.
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: ubuntu20.04
> - ROS2 galactic
> - The latest Autoware
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> No `make_shared` for [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/5a9f4f12a729dce102c4ce3e561013a8af644cae/simulator/simple_planning_simulator/src/simple_planning_simulator/simple_planning_simulator_core.cpp#L79) .
> 
> ### Additional context
> If not use shared_ptr, the error disappears. But I'm not sure this is the best solution.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1175

**Comments:**

> add margin in parameter file and  read them in code.

> margin variable  in parameter file.

### #1163 — Improve the lateral acceleration filter in motion velocity smoother

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-06-24  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-05  |  **Author:** @brkay54
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, priority:high
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1163

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> [Discussion](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/412)
> 
> In current implementation of lateral acceleration filtering in trajectory, we are estimating the curvature by selecting three point. Then, we are calculating the lateral acceleration with this curvature estimation. See [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/motion_velocity_smoother/src/smoother/smoother_base.cpp#L61)!
> 
> I want to suggest a new approach to estimate the curvature in trajectory points. We can estimate the curvature by using the orientation of trajectory points. I think orientation can give more accurate results because it is output of optimization.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Improve the velocity calculation of trajectory w.r.t. lateral acceleration limit.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> 
> We can calculate the desired steering angle with following equation:
> ![desired_steering_angle_eq](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45468306/173042936-fca51004-0e18-4789-a1f9-f8878d93b39b.svg)
> 
> After calculate the desired steering angles, `tan(steering_angle) / wheelbase` will give us the curvature of the trajectory point. We can set the velocities w.r.t. this calculation.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Implement the new approach

**Comments:**

### #1151 — Non-successive way points generated by A-star algorithm in freespace planner

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-06-22  |  **Closed:** 2022-09-06  |  **Author:** @NorahXiong
- **Labels:** type:bug, priority:low, component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1151

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Way points generated by A-star algorithm are not successive as the red circle shows. It could result in poor trajectory following performance.
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/174950870-7ad8e039-cd10-4c7c-8ae2-adbd0a27cf12.png)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Way points generated by A-star algorithm are successive. Here successive means the vehicle can move from the former point to the next point through a movement in the transition_table_. Possible transitions are defined as below.
> [AstarSearch::TransitionTable createTransitionTable function](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/freespace_planning_algorithms/src/astar_search.cpp#L74)
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Way points generated by A-star algorithm are not successive.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start autoware planning simulator using default
> 2. Set pose estimate and goal pose the parking lot
> 
> (These steps can not guarantee the problem will repeat. According to my experience, there is a higher probability if the number of arcs in ReesShepp solution is large.)
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 20.04
> - ROS2: Galactic
> - Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> 
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/175469788-9d030442-384e-4aec-8945-604ceaf725c7.png)
> 
> According to the transition table design, two consecutive points should be like the blue arrows. The yellow ones(shift_theta greater than d╬╕) and the green ones(can not reach the next point precisely through any of the transition types) should not have been appeared.
> 
> If the preceding node changed, the nodes behind should recheck the transition relation and recalculate the actual cost or just break the connection. But these steps are not implemented now. So if a node in the closed list is rewritten during the search, and its child node stays the same, the output may be as the green arrows show. 
> 
> For example. In the following picture, S is the start point, G is the goal point and P(P*) is the non-successive point. At first, nodes P* is in the closed list and its child D is in the open list. Then point C is chosen from the open list and node P is pushed into the open list (again) as a child of C. Actually P and P* are the same node in search space cause they are in the same grid and have the same orientation. In other words, P and P* use the same part of memory and share the same index in search space. Even though P is not totally equal to P*, D keeps pointing to P/P*. If D is chosen from the open list, the problem may appear as S-C-P-D-G has a chance to be selected as the best way. In that case, we will get a non-successive way point array as the figure shows.
> 
> ![astar](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/175006627-15ad050e-5e09-4146-8959-8470671b61cb.jpeg)
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-06-28)

> @TakaHoribe Could you assign someone from Planning team to take a look at this?

###### @NorahXiong (2022-08-03)

> The bug is caused by queuing a node more than once and modifying the node elements for different queues. Such operation results in incorrect data association and exploded when retrieving a queue to generate the final path.  It can be fixed by creating an new node instance for data storage every time the node is queued.  Another strategy is just to forbid a node to be queued second time just as the implementation in [ROS-Nav2](https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/blob/galactic/nav2_smac_planner/src/a_star.cpp#L372). 
> 
> I tried to fix it by the first method but the node data storage implementation [needs alteration](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2716) as we don't know exactly how many times will a node be queued. I simply substituted the pre-allocation by instant-allocation and the memory consumption obviously decreased and meanwhile the time consumption obviously increased. In general, the performance is not very good. Maybe some other container such as map could improve the instant-allocation performance.
> 
> So instead I used the second method with reference to ROS-Nav2 implementation even though it will block some possible paths. I tested several cases after the fix and it works for them all. Maybe the tiny constraint of search space has little influence on the result because the visit to search space is originally very sparse in most cases. In ROS-Nav2 implementation, some tricks as [AnalyticExpansion](https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/blob/galactic/nav2_smac_planner/src/a_star.cpp#L471) are composed into the main algorithm and I think it could benefit the algorithm to some extent. 
> 
> If there are better solutions, please let me know.

### #1127 — The LiDAR azimuth unit is ambiguous

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-06-20  |  **Closed:** 2022-11-16  |  **Author:** @badai-nguyen
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1127

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, the LiDAR's azimuth is output in hundredths of degree unit that makes the code unclear and error-prone when adding support for new LiDAR devices.
> This problem was recognized when adding support for a new LiDAR in this issue: #509 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Improve the code readability and ease of adding support for new LiDARs.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Change output azimuth unit to degree in range of [0.0f , 360.0f] or radian in range of [ 0.0f , 2*pi] in LiDAR drivers: [Velodyne](https://github.com/tier4/velodyne_vls) and [Hesai](https://github.com/tier4/hesai_pandar)
> - change the respectively unit of azimuth referenced in the related repository.  
>   - [dual_return_outlier_filter](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/dual_return_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp)
>   - [ring_outlier_filter](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/ring_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp)
>   - [LiDAR blockage_diagnostics](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/blockage_diag)
> 
> The degree unit seems easier for readers to imagine the value of angle setting, while the radian unit may give performance benefits for conversions in sinusoidal/co-sinusoidal related function. Since the main purpose is for readability, it is proposed to use the unit of degree for azimuth.  
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Unify the new unit of azimuth in AW. 
> - [ ] output azimuth unit change from Velodyne driver
> - [ ] output azimuth unit change from Hesai driver
> - [ ] input azimuth unit change for related code and parameter in universe

**Comments:**

###### @stale (2022-08-30)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @xmfcx (2022-11-15)

> My suggestion: Following the [discussions for the new point type `PointXYZIRCT`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-documentation/pull/180#issuecomment-1315272014) I think we can do the following:
> 
> - Don't calculate the azimuth in the driver.
> - Calculate ╬▒(azimuth) with `p.azimuth = std::atan2(p.y, p.x)` in the place it is necessary
> - The output will be a `double` or `float` (whatever precision is needed) in the range [-╧Ç , +╧Ç] radians 
> - Works for any kind of lidars, including solid state lidars too.
> 
> @aohsato @miursh 
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2022-11-15 16-52-13](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10751153/201936440-a7cbd491-4a76-416c-92f6-4e4f22b8aab7.png)
> 
> [VLP-16 User Manual](https://velodynelidar.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/63-9243-Rev-E-VLP-16-User-Manual.pdf)

###### @miursh (2022-11-15)

> @xmfcx In my opinion, calculating the azimuth for each point at the place requires extra calculation cost even though the drivers don't have to calculate since they know the exact azimuth based on the hardware laser configurations or based on sensor output. 
> Since we handle more than 200,000 points (e.g. for VLS128), I think we should avoid those extra computational cost
> 

###### @xmfcx (2022-11-15)

> @xmfcx check for how long it takes to compute std::hypot and std::atan2 for large amount of points just to see how much computation it takes.
> 
> Also list what nodes make use of azimuth and distance fields.
> 
> @esteve also suggests to send down the values because storage/memory is cheaper.

###### @xmfcx (2022-11-16)

> I've created a mini benchmark for this topic: https://github.com/xmfcx/bench_point_cloud#readme @esteve @miursh 
> 
> Let's continue this discussion in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-documentation/pull/180#issuecomment-1317583569

### #1116 — Obstacle stop planner is chattering in obstacle detection by pointcloud and its marker continue visualizing

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-06-16  |  **Closed:** 2022-08-31  |  **Author:** @h-ohta
- **Labels:** status:help-wanted, component:planning
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1116

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> There are two problems.
> - When pointcloud is blinking , obstacle detection is chattering.
> - When chattering is occured, but wall marker keeps visualizing.
> 
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9547070/173994863-3cae344c-584e-4343-9c75-75060ceb4b26.mp4
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> When blinking pointcloud, obstacle detection is not chattering. 
> Detecction result keeps for the user defined time.
> I believe that the wall marker should synchronize with its detection result.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> When pointcloud is blinking , obstacle detection is chattering.
> When chattering is occured, but marker keeps visualizing
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
>

### #1115 — Motion Utils Package in the Universe

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-06-16  |  **Closed:** 2022-10-25  |  **Author:** @purewater0901
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:planning
- **Comments:** 12  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1115

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Creating a new package called motion utils under the common directory. It contains common functions used in planning and control packages. 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Since there are many common functions in planning and control packages in the universe, we need one common package that contains those duplicated functions. Currently, tier4_autoware_utils has some useful functions to use many packages, but it does not have any functions only used in planning and control modules.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Creating a common utils package under the common directory.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Creating a package that contains common functions for planning and control packages.

**Comments:**

###### @purewater0901 (2022-06-16)

> @TakaHoribe @yukkysaito @kenji-miyake 
> What do you think about this idea? I also wonder if you have better names for the motion utils package. 

###### @yukkysaito (2022-06-16)

> How about creating trajectory utils, etc. in tier4_autoware_utils?
> Can you tell us more details about the common process for planning and control?
> 

###### @purewater0901 (2022-06-16)

> Currently, there are too many functions in tier4_autoware_utils, we'd like to separate some functions exclusive to planning and control modules. For example, I'd like to add a function called insertStopPoint which inserts a stop point to a trajectory, but this function is only used for planning and control modules. 
> 
> Therefore, I think creating a whole new package would be better .

### #1105 — Creating Test Codes to Check Simulator Compatibility with Autoware

- **State:** OPEN  |  **Created:** 2022-06-15  |  **Closed:** -  |  **Author:** @Soohyeok-Park
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1105

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> - according to the issue discussed on simulation WG(https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-projects/issues/21#issue-1203352244), MORAI Inc. has made a sample unit test package to check a simulator's compatibility with autoware.
> - the package covers test cases from ControlModeCommand& ControlModeReport(no. 1) to HazardLightsCommand & HazardLightsReport(no. 6). 
> - EmergencyState is not covered since it is not being determined yet.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - To ensure that any simulator is compatible with the latest version of Autoware
> - Ultimately, streamlining the development process of Autoware-compatible simulators
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> A very simple method to check the compatibility of MORAI SIM: Drive with Autoware is included in this documentation, which can give a very brief idea at least.
> [Link](https://morai.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/AWF/pages/1107034224/Shared+MORAI+SIM+Drive+Quick+Start+Guide+for+AWF#4.-Running-Samples-Codes-to-Demonstrate-autoware_auto_msgs-Compatibility)
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> [Current] cover the interface between the simulator and Autoware
> [Future] test would cover other requirements defined in the documentation (related discussion [link](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/234))
