### #1076 — Error in obstacle avoidance direction when using extended lane to avoid obstacles

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-06-10  |  **Closed:** 2022-06-27  |  **Author:** @shulanbushangshu
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1076

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The default .yaml configuration for the extended lane in the obstacle avoidance module is shown below:
> ![2022-06-10 17-50-24σ▒Åσ╣òµê¬σ¢╛](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102840938/173040401-eaf9ad5c-e282-4d0d-b7bb-a8b3cc2ebd45.png)
> Wrong direction for obstacle avoidance when placing an obstacle in the left lane.As shown below∩╝Ü
> ![2022-06-10 17-19-17σ▒Åσ╣òµê¬σ¢╛](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102840938/173040863-3aa34d46-aa8c-4bd7-a115-86cb778e0cfb.png)
> 
> When I change the default configuration∩╝Üdetection_area_left_expand_dist:1-->0,The above phenomena will not occur.
> 
> I think there is a problem with the code when using the extended lane for obstacle avoidance.
> 
> This phenomenon also occurs when we use relatively wide lanes (non-standard lanes) in reality
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Whether extended lanes or wide lanes are used for obstacle avoidance, the direction of obstacle avoidance shall not be different.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Wrong direction for obstacle avoidance when placing an obstacle in the left lane by using default .yaml configuration for the extended lane in the obstacle avoidance module
> ![2022-06-10 17-19-17σ▒Åσ╣òµê¬σ¢╛](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102840938/173042555-d865c130-707a-40f6-9c39-0f6722469424.png)
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1.Start autoware planning simulator using default;
> 2. Set initial position and gobal position;
> 3.Place an obstacle vehicle in the left lane
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> 1.OS: Ubuntun 20.04
> 2.ROS2: Galactic
> 3.Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> First, confirm whether the code supports wide lane obstacle avoidance and extended Lane obstacle avoidance.
> If it is not supported for design purposes, you need to change the default configuration file:detection_area_left_expand_dist:1-->0(Or delete relevant codes).
> 
> If the design needs support, I think there is a problem in the calculation of the obstacle avoidance module.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #1064 — Cannot stop at stop line after restarting

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-06-09  |  **Closed:** 2022-06-09  |  **Author:** @k-obitsu
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1064

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In case of the following simple route,
> ![Screenshot from 2022-06-09 14-54-45](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/56008637/172774629-5a8a8fcc-2958-472f-babb-45e5e08dfae7.png)
> The vehicle stop on the stop line.
> When the vehicle arrives at the goal point, manually return to the starting point.
> At that time, make sure to pass by the side of the stop line.(see below)
> ![Screenshot from 2022-06-09 15-02-43](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/56008637/172775651-4fbe0b9f-cc5e-4770-ab41-6d49b53c5a6d.png)
> After arrived at the starting point, publish a goal pose and let it run automatically again.
> 
> The vehicle run through the stop line without stop.
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Under the following conditions, the vehicle can stop on the stop line.
> 
> - Restart the vehicle after manual driving
> - Set the same goals as before.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The vehicle run through the stop line without stop.

###### @JianKangEgon (2022-06-07)

Sometimes lateral controller or even the whole control module was not able to be launched successfully either, and the info displayed was just like above "process has died" without any other helpful description. I had to relaunch the module or node individually. I'm not sure if this problem has something to do with the mechanism of container.

###### @maxime-clem (2022-06-09)

> ### Investigation
> 
> I reproduced the issue by following the **Steps to reproduce**.
> ~The only way (as far as I know) to debug a `ComposableNode` is with a core dump.~
>    - EDIT: in a python launch file, a `ComposableNodeContainer` can take a `prefix="gdb -ex run --args"` to run it with `gdb` (similar to a `Node`). However I have issues with this method when using the `scenario_runner` and I found the core dump method more reliable in this case.
> ```bash
> # enable core dump of unlimited size
> ulimit -c unlimited
> # add pid to file name
> echo -n 1 | sudo tee /proc/sys/kernel/core_uses_pid
> ```
> After reproducing the error, it generates a core file that can be replayed with `gdb`.
> - :warning: Usually this file goes in the current folder but with the `scenario_test_runner` I am not able to find the location of the file.
> - Alternative: a crash file `/var/crash/_opt_ros_galactic_lib_rclcpp_components_component_container_mt.1000.crash` was generated.
>   - The crash file needs to be unpacked `apport-unpack /var/crash/_opt_ros_galactic_lib_rclcpp_components_component_container_mt.1000.crash crash_folder`.
>   - The `crash_folder` then contains the `CoreDump` and other information (e.g., `ExecutablePath` with the path to the executable that crashed).
>   - Now we can debug with ``gdb `cat ExecutablePath` CoreDump``.
> 
> After checking the [backtrace](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/files/8866347/gdb.txt), the only issues I could find are vectors within `autoware_auto_perception_msgs::msg::PredictedPath` objects that have a larger length than capacity (`std::vector of length 2497072894800, capacity 2497072894629`) and negative length (`std::vector of length -22769416, capacity 60`).
> 
> ### Solution
> 
> ~The [PredictedPath message definition](https://github.com/tier4/autoware_auto_msgs/blob/tier4/main/autoware_auto_perception_msgs/msg/PredictedPath.idl#L7) is currently written in IDL format with a capacity limit of `100` to its `path` field. **Removing this capacity limit and rebuilding Autoware solves the issue** and I was able to run the complete scenario without any crash.~
> 
> ~I opened a PR to remove this capacity: https://github.com/tier4/autoware_auto_msgs/pull/32
> Please test it and confirm that this fixes the issue.~
> 
> EDIT: this solution does not seem to work, sorry for the mistake. I am investigating another solution.

###### @mehmetdogru (2022-06-09)

> @maxime-clem 
> Thank you for the solution you proposed however that didn't work for me even though I deleted build/install/log just to be sure and checked out your branch (fix-PredictedPath-remove_capacity_limit) and re-build whole autoware repo. Yet the same issue is still there.

###### @maxime-clem (2022-06-10)

> Sorry for my previous post. I was too quick to claim that the issue was solved.
> 
> I have found two problems so far that cause crashes of the `behavior_path_planner`.
> - `std::bad_alloc` happens when copying some messages.
>    - I have not found the root cause yet but some messages seem to have impossible sizes (e.g., `std::vector of length -17545788653642, capacity -17545788653637` as reported by `gdb`).
>    - Avoiding unnecessary copies help with this issue but they still sometimes occur (https://github.com/maxime-clem/autoware.universe/commit/6fe4bf7de76792fa21c36d941c66f0fffa79db2d).
>    - The capacity of IDL messages may be related to this issue but I need to experiment more to confirm that.
> - `vector::_M_range_check` happens when accessing pre-calculated indexes that somehow becomes out of bound.
>    - For example: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/scene_module/lane_change/util.cpp#L373-L383  
>       - Indexes for elements inside `PredictedObjects::ConstSharedPtr dynamic_objects` are precalculated.
>       - By the time the elements are accessed using these indexes, they can become out of bound.
>    - The only explanation I can find is that the pointer is updated while the function is running, changing to a message with less elements such that some of the calculated indexes are out of bound.
>    - Passing the `PredictedObjects::ConstSharedPtr` by value rather than by reference seems to solve the issue (https://github.com/maxime-clem/autoware.universe/commit/ca3b9afaf6dc0c9aafb4a0e9217c599a61d478dd) but I need to confirm that this works correctly.
> 
> These issues do not happen consistently and with my current test branch (https://github.com/maxime-clem/autoware.universe/tree/fix-issue1049-behavior_path_planner_crashes) I am sometimes able to run the full scenario without any crash.
> 
> I will keep investigating but any help or suggestion would be welcome.

###### @mehmetdogru (2022-06-13)

> @maxime-clem happens the same when I test [UC-PB-009-0001_Db20-Shalun](https://gitlab.com/autowarefoundation/operational-design-domains/-/blob/master/public_road_bus/UC-PB-009-0001_Db20-Shalun.yaml) as well. For the versions that I test please check [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1uWpaJw68MwdCS_wysQsbG8YyG9UaYK8V00AFTd7HiVs/edit#gid=0&range=A48:L48).

###### @maxime-clem (2022-06-14)

> @mehmetdogru Thank you for reporting another scenario where the issue occurs.
> I made a fix that should solve the issue for both scenarios: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1091

### #1023 — Motion_velocity_smoother should depend the steering_rate_limit

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-06-01  |  **Closed:** 2022-09-07  |  **Author:** @brkay54
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:planning
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1023

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Discussion [here](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/381)!
> Related: #567 
> 
> Hello everyone, 
> 
> I realized that planning module in Autoware do not depend the steering angle rate. In lateral controller, we can set steering_rate_limit ([here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/launch/tier4_control_launch/config/trajectory_follower/lateral_controller.param.yaml#L49)). When I set lower steering_rate_limit, the states that are calculated by lateral_controller are seem good. But longitudinal controller can not handle, It should slow down the vehicle because of low steering_angle_rate but it is not. vehicle could not turn over the high curvature paths.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> As mentioned in discussion, new function which change the velocities w.r.t. steering_rate_limit will be added to motion_velocity_smoother.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45468306/171392633-e09c78bd-8650-469e-b529-f71fd0dbdc97.png)
> New step will be added after `apply lateral acceleration limit` to decrease velocities where steering_rate > steering_rate_limit.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Design algorithm
> - [x] Create function and implement it

**Comments:**

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-06-04)

> Nice work. Thank you!

### #1019 — Improve shape estimator performance for vehicles

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-06-01  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-29  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:perception
- **Comments:** 13  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1019

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> As I have reported in some [other discussion](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/380#discussioncomment-2853796), I face important performance issue with my setup. I have identified a couple nodes that are unexpectedly slow on my machine. The `shape_estimator` is one of them.
> 
> I use the following test environment: my vehicle is parked and surrounded by a 3~4 other vehicles.
> ![test_env](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/171314463-b96c670b-1ace-44f9-bf3e-cafee096049a.png)
> 
> With this environment, the `ShapeEstimationNode::callback()` takes around 120ms to process each `apollo/labeled_clusters` message:
> ![base_result](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/171314881-2c0fe0b1-12cf-4c29-bd8c-d29133aeec70.png)
> 
> For just a couple vehicles, it seems way to slow.
> 
> The `shape_estimator` node implements the algorithm from paper "Efficient L-Shape Fitting for Vehicle Detection Using Laser Scanners". Interestingly, the "Algorithm 2" that is reproduced from the original paper is actually a very naive and inefficient minima finder:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/a1288448427eb9c05679ed96a2591402b238d33a/perception/shape_estimation/lib/model/bounding_box.cpp#L84-L109
> 
> In order to find the maximum of the `calcClosenessCriterion` function, the algorithm actually tries all the possible values between `min_angle` and `max_angle` (with fixed step `angle_precision`). With the current implementation, the function is evaluated 90 times (from 0 to 90 degrees with 1 degree step). A way better approach would be to use an actual minima finder algorithm instead, especially if we consider how continuous the closeness function looks like (in red below):
> 
> ![Screenshot from 2022-06-01 11-26-33](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/171317735-cd502df1-5911-4b9a-85e7-9115c8a72925.png)
> 
> Note: this would make https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/discussions/384 obsolete
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Improve `shape_estimator` performance for vehicle obstacles
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> As explained, a first step would be to use a minima finder function.
> 
> For example, I tested [`brent_find_minima`](https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_37_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/toolkit/internals1/minima.html) from boost library. There are maybe better options, I am no expert, I just picked what looked the simplest to use with no extra dependencies.
> 
> I modified the [Algo.2 section](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/a1288448427eb9c05679ed96a2591402b238d33a/perception/shape_estimation/lib/model/bounding_box.cpp#L84) like so:
> ```C++
>   // Paper : Algo.2 Search-Based Rectangle Fitting
>   auto closeness_func = [&](float theta) {
>     Eigen::Vector2f e_1;
>     e_1 << std::cos(theta), std::sin(theta);  // col.3, Algo.2
>     Eigen::Vector2f e_2;
>     e_2 << -std::sin(theta), std::cos(theta);  // col.4, Algo.2
>     std::vector<float> C_1;                    // col.5, Algo.2
>     std::vector<float> C_2;                    // col.6, Algo.2
>     for (const auto & point : cluster) {
>       C_1.push_back(point.x * e_1.x() + point.y * e_1.y());
>       C_2.push_back(point.x * e_2.x() + point.y * e_2.y());
>     }
>     float q = calcClosenessCriterion(C_1, C_2);
>     return -q; // so that brent_find_minima actually finds the maximum 
>   };
> 
>   int bits = 4; // max is std::numeric_limits<float>::digits/2 = 12
>   boost::uintmax_t max_iter = 20;
>   std::pair<float, float> min = boost::math::tools::brent_find_minima(closeness_func, min_angle, max_angle+epsilon, bits, max_iter);
>   float theta_star = min.first;
>   
>   const float sin_theta_star = std::sin(theta_star);
>   const float cos_theta_star = std::cos(theta_star);
> 
> ```
> 
> With `bits = 6`, processing time went down to ~40ms:
> ![brent_6_digit](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/171317059-86fd7b67-1e1c-45b0-8403-5a3d2c3424c2.png)
> 
> 
> And with `bits = 4`, processing time went down to ~30ms:
> ![brent_4_bit](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/171317080-373ede19-84e1-4680-84a7-c94941fdfc96.png)
> 
> Even with `bits = 4`, I think the precision should be better than the current one (`angle_resolution` is 0.01745 rad), yet it is 4 times faster on my machine.
> From the Rviz view, bounding boxes don't look any worse than with the default algorithm. 
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - `shape_estimator` can perform in "real-time" in an environment with several vehicle obstacles around the ego vehicle.

**Comments:**

###### @yukkysaito (2022-06-02)

> @VRichardJP Thank you for the good proposal!
> I'd like to measure on my PC, Cloud you share the rosbag including `/perception/object_recognition/detection/apollo/labeld_clusters`

###### @VRichardJP (2022-06-02)

> @yukkysaito I am sorry, I cannot easily share such data.
> But I think it should be possible to use the [demo rosbag](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/rosbag-replay-simulation/) as reference since many vehicles are visible. 

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-06-07)

> @VRichardJP This looks like a good improvement. Would you be able to create a PR for the proposal (maybe after @yukkysaito confirmed the feature)?

###### @VRichardJP (2022-06-08)

> No problem, I will wait for @yukkysaito to confirm the change does not impact detection quality

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-06-21)

> @angry-crab has volunteered to do the further investigation.

###### @angry-crab (2022-06-23)

> After a brief investigation about Brent's method and other numerical optimization algorithms, one concern is that Brent's method is not guaranteed to converge, which means there might be some potential issues undetected. I think we could add a parameter to `shape_estimation` node to be able to select among different optimization algorithms. I'll also test other numerical methods for this issue. 

###### @VRichardJP (2022-06-23)

> I think being able to chose between multiple implementation would be great.
> 
> According to [boost documentation](https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_63_0/libs/math/doc/html/math_toolkit/roots/brent_minima.html) and [wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brent%27s_method), Brent's method should at least converge to a local minima. It would be interesting to plot `-calcClosenessCriterion`, but from the paper it really looks like the function has only 1 minima, except when the minima is exactly at 0/90 degrees, in which case the function behavior may be strange (maybe?). But even if it was a thing, it should be able to fix that using a slighly larger search interval (e.g. [0, 100])
> 
> 

###### @xmfcx (2022-06-28)

> OpenCV has this: https://theailearner.com/2020/11/03/opencv-minimum-area-rectangle/
> 
> (Just for minimum area rectangle criteria)

###### @angry-crab (2022-06-29)

> Due to the issue of broken docker image, testing of this issue will be postponed. [CUDA](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/issues/2452)

###### @VRichardJP (2022-06-29)

> I feel a bit stupid, but I just realized the performance reported in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/1019#issue-1254768651 has been retrieved from a debug build...
> 
> Using optimizations from release and the same test environment than before, I get around  ~4 ms for the current implementation (or ~1 ms per box), and ~1 ms with the brent's method (with `bits = 6`). So the second method is still around 4 times faster than current implementation, yet with a similar precision. 
> 
> That said, their is no real performance issue in the first place. Even in a crowded parking area it would still be negligible. I would understand if you don't want to introduce some convoluted algorithm just for a few ms...
> 
> 
> 

###### @angry-crab (2022-06-29)

> @VRichardJP Thank you very much for your efforts. I think 4 times faster is a great improvement. 
> @mitsudome-r Do you think we should include this improvement? 

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-07-05)

> I think we can still include this improvement in Autoware.Universe to give more options to the users.

###### @angry-crab (2022-07-08)

> I've created a draft PR regarding this issue. Please feel free to make any comment.

> Hi,
> 
> I recently started to have this very error using `autoware_launch.launch.xml`. It does not occur every single time, but when it does it can be very frustrating.
> 
> Although the message seems to point out there is an issue with the plugin, it seems to me the problem appears when the plugin is tried to be loaded before the container is actually started.
> 
> The way I have found to fix that problem is to move the launch of the container from `autoware.launch.xml` to a separate launch file, which is to be started before `autoware.launch.xml` (same for other launch files). I have been using this for a few days and have not encountered the issue anymore since.
> 
> Like this `pointcloud_container.launch.xml`:
> ```xml
> <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
> <launch>
>   <!-- Pointcloud container -->
>   <arg name="pointcloud_container_name" default="pointcloud_container"/>
>   <group>
>     <include file="$(find-pkg-share autoware_launch)/launch/pointcloud_container.launch.py">
>       <arg name="use_multithread" value="true"/>
>       <arg name="container_name" value="$(var pointcloud_container_name)"/>
>     </include>
>   </group>
> </launch>
> ```

###### @xmfcx (2022-07-19)

###### @miursh (2022-07-25)

> The reason why this happens is because sensing.launch and perception.launch could start before the pointcloud container start, I think. 
> In autoware_launch.launch.xml/logging_simulator.launch.xml,  pointcloud container must be launched before the other components are launched, but I suspect current launcher does not guarantee the launch order.

###### @yukkysaito (2022-07-26)

> >@yukkysaito When this error happens, if you restart the computer, does it start working again?
> 
> yes
> sorry for late reply. ≡ƒÖÅ 

###### @xmfcx (2022-07-27)

> <img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10751153/181366571-5b730671-271e-46a3-9751-fbe388ff0efe.png" width="500">
> 
> @miursh is right, here is the launch call graph. 
> 
> It is absolutely too complicated and parameters passed around are basically a mess. It's very tedious to figure out where a parameter is set when the launch file graph is this deep.
> 
> What I figured out is, 
> - If `use_pointcloud_container == true`
>   - `pointcloud_preprocessor.launch.py` will try to put its components into `pointcloud_container.launch.py`'s component container instead of its own.
>   - If the `pointcloud_container.launch.py` hasn't started correctly by chance, it will give the error.
> 
> How do we fix this?
> - Non-performant solution:
>   - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/blob/main/autoware_launch/launch/logging_simulator.launch.xml#L49 set this `use_pointcloud_container` to false. It won't try to use that container. It will have more network overhead but at least it will work.
> - Performant but hacky solution:
>   - @VRichardJP 's solution: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/1009#issuecomment-1167079863 of running the container before the components.
> - Right solution:
>   - Somehow wait until the container starts, load the components once it happens.
> 
> I just don't like current launch system of Autoware. How can we make it better, I don't have an answer yet.

> `LoadComposableNodes` can load nodes even if the target container is launched after it, so I think the order of launch has nothing to do with this issue.

### #1008 — Test the perception stack on the raw lidar data

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-31  |  **Closed:** 2022-08-02  |  **Author:** @xmfcx
- **Labels:** priority:high, component:perception
- **Comments:** 12  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/1008

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Follow up from: 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/562#issuecomment-1102662448
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/564
> 
> Bag and pcap files: https://autoware-files.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/collected_data/2022-04-14_autocore-lidar-bag-pcap/Lidar_Data_220414_bag_pcap.zip
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> AutoCore.ai has recorded and shared lidar pcap and bag files from their autonomous vehicle. This task aims to test the lidar perception stack of Autoware Universe.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The bag files contain a single topic with:
> - name: `/sensing/lidar/top/rectified/pointcloud`
> - type: `sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2`
> 
> Run the perception stack on the data and obtain locally tracked objects.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] The required nodes determined and run.
> - [x] Ground segmentation works.
> - [x] The object bounding boxes are obtained.
> - [x] Local tracking results are obtained. (Without localization)
> - [x] List of nodes that were run are shared under this issue.
> - [x] Video(s) of the RViz showing the end result uploaded to youtube.

**Comments:**

###### @kaancolak (2022-06-10)

> I tested the perception pipeline with a given Velodyne point cloud bag file. I used velodyne_top as a base frame for each node.  multi_object_tracker contains a hard-coded parameter as a "base_link"   [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/perception/multi_object_tracker/src/multi_object_tracker_core.cpp#L222) for this reason running a multi-object tracker without "base_link" need an external change in the package.
> 
> List of nodes that were run:
> -  common_ground_filter
> -  euclidean_cluster
> -  detection_by_tracker_node
> -  initial_cluster_shape_estimation
> -  lidar_apollo_instance_segmentation or lidar_centerpoint
> -  obstacle_pointcloud_based_validator_node
> -  object_association_merger
> - multi_object_tracker
> 
> Ground remover on trucks bag file : 
> 
> [![Img alt text](https://img.youtube.com/vi/Ui7FGpx6E2E/0.jpg)](https://youtu.be/Ui7FGpx6E2E)
> 
> Ground remover on ped_vehicle bag file : 
> 
> [![Img alt text](https://img.youtube.com/vi/IP1axvmilUo/0.jpg)](https://youtu.be/IP1axvmilUo)
> 
> Tracking result on trucks bag file with Apollo 3D detections : 
> 
> [![Img alt text](https://img.youtube.com/vi/rCe-BWTDN9Q/0.jpg)](https://youtu.be/rCe-BWTDN9Q)
> 
> Tracking result on ped_vehicle bag file with Apollo  3D detections: 
> 
> [![Img alt text](https://img.youtube.com/vi/HdNmm0HtwOA/0.jpg)](https://youtu.be/HdNmm0HtwOA)
> 
> Additionally, lidar_centerpoint returned too many false positive detected objects in the provided bag files. I increased the score_threshold up to 0.60 false-negative detections decreased but still continue. I used a local frame "velodyne_top" as a densification_world_frame_id. 
> 
> [![Img alt text](https://img.youtube.com/vi/J8J2e_YI-SQ/0.jpg)](https://youtu.be/J8J2e_YI-SQ)
> 
> FYI:  @xmfcx @mitsudome-r @Sharrrrk
> 
> 

###### @xmfcx (2022-06-10)

> Wow thanks for the tests @kaancolak!
> 
> The most of the detection markers are coming from behind in the RViz2 visualizations.
> Do you know why is that the case?
> 
> I will open up issues to look into the problems if it is not the expected state.
> 
> 
> Also the pedestrian detection video looks poor in terms of detecting and tracking the person: https://youtu.be/J8J2e_YI-SQ?t=7
> 
> @yukkysaito are these results expected or do you think these results can be improved by simple tuning of the parameters?

###### @kaancolak (2022-06-12)

> I don't know the exact cause of this problem. I did not experience this problem when working with the "map" frame.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-06-13)

> The false-negative object might be caused by training set coming from a different lidar model. 
> 
> @yukkysaito or @aohsato Do you know how the current model was trained (e.g., sensor setup)? Also, is it possible to share the training script for the models? 

###### @aohsato (2022-06-14)

> @xmfcx Thank you for sharing! It's interesting.
> 
> Did you obtain your pcap data with Ouster OS1-64, correct?
> About your result of centerpoint, in [this video](https://youtu.be/J8J2e_YI-SQ), there may be a sensor model gap with the training model, but I think this pointcloud density is enough to detect the pedestrian.
> 
> We have found a similar issue and @yukke42 is currently working on it. This problem is that the sampling at centerpoint is not uniform and depends on the order of pointcloud.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-06-21)

> @aohsato 
> > We have found a similar issue and @yukke42 is currently working on it. This problem is that the sampling at centerpoint is not uniform and depends on the order of pointcloud.
> 
> Do you have any ETA on the fix? Please let us know if you would like help from the others.

###### @yukke42 (2022-06-28)

> Sorry for the late reply. I guess there are some points for worse performance:
> - lidar_centerpoint requires tf between base_link (or velodyne_top) and map to stack multi-frame pointcloud. You can set 0 [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/458a32d0e132a01a092e3e3814176e564021e91c/perception/lidar_centerpoint/launch/lidar_centerpoint.launch.xml#L14) but it gets worse performance.
> - The pointcloud data for model training is transformed to base_link of autoware.
> 
> We found that we can apply [voxel grid downsample filter](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/458a32d0e132a01a092e3e3814176e564021e91c/perception/lidar_centerpoint/launch/lidar_centerpoint.launch.xml#L14) to input cloud to detect close pedestrians with less overhead and less worse effect on the detection performance of other objects.

###### @xmfcx (2022-06-28)

> For single shot detection, if the target is moving, setting densification parameter larger than 0 would create a trail. Is this a good way of doing this? @yukke42 

###### @yukke42 (2022-06-29)

> > For single shot detection, if the target is moving, setting densification parameter larger than 0 would create a trail. Is this a good way of doing this? @yukke42
> 
> @xmfcx Yes. Densification makes better performance than only the current frame especially for pedestrian and bicycle. This method is generally used in recent 3D object detection papers.
> 

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-07-05)

> @kaancolak Could you create a separate issue for current issues that you see in perception stack?

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-08-02)

> From the ASWG meeting, we have decided to close this issue and let LeoDrive/ITRI to create more specific issues once they find any problems during integration.
> @mehmetdogru will have a final look on this issue to see if there are still remaining issues from the past discussion.

###### @mehmetdogru (2022-08-02)

> > [I will open up issues to look into the problems if it is not the expected state.](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/1008#issuecomment-1152378043)
> 
> @xmfcx please open up the issues if you already didn't do so.
> 
> I think we can close this issue.
> 
> 
>

> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The `pointcloud_preprocessor::Filter::computePublish` function seems to make unnecessary copy of intermediate point cloud:
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/a0ef0e9f4d9d074aa65dc7a1a08742b4b1a01921/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/filter.cpp#L162-L169
> 
> The `output` pointcloud is created then filled in `filter()`. Right after the cloud data is copied in a new `cloud_tf` pointer and never used again.
> 
> It is possible to verify that data is copied by using the following snippet:
> ```C++
>   auto cloud_tf = std::make_unique<PointCloud2>(output);  // set the output by default
>   printf("%p %p\n", (void*)&output.data[0], (void*)&cloud_tf->data[0]); 
> ```
> 
> Which shows on my machine:
> ```
> 0x5654f4df0650 0x5654f4d7a2c0
> 0x5654f4df0650 0x5654f4e355d0
> 0x5654f4e00f80 0x5654f4d7a2c0
> 0x5654f4df1660 0x5654f4f346d0
> ...
> ```
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Remove unnecessary copy of heavy data
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The function can be rewritten like so:
> 
> ```C++
> //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
> void pointcloud_preprocessor::Filter::computePublish(
>   const PointCloud2ConstPtr & input, const IndicesPtr & indices)
> {
>   auto cloud_tf = std::make_unique<PointCloud2>();
> 
>   // Call the virtual method in the child
>   filter(input, indices, *cloud_tf);
> 
>   // Check whether the user has given a different output TF frame
>   if (!tf_output_frame_.empty() && cloud_tf->header.frame_id != tf_output_frame_) {
>     RCLCPP_DEBUG(
>       this->get_logger(), "[computePublish] Transforming output dataset from %s to %s.",
>       cloud_tf->header.frame_id.c_str(), tf_output_frame_.c_str());
>     // Convert the cloud into the different frame
>     PointCloud2 cloud_transformed;
>     if (!pcl_ros::transformPointCloud(tf_output_frame_, *cloud_tf, cloud_transformed, *tf_buffer_)) {
>       RCLCPP_ERROR(
>         this->get_logger(), "[computePublish] Error converting output dataset from %s to %s.",
>         cloud_tf->header.frame_id.c_str(), tf_output_frame_.c_str());
>       return;
>     }
>     cloud_tf.reset(new PointCloud2(cloud_transformed));
>   }
>   if (tf_output_frame_.empty() && cloud_tf->header.frame_id != tf_input_orig_frame_) {
>     // no tf_output_frame given, transform the dataset to its original frame
>     RCLCPP_DEBUG(
>       this->get_logger(), "[computePublish] Transforming output dataset from %s back to %s.",
>       cloud_tf->header.frame_id.c_str(), tf_input_orig_frame_.c_str());
>     // Convert the cloud into the different frame
>     PointCloud2 cloud_transformed;
>     if (!pcl_ros::transformPointCloud(
>           tf_input_orig_frame_, *cloud_tf, cloud_transformed, *tf_buffer_)) {
>       RCLCPP_ERROR(
>         this->get_logger(), "[computePublish] Error converting output dataset from %s back to %s.",
>         cloud_tf->header.frame_id.c_str(), tf_input_orig_frame_.c_str());
>       return;
>     }
>     cloud_tf.reset(new PointCloud2(cloud_transformed));
>   }
> 
>   // Copy timestamp to keep it
>   cloud_tf->header.stamp = input->header.stamp;
> 
>   // Publish a boost shared ptr
>   pub_output_->publish(std::move(cloud_tf));
> }
> ```
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Cloud data no more duplicated in `computePublish`

**Comments:**

###### @yukkysaito (2022-05-31)

> @VRichardJP thank you for your PR
> Can I close this issue?

###### @VRichardJP (2022-05-31)

> Yes
> 
> I think it would make sense to create a new task to track and fix similar problems across the rest of the code base. The filter one was maybe the most important since it is used a lot with big clouds, but I saw that a few other files have the same pattern:
> 
> ```C++
> auto tmp = PointCloud2();
> someProcessing(in, tmp);
> auto output = std::make_xxx<PointCloud2>(tmp); // copy 
> ```
> 
> Where the copy can always be avoided by using the correct pointer type for tmp intermediate cloud.
> 

###### @esteve (2022-06-15)

> @BonoloAWF @VRichardJP I've created https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/1109 to track this issue across the code base, this issue can be closed IMHO

###### @esteve (2022-06-22)

> @VRichardJP
> 
> > but I saw that a few other files have the same pattern:
>

> 
> Thanks.
> 
>

### #993 — Vehicle stops ~1m further away than goal point or stop line

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-30  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-25  |  **Author:** @VRichardJP
- **Labels:** type:bug

> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> While testing autonomous driving in our vehicle, I observed that the car always stops ~1 meter after the goal point or stop line.
> 
> For example here, I set the target goal a few meters in front of the vehicle, then engage AD. The vehicle drives toward the goal, but instead of stopping exactly at the goal location (with base_link at the goal position) the vehicle drives too far and parks ~1 meter after:
> ![stop_line](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18645627/170956257-06b2981f-1486-458f-bb28-375e4cac04a9.png)
> 
> I also observed the same issue with a stop line. The vehicle stop systematically crosses the stop line and parks ~1 meter after.
> 
> I have never encountered that issue with autoware.ai or architecture proposal (ros1). My vehicle and its configuration are the same than what I used to test architecture proposal.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The vehicle base_link should stop exactly at the goal position
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The vehicle stops ~1m after goal
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. run autoware.launch in vehicle
> 2. set target goal
> 3. engage AD
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - Ubuntu 20.04
> - ROS2 galactic
> - autoware main branch
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> - wrong vehicle configuration?
> - delay on decision/cmd messages?
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

But I feel a little bit not smooth. If you have any advice to tune the brake_map for stopping behavior, could you let us know?

### #987 — motion_velocity_smoother and behavior_velocity_planner should use the same smoother algorithm

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-30  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @TomohitoAndo
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, priority:low, status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/987

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, behavior_velocity_planner uses the smoother to calculate the precise predicted velocity. But smoother algorithm type that behavior_velocity_planner uses is fixed to Analytical, so predicted velocity would be different if the motion_velocity_smoother node uses different smoother algorithm type.
> So I think the same smoother_type as motion_velocity_smoother should be passed to behavior_velocity_planner.
> 
> smoother_type for motion_velocity_smoother is specified here.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/launch/tier4_planning_launch/launch/scenario_planning/scenario_planning.launch.xml#L26-L27
> 
> behavior_velocity_planner creates an instance of smoother class (`AnalyticalJerkConstrainedSmoother` is always created)
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/src/node.cpp#L305-L310
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose of this task is to pass the `smoother_type` parameter to behavior_velocity_planner, and enables motion_velocity_smoother and behavior_velocity_planner to use the same smoother algorithm.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - modify the launch file to pass the `smoother_type` argument to behavior_velocity_planner
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Confirm motion_velocity_smoother and behavior_velocity_planner uses the same predicted velocity with all smoother type

> After discussing with @takayuki5168, I believe the issue is due to pairs of poses that are too close in distance, especially near the input poses of interpolation. This fact gives rise to a sudden change in yaw for the next consecutive poses.

> #1687 
> This PR fixes the issue somehow, but it is correcting the yaw afterwards. Increasing `epsilon` is still recommended.

So I edited `./launch/tier4_planning_launch/launch/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning/behavior_planning.launch.py` to run them in two different containers. Everything works.
> If you change the sequence of them in `behavior_planning.launch.py `, e.g `[behavior_path_planner_component, behavior_velocity_planner_component]` to `[behavior_velocity_planner_component ,behavior_path_planner_component]`, it can start. ### #957 — DRY code cleanup in the joy_controller package

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-24  |  **Closed:** 2022-05-24  |  **Author:** @samehmohamed88
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/957

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The joy_controller package has two [methods](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/control/joy_controller/src/joy_controller/joy_controller_node.cpp#L36) `getUpperShift` and `getLowerShift` which repeat the exact same code.
> 
> It's a simple DRY cleanup to refactor the code by adding a `getGearShift_` method that executes that block of code and is called by `getUpperShift` and `getLowerShift`.
> 
> I [implemented](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/compare/main...armuren:main) this in my fork, and confirm the package is building
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> DRY code cleanup
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Simple refactor.  There's no other type of issue that meets this criteria. It's not a bug or a feature request.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] CI/CD passes

**Comments:**

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-05-24)

> Hmm? I think they are not the same.

###### @samehmohamed88 (2022-05-24)

### #947 — Unreasonable freespace planning area in parking scenario

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-23  |  **Closed:** 2022-08-05  |  **Author:** @NorahXiong
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/947

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In parking scenario as below, the trajectory is extended to lanelets out of the parking lot.
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/169729706-d1d5d779-33c6-475f-9df1-d29c8ceb19cd.png)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Trajectory is limited in the parking lot when planning a trajectory to a parking spot using the freespace planner.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Trajectory is extended to lanelets out of the parking lot when planning a trajectory to a parking spot using the freespace planner.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start autoware planning simulator using default
> 2. Set pose estimate in lanelet within the parking lot
> 3. Put static obstacles to block the direct way to the target parking spot and then set the goal pose
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 20.04
> - ROS2: Galactic
> - Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> [CostmapGenerator::loadRoadAreasFromLaneletMap function](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/1696c2b081f81b43ff2900404e8478dec2cbb1c2/planning/costmap_generator/nodes/costmap_generator/costmap_generator_node.cpp#L231) - target should be limited to the parking area
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/317

### #941 — Inappropriate method in parking lot search function

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-20  |  **Closed:** 2022-06-14  |  **Author:** @NorahXiong
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/941

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> If the ego car coordinate is closer to a lanelet out of a parking lot(e.g. lanelet 34976 below) than to a lanelet in a parking lot(e.g. lanelet 35016 below), the scenario will be wrongly set to the lane-driving mode because no linked parking lots can be retrieved.
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/169473397-fb4abb45-03bb-4176-895b-3a2f378de9fa.png)
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Parking scenario activated and trajectory generated by freespace planner.
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103234047/169469119-ee500206-3eb0-45de-8eba-948b64f45c7a.png)
> 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Lane-driving scenario activated and trajectory to the goal position not correctly generated.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start autoware planning simulator using default
> 2. Set pose estimate in parking lot but not in lane, near lanelet 34976, far from lanelet 35016
> 3. Set goal pose in a parking spot
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntun 20.04
> - ROS2: Galactic
> - Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> In scenario_selector_node, if the nearest lanelet of ego car is within a parking lot then ego car will be supposed to be in the parking lot. If ego car is in lane when the system starts, everything goes right. But if the system starts inside a parking lot, unexpected result may appear. So maybe the parameter used when querying the linked parking lot should be changed from nearest lanelet to ego car position.
> 
> Related code:
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/scenario_selector/src/scenario_selector_node/scenario_selector_node.cpp#L40
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/map/lanelet2_extension/lib/query.cpp#L438
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

---

### #939 — Diagnostic topic of process_monitor sometimes may not be sent periodically

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-20  |  **Closed:** 2022-05-27  |  **Author:** @ito-san
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:system
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/939

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The diagnostic topic of process_monitor sometimes may not be sent periodically, every 1 second.
> This issue has been reported from the autonomous transportation project with evaluating on a reduced width road. 
> In addition, this issue has never been reported with a simulator.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The diagnostic topic of process_monitor should be sent periodically.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The diagnostic topic of process_monitor sometimes may not be sent periodically, almost every 1 second but sometimes 4.2 seconds.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start an autonomous driving test with a vehicle.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 20.04
> - ROS2: Galactic
> - Autoware: autoware.universe:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> I found it took 4.2 second to run `top` command, so diagnostic topic was not sent periodically.
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57388357/169437832-f16d4958-f0ac-4a3a-9803-34fb834c0b04.png)
> 
> I don't know what the root cause is, but `top` command runs in the thread of publishing diagnostic topics.
> The execution of  `top` command should be isolated from the thread of that. It should be processed in another timer thread.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @ito-san (2022-05-27)

> This issue was resolved by https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/948.

---

### #934 — Collision path when the part of obstacle crosses the centerline

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-19  |  **Closed:** 2022-06-13  |  **Author:** @shulanbushangshu
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When large obstacle is present and part of the obstacle crosses the centerline of the lane, the calculated maximum offset distance decreases rather than increases.
> In this case, the planned path would collide with the obstacle.
> ![2022-05-19 15-32-00σ▒Åσ╣òµê¬σ¢╛](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102840938/169242096-e15c2de3-dab6-4d0d-a2f3-0b3849f00021.png)
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The calculated offset distance will continue to grow, and the planned path will not collide with obstacles.
> The calculation of offset distance must be changed to deal with the obstacle (the part of obstacle crossing the centerline of the lane∩╝ë
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The calculated maximum offset distance decreases rather than increases in this case.
> The planned path collides with  large obstacle.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1.Start autoware planning simulator using default;
> 2. Set initial position and gobal position;
> 3.Set a larger obstacle(like a truck) which intersects the lanes (part of the obstacle crosses the centerline of the lane)between initial position and gobal position.
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> 1.OS: Ubuntun 20.04
> 2.ROS2: Galactic
> 3.Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The calculation of offset distance can not deal with obstacle that partially cross the centerline. The calculated maximum offset distance decreases in this case.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

> I think following parameters should be managed centrally at least, because if parameters are not commonized throughout the autoware, the possibility of unexpected malfunctions increases.
> 
> - velocity threshold to judge whether the vehicle has stopped
> - distance threshold to judge whether the vehicle has reached target point
> 
> Related Issue: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/744
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Load following parameters that should be managed centrally as global parameters.
> 
> - velocity threshold to judge whether the vehicle has stopped
> - distance threshold to judge whether the vehicle has reached target point
> - (Other parameters as needed.)
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - use `global_parameter_loader`
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] create common config file
> - [ ] all nodes in autoware can get common config as global parameters.

###### @esteve (2022-05-23)

> Here's a summary of what I learned about TVM (thanks @ambroise-arm for your help, please let me know if there's anything incorrect):
> 
>  - TVM aims to be backend agnostic when developing, but once it gets deployed it targets the desired backend
>  - The workflow is as follows:
>    - Parse the ONNX files via ARM's `tvm_cli.py` tool (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/modelzoo/blob/master/scripts/tvm_cli/tvm_cli.py), which will tune the model using AutoTVM.
>    - The script will generate several files:
>      - A network module in the form of a shared library (`deploy_lib.so`)
>      - A JSON file describing the network graph (`deploy_graph.json`)
>      - A file containing the parameters of the network (`deploy_param.params`)
>      - A header file with the configuration of the inference engine (`inference_engine_tvm_config.hpp`)
>  - In the C++ load the `deploy_lib.so` via TVM's `dload` mechanism, this enables the code to be platform agnostic while being performant at the same time
>  - TVM allows developers to use backend-specific code (e.g. CUDA), though the goal is to abstract that entirely
> 
> Notes
> 
>   - The TVM team is working on their own CLI tool called TVMC (https://tvm.apache.org/docs/tutorial/tvmc_command_line_driver.html), which would supersede `tvm_cli.py`
>   - ARM ported Autoware.AI's [lidar_point_pillars](https://github.com/Autoware-AI/core_perception/tree/master/lidar_point_pillars) package from TensorRT to TVM, this can be used as a reference on how to migrate to TVM. It currently contains backend-specific code through CUDA. Additionally, both TensorRT and TVM are supported and one is chosen at build time (TVM is the default).

The onnx neural network can be committed to the repository (with the relevant definition.yaml file, and possible modifications to the script to have it compile). That way the network will start to get compiled and uploaded automatically to the S3 bucket as part of the ModelZoo CI (currently for llvm and vulkan backends). (see [diagrams](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/2557) of the architecture)
> 
> Currently ModelZoo uses TVM 0.8 to compile the models. And the [tvm_vendor](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/tvm_vendor) package that provides the runtime capability to Autoware is also on version 0.8 at the moment.
> If there is a need to update to TVM 0.9 for Lidar Centerpoint to work, that can be scheduled. But we won't be using a development version, so no 0.10 until it is released.
> 
> #### Package
> 
> Yes, I think it is important to have a dedicated package for `lidar_centerpoint_tvm`. The [tvm_utility](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/common/tvm_utility) package provides a `pipeline.hpp` header so that all packages that make use of TVM in Autoware can use a common interface both for downloading the compiled models and for the inference. `tvm_utility` has a yolo_v2_tiny test case as an example. And `lidar_apollo_segmentation_tvm` acts as an example for a standalone package. I think it would be good for `lidar_centerpoint_tvm` to also use the interface provided by `tvm_utility`.
> That way, when the change in artifacts structure you mentioned with TVM 0.10 happens, it can be taken care of on the Autoware side by only changing `tvm_utility` instead of the individual packages that make use of it.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-12  |  **Closed:** 2022-09-29  |  **Author:** @rej55

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Develop an interface to compensate decisions from Autoware.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Operating an autonomous driving system, it often happens that the perception results are unreliable.
> This causes a unsafe planning.
> 
> However, it is difficult to get perfect perception results.
> So, some ways to compensate decisions are needed.
> 
> To achieve a safety operation under the uncertain perception, approving for decisions is one of the way.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Develop an interface class to cooperation.
> 
> There are many situations to need decisions with perception results.
> So, it is difficult to develop interfaces individually.
> 
> In this task, we aim to achieve the purpose by developing an interface class to cooperation.
> After developing, we can integrate individual scenes to request a cooperation for compensate decisions.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - Develop an interface class to cooperation
> - Integrate it to behavior modules

### #867 — Add more detail about the min_behavior_stop_margin parameter to the Obstacle Stop Planner documentation

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-09  |  **Closed:** 2022-05-20  |  **Author:** @ghost
- **Labels:** type:new-feature
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/867

**Body:**

> In https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/discussions/270, @08beeqtufail-sudo described a use case where a stop line is created (eg: at an intersection) but the ego vehicle stops earlier than expected due to an obstacle that exists just beyond the stop line. 
> 
> @takahoribe [explained that this behaviour can be managed with the `stop_planner.min_behavior_stop_margin` parameter](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/discussions/270#discussioncomment-2710929), and provided the following detail:
> 
> The stop_planner 's behavior is like this:
> 
>  - Set `v=0` at the point from `stop_margin` distance from an obstacle.
>  - If another stop point already exists between an obstacle and ego (like in this case), set `v=0` at the point from `min_behavior_stop_margin` distance from an obstacle.
> 
> Generally `min_behavior_stop_margin` is set to be smaller than the `stop_margin`. See the [default parameter](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/config/obstacle_stop_planner.param.yaml/#L4-L5). 
> 
> If you tune the parameter `min_behavior_stop_margin`, the vehicle will move as you expect.
> 
> 
> The information above should be added to the [existing Obstacle Stop Planner documentation](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/obstacle_stop_planner/#obstacle-stop-planner_1). 

**Comments:**

###### @satoshi-ota (2022-05-16)

> @LalithVipulananthan @TakaHoribe
> May I close this issue since more detail documentation about the `min_behavior_stop_margin` has been added in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/880 ?

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-05-20)

> Addressed in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/880

### #861 — A bug in scenario_simulator in the presence of multiple parking lots

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-06  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @kminoda
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:help-wanted, priority:low, status:stale, component:planning
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/861

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Related discussion: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/discussions/2576
> 
> The parking scenario in Autoware behaves oddly when there exist multiple parking lots on a map.
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44218668/166207450-2950ad13-2281-4e24-abee-ccaeef6625cb.mp4
> 
> When I initialized a robot on a parking_lot, the planning module selects a parking scenario even though the goal parking_space is on the other parking_lot.
> 
> From now on, I will refer to `parking_space` as a parking spot and `parking_lot` as a parking area (the same way as defined in lanelet2).
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> It is expected that the vehicle select lane_driving to approach the parking lot nearby the goal, and once it arrived, it should change its mode to parking scenario.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The planning module outputs a parking scenario trajectory even though the goal parking_space is on the other parking_lot area.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Build [this meta-repository](https://github.com/team-tier4-FY22/autoware.diff_drive)
> 2. Download [this file](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UjogQQPqm0Yc3tRLgUhjtGaj0TOY6dQQ/view?usp=sharing)
> 
> 3. Launch autoware_launch with the following command
> ```
> $ ros2 launch autoware_launch autoware.launch.xml vehicle_model:=sample_diff_drive sensor_model:=sample_diff_drive_sensor_kit map_path:=YOUR_MAP_PATH
> ```
> 4. On RViz, initialize the vehicle position on a parking_lot, and set the goal to a parking_space that is not on the parking_lot in which the vehicle is
> 5. See the calculated path on RViz
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 20.04
> - ROS2: galactic
> - Autoware (commit ID of autoware): af25faddd16bf8f9a1bace814b0f82e020803f5b
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> It seems that this issue is caused by a bug in `scenario_selector`.
> It appears that it proceeds to the parking scenario when the following two conditions are met:
> 1. the goal is on a `parking_space`
> 2. the vehicle is on the nearest `parking_lot`
> 
> However, when multiple `parking_lot` exist, the vehicle starts parking even though it's on a different `parking_lot` that corresponds to its goal `parking_space`. 
> 
> ### Additional context
> Related PR(draft): https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/860
> _No response_

### #859 — Monitoring a Bluetooth connection

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-05-06  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-05  |  **Author:** @ito-san
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:system
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/859

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Add a feature to monitor a Bluetooth connection to a wireless controller.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Autonomous delivery robot made by TIER IV uses a Bluetooth wireless controller (DUAL SHOCK4) to control a robot nearby.
> When far away from a robot, a wireless controller doesn't work, so monitoring a Bluetooth connection on the robot side is needed  to notify an operator that the controller is not working, or to stop driving.
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57388357/167051826-76450218-00fe-4f24-a279-a411308c7d1c.png)
> 
> It could occur that Bluetooth still connected but a controller doesn't work. so monitoring should be performed by check some kind of Bluetooth command.
> L2ping is a good approach to resolve this issue. L2ping generates PING echo command on Bluetooth L2CAP layer, and it is able to receive and check echo response from a wireless device.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Create a ROS2 node to monitor a Bluetooth connection. 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Create a ROS2 node to monitor a Bluetooth connection
> - [x] Run tests

### #833 — Potential collision risk with long obstacles

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-28  |  **Closed:** 2022-06-14  |  **Author:** @shulanbushangshu
- **Labels:** type:bug, priority:high, component:planning
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/833

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When the length of obstacle is long, the path planned  by avoidance of behavior_path_planner is too close to the obstacle when returning. Collisions is possible in this case.
> The influence of the length of obstacle on the path is not considered when calculating the maximum offset return point.
> <img width="511" alt="12" src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102840938/165696542-6bee8c6f-5386-49f7-9f77-a799d4d81fa2.png">
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The longitudinal distance of the maximum return point on the path should be calculated taking into account the length of the obstacle to prevent premature return.The  maximum return point  can be  behind obstacle.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The path planned during obstacle avoidance is too close to the obstacle when returning in  certain obstacle distributions
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1.Start autoware planning simulator using default;
> 2. Set  initial position and gobal  position;
> 3.Set a obstacle which intersects  the lanes (change the length of obstacle,like picture below) between  initial position and gobal  position.
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> 1.OS: Ubuntun 20.04
> 2.ROS2: Galactic
> 3.Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
> 
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> package : behavior_path_planner
> The influence of the length of obstacle on the path is not considered when calculating the maximum offset return point.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #832 — Separate surround_obstacle_checker from hierarchical planning flow by using external velocity limit

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-28  |  **Closed:** 2022-05-09  |  **Author:** @satoshi-ota
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:planning
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/832

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The function of surround_obstacle_checker is to keep the stopped state when the vehicle is stopped and there are obstacles around the vehicle. In current implementation, the feature is achieved by inserting ZERO velocity into trajectory in the hierarchical motion planning flow.
> On the other hand, the feature is also achieved by using external velocity limit with simpler implementation. (no need to insert stop point)
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - separate `surround_obstacle_checker` from hierarchical planning flow.
> - simplify `surround_obstacle_checker` implementation. (not handling trajectory topic in the node)
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - use external velocity limit in `surround_obstacle_checker`
> - insert ZERO velocity in `motion_velocity_smoother`
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - achieve the feature of `surround_obstacle_checker` by using external velocity limit

**Comments:**

###### @satoshi-ota (2022-05-09)

> cc @TakaHoribe @yukkysaito

### #822 — Steering angle limit reached in simulation

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-27  |  **Closed:** 2022-04-28  |  **Author:** @08beeqtufail-sudo
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/822

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Hello guys, 
> I am testing this repository in simulation with the sample lanelet2 and pointcloud maps provided. As i try to run the simulation with planning_simulator.launch.xml, i can see that the steering angle displayed in rviz reaches a limit of 20 degrees in the curves and never goes beyond it. It feels like somewhere the steering limit is being set to 20 degrees. The effect is more visible if we change the vehicle info parameters (bigger vehicle). In this case, the vehicle goes completely out of lane before coming back because the steering angle is limited to 20 degrees and it needs to steer more for bigger vehicles in curves. Do you guys have any suggestions as what could be the possible cause?
>  
> Note: I have already verified the max_steer_deg value in obstacle_avoidance_planner module and it is 40 degrees. Also, i have deactivated both EB optimization and mpt optimization to see whether it is related to optimization but it doesn't change the behavior.
> 
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/60785554/165594957-28df4685-4168-4005-a47c-06d3a24ac873.mp4
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> In a sharp curve, steering angle should not be saturated at 20 degrees. 
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The steering angle is saturated at 20 degrees
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> - Change the vehicle_info parameters as follows:
>     wheel_radius: 0.39
>     wheel_width: 0.42
>     wheel_base: 3.682 # between front wheel center and rear wheel center
>     wheel_tread: 1.750 # between left wheel center and right wheel center
>     front_overhang: 0.869 # between front wheel center and vehicle front
>     rear_overhang: 1.024 # between rear wheel center and vehicle rear
>     left_overhang: 0.360 # between left wheel center and vehicle left
>     right_overhang: 0.360 # between right wheel center and vehicle right
>     vehicle_height: 2.499
> 
> - Run the planning simulator
> - Give an initial pose and specify a goal pose such that the path has a sharp curve.
> You will see that the steering angle is saturate to 20 degrees in sharp curves, which leads to the vehicle going out of its lane.
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS : Ubuntu 20.04
> - ROS2: galactic
> - Autoware: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/tree/main 
>  The commit number b260f67085dda5c0161ade051b236a3fbdee4147  dated 29 March 2022
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @JianKangEgon (2022-04-28)

> @08beeqtufail-sudo Hi, although the video seems to be broken from my side. But you can just modify this value "steer_lim_deg" in the config file src/universe/autoware/launch/tier4_control_launch/config/trajectory_follower/lateral_controller.param.yaml
> 
> This parameter is to limit the output of lateral controller regarding steering angle. I've checked this param is currently updated to 40.0

###### @08beeqtufail-sudo (2022-04-28)

> @JianKangEgon Thank you for your response. Indeed that was the problem. It's working as expected now. I will close this issue.

- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> During lane change, no lane following path is generated.
> ![Screenshot from 2022-04-26 09-27-25](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93502286/165196172-4b2d7839-d63b-45ec-9e30-319e58cd98a5.png)
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> If the distance is sufficient, a lane following trajectory should also be visualize
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The should be two path generated in this case, the first is the lane following trajectory, and another is the candidate path.
> ![Screenshot from 2022-04-26 09-25-07](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93502286/165196313-6b5ac4f1-a939-4981-afc6-bd20f9cad03f.png)

> 
> 1. Run autoware
> 2. Select start and end pose. Then end pose should be a lane change and should not place after intersection.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntu 20.04
> - ROS: Galactic
> - Autoware: Universe
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> To check for an intersection, `checkLaneIsInIntersection`  requires at least two lanelets in the lane sequence. 
> 
> However, the lane sequence size check only look for `empty` and not `size == 1`
> 
> ```
> bool checkLaneIsInIntersection(
>   const RouteHandler & route_handler, const PathWithLaneId & reference_path,
>   const lanelet::ConstLanelets & lanelet_sequence, double & additional_length_to_add)
> {
>   if (lanelet_sequence.empty()) {
>     return false;
>   }
> 
>  .......
> }
> 
> ```
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

### #800 — The output of the gnss_poser package is not suitable for ekf

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-25  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-26  |  **Author:** @meliketanrikulu
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, priority:high, component:localization
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/800

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> The gnss_poser package generates the 21., 28., 35. indices of the 4x4 covariance matrix by giving default values. You can see in [these](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/b03d565c1ea455a23bd85f7cc751d3e508f63bfc/sensing/gnss_poser/src/gnss_poser_core.cpp#L134) lines.   (Because it only receives [nav_sat_fix](https://docs.ros.org/en/api/sensor_msgs/html/msg/NavSatFix.html) message as input. The nav_sat_fix message contains a 3x3 covariance matrix. So it only contains covariance values for x,y,z. Does not include covariance values for roll pitch yaw)
> 
> Therefore, when we want to use the ekf_localizer package with the output of the gnss_poser package, we get incorrect results in the returns. You can see results in this [link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VonYFqhLMW8)
> 
> We observed that the results improved when we gave the correct values to the 21st, 28th and 35th values of the covariance matrix in the gnss_poser package.  You can see results in this [link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C7mtFypo97U)
> 
> We will need to be able to run the ekf_localizer package with the gnss-ins data. So the gnss_poser package needs to be updated.
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> We observed that the results improved when we gave the correct values to the 21st, 28th and 35th values of the covariance matrix in the gnss_poser package. You can see results in this [link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C7mtFypo97U)
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> When we want to use the ekf_localizer package with the output of the gnss_poser package, we get incorrect results in the returns. You can see results in this [link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VonYFqhLMW8)
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> You can observe the results yourself by running the output of gnss_poser and ekf_localizer together.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The gnss_poser package generates the 21., 28., 35. indices of the 4x4 covariance matrix by giving default values. You can see in [these](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/b03d565c1ea455a23bd85f7cc751d3e508f63bfc/sensing/gnss_poser/src/gnss_poser_core.cpp#L134) lines.   (Because it only receives [nav_sat_fix](https://docs.ros.org/en/api/sensor_msgs/html/msg/NavSatFix.html) message as input. The nav_sat_fix message contains a 3x3 covariance matrix. So it only contains covariance values for x,y,z. Does not include covariance values for roll pitch yaw)
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @YamatoAndo (2022-04-26)

> @meliketanrikulu Thank you for your report!
> The default values were set without any verification, so I would like to be able to set them to appropriate values.
> 
> How about being able to change the values from a config file?

###### @xmfcx (2022-04-26)

> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/discussions/2550

###### @meliketanrikulu (2022-05-12)

> Hello. In autoware_universe, I see that GNSS is not currently used as a localization source in localization design. 
> 
> ![localization design](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13819566/167943612-418696de-2a0c-42fb-bb63-7983362465e5.png)
> 
> GNSS seems to be used only for initial_pose estimation. Is it planned to perform positioning by receiving the pose message from NDT and GNSS to ekf_localizer in the future? I think GNSS is an important source of localization. It may be more appropriate to fuse NDT and GNSS poses using EKF. What do you think about this? Maybe we can handle this issue this way too.

###### @YamatoAndo (2022-05-12)

> Yes! I have not gotten around to it yet, but that's what I was thinking!
> 
> As for other ways to use GNSS information, someone in my company is considering integrating GNSS information during NDT scan matching optimization calculations.

###### @xmfcx (2022-05-17)

> The required messages will be generated within the autoware_sensing_msgs in next week's Autoware Architecture Meeting.

###### @xmfcx (2022-05-17)

> The figure you've sent is outdated, there should be an arrow going from gnss_poser to ekf_localizer, we will update it in the documentation.

###### @xmfcx (2022-07-26)

> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/1230 has fixed this issue.
