### #798 — obstacle_avoidance_planner dies when the interval of path points is long

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-25  |  **Closed:** 2022-08-19  |  **Author:** @kosuke55
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:help-wanted, priority:low, component:planning
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/798

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> **This is a problem that does not occur with the current hard code, but could potentially occur.**
> 
> truncated_points size will be `1` when the interval of points in path is less than [`5.0`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/obstacle_avoidance_planner/src/node.cpp#L1384). This causes the node to die when it finally accesses [`seg_idx + 1`](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/common/tier4_autoware_utils/include/tier4_autoware_utils/trajectory/trajectory.hpp#L128)
> The interval between paths of `behavior_velocity` is [`1.0` with interporate](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/include/utilization/path_utilization.hpp#L31-L33), so this is implicitly avoided.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> obstacle_avoidance_planner does not die with any interval of path points.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> obstacle_avoidance_planner dies with interval longer than 5.0.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Set [interval of path points](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/include/utilization/path_utilization.hpp#L31-L33) greater than [clip length](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/obstacle_avoidance_planner/src/node.cpp#L1384) 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @kosuke55 (2022-04-25)

> @takayuki5168 

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-06-14)

> @kosuke55 @takayuki5168 Do you have any plan to fix this issue? (or do have any idea about the approach so that others can work on the implementation?)

###### @kosuke55 (2022-06-15)

> @mitsudome-r 
> Since this does not currently occur with the current hard code, there are no plans to deal with this issue as a low priority.

---

### #796 — Use /vehicle/status/velocity_status as the input for lat/lon controller instead of /localization/kinematic_state

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-25  |  **Closed:** 2022-05-16  |  **Author:** @JianKangEgon
- **Labels:** component:localization, component:control
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/796

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently, the control module takes the kinematic states from localization module as the input. In other words, the performance of control module relies on the localization results by a large margin. In simulator, it works fine indeed, because the localization module and vehicle module are actually fake. 
> 
> However, during road test on real vehicle, the robustness of localization module performs less reliable as vehicle driving-by-wire module, or wheel odometry sensor for robot. From my understanding, the algorithms of localization module (ICP / NDT matcher) are iterate computation progress.  Sometimes, the steering wheel jitters due to the lost localization matcher. In comparison, the can bus data or odometer could provide relatively more helpful information.
> 
> By communication with the vehicle can bus or wheel encoder, the control module is able to acquire a much more accurate value. Thus, I'd love to propose this issue and discuss if it's reasonable to do so.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Read vehicle velocity from can bus (or wheel encoder of robot) if these information are available.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - Remap the input topic for control module from /localization/kinematic_state to /vehicle/status/velocity_status as the velocity source.
> - Change the corresponding message type
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Rewrite the node file to change the topic message type.
> 
> - [ ] Build successfully without any conflict
> 
> - [ ] Validation and verification in both planning simulator and road test on real vehicle

**Comments:**

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-04-25)

> Thank you for your post.
> 
> The can bus speed information (` /vehicle/status/velocity_status`) is passed to the localization module for proper processing. If the can bus information is clearly more accurate than the localization matching, you can tell the information to the localization module through the error covariance.
> 
> The localization module also handles cases where the speed information from the can bus is disconnected. In such cases, the speed is calculated from the position estimation results. Therefore, I would suggest tuning the covariance parameters in Twist message sent to the EKF instead of sending the can bus information directly to the control module.

###### @JianKangEgon (2022-04-25)

> @TakaHoribe Thanks for your quick reply. This solves my concern. 

###### @Sharrrrk (2022-04-25)

> I would suggest to analyze from three perspectives: accuracy and delay and safety.
> 
> ### Aaccuracy
> **vehicle can speed**: in normal passenger cars, vehicle speed is calculated by ESP/ABS ECU based on WSS (wheel speed sensor), take narmal sedan for example, the accuracy of vehicle speed is around  0.002 m/s.
> **EKF output**: the accuracy the EKF could reach depends on the input source with best accuracy, RTK take xsens 680G as example has velocity accuracy of 0.05 m/s; while for NDT, I can not provide solid data, but it could not be better than 0.03m in range which leads to ~0.003m/s in speed with 10hz LiDAR scans. 
> **Result** We could say that they have similar accuracy performance.
> 
> ### Delay
> **vehicle can speed**: The delay of vehicle can speed is the processing time in ECU plus transmission time to AD computer, which is defined by n*10ms.
> **EKF output**: The EKF output delay depends on multiple sources, for EKF the delay is much smaller but with less confidence level, while with vehicle speed as input, the confidence level is high yet additional processing time is required for EKF algorism.
> **Result** Overall similar performance of both.
> 
> ### Safety
> **vehicle can speed**: The vehicle ECU and CAN netork is designed to have high safety level, as long as the AD computer can communicate via CAN, the safety of the signal chain is solid. Also as long as the AD computer could send out CAN control message, it definitely reads back the vehicle can speed.
> **EKF output**: With additional input sources and addtional nodes, more risks is introduced to the whole pipeline and makes it a less safe solution .
> **Result** vehicle CAN speed safer.
> 
> ### Summary
> 
> | Item | vehicle CAN speed | EKF twist output|
> | ---  | --- | --- |
> | Accuracy | Good | Good |
> | Delay | Good | Good |
> | Safety | Good | Not good|
> 
> So in my oppinion, it's better to use vehicle CAN speed directly in control module for bettery safety, while using EKF twist output does not introduce better perfomance in accuracy or delay.
> 

###### @plane-li (2022-04-26)

> 
> 
> 
> > Thank you for your post.
> > 
> > The can bus speed information (` /vehicle/status/velocity_status`) is passed to the localization module for proper processing. If the can bus information is clearly more accurate than the localization matching, you can tell the information to the localization module through the error covariance.
> > 
> > The localization module also handles cases where the speed information from the can bus is disconnected. In such cases, the speed is calculated from the position estimation results. Therefore, I would suggest tuning the covariance parameters in Twist message sent to the EKF instead of sending the can bus information directly to the control module.
> 
> I agree with you! However,sometimes, the output of localization will shake in the longitudinal direction,which will lead to small different in velocity between EKF and Can bus.  I think it may caused by the ndt when vehicle run on the road which has little variation in the longitudinal  direction.
> 

###### @Sharrrrk (2022-05-16)

> Refer to https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/291#discussioncomment-2731408
> Will close this issue.

---

### #744 — The dicision of vehicle state (vehicle is stopping or moving) should be judged by a common node.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-21  |  **Closed:** 2022-09-25  |  **Author:** @satoshi-ota
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:planning, component:control
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/744

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> In current architecture, various nodes judge whether the vehicle is stopping or moving independently. For example, the following nodes has function to judge the vehicle state and the threshold parameters individually:
> 
> - planning/behavior_velocity_planner
> - control/longitudinal_controller
> - control/vehicle_cmd_gate
> 
> On the other hand, these function has no common criteria for stopping or moving. I think if the criteria are not commonized throughout the autoware, the possibility of unexpected malfunctions increases. Futhermore, the maintenance costs also increase due to double management of parameters.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose of this task is to create node that judges whether the vehicle is stopping or moving and publishes the vehicle state to other nodes. In addition, I think that the elapsed time since the vehicle transitioned to the current status, because some nodes want to know that how many seconds have elapsed since the vehicle has stopped (e.g. `stop_line` module in behavior_velocity_planner).
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> - create new node
> - create new topic type
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [ ] Create node that judges and publishes the vehicle state (stopping or moving) with elapsed time since the vehicle transitioned to the current status.
> - [ ] Replace functions defined in various nodes with topics output from the node that created in this task.

**Comments:**

###### @satoshi-ota (2022-04-21)

> cc @TakaHoribe @yukkysaito 

###### @JianKangEgon (2022-04-22)

> It's a good idea to monitor vehicle state by one united node. From road test of real vehicle on site, as far as I'm concerned, the localization kinematics status and vehicle status from driving-by-wire module are supposed to be taken in to account as well. If these motion data are aligned with each other or not.

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-23)

> @satoshi-ota 
> We already have `stop_filter` package here. This is not used at all though.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/tree/main/localization/stop_filter

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-23)

> Currently velocity and angular velocity are considered. IMO, acceleration and angular acceleration must be considered as well, at least.

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
>

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.

> 
> When the goal pose is given to Autoware, usually by "2D Goal Pose" rviz plugin, mission_planner recognized that the goal pose's z is 0, and publishes the goal pose marker whose z is 0.
> This may cause some misleading to any calculation using the goal pose or visualization.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> For "2D Goal Pose", since it does not set a z value as the name suggests, mission planner should calculate the proper z value based on the lanelet so that the goal pose will be aligned to the lanelet.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> The goal pose's z is 0.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Just set the goal pose with "2D Goal Pose" rviz plugin.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-16)

> @yukkysaito @mitsudome-r What do you think.
> If the goal pose given to mission_planner may contain the z value in the future, we have to discuss more.

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-18)

> cc @TakaHoribe @kosuke55 

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-20)

> @yukkysaito @mitsudome-r kindly ping.

###### @xmfcx (2022-06-14)

> We can republish the 2D Goal Pose from the mission planner with correct Z coordinates.
> 
> @angry-crab would like to work on this.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-06-14)

> Additional description to @xmfcx's comment:
> 
> Right now, the mission_planner(global planner) is not capable of handling z value in the given pose/goal properly to search for closest lane in z direction so I don't think it's worth creating another rviz plugin. (I also feel uncomfortable to create a plugin that depends on a map message)
> 
> If it is just a visualization issue, we can make the mission_planner to realign the given goal pose with the lane height and republish the marker.

### #706 — Wrong path planned by avoidance module in a special case

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-15  |  **Closed:** 2022-06-21  |  **Author:** @shulanbushangshu
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/706

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When the ego vehicle encounters obstacles near discontinuous adjacent lanes (see picture below), part of the path planned by avoidance module of behavior_path_planner exceeds the driveable area.
> This triggers the corresponding protection function of obstacle_avoidance_planner to stop the ego vehicle.
> However, after the obstacle disappears, the vehicle will not withdraw from the obstacle avoidance behavior because the offset path has been calculated, thus causing the vehicle to be stuck in place.
> ![ssj_marked](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102840938/163552016-78c2929b-20c7-4593-b30a-41d86cf398a1.png)
> 
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Planned path shall be within the driveable area, not entering undefined area in vector map.
> Ego vehicle shall continue to drive after the obstacle disappears in the scene above.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Part of the planned path exceeds the driveable area and enters the undefined area of map.
> After the obstacle disappears, the ego vehicle stands still.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Start autoware planning simulator using default
> 2. Set a obstacle near discontinuous adjacent lanes (like picture below)
> 3. Engage
> 4. Delete the obstacle
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS: Ubuntun 20.04
> - ROS2:  Galactic
> - Autoware: Autoware.universe:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> behavior_path_planner only check the max shift point in planned path, which is this case, is within the driveable area. This check does not apply on other points of the planned path. But obstacle_avoidance_planner will check all the points of the planned path.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @yukkysaito (2022-04-15)

> Can you provide a map and rosbag?
> cc @takayuki5168 

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-04-15)

> Thank you for your issue! 
> We have recognized this issue before (please see the [design document - unimplemented parts - cancel avoidance when target disappears](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware.universe/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/behavior_path_planner_avoidance-design/#future-extensions-unimplemented-parts)). 
> And we are in the process of improvement.
> 
> There should be more items to be fixed, as you say, the behavior_path should be inside the drivable area. The avoidance still has an issue in this kind of edge place (where the lane boundary changes along the path).

### #705 — the "crop_box_filter" can cause error in the subsequent module.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-15  |  **Closed:** 2022-06-21  |  **Author:** @plane-li
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:perception, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/705

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> When run the autoware_launch,It always throw the error **Invalid input!** and the warning: **Invalid PointCloud (data = 513168, width = 167,height = 64,step = 48)**
> I think it was caused by the crop_box_filter_nodelet.cpp.
> And the subsequent module(common_ground_filter and random_downsample_filter  ) can not publish any topic.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> there should not be any error about the  pointcloud_preprocessor when run the autoware.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> common_ground_filter throws out error:"Invalid input" and the warning: "Invalid PointCloud"
> ![20220415-pointcloud_preprocessor](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103238330/163546437-e59fdb8f-6fb1-498d-9624-b78865b2364b.png)
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> ros2 launch autoware_launch autoware.launch.xml map_path:=/home/adlink/workspace/autoware.universe/map vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - OS:ubuntu20.04
> - ROS: ros-galactic
> - Autoware: autoware:main
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The errors are printed in
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/include/pointcloud_preprocessor/filter.hpp#L224-L235:  
> inline bool isValid(
>     const PointCloud2ConstPtr & cloud, const std::string & /*topic_name*/ = "input")
>   {
>     if (cloud->width * cloud->height * cloud->point_step != cloud->data.size()) {
>       RCLCPP_WARN(
>         this->get_logger(),
>         "Invalid PointCloud (data = %zu, width = %d, height = %d, step = %d) with stamp %f, "
>         "and frame %s received!",
>         cloud->data.size(), cloud->width, cloud->height, cloud->point_step,
>         rclcpp::Time(cloud->header.stamp).seconds(), cloud->header.frame_id.c_str());
>       return false;
>     }
> 
> The problem was cause by the  (cloud->width * cloud->height * cloud->point_step != cloud->data.size()).And in the 
> sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/crop_box_filter/crop_box_filter_nodelet.cpp
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/crop_box_filter/crop_box_filter_nodelet.cpp#L124-L130
>   output.data.resize(j);
>   output.header.frame_id = input->header.frame_id;
>   output.height = input->height;
>   output.fields = input->fields;
>   output.is_bigendian = input->is_bigendian;
>   output.point_step = input->point_step;
>   output.is_dense = input->is_dense; 
> 
> and I think in output.data.size() is less the the input pointcloud size before crop_box_filter.And the out.width,height and step are equal to the input. So It may cause the problem.
> 
> At present,I solve it by using the pcl as below:
> 
>   pcl::PCLPointCloud2::Ptr pcl_input(new pcl::PCLPointCloud2);
>   pcl_conversions::toPCL(*(input), *(pcl_input));
>   impl_.setInputCloud(pcl_input);
>   impl_.setIndices(indices);
>   pcl::PCLPointCloud2 pcl_output;
>   impl_.filter(pcl_output);
>   pcl_conversions::moveFromPCL(pcl_output, outpu
> 
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @plane-li (2022-05-10)

> the fix method can be seen in the pr #881

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-06-21)

> @plane-li Is this solved with https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/951? If so, can we close the issue?

###### @plane-li (2022-06-21)

> > @plane-li Is this solved with #951? If so, can we close the issue?
> 
> OK∩╝ü

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
>

> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.

> 
> ### Description
> 
> atfer LidarApolloInstanceSegmentation recv point cloud∩╝îit first change cloud from lidar frame(like velodyne_top) to target frame(like base_link), however,in 
> 
> >  bool LidarApolloInstanceSegmentation::transformCloud(
>   const sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2 & input, sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2 & transformed_cloud,
>   float z_offset)
> 
> transformed_cloud frame id is not set correctly.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> set  transformed_cloud frame_id to base_link
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> set  transformed_cloud frame_id to velodyne_top
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. set 'target_frame' in launch.xml to 'base_link'
> 2. play a liadr bag with frame_id 'velodyne_top' 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> frame_id of `pcl_transformed_cloud` is not properly set
> 
> ## solution
> add   `  pcl_transformed_cloud.header.frame_id = target_frame_;` 
> ``` diff
> bool LidarApolloInstanceSegmentation::transformCloud(
>   const sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2 & input, sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2 & transformed_cloud,
>   float z_offset)
> {
>   // TODO(mitsudome-r): remove conversion once pcl_ros transform are available.
>   pcl::PointCloud<pcl::PointXYZI> pcl_input, pcl_transformed_cloud;
>   pcl::fromROSMsg(input, pcl_input);
> 
>   // transform pointcloud to target_frame
>   if (target_frame_ != input.header.frame_id) {
>     try {
>       geometry_msgs::msg::TransformStamped transform_stamped;
>       transform_stamped = tf_buffer_.lookupTransform(
>         target_frame_, input.header.frame_id, input.header.stamp, std::chrono::milliseconds(500));
>       Eigen::Matrix4f affine_matrix =
>         tf2::transformToEigen(transform_stamped.transform).matrix().cast<float>();
>       pcl::transformPointCloud(pcl_input, pcl_transformed_cloud, affine_matrix);
>       transformed_cloud.header.frame_id = target_frame_;
> +      pcl_transformed_cloud.header.frame_id = target_frame_;
> 
>     } catch (tf2::TransformException & ex) {
>       RCLCPP_WARN(node_->get_logger(), "%s", ex.what());
>       return false;
>     }
>   } else {
>     pcl_transformed_cloud = pcl_input;
>   }
> 
>   // move pointcloud z_offset in z axis
>   pcl::PointCloud<pcl::PointXYZI> pointcloud_with_z_offset;
>   Eigen::Affine3f z_up_translation(Eigen::Translation3f(0, 0, z_offset));
>   Eigen::Matrix4f z_up_transform = z_up_translation.matrix();
>   pcl::transformPointCloud(pcl_transformed_cloud, pcl_transformed_cloud, z_up_transform);
> 
>   pcl::toROSMsg(pcl_transformed_cloud, transformed_cloud);
> 
>   return true;
> }
> ```
> 
>

>

### #701 — Change longitudinal controller from rate to period control

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-15  |  **Closed:** 2022-04-27  |  **Author:** @Sharrrrk
- **Labels:** priority:high, component:control
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/701

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Change the control type of longitudinal controller from rate to period.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Currently in trajectory_follower_nodes package, lateral controller is using parameter _ctrl_period_ to define the period, while logitudinal controoller is using _control_rate_ to define the rate. But on real vehicles, period is used to defined how long a control command should be sent. 
> For example, the _control_rate_ of logitudinal controller is defined as 30 by default, which leads to the period of the logitudinal control rate to be 33.33333 ms, which is not a possible period for real vehicle control interface. On the other hands, in code, rate is transferred to period to setup a timer callback, which is not necessary.
> The purpose of this task is to change the control type of longitudinal controller, so that control period is used to defined how long the longitudinal control command should be sent, so that it consistent with lateral controller and real vehicle.
> 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Replace the parameter _control_rate_ to _longitudinal_ctrl_period_, and update the code and doc accordingly.
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] Code update.
> - [x] Document update.
> - [x] Tested.

**Comments:**

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-04-15)

> Thank you for your issue! I totally agree with this approach.
> 

###### @JianKangEgon (2022-04-15)

> One thing to mention is that the duplicated name in parameter configuration file may cause conflict, so it's better to add prefix / suffix if necessary. Although, the namespace is supposed to be useful, but actually, from my own experience, it does not work at all......

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-04-15)

> @JianKangEgon Good point. In ros2, every parameter is basically defined under each node. Thus we have to call the parameter with the node name like `ros2 param get /trajectory_follower/lateral_controller control_rate`. This is exactly the mechanism introduced in ros2 to prevent the parameter conflicts you are concerned about. Does this solve your concern?
> 
> Also, at the code level, the parameter is stored in yaml file defined for each node. 

###### @JianKangEgon (2022-04-19)

> @TakaHoribe Thanks for the reply. Well, I understand your point and believe this kind of mechanism of ros2 functionality as well. However, I did meet such a confusing problem during my actual migration of autoware new Architecture proposal  about two or three months ago.  Here, I'd like to reproduce this issue in details as following:
> 
> - ubuntu 20.04
> - ROS2 Galactic
> - Autoware version: https://github.com/tier4/AutowareArchitectureProposal.proj
> 
> To realize transformation of the autoware control command to vehicle command, we have one vehicle driving-by-wire package named byd_dbw, its configuration file is shown as following:
> ![param_byd_controller](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/87111711/163909009-c5a46513-2364-4914-9e7f-6cd4ed0d0651.png)
> 
> We can see, there is one parameter named "control_rate" set to 100.0, to configure the frequency of vehicle command. And this package is launched in vehicle module. 
> 
> In comparison, the control_rate of velocity controller is defined in velocity_controller.launch.xml as "30.0" by default. And this node is launched in control module. 
> 
> When we run the autoware_launch file, we can see the interesting result:
> ![topic_hz](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/87111711/163910608-817cf795-3894-4250-8abd-5de704a8113e.png)
> 
> The topic hz of longitudinal controller is then set to 100. Although the parameters are defined in totally different modules and launched in different groups, there is still such an unpleasant problem occurred. Our solution is to rename the duplicated parameters.
> 
> Currently, we are working on migration of the autoware.universe to our real vehicle. It's much more reasonable to define each single parameter in yaml file rather directly in lauch file. After several tests, there does not exist conflict any more when duplicated names in different modules.

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-04-25)

> @JianKangEgon Thanks for sharing. This looks strange to me and I don't know why this is happening.
> 
> In this case, is the `longiturinal_controller/control_rate` parameter set to 100?

###### @JianKangEgon (2022-04-25)

> > @JianKangEgon Thanks for sharing. This looks strange to me and I don't know why this is happening.
> > 
> > In this case, is the `longiturinal_controller/control_rate` parameter set to 100?
> 
> @TakaHoribe Well, I was shocked at this problem as well and took a long time to figure it out. The longiturinal_controller/control_rate is always set to 30.0 by default. The planning simulator works always well because there is no any other control_rate defined in the launch file.
> 
> The first time I found this issue was about 3 months ago during our road test on site. The autoware_launch did not success to run the longitudinal controller all the time, and printed the "mismatched data type" on the screen. (The control_rate of byd_dbw was set to 100 at the very beginning, so there was the parameter declaration conflict between "int" and "double"). And we checked the launch file (longiturinal_controller/control_rate defined directly in it) again and again to confirm that this param was set correctly, until we found that there existed another control_rate even in different module in different launch file. 
> 
> Just amazing, for now, this issue seems to disappear after several attempts under the current mechanism to load parameter config. 
> 
> Thanks again for your reply and I'd love to share these unexpectable cases.

###### @Sharrrrk (2022-04-27)

> Merged.

### #684 — Isolate gtests in all packages

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-12  |  **Closed:** 2022-05-09  |  **Author:** @maxime-clem
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, priority:high
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/684

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Change the way gtests are run in all packages to ensure they are isolated from each other.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The change will prevent tests running in parallel and publishing topics to interfere with each other.
> For example, a test A subscribes to the `/tf` topic while a test B publishes transforms to the `/tf` topic.
> The purpose of this task is to ensure test A and B cannot interfere with each other.
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Replace the CMake commands `ament_add_gtest` with `ament_add_ros_isolated_gtest` similarly to what was done in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/661
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> All packages run gtests in isolation.

> 
> The diagnostics_aggregator is visualized in [rqt_robot_monitor](http://wiki.ros.org/rqt_robot_monitor), and DiagnosticsArray messages are also visualized in [rqt_runtime_monitor](http://wiki.ros.org/rqt_runtime_monitor).
> 
> However, we don't have any visualizer for `system_error_monitor` now.
> For example, when we fall into emergency, we have to echo some topics from `system_error_monitor` with terminal and analyse them to resolve.
>

> I believe this function can able to make our developers to resolve the problem like emergency more quickly.

> - create rviz plugin
> - create other GUI approaches

> - [ ] We can check the status and the problem by using them

### #662 — free space planner may collide obstacles with vehicle front

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-10  |  **Closed:** 2022-08-03  |  **Author:** @kosuke55
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:planning
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/662

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I think that the following lines shorten the forward length of the vehicle and may cause a collision.
> ``` 
>  for (double x = back; x <= front; x += costmap_.info.resolution) {
>     for (double y = right; y <= left; y += costmap_.info.resolution) {
> ```
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/freespace_planning_algorithms/src/abstract_algorithm.cpp#L135-L136
> 
> It's better to guarantee that `x(y)` exceeds `font(left)` like
> ``` 
>  for (double x = back; x <= front + costmap_.info.resolution; x += costmap_.info.resolution) {
>     for (double y = right; y <= left + costmap_.info.resolution; y += costmap_.info.resolution) {
> ```
> 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> The front of the vehicle does not collide with obstacles
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Sorry, I haven't reproduced it but the front of the vehicle may collide with obstacles.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Sorry, I haven't reproduced it but the front of the vehicle may collide with obstacles.
>

> _No response_

> _No response_

### #656 — Integration of Autoware Universe with Scenario Simulator

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-08  |  **Closed:** 2022-04-18  |  **Author:** @mitsudome-r
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/656

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> This tickets tracks the tasks required for the integration of TEIR IV's scenario simulator with Autoware Universe.
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> In Autoware.Auto we integrated TIER IV's [scenario simulator](https://github.com/tier4/scenario_simulator_v2) to do scenario based testing. The feature is needed for Autoware Universe as well in order to do regression testing in the CI.
> 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> In order to make the scenario simulator communicate with Autoware, we need to add adapter nodes which abstracts Autoware internal interface (topics) into topics used by the simulator and vice versa.
>  
> **NOTE:** We are also trying to refactor these nodes after reviewing the Interface designs in the future, but we would like to have something working to be merged first in order to remove the blocker for [planning module evaluation](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/566).  
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> * add TIER IV's ad_api_adapter repository as a dependency of universe https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/pull/156
> * add tier4_api_adapter launch files to universe https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/658
> * add launch tier4_api_adapter to high level launch files (like planning_simulator) https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/26

### #636 — behavior_path_planner can't plan a path with the first given goal command

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-05  |  **Closed:** 2022-04-08  |  **Author:** @mehmetdogru
- **Labels:** priority:high
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/636

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Most of the time, behavior_path_planner sometimes can't plan a path with the first given goal command from rviz2. And the node gives this error:
> ```
> [component_container_mt-13] [ERROR] [1649165181.816988526] [planning.scenario_planning.lane_driving.behavior_planning.behavior_path_planner]: behavior path output is empty! Stop publish.
> ```
> And when the second time a goal command is given (even though exactly the same goal pose as the first one) behavior_path_planner is able to plan the path.
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> behavior_path_planner should be able to calculate a path with the first goal pose given.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Most of the time, behavior_path_planner sometimes can't plan a path with the first given goal command from rviz2
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. Launch planning_simulator.launch.xml with any lanelet2 map and any .pcd file as it is described [here](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/#:~:text=%23-,Launch%20Autoware.,-source%20~/autoware/install).
> 2. Then [set an initial pose for the ego vehicle](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/#:~:text=Set%20a%20goal%20pose%20for%20the%20ego%20vehicle.).
> 3. [Set a goal pose for the ego vehicle](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/tutorials/ad-hoc-simulation/planning-simulation/#:~:text=Set%20a%20goal%20pose%20for%20the%20ego%20vehicle).
> 4. Repeat the 3rd step and observe if the path is created by behavior_path_planner.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - Autoware.universe commit hash: 70bc967d22a6bb8ca49c55296de833261a7f63fc
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @maxime-clem (2022-04-07)

> I am able to reproduce the issue but it is inconsistent and setting a goal sometimes works the first time.
> 
> Using `git bisect` I have identified the first bad commit as 982263a78e1079f054b428818636de1287801109.

###### @maxime-clem (2022-04-08)

> This issue was fixed by c341d4c4e4a79dd0b1f2259653a4f6cc3f7e4c50 but I observed a new issue where `behavior_planning` crashes after setting a goal. This crash happened only once but prevented the trajectory generation, even after setting the goal another time.
> ```
> [component_container_mt-13] Inconsistency detected by ld.so: ../elf/dl-tls.c: 481: _dl_allocate_tls_init: Assertion `listp->slotinfo[cnt].gen <= GL(dl_tls_generation)' failed!
> [ERROR] [component_container_mt-13]: process has died [pid 9361, exit code 127, cmd '/opt/ros/galactic/lib/rclcpp_components/component_container_mt --ros-args -r __node:=behavior_planning_container -r __ns:=/planning/scenario_planning/lane_driving/behavior_planning --params-file /tmp/launch_params_bzfw7nao'].
> ```
> EDIT: I cannot reproduce the crash and it might have been caused by an unclean build.

### #622 — dummy_perception_publisher publishes objects with acceleration

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-04-01  |  **Closed:** 2022-09-22  |  **Author:** @takayuki5168
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, component:tools
- **Comments:** 8  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/622

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Currently dummy_perception_publisher can publish the obstacle with the constant velocity. To realize more flexible use case, I'm thinking to add acceleration/deceleration functions to dummy_perception_publisher. This function will be helpful for obstacle stop/slow down (including adaptive_cruise_controller).
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> > To realize more flexible use case, I'm thinking to add acceleration/deceleration functions to dummy_perception_publisher. This function will be helpful for obstacle stop/slow down (including adaptive_cruise_controller).
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The current message to represent initial pose/twist of objects is `InitialState`.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/simulator/dummy_perception_publisher/msg/InitialState.msg
> 
> Instead of `InitialState`, how about `Motion` or `State` message as follows.
> ```
> geometry_msgs/PoseWithCovariance initial_pose_covariance
> geometry_msgs/TwistWithCovariance initial_twist_covariance
> double acceleration
> ```
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Objects' acceleration can be changed with dummy_perception_publisher.

**Comments:**

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-01)

> @yukkysaito 

###### @yukkysaito (2022-04-04)

> @takayuki5168 
> I agree with adding accel.
> 
> >how about Motion or State message as follows.
> 
> This was a little confusing.
> Are you saying that there is a type called Motion, State? If so, please provide a link.

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-04)

> @yukkysaito 
> > Are you saying that there is a type called Motion, State? If so, please provide a link.
> 
> Sorry to be confused. There is no existing messages. I just named Motion or State, whose content is as follows.
> ```
> geometry_msgs/PoseWithCovariance initial_pose_covariance
> geometry_msgs/TwistWithCovariance initial_twist_covariance
> double acceleration
> ```
> or it might be better like this
> ```
> geometry_msgs/PoseWithCovariance initial_pose_covariance
> geometry_msgs/TwistWithCovariance initial_twist_covariance
> geometry_msgs/Accel accel
> ```

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-04)

> I was thinking that in dummy perception publisher, in order to represent the case where the obstacle is running and will stop (= initial twist linear x is positive and acceleration is negative), the updated velocity (acceleration is added every cycle) will be made non-negative.
> But sometimes we may want to make obstacle running backward, which has a conflict with a rule that the update velocity is non-negative.
> 
> If we have max_velocity and min_velocity variable in a new message, which I named Motion or State, the conflict can be resolved, but I feel the number of variables is too many.
> Do you have any good idea.

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-05)

> max_velocity and min_velocity can be in config file of dummy_perception_publisher. Those values cannot be changed every obstacles though.

###### @yukkysaito (2022-04-05)

> I would prefer the following
> ```
> geometry_msgs/PoseWithCovariance initial_pose_covariance
> geometry_msgs/TwistWithCovariance initial_twist_covariance
> geometry_msgs/AccelWithCovariance initial_accel_covariance
> ```
> - The dummy perception may consider in the future.
> - Pose and twist are also cov for the above reason.
> 
> >max_velocity and min_velocity can be in config file of dummy_perception_publisher. Those values cannot be changed every obstacles though.
> 
> I agree with you.

### #610 — Add YOLO Custom Dataset Handler

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-30  |  **Closed:** 2022-07-06  |  **Author:** @goktugyildirim
- **Labels:** priority:high, component:perception
- **Comments:** 12  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/610

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Before training the YOLO object detector, we need to collect, manage, and combine the training and testing samples by being aware of their classes and label counts, etc. In order to facilitate the process, we need the YOLO label integration scripts for famous datasets consisting of related classes in autonomous driving in order to combine them and also the script for analyzing the whole samples coming from different datasets. Also, we need a script to send queries to the combined famous dataset database to generate our target dataset easily.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> The purpose of this feature is to make generating a custom dataset for the YOLO object detector easy using combined famous datasets such as KITTI, Waymo Open Dataset, etc. In sum, it makes it easy to increase and identify the labels of each image sample. 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Firstly, universal 2D object detection classes and important classes can be defined. Then running YOLO label integration scripts to provide a sample database with original labels. After providing YOLO label files for each sample, training huge YOLO nets like YOLOV4-p6 or YOLOV4-p7 for each important class element using maybe a million labels. We can do pseudo labeling over the samples to complete the missing class. For instance, KITTI Dataset doesn't consist of a traffic sign class and we can train a traffic sign detector using LISA Traffic Sign Dataset to do pseudo labeling over the KITTI dataset to increase our custom dataset size and identify labels of each image. Also, the handler script can take the specific queries to generate a custom dataset.
> 
> ![Design](https://github.com/goktugyildirim/autoware.universe/blob/yolo_custom_dataset_handler/perception/yolo_custom_dataset_handler/design.png?raw=true)
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Open to discussing 

**Comments:**

###### @xmfcx (2022-03-30)

> Thanks for creating this issue, I think maintaining a collective dataset is something we were always missing in autoware, it is great that someone is finally taking initiative on this task!
> 
> I propose to separate the `Custom Dataset Composer` and `Semi-Automatic Labeler` into different projects/issues.
> 
> Also I think it'd be best to use whatever classes the datasets contain for certain models. Like, if it doesn't contain a class we require, we just don't use that dataset for that purpose instead of auto-labeling (because these are always error-prone and should be manually checked).
> 
> So the custom dataset handler script would ask what classes are required for the collective dataset. And would select from the datasets that contain those classes.
> 
> And we should first analyze the pre-existing `Semi-Automatic Labeler` tools and see how our approach is different from them.
> 
> Some examples:
> - Free:
>   - https://github.com/virajmavani/semi-auto-image-annotation-tool
>   - https://github.com/jveitchmichaelis/deeplabel
>   - Maybe more from this list: https://github.com/heartexlabs/awesome-data-labeling
> - Paid:
>   - https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sms-automated-labeling.html

###### @goktugyildirim (2022-03-30)

> It can be named Custom Dataset Composer, it makes sense. In fact, pseudo labels will be improving our search algorithm on the datasets. You cannot combine the two datasets if they don't have common target classes. For instance, you want to train a custom detector with the target classes of "pedestrian" and "vehicle", and you have two different datasets having every single class.
> 
> dataset1: pedestrians (original labels)
> dataset2: vehicle (original labels)
> 
> In this case, you cannot take a sample from dataset1 if it contains a "vehicle" class. After "vehicle" pseudo labeling, you can find out which sample contains "vehicle" in dataset1 because the one class detector that has the high test scores can easily find out if the target sample contains a related class or not.  You can take samples from dataset1 not contains "vehicle". In sum, my approach is based on sample identification instead of Semi-Automatic Labeling. Also, one class detectors can improve the mAP of the YOLO model in the case of having too little sample from a class, even if the test scores of some classes are decreased. 
> 
> I added the " identify the labels of each image sample" part into the purpose section.

###### @xmfcx (2022-04-04)

> > You cannot combine the two datasets if they don't have common target classes.
> 
> I think we should take the datasets as they are and train only with the datasets with matching contents. If not it cannot be used. 
> 
> The datasets come with their list of labels that make clear what they contain. Anything else should be assumed non-labeled.

###### @goktugyildirim (2022-04-04)

> I got it, thanks for the reply. I'll only integrate the labels for YOLO, then implement a combining script.

###### @xmfcx (2022-04-19)

> @xmfcx create a new issue for renaming https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/simulator.repos to `tools.repos` and create & add autoware_datasets repository to there.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-05-24)

> @xmfcx Will do the creation of repo and update of repos this week.

###### @xmfcx (2022-05-31)

> @goktugyildirim I've created the repository here: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/custom_dataset_composer and gave you maintainer access on it.

###### @goktugyildirim (2022-05-31)

> > @goktugyildirim I've created the repository here: https://github.com/autowarefoundation/custom_dataset_composer and gave you maintainer access on it.
> 
> Thanks, @Zeysthingz is planning to take this issue on herself.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-06-21)

> @Zeysthingz Do you have any updates on this issue?

###### @Zeysthingz (2022-06-21)

> @mitsudome-r Yes I do. I will push updates  to repository but I try to understand how to do it in Autoware Universe. Probably I will update the repository in these two days.

###### @Zeysthingz (2022-07-06)

> @xmfcx Fatih can you assign available reviewers for pull request?

###### @xmfcx (2022-07-06)

> I think we can keep tracking this issue over the PR in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/custom_dataset_composer/pull/1/files

> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> - Ideally, the start request only can be triggered when the vehicle is reengaged.
> - But as now it only uses speed to decide the trigger, the start request is been triggered too easily.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> - Only trigger the start condition in a specific condition
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> The start request will only be triggered when the vehicle stop in the following cases
> 1. vehicle stop with stop_reason and the distance from the stop position is less than 0.5m
> 2. emergency state, 
> 3. current velocity is 0
>  
> Trigger start_request service after the stop_reason is gone, the emergency is clear, and desired velocity is more than 0
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Start request only trigger with above use case

###### @angry-crab (2022-05-31)

> **Instructions on running localization with KITTI**
> 
> Tools could be found in the following repo:
> [kitti_to_ros2bag](https://github.com/angry-crab/kitti_to_ros2bag)
> 
> 1. Create a pcd map
>  - clone the repo above
>  - in `create_map.cc`, change `pose_paths` and `pcd_paths` to where your data path, and path of saving output map. 
>  - `mkdir build && cd build`, `cmake ..`, `make`
>  - run `pcd_mapping` and wait for the map to be generated. 
> 
> 2. Create a ros2 bag
>  - in `create_bag.py`, change `base_dir`, `date`, and `drive` to the data you want to use.
>  - run `create_bag.py`
>  - wait for the bag to be generated.
> 
> (A ready-to-go dataset could be found here [sample map and bag](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hTePvUZ1_tTOefex4UgZqjdibGARjDtr/view?usp=sharing), I'm not sure if it is correctly shared, please let me know if it could not be accessed. )
> 3. Bring up `Universe`
> - Follow the instructions below, up to `vcs import src < autoware.repos` (DO NOT BUILD AT THIS TIME) [Autoware Doc](https://autowarefoundation.github.io/autoware-documentation/main/installation/autoware/docker-installation/)
> - Terminal 1
> `cd src/launcher/autoware_launch`
> `git checkout kitti_test`
> `cd ../../..`
> `colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`
> `source install/setup.bash`
> `ros2 launch autoware_launch logging_simulator.launch.xml map_path:=PATH_OF_YOUR_MAP vehicle_model:=sample_vehicle sensor_model:=sample_sensor_kit vehicle:=false system:=false map:=true sensing:=true localization:=true perception:=false planning:=false control:=false`
> - New Terminal 2
> `source ~/autoware/install/setup.bash`
> `ros2 launch autoware_launch kitti_static.launch.py`
> - New Terminal 3
> `source ~/autoware/install/setup.bash`
> `ros2 bag play PATH_TO_ROS2BAG/ros2_bag.db3 --qos-profile-overrides-path qos.yaml -d 3`
> - New Terminal 4
> `source ~/autoware/install/setup.bash`
> `ros2 service call /rosbag2_player/toggle_paused rosbag2_interfaces/srv/TogglePaused`
> - Go to Rviz of Terminal 1, set an intial pose, when Terminal 1 output `Alignment called`, go to Terminal 4 and rerun the last command. Then you are good to go. 
>  Check the link below for a video demonstration. [Sample Video](https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/334)

###### @angry-crab (2022-08-03)

> Duplicates of the related RP is found. Will try to merge this feature into the existing `localization_evaluator`.

### #584 — Function 'filterPointCloudByTrajectory' does not work as intended

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-25  |  **Closed:** 2022-04-25  |  **Author:** @maxime-clem
- **Labels:** type:bug, priority:low, priority:high
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/584

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Function `filterPointCloudByTrajectory` is used to filter a point cloud and only keep the points that are within a given distance from a trajectory. The current implementation is wrong and can return a point cloud with duplicate points and can be larger than the original point cloud.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/b06ff446a259b0f0bf4c0166d02c10a0628d8cab/control/obstacle_collision_checker/src/obstacle_collision_checker_node/obstacle_collision_checker.cpp#L52-L67
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> Function `filterPointCloudByTrajectory` returns a point cloud of size _at most_ equal to the size of the input.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> Function `filterPointCloudByTrajectory` can return a point cloud larger than the input.
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> Passing a very large `radius` will cause the bug.
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> The same `point` from the point cloud can be added multiple time if close enough to multiple `trajectory_point`.
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> Possible fix:
> ```C++
> for (const auto & point : pointcloud.points) {
>     for (const auto & trajectory_point : trajectory.points) {
>       const double dx = trajectory_point.pose.position.x - point.x;
>       const double dy = trajectory_point.pose.position.y - point.y;
>       if (std::hypot(dx, dy) < radius) {
>         filtered_pointcloud.points.push_back(point);
>         break;
>       }
>     }
>   }
> ```

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-04-05)

> @TakaHoribe Could you explain what control_performance_analysis is used for, and what kind of metrics are used to generate the result. 

###### @boyali (2022-04-07)

> This package computes;
> tracking error outputs:
> - lateral error ey
> - heading error eyaw
> 
> The tracking errors are computed by projecting current vehicle location on the current trajectory. In addition, the generated control vector u is used to compute an quadratic energy like value similar to we use in the MPC computations; uRu^T. We use the same kind of energy for the trackingΓÇÖs errors; xPx^T. 
> 
> The cost matrices R and P can simply be taken as unity matrices. However in the package we use an R and P matrices computed from stability LMI equations for a kinematic feedback controller.
> 
> In addition in the package we compute an approximate curvature for each waypoint on the trajectory.
> 
> Using the curvature, we can compute lateral velocity and acceleration. 
>

###### @mehmetdogru (2022-04-05)

> Some of the .yaml scenario files are created by ODD wg but testing them using scenario_test_runner with autoware.universe is not possible at the moment because of the current state of autoware.universe.

###### @mehmetdogru (2022-04-05)

> Here are the notes about the features I have tested so far using planning_simulator:
> 
> - **Stop Sign:** Tested in both Kashiwa and a custom map. For this feature to work hd-map must have an annotated stop_line and a stop_sign on the lane. Stops at stop_line while the vehicle's front bumper is on the stop_line. Waits as much as the time given as parameter. Then moves on.
> 
> - **Croswalk:** Tested in both Kashiwa and a custom map. For this feature to work hd-map must have an annotated crosswalk on the lane. Then it satisfies the conditions as explained [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/crosswalk-design.md). I have replicated those conditions using 2D Dummy pedestrian rviz tool while it was standing still and walking around/on the crosswalk. For vehicle to have a specific behavior for the crosswalk, any points of the pedestrian or any points of its predicted path should be in the annotated crosswalk polygon.
> 
> - **Swerve:** Obstacle avoidance feature works quite well. I used 2D dummy cars on several locations of the lanes and observed the ego vehicle behavior. Works as [it is proposed](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/behavior_path_planner_avoidance-design.md).
> 
> - **Lane Follow:** Module works as expected. Tested in both Kashiwa and a custom map. When there is a car(2D dummy car) in front of the ego vehicle, ego vehicle is able to apply ACC successfully.
> 
> - **Traffic Light:** When I test this module in Kashiwa map, ego vehicle stops at the red light and moves on at the green light. However in a custom map expected traffic light behavior has almost never been observed. I will create an issue about it and give more details about this problem. **Edit: fixed by** #623 
> 
> - **A bug:** #636 **Edit: fixed by** #650
> 
> - **Lane Change:** Tried this module on a custom map created wrt [this doc](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/behavior_path_planner_design_limitations.md) and made sure that neighbor lane is available. However lane_change module was never registered even though there is a car in front on the ego vehicle's lane moving forward with a slower speed. Further investigation is needed.
>

###### @sglee-morai (2022-05-23)

> For the scenario _UC-PB-005-0001-Hsinchu.yaml_, which I originally created, I see the note is written like below,
> 
> > * Vehicle doesn't stay on the stop line
> > * Vehicle sometimes can't make the right turn because of the narrow drivable area and gets stuck on the right turn. Fails with timeout"
> 
> The problem is that there is NO explicit stop line in the initial lane where the ego-vehicle is positioned initially. So please let me know if the scenario file itself should be modified.
> 
> Regardless of a stop line, the ego should stop anyway before entering any lane that is intersecting to the current lane that the ego is driving on, but I wonder what's your intention on the note whether to edit the scenario at the first place, so please let me know :) 

###### @mehmetdogru (2022-05-24)

> @sglee-morai 
> 
> The reason why I wrote this was that in ODD Design Document, initial case is defined as "EGO is stopping at the stop line" but the vehicle is not stopped on the stop line and it should be written :) You are right about that if the vehicle is already stopped before the turn, there is no difference between whether there is a stop line or not. It would matter tho if the initial vehicle speed was not zero, however no difference in this case.
> 
> There are no stop lines available on the lanelet2_map which would satisfy this _(UC-PB-005-0001)_ scenario design so there is nothing to be done on your end regarding the scenario content. Therefore I edited `Related Part` column for the scenario file as **lanelet2_map**. 
> 
> Thank you for the attention and the fine work.

### #565 — Evaluate performance of object detection pipeline

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-22  |  **Closed:** 2022-10-25  |  **Author:** @mitsudome-r
- **Labels:** priority:high, component:perception
- **Comments:** 12  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/565

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> Evaluate performance of perception pipeline.
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> Evaluate performance of perception pipeline to confirm if current perception has enough capability for BGus
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> Find available open datasets for evaluation and do benchmark testing.
> Possible datasets:
>  - Waymo dataset https://github.com/waymo-research/waymo-open-dataset
>  - KITTI dataset http://www.cvlibs.net/datasets/kitti/
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> - [x] plan data conversion for open datasets to feed into Autoware perception pipeline
> - [x] Develop benchmark tools to test perception pipeline
> - [x] Run tests on datasets and make results available in public. (e.g. in documentation)

**Comments:**

###### @kaancolak (2022-03-28)

> In the Autoware.Auto, we have 2D and 3D detection benchmark tools for the KITTI dataset. We can test our 2D/3D detections by integrating these tools into Autoware.Universe.
>  
>  In addition, I think, we need to evaluate the entire perception stack of Autoware.Universe from sensor output(Point Cloud/Camera Frame) to object tracking output, because all perception modules work together. Such as; deterministic and deep learning-based 3D bounding boxes are based merged or tracking results are merged with detected objects. For object tracking, the KITTI dataset has only 2D bounding box-based evaluation. For this reason, we are planning to implement Waymo dataset for 3D detection & tracking evaluation.

###### @kaancolak (2022-04-11)

> 
> ![waymo](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12658936/168068977-d7d8b636-b3e7-4633-9bc9-1d4a160db124.png)
> 
> I shared high-level architecture for the planned perception benchmark pipeline. If you have any comments feel free to share them with us. 
> 
> **Limitations when benchmarking with the Waymo dataset:** 
> 
> - We don't have PCD/Vector Map information from the Waymo dataset. The current perception pipeline can run with/or without PCD Map.  
> - In our codebase, a cylindrical prism is used when assigning shapes to pedestrians, we need 3D bounding boxes for pedestrians when evaluating with the Waymo dataset.
> 
> 
> **Current situation:**
> - I created a ROS interface that contains data conversion functionalities for the Waymo dataset.
> - I fed the data from the Waymo dataset to the lidar-only Autoware.Universe pipeline.
> 
> [![Img alt text](https://img.youtube.com/vi/iAdxLniX5CY/0.jpg)](https://youtu.be/iAdxLniX5CY)
> 
> There is small jittering I think caused by localization, base_link - global frame transformation.

###### @kaancolak (2022-05-12)

>  I shared the initial 3D tracking benchmark results in the README file of the PR. It contains only the results of the lidar-only pipeline. 
> 
>  For vehicles, everything works fine, but for pedestrians, we are giving a constant length and width size to the pedestrian bounding boxes in Autoware.Universe, it's equal to 1 meter.  But, Waymo Dataset has so strict IoU scores for matching tracked ground truth objects and predictions. When we give a fixed size to pedestrians, it falls below the cutoff score. (Vehicle: 0.7 , Pedestrian and Cyclist: 0.5)
> 
>  I will write a detailed explanation under the PR.  If you have any suggestions or advice please share them.

###### @WJaworskiRobotec (2022-05-23)

> @kaancolak I'm wondering if using Waymo Open Dataset Toolkit for evaluation is a good idea. I understand that the best solution would be to make it possible to use the same metric calculation software for Waymo, Kitti ( + other open datasets), as well as with synthetic data generated in the simulators. In this case, as Autoware is based on ROS2, it would be perfect to have metric calculation based on ROS topics directly, optionally on rosbags (like we develop in this [issue](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-projects/issues/11)) What is your opinion ? I'm not really familiar with Waymo Open Dataset toolkit, so I might misunderstand something.

###### @kaancolak (2022-05-25)

> @WJaworskiRobotec  Thanks for your feedback. 
> 
> Current benchmarking tool scripts subscribe to ROS2 topics and convert the tracked objects to the proto format desired by the Waymo dataset. If we want to compare our tracking result with other tracking submissions in the Waymo 3D Tracking Challenge, I think Waymo Open Dataset Toolkit is the best way for doing it, it contains a lot of special configurations for metric calculation. I chose the Waymo Dataset for the 3D tracking benchmark because most of the popular dataset doesn't contain a 3D tracking benchmark, like KITTI, Berkeley DeepDrive, and Lyft.
> 
>  If we want to evaluate our 2D, and 3D detection results with other open datasets and the synthetic data generated in the simulators, real-time evaluation directly over the ROS2 topic could be very useful, just need to implement proper metrics. I can easily extend the functionality of this tool. 

###### @WJaworskiRobotec (2022-05-25)

> Thanks a lot for the explanation. Pipeline that you created is perfect for comparing Autoware results with others, as well as it will be very easy to just connect metric calculation node that is created in the task I mentioned directly to the same topics that you connect the "data converter" converting to the Waymo format. Look perfect to me and once we have proper metrics we will connect it with your code.

###### @kaancolak (2022-05-27)

> @WJaworskiRobotec Instead of working on the different benchmarking pipelines, I think we can extend the metric calculation node. It's a more generic evaluator that contains the entire stack(evaluator, planning, control, detection, etc.) that makes sense. I would like to implement the perception(2D/3D perception) part on your metric calculation nodes, base algorithm will be very similar to this tool but must be in the same code format as your nodes.

###### @WJaworskiRobotec (2022-05-27)

> @kaancolak Sounds great. @djargot is currently working on the last node that we wanted to create as an example and it is related to perception (segmentation algorithm evaluation). Once it's done we will assign you as a reviewer, and you can continue with adding your nodes for 2D/3D Object Detection.

###### @kaancolak (2022-06-20)

> This PR waiting for review.

###### @xmfcx (2022-09-20)

> @kaancolak can you update the current status of this issue?

###### @kaancolak (2022-09-20)

> I have made some updates on the code base. Currently, it's waiting for review.

###### @epris (2024-05-24)

> Does the perception benchmark tool still work? It seems that there are some problems with the python version

### #561 — Improve Autoware performance on F1/10

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-22  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @HaoruXue
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/561

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I've agreed with the maintainers that I can plan this task.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> #### General performance
> 
> It was discussed in racing WG meeting regarding the general performance of Autoware.Auto on Jetson computers in terms of, for example, FPS and jigger of planning and perception outputs, and the possibility of using an entry level Jetson Nano. 
> 
> #### Localization
> 
> Current Autoware stack on F1/10 does not feature IMU sensor and KF for odometry, but instead uses odometry generated by motor and steering, unfiltered.
> 
> #### Perception 
> 
> a 2D object detection package needs to be identified and integrated with Autoware to enable multi-vehicle racing 
> 
> #### Planning 
> 
> for the record replay planner, the recorded trajectories should be generated by a trajectory optimization algorithm.
> 
> obstacle collision estimator should be integrated into dynamic trajectory modification.
> 
> #### Control (optional)
> 
> Replace pure pursuit with MPC
> 
> #### Operational (optional)
> 
> a low-cost, trackside telemetry solution is needed
> 
> Certain safety features in planning and control nodes that would estop the vehicle needs to be bypassed to allow longer running time on the track.
> 
> 
> 
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Purpose
> 
> To meet the need for the upcoming ICRA 2022 F1/10 competition, many can be done 
> 
> ### Possible approaches
> 
> #### General Performance 
> 
> Remove dependency on Rviz and run Jetson in headless mode.
> 
> #### Localization 
> 
> Configure an IMU as on the original F1/10.
> 
> Look into ΓÇÿrobot_localizationΓÇÖ for KF solutions.
> 
> #### Perception
> 
> 2D object detection TBD
> 
> #### Planning
> 
> Look into IAC teamsΓÇÖ open source trajectory optimization suite
> 
> 
> 
> ### Definition of done
> 
> Improve the baseline Autoware.Auto performance on F1/10 hardware in terms of reliability and lap time

**Comments:**

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @mitsudome-r (2026-03-24)

> I'm closing the issue that was inactive for a long time. Feel free to reopen if the issue is still relevant.

### #558 — Problems when add NPC to the scenario editor

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-22  |  **Closed:** 2022-05-10  |  **Author:** @beyzanurkaya
- **Labels:** type:bug
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/558

**Body:**

> ### Checklist
> 
> - [X] I've read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
> - [X] I've searched other issues and no duplicate issues were found.
> - [X] I'm convinced that this is not my fault but a bug.
> 
> ### Description
> 
> I created 5 different scenarios with the scenario editor. These scenarios were as follows:
> 
> 1. A single Ego vehicle is placed and a target position is in a different lane. The ego vehicle must change lane.
> 2. Ego vehicle and an NPC are in different lanes and their target positions are in their own lanes.
> 3. The Ego vehicle and an NPC are in different lanes, and their target position is in the lane the Ego vehicle is in. NPC must change lane.
> 4. The Ego vehicle and an NPC are in different lanes, and their target position is in the lane the NPC is in. The Ego vehicle must change lane.
> 5. The Ego vehicle and an NPC are in same lane, and their target position is in a different lane. Both vehicle must change lane. 
> 
> However, not all of these scenarios were successful.
> 
> In case 4, reference_trajectory msg cannot be received and autoware shut down.
> 
> > [openscenario_interpreter_node-3] [component_container-18] [INFO] [1647943781.308669420] [control.trajectory_follower.lane_departure_checker_node]: waiting for reference_trajectory msg... 
> 
> In case 5, the Ego vehicle changed lane but NPC didn't. 
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> 
> In case 4, reference_trajectory msg must be received and because of that the Ego vehicle should be able to change lane. 
> IN case 5, NPC, also should change lane.
> 
> ### Actual behavior
> 
> - NPC can not pass into the lane where the Ego vehicle is.
> - The Ego vehicle changed lane but NPC couldn't.
> 
> 
> 
> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> 1. I created several scenario in tier4 scenario editor.
> 2. If I add Ego vehicle and NPC in different lanes, and their destination point is the lane where ego vehicle is in, I can not get reference_trajectory msg, scenario can not be run and autoware shut down.
> 
> 
> 
> 
> ### Versions
> 
> - ROS2
> - autoware.universe 
> 
> ### Possible causes
> 
> _No response_
> 
> ### Additional context
> 
> _No response_

**Comments:**

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-05-10)

> This should be fixed now.
