### #535 — Max steer angle parameter is defined in each package, not in vehicle_info package

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-17  |  **Closed:** 2022-05-11  |  **Author:** @takayuki5168
- **Labels:** type:new-feature
- **Comments:** 14  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/535

**Body:**

> Since max steer angle parameter is not in the vehicle_info package, this parameter is defined in each packages' yaml file.

**Comments:**

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-03-17)

> cc @satoshi-ota 

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-03-17)

> Max jerk, acceleration, velocity are ~the same. (should be in vehicle_info package)~ in the common yaml, mentioned as follows.

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-03-17)

> @satoshi-ota @kenji-miyake @TakaHoribe 
> Do you agree, and if you do, do you have any other parameters to include in the `vehicle_info` package.

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-03-17)

> cc @yukkysaito @mitsudome-r @xmfcx 
> I agree that we should manage `max_steer_angle` as a global parameter.
> For what else, I have no concrete ideas, but I feel they should be categorized like `shape`, `hard_limit`, `soft_limit`, etc.
> 
> Also, as a long-term issue, we should write a design document for global parameters and re-design some packages for Autoware Core.

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-17)

> @kenji-miyake 
> We've already commonized max and min acceleration and jerk. It may be better to write max and min velocity as well here though.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/launch/tier4_planning_launch/config/scenario_planning/common/common.param.yaml
> 
> For the `vehicle_info` package, I don't have any parameters other than `max_steer_angle` so far.
> 
> @TakaHoribe 
> Could you give us your opinion. 

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-04-19)

> I agree to have `max_steer_angle` in the vehicle_info data. There already are some packages defining max_steer value in their local and it's getting messy.
> 
> About the velocity, it may be ok to have the max_velocity in the planning common param. In my opinion, we could have two max_velocity: `normal.max_velocity` and `limit.max_velocity`. They are like, "follow the limit if possible" and "vehicle must follow the limit". However the definition of the `normal` and `limit` is a little vague, so it'd be nice to add more detailed description for them when we add a max_velocty.
>  

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-20)

> I'm thinking about the name of the parameter, `max_steer_angle` or `max_tire_angle`. I'm not sure if `max_steer_angle` is confusing for non-Japanese people.
> 
> @xmfcx Could you tell me your opinion.

###### @xmfcx (2022-04-20)

> @takayuki5168 I think `max_steer_angle` is ok. 
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10751153/164230504-0f264013-1fc7-44cd-b3a1-e2d75fcd03e8.png)
> 
> Reference: http://street.umn.edu/VehControl/javahelp/HTML/Definition_of_Vehicle_Heading_and_Steeing_Angle.htm

###### @xmfcx (2022-04-20)

> @TakaHoribe 
> 
> > About the velocity, it may be ok to have the max_velocity in the planning common param. In my opinion, we could have two max_velocity: `normal.max_velocity` and `limit.max_velocity`. They are like, "follow the limit if possible" and "vehicle must follow the limit".
> 
> What is the difference between these 2? 
> 
> Why is a single speed limit not enough, like vehicle is never allowed to go over 50kmph?
> 
> The other speed limits are road related, not vehicle.

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-21)

> @TakaHoribe @kenji-miyake @xmfcx cc @tkimura4 @h-ohta 
> We found that `max_steer_angle` is not required for the differential wheeled robot.
> 
> So how about the following `vehicle_info.param.yaml`?
> Any major/minor comment would be welcome!
> ```
> /**:
>   ros__parameters:
>     wheel_radius: 0.39
>     wheel_width: 0.42
>     ...
>     vehicle_height: 2.5
> 
>     vehicle_model: "differential_model" # select the vehicle model from differential_model or bicycle_model
> 
>     differential_model:
>         # if there is any parameter for differential model.
>     bicycle_model:
>         max_steer_angle: 0.70 # [rad]
> ```

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-26)

> @TakaHoribe What do you think.

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-04-26)

> > What is the difference between these 2?
> 
> @xmfcx In my mind, just one velocity limit is enough.
> However, the concept of 2 limits (e.g normal.max_acc and limit.max_acc) is that different accelerations are use for emergency situations (like, a very large acceleration is required to avoid a risk) and non-emergency situations. And I think it is reasonable.
> 
> So we can apply the same idea to the velocity limit as well, that is, the two velocity limits for regular and emergency situations. For example, in the case of merging, ego-vehicle may sometimes need to accelerate beyond the velocity limit to avoid a collision to the behind vehicle.
> 
> But as you say, the velocity limit should be defined by the road, so just having two velocity limits as I wrote is not a good way.
> (I don't think we have to care about this right now though.)

###### @TakaHoribe (2022-04-26)

> @takayuki5168 
> The current policy for the adaptation to the differential drive robot is to consider the robot as a virtual Ackerman vehicle. 
> 
> In order to support the differential drive robot officially, we need to replace many parts of planning/control/vehicle modules.
> 
> Whereas, the drawbacks of the virtual Ackerman vehicle is handling of the non-essential parameters like steering angle and the lack of the pure angular-velocity rotation. This is not that burden compared to the modification of all Ackerman-specific modules.
> 
> So I suggest to have max_steer parameter for all types of vehicles (at least for now).

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-04-27)

> @TakaHoribe 
> 
> > In order to support the differential drive robot officially, we need to replace many parts of planning/control/vehicle modules.
> 
> Right. I've been thinking about using [this yaml file](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/535#issuecomment-1104791848) with the comment "the differential model is not officially supported. xxx have to be fixed.".
> 
> But I found this almost meaningless for now. Now I totally agree with your opinion. Thank you so much.

### #509 — Normalizing azimuth angle with wrong offset [dual_return_outlier_filter]

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-11  |  **Closed:** 2022-06-20  |  **Author:** @yucedagonurcan
- **Labels:** type:bug, component:sensing
- **Comments:** 6  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/509

**Body:**

> Hello,
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/67459763bd61a57e044132174dd1c403550c1f00/sensing/pointcloud_preprocessor/src/outlier_filter/dual_return_outlier_filter_nodelet.cpp#L180
> 
> Doesn't it need to be 360000.f? It looks like there is this error every time we try to normalize the angle.

**Comments:**

###### @badai-nguyen (2022-04-15)

> Hello @yucedagonurcan 
> I think the line is to make sure the difference of adjacent points in a ring azimuth_diff being in range [0.0f  36000.0f].
> Could you describe more details about the error have you get? 

###### @yucedagonurcan (2022-04-19)

> @badai-nguyen , I am guessing that we need to fix the difference between [0, 360) not [0, 36).

###### @badai-nguyen (2022-04-21)

> @yucedagonurcan Hi, I am sorry for misunderstanding your question. 
> 
> > Doesn't it need to be 360000.f? It looks like there is this error every time we try to normalize the angle.
> 
> Because the current LiDAR's azimuth represents angle in hundredths of degree so that it should be 36000.0f.

###### @yucedagonurcan (2022-04-24)

> Okay, it's a fair approach if we know it is `hundredths of degree`
> 
> But if we are parsing the sensor data from the Ouster, user tend to calculate the azimuth value as millidegrees which is the format of the incoming data. 
> 
> @badai-nguyen  maybe the best approach to make it a parameter rather than fix value? What do you think?

###### @badai-nguyen (2022-04-26)

> @yucedagonurcan yes, I totally agree that it is better to parameterize that. I will fix it. 

###### @badai-nguyen (2022-06-20)

> I close this issue because I created an related one here #1127 

---

### #508 — Easier way to find the emergency reason

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-11  |  **Closed:** 2022-03-18  |  **Author:** @takayuki5168
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 5  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/508

**Body:**

> Currently we manage emerngey with diagnostics, and we can see its reasons on rqt_robot/runtime_monitor.
> 
> However, we do not always run rqt_robot/runtime_monitor, so if the emergency occurrs, we have to run rqt_robot/runtime_monitor and reprocude the emergency again to find the reason.
> IMO, it's better to output emergency reason when it occurrs in standart output log with RCLCPP_WARN/ERR_THROTTLE (WARN for latent fault, and ERROR for single point fault), in order to easily find the emergency reason.
> 
> It's also very helpful to find the emergency reason of scenario test, which was run on CI since we have standard output log for each scenario test.

**Comments:**

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-03-11)

> @kenji-miyake What do you think? If you agree, I'll implement this output.

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-03-11)

> @takayuki5168 As a tentative way, I think it is acceptable.
> But ideally, we should define the interface for notifying the emergency reason from Autoware to the simulator because the console log isn't a good UI for everyone.
> Then the simulator catches the notification and shows it on the result page.
> 
> Also, could you show me a screenshot of the result page for reference?
> 
> @yukkysaito @mitsudome-r @isamu-takagi @xmfcx Any ideas?

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-03-11)

> @kenji-miyake 
> > Then the simulator catches the notification and shows it on the result page.
> 
> What I mentioned is not only for the scenario test analysis but also for running autoware with simple planning simulator or on the physical vehicle. I don't think it's not good to output the emergency reason on the standard output log for those cases.
> 
> Could I talk about how the scenario simulator gets the information of emergency reasons from Autoware in another issue since it's different from what I wanted to discuss :pray: 

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-03-11)

> @takayuki5168 I'm sorry, I couldn't understand that well. :cry: 
> What you want to do seems to me just adding a hacky interface.
> 
> For `simple_planning_simulator`, it's the same.
> The console log isn't a good interface because we cannot get it programmatically.
> People have to look into the logs and try to find out the reason, it's not efficient or scalable. It's just supplemental information. 
> 
> > Could I talk about how the scenario simulator gets the information of emergency reasons from Autoware in another issue
> 
> Yes, of course, it's fine.

###### @takayuki5168 (2022-03-11)

> I've talked with Miyake-san.
> In summary, we first implement just standard output of the emergency reasons, and see whether it works good for debugging from the point of view of development and product service (So far we don't even have a clear requirement). Then we may be able to think about the better idea based on how the current one works.
> 
> For the scenario simulator, I'll create another issue as I said.
> 
> Any comment would be welcome if you have.

---

- **Labels:**

### #494 — Map Based Prediction Incorrect Predictions

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-07  |  **Closed:** 2024-08-27  |  **Author:** @08beeqtufail-sudo
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale, component:perception
- **Comments:** 28  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/494

**Body:**

> Hello Everyone,
> I am testing the proposed map based prediction with some of the bag files and a map that I have at my disposal. I am facing the problem that the map_based_prediction outputs some strange trajectories (e.g, a trajectory going backwards for an object moving straight in its lane etc...) .After digging in the code a little bit, i can see that the condition to check whether to do a linear prediction or the normal prediction is decided based only on the object velocity x component (object.kinematics.twist_with_covariance.twist.linear.x) . But an object's velocity in map frame is not only x component. So i would like to know the rationale behind this. Thank you for your time and great work. 
> Regards,
> M.Tufail

**Comments:**

###### @yukkysaito (2022-03-18)

> @08beeqtufail-sudo 
> Thanks for the report.
> 
> We are currently working on a major revision and may be able to cure it there.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/491/files

###### @08beeqtufail-sudo (2022-03-18)

> @yukkysaito Thanks for your reply. I am following the repository you mentioned for future updates.
> 
> 

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-04-19)

> @08beeqtufail-sudo It seems like the PR mentioned by @yukkysaito is merged. Could you check if the issue still remains? If it still does, please provide a reproducing steps (or a rosbag) so that others can investigate the bug.

###### @08beeqtufail-sudo (2022-04-20)

> @mitsudome-r I am currently working on another project but i will test it within a couple of days and let you know.

###### @08beeqtufail-sudo (2022-04-21)

> @mitsudome-r @yukkysaito I was able to test the latest map_based_prediction with some bag files. I still have the same problem. I can see in the code that the part that decides whether to do linear prediction or normal prediction still checks the x component of twist of an object. But the tracked objects in my custom bag files are in map_frame. So the objects have a x velocity part and a y velocity part. So the speed of an object should be calculated based on both of these components. The decision to do linear prediction or not, should be based on this speed and not just x-component? 
> It is worth mentioning that the tracked objects i have in my bag file are coming from an independent perception module, not from the autoware.universe perception module. I just adapt the format in order to use with map_based_prediction module of autoware.universe. 
> So it is entirely possible that the tracked objects given by autoware.universe perception module only have x components, in that case, using only the x-component of velocity makes sense. 

###### @xmfcx (2022-05-17)

Note that this is a right-hand traffic scenario, similar to european countries. I have investigated the problem, some of the problems come from the fact that the estimated velocity is not stable in my case. 
> But another problem is that the map_based prediction performs a linear prediction based on whether an object's x velocity is less than a certain threshold, which in my case is not a good enough criteria. Because the objects have celocities in map frames and performing linear prediction based on x component value is not sufficient.

As i have earlier explained in my post, the problem is correctly identified. The fact that our perception and tracking system is different than that of autoware.universe, means we have x-velocity and y-velocity components of the tracked or detected objects. While in autoware.universe simulation, that's not the case. When i test the autoware.universe simulation, there's no problem. But when i test the autoware.universe planning with our own perception system, that's when the problem arises.

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-09-27)

> @mitsudome-r to discuss with the authors of prediction nodes to check about y-velocity component of prediction results.

###### @simon-t4 (2022-10-11)

> Hi ,if I understand correctly, the problem lies in the confusing the twist coordinate frame.
> The original Autoware publishes predicted objects using an object centric frame, while this issue describes a perception system where the predicted path is in map frame.
> 
> The ROS twist message is I think defined with linear and angular components rather than x,y of a map frame. 
> The velocity is meant to be independent of pose of object so an object centric frame is preferred.
> 
> A simple fix would be for the perception system described to convert x,y components into linear and angular components needed by Autoware (and consistent with ROS message definition) and perhaps publish the two messages as different topics (if x,y frame needed by other components).
> 
> 

###### @mitsudome-r (2022-10-25)

> From ASWG:
> - @xmfcx and @mitsudome-r agree to use object centric frame for velocity expression
> - We still need to update/improve prediction module so that it fills in y component as necessary depending on detected velocity. 

###### @xmfcx (2022-11-01)

> We will consider this feature while refactoring for the core architecture.

> Noted. Removed from Bus ODD Milestone and Project.

### #493 — Avoidance Planner for dynamic obstacles

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-07  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @purewater0901
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale
- **Comments:** 4  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/493

**Body:**

> Currently, Autoware does not have any functions to safely avoid collisions with dynamic obstacles. In order to safely navigate the vehicle in dynamic environment, we should add dynamic obstacle avoidance functions to the Autoware. The minimum requirements for the dynamic obstacle avoidance planner are
> 
> - Collision avoidance with vehicular obstacles
> - Considering comfortability of the passengers as well safety of the vehicle and other road participants.
> - Avoid unnecessary brake or deceleration

**Comments:**

>

>

> - The [Dynamic Avoidance Module](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/main/planning/behavior_path_planner/src/scene_module/dynamic_avoidance/dynamic_avoidance_module.cpp) has been implemented to realize this dynamic obstacle avoidance.

### #490 — Refactoring Map Based Prediction

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-07  |  **Closed:** 2023-03-22  |  **Author:** @purewater0901
- **Labels:** type:new-feature
- **Comments:** 3  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/490

**Body:**

> Autoware is currently using map based prediction to predict future trajectories of the object. However, this node has some limitations. 
> 
> - It only outputs one possible trajectory .
> - It does not calculate confidence correctly compared to its reference paper.
> - Predicted yaw angle of the object is not correct.
> - The readability of the code is not preferable level.
> 
> Therefore, we need to create a new architecture for prediction node to fix these problems.

### #488 — remove LibTorch dependencies from lidar_centerpoint

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-03-07  |  **Closed:** 2022-04-05  |  **Author:** @yukke42
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/488

**Body:**

> LibTorch (PyTorch C++ API) is useful to deploy the models trained on PyTorch and used for the lidar_centerpoint implementation, but this library has mainly two disadvantages for autoware.
> 
> - It needs to be built for every OS and CUDA version. (https://pytorch.org/)
> - It has fuge cuda libraries and they allocate more than 1GB of GPU memory, but most of them aren't used in lidar_centerpoint. (https://discuss.pytorch.org/t/pytorch-1-8-1-cu111-package-size-and-memory-usage-issue/128713)
> 
> Therefore, libtorch needs to be removed and the equivalent libraries used for lidar_centerpoint are to be reimplemented.

**Comments:**

###### @yukke42 (2022-04-05)

> PR is merged.

### #417 — Single LiDAR-Blockage diagnostics

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-02-18  |  **Closed:** 2022-04-15  |  **Author:** @badai-nguyen
- **Labels:** component:sensing
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/417

**Body:**

> **Problem**
> The LiDAR - blockage is phenomenon when some unwanted objects cling LiDARs and block the emitted/return light.
> Blockage situation as out of ODD which might significantly degrade the performance of LiDAR is necessary to be detected.
> The blockage might be cause by wide range of objects in the environments, for instance, leaf, plastic bag, dust, snow, ice ...
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/94814556/156111472-5fdab38b-50c4-4e24-b003-c78a40766c96.png)
> 
> 
> **Suggestion**
> 
> Blockage can be detected based on the empty return region of LiDAR point cloud or LiDAR depth map with considering the ground and sky range for each LiDAR. 
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/94814556/154658847-9324c1b9-b90b-4dec-aaee-ebb0507bf8af.png)
> 
> > Blank region in ground-range: high possibility of blockage 
> > Blank region is only in sky-range : low possibility of blockage
>  
> 
> 
> 

**Comments:**

###### @badai-nguyen (2022-04-15)

> This issue has been resolved by #461

### #398 — ekf_localizer fails when clcok rate is slower than predict_frecency

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-02-16  |  **Closed:** 2022-02-22  |  **Author:** @kosuke55
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/398

**Body:**

> [predict_frequency](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/tier4/proposal/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_localizer.cpp#L39) is 50 hz by default, but when `use_sim_time` is set to true and `/clock` is used, timer callback is called by hz of `/clock`. Therefore,  [the predict rate does not match to ekf_dt](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/tier4/proposal/localization/ekf_localizer/src/ekf_localizer.cpp#L368-L373) and localization fails. 
> 
> ex) predict_frequency:50 , clock_rate:20 [bag_file](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1hzUf6EPVlKw3mvlFBUi1QzjdLoa4dHAZ)
> `ros2 bag play <bag_file> --topics /vehicle/status/twist /sensing/imu/imu_data /diagnostics /localization/util/downsample/pointcloud /rosout /sensing/gnss/pose_with_covariance  --clock 20`
> https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39142679/154257037-a0fb2b01-5893-4bb1-a9b3-d02af28b79f7.mp4
>

### #390 — Add design document of interface_test.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-02-16  |  **Closed:** 2023-08-18  |  **Author:** @KeisukeShima
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, status:stale
- **Comments:** 7  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/390

**Body:**

> # The reason of this change
> By creating a framework for interface testing, we can perform efficient testing with less effort.
> Design documentation will be created to discuss the design and usage.
> 
> # Approach
> 
> We will use rclpy's API to gather information about the topics that nodes are sending and receiving. Since no actual messages are sent or received, the test can be completed in a short time.
> The predefined topic information is compared with the actual information to ensure that the specification and implementation are consistent.
> 
> # Alternatives
> 
> I considered using `launch_testing` to actually send and receive messages. However, this test is time consuming. It also requires more effort to set up the test than the above approach, since we have to define the appropriate inputs for each node.
> For these reasons, I did not adopt this approach.

**Comments:**

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-02-16)

> Same as this comment.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/issues/380#issuecomment-1038659995
> 
> If you create an issue, please write more descriptions so that people can understand.

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-02-17)

> @KeisukeShima Could you describe what errors can be prevented by this kind of test?
> For example, "if a developer mistakenly wrote here as ..., then it will cause the error of ...".

###### @KeisukeShima (2022-02-17)

> > @KeisukeShima Could you describe what errors can be prevented by this kind of test? For example, "if a developer mistakenly wrote here as ..., then it will cause the error of ...".
> 
> If a developer mistakenly specifies the wrong topic, then this test will fail.
> This ensures that the specification and implementation match on a node by node basis, and prevents topic inconsistencies between nodes.

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-02-17)

> Could you show me a concrete example of the mistake in `launch.xml` or `.cpp`? :thinking: 

###### @KeisukeShima (2022-02-18)

> > Could you show me a concrete example of the mistake in `launch.xml` or `.cpp`? thinking
> 
> I updated the design docs. I think this is the answer, so have a look at the link.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/391/files#diff-a790f3b1a2981da08ef8d466c4e13a5086a78ddba58a9f88f8b3b1b1c877525dR14-R15

### #389 — Improve autoware_testing

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-02-16  |  **Closed:** 2023-08-18  |  **Author:** @KeisukeShima
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, type:good-first-issue, status:stale
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/389

**Body:**

> ## Motivation
> 
> `autoware_testing` provides basic tests that can be used in common for all packages.
> However, the current implementation is only a `smoke_test`, and what can be checked with this test is limited.
> I read an issue on `Autoware.Auto` about the design of `autoware_testing` ([link](https://gitlab.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.auto/AutowareAuto/-/issues/700)) and thought it could be improved.
> Specifically, it solves the `smoke_test` problem and introduces a new interface test. This way, node activation and interface checking can be added to all packages with less effort.
> 
> ## Action Items
> 
> ### Smoke test
> 
> - [x] Resolve issues related to the return code. (Related: [link](https://gitlab.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.auto/AutowareAuto/-/merge_requests/1300#note_831669630))  -> #479
> - [ ] Add `smoke_test` to all packages.
> 
> ### Interface test
> 
> - [x] #390
> - [ ] Implement `interface_test`.
> - [ ] Add `interface_test` to all packages.
> 
> ## References
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware-documentation/issues/2#issuecomment-1031410200
> https://gitlab.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.auto/AutowareAuto/-/issues/951

### #372 — CodeCov does not show correct coverage diffs in PR comments

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-02-10  |  **Closed:** 2022-06-21  |  **Author:** @KeisukeShima
- **Labels:** type:bug, status:stale
- **Comments:** 9  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/372

**Body:**

> This is due to the fact that only the packages that have changed are being built and tested by CI.
> I am looking for a solution.
> 
> ex. https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/370#issuecomment-1034434086
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19993104/153360093-e2afff16-7453-43c4-9ff7-eac4c3c316c1.png)
> 

**Comments:**

###### @KeisukeShima (2022-02-10)

> Do I have to merge the differences with the overall coverage before uploading them?
> 
> ![codecov drawio](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19993104/153373692-bcb2e911-a40d-4951-b76b-7c410c7fdb6e.png)
> 

###### @KeisukeShima (2022-02-14)

> https://github.com/KeisukeShima/demos/pull/2
> 
> I found that in order to output the diff coverage, I need to specify the appropriate `.lcovrc` file and merge the results.
> The Coverage diff in the comments shows up fine, but the list of changed files still has problems.

###### @KeisukeShima (2022-02-14)

> > The Coverage diff in the comments shows up fine, but the list of changed files still has problems.
> 
> Now, the list of changed files works well.
> https://github.com/KeisukeShima/demos/pull/2#issuecomment-1038931083
> 
> The necessary requirements are listed in the comments below.
> https://github.com/KeisukeShima/demos/pull/2#issuecomment-1038969113

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-02-16)

> Could you summarize the problem, the solution, and the evidence, in addition to the results, please? :bow:

###### @KeisukeShima (2022-02-17)

> ## Problem
> 
> CodeCov does not show correct coverage diffs in PR comments.
> 
> ![img](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19993104/153360093-e2afff16-7453-43c4-9ff7-eac4c3c316c1.png)
> 
> ## Solution
> 
> Merge the coverage generated by the differential build with the full coverage results from the base branch. This tells CodeCov that there are no changes to the packages that were not built in the diff build.
> When merging, you need to specify `branch_coverage=1`.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/384/files#diff-0e24b6901e8528bd669e9e78acb1327c99dd72aed1affe58b818eb65899e1ce6R60
> 
> ```mermaid
> flowchart LR
>     A[Diff coverage] --> B[Merged coverage]
>     C[Total coverage] --> B
>     B --> CodeCov
> ```
> 
> Add `codecov.yaml` to the default branch.
> Include the following items in the yaml
> Set `flags` and enable `carryforward`. This is to carry forward the coverage of the base branch for packages that are not built in the diff build.
> 
> ```yaml
> flags:
>   total:
>     paths:
>       - ".*"
>     carryforward: true
> ```
> 
> Upload the coverage file, including the flags, to CodeCov. This is to enable the codecov.yaml settings.
> 
> ```yaml
>       - name: Upload coverage to CodeCov
>         if: ${{ steps.check-file-existence.outputs.exists == 'true' }}
>         uses: codecov/codecov-action@v2
>         with:
>           files: lcov/total_coverage.info,coveragepy/.coverage
>           fail_ci_if_error: false
>           verbose: true
>           flags: total
> ```
> 
> ## Evidence
> 
> I confirmed that it works with my fork.
> https://github.com/KeisukeShima/demos/pull/2#issuecomment-1038931083
> 
> ## Result
> 
> As shown in the linked image below, the CodeCov coverage report is displayed correctly in PR.
> https://github.com/KeisukeShima/demos/pull/2#issuecomment-1038931083
> 

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-02-17)

> @KeisukeShima Great! Thank you for your clear explanation! :smile: 

###### @KeisukeShima (2022-03-29)

> Related
> https://community.codecov.com/t/carryforward-flag-problems-with-delta-testing/3388/3

###### @stale (2022-06-18)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-06-21)

> I believe it's resolved by #384. So I'll close this issue.

### #359 — Drivable area from behavior_path oscillate, resulting in unstable path planning.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-02-08  |  **Closed:** 2022-03-11  |  **Author:** @takayuki5168
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/359

**Body:**

> In autoware.universe, drivable area is generated from behavior_path_planner and used in obstacle_avoidance_planner for path planning.
> 
> 1. Current drivable area has a issue that drivable area is generated in the ego coordinate,
> meaning that drivable area oscillates since ego pose estimation is noisy,
> resulting in unstable path planning since the road boundary is unstable (oscillates).
> We can make the drivable area coordiate fixed by setting the coordinate to the map coordinate.
> 
> 2. Drivable area is supposed to see enough area for the ego to follow in a few seconds.
> Previously, ego pose and drivable area pose are the same, so drivable area can see forward area with fixed drivable area size (100m forward, 50m backward).
> However, setting the drivable area coordinate to the map one requires dynamic drivable area size, since ego pose and drivable area pose are not the same and if sending very large drivable area, its topic or calculation cost of drivable area will become higher.
>

### #357 — Fine weather Lidar Visibility dropped issue

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-02-08  |  **Closed:** 2022-04-11  |  **Author:** @badai-nguyen
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/357

**Body:**

> **Background**
>  LiDAR Visibility is estimated based on noise point-cloud of weak_first_return from LiDAR Dual Mode. 
> 
> **Problem**
> In road-side scenes which contain sparse point cloud objects such as plants, leaves or sport plastic nets, the LiDAR Visibility results are dramatically dropped, even in fine weather condition.
> 
> The reason is that such objects also return weak_first point cloud and treated as raindrop.
> 
> **Suggestions** 
> 1. Add logic to detect the sparse point cloud objects from weak_first_return point cloud, by extending the range of segment points
> 2. Exclude weak_first_return point clouds close to the last_strong_return point clouds which tend to be objects
> + Pros: high sensitivity
> - Con: computation cost increase 
> 
> 2. Exclude weak_first_return point cloud by setting region of interest (ROI):
> + Pros: low computation cost
> - Cons: low sensitivity

**Comments:**

> 

###### @miursh (2022-04-11)

### #350 — make spline interpolation flexible

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-02-07  |  **Closed:** 2022-03-11  |  **Author:** @takayuki5168
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/350

**Body:**

> For spline interpolation, currently only static function `slerp(base_keys, base_values, query_keys)` is supported in interpolation package.
> 
> However, sometimes we'd like to use interpolation statically like
> - call interpolation function not statically (
> ```
> SplineInterpolation spline;
> spline.calcInterpolation(base_keys, base_values); // calculate spline interpolation matrix
> const auto res1 = spline.interpolate(query_keys1);
> const auto res2 = spline.interpolate(query_keys2);
> ```
> - or call both just interpolation function and yaw angle interpolation if we can.
> ```
> SplineInterpolation spline;
> spline.calcInterpolation(base_keys, base_values); // calculate spline interpolation matrix
> const auto res = spline.interpolate(query_keys;
> const auto res_yaw = spline.interpolateYaw(query_keys);
> ```
> 
> Of course static function is useful since we do not have to create an object for spline interpolation.
> Therefore, both static and non-static functions for spline interpolation is required for more flexible usage.

### #347 — osqp_interface cannot deal with warm start well.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-02-07  |  **Closed:** 2022-02-16  |  **Author:** @takayuki5168
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/347

**Body:**

> In order to use warm start in osqp_interface, P and A matrices have to meet a certain condition (the positions of zero does not change, the matrix size is fixed).
> However, the application can pass only raw P and A matrices to osqp_interface initializer, and csc matrix will be generated in osqp_interface, where the application cannot handle meeting the condition for warm start.
> 
> Therefore, the initializer of osqp_interface with csc matrix for P and A is required so that the application can assure that the condition for warm start will be satisfied.

---

### #289 — Add planning_evaluator package to evaluate planning module performance.

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-01-24  |  **Closed:** 2022-02-17  |  **Author:** @kyoichi-sugahara
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 0  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/289

**Body:**

> ## problem
> 
> The evaluation infrastructure for planning development is not in place, and degradation checking and performance evaluation depend on humans. This process should be automated and some quantitative indicators need to be defined and the results visualized.
> This allows for efficient evaluation of development and comparison between different planners.
> 
> ## suggestion
> 
> Using the trajectory generated by the planning module as input, create a node that can evaluate the smoothness of the trajectory, etc.
> This node can be activated separately from autoware when you want to evaluate the trajectory.
> If you want to evaluate different property, you can add functions to planning_evaluator.
> 
> ## pros and cons
> 
> By defining a reasonable index, quantitative evaluation of the trajectory becomes possible, but there is a possibility that the performance of autoware itself will deteriorate if the processing load of the planning_evaluator itself increases.
> 
> ## transition plan
> 
> Since there is currently no function that utilizes the output of this node, there is no need to consider it.

### #255 — Fix calcuation of angle difference

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-01-16  |  **Closed:** 2022-01-18  |  **Author:** @kyoichi-sugahara
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 2  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/255

**Body:**

> In the function of angle difference calculation, NaN value is returned when the absolute value of inner product is larger than 1.
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/045009c4834f9c0ae9c2a0513e6f6c12ee88e86a/map/lanelet2_extension/lib/query.cpp#L38-L45
> 
> This is because arg of atd::acos shouldn't be outside the range [-1.0, 1.0] expalined [here](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/numeric/math/acos).
> Numerical error happens in some cases so gurad needs to be added.

**Comments:**

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-01-18)

> @kyoichi-sugahara Could you explain specifically in what situations the inner product will be larger than 1, please?

###### @kyoichi-sugahara (2022-01-18)

> @kenji-miyake 
> Sorry for not describing the detail.
> I had same a same problem with the [link](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52138147/why-is-acos-resulting-in-nanind-when-using-the-result-of-a-dot-product)
> 
> When `angle1` and `angle2` are the same, `vec1.dot(vec2)` expected to be 1. but in some cases, the value which is larger than 1 is calculated because of numerical error.

### #239 — consider case when autoware overshoot internally or externally

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2022-01-11  |  **Closed:** 2022-01-28  |  **Author:** @taikitanaka3
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/239

**Body:**

> There are some modules which doesn't define case for overshooting stop line without fulfilling stop condition by internal control error or external manual input that causes "Stop forever until manual override is applied".  For example stop line defines stop state as 2 [sec] velocity below of 0.1[m/s] at 2[m] around stop line however if there is manual override or  control error occur and over stop line stop line without notice then it will never meet stop line condition and stop velocity insert forever. So we should clear dead line margin (margin after stop line) which "we don't consider distance to stop line as a stop condition". So my suggestion is if overshoot happens "stop anyway for 2 sec at any place, then GO".
> 
> overshoot: mostly caused by manual override by human who thinks already stopped and stop condition was met in autoware but actually not.  

**Comments:**

###### @taikitanaka3 (2022-01-28)

> close this issue solved  by #240

### #143 — Consider using global_parameter_loader

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2021-12-07  |  **Closed:** 2026-03-24  |  **Author:** @kenji-miyake
- **Labels:** type:new-feature, priority:low, status:stale
- **Comments:** 9  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/143

**Body:**

> With our current plan, there will be multiple `default_common.param.yaml`, but it might increase the maintenance cost, for example when the common parameter gets a new variable.
> 
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/c2e79c3a56956f867030b2cbc9675e2e7c7c1339/planning/external_velocity_limit_selector/config/default_common.param.yaml
> - https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/c2e79c3a56956f867030b2cbc9675e2e7c7c1339/planning/motion_velocity_smoother/config/default_common.param.yaml
> 
> To avoid this, we can consider `global_parameter_loader`.
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/c2e79c3a56956f867030b2cbc9675e2e7c7c1339/planning/behavior_velocity_planner/launch/behavior_velocity_planner.launch.xml#L3
> 
> https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/blob/c2e79c3a56956f867030b2cbc9675e2e7c7c1339/common/autoware_global_parameter_loader
> 
> ### Without global_parameter_loader
> 
> launch.xml:
> 
> ```xml
> // planning.launch.xml
> <launch>
>   <include file="behavior_planner.launch.xml">
>     <arg name="common_param_path" value="{path_to_file}" />
>     <arg name="vehicle_param_path" value="{path_to_file}" />
>   </include>
> </launch>
> 
> 
> // behavior_planner.launch.xml
> <launch>
>   // Don't consider the default values here because you can't use them when you debug in the real environment.
>   <arg name="common_param_path" />
>   <arg name="vehicle_param_path" />
> 
>   <node ...>
>   </node>
> </launch>
> ```
> 
> How to launch:
> 
> ```sh
> // autoware.launch.xml
> ros2 launch autoware_launch autoware.launch.xml vehicle_model:={vehicle_name}
> 
> // behavior_planner.launch.xml
> ros2 launch planning_launch behavior_planner.launch.xml common_param_path:={path_to_file} vehicle_info_param_path:={path_to_file}
> ```
> 
> ### With global_parameter_loader
> 
> launch.xml:
> 
> ```xml
> // planning.launch.xml
> <launch>
>   <include file="behavior_planner.launch.xml">
>     // No arg
>   </include>
> </launch>
> 
> // behavior_planner.launch.xml
> <launch>
>   <include file="$(find-pkg-share autoware_global_parameter_loader)/launch/global_params.launch.py"/>
> 
>   <node ...>
>   </node>
> </launch>
> ```
> 
> How to launch:
> 
> ```sh
> // autoware.launch.xml
> ros2 launch autoware_launch autoware.launch.xml vehicle_model:={vehicle_name}
> 
> // behavior_planner.launch.xml
> ros2 launch planning_launch behavior_planner.launch.xml vehicle_model:={vehicle_name}
> ```
> 

**Comments:**

###### @esteve (2022-05-26)

> @kenji-miyake this is how we solved this issue in Autoware.Auto: https://gitlab.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.auto/AutowareAuto/-/merge_requests/978 The solution was to move the vehicle characteristics (which are common to many packages and were duplicated everywhere) to a separate params file and then load it from launch files. The main difference between Autoware and Autoware.Auto is that we are using XML files to launch packages, but I think the Python scripts are more flexible.

###### @esteve (2022-06-15)

> @kenji-miyake are you actively working on this? I'd be happy to help :slightly_smiling_face: 

###### @kenji-miyake (2022-06-15)

> @esteve Thank you for your confirmation.
> Actually, no. I'm not working on this now.
> 
> If you can help with this, I think it's good to start by collecting developers' opinions in https://github.com/orgs/autowarefoundation/discussions/416.
> It's because there are no big technical issues and we only have to decide the design considering trade-offs of possible solutions.
> 
> Or I think it's also good to submit a draft PR so that everyone can have a more concrete image, and discuss the design there.

###### @stale (2022-08-14)

> This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity.
> 

###### @yukkysaito (2022-10-18)

> I agree with the introduction of global parameter because the maintenance cost of launch is high if the file path is passed.

###### @yukkysaito (2022-10-18)

> I will try to work on it this month.

###### @yukkysaito (2022-11-30)

> I'm working in [this PR](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_launch/pull/116)

### #112 — Consider using Composite Actions instead of Reusable Workflows in GitHub Actions

- **State:** CLOSED  |  **Created:** 2021-12-04  |  **Closed:** 2021-12-27  |  **Author:** @kenji-miyake
- **Labels:** 
- **Comments:** 1  |  **URL:** https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/112

**Body:**

> [Reusable Workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/learn-github-actions/reusing-workflows) are very useful, so I introduced [here](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.universe/pull/53).
> 
> However, I found it has a few disadvantages in some use cases.
> https://github.community/t/ref-head-in-reusable-workflows/203690/17
> 
> Therefore, I'll replace some of the Reusable Workflows with Composite Actions.
> 
> [Composite Actions]
> - To reuse some steps, not the entire job
> - To refer to local actions or files
> 
> [Reusable Workflows]
> - To reuse the entire job
> - To make the task's environment clean or separated

**Comments:**

###### @kenji-miyake (2021-12-27)

> Resolved by #161

## Appendix C — Extended Issue Digests (ranks 41–160 by comments)

> One-line digests derived from the issue bodies/comments, **grouped by area** for
> developer scanning. Full threads remain in Appendix B.

### Planning (behavior, motion, mission, parking)
- **#6452 behavior_planning_container dies because of guard_condition** — rclcpp guard-condition bug; fixed by upstream rclcpp (closed/fixed).
- **#3223 PullOver/Out limitation and development plan** — expanded goal/start/freespace planners (closed/implemented).
- **#1011 Update planning simulation** — sample map too narrow to turn; map + plugin fixed (closed/fixed).
- **#1958 obstacle_avoidance_planner randomly zigzags on a straight line** — high-speed pose/MPT; unreproducible (closed/no-conclusion).
- **#2079 Vehicle not able to avoid static obstacle by changing lane** — stale behavior tree config; merge fixed (closed/workaround).
- **#3368 Regression: planner stops for sudden "outside drivable area"** — drivable-area nearest-segment bug; reduced forward length (closed/workaround).
- **#2125 behavior_path_planner generating invalid path orientation** — yaw not checked across lanes; no fix (closed/no-conclusion).
- **#6546 Invalid path when goal behind vehicle** — start_planner lacks backward routing (closed/unsupported).
- **#934 Collision path when obstacle crosses centerline** — max-shift limitation; removed via PR (closed/fixed).
- **#1793 Path out of lane when obstacle near intersection** — avoidance lacked intersection check (closed/workaround).
- **#1716 Checking only 4 corners in drivable area** — footprint check too sparse (closed/stale).
